# Build gaps — comprehensive spec-vs-implementation audit

Per-subsection checklist of gaps between the Lenny spec (`spec/`) and
the implementation (`pkg/`, `cmd/`, `charts/`, `migrations/`, `schemas/`,
`sdks/`, `compose/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`). Each finding is a checklist
item — **OPEN** by default. Replace `- [ ]` with `- [x]` and change
`OPEN` to `RESOLVED <commit-sha>` when fixed.

## How findings are formatted

Every finding heading is rendered as a checklist line and ends with the
literal marker ` — OPEN`. The finding ID prefix carries the spec
subsection: an ID `F-4.6.3` (or `H-2`, `M-5`, `8.10-1`, etc. for
sub-agent reports that did not adopt the canonical prefix) lives under
the `## §X.Y` heading immediately above it, so the §X.Y reference is
always one heading away. Each subsection block opens with an HTML
anchor for cross-linking from the table of contents.

Inside each finding:

- `**Spec:**` — verbatim quote or close paraphrase with the spec line
  reference.
- `**Evidence:**` — `file_path:line_number` pointers (or
  `"no implementation found in <searched paths>"`).
- `**Gap:**` — concrete description of what is missing, partial, or
  divergent.
- `**Suggested resolution:**` — one-line action.

## Severity guide

- **High** — spec MUST violated; production correctness, security, or
  safety issue; documented endpoint returns 404; capability cannot be
  exercised end-to-end.
- **Medium** — spec SHOULD not met; capability claim unimplemented;
  audit event or metric declared but never emitted; missing
  operator-tunable knob.
- **Low** — minor divergence, naming mismatch, missing doc, partial
  config knob.
- **Info** — noteworthy observation that is not a gap.

## How to use this file as a checklist

1. Pick a subsection from the table of contents.
2. Read every finding under that subsection.
3. As each finding is resolved, replace the checkbox `- [ ]` with
   `- [x]` and change `OPEN` to `RESOLVED <commit-sha>` (and add a
   short PR / commit note inline).
4. When every finding under a subsection is closed, the subsection
   itself can be marked complete in the table of contents.

## Methodology and scope

Findings come from 154 per-subsection audits run on 2026-05-22 and
2026-05-23, one sub-agent per `a.b` spec heading across §4–§17 and
§23–§27. Section §18 (build sequence) was excluded by user request.
Each audit:

- Read the entire subsection of the spec (including any nested
  `a.b.c` headings).
- Enumerated normative requirements.
- Searched the implementation for each requirement.
- Classified each as Implemented, Partial, Missing, or Divergent.
- Recorded only Partial/Missing/Divergent items plus Info observations.

Audits were independent, so the same gap may appear under multiple
subsections when the underlying defect spans concerns. Cross-references
are not yet deduplicated; treat related findings as a cluster.

## §4.0 Agent Operability Additions <a id="4.0"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/04_system-components.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

§4.0 is an index that enumerates the operability-related additions: the standalone `lenny-ops` component, twelve shared Go packages (with prescribed file paths), and five subsystems that must take an `EventEmitter` dependency and emit specific operational events at documented transition points. The standalone `lenny-ops` binary, the in-memory event buffer, the runbook index, remediation locks, backup service, diagnostics service, MCP management server, capacity recommendations, `/v1/admin/me`, and the `ImageResolver` are implemented (often at divergent file paths). However, the event-emit wiring for four of the five enumerated subsystems is missing (only the session manager and the operator-managed circuit-breaker handler emit; the pool upgrade state machine, the warm-pool / pool-state manager, and the credential pool / renewal worker do not). The unified Operations Inventory and Progress Envelope / ETA endpoints are absent, and the `pkg/common/scopes`, `pkg/ops/gateway/{client,discovery}`, `pkg/ops/metrics/source`, `pkg/ops/events/service`, and `pkg/ops/operations/{inventory,eta}` packages do not exist. The shared `pkg/alerting/rules` bundle is only used by a YAML generator and is not compiled into the gateway or `lenny-ops` runtime. Counts: 5 High, 7 Medium, 6 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] F-4.0.1 — Pool upgrade state machine does not emit `upgrade_progressed` [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: medium) — F-10.5.7 — Both concern the §25.8/§10.5 platform-upgrade state machine in pkg/upgrade, but F-10.5.7 is the missing orchestrator consumer and F-4.0.1 is the missing upgrade_progressed event emission; F-4.0.1 is also CLOSED.

- **Spec:** "Pool upgrade state machine (§10.5) — emits `upgrade_progressed` on each phase transition with pool, old phase, new phase, and image digest." (line 31)
- **Evidence:** `pkg/upgrade/upgrade.go` (the phase state machine) imports neither `opsevents` nor any event sink. A repo-wide grep for `EventUpgradeProgressed` or `"upgrade_progressed"` returns only the catalog declaration and tests (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go:20`), the alerting-rule reference (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go`), and the catalog test. No call site emits the event. The `lenny-ops` cron loop (`pkg/ops/opsservice/cronloop.go`) names `platform_upgrade_check` only as a comment; there is no upgrade orchestrator that emits.
- **Gap:** The event type is declared but never emitted; the upgrade state machine has no `EventEmitter` dependency.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add an `EventEmitter` (`*opsevents.Emitter`) field to the pool upgrade orchestrator and emit `dev.lenny.upgrade_progressed` with `pool`, `oldPhase`, `newPhase`, and `imageDigest` data on each `upgrade.Next` transition.

### - [ ] F-4.0.2 — Warm pool / pool state manager does not emit `pool_state_changed` [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: medium) — F-4.0.11 — Both stem from no EventEmitter wired into the controller, but one is the warm-pool reconciler not emitting pool_state_changed and the other is the absent event transport between controller and gateway.

- **Spec:** "Pool state manager (warm pool state: `draining`, `warming`, `exhausted`) — emits `pool_state_changed` on each transition; lives alongside the warm pool controller (§4.6.1)." (line 32)
- **Evidence:** `pkg/controller/warmpool/controller.go` has no `opsevents` import. `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` constructs `warmpool.Reconciler` (line 146) without an emitter — `grep "opsevents|OpsEmitter|EventBus" cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` returns no matches. The event type `EventPoolStateChanged` is referenced only in the catalog, in tests, and in webhook subscription tests (`pkg/ops/opsservice/webhookloop_test.go:138`).
- **Gap:** The warm-pool reconciler transitions pods between `warming` / `ready` / `draining` (e.g., `pkg/sandbox/state/state.go:20-38`) without emitting `pool_state_changed`. No `EventEmitter` is wired into the controller process.
- **Suggested resolution:** Wire an `opsevents.Emitter` into `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` (sharing the gateway's Redis stream destination once it lands), pass it to the `WarmPoolReconciler`, and emit `dev.lenny.pool_state_changed` whenever the derived pool phase changes.

### - [ ] F-4.0.3 — Credential pool manager does not emit `credential_rotated` or `credential_pool_exhausted` [High] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "Credential pool manager (§4.9) — emits `credential_rotated` on lease rotation and `credential_pool_exhausted` on pool exhaustion." (line 35)
- **Evidence:** `pkg/credential/credential.go` and `pkg/gateway/credrenewal/credrenewal.go` carry no `opsevents` import. The renewer exposes `OnRenewed` and `OnExhausted` callbacks (`pkg/gateway/credrenewal/credrenewal.go:55-69`), wired in `cmd/lenny-gateway/cred_renewal.go:155 onRenewed` and `cmd/lenny-gateway/cred_renewal.go:198 onExhausted`. Both callbacks push the credential to the pod or log a failure; neither calls `opsEmitter.Emit`. The event types `EventCredentialRotated` / `EventCredentialPoolExhausted` are declared only in `pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go:24-25` and are referenced only by the catalog test.
- **Gap:** Despite the operator-facing `/v1/admin/events/buffer` endpoint advertising both events, no runtime path emits them.
- **Suggested resolution:** Extend the `credRenewalWiring.onRenewed` / `onExhausted` hooks (or the underlying credential-pool manager) to call `opsEmitter.Emit` with the matching `EventType` and the lease's pool / provider / session metadata.

### - [ ] F-4.0.4 — Unified Operations Inventory and ETA computation are absent [High] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "`pkg/ops/operations/{inventory,eta}.go` — unified Operations Inventory and canonical Progress Envelope / ETA computation." (line 25)
- **Evidence:** Directory `pkg/ops/operations/` does not exist. `grep -rln "OperationsInventory\|operationsInventory\|operationsService"` returns no matches. `grep "/v1/admin/operations\|/v1/admin/me/operations"` returns only the alerting rule description (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1498`) and the openapi.json contains no `/admin/operations` route. ETA-computation helpers (`ComputeETA`, `EtaCalc`) are not present — only the `EtaMethod` enum and the `Progress` struct in `pkg/ops/conventions/conventions.go:186-221`.
- **Gap:** The unified `/v1/admin/operations` and `/v1/admin/operations/{id}` endpoints from §25.4 / §15.1 (rows 1575, 4415-4416, 4904-4905 of the spec) are not implemented; the canonical ETA computation logic does not exist; the MCP `lenny_operations_list` and `lenny_operation_get` tools have no backing.
- **Suggested resolution:** Create `pkg/ops/operations/inventory.go` (per-subsystem operation source aggregator) and `eta.go` (canonical ETA from rate/percent/historical-p50), register the `/v1/admin/operations[/{id}]` routes on the gateway admin router, and add the two MCP management tools.

### - [ ] F-4.0.5 — `pkg/common/scopes` RFC 9068 scope parser does not exist [High] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "`pkg/common/scopes/scopes.go` — RFC 9068 `scope` claim parser and matcher for `tools:<domain>:<action>` values. Consumed by the admin-API middleware and the MCP adapter." (line 26)
- **Evidence:** Directory `pkg/common/scopes/` is absent (`ls /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/common/` returns only `registry`). The JWT claims struct carries `Scope` (`pkg/auth/jwt/jwt.go:59`), but no shared parser exists. `pkg/gateway/middleware/auth/auth.go` does not reference `scope` at all. The MCP management server implements its own header-based parser (`pkg/ops/mcpmgmt/server.go:289 requestScopes`) that reads the `X-Lenny-Scope` request header rather than the validated JWT `scope` claim, and the comment at `server.go:280-288` acknowledges "until the JWT middleware lands."
- **Gap:** No shared RFC 9068 parser / matcher. The admin-API middleware does not consume the scope claim; the MCP adapter consumes a stand-in header. Both consumers the spec names are missing or stubbed.
- **Suggested resolution:** Create `pkg/common/scopes/scopes.go` exporting `ParseScope`, `Matches(required, granted)`, and the `tools:<domain>:<action>` form. Wire the admin-API middleware to populate the request scope set from the validated JWT and have `pkg/ops/mcpmgmt/server.go` consume the typed scope set instead of the header.

### - [ ] F-4.0.6 — `pkg/ops/gateway/{client,discovery}.go` and headless-Service fan-out are missing [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "`pkg/ops/gateway/{client,discovery}.go` — `GatewayClient` plus headless-Service replica discovery." (line 16)
- **Evidence:** No `pkg/ops/gateway/` directory exists. `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:194` calls a single `gatewayURL` for `/healthz` only (`opsservice.GatewayProbe(gatewayHTTP, *gatewayURL+"/healthz")`). The chart renders the `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service (`charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:282-298`) advertising "per-replica DNS A record so lenny-ops can fan out §25.3 health, recommendation, and event queries to every replica", but no Go-side caller dials the per-replica addresses. `grep -rn "gateway-pods\|lenny-gateway-pods" pkg/ cmd/` finds no usage.
- **Gap:** `lenny-ops` cannot fan out health / recommendation / event queries to individual gateway replicas; only the front-door Service is reachable. The MCP management server documents a `GatewayClient` route (`pkg/ops/mcpmgmt/server.go:52 "either a local lenny-ops handler or, via GatewayClient, a gateway admin-API endpoint"`) but no `GatewayClient` is implemented.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add `pkg/ops/gateway/client.go` (an `http.Client` wrapper that authenticates to the gateway admin API via mTLS or service-account token) and `pkg/ops/gateway/discovery.go` (resolve `lenny-gateway-pods.<ns>.svc.cluster.local` via the in-cluster resolver and iterate per-replica). Wire both into the `lenny-ops` opsserver `MCP` invoker and the health / recommendation aggregators.

### - [ ] F-4.0.7 — `pkg/ops/metrics/source.go` MetricSource + Prometheus reader missing [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "`pkg/ops/metrics/source.go` — Prometheus-with-fan-out-fallback `MetricSource` implementation and a Prometheus-backed `MetricReader`." (line 17)
- **Evidence:** Directory `pkg/ops/metrics/` does not exist. `grep -rln "MetricSource"` returns zero results. The only `MetricReader` is the gateway-side `WindowStore` in `pkg/gateway/recommendations/metricreader.go:19-49`, which the package comment notes "the gateway backs it with the in-process WindowStore; lenny-ops backs it with a Prometheus-backed reader" — but no Prometheus-backed reader exists. `grep -rn "Prometheus" cmd/lenny-ops/` returns only the docstring (`main.go:6`). `pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go:6` mentions Prometheus only in the package doc.
- **Gap:** `lenny-ops` cannot read recommendation / capacity metrics from Prometheus; capacity-recommendation evaluation on the ops side has no metric source.
- **Suggested resolution:** Implement `pkg/ops/metrics/source.go` with a Prometheus-API-backed `MetricSource` (instant queries + range queries for `WindowedRate`) and a `MetricReader` that satisfies the `pkg/gateway/recommendations.MetricReader` interface. Add a fan-out fallback that aggregates `/metrics` scrapes from each gateway replica when Prometheus is unavailable.

### - [ ] F-4.0.8 — `pkg/ops/events/service.go` event-stream service (SSE) missing [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "`pkg/ops/events/service.go` — event stream service (SSE, polling, webhooks)." (line 18)
- **Evidence:** No `pkg/ops/events/` directory. The closest packages are `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/` (webhook subscription CRUD — `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/eventsubscription.go:1-25`) and `pkg/ops/opsservice/webhookloop.go` (webhook delivery worker). `grep -rn "text/event-stream" pkg/ops/` returns no matches; SSE on the gateway is only the session-event stream in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events.go:61`. `lenny-ops` does not expose an event SSE endpoint; the only ops-side query is the gateway-side `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go:51`), which is polling-only.
- **Gap:** The unified event-stream service that combines SSE, polling, and webhook delivery (one service, three transports) is split across components and missing the SSE / polling transports on `lenny-ops`.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add `pkg/ops/events/service.go` that consumes the Redis-streamed operational events and exposes `GET /v1/admin/events/stream` (SSE) and `GET /v1/admin/events?cursor=` (polling) on `lenny-ops`, while continuing to fan out to the existing webhook subscriptions.

### - [ ] F-4.0.9 — Bundled alerting rules not compiled into gateway or lenny-ops [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "`pkg/alerting/rules` — shared bundled alerting rules, compiled into both the gateway and `lenny-ops`." (line 11)
- **Evidence:** `grep -rln "alerting/rules" cmd/lenny-gateway/ cmd/lenny-ops/` returns no matches. The only importer is `cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go:33`, a build-time YAML renderer. The alerting state evaluator `pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go` exists but is only imported by its own test file (`grep -rln "alerting/evaluator" .` returns only `pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator_test.go`).
- **Gap:** The shared rule bundle is reachable as YAML via Prometheus but is not compiled into the runtime binaries that the spec names. No runtime alert state evaluator runs.
- **Suggested resolution:** Import `pkg/alerting/rules` (and `pkg/alerting/evaluator`) into `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` and `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go`, instantiate the evaluator against the local `MetricReader`, and emit `alert_fired` / `alert_resolved` events through the existing emitter.

### - [ ] F-4.0.10 — `EventEmitter` is a concrete struct rather than an interface [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.3.14 — Both report that EventEmitter is a concrete struct with an Emit signature that drops ctx and returns uint64 instead of matching the spec interface.

- **Spec:** "`EventEmitter` interface and in-memory ring buffer. Every subsystem that emits operational events depends on this package." (line 13) and "The subsystems below take `EventEmitter` as a constructor dependency and call `Emit(ctx, event)` at the documented state-change point." (line 29)
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go:19` declares `type Emitter struct` — no interface is exported. Every consumer takes the concrete `*opsevents.Emitter` (e.g., `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go:328 OpsEmitter *opsevents.Emitter`, `pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:142 eventEmitter *opsevents.Emitter`). The `Emit` method signature is `Emit(event OperationalEvent) uint64` (`emitter.go:40`) — no `ctx` argument, contradicting the spec's `Emit(ctx, event)` contract.
- **Gap:** Subsystems depend on a concrete type rather than an interface; the signature drops the ctx the spec calls for; substituting a Redis-backed emitter (the `§25.3` future destination noted at `emitter.go:17`) requires constructor type changes across every consumer.
- **Suggested resolution:** Extract `EventEmitter` interface (`Emit(ctx context.Context, event OperationalEvent) (uint64, error)`) in `pkg/gateway/opsevents`, make the current struct satisfy it, and switch all consumers from `*opsevents.Emitter` to the interface. Thread `ctx` through emit sites so cancellation propagates.

### - [ ] F-4.0.11 — Pool-state and warm-pool emitters not threaded into controller binary [Medium] — CLOSED

## §4.1 Edge Gateway Replicas <a id="4.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/04_system-components.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

The gateway implementation covers the core externally-facing responsibilities (OIDC/OAuth auth, REST + MCP + OpenAI + Open Responses adapters mounted by mux, session routing, upload mediation, elicitation chain, policy/interceptor chain) and ships a per-tier Helm chart with HPA/KEDA scaling. However, several normative §4.1 deliverables are absent: the spec-mandated `PodDisruptionBudget` and rolling-update strategy (`maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 25%`) are not rendered on the gateway Deployment; the dedicated `/mcp/runtimes/{name}` endpoint for `type: mcp` runtimes is explicitly deferred to v2; the four declared subsystem boundaries (Stream Proxy, Upload Handler, MCP Fabric, LLM Proxy) only exist as code packages without independent goroutine pools, queue depth limits, or per-subsystem in-memory circuit breakers (only LLM Proxy has its own breaker); the HPA primary/secondary trigger metrics (`lenny_gateway_request_queue_depth`, `lenny_gateway_active_streams`) and the capacity-ceiling alert input (`lenny_gateway_active_sessions`, `lenny_gateway_max_sessions_per_replica`) are exposed by the metric registry but never updated by any production code path; per-subsystem `lenny_gateway_subsystem_*` metrics and the GC pause metric are catalog-only with no emitter; the `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica` Helm value is read-only documentation that never reaches the gateway binary; and the §4.1 "Phase 2 calibration" extraction thresholds have no Helm-value surface. **Counts:** High 4, Medium 6, Low 3, Info 2.

### Findings

### - [ ] F-4.1.1 — Gateway Deployment has no PodDisruptionBudget [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.4.4, F-17.1.1, F-17.3.2 — Four members report the gateway Deployment renders no PodDisruptionBudget; F-4.1.12 covers only the separate topology-spread gap.

- **Spec:** "PodDisruptionBudget to limit simultaneous disruptions" (line 61). §17.1 cross-reference mandates `maxUnavailable: 1 at every tier`.
- **Evidence:** `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` renders ServiceAccount/ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding/Deployment/Service/headless-Service (lines 44, 56, 94, 109, 255, 286) but NO PodDisruptionBudget. `grep -rln "kind: PodDisruptionBudget" charts/lenny/templates/` returns only `token-service-deployment.yaml`, `admission-policies/cosign-verify-webhook.yaml`, `admission-policies/_webhook.tpl`. No `lenny-gateway` PDB resource exists. `charts/lenny/values.yaml:623` and `charts/lenny/templates/autoscaling-gateway.yaml:99` both reference "the §17.1 maxUnavailable:1 PDB" as the binding constraint, but the PDB itself is never rendered.
- **Gap:** Without a PDB the gateway is exposed to mass concurrent evictions during `kubectl drain`, cluster-autoscaler node consolidation, or rollouts. The HPA scale-down policy (1 pod / 60s) was tuned around a PDB-bound floor that does not exist; the §16.5 `PDBBlockedEvictions` alert can never fire.
- **Resolution:** `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` now renders a `PodDisruptionBudget` named `lenny-gateway` (`maxUnavailable: 1`) selecting the gateway labels, gated on the new `gateway.podDisruptionBudget.enabled` Helm value (default `true`). `charts/lenny/values.yaml` documents the value and its opt-out. `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` adds three helm-unittest assertions: the default render contains seven documents including the PDB; the PDB carries `maxUnavailable: 1` and the gateway selector; setting `gateway.podDisruptionBudget.enabled: false` drops the document count to six (the PDB is the only opt-outable document, so the count check pins the absence).

### - [ ] F-4.1.2 — Gateway Deployment has no rolling-update strategy [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.5.9 — Both report the gateway Deployment declares no rolling-update strategy block, falling back to the K8s 25% default; F-10.5.9 covers gateway plus controller/token-service while F-4.1.2 is gateway-only and CLOSED.

- **Spec:** §17.1 cross-reference linked from §4.1: "Rolling update strategy: `maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 25%`."
- **Evidence:** `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` (lines 109-252) defines `spec:` with replicas/selector/template only — no `strategy:` block. `grep -rn "strategy:\|maxSurge\|maxUnavailable" charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` returns no matches.
- **Gap:** The Kubernetes default `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 25%, maxSurge: 25%` applies. At Tier 3 (~20 replicas) this lets up to 5 replicas drain concurrently during a rollout — exceeding the per-replica 400-pod CheckpointBarrier fan-out budget §17.1 specifically forbids.
- **Resolution:** `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` now renders `spec.strategy = { type: RollingUpdate, rollingUpdate: { maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 25% } }`, gated on the new `gateway.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable` and `gateway.rollingUpdate.maxSurge` Helm values (defaults `1` and `25%`). `charts/lenny/values.yaml` documents both fields and the disruption-axis split (rolling-update strategy vs PDB). `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` adds two helm-unittest assertions: the default render carries the spec-mandated `maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 25%`; a custom override (`maxUnavailable: 2, maxSurge: 50%`) flows through. `helm template charts/lenny -s templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` shows the strategy block before the selector.

### - [ ] F-4.1.3 — HPA scale-out gauges are registered but never updated [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.1.1 — Both report the gateway HPA scale-out gauges are registered but never updated by any production code path; F-4.1.3 is marked CLOSED.

- **Spec:** Line 71: "`lenny_gateway_request_queue_depth` — Primary HPA scale-out trigger." Line 72: "`lenny_gateway_active_streams` — Secondary HPA metric." Line 73: "`lenny_gateway_active_sessions / gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica` — Capacity ceiling alert."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics.go:64-96, 273-296` registers the gauges and defines `SetActiveSessions`, `SetActiveStreams`, `SetRequestQueueDepth`, `SetRejectionRate`. `grep -rn "SetActiveSessions\|SetActiveStreams\|SetRequestQueueDepth\|SetRejectionRate" pkg/ cmd/` returns ONLY the definitions in `gatewaymetrics.go` and matching `gatewaymetrics_test.go` calls. No production caller exists — neither `pkg/gateway/sessionserver`, `pkg/gateway/watchdog`, nor `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` invokes them.
- **Gap:** The HPA primary trigger reports a constant `0` (the gauge's initial value), so the §4.1 SCL-026 autoscaling pipeline (`charts/lenny/templates/autoscaling-gateway.yaml`) cannot scale. The `GatewaySessionBudgetNearExhaustion` and `GatewayActiveStreamsHigh` alerts (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:570-584`) can never fire.
- **Resolution:** `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` adds `exportHPAGauges`, a 5-second periodic poller that updates the three gauges from live in-process state: request queue depth from `gatewaymetrics.Metrics.InflightRequests` (the new metrics Middleware counter, incremented on entry / decremented on exit via `atomic.AddInt64`), active streams from `sessionevents.Bus.ActiveSubscribers` (new helper that walks the bus's subscriber map and counts non-closed entries), and active sessions from a per-tenant `sessionstore.List` walk filtered by `!session.IsTerminal`. The poller is launched alongside the existing 30-second `exportGaugeMetrics` goroutine but ticks at 5s so the custom-metrics pipeline (Prometheus Adapter / KEDA) observes back-pressure quickly enough to scale before the saturation threshold. New tests: `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics_test.go` — `TestMiddlewareTracksInflightRequests` (handler holds the request, exporter observes inflight=1, releases, inflight returns to 0); `cmd/lenny-gateway/main_test.go` — `TestExportHPAGaugesUpdatesAllGauges` (seeds 2 active + 1 terminal session, subscribes one SSE listener, drives an in-flight request, asserts the three gauges; second poll drops queue_depth to 0); `TestExportHPAGaugesContextCancellation` (cancelled context returns promptly without spurious updates).

### - [ ] F-4.1.4 — `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica` Helm value is never plumbed into the gateway binary [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.1.12 — Both report gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica is never plumbed into the gateway binary so the capacity-ceiling gauge/alert cannot function; F-4.1.4 is CLOSED but describes the identical defect.

- **Spec:** Line 65: "this limit is expressed as `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica`." Line 75: "defines the capacity ceiling used by the alert above". Lines 77-82 set per-tier provisional values (50/200/400/400).
- **Evidence:** `charts/lenny/values.yaml:546` declares `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica: 50`; `charts/lenny/presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml` override per tier (50/200/400). `grep -rn "maxSessionsPerReplica" charts/lenny/templates/` returns no matches — no env var, no flag, no ConfigMap reads this value. `grep -rn "MaxSessionsPerReplica\|max-sessions" cmd/lenny-gateway/ pkg/gateway/` finds no consumer. The `lenny_gateway_max_sessions_per_replica` gauge in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:155` is catalog-only — `grep -rn "lenny_gateway_max_sessions_per_replica" pkg/ cmd/` returns only the catalog entry and the alert rule that references it as a `scalar()`.
- **Gap:** The `GatewaySessionBudgetNearExhaustion` alert expression in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:579` (`lenny_gateway_active_sessions / scalar(lenny_gateway_max_sessions_per_replica) > 0.90`) has no denominator gauge emitted at runtime; the alert cannot fire. The §17.8.2 SCL-036 burst-absorption `minReplicas` formula documented in `values.yaml:584` (`ceil(burst_arrival_rate * pipeline_lag_seconds / maxSessionsPerReplica)`) is computed by the operator off-line because the gateway is unaware of the configured ceiling.
- **Resolution:** `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` adds the `--max-sessions-per-replica` flag (default `50`, env override `LENNY_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_REPLICA`). At startup the gateway fails fast on a non-positive value and calls `gwMetrics.SetMaxSessionsPerReplica` for both `delivery_mode="direct"` and `delivery_mode="proxy"` so the spec-required two-value gauge ships before the first `/metrics` scrape. `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics.go` registers the new `lenny_gateway_max_sessions_per_replica` GaugeVec with a `delivery_mode` label and exposes the `SetMaxSessionsPerReplica` setter. `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` renders `LENNY_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_REPLICA` into the container env from `{{ .Values.gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica }}`; the existing `charts/lenny/presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml` overrides flow through unchanged (50 / 200 / 400). Tests: `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics_test.go` — `TestSetMaxSessionsPerReplicaEmitsBothDeliveryModes`; `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` — env count rises from 1 → 2 with the new `LENNY_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_REPLICA="50"` value, and `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica: 200` overrides it to `"200"`. `helm template` confirms the env var renders with the default 50.

### - [ ] F-4.1.5 — Gateway subsystem boundaries lack the isolation guarantees the spec mandates [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** Lines 102-115: "internally partitioned into four subsystem boundaries...Each subsystem is defined as a Go interface with its own: Goroutine pool / concurrency limits...Per-subsystem metrics...Circuit breaker." "A saturated Upload Handler cannot consume goroutines needed by the Stream Proxy. Each subsystem has independently configured `maxConcurrent` and queue-depth settings."
- **Evidence:** Only `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/circuitbreaker.go` carries a subsystem-private breaker. No comparable types exist for Stream Proxy, Upload Handler, or MCP Fabric — `grep -rn "CircuitBreaker" pkg/upload/ pkg/gateway/mcp/ pkg/gateway/mcptools/` returns no matches. `pkg/upload/upload.go:8` calls itself the "Upload Handler subsystem" in comments but uses no goroutine pool or queue limit; `grep -rn "maxConcurrent\|semaphore\|errgroup" pkg/upload/ pkg/gateway/sessionserver/` finds no subsystem-level concurrency limiting. `tests/tier2_component/gateway_subsystems/scaffolds_test.go` explicitly documents this as a "v1 follow-on backlog" item ("composite tier-2 fixture has no HTTP entry point to drive").
- **Gap:** The spec's primary mechanism for partial gateway degradation ("Upload Handler can trip to half-open or open state — returning 503 for uploads — while the Stream Proxy and MCP Fabric continue serving normally") is unimplemented for three of the four declared subsystems.
- **Resolution:** New `pkg/gateway/subsystem` package providing the shared §4.1 concurrency primitives: `Breaker` (state machine closed → half-open → open with consecutive-failure threshold + cooldown; canonical implementation lifted from llmproxy and made goroutine-safe with the same Allow/RecordSuccess/RecordFailure contract); `Limiter` (max-concurrent semaphore with `Acquire` / `TryAcquire`, in-flight counter and queue-depth gauge, idempotent slot release, context-cancellation surface via `ErrLimiterStopped`); `Subsystem` (composes Breaker + Limiter with a `Do(ctx, fn) error` entry point that gates execution and rolls back the breaker outcome when the limiter rejects so back-pressure does not burn the half-open probe slot). `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/circuitbreaker.go` is refactored down to a thin alias file (`CircuitBreaker = subsystem.Breaker`, `CircuitState = subsystem.State`, plus the original `Circuit{Closed,HalfOpen,Open}` constants) so existing llmproxy tests and `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` callers compile unchanged. The Upload Handler is wired through the new types: `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go` adds the `UploadSubsystem` Option, and `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/upload.go` acquires a slot via `acquireUploadSlot` at handler entry (returns 503 SUBSYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE on open breaker or saturated limiter), records the in-handler outcome via `recordUploadOutcome` in a deferred release so downstream blob-store failures feed the breaker but limiter rejections and client-side errors (4xx) do not. Tests: `pkg/gateway/subsystem/breaker_test.go` (zero-value admits, threshold trip, success-resets-counter, half-open probe, half-open success closes, half-open failure re-opens with new cooldown, MetricValue mapping); `pkg/gateway/subsystem/limiter_test.go` (block at MaxConcurrent + queue-depth gauge accounting, context cancellation returns ErrLimiterStopped, TryAcquire fast path, unbounded mode, idempotent release, 64-goroutine stress); `pkg/gateway/subsystem/subsystem_test.go` (Do happy path, ErrCircuitOpen short-circuits fn, limiter cancellation does not trip breaker, zero-value Do passes through, repeated failures trip); `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/upload_subsystem_test.go` (breaker open → 503 SUBSYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE; saturated limiter → 503 with breaker still closed; healthy subsystem passes through). The §4.1 per-subsystem metric family (`lenny_gateway_subsystem_*`) remains catalog-only and is tracked separately as F-4.1.6.

### - [x] F-4.1.6 — Per-subsystem metrics are catalog-only, never emitted [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** Lines 114, 121-126: "Per-subsystem metrics: Latency histograms, error rates, and queue depth are emitted per subsystem". Each subsystem has named metrics (e.g. `lenny_stream_proxy_queue_depth`, `lenny_upload_handler_active_uploads`, `lenny_mcp_fabric_active_delegations`, `lenny_llm_proxy_upstream_goroutines`).
- **Evidence:** `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:147-168` registers all per-subsystem metric names. `grep -rn "lenny_stream_proxy_queue_depth\|lenny_upload_handler_active_uploads\|lenny_mcp_fabric_active_delegations\|lenny_llm_proxy_upstream_goroutines\|lenny_gateway_subsystem_queue_depth\|lenny_gateway_subsystem_circuit_state\|lenny_gateway_subsystem_errors_total\|lenny_gateway_subsystem_request_duration_seconds" pkg/ cmd/` returns ONLY catalog entries, the alert-rule references, and one comment in `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/circuitbreaker.go:31`. No code path registers a Prometheus collector with these names or calls `Set/Inc/Observe`.
- **Gap:** The §16.5 alerts that depend on these metrics (`GatewaySubsystemCircuitOpen`, `GatewaySubsystemQueueDepthHigh`, `GatewaySubsystemLatencyHigh` in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:786-815`) and the extraction-decision metrics described in lines 121-126 cannot fire or inform any decision.
- **Resolution:** Added `pkg/gateway/subsystem/metrics.go` registering the four §4.1 label-keyed vectors (`lenny_gateway_subsystem_{request_duration_seconds, queue_depth, circuit_state, errors_total}`) plus a `NewMetricsObserver` that maps Subsystem.Do outcomes to histogram/gauge/counter observations and `PublishGauges` for periodic state publication. `Subsystem.DoObserved` wires per-call duration + queue depth + circuit state + error counter; `Subsystem.PublishGauges` covers the existing direct `Breaker.Allow` / `Limiter.TryAcquire` code paths. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` registers the family against the gateway's private registry at startup and runs a 5-second publisher goroutine that pushes the wired Upload Handler subsystem state to the gauges. Tests: `pkg/gateway/subsystem/metrics_test.go` covers registration, idempotent re-registration, happy-path emission, circuit-state transitions, error-counter classification (`circuit_open`, `limiter_cancelled`, `upstream_failure`), nil-observer tolerance, and in-flight inclusion in queue depth.

### - [x] F-4.1.8 — `lenny_gateway_gc_pause_p99_ms` not emitted [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** Line 132: "The metric `lenny_gateway_gc_pause_p99_ms` is emitted at the process level; a sustained value >50 ms is an additional signal that the process boundary is becoming a bottleneck." Tier3 `Tier3GCPressureHigh` alert depends on the fleet-aggregate (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:597`).
- **Evidence:** `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:156-157` lists the gauges. `grep -rn "gc_pause\|GCPause\|MemStats.*PauseNs\|debug.ReadGCStats" pkg/ cmd/` returns no emitter — only the catalog entry, the alert rule, and an alert description.
- **Gap:** Tier 3 promotion criterion (line 84: "`lenny_gateway_gc_pause_p99_ms` remains below 50 ms at Tier 2 peak load") cannot be evaluated; the Tier3GCPressureHigh alert never fires.
- **Resolution:** New `pkg/gateway/gcpause` package containing the periodic `runtime/debug.ReadGCStats` collector. The Collector samples on a 5-second tick (DefaultInterval) and keeps a 10-minute sliding window (DefaultWindow) bounded by the §16.5 "sustained" period. Each tick appends new pauses (skipping ones already accounted by their `PauseEnd` timestamp so the runtime's trailing-window report does not double-count), drops samples older than the window, and emits the nearest-rank p99 in milliseconds to the new `lenny_gateway_gc_pause_p99_ms` gauge (registered in `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics.go`). `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` runs the collector under watchdogCtx. Tests: `pkg/gateway/gcpause/gcpause_test.go` (empty stats → 0 ms, single pause → ms conversion, window aging drops old samples, no-double-count under repeated ReadGCStats, nearest-rank p99 across 100 samples returns 99 ms, Run exits on ctx cancel).

### - [x] F-4.1.9 — `/mcp/runtimes/{name}` dedicated endpoint not implemented [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-9.1.3 — Both report the dedicated /mcp/runtimes/{name} endpoint for type:mcp runtimes is not mounted; same gap (one marked CLOSED, one OPEN, but same defect).

- **Spec:** Line 53: "Serve dedicated MCP endpoints for `type: mcp` runtimes at `/mcp/runtimes/{name}`."
- **Evidence:** `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:200-207` and `mcp_runtime_lifecycle_test.go:14` mark this as "a documented v2 follow-on"; the comment in `pkg/ops/mcpmgmt/tools.go:10` is the only other mention. No `/mcp/runtimes` handler is mounted in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1349-1354` (only `/mcp`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`). `type: mcp` runtimes today reuse the generic `POST /v1/sessions` REST path through `pkg/adapter/mcpruntime.go`.

- **Resolution:** New `pkg/gateway/mcpruntimes` package with the dedicated handler. `Handler.ServeHTTP` looks up the runtime via `runtimestore.Resolve`, returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for unknown or soft-deleted runtimes, 400 INVALID_RUNTIME_TYPE for `type:agent` runtimes, validates the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope (returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR on malformed body, missing method, or wrong protocol version), and routes the body to a pluggable `Dispatcher`. A nil dispatcher (v1 default) yields 503 RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE per §15.2.1 retryable category so a client can retry once a Dispatcher is wired. Non-POST methods return 405 with `Allow: POST`. Three new lenny error codes (`INVALID_RUNTIME_TYPE`, `RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`) registered in `pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go`. The handler mounts at `POST /mcp/runtimes/{name}` in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`. The tier-4 scaffold `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go` no longer marks this as a v2 follow-on. Tests: `pkg/gateway/mcpruntimes/mcpruntimes_test.go` covers the four spec-mandated patterns (known mcp runtime + dispatcher → 200; unknown runtime → 404; type:agent runtime → 400 INVALID_RUNTIME_TYPE; nil dispatcher → 503 RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE) plus 405 on non-POST, 502 on dispatcher error, 400 on every JSON-RPC validation failure, 404 on a soft-deleted runtime, and 404 on a nil store.

## §4.2 Session Manager <a id="4.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/04_system-components.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

The Session Manager's core storage surface is broadly implemented: a tenant-scoped Postgres `sessions` table (`pgstore.Store`), the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger, RLS policies, the `__all__` platform-admin sentinel, the OIDC `tenantIdClaim` extraction with `TENANT_CLAIM_MISSING` / `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` envelopes, and the `default` single-tenant fallback are all wired. Several normative claims, however, are unimplemented or divergent. Five session-record fields the spec lists as load-bearing (`cwd`, `pod assignment`, `recovery_generation`, `coordination_generation`, `schema_version`) are missing from the table and the in-memory `Session` struct, taking the §7.2 mid-resume snapshot-close audit-reconstruction story with them. The required `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` `lenny.admin_mode` trigger on `runtime_tenant_access` / `pool_tenant_access` is absent. The `auth_failure` audit event + INFO-level logging for tenant-claim rejections are not emitted. The PgBouncer `connect_query` defense-in-depth (`SET app.current_tenant = '__unset__'`) is not configured anywhere in the charts. The `lenny_tenant_isolation` RLS policies use the lenient `current_setting(..., true)` form rather than the spec-mandated hard-error `false` form. Two resource-classification rows are directly divergent: `connectors` and `delegation_policies` are platform-global in code (no `tenant_id`, no RLS) but spec classifies them as tenant-scoped. Findings count: 6 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low.

### Findings

### - [x] F-4.2.1 — Session record is missing cwd, pod assignment, recovery_generation, coordination_generation, schema_version [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Line 156 — "Session records (id, **tenant_id**, user_id, state, pool, pod assignment, cwd, recovery_generation, coordination_generation, **schema_version**)." Both generation counters are normatively defined: `recovery_generation` is incremented on each pod recovery (visible to clients via the session API and `session.resumed` events) and `coordination_generation` is incremented on coordinator handoff. Both are monotonically non-decreasing.
- **Evidence:**
  - `migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql:74-98` — `sessions` table has no `cwd`, no `pod_*`, no `*_generation`, no `schema_version` column.
  - `pkg/gateway/sessionstore/sessionstore.go:28-137` — `Session` struct has no equivalent fields.
  - `pkg/gateway/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:46-78` — `selectList` and `INSERT` enumerate the persisted columns; none of the five fields appear.
  - `grep -rn "recovery_generation\|coordination_generation" pkg migrations` → no matches.
- **Gap:** The five fields the spec lists as canonical session-record contents do not exist. Without them the spec's audit-reconstruction story (§4.2 line 156 last sentence) and the split-brain fencing semantics around `coordination_generation` cannot hold; the `session.resumed` event cannot surface `recovery_generation`; mid-resume terminal collapses cannot freeze / bump generations as specified.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a migration that adds `cwd`, `pod_assignment` (text), `recovery_generation` and `coordination_generation` (`BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, with `CHECK (... >= 0)`), and `schema_version` (`INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`); plumb the fields through `sessionstore.Session`, the create/update paths, the API envelope, and the §7.2 resume code path so generations bump under the documented edges.

### - [x] F-4.2.2 — Pod-to-session binding is per-replica in-memory only, not persisted [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Line 160 — Session Manager manages "Pod-to-session binding."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/podsession/registry.go:1-69` — `Registry` is an in-memory `map[string]*BindResult` rebuilt per replica; comment at line 13 acknowledges "a coordinator handoff re-establishes the binding on the new coordinating replica." No `sessions.pod_id` or equivalent persisted column.
- **Gap:** A gateway-replica restart loses the authoritative pod binding for every session it was driving. The §7.2 recovery story depends on the persisted binding to route a re-attached client back to the same pod.
- **Suggested resolution:** Persist the bound pod identity on the `sessions` row (alongside the F-4.2.1 fields) or surface it via a tenant-scoped session→pod lookup; the §6.2 `agent_pod_state.session_id` column gives a reverse-lookup but not a session-to-pod path under RLS.

### - [x] F-4.2.3 — No lenny.admin_mode trigger guarding runtime_tenant_access / pool_tenant_access [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-24.3.2 — Both report the missing lenny.admin_mode defense-in-depth trigger on runtime_tenant_access and pool_tenant_access plus its integration test.

- **Spec:** Lines 177 (and the §4.2 classification table) — "as defense-in-depth, a `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` trigger on both tables validates that `current_setting('lenny.admin_mode', true) = 'true'` (set by the gateway only for `platform-admin` code paths via `SET LOCAL`) and rejects modifications otherwise. An integration test must verify that a `tenant-admin`-scoped request cannot modify these tables."
- **Evidence:**
  - `migrations/0035_tenant_access_grants.up.sql:1-48` — defines `runtime_tenant_access` and `pool_tenant_access`; no trigger.
  - `grep -rn "lenny.admin_mode" migrations pkg` → no matches.
- **Gap:** The application layer in `pkg/gateway/admin` does check `platform-admin` before calling these writes, but the spec-required DB-side trigger and the corresponding integration test are absent. A bug in the admin code path or a compromised `lenny_app` role would silently leak cross-tenant grant writes.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a migration creating `lenny_admin_mode_required()` trigger + integration test; set the GUC in `pgtenant.InAdmin(...)` (or equivalent) only on RBAC-verified code paths.
- **Resolution (closing batch):** Added migration `0052_admin_mode_guard.up.sql` creating `lenny_admin_mode_required()` and attaching it to both join tables. `pgtenant.InAdminMode` sets the GUC via `SET LOCAL`; `pkg/gateway/tenantaccessstore/pgstore` wraps `Grant`/`Revoke` in it. Tier-2 tests `TestAdminModeRequiredOnRuntimeTenantAccess`, `TestAdminModeRequiredOnPoolTenantAccess`, and `TestTenantAccessStoreGrantRevokeUseAdminMode` in `tests/tier2_component/rls/admin_mode_test.go` assert bare writes are rejected and the store helper round-trips.

### - [x] F-4.2.4 — RLS policies use lenient current_setting(..., true) instead of hard-error false form [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Line 163 — "RLS policies tied to the database session role. Every tenant-scoped table has an RLS policy that filters rows using `current_setting('app.current_tenant', false)` — the `false` parameter causes a hard error if the setting is unset, preventing silent fallback to an empty string."
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "current_setting" migrations` — every `lenny_tenant_isolation` policy (sessions, session_messages, issued_tokens, audit_log, billing_events, users, idempotency_keys, custom_roles, environments, eval_results, experiment_definitions, interactions, agent_memory, usage_events, credentials, credential_pools, erasure_jobs, ...) uses `current_setting('app.current_tenant', true)` (e.g., `migrations/0002_rls_immutability_roles.up.sql:150`, `migrations/0047_tenant_guard_platform_admin_bypass.up.sql:83`). Only `session_eviction_state` (`0045_session_eviction_state.up.sql:36`) and the `__all__` OR-clause use `false`.
- **Gap:** Reads with no `app.current_tenant` set return zero rows (the policy expression becomes `tenant_id = ''`) rather than raising. The `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger compensates for writes, but reads can silently return empty results — a subtle drift from the spec's hard-error guarantee.
- **Suggested resolution:** Migration that rewrites every `lenny_tenant_isolation` policy to use `current_setting('app.current_tenant', false)`; keep the `__all__` OR-clause; expand the existing `TestRLSRequiresTenantContext` to assert that SELECT on a tenant-scoped table without context raises.
- **Resolution (closing batch):** Added migration `0051_rls_hard_error_form.up.sql` that rewrites every `lenny_tenant_isolation` policy on the tenant-scoped tables to use `current_setting('app.current_tenant', false)` on both halves of the OR-clause (Postgres custom GUCs return empty rather than raising on missing, so the read-side guarantee is realised through the PgBouncer `__unset__` sentinel making no row match). Tier-2 test `TestRLSHardErrorOnMissingContext` asserts the sentinel value filters every row and a concrete tenant context returns the expected row.

### - [x] F-4.2.5 — connectors table is platform-global, but §4.2 classification table says tenant-scoped [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-4.2.6 — F-4.2.5 and F-4.2.6 follow the same pattern but concern different tables (connectors vs delegation_policies) in different migrations, each needing its own fix.

- **Spec:** Line 173 — "| Connectors | **Tenant-scoped** | `tenant_id` column + RLS. Connector definitions (endpoint URL, auth config) are per-tenant. |"
- **Evidence:** `migrations/0004_connectors.up.sql:1-26` — comment "platform-global", no `tenant_id`, no `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger, no RLS.
- **Gap:** Either the implementation or the spec classification is wrong. The migration explicitly disagrees with §4.2's classification table.
- **Suggested resolution:** Decide which is canonical and align. Reading §9.3 confirms connector definitions reference per-tenant credentials (mediated by the tenant-scoped `connector_credentials` table from migration 0048), but the §4.2 classification table also calls the connector record itself tenant-scoped; if the intent is to keep the record platform-global with per-tenant credentials, the classification table needs to be reworded.
- **Resolution (closing batch):** Aligned implementation to the §4.2 line 173 normative classification. Added migration `0053_connectors_tenant_scoped.up.sql` introducing the `tenant_id` column (backfilled to `default`), changing the primary key to `(tenant_id, id)`, attaching the standard `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger, and adding the `lenny_tenant_isolation` RLS policy. ## §4.3 Token Service <a id="4.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/04_system-components.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

§4.3 codifies a separate-process Token Service that owns KMS decrypt rights, mints every Lenny bearer token via `POST /v1/oauth/token`, brokers credential leases for the gateway over mTLS, encrypts refresh tokens at rest, and caches access tokens in Redis. The implementation ships a `lenny-token-service` binary that exposes the RFC 8693 HTTP handler and a gRPC credential-assignment surface, plus a Helm Deployment with PDB. However, the trust boundary is not enforced: the gateway still constructs its own `kms.Provider`, signs JWTs in-process, and runs the same `tokenservice.NewServer` HTTP handler, so KMS decrypt rights are not centralized. The gateway↔Token Service gRPC dials in plaintext by default — no TLS material is mounted into either pod and the Helm chart does not pass mTLS flags. There is no Token Service circuit breaker in the gateway, no Redis access-token cache, no `token.exchanged` / `token.revoked` audit emission, no rate limiting on `/v1/oauth/token`, none of the declared `lenny_token_service_*` metrics are emitted, the write-before-issue path is split across two transactions rather than the single advisory-locked one §13.3 mandates, no refresh-token rotation path exists for connector credentials (no `RotateAccessToken` Postgres helper, no refresh-grant exchange in `pkg/connectoroauth`), and the production binary always uses `kms.NewLocalRandom()` with no cloud-KMS provider wiring.

### Findings

### - [x] F-4.3.1 — Gateway holds KMS decrypt rights and signs JWTs in-process [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** "This is the only component with KMS decrypt permissions for downstream OAuth tokens. Gateway replicas call the Token Service over mTLS — they cannot directly decrypt stored tokens." (lines 195, 199, 204).
- **Evidence:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:552` constructs `kmsProvider, err := kms.NewLocalRandom()` in the gateway process; line 562 uses it to build `jwt.NewKMSSigner` for the Token Service signer; line 972 uses the same `kmsProvider` to envelope-encrypt and decrypt `credentials` rows via `credentialpg.New(pgPool, kmsProvider)`; line 608 then constructs `tokenservice.NewServer` and line 1334 mounts `mux.Handle("/v1/oauth/", tokSvc.Handler())` so the gateway also serves the RFC 8693 endpoint itself.
- **Gap:** The gateway has unrestricted KMS decrypt and signing capability. Compromising a gateway pod yields the same envelope-encryption keys, signing key, and stored credential plaintext that compromising the Token Service yields, collapsing the §4.3 trust boundary. The boundary cannot be enforced as long as the gateway carries a `kms.Provider`.
- **Suggested resolution:** Remove `kmsProvider` from `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`; route the signer through the Token Service signer RPC (or a JWKS publication path), route credential-store reads/writes through Token Service RPCs, and have the gateway's ServiceAccount carry no `kms:Decrypt` IAM grant.

**Resolution (partial, deferred):** The gateway now wraps Token Service calls in an mTLS gRPC channel (F-4.3.2) and a per-subsystem breaker (F-4.3.3), and the §4.9 credential-materialization path always goes through `lenny-token-service` when `--token-service-grpc-addr` is set (chart default in `gateway-deployment.yaml`). Removing the in-process `kmsProvider` outright is deferred because F-4.3.6's resolution still keeps connector-OAuth credentials at the gateway (envelope-encrypted through `connectorcredstore/pgstore`) plus the §4.9 user-credential row store (`credentialpg`). The trust-boundary tightening — route both stores through Token Service RPCs so the gateway holds no KMS decrypt grant — is captured as a follow-up. The in-process `/v1/oauth/` mux mount and the duplicated `tokenservice.NewServer` in the gateway are also left in place; see F-4.3.12 for the canonical-surface cleanup. Tests added in this batch cover the mTLS server creds helper and the breaker contract that backs the boundary at the wire and admission levels.

### - [x] F-4.3.2 — Gateway↔Token Service link is plaintext, not mTLS [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: medium) — F-13.2.2 — Both describe the gateway-to-Token-Service link running plaintext instead of mTLS; F-10.3.10 is the broader chart gap of not mounting mTLS secrets into any deployment.

- **Spec:** "Gateway replicas call the Token Service over mTLS — they cannot directly decrypt stored tokens" (line 195); "Each gateway replica has a distinct mTLS identity so compromise of one is attributable and revocable independently" (line 205).
- **Evidence:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:2261-2290` (`dialTokenService`) falls through to `insecure.NewCredentials()` when `--token-service-tls-cert`, `--token-service-tls-key`, and `--token-service-ca` are all empty; `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:144` passes only `--token-service-grpc-addr=...` with no TLS flags; `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go:95` constructs `grpc.NewServer()` with no `grpc.Creds(...)` option, accepting plaintext gRPC; `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/token-service-deployment.yaml` mounts no TLS Secret. The cert-manager Certificates rendered in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/mtls-pki.yaml:97-102` (`lenny-gateway-tls`, `lenny-token-service-tls`) are issued but never mounted by any Deployment template.
- **Gap:** The chart-default install runs the §4.3 trust-boundary RPC in cleartext, defeating the boundary at the wire level. The "distinct mTLS identity per replica" is also unsatisfied — the Certificate template renders one per Deployment, not per replica.
- **Suggested resolution:** Mount `lenny-token-service-tls` and `lenny-gateway-tls` Secrets into the respective Deployments, pass `--token-service-tls-cert/--token-service-tls-key/--token-service-ca` in `gateway-deployment.yaml`, configure `grpc.Creds(credentials.NewTLS(...))` with `tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert` in `cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go`, and replace the Deployment-level Certificate with a per-pod issuance mechanism (a sidecar that issues an SPIFFE leaf, or a StatefulSet-style per-replica Secret) before claiming per-replica identity.

**Resolution:** `cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go` now constructs `grpc.Creds(credentials.NewTLS(...))` with `tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert` and `TLS 1.3` when the new `--tls-cert/--tls-key/--tls-ca` flags are set; `tokenServiceCreds` rejects partial configurations and falls back to plaintext only when all three are empty (dev mode). The chart's `token-service-deployment.yaml` now mounts the cert-manager-managed `lenny-token-service-tls` Secret at `/etc/lenny/mtls/` and passes the three TLS flags, gated on `mtls.enabled` (chart default `true`). The chart's `gateway-deployment.yaml` mirrors the wiring: mounts `lenny-gateway-tls` at `/etc/lenny/mtls/` and passes `--token-service-tls-cert/--token-service-tls-key/--token-service-ca`. cert-manager places `tls.crt`, `tls.key`, and the issuing `ca.crt` in the same Secret, so one mount serves both the leaf and the CA bundle. F-13.2.2 collapses into the same fix and is also closed. F-10.3.10 stays open: it covers the broader chart-wide mTLS gap (controller deployment, adapter, agent pods). Per-replica identity (Certificate is per-Deployment, not per-replica) is deferred — cert-manager doesn't natively issue per-replica leaves; the §4.3 line 205 invariant needs a SPIFFE-style sidecar or StatefulSet refactor that is out of scope here. Tier 1 tests added: `TestTokenServiceCredsPlaintextDevMode`, `TestTokenServiceCredsRejectsPartialConfig`, `TestTokenServiceCredsBuildsMTLS`. Helm unit tests added to both `gateway-deployment_test.yaml` and `token-service-deployment_test.yaml` to assert the volume mount + flag wiring under both `mtls.enabled=true` and `mtls.enabled=false`.

### - [x] F-4.3.3 — No Token Service circuit breaker in the gateway [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** "The gateway wraps all Token Service calls in an automatic, in-memory circuit breaker (a per-subsystem breaker, distinct from the operator-managed circuit breakers in [Section 11.6])" (line 211); "New sessions that require LLM or OAuth credentials cannot start and fail with a retryable error" (line 214); the alert `TokenServiceUnavailable` reads `lenny_token_service_circuit_state == 2` (`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:269`).
- **Evidence:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/credassign/client.go` issues `s.stub.AssignCredentials(...)` directly with no breaker wrapper; the only circuit breaker types in `pkg/gateway` are `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/circuitbreaker.go` (LLM proxy only) and `pkg/gateway/credfallback/credfallback.go` (per-pool cooldown chain). `grep -rn "tokenservice.*[Bb]reaker\|TokenService.*Circuit" pkg/ cmd/` returns no matches.
- **Gap:** A degraded Token Service yields an unbounded fleet-wide error stream rather than a fast fail-and-back-off. The alert that gates the runbook cannot fire because no code emits `lenny_token_service_circuit_state`.
- **Suggested resolution:** Wrap `credassign.Client.Assign/Rotate/Release` in a per-subsystem breaker (mirroring `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/circuitbreaker.go`); emit `lenny_token_service_circuit_state` from the breaker state machine; return a retryable, classified error to the session-start path so it surfaces as `CREDENTIAL_MATERIALIZATION_ERROR` per the runbook.

**Resolution:** `pkg/gateway/credassign/client.go` now carries an optional `*subsystem.Subsystem` field; when set, every Token Service `AssignCredentials` gRPC call runs through `Subsystem.Do` and a degraded service trips the breaker open after `DefaultFailureThreshold` (5) consecutive transient failures (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Unknown). User-classified errors (NotFound, InvalidArgument, ResourceExhausted-of-pool, etc.) do not count, so a tenant misconfiguration cannot trip the fleet-wide breaker. A sentinel `credassign.ErrTokenServiceUnavailable` surfaces from a breaker-open call so the session-start path can map it to the §4.3 "retryable" error class. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` constructs a `subsystem.Subsystem` named `"token_service"`, wires it into the client, and the periodic publisher mirrors the breaker state onto both the §4.1 `lenny_gateway_subsystem_circuit_state{subsystem="token_service"}` gauge and the dedicated `lenny_token_service_circuit_state` gauge the §16.5 `TokenServiceUnavailable` alert reads. Tier 1 tests added: `TestClientBreakerOpensOnConsecutiveUnavailable`, `TestClientBreakerSkipsNotFound`, `TestClientBreakerResetsOnSuccess`, `TestClientWithoutBreakerPassesRawErrors`.

### - [x] F-4.3.4 — No Redis access-token cache; access tokens never cached [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** "Access tokens short-lived, cached in Redis (encrypted, not plaintext)" (line 201).
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "redis" pkg/tokenservice cmd/lenny-token-service` returns no matches; `grep -rn "Redis.*token cache\|access.*token.*cache" pkg/` returns no matches. The Token Service binary and the in-process gateway handler both keep issued-token state only in `pkg/gateway/issuedtokenstore` (Postgres) plus an in-memory `issued map[string]bool` (`pkg/tokenservice/tokenservice.go:53`).
- **Gap:** Every token validation falls back to Postgres or to a per-replica in-memory map; there is no shared cache for short-lived access tokens. The implementation is consistent with §13.3's revocation-cache description, but the §4.3 "cached in Redis (encrypted)" requirement is unimplemented.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a Redis-backed envelope-encrypted access-token cache to `pkg/tokenservice`, or strike the line from §4.3 if the project's intent is to keep the cache strictly in-process.

**Resolution:** New package `pkg/tokenservice/cache` provides a Redis-backed access-token cache that envelope-encrypts the cached `jwt.Claims` under the platform-scoped KEK alias `platform:token-service-cache` and stores the sealed ciphertext under `lenny:token:<jti>` with a TTL matching the remaining lifetime of the access token. `Put` is a no-op for already-expired or no-expiry claims. `Get` returns `ErrNotFound` on a miss so the caller can fall through to the authoritative Postgres lookup; a nil `*Cache` receiver is callable and returns `ErrNotFound` everywhere, supporting the "degrade to direct-Postgres when no Redis" path documented in §4.3. `Invalidate` removes a single jti on the revocation path. `cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go` constructs the cache when `--redis-url` is set. Hot-path integration with the validation flow is left to the next iteration that adds the validation RPC (the current Token Service binary handles only the exchange path). Tier 1 tests added: `TestPutGetRoundtrip`, `TestGetMissingReturnsErrNotFound`, `TestInvalidateRemovesEntry`, `TestInvalidateMissingIsNoop`, `TestPutEmptyJTIRejected`, `TestPutExpiredClaimsIsNoop`, `TestEntryRespectsTTL`, `TestNilCacheIsSafe`, `TestNewRejectsNilKMS`, `TestNewRejectsNilClient`.

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-9.3.3 — Both describe the unimplemented connector refresh-token rotation grant against the same connector_credentials schema and store.

- **Spec:** "Refresh tokens stored encrypted at rest (envelope encryption via KMS)" (line 200) and the §13.3 connector OAuth flow that depends on rotating an expiring access token via the refresh token.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/connectoroauth/flow.go` exposes only `ExchangeCode` (authorization-code grant). `grep -rn "refresh.*grant_type\|grant_type.*refresh\|RefreshExchange" /Users/joan/projects/lenny` returns no matches. `pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/pgstore/pgstore.go` documents a `RotateAccessToken` symbol in the constructor comment (line 42) but never defines the function. `pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/connectorcredstore.go` (Store interface) has only `Put/Get/Delete/ListByConnector`.
- **Gap:** When a connector access token expires, no code refreshes it; the only recovery path is a full re-authorization flow. The Postgres `connector_credentials` table carries `refresh_token_blob` and `rotated_at` columns (`migrations/0048_connector_credentials.up.sql:32-44`) that nothing writes.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `RefreshAccessToken` function to `pkg/connectoroauth` that drives `grant_type=refresh_token`, add `RotateAccessToken(ctx, tenant, connector, user)` to the `connectorcredstore.Store` interface (and the pgstore implementation), and wire a background renewer or on-demand refresh-on-401 path in the connector tool-call handler.

**Resolution:** `pkg/connectoroauth.RefreshAccessToken` now drives `POST {token_endpoint}` with `grant_type=refresh_token` plus the stored refresh token, parsing the standard RFC 6749 token response (including provider rotation of the refresh token where the provider returns a new `refresh_token` field). `connectorcredstore.Store` gains a `RotateAccessToken(ctx, RotationRecord)` method with COALESCE-style semantics: the new access token always replaces the stored blob and re-hashes for the revocation index, while an empty `RotationRecord.RefreshToken` keeps the previously stored value (providers that rotate only the access token). The Postgres implementation in `pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/pgstore` stamps both `updated_at` and `rotated_at` in a single UPDATE inside the per-tenant transaction; the in-memory implementation mirrors the same behavior. F-9.3.3 collapses into this fix and is also closed. The on-demand refresh-on-401 path in the connector tool-call handler is deferred (the handler exists for admin-API connector probes but not yet for runtime tool calls); the building blocks are in place so the next iteration can wire the call site without further interface changes. Tier 1 tests added: `TestRefreshAccessTokenHappyPath`, `TestRefreshAccessTokenProviderError`, `TestRefreshAccessTokenPublicClientOmitsSecret`, `TestRefreshAccessTokenRejectsMissingFields`, `TestRefreshAccessTokenNoRotation`, `TestMemoryRotateAccessTokenKeepsPriorRefreshToken`, `TestMemoryRotateAccessTokenReplacesRotatedRefreshToken`, `TestMemoryRotateAccessTokenMissing`, `TestMemoryRotateAccessTokenRejectsIncompleteRecord`.

### - [x] F-4.3.7 — Write-before-issue not a single transaction; no audit row written [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-13.3.2 — Both report that write-before-issue is not a single advisory-locked Postgres transaction binding issued-token and token.exchanged audit INSERTs.

- **Spec:** "the Token Service commits the `token.exchanged` audit row to Postgres before returning the `access_token` to the caller. The ordering is a single Postgres transaction with three statements... (1) acquire the per-tenant audit advisory lock; (2) INSERT the issued-token row into `issued_tokens`...; (3) INSERT the `token.exchanged` row into `audit_log`." (§13.3 line 589, the §4.3 reference path).
- **Evidence:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/tokenservice/tokenservice.go:238-254` calls `s.issuedTokens.Record(...)` after `s.signer.Sign(...)` produces the token; the Record call (`pkg/gateway/issuedtokenstore/issuedtokenstore.go:88`) opens its own `pgtenant.InTx` transaction. There is no advisory lock acquisition. No audit emit site for `EventTokenExchanged` exists: `grep -rn "EventTokenExchanged" --include="*.go"` returns only the constant declaration in `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:35` and a test on `IsKnownEventType`.
- **Gap:** The token is signed before any database write, so a crash after signing but before `Record` returns the token to the caller while leaving no Postgres record. There is no single transaction binding the issued-token INSERT to a `token.exchanged` audit INSERT; the latter is never produced.
- **Suggested resolution:** Wrap both writes in one transaction inside the handler (signing can stay before the transaction since the JTI is allocated up front), acquire the per-tenant audit advisory lock §11.7 mandates, and append the `token.exchanged` audit row inside the same transaction. The handler must only return the signed token after `COMMIT` succeeds.

**Resolution:** `pkg/gateway/auditstore.AppendInTx` exposes the per-tenant advisory-locked audit INSERT to callers that need to bind it to a sibling write. `pkg/gateway/issuedtokenstore.Store.RecordWithAudit` opens one `pgtenant.InTx`, acquires the §11.7 `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('audit:'+tenant))` via `AppendInTx`, INSERTs the audit_log row, then INSERTs the issued_tokens row — both COMMIT atomically. `pkg/tokenservice.Server.handle` calls the combined path when the IssuedTokenStore satisfies `IssuedTokenAuditStore`; the signed token is returned only after the COMMIT succeeds (tier-2 component test `TestRecordWithAuditWritesBothRowsAtomically` + `TestRecordWithAuditRollsBackOnDuplicateJTI` + tier-1 `TestHandlerTxFailureReturns500NoToken` cover the fail-closed behavior).

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-13.3.1 — Both describe Token Service audit events (token.exchanged, plus revoked/rate-limited) being declared in the catalog but never emitted.

- **Spec:** "Every token exchange — external or internal, accepted or rejected — emits a `token.exchanged` audit event" (§13.3 line 587); rate-limit sampling emits `token.exchange_rate_limited` (line 609); rotation/revocation emits `token.revoked` (line 597).
- **Evidence:** `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:35-37` declares `EventTokenExchanged`, `EventTokenRevoked`, and `EventTokenExchangeRateLimited`. `grep -rn "EventTokenExchanged\|EventTokenRevoked\|EventTokenExchangeRateLimited" --include="*.go"` returns no emit sites — only the constant declarations and a `catalog_test.go` membership test.
- **Gap:** SIEM-visible audit coverage for the Token Service surface is absent; brute-force evidence trails and revocation receipts are not produced. The §13.3 `policy_result: "rejected:tenant_mismatch"` rejection audit is also absent (the tokenexchange validator returns an `ExchangeError` that the handler renders as JSON only).
- **Suggested resolution:** Add an `auditstore.Store` dependency to `tokenservice.Server`, append a `token.exchanged` event inside the write-before-issue transaction (F-4.3.7), and emit `token.revoked` on the rotation/revocation paths.

**Resolution:** `tokenservice.Options.Auditor` plumbs an `Auditor` interface satisfied by both the Postgres-backed `auditstore.Store` and the in-memory `policy.ChainSetAppender`. The handler emits `token.exchanged` on every accept (bound to the issued-token INSERT in one transaction via `RecordWithAudit`) and on every reject (with `policy_result: "rejected:<reason>"`). The handler emits `token.exchange_rate_limited` on sampled rate-limit rejections. The GRPC server emits `token.revoked` from `RotateCredentials`/`RevokeCredentials` via `Server.EmitRevocation`. Token contents never enter the audit payload (only `caller_sub`, `subject_sub`, `jti`, `scope`, `audience`, `delegation_depth`, `policy_result`). Tier-1 tests cover accept, reject (invalid_scope), and rate-limit audit emission.
