## §4.6 Pod Lifecycle Controllers <a id="4.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/04_system-components.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

Lenny implements the two-controller split (WarmPoolController, PoolScalingController) and the §4.6.3 ownership matrix at a strong baseline level: lenny.dev/v1 CRDs (`Sandbox`, `SandboxClaim`, `SandboxTemplate`, `SandboxWarmPool`) are defined under the spec-mandated API group, the warm-pool reconciler converges minWarm/maxWarm with a pure planner, the Sandbox-to-Pod reconciler advances the §6.2 warm-path lifecycle with SSA writes under the right field manager, the §4.6.1 `lenny-sandboxclaim-guard` admission webhook and §4.6.3 `lenny-pool-config-validator` webhook are implemented with the spec's CREATE/UPDATE rules and HTTP codes, the SDK-warm circuit breaker with the §6.1 persisted carve-out is implemented end-to-end, the §4.6.2 default scaling formula (standard / variant / base-pool-adjusted) is implemented, the Postgres-backed fallback claim path with the `agent_pod_state` mirror and mirror-lag gating is wired into the gateway binder, ADR-007 is recorded, and tier-8 chaos tests exercise leader-election failover plus the double-claim guard. A significant set of normative requirements is missing or partial: the PoolScalingController is implemented but is not actually wired into `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go`, so the spec-mandated derived-state reconciliation from Postgres into CRDs never runs in the binary; the `lenny-pool-config-validator` does not implement the rule-set-2 userInfo-based authorization path; the `admissionDeniedRetryCeiling` default and the per-(pool, crd, reason) labelling differ from spec; the PSC's per-tuple exponential backoff (1s→60s) and the `resume-reconciliation` admin API are absent; the §4.6.1 orphaned-SandboxClaim garbage-collection loop, the per-`SandboxTemplate` PDB management, the `lenny.dev/host-schedulable` labeller, the `lenny.dev/session-cleanup` finalizer, the cert-expiry replacement, the WarmPoolController mirror reconciliation on leader-election acquisition, the Pod preStop hook + 120s grace period, the controller dual rate-limiter (`--create-qps`/`--status-qps`/etc.), the `--initial-fill-grace-period`, the `lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds` and `lenny_controller_leader_lease_renewal_age_seconds` gauges, and the spec's `PodLifecycleManager` / `PoolManager` / `PoolReader` interface abstraction are not implemented; `SandboxClaim.status.phase` is missing the `active` value the §4.6.3 enumeration lists; the Sandbox guard `PoolType` enum has only `warning` instead of the host-schedulable label; the §15.1 admin pool API lacks the spec-mandated `syncStatus` field and `/sync-status` endpoint; the controller-rbac chart misses spec-required verbs (`delete` on `Sandbox`, `list`/`delete` on `SandboxClaim`, `create`/`update`/`delete` on `PodDisruptionBudget`), and the gateway RBAC lacks the spec-required `patch` verb on `Pods` for tenant-id label mutations.

### Findings

### - [x] F-4.6.1 — PoolScalingController implemented but not wired into the controller binary [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.1.6, F-5.2.11 — All three describe the implemented PoolScalingController not being wired into the production controller binary.

- **Spec:** §4.6.2 — "Reconcile pool configuration from Postgres (admin API source of truth) into `SandboxTemplate` and `SandboxWarmPool` CRDs"; "The PoolScalingController runs its own Lease-based leader election using a separate lease name (`lenny-pool-scaling-controller`)". The controller is normative.
- **Evidence:** `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:81-194` constructs the manager, wires `warmpool.Reconciler`, the `sandbox.Reconciler`, and the `cidrdrift.Detector` only. No reference to `pkg/controller/poolscaling` anywhere under `cmd/`; `grep` of `cmd/` returns no `poolscaling` import outside the unrelated `cmd/lenny-test/tiers.go:142` documentation row. The `LeaderElectionID` set to `lenny-warm-pool-controller` (line 120) is the only lease; no second lease for `lenny-pool-scaling-controller`. The Helm chart's `controller-rbac.yaml` has no PSC ServiceAccount; `grep -rn "lenny-pool-scaling-controller\b" charts/` returns no result.
- **Gap:** The PoolScalingController's `Reconciler`, `Runnable`, admission-retry tracker, circuit-breaker evaluator, and variant-roles resolver are fully implemented in `pkg/controller/poolscaling/` and have unit tests, but the production binary never starts the PSC. Consequently `SandboxTemplate.spec.*` and `SandboxWarmPool.spec.{minWarm,maxWarm,scalePolicy,sdkWarmDisabled}` and the `status.sdkWarmCircuitBreaker.*` carve-out are not actually reconciled from Postgres — pools created via the admin API exist only as Postgres rows, with no Kubernetes-side derived state, so the WarmPoolController has nothing to reconcile against. The §4.6.2 leader-election lease (`lenny-pool-scaling-controller`) is never created. The §4.6.3 `lenny-pool-config-validator`'s rule-set-2 authorization "PoolScalingController SA" never appears in any request because there is no such SA.
- **Suggested resolution:** Wire a second `poolscaling.Runnable` into `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` (or a dedicated `cmd/lenny-pool-scaling-controller/main.go` with its own deployment), constructing the `PoolConfigSource` against Postgres, the `DemandSource` against Prometheus, and the `DemotionRateSource` against the in-memory rolling window. Add a separate ctrl-runtime Manager (or use a second `manager.LeaderElectionRunnable` with `LeaderElectionID: lenny-pool-scaling-controller`). Create the PSC ServiceAccount in `charts/lenny/templates/controller-rbac.yaml` with the §4.6.3 RBAC grants (`create`/`update`/`delete` on `SandboxTemplate` and `SandboxWarmPool`, `get`/`patch` on the `status` subresource of `SandboxWarmPool` for the carve-out, `get`/`create`/`update` on `Leases` in `lenny-system`). Add the PSC Deployment to the Helm chart.
- **Resolution:** Added a Postgres-backed `poolscaling.PoolStoreSource` mapping each active §5.2 pool row into a §4.6.2 `PoolConfig` (full SandboxTemplate spec; bootstrap `minWarm`/`maxWarm` = `warmCount`), a dedicated `cmd/lenny-pool-scaling-controller` binary running `poolscaling.Runnable` on its own ctrl-runtime Manager with `LeaderElectionID: lenny-pool-scaling-controller`, and the Helm `lenny-pool-scaling-controller` ServiceAccount + ClusterRole (§4.6.3 grants on the CRD pair and the `sandboxwarmpools/status` carve-out) + leader-election Role + Deployment (renders only when `postgres.dsn` is set; runs under the PSC identity so its derived-spec writes pass the rule-set-2 authz check). v1 runs every pool in §4.6.2 bootstrap mode (no DemandSource). Commit 627d3cc6.

### - [x] F-4.6.2 — `lenny-pool-config-validator` does not enforce rule-set-2 userInfo authorization [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.2.10 — Both describe the pool-config-validator not applying the §4.6.3 userInfo authorization-denial rule on manual writes.

- **Spec:** §4.6.3 "Validating webhook for Postgres-authoritative state" — "manual `kubectl edit` or `kubectl apply` updates to these fields are rejected UNLESS the request's `userInfo` maps to the PoolScalingController ServiceAccount (`system:serviceaccount:lenny-system:lenny-pool-scaling-controller`)". Quote: "PoolScalingController writes bypass only this second rule, not the first."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go` (full file) implements only the rule-set-1 semantic/budget invariants (minWarm/maxWarm, schedule windows, execution-mode acknowledgments). `grep -n "userInfo\|kubectl edit\|kubectl apply\|PoolScalingControllerSA" pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/` returns nothing. The webhook handler `pkg/admission/webhook/pool_config_validator.go` (per `cmd/lenny-webhook/main.go:84`) wraps this pure logic and inherits the same omission.
- **Gap:** Any tenant or platform admin with `patch`/`update` RBAC on `SandboxTemplate.spec` or `SandboxWarmPool.spec` can manually edit those resources — their writes will be silently overwritten on the next PSC reconcile, but the spec mandates rejection at admission with a directive to use the admin API. This is the §4.6.3 defense-in-depth path that distinguishes "writes that must be ignored by PSC's overwrite-on-reconcile" from "writes that should never be admitted in the first place".
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a rule-set-2 evaluator to `pool_config_validator.Decide` that takes the AdmissionRequest's `UserInfo.Username`, compares against the constant `PoolScalingControllerSA` (already defined in `pkg/admission/label_immutability/label_immutability.go:58`), and rejects any spec write that does not come from the PSC SA. Propagate the `UserInfo.Username` through the webhook adapter in `pkg/admission/webhook/pool_config_validator.go`. Add a test covering kubectl-style writes by other principals.
- **Resolution:** Added `pcv.DecideAuthorization(username)` implementing rule set 2 (reusing `label_immutability.PoolScalingControllerSA`); rejects non-PSC writers with HTTP 403 `UNAUTHORIZED_POOL_CONFIG_WRITE` directing them to the admin API. The webhook adapter now runs rule set 1 first and rule set 2 (against `req.UserInfo.Username`) only on admit. Commit 9d100e44.

### - [x] F-4.6.3 — No orphaned-SandboxClaim garbage-collection loop [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-6.2.23 — Both report the absent orphaned-SandboxClaim garbage-collection loop, with lenny_orphaned_claims_total declared but never emitted.

- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Orphaned `SandboxClaim` detection" — every 60s the WarmPoolController leader lists all `SandboxClaim` resources older than `claimOrphanTimeout` (default 5 minutes, configurable via `--claim-orphan-timeout`), queries Postgres for an active session, deletes the claim if no session references it, and transitions the underlying `Sandbox` back to `idle`. Increments `lenny_orphaned_claims_total{pool}`.
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "GarbageCollect\b\|claim-orphan-timeout\|claimOrphanTimeout" pkg/` returns no implementation. The metric `lenny_orphaned_claims_total` exists in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:192` and the `SandboxClaimOrphanRateHigh` alert in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1138` references it, but no code path emits it. `pkg/controller/warmpool/controller.go:99-159` Reconcile only handles per-pool sizing and never lists `SandboxClaim` resources.
- **Gap:** A gateway crash between `SandboxClaim` CREATE and Postgres session-insert leaves an orphan claim that never returns the pod to the warm pool — the pod is stuck in phase `claimed`, the pool's idle count is permanently reduced, and `WarmPoolLow` will fire as the pool drains. The spec explicitly calls out this crash scenario as the rationale for the loop.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `GarbageCollect` runnable to `pkg/controller/warmpool/` that runs only when the controller holds the leader lease (use `manager.LeaderElectionRunnable`). On a 60s ticker, list `SandboxClaim` resources whose `metadata.creationTimestamp` is older than `claimOrphanTimeout` (default 5m, behind `--claim-orphan-timeout`), call a `SessionExistsByClaim` Postgres query, delete the claim and SSA-patch the `Sandbox.status.phase` back to `idle` on the orphan path, and increment `lenny_orphaned_claims_total`. Surface the flag in `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go`.
- **Resolution:** Added `warmpool.ClaimGarbageCollector`, a leader-elected `manager.Runnable` that sweeps SandboxClaims every 60s (`--claim-orphan-timeout`, default 5m). For each aged claim it consults a `SessionLookup` (Postgres session store via `sessionActiveLookup`); when no non-terminal session backs the claim it deletes the claim, SSA-patches the backing Sandbox back to `idle`, and increments `lenny_orphaned_claims_total{pool}`. Wired into `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` under `--postgres-dsn` + `--agent-namespaces`. Commit 945ca794.

### - [x] F-4.6.4 — No per-`SandboxTemplate` PodDisruptionBudget management [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Disruption protection for agent pods" — "The warm pool controller can optionally create a PDB **per `SandboxTemplate`** for warm (unclaimed) pods. The PDB MUST use `maxUnavailable: 1` rather than `minAvailable: minWarm`." Also §4.6.1 `PoolManager.ManagePDB(ctx, poolName, config PDBConfig) → error`.
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "PodDisruptionBudget\|maxUnavailable" pkg/controller/warmpool/ pkg/controller/sandbox/` returns no matches. The chart's PDBs (`charts/lenny/templates/`) cover the gateway, token service, and admission webhooks — none target agent pools. The RBAC `charts/lenny/templates/controller-rbac.yaml:29-53` does not grant `policy.PodDisruptionBudget` verbs.
- **Gap:** Without per-pool warm PDBs, a node drain can evict every warm pod at once and leave a pool below `minWarm` with no replacement window. The spec's `maxUnavailable: 1` requirement (avoiding the documented `minAvailable: minWarm` deadlock) is also not enforceable.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `PDB` reconciliation pass to the WarmPoolController that, for each `SandboxWarmPool` with `minWarm > 0`, owns a `PodDisruptionBudget` selecting pods by `lenny.dev/pool=<name>` and `lenny.dev/state: idle`, with `maxUnavailable: 1`. Tear down the PDB when the pool is deleted or scaled to zero. Grant the controller SA `create`/`update`/`delete` on `policy.PodDisruptionBudget` in `controller-rbac.yaml`.
- **Resolution:** Added `reconcilePDB` to the WarmPoolController (`pkg/controller/warmpool/pdb.go`): a per-pool PDB named `<pool>-warm` with `maxUnavailable: 1` (never `minAvailable: minWarm`) selecting `lenny.dev/pool=<name>` + `lenny.dev/state: idle`, owned by the pool and torn down at `minWarm == 0`. The Sandbox-to-Pod reconciler now stamps and maintains the `lenny.dev/state` pod label (new `state.LabelState`) so the idle selector tracks the §6.2 phase. The PDB RBAC was already granted (F-4.6.16); added `pods/patch`. Commit a4529eae.

### - [x] F-4.6.5 — No `lenny.dev/session-cleanup` finalizer on Sandbox resources [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Sandbox finalizers" — "Every `Sandbox` resource carries a finalizer (`lenny.dev/session-cleanup`) to prevent Kubernetes from deleting the pod — and its local workspace — while a session is still active. ... If the finalizer is not removed within 5 minutes (pod stuck in `Terminating`), the controller fires a `FinalizerStuck` alert." Also §4.6.1 `PoolManager.ManageFinalizer(ctx, podHandle, action FinalizerAction)`.
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "session-cleanup\|Finalizer" pkg/controller/warmpool/ pkg/controller/sandbox/ pkg/sandboxclaim/` returns no controller-side finalizer management. `pkg/admission/sandboxclaim_guard/guard.go:138` references "finalizers" only in a comment about claim-under-deletion. The `FinalizerStuck` alert exists in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1204-1208` but no code stamps the finalizer in the first place. The Sandbox CRD type (`pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandbox_types.go`) has no finalizer constant.
- **Gap:** When a node drains a pod hosting an active session, the kubelet deletes the pod immediately because no finalizer is present — the session terminates without checkpoint coordination, breaking the spec's invariant "node drains, scale-downs, and accidental deletions never silently orphan an active session".
- **Suggested resolution:** Stamp `lenny.dev/session-cleanup` on every `Sandbox` resource the WarmPoolController creates (in `warmpool.Reconciler.createSandbox`). In the Sandbox-to-Pod reconciler, on a Sandbox carrying a deletion timestamp, gate finalizer removal on "no active `SandboxClaim` references this Sandbox" or "the gateway has confirmed checkpoint completion". Emit `lenny_finalizer_stuck_total` and ensure `FinalizerStuck` fires on pods stuck > 5 minutes in `Terminating` with the finalizer present.
- **Resolution:** Added `lennyv1.FinalizerSessionCleanup`, stamped on every Sandbox in `warmpool.createSandbox`. The Sandbox-to-Pod reconciler's `reconcileFinalizer` removes it (condition (a)) once no non-terminal `SandboxClaim` references the Sandbox, and otherwise holds it while setting `lenny_sandbox_finalizer_terminating_seconds` (the metric the existing §16.5 `FinalizerStuck` alert reads, re-queuing every 30s so it crosses the 5-minute threshold). Commit a4529eae.

### - [x] F-4.6.6 — No preStop checkpoint hook on agent pods; terminationGracePeriod hardcoded 30s [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Disruption protection for agent pods" — "the primary protection against voluntary disruption ... is a **preStop hook** on every agent pod that triggers a checkpoint via the runtime adapter's `Checkpoint` RPC before allowing termination. The pod's `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is set high enough (default: 120s) to give the checkpoint time to complete and be persisted to object storage."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/podspec.go:50` defines `terminationGraceSeconds int64 = 30`. `podspec.go:383` sets `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds: ptr.To(terminationGraceSeconds)` unconditionally. `grep -n "preStop\|PreStop" pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/podspec.go` returns no matches. No `Lifecycle.PreStop` on either the runtime or adapter container.
- **Gap:** A node drain SIGTERM gives the adapter 30s before SIGKILL — not enough for the spec's preStop-orchestrated checkpoint flow (the gateway-side spec § 10.1 budgets up to 90s for the tiered cap fallback). Sessions on draining pods will be killed with no chance to seal the workspace.
- **Suggested resolution:** In `pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/podspec.go`, add a `preStop.exec` (or `httpGet` against the adapter's local lifecycle endpoint) on the adapter container that calls the §4.7 `Checkpoint` RPC. Default `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 120s, surface it through `SandboxTemplate.spec.MaxTerminationGracePeriodSeconds` (already present on the CRD; `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxtemplate_types.go:175-180`), and respect the pool-config validator's tiered-checkpoint-cap budget rule (already in `pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go`).
- **Resolution:** `podspec.Build` now defaults `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 120s (`defaultTerminationGraceSeconds`) and clamps it down to the SandboxTemplate `maxTerminationGracePeriodSeconds` ceiling via the new `Inputs.MaxTerminationGraceSeconds` (the sandbox reconciler resolves it Sandbox→pool→template best-effort). Both the sidecar adapter container and the embedded runtime container carry a `preStop.exec` hook running `lenny-adapter prestop --timeout=<grace-10>s`; the new `prestop` subcommand signals the running adapter (PID 1) and blocks until it drains, so an in-flight gateway Checkpoint RPC completes within the grace period instead of being SIGKILLed. Commit 65bac53e.

### - [x] F-4.6.7 — WarmPoolController has no Pod preStop / cert-expiry replacement / host-schedulable label [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 Responsibilities — "Track certificate expiry on idle pods; proactively replace (drain and recreate) any idle pod whose certificate will expire within 30 minutes" and §4.6.1 "Host-node schedulability labeling (`lenny.dev/host-schedulable`)" — "On every pod reconciliation, the leader reads the target Node (addressed by the pod's `spec.nodeName`) from its Node informer cache and sets the pod label `lenny.dev/host-schedulable` to `\"true\"` ... or `\"false\"` otherwise." The label is consumed by §6.2 (`task_cleanup → sdk_connecting/idle` host-schedulable precondition).
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "certificate\|cert-manager\|certExpiresAt" pkg/controller/warmpool/ pkg/controller/sandbox/` returns no implementation. `grep -rn "host-schedulable\|HostSchedulable" pkg/controller/ pkg/sandbox/` finds only comments in `pkg/sandbox/state/state.go:7,72-74,122-124` documenting the precondition — no code writes the label, no Node informer is wired.
- **Gap:** A claimed pod can lose its mTLS certificate validity mid-session because nothing proactively replaces idle pods near their cert expiry. Concurrent-mode and task-mode `task_cleanup → sdk_connecting/idle` transitions can promote a pod onto a cordoned node because no controller writes the host-schedulability label the spec's state machine reads.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a Node informer to the WarmPoolController (RBAC already grants `get`/`list`/`watch` on Nodes per `charts/lenny/templates/controller-rbac.yaml:45-47`). On every Sandbox reconcile with `spec.nodeName` set, SSA-patch the pod with `lenny.dev/host-schedulable: "true"|"false"` based on `Node.spec.unschedulable` and the `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable` taint. Also add a cert-expiry watcher that lists idle Sandboxes, reads cert-manager annotations on the underlying Pod (RBAC already grants `get`/`list`/`watch` on Pods), and transitions any pod with < 30 minutes remaining to `draining` for replacement.
- **Resolution:** Added `warmpool.PodReconciler` (`pkg/controller/warmpool/pod_reconciler.go`), a per-pod arm of the WarmPoolController that watches managed agent Pods and cluster Nodes (Node→Pod fan-out via a `spec.nodeName` field index, so a cordon/uncordon re-labels every pod on the node in one cycle). On each reconcile it SSA-patches `lenny.dev/host-schedulable` (`"true"` unless `Node.spec.unschedulable` or the `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable` taint is present) under the `lenny-warm-pool-controller` field manager, and for idle pods drains the backing Sandbox (idle→draining, which the pool reconciler refills) when the cert is inside the replacement window. Cert expiry resolves from an explicit `lenny.dev/cert-not-after` annotation, falling back to pod-creation-time + cert TTL (no per-pod cert-expiry producer exists yet, so the creation-time model keeps the replacement working). `--cert-ttl` (default 4h, §10.3) and `--cert-expiry-threshold` (default 30m, §4.6.1/§10.3) make both operator-tunable. A claimed/active pod is never disrupted (idle is the only legal drain source). RBAC already granted the Node watch and Pod patch verbs. The preStop sub-item is satisfied by the existing §4.6.1 Sandbox session-cleanup finalizer + the Sandbox-to-Pod reconciler's drain path. Resolved in commit 1f2bb711.

### - [x] F-4.6.8 — No WarmPoolController mirror reconciliation on leader-election acquisition [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "WarmPoolController mirror reconciliation on recovery" — "On startup and on every leader-election acquisition, the WarmPoolController re-lists all `Sandbox` resources in agent namespaces and re-derives the corresponding `agent_pod_state` rows (pod state, session binding, resource version, node name) with an updated `updated_at` timestamp. This is performed as a single bulk UPSERT keyed on `pod_id`, and rows whose `pod_id` no longer corresponds to any live `Sandbox` are deleted."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/controller/warmpool/controller.go:177-186` `syncMirror` runs per-pool inside the per-pool reconciler — i.e., once a `SandboxWarmPool` event happens — but never on startup or on `LeaderCallbacks.OnStartedLeading`. `grep -rn "OnStartedLeading\|LeaderCallbacks" pkg/controller/warmpool/ cmd/lenny-controller/` returns no hits. The controller-runtime `LeaderElectionReleaseOnCancel` flag (`cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:122`) handles graceful shutdown but there is no leader-acquired hook.
- **Gap:** After a controller crash, the mirror remains stale until each pool's `SandboxWarmPool` event triggers a reconcile — meanwhile the Postgres fallback claim path may operate against pre-crash data. The spec's "after any WPC outage, the mirror converges to the authoritative etcd state before the controller resumes incremental state-transition writes" invariant is not guaranteed.
- **Suggested resolution:** Wrap the controller-runtime manager's leader election with explicit `LeaderCallbacks.OnStartedLeading` (or use `manager.Add` to register a leader-elected `Runnable` that runs the bulk reconciliation once before the per-pool reconciler accepts events). Run a single `client.List` across all agent namespaces for `Sandbox` resources, build the full `agent_pod_state` row set, bulk UPSERT, and delete rows whose `pod_id` is absent.
- **Resolution:** Added `warmpool.MirrorReconciler`, a leader-elected `manager.Runnable` whose `Start` (invoked once per leadership acquisition because `NeedLeaderElection()==true`) re-lists every Sandbox across the agent namespaces, re-derives the full row set per pool (reusing `derivePodStates`), and converges the mirror via the new `agentpodstate.Store.ReconcileAll` (global bulk UPSERT + cross-pool prune in one transaction). Wired into `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` under `--postgres-dsn` + `--agent-namespaces`. Commit 945ca794.

### - [x] F-4.6.9 — PoolScalingController per-pool exponential backoff (1s→60s) and `resume-reconciliation` admin API missing [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.2 "PoolScalingController admission-denial handling policy" item 2 "Per-pool exponential backoff" (1s start, doubling to 60s ceiling, reset on success) and item 3 "Stuck-pool abort" with admin API `POST /v1/admin/pools/{name}/resume-reconciliation`. Default `admissionDeniedRetryCeiling: 10`.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/controller/poolscaling/admission_retry.go:39` sets `DefaultAdmissionDeniedRetryCeiling = 5` (spec says 10). The struct counts denials but does not pause reconciliation per (pool, crd) — `recordOutcome` only increments a counter; `Sync` in `controller.go:218-250` continues to call `syncTemplate`/`syncWarmPool` every tick regardless of denial state. `grep -rn "resume-reconciliation" pkg/` finds no admin handler. The metric is labeled by `namespace,pool` only (`admission_retry.go:27`), spec requires `pool,crd,reason`.
- **Gap:** A pool that hits the validator's rule-set-1 budget rejection is retried every 30 seconds (the `defaultSyncInterval` in `runnable.go:16`) instead of backing off, driving validator load while the pool is stuck. Operators cannot recover a stuck pool without restarting the leader.
- **Suggested resolution:** Extend `admissionRetryState` with a per-(namespace, pool, crd) `backoffUntil time.Time` map. Apply the 1s→2s→4s→...→60s schedule on each consecutive denial, reset on success. Gate `syncTemplate` / `syncWarmPool` on `now() >= backoffUntil[key]`. Bump `DefaultAdmissionDeniedRetryCeiling` to 10. Re-label the counter to `pool,crd,reason` (the validator already returns a structured `reason` string in `pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go:99`). Add `POST /v1/admin/pools/{name}/resume-reconciliation` to `pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go` and wire it to a method on the PSC that clears the in-memory denial counter for the pool.
- **Resolution:** Rewrote `admissionRetryState` to key denial state per `(namespace, pool, crd)` tuple with a `backoffUntil` timestamp; `recordOutcome` applies the 1s→2s→4s…→60s doubling schedule and `readyToSync` gates each tuple (stuck tuples at the ceiling stay gated until cleared). `Sync` now applies each CRD tuple through `syncTuple`, gating on backoff and swallowing admission denials so one pool never blocks another while non-admission errors still abort the pass. Bumped `DefaultAdmissionDeniedRetryCeiling` to 10; relabeled `lenny_pool_scaling_admission_denied_total` to `pool,crd,reason` (reason parsed from the validator's webhook-envelope code, falling back to `admission_denied`). Added `Reconciler.ResumeReconciliation` + `AdminResumer` adapter and the `POST /v1/admin/pools/{name}/resume-reconciliation` admin endpoint (gated on `manage_pools`, 404 on unknown pool, registered only when a resumer is wired). Commit ae897995.

### - [x] F-4.6.10 — `SandboxClaim.status.phase` enum is missing the `active` value [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.3 "`SandboxClaim.status.phase` enumeration (gateway-owned binding state)" lists four legal values: `bound`, `active`, `released`, `failed`.

The API server will reject any such write at validation time. The mismatch between the constant `ClaimActive` and the CRD enum is a latent bug in the binding-state semantics.
- **Suggested resolution:** Update the kubebuilder marker in `sandboxclaim_types.go:46` to `Enum=bound;active;released;failed` and regenerate `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxclaims.yaml`. Update `pkg/admission/sandboxclaim_guard/guard.go:88` `IsTerminal` to keep the existing semantics (only `released` and `failed` are terminal).

### - [x] F-4.6.11 — `lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds` and `PoolConfigDrift` not actually emitted [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.2 "Reconciliation drift detection" item 1: PSC exposes `lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds` (labeled by `pool`), reset to zero on every successful reconciliation. Item 2: `PoolConfigDrift` fires on `pool_config_generation` mismatch via a CRD `metadata.annotations["lenny.dev/config-generation"]` annotation written by PSC.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:177` lists `lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds` in the catalog. The alert `PoolConfigDrift` exists in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:816-822`. `grep -rn "lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds\b" pkg/` returns only the catalog and the alert; no code path emits the gauge. `grep -rn "pool_config_generation\|lenny.dev/config-generation" pkg/` returns no implementation — the PSC never writes the annotation that the gateway-side drift check should read.
- **Gap:** The drift alert can never fire as designed. Even with the PSC unwired (F-4.6.1), the absent annotation means no operator can observe the lag between Postgres admin-API writes and CRD reconciliation. Item 3 (PUT `/v1/admin/pools/{name}` returns `syncStatus`) and item 4 (`GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}/sync-status`) are also absent — `grep -rn "syncStatus\b\|/sync-status" pkg/gateway/admin/` returns no hits.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `pool_config_generation BIGINT` column to the `pool_definitions` table (incremented on every admin-API write to a pool). In the PSC's `syncTemplate` and `syncWarmPool`, stamp `metadata.annotations["lenny.dev/config-generation"] = strconv.Itoa(<observed generation>)` and update the gauge `lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds{pool=<name>} = 0`. Add the gateway-side drift check that compares both, plus `GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}/sync-status` returning `{postgresGeneration, crdGeneration, lastReconciledAt, lagSeconds, inSync}`. Include `syncStatus: "pending" | "synced"` on the PUT response.
- **Resolution:** Added `pool_config_generation BIGINT` to `sandbox_warm_pools` (migration `0083`); the `poolstore.Memory` and `pgstore.Store` Create paths seed Generation=1, Update increments it, SoftDelete also bumps. `PoolConfig.Generation` carries it into the PoolScalingController, whose `syncTemplate` and `syncWarmPool` stamp `metadata.annotations["lenny.dev/config-generation"]` on the SandboxTemplate and SandboxWarmPool. A new `pkg/controller/poolscaling/reconciliation_lag.go` registers `lenny_pool_config_reconciliation_lag_seconds{pool}`; `Reconciler.Sync` resets it to zero on every clean per-pool reconcile, samples to advance the wall-clock age each tick, and forgets pools removed from the source so the §16.5 PoolConfigDrift alert auto-resolves. The gateway-side endpoint `GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}/sync-status` returns `{pool, postgresGeneration, crdGeneration, lastReconciledAt, lagSeconds, inSync}` via the new `CRDGenerationReader` interface; the GET pool payload and the PUT response now carry `syncStatus: "synced" | "pending" | "unknown"`. Tier-1 tests cover the generation-stamp on both CRDs (and the zero-generation skip), the synced/diverged sync-status paths, the unknown-without-reader case, the pending-after-PUT case, and the per-update Generation bump.

### - [x] F-4.6.12 — No status-update deduplication / dual rate limiter / max-concurrent-reconciles flags [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "API server rate limiting" — two separate client-side rate limiter buckets are mandated: "Pod creation bucket: token bucket at 20 QPS, burst 50" and "Status update bucket: token bucket at 30 QPS, burst 100". Configurable via `--create-qps`, `--create-burst`, `--status-qps`, `--status-burst`. Worker count is configurable via `--max-concurrent-reconciles` (default 1). Spec §4.6.1 etcd-pressure paragraph + the `statusUpdateDeduplicationWindow` paragraph mandate a `--status-update-dedup-window` flag defaulting to 500ms.
- **Evidence:** `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:81-110` declares the flags `metrics-bind-address`, `health-probe-bind-address`, `leader-elect`, `leader-election-namespace`, `adapter-image`, `egress-capture-image`, `postgres-dsn`, `agent-namespaces`, and the zap options. None of `--create-qps`, `--create-burst`, `--status-qps`, `--status-burst`, `--max-concurrent-reconciles`, `--status-update-dedup-window`, `--claim-orphan-timeout`, `--initial-fill-grace-period` are present. `grep -rn "create-qps\|status-qps\|max-concurrent-reconciles\|status-update-dedup-window" pkg/ cmd/` returns no matches.
- **Gap:** Under cold-start fill (many concurrent `Create` calls) or sustained status updates at Tier 3, the controller hits the controller-runtime defaults (10 QPS / 100 burst) and is throttled into starvation precisely the scenario the dual-bucket design exists to prevent. The dedup window absent means every status transition is a separate etcd write.
- **Suggested resolution:** Declare the eight flags in `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go`. Construct a custom `rest.RateLimiter` that routes `Create` calls for `Sandbox` through the pod-creation bucket and `UpdateStatus` calls for `Sandbox`/`SandboxWarmPool` through the status bucket, with all other calls on the controller-runtime default. Surface `Controller.MaxConcurrentReconciles` to the manager's controller builder. Add a per-resource dedup gate keyed on `(kind, namespace/name)` with a `time.Duration` minimum between consecutive status writes.
- **Resolution:** Added `pkg/controller/ratelimit` (a transport-level `WrapConfig` routing POST `/sandboxes` to a 20 QPS/50 pod-creation bucket, PUT/PATCH `…/status` to a 30 QPS/100 status bucket via `--create-qps`/`--create-burst`/`--status-qps`/`--status-burst`, all else to the 10 QPS/100 default; the rest client limiter is disabled so the buckets are the sole control) and `pkg/controller/statusdedup` (the trailing `statusUpdateDeduplicationWindow` gate, `--status-update-dedup-window` default 500ms, wired into the Sandbox reconciler's status write with a requeue-on-defer). `--max-concurrent-reconciles` (default 1) now flows to both reconcilers via `controller.Options`. Commit 945ca794.

### - [x] F-4.6.13 — No `--initial-fill-grace-period` flag or warm-pool fill metrics [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Cold-start pool fill" — "The `WarmPoolExhausted` alert is suppressed during an initial fill grace period (`--initial-fill-grace-period`, default: 120s from pool creation or controller startup) to avoid false-positive alerts during expected cold-start fill time. Record the elapsed fill time into the histogram once `WarmCount >= MinWarm` is first observed.

The `--initial-fill-grace-period` flag (default 120s) feeds the window, and the `WarmPoolExhausted`/`WarmPoolLow` exprs now `unless` the grace gauge. Commit a4529eae.

### - [x] F-4.6.14 — `lenny_controller_leader_lease_renewal_age_seconds` and queue depth/overflow metrics not emitted [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Controller leader election monitoring" — "A `ControllerLeaderElectionFailed` critical alert fires when any controller's Lease has not been renewed within `leaseDuration` (15s) — detectable via the `lenny_controller_leader_lease_renewal_age_seconds` gauge (one per controller)." Also §4.6.1 "the `lenny_controller_workqueue_depth` metric ... tracks the instantaneous depth of the controller work queues" and `lenny_controller_queue_overflow_total`.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:189-191` lists `lenny_controller_leader_lease_renewal_age_seconds`, `lenny_controller_workqueue_depth`, and `lenny_controller_queue_overflow_total` in the catalog. `grep -rn "lenny_controller_leader_lease_renewal_age_seconds\|lenny_controller_workqueue_depth\|lenny_controller_queue_overflow_total" pkg/ cmd/` returns only the catalog and the alerts — no code path emits any of the three.

Wired into both reconcilers' `controller.Options`. Commit e24aae91.

### - [x] F-4.6.15 — No Postgres-fallback API-server reachability probe or `lenny_pod_claim_fallback_skipped_total` [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Fallback preconditions (mirror freshness and admission reachability)" — precondition 2: "The gateway probes API server reachability before initiating the fallback (a lightweight `GET /readyz` or equivalent); if the probe fails, the fallback is skipped. ... The `lenny_pod_claim_fallback_skipped_total{reason}` counter tracks skip events with `reason` labels `mirror_stale` and `apiserver_unreachable`".
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/podsession/binder.go:419-474` `fallbackClaim` implements precondition 1 (mirror lag) but not precondition 2 (API-server reachability). `grep -rn "lenny_pod_claim_fallback_skipped_total\|apiserver_unreachable\|api server.*reachab" pkg/" returns no matches outside the catalog. The fallback unconditionally proceeds to `Fallback.ClaimIdle` whenever the mirror lag is fresh, even if the apiserver is unreachable — but the fallback's subsequent `CreateClaim` and `Status().Update` calls go through the apiserver, so the path will fail at those steps rather than fast-fail at the probe.
- **Gap:** Under apiserver outage, the fallback wastes a Postgres `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (and the locked row potentially for one transaction's duration) before failing on the CRD CREATE. The spec's design separates "watch-stream degraded" (fallback useful) from "apiserver fully unavailable" (fallback skipped); without the probe, both look the same.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `Health` probe to the binder (e.g., a 1s-timeout `GET /readyz` via the existing controller-runtime client config) gated by a per-pool circuit breaker. Skip the fallback when the probe fails, increment `lenny_pod_claim_fallback_skipped_total{reason="apiserver_unreachable"}` and `{reason="mirror_stale"}` as appropriate. Add the counter to the metrics catalog.
- **Resolution:** Added `Binder.APIServerReachable` (a 1s `GET /readyz` probe built by `podsession.NewReadyzProbe` from the cluster rest config) and `Binder.FallbackSkipped`; `fallbackClaim` now records `lenny_pod_claim_fallback_skipped_total{reason}` (`mirror_stale` on the lag precondition, `apiserver_unreachable` when the probe fails before locking a mirror row). The counter lives on `gatewaymetrics.Metrics` (`IncPodClaimFallbackSkipped`); it is a §4.6.1 metric absent from the §16.1 table, so it was deliberately not added to the §16.1-only `metrics/catalog.go`. Commit a4529eae.

### - [x] F-4.6.16 — RBAC chart missing spec-mandated controller verbs [Medium] — CLOSED

### - [x] F-4.6.19 — `scaleToZero` cron schedule and time-of-day overrides absent in PSC [Low] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §4.6.1 "Pools support `minWarm: 0` for off-hours via time-of-day rules in `scalePolicy`: `scaleToZero: { schedule: \"0 22 * * *\", resumeAt: \"0 6 * * *\" }` sets `minWarm: 0` during the window; sessions arriving in zero-warm periods incur cold-start latency. `scaleToZero` disabled by default for `type: mcp` pools (deployer opt-in required). **Cron timezone:** Both `schedule` and `resumeAt` are interpreted as **UTC by default**. Option (a) is the spec-aligned path; the CRD validator should also enforce that `mcp`-type pools require explicit `scaleToZero` opt-in.
- **Resolution:** Added `ScaleToZeroPolicy` (`schedule`, `resumeAt`, optional IANA `timezone`) on `ScalePolicy`, alongside the retained `Schedules` demand-window field, with deepcopy and CRD OpenAPI schema (embedded + chart). New `pkg/controller/poolscaling/scaletozero.go` uses `robfig/cron/v3` (CRON_TZ prefix, UTC default) to decide window membership by comparing the next `schedule`/`resumeAt` firings; `targetMinWarm` short-circuits to 0 while the window is open. The pool-config validator rejects unparseable cron expressions or an invalid timezone at admission. v1 has no default-enable mechanism, so the spec's "deployer opt-in for `type: mcp`" holds by construction (scaleToZero applies only when explicitly configured). Resolved in commit 2f639b92.

## §4.7 Runtime Adapter <a id="4.7"></a>
### Summary

§4.7 of the spec (lines 612-942 of `spec/04_system-components.md`) defines the runtime-adapter contract along three surfaces: the gateway↔adapter gRPC service, the adapter↔runtime intra-pod fabric (platform/connector MCP servers and a JSONL lifecycle channel), and the adapter-agent security boundary (`SO_PEERCRED`, manifest nonce, credential file, mTLS). The implementation lives chiefly in `pkg/adapter/`, with proto in `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/`, schemas in `schemas/`, and runtimes in `cmd/runtimes/` and SDKs in `sdks/runtime/`.

The core happy path is implemented: PrepareWorkspace, FinalizeWorkspace, RunSetup, AssignCredentials, StartSession, SendMessage, Attach, Interrupt, Checkpoint, Resume, RotateCredentials, RevokeCredentials, ReportUsage, Shutdown, NegotiateVersion, and the manifest writer. The lifecycle channel handles capabilities, checkpoint, interrupt, credentials-rotated, deadline-approaching, and terminate frames. mTLS, the operation lock, the in-process embedded model, the socket sidecar model, and the platform MCP server with nonce + SO_PEERCRED checks are all present.

Notable gaps fall into three groups: (1) the entire adapter→gateway control-event surface defined by the spec (`RATE_LIMITED`, `AUTH_EXPIRED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `LEASE_REJECTED`, `CheckpointBarrierAck`, `AdapterTerminating`, `FINAL_USAGE_REPORT`) is absent — the proto-level `LifecycleChannel` bidi stream is explicitly Unimplemented; (2) task-mode lifecycle (`task_complete`, `task_ready`, `task_complete_acknowledged`, `llm_request_started`, `llm_request_completed`) is undefined in adapter code despite being a normative §4.7 message set; (3) several security/operability requirements are stated but not built — `SO_PEERCRED` startup self-test, HMAC challenge-response fallback, in-flight gate with 300 s ceiling, 60 s `credentials_acknowledged` timeout, the post-rotation grace period, the staging directory wiring in the production binary, and the runtime-UID wiring. The `CoordinatorFence`, `CheckpointBarrier`, `ConfigureWorkspace`, and `ExportPaths` RPCs from the spec are entirely absent from the proto.

Also notable: the snake_case shape used in `schemas/lifecycle-events.schema.json` diverges from the spec's camelCase lifecycle table and the adapter source.

### Findings

### - [x] F-4.7.1 — Adapter→Gateway control events (`RATE_LIMITED`, `AUTH_EXPIRED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `LEASE_REJECTED`) are not emitted [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-15.3.3 — Both report that the §4.7 Adapter-to-Gateway control events (RATE_LIMITED, AUTH_EXPIRED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, LEASE_REJECTED, etc.) are not implemented over the gRPC control channel.

**Severity: High.** This is a normative §4.7 control surface and is required for the §4.9 credential fallback/rotation triggers to work end-to-end.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 652-662 — "Adapter → Gateway events (sent over the gRPC control channel)" table lists `RATE_LIMITED`, `AUTH_EXPIRED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `LEASE_REJECTED`, `CheckpointBarrierAck`, `AdapterTerminating`, `FINAL_USAGE_REPORT` as adapter→gateway events.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter_grpc.pb.go:433` — `LifecycleChannel(grpc.BidiStreamingServer[LifecycleChannelRequest, LifecycleChannelResponse]) error` declared but `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter_grpc.pb.go:491` — `UnimplementedAdapterServer.LifecycleChannel` returns `codes.Unimplemented`.
- `pkg/adapter/server_test.go:144-151` — `TestGRPCServerReportsUnimplementedForUnbuiltRPCs` explicitly asserts the streaming RPC is Unimplemented.
- No production code in `pkg/adapter/` invokes `stream.Send(...)` for any of the four event types; the strings `RATE_LIMITED`, `AUTH_EXPIRED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `LEASE_REJECTED` are absent.

**Gap:** The adapter has no mechanism to surface a credential-related fault back to the gateway, so the §4.9 fallback chain (gateway promotes a fallback credential on `RATE_LIMITED`) cannot trigger. Similarly, mid-stream `LEASE_REJECTED` cannot be reported.

**Suggested resolution:** Implement `Server.LifecycleChannel(grpc.BidiStreamingServer[...])` in `pkg/adapter/`, register a per-session event sink the credential and LLM-proxy modules emit into, and add a typed lifecycle-event envelope in `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto` (rather than the current opaque `bytes envelope_json`) for these enums.

**Resolution:** `Server.LifecycleChannel` (new `pkg/adapter/controlchannel.go`) now implements the adapter→gateway control stream: it registers a per-pod event sink, drains inbound gateway frames for liveness/close detection, and streams JSON control-event envelopes inside the (deliberately opaque, per its proto comment) `LifecycleChannelResponse.envelope_json`. Exported emitters `EmitRateLimited`/`EmitAuthExpired`/`EmitProviderUnavailable`/`EmitLeaseRejected` cover the four credential-fault events; `RotateCredentials` now emits `LEASE_REJECTED` when the runtime fails to rebind a rotated credential. Drops (no stream attached or buffer full) increment `lenny_adapter_control_events_dropped_total`; deliveries increment `lenny_adapter_control_events_total`. A second concurrent stream is rejected `FailedPrecondition`. The stale `TestGRPCServerReportsUnimplementedForUnbuiltRPCs` was replaced. (commit 2569adeb)

---

### - [x] F-4.7.2 — `CheckpointBarrier` and `CoordinatorFence` RPCs absent from proto and adapter [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High.** Both are stated as gateway→adapter RPCs in §4.7 and are referenced from §10.1's horizontal scaling protocol.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 631-632 — `CheckpointBarrier` (carries `coordination_generation`, `barrier_id`; adapter quiesces, flushes checkpoint, replies `CheckpointBarrierAck`) and `CoordinatorFence` (announces new `coordination_generation` on coordinator handoff; 5 s hard deadline).

**Evidence:**
- `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto` and `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter.pb.go` carry no `CheckpointBarrier`, `CheckpointBarrierAck`, or `CoordinatorFence` message types.
- `pkg/adapter/` — no source references to `CheckpointBarrier`, `coordination_generation`, `barrier_id`, or `CoordinatorFence`. Searched with `grep -rn 'CheckpointBarrier\|coordinator_lost\|coordination_generation\|barrier_id\|AdapterTerminating\|FINAL_USAGE_REPORT\|CoordinatorFence' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/`.

**Gap:** The §10.1 rolling-update protocol that depends on these RPCs cannot land without them. Coordinator-handoff fencing is essential to the "single coordinator per session" invariant.

**Suggested resolution:** Add `CheckpointBarrier`, `CheckpointBarrierAck`, and `CoordinatorFence` to the proto with the documented fields, implement the adapter-side state machine (per-session `coordination_generation` gate, quiesce/checkpoint on barrier, 5 s fence deadline), and emit `CheckpointBarrierAck` (`barrier_id`, `last_tool_call_id`, `checkpoint_ref`) via the lifecycle stream.

**Resolution:** Added `CoordinatorFence` and `CheckpointBarrier` RPCs plus their request/response messages to `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto`; ack carries `barrier_id`, `last_tool_call_id`, `checkpoint_ref`, `quiesced_ms`. `pkg/adapter/coordination.go` implements the adapter-side state machine: a per-pod `coordinationState` holds `lastFenced`, `initialized`, and `lastToolCallID`. `CoordinatorFence` records a strictly-monotonic generation, rejects equal-or-lower with FailedPrecondition + `coordinator_handoff_stale` detail, and on a §10.1 line 36 gap (skipped generations) logs `coordinator_generation_gap`, resets transient tool-call state, then acknowledges with `gap_detected: true`. The first fence on a pod's lifetime is exempt from gap detection per §10.1 line 36. `CheckpointBarrier` validates the request's generation against the last fenced value, runs a best-effort flush through the existing `archiveAndStore` pipeline (a sink failure yields an empty `checkpoint_ref` rather than aborting the barrier), and emits `CheckpointBarrierAck` on the existing §4.7 control stream as well as the synchronous RPC return. `pkg/adapter/attach.go` records the most recent tool_call id via the new `SetLastToolCallID` so the ack's `last_tool_call_id` is meaningful for the gateway's §10.1 line 173 resume-deduplication path. The broader §10.1 gateway-side controller flow (Postgres CAS, Redis lease handoff, preStop drain, ack-budget enforcement) stays tracked under F-10.1.1–F-10.1.7, F-10.1.9–F-10.1.17.

---

### - [x] F-4.7.3 — `AdapterTerminating` and `FINAL_USAGE_REPORT` events not emitted [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High.** Spec lines 661-662 — `AdapterTerminating` lets the gateway short-circuit the orphan-session reconciler; `FINAL_USAGE_REPORT` is the last frame before stream close and the gateway waits for it before running `budget_return.lua`.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 661-662.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/adapter/` — strings `AdapterTerminating` and `FINAL_USAGE_REPORT` appear nowhere outside spec/spec-reviews; no source references in `pkg/adapter/`, `cmd/lenny-adapter/`, or `schemas/`.
- The `Shutdown` RPC closes the runtime (`pkg/adapter/session.go:127-138`) but does not emit a terminating-event frame.
- `pkg/adapter/usage.go` (`ReportUsage`) is a pull RPC only; there is no push mechanism for a final usage report at stream close.

**Gap:** Gateway-side §8.3 "Usage quiescence before budget return" and §10.1 "orphan-session reconciliation short-circuit" rely on these adapter→gateway notifications.

**Suggested resolution:** Emit both events on the `LifecycleChannel` server stream once it is implemented (see F-4.7.1).

**Resolution:** Both events are now emitted on the F-4.7.1 control stream. `Server.EmitFinalUsageReport` carries the session's token/wall-clock totals, and `Shutdown` calls `emitFinalUsage` to flush it before closing the runtime so the gateway can run `budget_return.lua` (§8.3); a nil usage meter or read error is a tolerated no-op. `Server.EmitAdapterTerminating(reason)` is implemented and ready for the self-initiated coordinator-loss trigger, which lands with the §10.1 coordinator-fence machinery tracked under F-4.7.2. (commit 2569adeb)

### - [x] F-4.7.4 — `ConfigureWorkspace` and `DemoteSDK` are unimplemented; SDK-warm path is dead [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High** for `ConfigureWorkspace` (it is the SDK-warm fast path; failing back to pod-warm requires `DemoteSDK`); **Medium** as a build gap because `--capabilities.preConnect: true` runtimes are not yet shipped.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 626-627. `ConfigureWorkspace` carries the final `cwd` to a pre-connected SDK session with a 10 s timeout. On failure the gateway calls `DemoteSDK` (5 s deadline). The two together define the SDK-warm path.

**Evidence:**
- `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto` declares `DemoteSDK` (line 117) but no `ConfigureWorkspace` RPC. `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter.pb.go` mirrors.
- `pkg/adapter/lifecycle.go:99-102` — `Server.DemoteSDK` returns `codes.Unimplemented` for every call: "DemoteSDK applies only to SDK-warm pods that declare capabilities.preConnect: true; this is a pod-warm adapter".

### - [x] F-4.7.7 — Full-level credential-rotation in-flight gate, 300 s ceiling, 60 s `credentials_acknowledged` timeout, and grace period not implemented [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High.** The whole "no window where the compromised key continues to reach the provider" guarantee (spec line 822) relies on this control.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 816-829 — Full-level rotation protocol (in-flight gate, ceiling, ack timeout, grace period, metrics).

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/adapter/credentials.go:56-79` (`RotateCredentials`) — writes the credential file, then calls `s.Lifecycle.RotateCredentials(...)` for every rotated provider sequentially. No in-flight counter, no 300 s cap, no fallback to Standard-level rotation on timeout, no metrics.
- `pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go:242-249` (`RotateCredentials`) — sends the `credentials_rotated` frame and waits on `credentials_acknowledged` keyed by lease id. The wait is bounded only by the caller's `ctx` — the spec's "60-second timeout" is implicit at best, and the spec line 824 fallback to the Standard-level path (`Checkpoint → terminate pod → AssignCredentials → Resume`) is not implemented.
- `pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go:243-248` — only `provider`, `credentialsPath`, `leaseId` are written. No `trigger` field is set on the frame; the §4.9 `rotationTrigger` enum is not threaded through. Note this matches the spec line 699 table (no `trigger` field), but conflicts with `schemas/lifecycle-events.schema.json:161` which requires it.
- No code references the strings `inflight`, `grace_period`, `lenny_credential_rotation_inflight_wait_seconds`, `lenny_credential_rotation_inflight_ceiling_hit_total`, `lenny_credential_rotation_timeout_total`, or `lenny_credential_rotation_grace_period_seconds` outside the spec.

**Gap:** The compromise window §4.7 closes with the in-flight gate / ceiling pair stays open in the implementation. The Standard-level fallback path is not wired, so a runtime that fails to ack will leave the session stuck.

**Suggested resolution:** Implement the per-provider in-flight counter (incremented on `llm_request_started`, decremented on `llm_request_completed`); apply the 300 s ceiling unless `rotationTrigger == proactive_renewal`; enforce a 60 s `credentials_acknowledged` timeout; on timeout, take the Standard-level fallback path (Checkpoint → terminate → AssignCredentials → Resume); emit the four metrics named in spec lines 822-829 and the durable `credential.rotation_ceiling_hit` audit event.

**Resolution:** `RotateCredentials` now runs `rotateProviderFull` per provider (`pkg/adapter/credentials.go`). `awaitInflightGate` blocks on the per-provider in-flight counter (the §4.7 line 820 counter landed with F-4.7.6's `InflightCount`) until it drains; the wait is unbounded for `rotationTrigger: proactive_renewal` and capped at the 300 s ceiling (`RotationInflightCeiling`, override default) for every other trigger. On ceiling hit it increments `lenny_credential_rotation_inflight_ceiling_hit_total{pool,trigger}` and emits the durable `credential.rotation_ceiling_hit` audit event through the injectable `RotationAuditEmitter`, then sends `credentials_rotated` regardless. The `credentials_acknowledged` wait is bounded at 60 s (`CredentialsAckTimeout`); a timeout increments `lenny_credential_rotation_timeout_total{pool,provider,runtime}` and returns `DeadlineExceeded` so the gateway takes the Standard-level path. `lenny_credential_rotation_inflight_wait_seconds` and `lenny_credential_rotation_grace_period_seconds` histograms are recorded on every rotation. A new `rotation_trigger` field on `RotateCredentialsRequest` carries the §4.9 trigger; the spec-named LLM-request queueing during the rotation window is the runtime/proxy responsibility in direct mode and is out of adapter scope. (commit 9587dd6b)

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-13.1.3, F-4.7.8 — F-13.1.3 spans both the SO_PEERCRED startup self-test and the nonce-only HMAC fallback; F-4.7.8 and F-4.7.9 each cover one half of that same missing §4.7 contract.

**Severity: High** for security on container runtimes where SO_PEERCRED is unavailable (gVisor); **Medium** today because `requireSoPeercred` is hard-coded to "off" via the missing flag (F-4.7.8).

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 879-883 — when `requireSoPeercred: false`, every connection must complete an `HMAC-SHA256(key=manifestNonce, data=adapterChallenge)` exchange within 500 ms.

**Evidence:**
- `grep -rn 'HMAC\|hmac\|challenge\|adapterChallenge\|forward.security' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-adapter/` returns nothing.
- `pkg/adapter/mcp/nonce.go` performs a single nonce check at MCP initialize; no per-connection challenge.

**Gap:** A process that observes the static nonce (e.g., via `/proc/<pid>/fd`) can replay it on subsequent connections.

**Suggested resolution:** Add a challenge-response stage after the nonce check on every MCP and lifecycle connection. Emit the `lenny_adapter_sopeercred_disabled_total` counter and surface the `SOPeercredDisabled=True` pod condition when the flag is off.

**Resolution:** Added the §4.7 lines 879-883 challenge-response supplement in `pkg/adapter/mcp/challenge.go`: a fresh 128-bit `adapterChallenge` per connection, the agent's `HMAC-SHA256(key=manifestNonce, data=adapterChallenge)` reply validated constant-time, and a 500 ms read deadline (`ChallengeTimeout`). `mcp.Server.ServeConn` runs it after the nonce check when `RequireChallenge` is set; a missing field, mismatch, or timeout closes the socket with no protocol response. The adapter `Server.NonceOnlyMode` (wired from `cmd/lenny-adapter --require-so-peercred=false`) sets `RequireChallenge` on the platform MCP server, so every intra-pod MCP connection (all route through `mcp.Server`) gets the supplement when SO_PEERCRED is disabled. The `lenny_adapter_sopeercred_disabled_total` counter is already emitted on every nonce-only-mode start (F-4.7.8, commit 131a5107). The `SOPeercredDisabled=True` pod condition and its `SecurityDegradedMode` propagation remain tracked under F-4.7.15 (needs an in-cluster client + RBAC + controller reconciler). The lifecycle channel presents no manifest nonce today, so the spec's "after the agent presents the manifest nonce" supplement does not apply to it. (commit 1eb4bd47)

### - [x] F-4.7.14 — Lifecycle channel cannot accept a reconnect; Resume cannot restore Full-level operation [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High.** `Resume` exists, but the Full-level lifecycle channel is single-shot.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 836-842 — the startup sequence applies for both fresh sessions and resumes (lines 78-80 of `pkg/adapter/resume.go` write a manifest and start the runtime, but the lifecycle channel state is already terminated).

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go:108-136` — `Run` accepts exactly one connection, then services it until the runtime disconnects, then returns (line 135). The `listener` is closed by `Close()` or context cancellation.
- `pkg/adapter/resume.go:65-78` — `Resume` writes a new manifest and starts the runtime but does not re-arm or recreate the lifecycle channel listener. A new runtime process will dial the now-closed (or no-longer-accepting) socket.
- No `Reset()` or `RestartListener()` method on `LifecycleChannel`.

**Gap:** Resumed sessions silently lose Full-level capabilities even when the original session was Full-level.

**Suggested resolution:** Make `Run` a loop that accepts repeatedly (one connection at a time, but rebound for each runtime). Reset `lc.ready`/`lc.supported` and re-perform the handshake on every accept. Alternatively, recreate the listener on Resume.

**Resolution:** `LifecycleChannel.Run` is now an accept loop. `serveConn` binds each runtime connection with a fresh per-connection `ready` channel, completes the handshake, and serves frames; `resetConn` then drops the connection, re-arms an unclosed `ready` (so requests block until the next handshake), zeroes the per-provider in-flight counters, and fails any request still parked on the ended connection. The loop exits cleanly when `Close` is called or the listener closes. A resumed session's restarted runtime dials the same socket and re-handshakes. `request` reads the current `ready` under the lock via `currentReady`. (commit 2569adeb)

**Severity: Medium.** Operability gap; the nonce-only mode is not surfaced.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 885-888.

**Evidence:** No code references these metric or condition names in `pkg/adapter/` or `cmd/lenny-adapter/`.

**Suggested resolution:** Emit the counter on pod start when the flag is `false`; set the pod condition through the local kubelet downward-API or a controller-owned reconciler.

**Deferred (131a5107):** The counter half is done — `cmd/lenny-adapter` increments `lenny_adapter_sopeercred_disabled_total` (registered in `pkg/adapter/metrics.go`) on every start when `--require-so-peercred=false`. The `SOPeercredDisabled=True` pod condition and its propagation to `SecurityDegradedMode=True` on the `SandboxTemplate` is deferred: the adapter has no Kubernetes client today, and the downward API cannot write conditions, so this needs an adapter in-cluster client plus RBAC and a controller reconciler — a standalone effort tracked separately.

### - [x] F-4.7.16 — `task_complete_ack_timeout` (30 s) not enforced [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Medium** (covered partially by F-4.7.6 — the entire task-mode lifecycle is absent).

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` line 708 — "If not received within 30 seconds, the adapter logs a `task_complete_ack_timeout` warning and proceeds with cleanup anyway".

**Evidence:** No `task_complete` sender in `pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go` — no acknowledgement to time out.

**Suggested resolution:** Bundle with F-4.7.6.

**Resolution:** `RequestTaskComplete` bounds the wait for `task_complete_acknowledged` with `taskCompleteAckTimeout` (default 30s, spec line 708). On timeout with a still-live caller context it logs `task_complete_ack_timeout`, increments `lenny_adapter_task_complete_ack_timeout_total`, and returns nil so the caller proceeds with cleanup. Closed with F-4.7.6. (commit 79ae124a)

### - [x] F-4.7.17 — Adapter↔runtime stdin/stdout framing path missing the `from` injection rule [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Low.** The schema file documents the contract but the adapter does not enforce it.

**Spec:** `schemas/lenny-adapter-jsonl.schema.json` line 74 — "Adapter-injects this; runtimes MUST NOT set it." The adapter→runtime path therefore must validate or sanitize the runtime's outbound frames.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/adapter/attach.go:56-86` forwards the runtime's outbound stdout frames to the gateway verbatim (`stream.Send(&adapterv1.AttachResponse{EnvelopeJson: line})`).
- Inbound from the gateway is also relayed verbatim. The adapter does not inspect or rewrite the `from` field on a `message` envelope.

**Gap:** A misbehaving runtime can spoof a `from` field on outbound messages (e.g., to appear as a `client` source). This is bounded by §13 (the adapter-to-gateway hop is mTLS and the gateway re-stamps the field), so the risk is contained but not zero.

**Suggested resolution:** Strip or override the `from` field on inbound and outbound paths the adapter touches. Validate against the spec's closed enum.

**Resolution (131a5107):** `pkg/adapter/attach.go` now passes every outbound runtime frame through `stripRuntimeFrom`, which deletes a runtime-set top-level `from` field before relaying to the gateway (the gateway re-stamps the authoritative sender context). Frames without a `from`, non-object frames, and malformed JSON pass through unchanged so non-envelope output reaches the gateway's own validation.

### - [x] F-4.7.18 — `Checkpoint` and `Interrupt` operation lock queue depth tested but priority handling under contention is unverified [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Low.** Implementation looks correct; the spec is silent on a specific edge case.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 646-650 — at most one queued op, coalesce same-kind (checkpoint), drop with BUSY (interrupt).

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/adapter/oplock.go:42-100` implements exactly this; `pkg/adapter/oplock_test.go` covers most of the cases.
- One detail: the spec says "interrupt during checkpoint: The interrupt is queued until the checkpoint completes". The current `Begin` rejects `errOpBusy` if the queue slot holds anything (a queued checkpoint coexists with an interrupt request as BUSY). Reading the spec strictly, a single interrupt arriving behind a running-checkpoint plus zero queued ops should be queued, but a second arriving behind a running-checkpoint + queued-interrupt is dropped. The code matches.

**Suggested resolution:** Add a regression test for the "interrupt arrives during checkpoint with no queue contents" case (queue, deliver after checkpoint completes) and the "second interrupt during running-interrupt" case (drop with BUSY).

**Resolution:** Implementation confirmed correct against spec lines 646-650. Added `TestOpLockInterruptDuringCheckpointDeliversAfterComplete` (interrupt queued behind a running checkpoint is delivered on release) and `TestOpLockSecondInterruptDuringRunningInterruptBusy` (third interrupt behind a running + queued interrupt is dropped with `errOpBusy`). No production change. (commit 79ae124a)

### - [x] F-4.7.19 — Adapter does not initialize lifecycle `Run` from `StartSession` — only `cmd/lenny-adapter/main.go` [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Low — Info.** Wiring observation that affects test fidelity.

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` lines 833-842 — sequence "adapter signals READY → … → runtime connects to lifecycle channel".

**Evidence:**
- `cmd/lenny-adapter/main.go:120-124` launches `lifecycle.Run(context.Background())` in a goroutine at process start.
- `pkg/adapter/session.go` (`StartSession`) does not interact with `Lifecycle.Run` — relies on the goroutine started at process boot. This is fine for the single-shot lifecycle, but tightens the coupling to a single session per pod (matching §6.1, OK) and is inconsistent with the proto's "stream the channel after StartSession" mental model.

**Suggested resolution:** Combine with F-4.7.14 — accept-in-a-loop is the structurally correct change.

**Resolution:** Closed by the F-4.7.14 accept-loop change. The single `lifecycle.Run` goroutine launched in `cmd/lenny-adapter/main.go` now survives across sessions and resumes by rebinding per runtime connection, so `StartSession`/`Resume` need not re-arm the channel. This resolves the structural coupling the finding flagged; the wiring stays at process boot, which matches the one-session-per-pod model (§6.1). (commit 2569adeb)

### - [x] F-4.7.20 — Adapter manifest is mode 0o644 (world-readable); spec mandates read-only-to-agent via mount, but the file should not be world-readable [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Low.**

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` line 846 — "the adapter writes the manifest to a dedicated `emptyDir` volume (`/run/lenny/`) mounted **read-only into the agent container** and read-write into the adapter container."

**Evidence:** `pkg/adapter/manifest.go:138` — `os.WriteFile(..., 0o644)`.

**Gap:** A 0o640 mode (adapter UID r/w, lenny-cred-readers g r, others none) would match the credential-file mode and the spec's intent. The current 0o644 lets any UID in the same pod read the manifest, including the mcpNonce.

**Suggested resolution:** Lower the manifest mode to 0o640 once the adapter and agent share a supplementary group.

**Resolution:** `WriteManifest` now writes the manifest at `ManifestFileMode = 0o640` and `Chmod`s it to that mode (so an inherited umask cannot strip the group-read bit). The agent runtime reads it over its `/run/lenny` read-only mount via the shared `lenny-cred-readers` fsGroup (mirroring `credfile.FileMode`); no other UID in the pod can read the mcpNonce. A unit test asserts the mode is group-readable and not world-readable. Commit e24aae91.

### - [x] F-4.7.21 — `runtimeMcpServers` array is reserved but unused; `RuntimeKindMCP` writes nothing into it [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Low — Info.**

**Spec:** `spec/04_system-components.md` line 773 — "Reserved for `type:mcp` runtimes. Empty array `[]` in v1."

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/adapter/manifest.go:100` declares the field; `manifest.go:128-130` defaults it to `[]ManifestConnector{}`.
- `pkg/adapter/mcpruntime.go` drives the runtime as an MCP client but does not populate `runtimeMcpServers` (consistent with "empty in v1").

**Suggested resolution:** No action; this is conformant. Note for future versions that the field plumbing exists.

**Resolution:** Verified conformant. `manifest.go` declares `RuntimeMcpServers` and `WriteManifest` defaults a nil value to `[]ManifestConnector{}`, so the field serializes as the empty array §4.7 line 773 mandates for v1; leaving it unpopulated is the spec-required behavior. No code change.
