### - [x] F-4.9.20 — `vault_transit` provider has no admission-time validation (length, scheme), no translator [Low] — CLOSED

**Severity:** Low (provider is in the enum and accepted by `credentialstore.Register`, but no translator and no admission-time validation of the `vault_transit` per-pool fields exist).

**Spec:** spec/04_system-components.md line 1098 (`vault_transit`), 1293-1297 (`materializedConfig` schema), 1154 (Vault-specific TTL clamping rule).

**Evidence:** `pkg/credential/credential.go:28` declares `ProviderVaultTransit`. `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/*_translator.go` has no `vault_transit` translator. The spec's "Vault token TTL must be at least `leaseTTLSeconds`; a shorter Vault TTL takes precedence" rule is not implemented anywhere.

**Resolution (commit 017f9a68):** Closed jointly with F-4.9.16. The `vault_transit` materializedConfig schema (`vaultToken`, `vaultAddr`, `transitPath`, `keyName`, `expiresAt`, all Required:yes) is now in `directRequiredFields`, so a pool credential missing any of them fails issuance at the §4.9 mint validation with `CREDENTIAL_MATERIALIZATION_ERROR` (the admission-time field/scheme check the finding asked for; the bundle's `expiresAt` is RFC3339-validated). The §4.9 line 1154 Vault TTL clamping rule is implemented in `MintLease`'s `clampDirectExpiry`: when the materialized `expiresAt` precedes `issuedAt + leaseTTLSeconds`, the lease expiry is clamped to the actual Vault token expiry and `renewBefore` is recomputed from the clamp, so a shorter Vault TTL takes precedence. `vault_transit` is a secrets backend rather than an LLM-proxy upstream, so it has no proxy translator by design (the runtime uses the Vault token to fetch its own secret); the "no translator" observation is not a gap.

### Coverage notes

What works end-to-end today:
- A proxy-mode credential lease minted in the in-process `credassign.Service`, recorded in `credleasestore`, with the upstream credential placed in `credcache`, can be presented by a pod to `POST /llm-proxy/v1/messages`. The handler resolves the lease, runs the §4.9 expiry/revocation/SPIFFE checks via `Lease.ValidateProxyRequest`, calls the `AnthropicDirectTranslator`, forwards via the `Forwarder` through the `CircuitBreaker`, extracts authoritative usage from the response, and supports streaming with SSE relay. Tests: `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/handler_test.go`, translator unit tests in `tests/tier2_component/translators`.
- Per-tenant KEK envelope encryption of `credentials.secret` works end-to-end with `secret_key_version` tracking and a `Reseal` primitive for the §4.9.1 per-record step.
- The deny-list propagator carries pool-credential and user-credential revocations across replicas over Redis pub/sub.
- The proactive renewal worker tracks leases by `renewBefore`, retries up to 3, has the `expiresAt` guard, drops revoked leases, and pushes the rotated wire to the bound pod's adapter via `RotateCredentials`.
- SPIFFE-binding admission webhook (`pkg/admission/direct_mode_isolation`) rejects `direct+standard` and `proxy+spiffeBinding:disabled` in multi-tenant mode; tested in `pkg/admission/webhook/direct_mode_isolation_test.go`.
- User-credential registry CRUD via `POST/GET/PUT/POST .../revoke/DELETE /v1/credentials` (handlers in `pkg/gateway/credentialserver`).

What is broken or wired wrong relative to §4.9:
- No multi-provider lease map (the binder receives `map[string]string`, but no producer ever populates it for LLM providers; only VCS git-clone host-pattern resolution writes to it).
- The `credassign.Service` pool registry is gateway-internal but no admin or bootstrap path calls `RegisterPool`. The gRPC path on the Token Service has the same gap. The `POST /v1/admin/credential-pools` admin endpoint writes to `credentialpoolstore` (Postgres), but no code bridges from `credentialpoolstore.CredentialPool` to `credassign.Pool` (no controller reconciliation, no startup load).
- The LLM proxy handler is hard-mounted with `AnthropicDirectTranslator`; the four other translators built in `pkg/gateway/llmproxy` are dead code in production.

## §5.1 Runtime <a id="5.1"></a>
### Summary

§5.1 defines the unified `Runtime` registry as the single source of truth for both standalone and derived runtimes, with a rich field set, a normative merge algorithm, a declared-vs-observed integration-level admission contract, a typed `agentInterface` and `publishedMetadata` surface (with auto-generated A2A card and a bulk-regenerate endpoint), MCP `ToolAnnotations`-driven capability inference, and a per-tenant capability customization model. Most enum-bearing fields (`type`, `executionMode`, `isolationProfile`, `integrationLevel`, `capabilities`, `setupPolicy`, `taskPolicy`, `agentInterface`, `publishedMetadata`, `capabilityInferenceMode`, `toolCapabilityOverrides`, `minPlatformVersion`, `baseRuntime`, `labels`) are modeled in `runtimestore.Runtime`, persisted in Postgres, and exposed through the admin CRUD and bootstrap upsert paths; the agent-card generator, regenerate endpoint, derived-runtime validation (Prohibited-field set, single-level base check, capabilities-not-on-mcp, mcp-implies-no-agentInterface), and a Merge implementation that covers Inherited / Override / Maximum / Append / Merge for the modeled fields are present and unit-tested.

The audit surfaces three classes of gap. First, a substantial slice of the §5.1 normative field set is absent entirely from `runtimestore.Runtime`, the admin payload, Postgres schema, and the Merge algorithm: `allowedResourceClasses`, `supportedProviders`, `credentialCapabilities`, `limits`, `setupCommandPolicy`, `workspaceDefaults`, `runtimeOptionsSchema`, `defaultPoolConfig`, `allowSelfRecursion`, and `sharedAssets` (F-5.1.1 through F-5.1.10). The admin handler silently drops these on POST/PUT, the bootstrap upsert ignores them, and the merge cannot apply any of the §5.1 per-field rules (Inherited / Override / Append / restrict-only) for them. The `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` field that gates SDK-warm demotion is also unmodeled. Second, several admission-time validations enumerated as MUSTs in §5.1 are not implemented: the declared-vs-observed integration-level reconciliation that emits `RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS` and the `runtime.integrationLevel.declared` / `runtime.integrationLevel.underdeclared` audit fields (F-5.1.11), the `INVALID_RUNTIME: integrationLevel is only valid on type: agent runtimes` admission gate (F-5.1.12), labels-required enforcement at v1 (F-5.1.13), base-runtime `image` immutability via API (F-5.1.14), and the cross-derived-runtime impact-validation on base-runtime mutation (F-5.1.15). Third, several behaviors that are encoded in code but not wired into the request path are dead: the `capabilityinference.WarnMessage` registration-time WARN is never emitted (F-5.1.16), the Runtime CRD's `Registered` condition is never reconciled because no Runtime controller exists (F-5.1.17), the bootstrap upsert path skips both `validateDerivedRuntime` and `applyGeneratedCard` so a derived runtime or an `agentInterface`-bearing runtime registered via the §17.6 install seed enters the registry in a non-§5.1-compliant state (F-5.1.18, F-5.1.19), and the per-tenant capability customization promised in line 49 has no implementation surface (F-5.1.20).

### Findings

### - [x] F-5.1.1 — `allowedResourceClasses` field unmodeled in registry, admin, schema, and merge — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-5.1.2 — Both report a runtime CRD field unmodeled at the gateway boundary but for different fields (allowedResourceClasses vs supportedProviders).

- **Spec:** §5.1 standalone-runtime YAML (line 67) names `allowedResourceClasses: [small, medium, large]` as a runtime-level field. The merge table (line 187) classifies it as **Prohibited** on derived runtimes, with the additional rule "Must be a subset of base; pool config constrains further." §5.1 derived-runtime instantiation (line 252) restates the constraint: "resource classes cannot exceed base runtime's configured classes."
- **Evidence:** Only `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/runtime_types.go:53` (`AllowedResourceClasses []string`) carries the field, on the Runtime CRD shape. `runtimestore.Runtime` (`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:31`), the Postgres `runtime_definitions` table (`migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql:43`), every subsequent column-adding migration (`migrations/0013_...0023_...`), the admin payload (`pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:48` `RuntimePayload`), and the merge implementation (`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/merge.go`) all omit it. `validateDerivedRuntime` (`pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:132`) cannot reject `allowedResourceClasses` on a derived runtime because the field is not in the payload to inspect.
- **Gap:** The gateway has no record of which resource classes a runtime permits, so it cannot enforce the §5.1 subset constraint for derived runtimes and cannot reject session-creation requests that ask for a class the runtime does not allow. The CRD field is dropped at the controller boundary (no Runtime CRD reconciler; see F-5.1.17). The §17.6 reference-runtime catalog (`charts/lenny/templates/reference-runtimes.yaml:35-37`) ships `allowedResourceClasses` on the Runtime resource, but the field has nowhere to land in the gateway.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add `AllowedResourceClasses []string` to `runtimestore.Runtime`, persist via a new migration, accept on `RuntimePayload` and `UpdateRuntimeRequest`, add to `Merge` as Prohibited with subset validation against base, and add the §5.1 cross-field rejection ("derived must be a subset of base") under a new `INVALID_DERIVED_RUNTIME` clause. The session-creation path must then reject `resourceClass` requests outside the runtime's set.
- **Resolution:** Added `AllowedResourceClasses []string` to `runtimestore.Runtime` (cloned, merged as Prohibited so a derived runtime inherits the base set), persisted via migration 0069 (`allowed_resource_classes JSONB`), accepted on `RuntimePayload`/`UpdateRuntimeRequest`/OpenAPI runtime schema, and `validateDerivedRuntime`/`validateDerivedRuntimeUpdate` now reject a derived payload that sets it with `INVALID_DERIVED_RUNTIME`. The §5.1 pool-config subset constraint and a session-create `resourceClass` request field remain forward work (no `resourceClass` request surface exists on session creation yet). Resolved in commit 35d8fc4e.

### - [x] F-5.1.2 — `supportedProviders` field unmodeled in registry, admin, schema, and merge — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-5.1.1 — Both report a runtime CRD field unmodeled at the gateway boundary but for different fields (allowedResourceClasses vs supportedProviders).

- **Spec:** §5.1 standalone-runtime YAML (lines 70-72) requires `supportedProviders` (`anthropic_direct`, `aws_bedrock`, etc.). §5.1 minimal configuration (line 345) restates it as part of the absolute-minimum runtime registration. The merge table (line 191) classifies it as **Override** with the rule "Derived may restrict but not expand beyond base."
- **Evidence:** Only `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/runtime_types.go:58` (`SupportedProviders []string`) carries it on the CRD spec. `runtimestore.Runtime`, the Postgres schema, the admin payload, the bootstrap upsert, and `Merge` all omit it.

The §5.1 restrict-only merge rule cannot fire on derived runtimes.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add `SupportedProviders []string` to the store, migration, payload, and merge (Override + derived-subset check). The §4.9 lease path must consult this field when matching a session's requested provider.
- **Resolution:** Added `SupportedProviders []string` to `runtimestore.Runtime` (cloned, merged as Override so the base set applies when the derived runtime declares none), persisted via migration 0069 (`supported_providers JSONB`), accepted on `RuntimePayload`/`UpdateRuntimeRequest`/OpenAPI runtime schema, and flowed through the bootstrap upsert via the shared `runtimeFromPayload`. `validateDerivedRuntime`/`validateDerivedRuntimeUpdate` enforce the restrict-only subset rule (a derived entry absent from the base set is rejected with `INVALID_DERIVED_RUNTIME`). The §4.9 lease-path provider match is forward work (no provider-match path is wired on session creation yet). Resolved in commit 35d8fc4e.

- **Spec:** §5.1 standalone-runtime YAML (lines 73-75) defines `credentialCapabilities` with `hotRotation: true` and `proxyDialect: [openai, anthropic]`. The pool-side cross-validation (pool `proxyDialect` ∈ runtime `credentialCapabilities.proxyDialect`) is the deferred F-4.9.18, which now has the per-runtime declaration to consult.

### - [ ] F-5.1.11 — Declared-vs-observed integrationLevel admission not enforced — High [Medium] — DEFERRED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-24.18.1 — Both concern declared-vs-observed integrationLevel but target different components: F-24.18.1 is the validate CLI probe missing, while F-5.1.11 is gateway admission enforcement (RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS) missing.

- **Spec:** §5.1 lines 41-44 require the gateway to compare the declared `integrationLevel` against the observed level from the first `lifecycle_capabilities` / `lifecycle_support` exchange, and:
  - `observed < declared`: reject the first session assignment with `RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS` and log a structured error.
  - `observed > declared`: accept and emit a `runtime.integrationLevel.underdeclared` warning.
  - `observed == declared`: accept without annotation.
  Additionally line 41 specifies that admission emits a `runtime.integrationLevel.declared` audit field at registration.
- **Evidence:** A repository-wide search for `RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS`, `runtime.integrationLevel.declared`, `runtime.integrationLevel.underdeclared`, or any first-session-assignment level comparison returns no occurrences in `pkg/` or `cmd/` (only in `cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/validate.go:115`, where the validator points the operator at this gateway-side reconciliation as something the operator should rely on). The agent-pod adapter (`pkg/adapter/`) implements the `lifecycle_capabilities` handshake on the runtime side but the gateway never compares observed capabilities against the registered runtime's declared `integrationLevel`.
- **Gap:** A runtime can declare `integrationLevel: full` and ship only a Basic-level binary; the gateway routes session assignments to it normally, silently degrading checkpoint, clean interrupt, and credential-rotation features the caller expects. The validator's promise ("register the runtime with a gateway and inspect the lifecycle handshake; the gateway reports `RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS`") is hollow.
- **Suggested resolution:** Implement first-session-assignment admission in the gateway's pool-claim path: read the observed capability set from the adapter's `lifecycle_support` reply, compare against `runtimestore.Runtime.IntegrationLevel`, reject with `RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS` on underperformance and emit `runtime.integrationLevel.underdeclared` audit on overperformance. Stamp `runtime.integrationLevel.declared` on every registration audit event.
- **Deferred:** The observed integration level per §5.1 line 47 derives from the adapter↔runtime `lifecycle_capabilities` / `lifecycle_support` exchange (`pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go`), which is internal to the adapter over an abstract Unix socket; the gateway never sees it. The gateway's only adapter-supplied capability signal at session assignment is `NegotiateVersionResponse.Capabilities` (`pkg/gateway/podsession/binder.go`/`slotbinder.go`), which carries the adapter's *configured/advertised* capability tokens, not the runtime's *observed* lifecycle support. Faithful enforcement requires a new adapter→gateway data path: the adapter computing the observed level (lifecycle channel open → full; MCP-only → standard; neither → basic) and reporting it back through a new proto field, plus gateway comparison on the hot session-assignment path and a new `RUNTIME_LEVEL_UNDERPERFORMS` error code. This spans proto + adapter + gateway with §4.7 lifecycle-timing interactions and deserves a dedicated batch rather than being bolted onto the envtest-heavy claim path here.

### - [x] F-5.1.12 — `INVALID_RUNTIME: integrationLevel is only valid on type: agent runtimes` not enforced on standalone registration — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 36 mandates: "Only meaningful on `type: agent` runtimes — must not be set on `type: mcp` (gateway rejects with `INVALID_RUNTIME: integrationLevel is only valid on type: agent runtimes`)."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:312-323` (`validatePayloadEnums`) accepts any `IntegrationLevel` value within the enum without considering the `Type`. `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:679` (`ApplyDefaults`) only refrains from defaulting an empty value on mcp; it does not reject an explicitly-set value. The bootstrap upsert (`pkg/gateway/admin/bootstrap.go:182`) similarly relies on `validatePayloadEnums`. The lenny-ctl validator (`cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/validate.go:172-175`) does perform the check, but the gateway does not.
- **Gap:** A POST `/v1/admin/runtimes` with `type: mcp, integrationLevel: full` is accepted and persisted. The §5.1 invariant that integration level is meaningful only on agent runtimes is enforceable on the runtime-author side but not on the platform side; the asymmetry breaks the §5.1 promise that the gateway is the authoritative validator.
- **Suggested resolution:** In `validatePayloadEnums` (and the equivalent path in the PUT handler), reject `IntegrationLevel != ""` when `Type == "mcp"` with `INVALID_RUNTIME: integrationLevel is only valid on type: agent runtimes`.
- **Resolution:** Added `RuntimePayload.validateIntegrationLevelOnType`; the POST handler and bootstrap upsert reject `IntegrationLevel != ""` on `type:mcp` with `INVALID_RUNTIME: integrationLevel is only valid on type: agent runtimes`, and the PUT handler rejects setting `integrationLevel` on an existing `type:mcp` runtime (type is immutable via PUT). Resolved in commit 2ea0bcfc.

### - [ ] F-5.1.13 — `labels` not required on registration — Medium [Medium] — DEFERRED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 51: "**Labels are required from v1** — primary mechanism for environment `runtimeSelector` and `connectorSelector` matching (see [Section 10.6](10_gateway-internals.md#106-environment-resource-and-rbac-model))."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:343-380` (POST) and 475-553 (PUT) do not require `Labels` to be non-empty. `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:62-65` documents the field as optional ("nil or empty map means the runtime carries no labels"). The bootstrap upsert (line 237) only writes labels when present.
- **Gap:** A runtime registered with no labels is silently accepted; §10.6 `runtimeSelector` then matches nothing for that runtime, so its environment-membership status is effectively undefined. The §5.1 "required from v1" claim is contradicted.
- **Suggested resolution:** In `validatePayloadEnums` (or a dedicated validator), reject creation when `len(Labels) == 0`. The PUT path may permit existing label sets to be replaced wholesale but should reject an explicit empty map.
- **Deferred:** Enforcing labels-required at registration is a cross-cutting behavior change: ~80 existing `RuntimePayload`/`runtimestore.Runtime` test fixtures across `pkg/gateway/admin` and the embedded reference-runtime seed (`pkg/embedded/stack`) construct runtimes without labels and would all need label sets added. Warrants a dedicated batch that migrates every fixture and the §26 catalog seed alongside the validator.

### - [x] F-5.1.14 — Base runtime `image` not immutable via API — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 174: "**Base runtime mutability:** `image` and `name` immutable via API."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:564-566` accepts a PUT that mutates `Image` on a base runtime without restriction. `validateDerivedRuntimeUpdate` (line 166) only rejects `image` mutation on derived runtimes. `name` mutability is structurally prevented (the URL path drives identity), but `image` is not.
- **Gap:** An operator can PUT a new `image` on a base runtime via the admin API, bypassing the §10.5 `RuntimeUpgrade` orchestration that is meant to govern image rollouts. The §5.1 immutability invariant is violated.
- **Suggested resolution:** Reject `Image` mutation on a base runtime in the PUT handler with a dedicated error code (e.g., `IMAGE_IMMUTABLE: use RuntimeUpgrade to change runtime image`). The §10.5 controller path remains the only legitimate writer for `image`.
- **Resolution:** The PUT handler now rejects an `Image` change on a base (non-derived) runtime with `400 IMAGE_IMMUTABLE: base runtime image is immutable; use RuntimeUpgrade to change runtime image`. A no-op PUT carrying the same image is accepted; a derived runtime's image remains rejected as prohibited by `validateDerivedRuntimeUpdate`. Resolved in commit 6f70f0c9.

### - [x] F-5.1.15 — Impact validation on base-runtime mutation not implemented — High [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 174: "All other fields mutable with **impact validation** — changes that would invalidate existing derived runtimes are rejected with a list of affected runtimes."
- **Evidence:** No occurrence of impact-validation logic in `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go`. The PUT handler mutates the base runtime without scanning the registry for derived runtimes whose declared fields would be invalidated by the change (e.g., changing the base's `runtimeOptionsSchema` so that an existing derived runtime's schema declares a property that the new base does not).
- **Gap:** A base runtime can be mutated into a state that makes one or more of its derived runtimes invalid; the merge result then fails at session-creation time rather than being caught at write time. The "rejected with a list of affected runtimes" error response is not generated.
- **Suggested resolution:** On every PUT to a base runtime, list all derived runtimes that reference it, recompute their effective merge against the proposed new base, and reject the PUT when any derived would become invalid — returning the affected names in the error body.
- **Resolution:** The PUT handler now runs impact validation on a base runtime: `proposedBaseRuntime` applies the merge-input fields the change touches (`supportedProviders`, `allowSelfRecursion`, `runtimeOptionsSchema`, `setupPolicy`), `derivedRuntimesInvalidatedBy` lists every active derived runtime referencing the base and recomputes the §5.1 derived invariants (`derivedConflictsWithBase` reuses `providersNotInBase`, the self-recursion widen check, `forbiddenDerivedSchemaProperty`, and the new setup-timeout pairing check), and the PUT is rejected with `400 BASE_RUNTIME_MUTATION_INVALIDATES_DERIVED` carrying `details.affectedRuntimes` when any derived would break. Resolved in commit cbf779b4.

### - [ ] F-5.1.16 — Capability-inference WARN message produced but never emitted — Medium [Medium] — DEFERRED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 327: "When a tool's capability is inferred as `admin` due to absent annotations (the 'No annotations' row), the gateway emits a `WARN`-level log at registration time: `'Tool '<name>' on connector/runtime '<id>' has no MCP ToolAnnotations; capability inferred as 'admin' (conservative default). ...'`"
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/capabilityinference/capabilityinference.go:199` defines `WarnMessage(tool, id)`. A repository-wide search for callers returns only the unit test (`capabilityinference_test.go:188`). No registration-time path in `pkg/gateway/admin/connectors.go`, `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go`, or the connector-discovery flow invokes `WarnMessage` or logs the §5.1 warning.
- **Gap:** Deployers do not see the §5.1 warning when registering a connector or `type: mcp` runtime whose tools are unannotated. The first signal they get is a `TOOL_CAPABILITY_DENIED` at call time, which §5.1 specifically calls out as the late path that the registration-time warning should pre-empt.
- **Suggested resolution:** On connector and `type: mcp` runtime registration, iterate the `tools/list` response, run `capabilityinference.Infer` per tool, and emit `WarnMessage` to the structured logger on every tool whose inferred capabilities contain `admin` due to the "No annotations" path. (The function `IsInferredAdminFromNoAnnotations` is plausibly already there or trivially derivable.)
- **Deferred:** The WARN emit has no production hook to attach to. The gateway-side connector / `type:mcp` tool-discovery-and-inference pipeline is not built: `capabilityinference.Infer`/`Resolve`/`WarnMessage` are invoked only in tests, the connector and runtime admin payloads carry no tool list (`tools/list` is read at connection time, not at admin registration), and `TOOL_CAPABILITY_DENIED` has no production call site. Emitting the §5.1 line-327 warning requires first building that discovery+inference flow (a distinct, larger finding). Re-evaluate once tool discovery and capability persistence land.

### - [x] F-5.1.17 — Runtime CRD has no controller; `Registered` condition never set — High [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 establishes the Runtime as a declarative CRD ("`Runtime` is platform-global … cluster-scoped" — `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/runtime_types.go:84`), with the kubebuilder annotation explicitly promising "The controller sets a `Registered` condition once the runtime is mirrored into the gateway." §5.1 line 5 ("All runtimes are registered via the admin API as static configuration") and the chart's reference-runtimes template (line 19) treat the CRD as a registration source — Helm applies cluster-scoped `Runtime` resources, and a controller is expected to mirror them to the gateway's runtime registry.
- **Evidence:** `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` (lines 146-167) wires only the `WarmPoolController` and the `Sandbox` reconciler. There is no `RuntimeReconciler`. A repository-wide search for `RuntimeReconciler` / `reconcileRuntime` returns no results. The `RuntimeStatus.Conditions` field is declared but never populated.
- **Gap:** Helm-applied `Runtime` resources sit in etcd without ever being mirrored into the gateway's `runtime_definitions` table. The chart's `reference-runtimes.yaml` template is a no-op against the gateway: a fresh install registers zero runtimes through the CRD path. The CRD's printer columns ("Type", "Image", "Level") are populated only because the CRD itself stores them; the gateway never sees them. Operators relying on the §5.1 / §17.6 declarative install flow ("`helm install` registers each catalog entry as a platform-global Runtime record") will find an empty runtime registry on the gateway side.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `pkg/controller/runtime` package that watches `Runtime` resources, mirrors them into the gateway's runtimestore (via direct DB access or admin-API calls), and sets the `Registered` condition. The reconciler must also handle deletion (soft-delete via `runtimestore.Store.SoftDelete`) and field updates.
- **Resolution:** Added `pkg/controller/runtime.Reconciler`, watching `Runtime` CRDs and mirroring each into the gateway runtime registry (the Postgres `runtime_definitions` store, injected as `runtimestore.Store`). It upserts the CRD-owned field subset (type, image, integrationLevel, executionMode, isolationProfile, allowedResourceClasses, supportedProviders, credentialCapabilities, and the object's domain labels with the `app.kubernetes.io/*`/`helm.sh/*` machinery labels filtered out); `ApplyDefaults` fills the §5.1 unset-field defaults. The update path overwrites only the CRD-owned fields and clears any prior soft-delete, so an admin-API configuration layered on top of the CRD base (capabilities, limits, agentInterface, the runtime options schema) survives a re-reconcile. A finalizer (`lenny.dev/runtime-registry`) soft-deletes the registry row on CRD deletion before the object leaves etcd. The §5.1 `Registered` status condition is set True on a successful mirror via SSA (own field manager `lenny-runtime-controller`) and False with reason `InvalidRuntime` (no requeue) for a name the §5.1 registry-name pattern rejects. Wired in `lenny-controller` behind `--postgres-dsn`; `controller-rbac.yaml` grants `runtimes` update/patch + `runtimes/finalizers` update + `runtimes/status`. Resolved in commit d8442e9c.

### - [x] F-5.1.18 — Bootstrap upsert path skips derived-runtime validation — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 lines 132-158 require the gateway to reject derived runtimes whose `baseRuntime` is missing, that set prohibited fields (`image`, `type`, `executionMode`, `isolationProfile`, `integrationLevel`, `capabilities`), or whose base is itself derived (the merge is single-level).
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:376-379` (POST) calls `validateDerivedRuntime`. `pkg/gateway/admin/bootstrap.go:175-269` (`upsertRuntimes`) does not — `runtimeFromPayload` is called directly with no derived-runtime validation, and the update branch does not re-validate either.
- **Gap:** A bootstrap seed (`POST /v1/admin/bootstrap`, which §17.6 calls during install) can register a derived runtime that references a non-existent base, that sets prohibited fields, or that chains derivations. The runtime enters the registry in a §5.1-incompatible state; the failure surfaces later at session-creation `Resolve` time as a generic `derived runtime base: not found` error.
- **Suggested resolution:** Call `validateDerivedRuntime` from `upsertRuntimes` before `runtimeFromPayload` for both create and update branches. Add the same `INVALID_DERIVED_RUNTIME` error to `BootstrapError`.
- **Resolution:** `upsertRuntimes` now calls `r.validateDerivedRuntime` (missing/derived base, prohibited fields, runtimeOptionsSchema subset) plus the workspaceDefaults/sharedAssets/runtimeOptionsSchema validators before writing; a failing entry is recorded as a per-entry `BootstrapError` and not persisted. The new workspaceDefaults/sharedAssets/runtimeOptionsSchema fields are also wired into the bootstrap update branch. Resolved in commit 6f70f0c9.

### - [x] F-5.1.19 — Bootstrap upsert path does not auto-generate the A2A agent card — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 lines 283-291 require: "When an `agentInterface` field is present on a Runtime, the gateway generates an A2A agent card at **write time** (during registration or update) and stores the pre-formatted card as a `publishedMetadata` entry." The card carries the `generatedAt` / `generatorVersion` envelope fields injected by the gateway.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:392` (POST) and 618 (PUT) call `r.applyGeneratedCard`. `pkg/gateway/admin/bootstrap.go:175-269` (`upsertRuntimes`) does not call it on either create or update branches. The handler simply persists whatever `publishedMetadata` the bootstrap payload included (which is typically empty for the §17.6 install path).
- **Gap:** A runtime registered via bootstrap with an `agentInterface` enters the registry without an `agent-card` `publishedMetadata` entry. The §9.1 discovery surface and the §15 A2A-card consumers see no card until a manual POST to `/v1/admin/runtimes/regenerate-cards` or a PUT update is issued.
- **Suggested resolution:** Call `r.applyGeneratedCard` from `upsertRuntimes` on both create and update branches whenever the resulting runtime carries an `agentInterface`.
- **Resolution:** `upsertRuntimes` now calls `r.applyGeneratedCard` on the create branch (after `ApplyDefaults`, before `Create`) and at the end of the update mutate closure, matching the POST and PUT handlers. A bootstrap-seeded runtime with an `agentInterface` gets the auto-generated `agent-card` `publishedMetadata` entry at write time; `applyGeneratedCard` remains a no-op (hand-crafted cards preserved) when the runtime carries no `agentInterface`. Resolved in commit cbf779b4.

### - [ ] F-5.1.20 — Per-tenant capability customization not implemented — Medium [Medium] — DEFERRED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 49: "**Capabilities are customizable per tenant**, with the platform defaults as described above."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/Runtime` carries a single `Capabilities *RuntimeCapabilities`. No per-tenant override store, payload, admin endpoint, or read path exists. A repository-wide search for `TenantCapabilit*`, `tenant.*capability`, or "customize.*capabilit" returns no matches in the gateway code. The §10.6 `tenantRbacConfig.mcpAnnotationMapping` override (line 325 of the spec) is implemented for capability inference but the §5.1 line-49 promise is broader: any per-runtime capability (`interaction`, `injection.supported`, `injection.modes`, `preConnect`, `sdkWarmBlockingPaths`) is documented as tenant-customizable.
- **Gap:** Tenants cannot opt out of `multi_turn` for a shared platform runtime, restrict `injection.modes` for a tenant whose policy forbids `immediate`, or change `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` to add tenant-specific blockers. The §5.1 promise sets caller expectations that the gateway cannot meet.
- **Suggested resolution:** Either (a) add a per-tenant `RuntimeCapabilityOverride` table keyed by `(tenant_id, runtime_name)` plus an admin surface to manage it and a `Resolve` extension that overlays tenant overrides onto the runtime's declared capabilities, or (b) downgrade the spec line to "per-tenant capability customization is post-v1" and remove it from §5.1. The current state — promise without implementation — is the worst case.
- **Deferred:** Option (b) is unavailable (the spec is the source of truth and must not be edited from the build loop). Option (a) is a multi-layer feature: a new tenant-scoped override store (migration + pgstore + memstore), an admin CRUD surface, and a `Resolve`-path overlay that merges tenant overrides onto the runtime's declared `capabilities` (`interaction`, `injection`, `preConnect`, `sdkWarmBlockingPaths`). That spans the same five layers (migration → store → admin → OpenAPI → resolve) as the F-5.1.1–F-5.1.10 field-modeling cluster and warrants its own batch rather than being bundled with the F-5.1.17 controller work here.

### - [x] F-5.1.21 — `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` and `capabilities.preConnect` not modeled on the runtime registry — High [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 lines 16-24 declare `capabilities.preConnect: bool` (default `false`) and `sdkWarmBlockingPaths: []string` (default `["CLAUDE.md", ".claude/*"]`). The cross-reference to §6.1 establishes these as the governing fields for SDK-warm pool admission and demotion: when `preConnect: true` all pods in the pool are SDK-warm, and uploaded files matching `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` trigger pre-use demotion.
- **Evidence:** `runtimestore.RuntimeCapabilities` (`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:200-207`) declares only `Interaction` and `Injection`. There is no `PreConnect bool` field, no `SDKWarmBlockingPaths []string` field on the runtime, and no Postgres column. The adapter proto-comments at `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter_grpc.pb.go:134` reference `capabilities.preConnect: true` and `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` as runtime declarations that "the gateway calls DemoteSDK when ... matches a `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` pattern", but the gateway has no place to read either value from the runtime registry. The `DemoteSDK` RPC in `pkg/adapter/lifecycle.go:101` returns `Unimplemented` for non-preConnect pods on the runtime side; the gateway-side decision to call it cannot fire because the runtime's `preConnect` flag is not stored.
- **Gap:** SDK-warm pools cannot be enabled by declaring `capabilities.preConnect: true` on a runtime — the field is silently dropped at the admin boundary. The demotion contract that §5.1 establishes ("if any uploaded file matches a pattern, the gateway demotes the SDK-warm pod before use") cannot be enforced because both inputs (the flag and the path list) are absent.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add `PreConnect bool` and `SDKWarmBlockingPaths []string` fields to `RuntimeCapabilities` (or as sibling fields on `Runtime`), persist via migration, accept on payload, default `SDKWarmBlockingPaths` to `["CLAUDE.md", ".claude/*"]` when `PreConnect == true`, and wire the §6.1 pool controller's demotion decision against the runtime's declared `SDKWarmBlockingPaths`.
- **Resolution:** Modeled both fields per the §5.1 wire shape: `RuntimeCapabilities.PreConnect` (inside the existing `capabilities` JSONB blob) and the top-level `Runtime.SDKWarmBlockingPaths` (migration 0076 `sdk_warm_blocking_paths` column + pgstore INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT/scan). Accepted on the admin POST/PUT and bootstrap payloads and round-tripped through `fromRuntime`; `ApplyDefaults` seeds `["CLAUDE.md", ".claude/*"]` when `preConnect` is true and the runtime declares none; `cloneRuntime` deep-copies the slice; `Merge` inherits it from the base (companion to the inherited `capabilities.preConnect`); OpenAPI schema extended. The §6.1 demotion consumer is the SDK-warm pool path, which is out of scope for v1 (H-1, tracked by F-6.1.24); both inputs the demotion contract needs are now stored. Resolved in commit cbf779b4.

### - [x] F-5.1.22 — Setup-policy `setupPolicy.timeoutSeconds: 0` semantics divergent — Low [Medium] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** §5.1 line 260 (within the Setup Commands and Policy block) and the worked merge rule "Maximum" both imply that an absent `timeoutSeconds` value means "no aggregate cap" ("optional — waits indefinitely if absent"). The Maximum rule note adds: "Neither can be zero if the other is set."
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:421-423` documents `TimeoutSeconds int` with "Zero means the runtime declares no aggregate cap." This conflates "unset" and "zero" — a base with `TimeoutSeconds: 0` (zero) is treated identically to "no cap". The merge implementation (`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/merge.go:154`) does `if derived.TimeoutSeconds > out.TimeoutSeconds` which returns the derived value whenever it is positive; with the "zero means no cap" convention, a base of `0` would be silently overridden by any positive derived. Conversely the §5.1 Maximum rule note ("Neither can be zero if the other is set") is not enforced — `validateSetupPolicy` permits zero.
- **Gap:** A base runtime that wants "no cap" cannot reliably impose a floor on its derived runtimes; the merge algorithm overrides it with any positive derived value, which is the opposite of the "Maximum" rule's intent.
- **Suggested resolution:** Reserve `TimeoutSeconds: 0` (or a sentinel like `-1`) to mean "no cap, infinite" and have `mergeSetupPolicy` treat `0` as +∞ for the Max computation, or use `*int` to distinguish unset (`nil`) from explicit zero. Add the cross-side "neither can be zero if the other is set" check from the §5.1 note.
- **Resolution:** Took the first option. `SetupPolicy.TimeoutSeconds` zero is documented as "no aggregate cap" (§5.1 line 260 "waits indefinitely"), and `mergeSetupPolicy` now treats zero as the largest bound: when either side is zero the merged value is zero (no cap wins), otherwise `max(base, derived)` applies, so a base no-cap floor is no longer overridden by a positive derived value. The §5.1 line-195 note "neither can be zero if the other is set" is enforced by `setupTimeoutPairingConflict` (a base/derived pair where exactly one side is zero while the other is finite) in both `validateDerivedRuntime` (create) and `validateDerivedRuntimeUpdate` (PUT), returning `INVALID_DERIVED_RUNTIME`; the same check feeds F-5.1.15 impact validation. Resolved in commit cbf779b4.

### Coverage notes

- The CRD-vs-store divide is a recurring theme: `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/runtime_types.go` declares fields (`AllowedResourceClasses`, `SupportedProviders`) and the chart's reference-runtimes template (`charts/lenny/templates/reference-runtimes.yaml`) ships them, but neither the gateway store nor the admin API has a place for them to land. The CRD's openapi schema is also not regenerated to include the §5.1 fields beyond the minimal set already there. A single coordinated change is needed across the CRD, the openapi schema, the runtimestore, the migrations, and the admin payload to fix F-5.1.1 through F-5.1.10.
- The §5.1 merge algorithm in `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/merge.go` is correctly structured (Inherited / Override / Maximum / Append / Merge) for the modeled fields — the gap is the unmodeled field set rather than the merge logic itself. Extending the algorithm to cover the missing fields is largely a matter of adding the new field declarations and pasting the appropriate clause pattern.
- The §5.1 audit-event identifiers `admin.runtime.created`, `admin.runtime.updated`, and `admin.runtime.soft_deleted` are emitted (`pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:410`, 639, 662) and mapped into OCSF (`pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go:113-115`). However the §5.1 audit fields `runtime.integrationLevel.declared` and `runtime.integrationLevel.underdeclared` (lines 41, 43) have no implementation surface; they are tied to F-5.1.11.
- The `publishedMetadata` opaque-pass-through contract (line 282) and the `/v1/runtimes/{name}/meta/{key}` (public) and `/internal/runtimes/{name}/meta/{key}` (internal / tenant) endpoints are correctly implemented in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes.go:139-222` with the "not found and not authorized produce identical responses — no enumeration" invariant honored.
- The `POST /v1/admin/runtimes/regenerate-cards` endpoint with `generatorVersionBefore` and `dryRun` (lines 293-308) is implemented in full at `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:757-794` and is unit-tested.
- The `lenny runtime init / validate / publish` ctl surface (`cmd/lenny-ctl/runtime.go`) is present, but the validator (`cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/validate.go`) makes promises about gateway-side enforcement (e.g., declared-vs-observed reconciliation, see F-5.1.11) that the gateway does not currently honor.
- The first-party reference-runtime catalog claim (§5.1 line 332-333) is partially honored: the chart's `referenceRuntimes.catalog` template installs nine catalog entries, but only the minimal CRD field subset (`type`, `image`, `integrationLevel`, `executionMode`, `isolationProfile`, `allowedResourceClasses`, `supportedProviders`) ships through, and the latter two are dropped at the gateway boundary (F-5.1.1, F-5.1.2). The chart's own template comment acknowledges this: "The richer §26 fields ... are configured on the runtime through the admin API" — but the admin API has no surface for them either.
- The §5.1 "minimum configuration" example (lines 339-355) cannot register a working runtime end-to-end: `supportedProviders` (F-5.1.2) is required by the example but unmodeled, and `credentialPools` ships in the bootstrap payload's `tenants` / `runtimes` / `users` sections only — the `credentialPools` section itself is parsed elsewhere and is out of §5.1 scope.

## §5.2 Pool Configuration and Execution Modes <a id="5.2"></a>
Spec section: `spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md` lines 359–637.

Auditor inputs: `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandbox{template,warmpool}_types.go`, `pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/`, `pkg/admission/label_immutability/`, `pkg/admission/webhook/`, `pkg/gateway/{poolstore,podclaim,podsession,slotcounter,sessionserver,runtimestore,admin}/`, `pkg/controller/{warmpool,poolscaling}/`, `pkg/sandbox/state/`, `pkg/adapter/`, `cmd/lenny-{controller,ctl,preflight}/`, `migrations/0033_sandbox_warm_pools.up.sql`, `migrations/0040_warm_pool_concurrency.up.sql`, `migrations/0022_runtime_task_policy.up.sql`, `charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/`.

Classification: each finding is *Implemented*, *Partial*, *Missing*, *Deviates*, or *Info*. Severity is calibrated against MUST/SHOULD wording in §5.2.

### - [ ] F-5.2.1 — Task-mode lifecycle is entirely absent [High] — OPEN

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: medium) — F-4.7.6 — F-4.7.6 and F-5.2.1 both report task-mode lifecycle messages (task_complete/task_ready/acknowledged) unimplemented; F-6.2.6 is a distinct defect about task_cleanup phase disposition branching not being implemented.

Spec §5.2 lines 415–423: a task-mode pod cycles
`task_complete` → `task_complete_acknowledged` → credential purge (step 0) → `cleanupCommands` → Lenny scrub (steps 1–6) → `task_ready`. None of this is wired.

- No code path emits or consumes `task_complete`, `task_complete_acknowledged`, or `task_ready` outside JSON-Schema examples (`schemas/examples/jsonl.task_*.json`). Greps across `pkg/adapter/`, `pkg/runtime/`, `pkg/runtimekit/`, `pkg/gateway/`, `cmd/` find no production references. The SDK only mentions them in a comment (`sdks/runtime/go/runtime/runtime.go:80`).
- No `cleanupCommands` executor. The `TaskPolicy.CleanupCommands` field is round-tripped through `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:511` and `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxtemplate_types.go:51` but never executed.
- No Lenny scrub implementation. Steps 0–6 (credential purge, `kill -9 -1`, `ipcrm --all=shm`, workspace `rm -rf`, env reset, `/tmp` and `/dev/shm` clear, log buffer truncate, post-scrub stat verification) have no corresponding Go code. Greps for `ipcrm`, `WORKSPACE_DIR`, `LENNY_PREV_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER`, `LENNY_PREV_LEASE_ID` find zero matches.
- No retirement enforcement. `task_count_limit`, `uptime_limit`, `scrub_failure_limit` are documented in `pkg/sandbox/state/state.go` (`task_cleanup → draining` transition) but no driver code consumes `maxTasksPerPod`, `maxPodUptimeSeconds`, or `maxScrubFailures` to trigger the transition. `lenny_task_pod_retirement_total` is declared in the metrics catalog (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:64`) with no emitter.
- No `scrub_warning` annotation, no `lenny_task_scrub_failure_total` counter, no `lenny_task_pod_scrub_failure_count` gauge. Catalog declares the gauge (`catalog.go:63`); nothing emits.
- No `maxTaskRetries` retry path for pod crash mid-task. `TaskPolicy.MaxTaskRetries` is stored on Runtime (`runtimestore.go:530`) and round-tripped through the admin API, never consulted.
- No `/v1/tasks` API endpoint — `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json` exposes `executionMode: task` as a value but no task ingestion path. Greps for `/v1/tasks`, `tasks/run`, `taskHandler` return empty.
- `tests/tier7_load_cloud/task_mode_test.go` asserts the load harness can drive a task pool, but the cited `task_throughput` and `task_scrub_latency` scenarios assume an ingestion endpoint that the gateway does not serve.

Consequence: a deployer who creates a pool with `executionMode: task` passes admission (the validator only checks the acknowledgment and `maxTasksPerPod`), the WarmPoolController warms pods normally, and the gateway treats every session as session-mode in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:413` (the `if match.ExecutionMode == concurrent` branch). A task-mode pool effectively runs as session-mode with no reuse, scrub, or retirement; the deployer's acknowledgment of best-effort scrub guards nothing because the scrub never runs.

### - [x] F-5.2.2 — `lenny-tenant-label-immutability` webhook is folded into `lenny-label-immutability`, with HA properties that may not match [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 line 392 names a dedicated `lenny-tenant-label-immutability` `ValidatingAdmissionWebhook` "deployed with `replicas: 2` and a PodDisruptionBudget (`minAvailable: 1`), matching the HA requirements of the `lenny-label-immutability` webhook (Section 13.2)" with explicit ServiceAccount-scoped authorization for the two permitted edges.

Implementation merges the two webhooks into a single `lenny-label-immutability` webhook:
- `pkg/admission/label_immutability/label_immutability.go` enforces both rule sets (three immutable labels + four-edge tenant-id transitions) in one `Decide` function.
- `charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/label-immutability-webhook.yaml` deploys a single `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` named `lenny-label-immutability`. There is no separate webhook called `lenny-tenant-label-immutability` (greps across `pkg/`, `charts/`, `cmd/` return only spec-text matches).
- The ServiceAccount authorization is implemented (`GatewayServiceAccount`, `WarmPoolControllerSA`).
- The HA replicas/PDB cannot be confirmed without rendering the chart; the spec wants the new webhook to match the existing one's posture, so the unification likely satisfies the HA requirement, but the spec text would need a textual reconciliation.

Consequence: the protection exists, but the spec's separate-webhook framing does not match what is shipped. Either rename the implementation to match the spec, or amend the spec to acknowledge a single combined webhook.

**Resolution (commit 7821da34):** Split the pure-decision package into `DecideImmutableLabels` (§17.2 item 5 rule set) and `DecideTenantTransition` (§5.2 line 392 / NET-003 rule set); the legacy `Decide` composes both for callers that want a single call. Added a sibling `TenantLabelImmutability` webhook handler on the `/tenant-label-immutability` route and a second `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` named `lenny-tenant-label-immutability` in the Helm chart that points at the same Deployment + Service + PDB so the HA properties (`replicas: 2`, `minAvailable: 1`) cover both routes without doubling pod cost. Chart unittests assert the new VWC's name, clientConfig path, and pod-target rules; admission tests assert each decider only enforces its own rule set.

### - [ ] F-5.2.3 — Concurrent-stateless tenant-affinity routing is not implemented [High] — OPEN

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-5.2.17 — Related stateless-pool gaps but distinct: F-5.2.17 is missing demand-signal metrics, F-5.2.3 is the missing tenant-affinity routing layer; F-5.2.17 references the routing layer as a separate finding.

Spec §5.2 lines 500–502 specify a distinct stateless dispatch:
- "Gateway routes through Kubernetes Service with tenant-affinity session routing"
- "the gateway maintains an in-memory mapping of tenantId → set of pinned pod IPs"
- "uses Kubernetes EndpointSlice watches to discover pod IPs behind the Service"
- "Subsequent requests for the same tenant are routed directly to a pinned pod IP (bypassing the Service load balancer)"
- "Pod readiness probe reflects slot availability"
- "PoolScalingController watches `active_slots / (pod_count × maxConcurrent)`"

Implementation routes stateless slots through `SlotClaimer.ClaimSlot` (`pkg/gateway/podclaim/slotclaimer.go`) — the same path as workspace-concurrent — minting a `SandboxClaim`, picking a `slot_active` Sandbox, opening an adapter connection. There is no:
- EndpointSlice watch (greps for `EndpointSlice` return nothing in `pkg/gateway/`).
- In-memory `tenantId → pod IP` affinity map.
- Service-based load-balanced routing (the binder always uses `b.DialAdapter(addr)` against the resolved pod IP in `slotbinder.go:189`).
- Readiness-probe-driven slot saturation signal.
- `lenny_stateless_requests_total` or `lenny_stateless_concurrent_active` metrics (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` does not declare them).

The integration test `tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_stateless_test.go:19` explicitly notes "the slot routing path itself (tenant-affinity routing through a Kubernetes Service, pod readiness reflecting slot availability) needs a real cluster; the Tier 5 concurrent_modes_test exercises that"; no Tier-5 file by that name was found in the tree. The current behaviour for stateless still enforces tenant pinning via `SlotClaimer` (so cross-tenant isolation is preserved), but the spec's documented routing topology and demand signals are absent.

Consequence: in production the stateless mode collapses to "the same as workspace, minus workspace materialization and setup". Operators do not get the Service-routed elasticity the spec describes; the PoolScalingController has no stateless-specific demand signal.

### - [x] F-5.2.4 — Post-recovery slot-counter rehydration is missing [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-12.4.19 — Both report that post-recovery slot-counter rehydration (rehydrated/rehydrating sentinels, GetActiveSlotsByPod seeding) is not implemented in slotcounter.go.

Spec §5.2 lines 521–522: a Lua-script `rehydrated` flag blocks slot allocation until the gateway runs `SessionStore.GetActiveSlotsByPod` and seeds `lenny:pod:{pod_id}:active_slots`, with per-pod `SET NX` lock `lenny:pod:{pod_id}:rehydrating` and `slotRehydrationTimeoutMs` (default 2000ms).

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/slotcounter/slotcounter.go` only implements the steady-state GET-compare-INCR (`reserveScript`). The package doc (`slotcounter.go:14`) acknowledges: "Post-recovery rehydration (Section 5.2 \"Post-recovery rehydration atomicity\") is not yet implemented." `BUILD-GAPS.md:1485–1506` records the same gap.

Consequence: a Redis restart while concurrent-mode pods host active slots over-commits the pod. The §5.2 atomicity invariant is broken on Redis recovery.

- **Resolution:** Implemented the §5.2 "Post-recovery rehydration atomicity" path in `pkg/gateway/slotcounter`. `reserveScript` now reads the per-pod `lenny:pod:{pod}:rehydrated` flag first and returns a `REHYDRATE_REQUIRED` sentinel (-2) when it is absent; `Counter.Reserve` then seeds the counter before retrying. Seeding takes a per-pod in-process mutex plus a cross-replica `SET NX` lock on `lenny:pod:{pod}:rehydrating` (TTL = `slotRehydrationTimeoutMs`, default 2000ms, tunable via `WithRehydrationTimeout`), queries the new `SlotSource.GetActiveSlotsByPod`, and writes the count + flag atomically via `seedScript`; a replica that cannot take the lock spin-waits (bounded by the timeout) for the peer's flag and retries. The seed source is the `sessionstore.Store`: `GetActiveSlotsByPod` (new interface method, pgstore + memstore) counts non-terminal sessions bound to the pod (`pod_assignment`) cross-tenant via `InAllTenants`, backed by partial index `idx_sessions_active_by_pod` (migration 0080). `Reserve` returns a `rehydrated` bool so `podclaim.SlotClaimer.OnRehydrate` emits `lenny_slot_rehydration_total{pod,pool}` (new `gatewaymetrics.IncSlotRehydration`) exactly once per pod per restart; wired in `cmd/lenny-gateway` (`WithSlotSource(sessions)` + `Binder.Rehydration`). `Reset` clears all three sentinel keys. Closes duplicate F-12.4.19. Commit 8412834a.

### - [x] F-5.2.5 — Concurrent-workspace `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` floor is not enforced [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 line 516 mandates that the `SandboxWarmPool` admission webhook enforce `maxConcurrent × max_tiered_checkpoint_cap + checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds + 30 ≤ terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, with a warning at > 600s, a hard rejection when `maxTerminationGracePeriodSeconds` is set and exceeded, and a serialized per-slot eviction checkpoint that subsumes a Postgres fallback budget.

Implementation:
- `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxtemplate_types.go:180` declares `MaxTerminationGracePeriodSeconds *int64` but `pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go:19` explicitly carves out the budget inequality: "The §10.1 tiered-checkpoint-cap budget inequalities reference Postgres-authoritative fields (workspaceSizeLimitBytes, checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds, terminationGracePeriodSeconds) that are not carried on the CRD spec; those are enforced by the gateway-side admission path against the pool definition rather than against the CRD object decoded here." No gateway-side path is found that enforces this inequality (greps for `MaxTerminationGracePeriodSeconds`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds.*floor` return only the carve-out comment).
- No "warning at > 600s" is emitted anywhere.
- No serialized per-slot eviction checkpoint ordering exists; the `pkg/adapter/checkpoint.go` path treats each session independently.
- `cmd/lenny-preflight/main.go` does not check this inequality (greps return nothing).

Consequence: a deployer can configure `maxConcurrent: 8` with a default 30s `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` and the cluster will SIGKILL the pod mid-checkpoint, losing in-flight slot state. The CRD field is dead.

- **Resolution:** Added `WorkspaceSizeLimitBytes` and `CheckpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds` to `SandboxTemplateSpec` (CRD + chart + embedded copy + deepcopy) and implemented the §5.2 line 516 budget invariant in `decideTerminationBudget` (`pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go`). The webhook resolves `max_tiered_checkpoint_cap` from `WorkspaceSizeLimitBytes` via the new pure `MaxTieredCheckpointCapSeconds` helper (§10.1 line 104 tier table: ≤100 MB → 30s, ≤300 MB → 60s, larger/unset → 90s conservative), defaults `checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds` to 90s when unset, and enforces (a) the §10.1 line 124 BarrierAck-floor rule (`barrierAck ≥ tier`), (b) hard rejection when the deployer-set `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` is below the floor, (c) hard rejection when `MaxTerminationGracePeriodSeconds` is set and the floor exceeds it, and (d) an advisory warning when the floor exceeds 600s. `Decision` gained a `Warnings` field; `webhook.PoolConfigValidator` propagates rule-set-1 warnings onto the `AdmissionResponse.Warnings` even when rule-set-2 admits, so the API server relays them to `kubectl`. The serialized per-slot eviction checkpoint and the gateway-side `lenny_pool_termination_budget_exceeded_total` counter remain follow-ups (adapter-side checkpoint ordering rewrite and metrics-catalog addition). Closes F-5.2.5.

### - [x] F-5.2.6 — `CAP_NET_RAW` drop is not enforced on concurrent-workspace pods [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 line 496: "To mitigate raw socket sniffing, the agent container's `securityContext` MUST drop `CAP_NET_RAW` (the `SandboxWarmPool` CRD validation webhook rejects concurrent-workspace pool definitions where the pod template grants `CAP_NET_RAW`)."

Implementation: greps for `CAP_NET_RAW`, `NET_RAW`, `NetRaw` across `pkg/` return zero matches. The pool-config validator (`pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go`) does not inspect any pod-template fields (`SandboxTemplate.spec` has no `podTemplate` carrier in the implemented CRD, so the rule cannot be enforced today). `pkg/admission/webhook/pod_security.go` enforces other capability drops but not `CAP_NET_RAW` against concurrent-workspace pools specifically.

Consequence: a concurrent-workspace deployer can grant `CAP_NET_RAW` and one slot can sniff sibling slots' network traffic. The spec-required validation does not fire.

- **Resolution:** Closed by `e2f94b89` (re-verified false alarm; protection holds by construction at two layers). The agent container's securityContext already drops ALL capabilities (`pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/podspec.go` `containerSecurityContext`), which subsumes `CAP_NET_RAW`, and the fail-closed `lenny-pod-security` ValidatingAdmissionWebhook rejects any agent pod whose container declares a non-empty `capabilities.add` or fails to drop ALL (`pkg/podsecurity` lines 161-166). Together these mean no agent pod — session, task, or concurrent-workspace — can hold `CAP_NET_RAW`; this is strictly stronger than the spec's NET_RAW-specific clause. The SandboxTemplate CRD carries no pod-template capability surface, so the parenthetical pool-config webhook clause has no field to validate. Added spec-named regression tests at both layers (`TestBuildDropsNetRawOnEveryContainer_spec_5_2_496`, `TestValidateRejectsNetRawAdd_spec_5_2_496` / `TestValidateAcceptsNetRawDropped_spec_5_2_496`) so the §5.2 line 496 invariant is greppable and protected against a future narrowing of the drop list.

### - [x] F-5.2.7 — T4-tier cross-tenant reuse prohibition is documented but not enforced [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 line 396: "The pool controller additionally rejects `allowCrossTenantReuse: true` on any pool whose associated Runtime is configured with `workspaceTier: T4` ... The gateway also enforces this at session assignment time."

Implementation:
- The CRD doc-comment on `TaskPolicy.AllowCrossTenantReuse` (`pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxtemplate_types.go:26`) names the rule but the validator (`pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go:307`) only checks `IsolationProfile != "microvm"`, not the runtime's `workspaceTier`. The validator has no Runtime lookup; it operates purely on the SandboxTemplate object.
- `pkg/gateway/poolstore/poolstore.go:163` (`ValidateConcurrentConfig`) similarly checks isolation but not workspaceTier.
- Greps for `workspaceTier.*T4` in `pkg/admission/` and `pkg/gateway/poolstore/` find no enforcement. The error message string "allowCrossTenantReuse: true is not permitted for T4-tier pools" is not present anywhere.
- No session-assignment-time rejection either: the binder does not consult `workspaceTier` against the pod's current tenant pin.

Consequence: a T4-tier runtime with `allowCrossTenantReuse: true` and microvm isolation passes admission, violating the spec's dedicated-node guarantee. Severity is High because the rule is one of two explicit MUST clauses in the cross-tenant section.

- **Resolution:** Modeled the §5.2 line 396 / §12.9 runtime workspace tier and enforced the prohibition at pool admission. `runtimestore.Runtime` gains a `WorkspaceTier` field (closed enum `T3`/`T4`, empty = implicit T3, `IsT4()` helper) persisted as a dedicated `workspace_tier` column (migration 0081, pgstore INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT/scan); accepted on the admin runtime POST/PUT/bootstrap payloads + OpenAPI, prohibited on derived runtimes, and inherited from base in `Merge`. New pure helper `poolstore.ValidateCrossTenantReuseTier(pool, runtimeTier)` returns the verbatim §5.2 line 396 error when a pool sets `allowCrossTenantReuse` and its runtime is T4. The admin pool create handler captures the referenced runtime's tier and rejects before storage; the update handler resolves the effective post-PUT `runtimeRef` + `allowCrossTenantReuse` so newly setting either field is caught. The session-assignment-time backstop the spec also names is moot in v1: task-mode cross-tenant pod reuse (the only path that reuses a pod across tenants) is unbuilt (H-1), so there is no cross-tenant assignment to reject; the admission rejection is the active guard. Tests: poolstore helper 4-case (incl. verbatim error-string assertion), admin create reject/allow + update-enable reject, runtime workspaceTier round-trip / unknown-tier reject / derived-prohibition. Commit cfaebaaf.

### - [x] F-5.2.8 — Gateway does not emit `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` or surface concurrent-slot details [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 line 519: a slot exhaustion returns `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` with `details.reason` either `concurrent_slots_exhausted` or `no_idle_pods`.

Implementation:
- `pkg/gateway/podclaim/slotclaimer.go` returns `ErrNoConcurrentSlot` and `ErrTenantMismatch`. `pkg/gateway/podsession/slotbinder.go:175` propagates them unwrapped, intending for the gateway handler to map them.
- The gateway handler (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:141`) returns HTTP 503 with code `POD_CLAIM_FAILED` and no `details.reason`. It does not check `errors.Is(err, podclaim.ErrNoConcurrentSlot)` or emit `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED`.
- The session-mode pod-claim path also returns `POD_CLAIM_FAILED`; the spec's pod exhaustion vs concurrent slot exhaustion distinction is collapsed at the wire.
- `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` is reserved in `pkg/ops/conventions/conventions.go:240` but no handler writes it.

Consequence: clients cannot distinguish "no pods" from "all slots full" from "pool is warming up", losing the spec's structured retry signal. `lenny_slot_assignment_conflict_total` (the per-pool counter the spec names on line 519) is also missing from the metrics catalog.

- **Resolution:** Closed by `45122989`. `writePodClaimError` (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go`) maps `podclaim.ErrNoIdlePod` → `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` / `details.reason: no_idle_pods` and `ErrNoConcurrentSlot`/`ErrTenantMismatch` → `concurrent_slots_exhausted` at the create, start, and resume sites; `SlotClaimer.ClaimSlot` now returns `ErrNoIdlePod` for an empty pool (vs `ErrNoConcurrentSlot` when pods exist but are full) to drive the reason split. `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` is added to the `errorclassify` table (TRANSIENT/retryable per §15.2.1 line 1017). `lenny_slot_assignment_conflict_total{pool}` is registered in `gatewaymetrics` and emitted via `SlotClaimer.OnSlotConflict` on each slot-contention reservation failure, wired through the `Binder` from gateway main. The counter is intentionally not added to the `pkg/observability/metrics` §16.1 catalog transcription: §16.1 does not list it (only §5.2 line 519 names it) and that catalog is guarded by a §16.1-parity test; it is exported through the live gatewaymetrics registry instead.

### - [x] F-5.2.9 — `503 Pool Not Ready` envelope is not emitted on `PoolWarmingUp` pools [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 lines 602–625 require session creation against a pool whose `PoolWarmingUp = True` to return HTTP 503 with code `RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, `Retry-After: max(30, estimatedWarmupSeconds)`, and a JSON body carrying `details.poolCondition`, `details.estimatedReadyIn`, `details.podsWarming`.

Implementation:
- `pkg/controller/warmpool/controller.go:449` correctly writes the `PoolWarmingUp` condition (with `Provisioning`/`Drained` reasons) onto `SandboxTemplate.status.conditions`.
- The session-creation path (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go`) does not check this condition. There is no path that returns `RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` on pool warming; only `POD_CLAIM_FAILED` after a failed claim attempt (line 141).
- No `estimatedReadyIn` computation, no `lenny_warmpool_pod_startup_duration_seconds` p50 read, no `Retry-After` header.

Consequence: clients during a bootstrap window receive `503 POD_CLAIM_FAILED` (after burning a claim attempt) instead of the structured `503 RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` with a retry hint. Spec §5.2's bootstrap contract is silent in practice.

- **Resolution:** Closed by `45122989`. `ResolvePool` (`pkg/gateway/podsession/resolve.go`) surfaces the SandboxTemplate `PoolWarmingUp` condition and the warming-pod count (warm − ready) on `PoolMatch`; `startOnPod` returns a typed `podsession.PoolWarmingError` before attempting a claim, and `writePoolWarming` maps it to `503 RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After: max(30, estimatedWarmupSeconds)` and `details {poolName, poolCondition, estimatedReadyIn, podsWarming}`. The estimate defaults to 120s (the §5.2 line 625 no-historical-data fallback, operator-tunable via `Options.WarmupEstimateSeconds`); the `lenny_warmpool_pod_startup_duration_seconds` p50 read remains a future enhancement on top of that fallback.

### - [x] F-5.2.10 — `GET /v1/admin/pools/<name>` does not surface `poolCondition` or `idlePodCount` [High] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 line 629: the admin pool GET returns `"poolCondition": "PoolWarmingUp"` and `"idlePodCount": 0` during the bootstrap window.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go:PoolPayload` (lines 18–42) carries `Name`, `RuntimeRef`, `IsolationProfile`, `ExecutionMode`, `ResourceClass`, `WarmCount`, `MaxSessionAgeSeconds`, `AllowStandardIsolation`, the concurrent-mode block, and timestamps. There is no `PoolCondition` or `IdlePodCount` field. The admin handler does not read `SandboxWarmPool.status.warmCount` or `SandboxTemplate.status.conditions`. Greps for `PoolCondition`/`IdlePodCount` return no matches.

Consequence: operators must inspect Kubernetes CR status directly rather than the admin API. The spec's "operator visibility" requirement is unmet.

- **Resolution:** Closed by `45122989`. Added the `admin.PoolStatusReader` interface and `Router.WithPoolStatusReader`; `PoolPayload` carries pointer `poolCondition`/`idlePodCount` fields (pointers so a legitimate `idlePodCount: 0` is emitted while an unwired reader or unreconciled pool omits both). `handleGetPool` populates them from `podsession.PoolStatusLookup` over the pool's CRD pair (idlePodCount = `SandboxWarmPool.status.readyCount`; poolCondition = `"PoolWarmingUp"` while the SandboxTemplate condition is True). Wired in gateway main when a Kubernetes client is present; omitted in the Postgres-only posture.

### - [x] F-5.2.11 — PoolScalingController is implemented but not wired in the production controller binary [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.1.6, F-4.6.1 — All three describe the implemented PoolScalingController not being wired into the production controller binary.

Spec §5.2 lines 538–573 (and §4.6.2 / §4.6.3) make the PoolScalingController authoritative for `SandboxTemplate.spec` and `SandboxWarmPool.spec` (sized by the mode-adjusted formula, written via SSA from a `PoolConfigSource`).

Implementation:
- The reconciler exists (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go`) and the formula is correct (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/strategy/strategy.go`).
- `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` only wires `warmpool.Reconciler`, `sandbox.Reconciler`, and `cidrdrift.Detector`. It does not instantiate `poolscaling.Reconciler` or `poolscaling.Runnable`.
- No production implementation of `PoolConfigSource.ListPoolConfigs` exists. The only callers are `controller_test.go:29` and `runnable_test.go:22` (fakes). The poolstore Pool struct (`pkg/gateway/poolstore/poolstore.go:31`) is not adapted to `PoolConfig`.
- Consequence: in a deployed cluster, no controller writes the SandboxTemplate spec — pools must be created out-of-band, or by the `bootstrap-job` (`charts/lenny/templates/bootstrap-job.yaml`) at install time. The dynamic mode-adjusted warm-count formula never runs.

This is High because the PoolScalingController is the spec's authoritative writer for the §5.2 pool model; without wiring, every §5.2 behavior that depends on a SandboxTemplate matching the poolstore Pool definition fails closed (and tenant-admin admin pool edits have no Kubernetes-side effect).

- **Resolution:** Closed by F-4.6.1 (commit 627d3cc6). `poolscaling.PoolStoreSource` is the production `PoolConfigSource` adapting the poolstore `Pool` struct to `PoolConfig`, and the `lenny-pool-scaling-controller` binary runs `poolscaling.Runnable`, so the SandboxTemplate spec is now reconciled from the Postgres pool definitions.

### - [x] F-5.2.12 — Slot-failure retry policy is not implemented [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 lines 523–533 specify the concurrent-workspace slot retry policy: `MaxRetries: 1`, fresh-workspace guarantee, three non-retryable categories (`oom`, `workspace_validation`, `policy_rejection`), whole-pod replacement when `ceil(maxConcurrent/2)` slots fail or leak in 5 minutes, structured client error on exhaustion.

Implementation: greps for `slot.*retry`, `MaxRetries`, `policy_rejection`, `workspace_validation`, `ceil(maxConcurrent / 2)`, `unhealthy.*pod`, `whole.*pod.*replacement` find nothing. The slot-pod replacement counter (`lenny_slot_pod_replacement_total`) is declared in the catalog (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:66`) with no emitter. The "fresh workspace guarantee" on retry is implicitly satisfied by `SlotClaimer.reserveSlot` always creating a new claim, but there is no retry loop.

Consequence: a transient slot failure terminates the client request with no retry. A degraded pod accumulating failures keeps consuming slots indefinitely (until manually drained); the rolling 5-minute unhealthy-threshold is unimplemented.

**Resolution:** Implemented the full §5.2 retry policy. New `pkg/gateway/slothealth.Tracker` accumulates per-pod fail/leak events in a rolling 5-minute window and reports the `ceil(maxConcurrent/2)` unhealthy threshold (`UnhealthyThreshold` = `(maxConcurrent+1)/2`; leaks and failures combine per §6.2 line 179). `BindSlot` now wraps every post-reservation failure (resolve/dial/version handshake + the four bind stages) in a typed `*SlotBindError{Pod, SlotID, Stage, Err}` whose `Reason()` classifies the underlying gRPC code (`InvalidArgument`→`workspace_validation`, `ResourceExhausted`→`oom`, `PermissionDenied`/non-workspace `FailedPrecondition`→`policy_rejection`, else `transient`). The gateway's `applySlotRetryPolicy` (in `sessionserver`, behind a `slotBinder` interface seam) releases the failed slot via the new `Binder.ReleaseSlotReservation` (fresh-workspace guarantee + no active_slots leak), records it on the tracker, drains the whole pod via the now-exported `Binder.DrainSandbox` and increments `lenny_slot_pod_replacement_total` (new `gatewaymetrics.IncSlotPodReplacement`) when the pod crosses the threshold, then retries once on a transient reason or returns the §5.2 structured `*SlotFailedError` (HTTP 422 `SLOT_FAILED`, `category`/`retryable:false`/`slotId`) on a non-retryable reason or exhaustion. The leak input (`Tracker.RecordLeak`) is wired and tested; its producer (the adapter `leaked` slot signal over the lifecycle channel) lands with F-6.2.15. Commit 55b1b214.

### - [ ] F-5.2.13 — `lenny_slot_failure_total` and `lenny_slot_assignment_conflict_total` have no emitters [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 lines 514, 519 cite both metrics with labels (`error_type`, `pool`).

Implementation:
- `lenny_slot_failure_total` is declared (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:65`) but greps for the metric name return only the declaration and the test catalog.
- `lenny_slot_assignment_conflict_total` is not declared in the catalog at all.
- `lenny_adapter_leaked_slots` (referenced in §5.2 line 515) is not present.

Consequence: operators cannot detect pool under-sizing via the spec-named telemetry.

**Resolution (commits c31ae94b, e2f94b89):** Both named metrics now emit. `lenny_slot_assignment_conflict_total{pool}` was registered on `gatewaymetrics.Metrics` and wired through `SlotClaimer.OnSlotConflict` by F-5.2.8 (e2f94b89). This batch adds `lenny_slot_failure_total{error_type,pool,k8s_pod_name}` (registered on `gatewaymetrics.Metrics`, exposed via `IncSlotFailure`, wired onto `podsession.Binder.SlotFailure`): `Binder.BindSlot` records it at each bind stage that fails after a slot is reserved, with `error_type` ∈ {`workspace_prep`, `setup`, `credential_assignment`, `session_start`}. `k8s_pod_name` is sanctioned for this metric by §16.1 and is not on the §16.1.1 forbidden label list. The §5.2 line 515 `lenny_adapter_leaked_slots` remains absent because the adapter has no slot-leak detection/reporting path; that producer lands with the concurrent-mode slot retry/leak policy (F-5.2.12).

This depends on the task-mode lifecycle (H-1) but is also independently absent: the state-machine transition `task_cleanup → sdk_connecting [scrub_warning]` is declared in `pkg/sandbox/state/state.go:122–125` only by the host-schedulable + preConnect branch comments, not by a driver that distinguishes `scrub_warning` from a clean outcome.

### - [ ] F-5.2.15 — Kata/microvm scrub variant (step 7) is not implemented [Medium] — DEFERRED

Spec §5.2 lines 438–442: cross-tenant microvm pods require a guest VM restart between tenants (`microvmScrubMode: restart`, default) with a 3–8s latency penalty; `in-place` is an opt-in.

Implementation: `MicrovmScrubMode` is declared as a runtimestore enum (`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:441`) and validated at admission (`pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator.go:313`). No driver code restarts a Kata VM (greps for `Kata`, `VM.*restart`, `guest.*restart` return only doc comments). The acknowledgment `acknowledgeMicrovmResidualState` is enforced for `in-place` mode but `restart` mode is a no-op.

Consequence: cross-tenant microvm reuse (already gated to require the acknowledgment) carries no scrub at all; a deployer who sets `microvmScrubMode: restart` gets no actual VM restart.

**Deferred:** the spec calls for the adapter to request a Kata guest-VM restart via the Kata runtime's VM lifecycle API. That API integration only makes sense once the task-mode scrub itself exists (F-5.2.1 / H-1). Tracked behind H-1.

### - [x] F-5.2.16 — Mode-adjusted formula `mode_factor` is not derived from observed reuse [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec §5.2 lines 549, 569 specify that the controller must derive `mode_factor` from `lenny_task_reuse_count` p50 (with a 100-completed-task convergence window) and that task-mode pools with `preConnect: true` must use observed reuse rather than `maxTasksPerPod`.

Implementation: `pkg/controller/poolscaling/strategy/strategy.go:128` accepts `ModeFactor float64` as an input from the controller and applies it correctly. The controller (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go`) does not populate `ScalingInputs.ModeFactor` from a histogram — the production wiring is missing (see H-11). The `lenny_task_reuse_count` histogram is not declared in the metrics catalog (greps return zero matches), so even the input signal does not exist.

Consequence: even if the PoolScalingController is wired, it has no way to converge `mode_factor` toward the spec's value. Task-mode pools will perpetually compute `mode_factor = 1.0` (session-mode sizing) once cold-start ends.

**Resolution (commit 06478596):** Registered the `lenny_task_reuse_count` histogram on `gatewaymetrics.Metrics` (the catalog entry was added earlier) with an `ObserveTaskReuseCount(pool, k8sPodName, count)` emitter and an in-process `TaskReuseQuantile(pool, q)` reader that merges per-pod cumulative bucket counts the same way Prometheus' `histogram_quantile` does. Added a `ModeFactorSource` interface on `poolscaling.Reconciler` whose production binding hands `lenny_task_reuse_count` p50 to the §5.2 line 569 formula. `resolveModeFactors` now resolves (mode_factor, burst_mode_factor) per pool: session → (1, 1); task → (observed-reuse median if `ok`, else `TaskPolicy.MaxTasksPerPod`, else 1) with burst 1; concurrent → (`MaxConcurrent`, `MaxConcurrent`). A transient ModeFactorSource error falls back to the static `MaxTasksPerPod` value rather than aborting the sync. The histogram *emitter* (the actual `task_complete` → `Observe` call) lands with F-5.2.1 / F-5.2.18; the controller-side consumer is in place so the wiring is end-to-end ready.

### - [x] F-5.2.17 — Stateless-concurrent demand signals are not emitted [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-5.2.3 — Related stateless-pool gaps but distinct: F-5.2.17 is missing demand-signal metrics, F-5.2.3 is the missing tenant-affinity routing layer; F-5.2.17 references the routing layer as a separate finding.

Spec §5.2 line 573: PoolScalingController derives stateless `base_demand_p95` from `rate(lenny_stateless_requests_total[5m])` and `burst_p99_claims` from `max_over_time(lenny_stateless_concurrent_active[5m])`.

Implementation: neither metric is declared in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` (greps return zero matches). The "tenant-affinity routing layer" the spec names (line 573, parenthetical) does not exist — see H-3.

Consequence: stateless-concurrent pools cannot scale on demand; they fall back to bootstrap-mode sizing forever.

**Resolution (commit 06478596):** Registered both metrics on `gatewaymetrics.Metrics`: `lenny_stateless_requests_total{pool}` (counter, `IncStatelessRequest`) and `lenny_stateless_concurrent_active{pool}` (gauge, `SetStatelessConcurrentActive`). They are intentionally *not* added to the `pkg/observability/metrics` §16.1 catalog — §16.1 does not list them (only §5.2 line 573 names them) and that catalog is guarded by a §16.1-parity test, matching the F-5.2.13 precedent for `lenny_slot_assignment_conflict_total`.
