## §8.3 Delegation Policy and Lease <a id="8.3"></a>
Audit of `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md` §8.3 (lines 131-513) against the
implementation. Method: enumerate normative requirements, grep for the
named symbols / error codes / events that back them, classify each
unmet rule.

### Scope and Evidence Anchors

- **DelegationPolicy registry**: `pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/`
  - In-memory + Postgres-backed `Store` interface, `Validate`,
    `ApplyDefaults`, soft-delete.
  - Wire payload: `pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go`.
  - Tag-matched `Evaluate(Candidate) bool`:
    `pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/evaluate.go`.
- **Delegation lease math**: `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go` — pure
  `LeaseSlice`, `ResolveMaxDepth`, `CheckDepth`, `ValidateChildSlice`.
- **Delegation service** (constructs child sessions):
  `pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go`.
- **`lenny/delegate_task` MCP handler**: `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`
  lines 916-1022.
- **PreExportMaterialization scan**: `pkg/gateway/interceptor/export.go`.
- **§8.6 extension control plane (related)**:
  `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go`.
- **Audit catalog**: `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go`.
- **Opsevents catalog**: `pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go`.

The §8.3 `DelegationPolicy` admin CRUD, the `EXPORT_SCAN_REQUIRES_INTERCEPTOR`
admission check, the runtime-dependents deletion guard, and the
`delegation_policy.export_scan_weakened` / `_strengthened` events are
present and tested. Most of the other §8.3 normative rules — the
`Evaluate` call at delegation time, the lease record, content-policy and
cooldown enforcement, and a large fraction of the audit events — are not
wired through the `lenny/delegate_task` request path.

---

### Findings

#### 8.3-H1 — `DelegationPolicy.Evaluate` is never invoked at delegation time

§8.3 makes the named `DelegationPolicy` the authoritative target-allow
list (`«allowedRuntimes», «allowedConnectors», «allowedPools» fields are
replaced by named DelegationPolicy resources with tag-based matching
evaluated at delegation time»`, line 135; `«policy is re-evaluated on
each delegate_task call using the pool's live labels at the moment of
that call»`, line 199). The pure evaluator is implemented at
`pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/evaluate.go:52`
(`DelegationPolicy.Evaluate`) and unit-tested, but no production caller
invokes it. Grep across the repo finds zero non-test callers:

```
$ grep -rn "\.Evaluate(" pkg/gateway/mcptools pkg/gateway/delegation
(no matches)
```

The `lenny/delegate_task` handler
(`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:921-1021`) performs §10.6 environment
scoping, runs the PreDelegation interceptor, and calls
`delegation.Service.Delegate`. `Service.Delegate`
(`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go:156-232`) does cycle detection, an
isolation-monotonicity check, and a depth check, but reads neither
`Runtime.DelegationPolicyRef` nor the resolved `DelegationPolicy` —
neither `delegationpolicystore` nor any pool label set is wired into
the call. The `delegationPolicies` store is present on the admin
router only. Effect: a delegation target outside the runtime's
`delegationPolicyRef` allow-list is still admitted as long as it is in
the caller's environment scope. The default-deny posture documented in
the package comment (`«the default is deny»`, evaluate.go:50) is not
enforced.

#### 8.3-H2 — Runtime `delegationPolicyRef` is stored but ignored

`runtimestore.Runtime.DelegationPolicyRef` exists and is set by
`POST /v1/admin/runtimes`
(`pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes.go:56`, line 111), and the derived/base
merge prefers the derived value when set
(`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/merge.go:66-68`). Nothing reads it at
delegation time: there is no resolver in
`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go` that takes the parent's runtime's
`delegationPolicyRef`, intersects it with a derived runtime policy, and
evaluates the candidate target. The §8.3 "Two policy levels"
(line 192) and `«Effective policy = base_policy ∩ derived_policy»`
(line 197) rules are therefore unimplemented.

#### 8.3-H3 — `contentPolicy.maxInputSize` is never enforced (no `INPUT_TOO_LARGE`)

§8.3 line 157: `«maxInputSize is a hard byte-size limit on
TaskSpec.input per delegation — delegations exceeding it are rejected
with INPUT_TOO_LARGE before pod allocation»`. `MaxInputSize` is stored
on the policy (`delegationpolicystore.go:54-55`) and validated to be
non-negative, but no caller compares any payload length against it.

```
$ grep -rn "INPUT_TOO_LARGE" pkg cmd
(no matches)
```

The `lenny/delegate_task` handler accepts a `taskInput` string and
passes it through the `PreDelegation` interceptor without any size
check. The `BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED`, `INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, and other §8.3
error codes are absent from `pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go`
(only `INTERCEPTOR_COOLDOWN_IMMUTABLE` from §8.3 is registered, and
that one is also not produced anywhere).

#### 8.3-H4 — `interceptorRef` weakening cooldown not enforced at `delegate_task` time

§8.3 (line 218): during the cooldown window after a
`fail-closed → fail-open` transition (or a `scanExportedFiles: true →
false` flip, line 181) the gateway must reject every `delegate_task`
call whose effective `DelegationPolicy` references the affected
interceptor with `INTERCEPTOR_WEAKENING_COOLDOWN` (`TRANSIENT`,
HTTP 503). The admin handler does emit
`delegation_policy.export_scan_weakened` and tags it with
`cooldown_seconds: 60`
(`pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go:130-146`), but the in-line
package comment makes the gap explicit:

```
// The cooldown enforcement at `delegate_task` time (rejecting with
// INTERCEPTOR_WEAKENING_COOLDOWN during the window) is deferred — it
// belongs to the delegation request path.
//   pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go:127-129
```

Grep confirms no enforcement site exists:

```
$ grep -rn "INTERCEPTOR_WEAKENING_COOLDOWN" pkg cmd
(no matches)
```

`transition_ts` is also not persisted anywhere — it is computed only
inside the event detail block, so a gateway replica restart loses the
window. The `transition_ts` server-mint / admin-immutability /
meta-cooldown rules (line 220-224) are correspondingly unbacked.

#### 8.3-H5 — `interceptorRef` substitution and inheritance restrictiveness are unenforced

§8.3 line 183-188 fixes four identity-based rules for `interceptorRef`
restrictiveness on child leases:

1. same name — permitted,
2. null → non-null — permitted,
3. non-null → null — rejected with `CONTENT_POLICY_WEAKENING`,
4. different non-null — rejected with
   `CONTENT_POLICY_INTERCEPTOR_SUBSTITUTION`.

Neither `CONTENT_POLICY_WEAKENING` nor
`CONTENT_POLICY_INTERCEPTOR_SUBSTITUTION` is produced anywhere in
`pkg/`. The `Service.Delegate` request type
(`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go:33-59`) carries no policy-ref
field, so the parent's effective `interceptorRef` is not consulted on
the child path.

#### 8.3-H6 — Delegation lease record is not persisted; lease fields are absent from the session row

§8.3 (line 252-279) lists the full delegation-lease envelope —
`maxDepth`, `maxChildrenTotal`, `maxParallelChildren`, `maxTreeSize`,
`maxTokenBudget`, `delegationPolicyRef`, `maxDelegationPolicy`,
`minIsolationProfile`, `perChildRetryBudget`, `perChildMaxAge`,
`fileExportLimits`, `approvalMode`, `cascadeOnFailure`,
`credentialPropagation`, `allowedExternalEndpoints`,
`messagingRateLimit`, `maxTreeMemoryBytes`, `snapshotPolicyAtLease`,
`treeVisibility`, `experimentContext`, `tracingContext`. The
`sessionstore.Session` row (`pkg/gateway/sessionstore/sessionstore.go:28-137`)
persists only `TracingContext`, `ExperimentContext`,
`CascadeOnFailure`, `IsolationProfile`, and `ParentSessionID`. The
remaining lease fields have no Go representation in the session
store, so they cannot be recovered after a gateway restart, cannot
appear in `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`, and cannot be enforced by the
runtime code. The pure `lease.LeaseSlice` struct
(`pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go:24-47`) holds budgets in-process for
test purposes only — no Redis or Postgres writer exists.

The §8.3 sentence `«The snapshot is stored as snapshotted_pool_ids in
the lease record»` (line 208) has no schema or code to match —
`snapshotPolicyAtLease`, `snapshotted_pool_ids`, and the
"snapshot-once-at-root" behaviour are not implementable in the
current state.

#### 8.3-H7 — `maxDelegationPolicy` field absent from runtime types and enforcement

§8.3 (line 227-242) introduces `maxDelegationPolicy` as the
session-level policy cap intersected with `delegationPolicyRef`, with
strict monotonicity ("Child omits → inherit", "Child specifies a
non-null → must be at least as restrictive", error code
`DELEGATION_POLICY_WEAKENING`).

```
$ grep -rn "MaxDelegationPolicy\|maxDelegationPolicy" pkg cmd
pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/delegationpolicystore.go:77:   //
                          referenced by `delegationPolicyRef` and `maxDelegationPolicy`.
$ grep -rn "DELEGATION_POLICY_WEAKENING" pkg cmd
(no matches)
```

The only occurrence is a comment. The runtime type, the wire payload,
and the inheritance check are all missing.

#### 8.3-H8 — `treeVisibility` not present in lease type and not enforced

§8.3 (line 311-326) specifies `treeVisibility` ∈ {`full`,
`parent-and-self`, `self-only`}, the inheritance monotonicity rule
(child cannot widen), the `TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING` rejection, and
the `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE` compatibility
check with `messagingScope: siblings`. The implementation
acknowledges the gap in-line:

```
// The minimal gateway returns the full subtree (the §8.3 `treeVisibility`
// `parent-and-self` / `self-only` scoping is applied by the
// delegation-policy layer that ships with `lenny/delegate_task`).
//   pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:34-37
```

There is no `TreeVisibility` field on `sessionstore.Session`, no
`TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING` or
`TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE` constant, and no
scoping applied to `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree`.

#### 8.3-H9 — `allowSelfRecursion` inheritance not propagated onto child lease

§8.3 line 154 introduces `allowSelfRecursion` (default false) as the
third layer of the §8.2 cycle-detection AND gate, with the
monotonicity rule (line 328-334) "child may narrow `true → false` but
never widen `false → true`", surfacing `DELEGATION_POLICY_WEAKENING`
on violation. The field is stored on the `DelegationPolicy`
(`delegationpolicystore.go:88`) but `delegation.Service.Delegate`
never reads it: there is no parent-policy lookup, no inheritance
copy, and no `DELEGATION_POLICY_WEAKENING` error code emitted
anywhere. The `pkg/delegation/cycle` package consumes the spec's
three-layer AND gate against a static decision input but does not
take `allowSelfRecursion` from any per-session lease.

#### 8.3-H10 — Active-lease half of the `DelegationPolicy` deletion guard is missing

§8.3 (line 246) requires the deletion guard to reject when "(a) a
Runtime or derived runtime whose `delegationPolicyRef` names this
policy, or (b) **an active (non-terminal) delegation lease whose
`delegationPolicyRef` or `maxDelegationPolicy` names this policy**".
The runtime-side of the guard is implemented and tested
(`pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go:271-301` /
`_test.go:248-290`). The active-lease side is documented as deferred
in code:

```
// handleDeleteDelegationPolicy implements DELETE per §8.3: the policy
// is soft-deleted unless an active runtime still references it, in
// which case the §8.3 deletion guard rejects the request. The
// active-lease half of the §8.3 guard is deferred — delegation leases
// are not enumerable from the admin Router.
//   pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go:304-308
```

Because finding 8.3-H6 (no lease persistence) is unresolved, the
active-lease guard cannot be wired today. A delete during an active
session that references the policy via `delegationPolicyRef` would
succeed silently and yield the "dangling reference" failure mode the
guard exists to prevent.

#### 8.3-H11 — Per-file export scan path is not wired to `delegate_task`

The pure interceptor primitive
`interceptor.RunPreExportMaterialization`
(`pkg/gateway/interceptor/export.go:137-156`) is implemented with the
per-file size ceiling, REJECT short-circuit, and MODIFY rewrite
behavior the §8.3 file-scan rules demand. The §8.7 caller never
invokes it. The file acknowledges:

```
// SEAM — export-path wiring is a follow-on. The §8.7 delegation
// file-export materialization path (fileExport glob resolution,
// parent-pod file fetch, child-workspace persistence) is not yet built:
// delegation.Service.Delegate creates the child session but does not
// materialize exported files, and delegate_task carries no fileExport
// field.
//   pkg/gateway/interceptor/export.go:98-104
```

Concretely, `scanExportedFiles` admission control is fully tested at
the admin layer (rule 1 of §8.3, the
`EXPORT_SCAN_REQUIRES_INTERCEPTOR` check is implemented and verified
in `delegation_policies_test.go:90-102` and 200-215), but no
delegation request ever reaches the scan code. The
`EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_REJECTED`, `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_SIZE_EXCEEDED`, and
`EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE` paths therefore cannot fire on a real
delegation.

#### 8.3-H12 — Budget reservation Lua script and per-tree budget keys do not exist

§8.3 (line 358-431) is normative on the atomic reservation /
return model: a single `budget_reserve.lua` operating on six
counters (token budget, parent usage, tree size, `childrenTotal`,
`parallelChildren`, tree memory) with the documented hash-tag
convention `{root_session_id}:dlg:*`, a partner `budget_return.lua`,
`BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED` sentinel-key detection, and TTL-based
defense-in-depth. Findings:

- No `.lua` file exists in the repo (`find . -name "*.lua"`
  returns nothing).
- No Redis-backed delegation budget store exists — there is no
  `DelegationBudgetStore` interface or pgstore equivalent.
- The §8.6 `BudgetSource` interface
  (`pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:83-103`) covers the
  extension control plane only; its `MemoryBudgetSource` does not
  implement reserve / return atomicity for the six §8.3 counters.
- No error code `TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `TREE_SIZE_EXCEEDED`,
  `CHILDREN_TOTAL_EXCEEDED`, `PARALLEL_CHILDREN_EXCEEDED`,
  `TREE_MEMORY_EXCEEDED`, or `BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED` is produced from
  Go code (the proto file lists `TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` and
  `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` only). The §8.3 sentinel-key cascade-cancel
  flow (line 408-417) is therefore unbacked.

Effect: every `delegate_task` admits without checking any tree-wide
budget. The deepest delegation tree the test bed observes is
governed entirely by `MaxDepth` plus the cycle detector; budget
exhaustion does not exist at runtime.

#### 8.3-H13 — `delegation.created` / `delegation.completed` audit events are missing

§8.3 line 301 names `delegation.created` and `delegation.completed`
as the audit events that log `tracingContext` keys. The
audit catalog enumerates §16.7 events; neither is present:

```
$ grep -n "delegation\\.created\|delegation\\.completed" \
        pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go
pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go:32: EventDelegationCompleted = "delegation_completed"
```

The single related entry is `delegation_completed` (underscore) on
the §16.6 operational event stream, not the §11.7 audit event
`delegation.completed` (dot). `delegation.created` has no
equivalent. Consequence: per-delegation audit trail required by
§8.3 / §11.7 is not produced.

#### 8.3-M1 — `pool.isolation_warning` proactive audit is unimplemented

§8.3 (line 349-352, "Proactive pool-registration enforcement")
requires the gateway to evaluate all active `DelegationPolicy` rules
on `POST/PUT /v1/admin/pools` and emit `pool.isolation_warning` for
each rule where a more-restrictive parent could match while a
less-restrictive new pool could be a delegation target.

```
$ grep -rn "pool.isolation_warning\|pool\\.isolation_warning" pkg cmd
(no matches)
```

The `delegation.isolation_violation` (runtime path) event is wired
(`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:997`), but the pool-registration
warning path is absent. The `lenny-ctl policy audit-isolation` CLI
referenced in the spec deployer guidance (line 352) is also not
present.

#### 8.3-M2 — Discovery scoping for `lenny/discover_agents` ignores the calling session's delegation policy

§8.3 (line 244): `«lenny/discover_agents returns only targets
authorized by the calling session's effective delegation policy»`.
The current handler (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:818-861`)
filters by §10.6 environment access and runtime type, but not by
the caller's effective `delegationPolicyRef`. Because finding
8.3-H1 leaves the evaluator unwired anywhere, this would block on
the same change set.

#### 8.3-M3 — Snapshot policy / pool set not recorded on a lease

§8.3 (line 208): `«the gateway snapshots the set of matching pool
IDs for all DelegationPolicy resources in the effective policy
computation … at lease issuance time … records them in the
delegation lease … stored as snapshotted_pool_ids»`. There is no
lease record, no Postgres column, and no in-memory field
representing `snapshotPolicyAtLease` or the snapshotted pool IDs.
This is downstream of 8.3-H6 — adding the lease record is the
prerequisite.

#### 8.3-M4 — `tracingContext` validation rules are not enforced

§8.3 (line 288-298) tabulates the validation rules with explicit
error codes (`TRACING_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`,
`TRACING_CONTEXT_SENSITIVE_KEY`, `TRACING_CONTEXT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED`)
and limits (4 KB serialized, 128 B key, 256 B value, 32 entries,
sensitive-key blocklist, URL blocklist).

```
$ grep -rn "TRACING_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE\|TRACING_CONTEXT_SENSITIVE_KEY\|TRACING_CONTEXT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED" pkg cmd
(no matches)
```

The `delegation.Service` copies the parent's `tracingContext` onto
the child (`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go:308-317`), so a
parent-side validation pass is the natural enforcement point. None
exists; an oversized or sensitive-key context propagates without
diagnosis. The §8.3 audit/redaction rule (line 301, "log keys only —
values are redacted") is also unbacked because 8.3-H13 (no
`delegation.created` event) blocks it.

#### 8.3-M5 — Credential-propagation modes and cross-environment compatibility check are missing

§8.3 (line 437-490) defines `credentialPropagation` ∈ {`inherit`,
`independent`, `deny`}, per-hop semantics, the
`CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` check at cross-environment
delegation, and the origin-pool identity rule for multi-hop
`inherit` chains.

```
$ grep -rn "credentialPropagation\|CredentialPropagation\|CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_MISMATCH" pkg cmd
(no matches)
```

There is no `CredentialPropagation` field on the request type, on
the session row, or on the runtime. The §8.3 pre-claim availability
check is therefore not specific to the propagation mode. Because
8.3-H6 leaves no lease persistence layer, this can only be added in
the same pass that introduces the lease record.

#### 8.3-M6 — Delegation presets are not implemented

§8.3 (line 492-513) defines named delegation presets (`simple`,
`standard`, `orchestrator`) and the convention
`delegationLease: "standard"` (or `{preset: "standard", maxDepth: 2}`)
on a WorkspacePlan. There is no `delegationPresets` config struct,
no resolver in the lease package, and no schema field on the §14
WorkspacePlan code path.

```
$ grep -rn "delegationPresets" pkg cmd charts
(no matches)
```

Deployers cannot reference a preset by name; the `MaxDepth`
parameter passed through `delegate_task` is the only knob.

#### 8.3-M7 — `perChildRetryBudget`, `perChildMaxAge`, `fileExportLimits`, `messagingRateLimit`, `maxTreeMemoryBytes` are stored nowhere

These five fields are listed in the lease envelope (§8.3 line
252-279) and explained in detail at line 305-309 and 433. None has
a Go field on `sessionstore.Session`, `LeaseSlice`, or any
configuration struct; none of the related error codes exists
(`RATE_LIMITED` is defined elsewhere, but the inbound aggregate
limit specified at line 309 has no enforcement). Downstream of
8.3-H6.

#### 8.3-M8 — `defaultDelegationFraction` and minimum-budget threshold are not configured

§8.3 line 419: `«When lease_slice is omitted, the child receives
min(remaining_parent_budget, deployer_configurable_default_fraction).
The default fraction is 50% … configurable per environment via
defaultDelegationFraction (range: 0.1 to 1.0). If the remaining
budget is below a minimum usable threshold (configurable, default
10,000 tokens), the delegation is rejected.»`

```
$ grep -rn "defaultDelegationFraction\|delegation.minUsableBudget" pkg cmd charts
(no matches)
```

The Helm value, the env var, and the rejection at zero remaining
budget all need wiring. Downstream of 8.3-H12 (no budget
reservation path).

#### 8.3-M9 — Usage-quiescence step before budget return is absent

§8.3 (line 423-429) requires a usage-quiescence step before
`budget_return.lua`: wait for `FINAL_USAGE_REPORT` on the lifecycle
stream or for the configured timeout (`delegation.usageQuiescenceTimeoutSeconds`,
default 5 s), then emit `delegation.budget_return_usage_lag` on
timeout. None of these symbols appears in code. Downstream of
8.3-H12.

#### 8.3-M10 — `delegation.budget_return_usage_lag` metric and audit event are absent

§8.3 line 429: `«rate-limited to one per session and can be
monitored via lenny_delegation_budget_return_usage_lag_total»`. No
such metric in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`; no such
audit event in `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go`. Downstream of
8.3-M9 and 8.3-H13.

#### 8.3-L1 — `MaxDelegationPolicy` field marked as planned in code comment but no follow-on TODO

`pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/delegationpolicystore.go:76-78`
states the field is "referenced by `delegationPolicyRef` and
`maxDelegationPolicy`" but the type carries only `Name` for the
referent — there is no struct field for `maxDelegationPolicy` on
any consumer. The doc comment is therefore implicitly aspirational;
either add a `// SEAM` comment or rephrase pending lease persistence.

#### 8.3-L2 — `interceptorWeakeningCooldownSeconds` is a private `const` in admin only

`pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go:117`:
`const interceptorWeakeningCooldownSeconds = 60`. The §8.3 spec
says this is `gateway.interceptorWeakeningCooldownSeconds`,
cluster-scoped Helm config, admin-immutable (line 218). The
constant has no Helm value plumbing, no per-replica config refresh,
and no admin-API write attempt is rejected with
`INTERCEPTOR_COOLDOWN_IMMUTABLE` (the error code is registered in
`errorclassify.go:78` but never produced). The hard-coded value
also disregards the spec's documented `min 30 s / max 600 s`
clamp.

#### 8.3-L3 — Active-runtime list includes derived runtimes only implicitly

`delegationPolicyRuntimeDependents`
(`pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies.go:276-302`) lists every
runtime whose `delegationPolicyRef == name`. The spec sentence
"(a) a Runtime or derived runtime" (line 246) and the requirement
that the error envelope reports
`type: "runtime" | "derived_runtime"` separately are not honored —
all dependents are reported under `type: "runtime"`. Minor, but a
deployer hunting the blocking reference will not see which derived
runtime to update.

#### 8.3-L4 — Audit events for §8.3 transitions are not in the `audit.Catalog()` enumeration

`pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` is described as the typed
enumeration of §16.7 audit events. The §8.3-specific events
`delegation.isolation_violation`, `delegation_policy.export_scan_weakened`,
`delegation_policy.export_scan_strengthened`,
`delegation.export_scan_failed_open`,
`delegation.export_file_scan_rejected`,
`delegation.budget_keys_expired`,
`delegation.budget_return_usage_lag`,
`interceptor.weakening_cooldown_active`,
`pool.isolation_warning`, `delegation.created`,
`delegation.completed` are not registered (only
`gateway.cycle_detection_mode_changed`,
`gateway.allow_self_recursion_changed`,
`gateway.default_max_depth_changed`, and the §8.2
`delegation.self_recursion_allowed` / `cycle_warning` events from
the same area appear). An audit-catalog completeness lint would
miss them today.

#### 8.3-I1 — Effective-policy intersection (`base ∩ derived`) is described but no policy-level intersection helper exists

§8.3 (line 197) names the operation `Effective policy =
base_policy ∩ derived_policy`. The store layer carries no
intersection method on `DelegationPolicy`, and the only `Evaluate`
method (`evaluate.go:52`) takes a single policy and a candidate.
Wiring 8.3-H1 will need a small helper that yields the effective
rule list (the spec is implicit on how rule-list intersection
works; a candidate must satisfy both policies' allow-list and
neither deny).

#### 8.3-I2 — `lenny-ctl policy audit-isolation` CLI is documented but absent

§8.3 line 352 and §17.6 reference the on-demand audit CLI. The
`cmd/lenny-ctl` tree (not enumerated here) does not provide a
`policy audit-isolation` subcommand. Tracked as Info because the
behavior is informational; the runtime check (8.3-M1) is the
primary requirement.

#### 8.3-I3 — Postgres pgstore handles the §8.3 structural invariants but exposes no list-by-interceptor query

`delegationpolicystore/pgstore/pgstore.go` stores the policy body
as `jsonb` and runs `Validate` on every write. There is no index
or query to find all `DelegationPolicy` rows that reference a
given `interceptorRef` — the §8.3 deletion guard for interceptors
(line 225) and the `interceptor.fail_policy_weakened` audit event's
`affected_policy_names` enrichment (line 224) will require such a
query. Documented now so the gap is visible when those events are
wired.

---

### Summary

§8.3 covers a large surface area: the registry, the delegation-time
policy evaluator, the lease record, content-policy enforcement,
budget reservation, audit events, and presets. The implementation
covers a meaningful subset (the policy registry CRUD, the
`EXPORT_SCAN_REQUIRES_INTERCEPTOR` admission check, the
runtime-dependents deletion guard, the `scanExportedFiles`
weakened/strengthened admin events, the cycle detector, the
isolation-monotonicity check, the file-scan primitive, and the
extension control plane) but stops short of wiring the
delegation-time policy evaluation, the lease record, the budget
counters, and most of the §8.3 audit events. Findings 8.3-H1 (no
`Evaluate` caller), 8.3-H6 (no lease persistence), 8.3-H12 (no
budget reservation Lua), and 8.3-H13 (no per-delegation audit
events) are the load-bearing gaps the rest of the section
transitively depends on.

## §8.4 Approval Modes <a id="8.4"></a>
**Spec scope.** §8.4 of `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md` (lines 515–521) is a single normative table defining the closed enum `approvalMode` carried on the `delegation lease` (referenced by the example at §8.3 line 265 `"approvalMode": "policy"`). The table defines three legal values:

| Mode | Spec text (normative) |
| --- | --- |
| `policy` | Gateway auto-approves if request matches lease constraints |
| `approval` | Reserved — not implemented in v1. The `approval` value is accepted at policy registration time but the gateway treats it identically to `policy` mode in v1. Full implementation (dedicated approval API, approval timeout, concurrent-request handling, denial error code) is deferred to post-v1. |
| `deny` | Delegation not permitted |

The §8.4 surface is therefore three requirements: (a) `approvalMode` is a recognised lease field with that closed enum, (b) `policy` causes the gateway to auto-approve when the request matches lease/policy constraints, (c) `deny` causes every `delegate_task` under that lease to be rejected, and (d) `approval` is accepted at registration but behaviourally aliased to `policy` in v1.

Evidence collected from the implementation directories the audit was asked to cover (`pkg/delegation/`, `pkg/gateway/delegation/`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools/`, `pkg/gateway/interceptor/`, `pkg/elicitation/`, `pkg/gateway/inputwait/`) plus the related `delegationpolicystore` and `sessionstore` packages.

---

### Findings

### - [x] F-8.4.1 — `approvalMode` field is not modelled, parsed, or enforced anywhere in v1 [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-8.4.2, F-8.4.3 — All three concern approvalMode in §8.4 but describe distinct gaps: missing modeling/enforcement, missing ingest enum validation, and missing audit emission.

**Spec requirement.** §8.4 defines `approvalMode` as a closed enum on the delegation lease (`policy` | `approval` | `deny`). §8.3 line 265 shows it as a lease field (`"approvalMode": "policy"`). The values are normative — each one carries a distinct behavioural contract.

**Evidence — absent in the implementation.**

- Repo-wide search for `ApprovalMode`, `approval_mode`, or `approvalMode` (Go, proto, YAML, JSON) returns no matches outside the spec text itself (`spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:265`) and the spec-review log. Confirmed via:
  - `grep -rn "ApprovalMode\|approval_mode\|approvalMode" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/`.
- The §8.2 lease arithmetic struct, `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go:24` `LeaseSlice`, carries five numeric fields (`MaxTokenBudget`, `MaxChildrenTotal`, `MaxTreeSize`, `MaxParallelChildren`, `PerChildMaxAge`). There is no `ApprovalMode` field, no enum constants, and no JSON tag.
- The §8 delegation service, `pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go:33` `Request`, accepts only `ParentSessionID`, `RuntimeRef`, `PoolRef`, `IsolationProfile`, `MaxDepth`, and `UserID`. No `approvalMode` is plumbed through.
- The §8.5 `lenny/delegate_task` MCP handler at `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:920` declares its input schema as `{parentSessionId, runtimeRef, poolRef, maxDepth, taskInput}`. The handler never reads or validates an `approvalMode`.
- The `DelegationPolicy` resource in `pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/delegationpolicystore.go:75` carries `Rules`, `ContentPolicy`, and `AllowSelfRecursion` — but no `ApprovalMode`. Allow/deny on this resource is per-rule (per target), not a lease-level mode enum.
- `sessionstore.Session` at `pkg/gateway/sessionstore/sessionstore.go:28` records `CascadeOnFailure`, `TracingContext`, `ExperimentContext`, etc., but no `ApprovalMode`.

**Behavioural consequence.**

- A `delegate_task` call always falls through the same auto-approval path: §10.6 environment-scope check, §4 PreDelegation interceptor chain (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:961-981`), §8.2 cycle detection + §8.2.bis depth, §8.3 isolation monotonicity, then session row creation. The lease's declared `approvalMode` does not influence the path taken.
- A lease that should carry `approvalMode: "deny"` is not rejected. There is no early `DELEGATION_DENIED` error code emitted before pod allocation when the lease declares `deny` — the gateway will proceed exactly as if it were `policy`. The closed enum is unenforced at the wire boundary.
- A lease that carries the v1-reserved `approvalMode: "approval"` is also indistinguishable from `policy`. The spec mandates that the value be **accepted at policy registration time** (so that operators can author leases with `approval` today and have them aliased to `policy`), and that no implementation-related behaviour leak — but there is no acceptance/validation layer that recognises the field at all. An operator who types `approvalMode: "approval"` and an operator who types `approvalMode: "invalid_value"` are not distinguished.

**Why this is High.**

- The `deny` mode is the only platform-provided mechanism for an operator (e.g., on a low-trust tenant lease, or an opt-out runtime) to declare that this lease is non-delegating, distinct from omitting delegation tools or setting `maxDepth: 0`. With `deny` unimplemented, that capability is silently absent. A lease author who relies on `deny` to gate downstream delegation will discover that the gateway permits delegation regardless.
- This is a normative MUST (a closed enum with documented per-value behaviour); the cost of acceptance + a `policy ↔ approval` alias is small (one validated string field plus a switch), while the security surface — silent acceptance of `deny` — is exactly the failure mode `deny` is meant to defeat.

**Suggested remediation pointers (informational only — do not implement).**

- Add `ApprovalMode` as a string-typed field on the delegation lease record passed through `delegation.Service.Delegate`, with explicit enum constants in `pkg/delegation/lease` (`ApprovalModePolicy = "policy"`, `ApprovalModeApproval = "approval"`, `ApprovalModeDeny = "deny"`) and a validator that rejects unknown strings at admin-API ingest and at `delegate_task` time.
- At delegation evaluation, branch on the mode: `policy` and `approval` (per the v1 aliasing rule) take today's auto-approval path; `deny` short-circuits with a `DELEGATION_DENIED` (or equivalent §15.1 catalog) error before pod allocation and before the PreDelegation interceptor.
- Audit emission should record the effective `approvalMode` on the existing delegation audit event so operators can confirm that a v1 `approval` value is being treated as `policy`.

**Resolution:** Added `ApprovalMode` type + `ApprovalModePolicy`/`ApprovalModeApproval`/`ApprovalModeDeny` constants + `ValidateApprovalMode` + `EffectiveApprovalMode` (alias `approval → policy`) in `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go`. `delegation.Request.ApprovalMode` field threads through `Service.Delegate`, which validates the closed enum at the boundary and short-circuits `deny` with new `ErrDelegationDenied` before parent lookup. `lenny/delegate_task` MCP handler exposes the field on the input schema (enum-constrained to `policy`/`approval`/`deny`), maps `ErrDelegationDenied → DELEGATION_DENIED`, and maps `*lease.InvalidApprovalModeError → INVALID_LEASE_FIELD`.

---

### - [x] F-8.4.2 — No closed-enum validation at admin/API ingest for `approvalMode` [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-8.4.1, F-8.4.3 — All three concern approvalMode in §8.4 but describe distinct gaps: missing modeling/enforcement, missing ingest enum validation, and missing audit emission.

**Spec requirement.** §8.4 defines a closed enum. The §8.4 row for `approval` says it "is accepted at policy registration time but the gateway treats it identically to `policy` mode in v1." This implies a registration-time validator that **accepts** the three documented values and **rejects** any other string. The v1 alias for `approval → policy` is a behavioural choice on top of acceptance, not a substitute for it.

**Evidence.**

- The admin API for delegation policies (`pkg/gateway/admin/delegation_policies_test.go` and the corresponding `delegation_policies.go`) and the delegation policy store (`pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore/delegationpolicystore.go`) do not declare an enum or a validator for `approvalMode`. The `DelegationPolicy` Go struct has no such field (see 8.4-001).
- The lease-related JSON ingress at `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:920` declares no `approvalMode` field in its input schema, so a malformed value passes silently as "ignored extra property" rather than triggering an `INVALID_LEASE_FIELD` rejection.

**Behavioural consequence.** Operators authoring `delegationLease` JSON (e.g., in a Helm-side preset or the §15.1 admin API surface that wires `delegationLease` onto a Runtime's `defaultPoolConfig`) get no feedback when they typo `approvalMode: "polic"` or `approvalMode: "Approval"`. Downstream code never reads the field, so the typo behaves identically to a missing field — silent acceptance of the implicit default. This is a usability and configuration-correctness gap separate from 8.4-001.

**Why Medium.** The validator omission is the lighter half of 8.4-001 (acceptance + alias to `policy` without enforcement of `deny`). Even before `deny` is wired, a closed-enum validator would let operators discover authoring mistakes immediately rather than at the next security review.

**Resolution:** Closed alongside F-8.4.1. `ValidateApprovalMode` (in `pkg/delegation/lease`) is invoked at both the `lenny/delegate_task` MCP boundary (mapping a malformed value to `INVALID_LEASE_FIELD` with `details.field=approvalMode`, `details.value=<input>`) and at the `delegation.Service.Delegate` boundary as defence-in-depth. `Validate*` accepts only `""` / `"policy"` / `"approval"` / `"deny"` and returns `*lease.InvalidApprovalModeError` on any other input. The §8.5 input schema's `enum` keyword also documents the accepted values.

---

### - [x] F-8.4.3 — Audit emissions for delegation do not record the (would-be) `approvalMode` [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-8.4.1, F-8.4.2 — All three concern approvalMode in §8.4 but describe distinct gaps: missing modeling/enforcement, missing ingest enum validation, and missing audit emission.

**Spec requirement.** §8.4 establishes three distinct behavioural modes. The §8.6 lease-extension audit (line 743) records `approvalMode` for every extension request. By analogy, and as direct consequence of the §11.7 audit rule that every delegation decision be reconstructable from audit, every `delegation.created` / `delegation.rejected` event should record the effective `approvalMode` so an auditor can tell which mode authorised a given child session.

**Evidence.**

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:997` emits `delegation.isolation_violation` with a fixed detail map (`parentSessionId`, `runtimeRef`, `poolRef`, `parentProfile`, `childProfile`, `cross_environment`). There is no `approvalMode` field, and no other delegation-decision audit events are emitted from the `delegate_task` handler — the only success-path observability is the gRPC-level child-session creation.
- `pkg/delegation/cycle/cycle.go:18` emits `delegation.self_recursion_allowed` and `delegation.cycle_warning`, but again no `approvalMode`.
- Search for any audit event recording the approval mode (`grep -rn "approval_mode\|approvalMode" pkg/`) returns nothing.

**Behavioural consequence.** Even if 8.4-001 is fixed and `deny` begins rejecting deliveries, operators auditing the delegation chain cannot determine, after the fact, whether a given child session was approved by `policy` mode or by the v1-aliased `approval` mode. When the post-v1 `approval` mode actually ships, distinguishing the two in the audit log will be the only way to confirm a back-fill or staged rollout.

**Why Medium.** Audit lineage matters even before the dedicated `approval` API exists, because the spec's v1 contract is that `approval` is *accepted as input* and *recorded as having been input* even while the gateway processes it identically to `policy`. Without the audit field, the v1 aliasing is invisible.

**Resolution:** Closed alongside F-8.4.1. `delegation.spawned` audit detail now carries `approval_mode` (the declared value, with the empty default reported as `"policy"`) and `effective_approval_mode` (the post-alias value the gateway evaluated — `approval → policy`, `deny → deny`). `delegation.isolation_violation` detail also carries `approval_mode` so the post-incident replay can reconstruct the authorisation. `delegation.self_recursion_allowed` / `delegation.cycle_warning` continue to use the cycle-only attribution set introduced under F-8.5.9; the spawned event covers the per-hop approval lineage.

---

### Items checked and found correct (no finding)

- **No mention of a per-delegation `approvalMode` override at the `delegate_task` call site.** The §8.4 contract is set by the lease (which is itself resolved per §8.3 inheritance), not by the per-call `delegate_task` arguments. The MCP tool schema's omission of an override is consistent with the spec.
- **No client-facing "approval" message type or elicitation channel for delegations.** §8.4 explicitly defers the dedicated approval API to post-v1, so the absence of an elicitation-based approval surface (`pkg/elicitation`, `pkg/gateway/inputwait`) is **spec-conformant** for v1. `inputwait` is the §8.5 `lenny/request_input` registry only; `elicitation` carries §9.2 integrity primitives. Neither has any §8.4 contract to honour in v1.
- **The §4 PreDelegation interceptor chain is a content-policy gate, not a `policy`-mode approval gate.** It is correctly wired (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:961-981`) and rejects with `delegation rejected by policy` on `ActionReject`. This is the spec-authored hook the `policy` mode uses to enforce content rules; it does not need an `approvalMode` switch around it because the spec's `policy` mode is "auto-approve subject to constraints" — the PreDelegation phase enforces the constraints.

### Findings

### - [x] F-8.5.1 — `lenny/get_task_tree` omits per-node `runtimeRef` — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.9.5 — Both report the MCP get_task_tree treeNode omitting runtimeRef (and using sessionId instead of taskId) versus the correct REST TreeNode.

**Severity: High** (spec MUST violation — wire-schema deviation visible to all callers)

Spec §8.5 row for `get_task_tree`: "Each node includes `taskId`, `state`, and `runtimeRef`."

Implementation `treeNode` (mcptools.go:1112) carries only `sessionId`, `state`, `children`. The REST surface's `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:14` `TreeNode` correctly includes `RuntimeRef`. The MCP path returns a strictly smaller projection than REST, breaking the §15.2.1 semantic-equivalence rule for this overlapping operation.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1112-1116` (`treeNode` struct definition)
- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1423-1426` (`walk()` populates only the two fields)
- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:14-19` (REST `TreeNode` carries `RuntimeRef`)

**Resolution:** `treeNode` now carries `RuntimeRef` and `walk()` populates it from the session row; the §8.5 MCP projection matches the REST `/tree` shape. `TestGetTaskTreeIncludesRuntimeRef_spec_8_5_F_8_5_1` pins the contract.

### - [x] F-8.5.2 — `lenny/get_task_tree` ignores `treeVisibility` — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.9.2 — F-8.5.2 and F-8.9.2 both report that get_task_tree applies no treeVisibility filtering; F-13.5.8 covers the separate delegate-time messaging-scope rejection check.

**Severity: High** (security/correctness: spec MUST visibility boundary)

Spec §8.5 normatively defines `treeVisibility` as the visibility boundary on `get_task_tree` results, with three enum values (`full`, `parent-and-self`, `self-only`) and ties `messagingScope: siblings` reachability to a `full` value via the `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE` rejection (§8.3, §8.5 row).

The implementation returns the entire descendant subtree under the requested session and applies no visibility scoping. `buildTree()` (mcptools.go:1413-1421) and `walk()` (mcptools.go:1423-1433) just unconditionally walk all `byParent` children. No lease lookup, no `treeVisibility` field on the lease, no scoping at all. Consequently:

- A child whose lease declared `treeVisibility: self-only` can still enumerate siblings via the MCP tool.
- `treeVisibility` weakening (`TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING`) and `messagingScope`/`treeVisibility` compatibility (`TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE`) are not enforced anywhere in the delegation path either; no grep hits for either code.

The REST equivalent in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:30-37` openly acknowledges the omission ("the §8.3 `treeVisibility` `parent-and-self` / `self-only` scoping is applied by the delegation-policy layer that ships with `lenny/delegate_task`"), but the MCP handler that ships with `lenny/delegate_task` performs no such scoping either.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:345-367`, `:1413-1433`
- `grep "TREE_VISIBILITY" pkg/` returns no hits.

**Resolution:** Closed by `ad19c525`. `treeVisibility` is now persisted on
the session row (`session.TreeVisibility`, migration `0094`), and both the
MCP `lenny/get_task_tree` walker and the REST `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree`
handler route through `sessionstore.VisibleTree` to scope the response by
the caller's effective visibility: `full` roots at the tree apex (siblings
visible), `parent-and-self` returns parent+self, `self-only` returns self
alone. The delegation Service stamps the monotonically-resolved value onto
every child and rejects a widening child lease with `TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING`
(the `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE` half is in F-13.5.8,
also closed by the same commit).

The `lenny/delegate_task` schema at `mcptools.go` now carries both objects and `delegation.Request` carries `FileExport`/`FileExportLimits`/`LeaseSlice`. The residual `target` opacity rename and `task: TaskSpec` envelope remain tracked under F-8.2.1. This finding's stated gap (LeaseSlice or fileExport not surfaced) is resolved (verified at commit ab8275e2).

### - [x] F-8.5.5 — `lenny/await_children` is polling, not streaming, and does not yield `input_required` partials — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.8.5 — F-8.5.5 and F-8.8.5 both describe await_children not streaming input_required partials; F-11.3.4 is the narrower request_input_expired emission gap, related but a distinct defect.

**Severity: High** (spec MUST: streaming contract; §8.8 multi-child handling pattern broken)

Spec §8.5 row: "`lenny/await_children(child_ids, mode)` — Wait for multiple children (`all`, `any`, or `settled`). Streaming response — unblocks on `input_required`."

Spec §8.8 explicitly describes the streaming contract:

- "When a child enters `input_required` state, the parent's `lenny/await_children` call yields a partial result..."
- "A single `lenny/await_children` stream can yield multiple `input_required` partial results..."
- "The parent does **not** need to close and re-open the `await_children` call between partial results..."
- `request_input_expired` and `deadlock_detected` partial events are spec-defined for this stream.

Implementation (mcptools.go:422-481) polls `deps.Store.Get` every 25 ms (`awaitPollInterval`) until all/any/settled criteria are met, then returns one and only one JSON blob. It never observes `input_required`, never yields a partial event, never relays `request_input_expired`. The MCP transport in `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go` is itself "every method returns a single JSON-RPC response" (line 21), so the streaming contract has no transport hook either.

Consequence: a parent that has multiple delegated children, any of which transitions to `input_required`, will block forever (or until polling timeout via `ctx.Done()`) without ever learning the children are awaiting input. The §8.8 "multi-child `input_required` handling pattern" is not implementable through this MCP tool.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:422-481` (the for-loop poller)
- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1385-1411` (`collectChildResults` reads only terminal state, never `input_required`)
- `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:1-22` (single-response transport)

**Resolution:** `lenny/await_children` now yields an `input_required` partial. The §11.3 question `parts` are stored with the pending request (`inputwait.Registry.Register` + new `PendingDetailsForSession`), and the await poll loop, on every non-settled tick, returns `{partial:true, inputRequired:[{childId,state,requestId,parts}]}` (helper `collectInputRequired`) so the parent learns which children are blocked and can answer via `lenny/send_message` (inReplyTo), then re-await. The §8.8 line 951 `request_input_expired` event is already emitted on the parent's event stream (F-11.3.4, `mcptools.go` request_input timeout path). True gRPC/SSE multi-yield-without-reopen remains the documented post-v1 transport (`mcp/mcp.go`); the unary partial+re-await realizes the same unblock contract under the v1 transport. Closes the "blocks forever" defect (commit ab8275e2). Duplicate F-8.8.5 closed by the same change.

### - [x] F-8.5.6 — `lenny/send_message` does not return a `deliveryReceipt`, does not enforce `messagingScope`, does not rate-limit — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-7.2.10 — Both report lenny/send_message does not return the deliveryReceipt envelope; F-8.5.6 additionally covers messagingScope and rate-limit gaps but shares the receipt root cause.

**Severity: High** (spec MUST: §7.2/§15.4 normative envelope; §7.2 normative security boundary)

Spec §7.2 (line 231 onward) and §15.4 (line 1725, `delivery_receipt` schema) define the canonical synchronous return type and the policy gates:

- Return: `delivery_receipt` object with `messageId`, `status` (`delivered | queued | dropped | expired | rate_limited | error`), `reason`, `deliveredAt`, `queueDepth`.
- `messagingScope` MUST be evaluated and a `SCOPE_DENIED`/`scope_denied` outcome surfaced for targets outside scope.
- Inter-session messages from a sender whose `tenant_id` does not match the target's MUST be rejected with `CROSS_TENANT_MESSAGE_DENIED` (§7.2).
- `messagingRateLimit` per-session caps MUST be applied (§7.2, §8.3 `messagingRateLimit`).
- Pre-running, recovering, and terminal target states have distinct dispositions (`queued`, `dropped`, `expired`, error reasons).

Implementation (mcptools.go:275-343): the tool returns the raw response parts from `executor.Send`. There is no `deliveryReceipt` envelope. There is no `messagingScope` evaluation (no grep hits in mcptools or elicitation packages). There is no rate limiter. There is no `inReplyTo`-vs-non-`inReplyTo` distinction for `delivery: immediate` semantics. Cross-tenant validation collapses to the implicit "single-tenant adapter" assumption (`tenant := deps.TenantID`), which means the gateway cannot host multi-tenant MCP servers; for a multi-tenant transport this is a §7.2 normative bypass.

Consequence: from the MCP surface, a parent cannot programmatically distinguish a `delivered` message from a `queued` or `dropped` one; cannot detect overflow; cannot use durable-inbox semantics; cannot resume a `suspended` target via `delivery: immediate`. The §8.5 row also requires "Returns error for terminal targets; queues with TTL for recovering targets." The impl returns a raw error for terminal targets (good) but has no queueing path for recovering targets (`resume_pending`, `awaiting_client_action` are not modelled here).

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:275-343` (no deliveryReceipt construction)
- `grep -r "deliveryReceipt\|delivery_receipt" pkg/gateway/mcptools/ pkg/gateway/executor/` returns no hits
- `grep -r "CROSS_TENANT_MESSAGE_DENIED\|SCOPE_DENIED\|scope_denied\|messagingScope" pkg/gateway/mcptools/` returns no hits

**Resolution:** Closed by F-7.2.6 (same `lenny/send_message` governance fix; confirmed duplicate). The `deliveryReceipt` envelope was already added by F-7.2.10; F-7.2.6 wired the three remaining gates this finding names — `messagingScope` direct/siblings enforcement, the per-sender + per-target rate limits surfacing a `RATE_LIMITED` receipt, and the `CROSS_TENANT_MESSAGE_DENIED` guard. The `rate_limited` receipt status (previously unreachable) now fires from the limiter. The recovering-target queueing path (`resume_pending` / `awaiting_client_action` → queued-with-TTL) the §8.5 row also names lands with the §7.2 inbox + DLQ machinery (F-7.2.4); terminal targets are still rejected as before.

### - [x] F-8.5.7 — `lenny/discover_agents` does not filter by effective `DelegationPolicy` — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High** (spec MUST: §8.3 effective-policy filtering boundary)

Spec §8.3 line 244: "`lenny/discover_agents` returns only targets authorized by the calling session's effective delegation policy."

Implementation (mcptools.go:819-861) accepts no `parentSessionId`/session context at all, then filters the candidate set by (a) `Type=agent` (correctly skips `type: mcp`) and (b) §10.6 environment access. There is no consultation of the calling session's `delegationPolicyRef`, no consultation of the lease's effective `maxDelegationPolicy`, no tag-match evaluation against the parent's policy. A parent whose lease restricts targets to "read-only" runtimes will still see the full agent catalog in discovery.

Note that the §8.3 effective-policy resolution (Runtime `delegationPolicyRef` ∩ lease `maxDelegationPolicy` ∩ ancestral narrowing, with `snapshotPolicyAtLease` if set) requires the caller's session to be looked up. The MCP tool input schema has no `sessionId` parameter to feed that lookup.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:819-861` (no session lookup, no policy consultation)
- `grep -r "delegationPolicyRef\|maxDelegationPolicy\|DelegationPolicy" pkg/gateway/mcptools/` returns no hits

**Resolution (2e3e2279):** Added `delegation.Service.EffectiveDelegationPolicy(ctx, tenantID, sessionID)`, which resolves the §8.3 effective policy for a calling session — the policy named by the session's resolved runtime via `DelegationPolicyRef`, the same input the `Delegate` cycle-gate already reads. It returns `(policy, true, nil)` only when an active policy resolves and otherwise `(zero, false, nil)`, so an unresolved session/runtime/policy imposes no restriction (matching `Delegate`'s treatment of an absent ref). The `lenny/discover_agents` handler now accepts the caller `sessionId` (principal `SessionID` claim, with a dev/test transport-fallback arg), lists `type:agent` runtimes, applies the §10.6 environment filter, then narrows through the new `filterByEffectiveDelegationPolicy` helper: each surviving runtime is evaluated as a §8.3 `delegationpolicystore.Candidate{ID,Type,Labels}` against `DelegationPolicy.Evaluate`, so the existing tag-based allow/deny rule set (deny-overrides-allow, default-deny) governs visibility. Tier-1 `pkg/gateway/mcptools/discover_agents_policy_test.go` covers allow/deny matching, explicit-deny-over-allow precedence, no-effective-policy (returns all), unbound-caller fail-open, and policy resolution via the `sessionId` arg. The lease-level `maxDelegationPolicy` intersection and ancestral narrowing are not yet in either path; when they land in `Delegate` they extend the shared resolver.

Spec §11.7 event catalogue (line 62): `delegation.spawned` — "A child session is created via recursive delegation". ### - [x] F-8.5.9 — `lenny/delegate_task` does not emit the §8.2 three-layer cycle audit pair (`delegation.self_recursion_allowed`, `delegation.cycle_warning`) — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High** (spec MUST: §16.7 audit catalogue, §16.1 paired counter)

Spec §8.2 and §16.7 normatively require:

- `delegation.self_recursion_allowed` on every admitted self-recursive hop under `mode: enforce`.
- `delegation.cycle_warning` on every "would-have-blocked" hop under `mode: warn`, paired with the `lenny_delegation_would_have_blocked_total` counter (§16.1).

The `pkg/delegation/cycle/cycle.go` decision module computes the `Outcome` values (`OutcomeAdmitted`, `OutcomeWouldHaveBlocked`, `OutcomeRejected`) and `BlockedBy` field; the audit-catalog enum (`pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:47-48`) defines both event types. The gateway wiring, however, never calls either. The delegate_task handler (mcptools.go:982-988) calls `deps.Delegation.Delegate(...)`, and the Delegate path (`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go:191-195`) only routes `OutcomeRejected` into an error; `OutcomeAdmitted` with a true self-recursion and `OutcomeWouldHaveBlocked` are both treated identically (no error, no audit, no metric increment).

Evidence:

- `grep -r "EventDelegationSelfRecursionAllowed\|EventDelegationCycleWarning\|delegation\.self_recursion_allowed\|delegation\.cycle_warning" pkg/gateway/` returns no emission sites (only the catalog definition + OCSF mapping).
- `pkg/delegation/cycle/cycle.go:18-19` explicitly defers emission to the gateway: "audit emission ... lives in the gateway binary".

**Resolution:** `delegation.Service.recordCycleAudit` fires alongside `recordCycleDecision` for every self-recursive hop: an admitted hop under `enforce` mode emits `delegation.self_recursion_allowed` with the three-layer-gate inputs; a `would_have_blocked` outcome under `warn` mode emits `delegation.cycle_warning` with `blocked_by` and the full `would_have_blocked_layers` set. The non-self-recursive admission path stays silent so the audit log is not flooded. `TestDelegateEmitsSelfRecursionAllowedAudit_spec_8_2_F_8_5_9`, `TestDelegateEmitsCycleWarningAudit_spec_8_2_F_8_5_9`, and `TestDelegateNoCycleAuditWithoutSelfRecursion_spec_F_8_5_9` pin the matrix.

### - [x] F-8.5.10 — Error envelopes for §8.5 tool errors fall back to `INTERNAL_ERROR` — High [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: High** (spec MUST: §15.2.1 REST/MCP parity on `(category, retryable)` for the same code)

Spec §15.2.1 rule 3 (Shared error taxonomy): "MCP tool errors use the same `code` and `category` fields inside the MCP error response format, so clients can apply a single error-handling strategy regardless of API surface." Rule 5(d) requires identical `(category, retryable)` flags across surfaces.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:240-269` correctly extracts a `*ToolError`'s code when present; without a `*ToolError`, the wrapped error code defaults to `INTERNAL_ERROR`. Across all §8.5 tool handlers in mcptools.go (apart from `lenny/create_session` at lines 249/253), only one returns a `*ToolError`. Every other handler returns raw `errors.New` / `fmt.Errorf` with the spec code embedded in the message string:

- `mcptools.go:619-621` — `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` returned as `fmt.Errorf("REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT: ...")` (becomes `INTERNAL_ERROR`/`TRANSIENT`/retryable=true). Spec §15.1 says `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` is `TRANSIENT`/504 — category accidentally happens to match, but the canonical code is lost.
- `mcptools.go:805,809` — `ELICITATION_TIMEOUT` (not in spec error catalog but referenced by tests; fallback `INTERNAL_ERROR`).
- `mcptools.go:105` (elicitation.go) — `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWLISTED` returned in the message string.
- `mcptools.go:135` (elicitation.go) — `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED` returned in the message string. Spec §15.1 line 1085 says this is `PERMANENT/409` — the impl loses both the canonical code and the category.
- `mcptools.go:1006` — `ISOLATION_MONOTONICITY_VIOLATED` returned in the message string. Spec maps this to `PERMANENT`/422.
- `mcptools.go:957` — `target_not_in_scope` returned in the message string (and lowercased, no canonical mapping in the error code table).

In addition, `pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go:56-83` does not include any of these codes in the `table`. Even when the lenny code is recovered (which it isn't here), `Classify("REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT")` would fall through to `(CategoryTransient, true)`. Codes missing from the table:

`REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT`, `ELICITATION_TIMEOUT`, `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED`, `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`, `ISOLATION_MONOTONICITY_VIOLATED`, `TARGET_NOT_IN_SCOPE`, `CROSS_TENANT_MESSAGE_DENIED`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE`, `TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING`, `TARGET_NOT_AN_AGENT`, `TRACING_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`, `TRACING_CONTEXT_SENSITIVE_KEY`, `TRACING_CONTEXT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Consequence: the §15.2.1 parity contract is structurally broken for every §8.5 tool error path. REST callers and MCP callers see different `category` + `retryable` values for the same logical failure.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:240-269` (envelope dispatch)
- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:619,805,809,1006,957` (raw `fmt.Errorf` returns)
- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/elicitation.go:105,135`
- `pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go:56-83`

**Resolution:** Every §8.5 tool error path that previously embedded a code in the message string now returns `*mcp.ToolError` carrying the canonical lenny code, so the §15.2.1 envelope surfaces `(code, category, retryable)` with the parity contract intact:

- `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT`, `TARGET_NOT_AN_AGENT`, `TARGET_NOT_IN_SCOPE`, `ISOLATION_MONOTONICITY_VIOLATED`, `DELEGATION_PARENT_NO_USER` in `mcptools.go`.
- `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`, `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED` in `elicitation.go`.
- The service-layer `delegation.ErrTargetNotAgent` path in the delegate_task handler also surfaces `TARGET_NOT_AN_AGENT` (defence-in-depth for non-MCP callers).

`pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go` gains entries for `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT`, `TARGET_NOT_AN_AGENT`, `TARGET_NOT_IN_SCOPE`, `CROSS_TENANT_MESSAGE_DENIED`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE`, `TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING`, and `DELEGATION_PARENT_NO_USER` (the codes already in the table — `ELICITATION_TIMEOUT`, `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED`, `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`, `ISOLATION_MONOTONICITY_VIOLATED`, `TRACING_CONTEXT_*` — are unchanged). `TestDelegateTaskRejectsMCPTargetSurfacesEnvelopeCode_spec_15_2_1_F_8_5_10` and `TestRequestInputTimeoutSurfacesEnvelopeCode_spec_15_2_1_F_8_5_10` verify the envelope on the MCP transport.

### - [x] F-8.5.11 — `lenny/output` differs from spec — emits to event stream instead of to parent/client; requires `sessionId` not in spec schema — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Medium** (spec MUST schema; semantics need re-evaluation against §15.4.1)

Spec §8.5 line 533: "Emit output parts to the parent/client". Spec JSON Schema (line 544): required `output` only.

Implementation (mcptools.go:527-565):

- Input schema requires both `sessionId` AND `output`. The spec schema lists only `output` as required and has no `sessionId` property at all.
- Behaviour: publishes the `output` array to the session's own event bus as an `agent_output` event (mcptools.go:559-562). The spec says "to the parent/client". For a delegated child, the §15.4.1 contract (line 1891) is that `lenny/output` parts are concatenated with the child's `response.output` to form the complete task output the parent observes via `await_children` and the gateway's adapter concatenation. Publishing to the calling session's own event stream is observable to a caller that subscribes via `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`, but it does not deliver to "the parent" through the §8.2 virtual MCP child interface. The spec does not require the gateway's mechanism to be the calling session's own event stream; it just requires the parts to reach the parent.

The §15.4.1 expectation also says `lenny/output` parts are tracked so they are NOT duplicated when the child's terminal `response.output` arrives. No such reconciliation surface exists in the impl path.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:527-565`
- `spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1891` (`lenny/output` reconciliation contract)

**Resolution:** `lenny/output`'s InputSchema now matches the §8.5 line 544 spec — `required: ["output"]` only. `sessionId` remains as an optional transport-fallback property and is resolved from `authmw.FromContext(ctx).SessionID` first via the shared `callerSessionID` helper so the spec-compliant principal-bound path is preferred. The agent-output emission still publishes to the calling session's event stream; the §15.4.1 reconciliation contract with terminal `response.output` is the separate child→parent delivery work tracked elsewhere. A new `TestOutputSchemaMatchesSpec_spec_8_5_F_8_5_11` reads the schema off `tools/list` and asserts `sessionId ∉ required`.

### - [x] F-8.5.12 — `lenny/request_input` schema disagrees with spec — `parts` vs `prompt` — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity: Medium** (spec schema MUST: `request_input(parts)`; impl ships `prompt`)

Spec §8.5 row: "`lenny/request_input(parts)` — Block until answer arrives (replaces stdout `input_required`)". The argument type is `parts` (an `OutputPart[]`, matching the §15.4.1 protocol).

Implementation (mcptools.go:572-626): input schema is `{sessionId, requestId, prompt}` — a single string `prompt`, not a `parts` array. The `Prompt` is broadcast as the `prompt` field of the `request_input` event payload (mcptools.go:602-607). An agent that wants to send a structured question (e.g., a JSON schema, or a multi-part request with rich content) has no path.

The spec's `parts` typing is also load-bearing for the §8.8 "yields a partial result carrying the child's question" pattern — `await_children` is expected to surface the `parts` array, not a flat `prompt` string.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:572-626`
- `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:539` (`lenny/request_input(parts)`)
- `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:951-971` (await_children multi-child pattern uses `parts`)

**Resolution:** Schema now requires `parts` (an OutputPart[]) and drops `prompt` entirely; `sessionId` and `requestId` are optional. The handler decodes `parts: []json.RawMessage`, generates a `req_` prefixed id when the caller omits one, and the published `elicitation_request` event payload carries the structured `parts` array instead of the legacy flat `prompt` so rendering surfaces can re-use the same OutputPart visitor the runtime adapter applies. Verified by `TestRequestInputSchemaMatchesSpec_spec_8_5_F_8_5_12` and `TestRequestInputEmitsPartsOnEventStream_spec_8_5_F_8_5_12`.

- `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:577-613`

Verified by `TestMemoryWriteSchemaMatchesSpec_spec_8_5_F_8_5_14`, `TestMemoryQuerySchemaMatchesSpec_spec_8_5_F_8_5_14`, `TestMemoryWriteRejectsNonStringMetadata_spec_8_5_F_8_5_14`, and `TestMemoryQueryDefaultsLimitToTen_spec_8_5_F_8_5_14`.

### - [x] F-8.5.15 — `lenny/cancel_child` schema deviates from spec — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-8.5.19 — Both concern the cancel_child MCP tool but describe different defects: F-8.5.15 is the schema deviation (extra parentSessionId arg) while F-8.5.19 is the ignored cascadeOnFailure policy in cancelSubtree.

The §8.5 row says "Cancel a child (cascades to its descendants per policy)" — the spec also references `cancel_child` from §7.2 with the implicit caller being the parent. - `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:369-420`
- `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:531`

**Resolution:** Schema now requires only `childSessionId` per §8.5 line 531; `parentSessionId` drops out of `required` and is resolved from the calling principal via `callerSessionID`. The descendant authorization check still runs against the resolved parent id so cross-subtree cancellation remains blocked. Verified by `TestCancelChildSchemaMatchesSpec_spec_8_5_F_8_5_15`. The cascadeOnFailure-policy gap is tracked separately under F-8.5.19.

### - [x] F-8.5.19 — `cancel_child` cascade-on-failure policy not consulted — Medium [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-8.5.15 — Both concern the cancel_child MCP tool but describe different defects: F-8.5.15 is the schema deviation (extra parentSessionId arg) while F-8.5.19 is the ignored cascadeOnFailure policy in cancelSubtree.

**Severity: Medium** (spec MUST: §8.10 `cascadeOnFailure` per-lease setting)

Spec §8.5 row for `cancel_child`: "cascades to its descendants per policy". Spec §8.10 enumerates `cascadeOnFailure` modes (`cancel_all`, `await_completion`, `detach`).

Implementation (mcptools.go:1459-1497, `cancelSubtree`): unconditional subtree cancellation. Every non-terminal descendant is set to `cancelled` (cancelSubtree:1487-1493). The lease's `cascadeOnFailure` field is never consulted; an `await_completion` or `detach` policy will be ignored.

Evidence:

- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1459-1497`
- `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:1068` (`cascadeOnFailure` policy applies to all terminal transitions including manual cancel)

**Resolution:** `cancelSubtree` now respects each node's `CascadeOnFailure.Resolve()`. The explicit `lenny/cancel_child` target is always cancelled (per §8.5 row); descendants are queued only when the parent's resolved policy is `cancel_all`, so `await_completion` and `detach` siblings stay running. Terminal nodes' own cascades already ran when they settled so the traversal does not descend through them. `TestCancelChildTool` updated to the spec-compliant behavior; `TestCancelChildToolHonoursAwaitCompletion` and `TestCancelChildToolHonoursDetach` exercise the new policy branches.

---

### Summary

The §8.5 tool surface is broadly present — every tool the spec names is registered, and the wiring against the delegation, elicitation, memory, and session-store services is in place. The high-severity gaps fall into three clusters:

1. **Wire-schema and capability deviations** that change what callers can do: `get_task_tree` drops `runtimeRef` (F1) and ignores `treeVisibility` (F2); `delegate_task` lacks `LeaseSlice` and `fileExport` (F3) and never rejects `type: mcp` targets (F4); `await_children` is a poller, not a streaming partial-yielding tool (F5); `send_message` has no `deliveryReceipt`, no scope check, no rate limit (F6); `discover_agents` is not policy-scoped (F7).

2. **Audit emission gaps** that leave §11.7/§16.7 consumers blind: no `delegation.spawned`/`delegation.created`/`delegation.completed` on success (F8); no `delegation.self_recursion_allowed` or `delegation.cycle_warning` despite the cycle-decision module computing the outcomes (F9); the one event the impl does emit (`delegation.isolation_violation`) uses non-spec field names (F18).

3. **REST/MCP error-envelope parity is structurally broken** (F10): canonical codes are stuffed into raw error strings rather than `*ToolError`, and the `errorclassify` table is missing every §8.5-relevant code, so MCP callers see `INTERNAL_ERROR`/`TRANSIENT`/retryable=true for failures REST would surface as `PERMANENT`/`POLICY`/non-retryable.

The medium- and low-severity findings (F11–F25) cover input-schema deviations, missing `cascadeOnFailure` consultation, partial `taskResult` envelopes, and inconsistent application of the "add `sessionId`" pattern across session-bound tools.

**Spec sections newly identified as light or unstable that drove this audit:** §8.5 has a tightly defined tool table and JSON Schemas; §8.3 + §7.2 + §15.4 carry the bulk of the normative behaviour the §8.5 row delegates to. The audit found no spec-side gaps in §8.5 itself.

## §8.6 Lease Extension <a id="8.6"></a>
Audit of `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md` §8.6 (lines 625–743) against the implementation under `pkg/leaseextension/`, `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/`, `pkg/adapter/`, the proto in `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto`, the gateway wiring in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`, and §15.1 admin surface.

### Method

§8.6 normative requirements enumerated:

1. **Trigger** — the adapter calls `ExtendLease` when the LLM proxy rejects a request for budget exhaustion. The runtime never sees the call. On `GRANTED`/`PARTIALLY_GRANTED` the adapter retries the failed LLM call. On `CEILING_REACHED` the adapter MUST NOT retry the extension. On `REJECTED` the adapter propagates `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`.
2. **Request payload** — `extensions{additionalChildren, additionalTokenBudget, additionalMaxAge}`. Extendable fields: `maxChildrenTotal`, `maxParallelChildren`, `maxTokenBudget`, `maxTreeSize`, `perChildMaxAge`, `fileExportLimits`. Non-extendable: `maxDepth`, `minIsolationProfile`, `delegationPolicyRef`, `perChildRetryBudget`, `treeVisibility`, `allowSelfRecursion`.
3. **Hard ceilings** — effective max = `min(deployment max, tenant max if set)`; child cannot exceed parent's own lease limits.
4. **Configuration layering** — three layers (deployment / tenant / runtime) for `extensionApproval`, `coolOffSeconds`, `maxExtendableBudget`. Result capped by tenant max then deployment max.
5. **Approval modes** — `auto` and `elicitation` (default).
6. **Auto mode** — independent grants; rate limit (`maxAutoExtensionsPerMinute`) layered like the other fields; when exceeded fall back to `elicitation` and log `lease_extension_auto_rate_limit_exceeded`.
7. **Elicitation mode** — per-tree serialization, generic single elicitation, silent concurrent batching, success cool-off window auto-grants new requests, batch id groups requests, statuses `GRANTED|PARTIALLY_GRANTED|CEILING_REACHED|REJECTED`, adapter MUST NOT retry on `CEILING_REACHED`.
8. **User rejection** — flags requesting subtree `extension-denied`; persisted to `delegation_tree_budget` Postgres table keyed by `root_session_id` (with row-scoped `subtree_id` key); read before serving; in-flight requests re-check inside the same Postgres transaction under the row lock that increments counters; `cool_off_expiry` stored as `TIMESTAMPTZ` and compared against database `NOW()` (never local wall-clock); rejection cool-off (`rejectionCoolOffSeconds`, default 300) layered like the other fields.
9. **Admin API** — `DELETE /v1/admin/trees/{rootSessionId}/subtrees/{sessionId}/extension-denial` clears the flag.
10. **Scope** — extension applies to requesting session only; existing children unaffected; only new children benefit.
11. **Audit** — every request logged with: requesting session, requested amounts, approval mode, outcome, approver (gateway-auto or client), granted amount, effective max at request time, resulting new limits, batch id, service_instance_id, client_ip.

Each is mapped to the implementation below.

### - [x] F-8.6.1 — ExtendLease wire schema covers only one of three extendable dimensions [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §8.6 request payload (line 633–641) carries `additionalChildren`, `additionalTokenBudget`, `additionalMaxAge`. Extendable fields enumeration (line 643) includes `maxChildrenTotal`, `maxParallelChildren`, `maxTokenBudget`, `maxTreeSize`, `perChildMaxAge`, `fileExportLimits`.

**Implementation:** `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto:506–510` declares only `requested_tokens` (int64) and `requested_seconds` (int32). `granted_children`, `maxTreeSize`, `maxParallelChildren`, `fileExportLimits` have no wire representation. The gateway service in `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:244–248` invokes `leaseextension.Grant` against `requested_tokens` only; `requested_seconds` is in the proto but the handler never reads it (`grep RequestedSeconds pkg/gateway/leasecontrol` returns nothing). `pkg/leaseextension/leaseextension.go:50–62` is a single-dimension grant function.

**Effect:** The adapter cannot request, and the gateway cannot grant, `maxChildrenTotal`, `maxParallelChildren`, `maxTreeSize`, or `fileExportLimits` extensions. A runtime that exhausts its child or tree-size budget rather than its token budget has no extension path; the spec's `additionalChildren: 5` example does not translate to a valid wire message.

**Severity:** High — the wire and decision surface omit four of the six extendable dimensions §8.6 mandates.

**Files:** `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto:506–526`; `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter.pb.go:2440–2553`; `pkg/leaseextension/leaseextension.go:50–62`; `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:208–275`.

**Resolution (ea5a80a7):** `ExtendLeaseRequest`/`ExtendLeaseResponse` now carry `requested_children`/`requested_parallel_children`/`requested_tree_size` and a `FileExportLimitsDelta` (`requested_/granted_file_export_limits`), so all six §8.6 line 643 extendable dimensions are on the wire. `leasecontrol` models the extendable set as a `Dimensions` value and runs the `leaseextension.Grant` math over each via a single `allDims` enumeration; per-dimension effective ceilings and the §8.6 line 648 parent-lease caps, the §8.6 line 737-741 per-session scoping, and the line 743 audit fields extend to every dimension. The adapter convenience wrapper still sends only tokens because its production trigger (F-8.6.6, the LLM-proxy budget-rejection caller) remains a v1 follow-on; the wire and gateway grant all dimensions.

### - [x] F-8.6.2 — No approval-mode dispatch; the gateway acts as if `auto` mode is the only behavior [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §8.6 defines two approval modes (line 710–714): `auto` (independent grants, no elicitation/queuing/cool-off) and `elicitation` (default — serialized per task tree, single generic elicitation, silent concurrent batching, success cool-off window).

**Implementation:** `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:208` (`ExtendLease`) is one straight-line handler that always grants up to the ceiling (the `auto` behavior). There is no per-tree serialization, no elicitation dispatch, no batching of concurrent requests, no success cool-off window after approval, no `extensionApproval` field on `TreeConfig` (`pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/membudget.go:97–121` — the field is absent), and no resolver that picks between modes. `grep -rn "extensionApproval\|approval.*mode" pkg --include="*.go"` returns nothing in the lease-extension code.

**Effect:** The spec default is `elicitation`. The implementation effectively forces `auto`, bypassing the §8.6 user-consent loop entirely. A production deployment configured to require human approval cannot enforce it because the configuration knob does not exist and no elicitation path is wired.

**Severity:** High — the spec default approval mode is unimplemented; the human-in-the-loop budget gate §8.6 designs is absent.

**Files:** `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:208–275`; `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/membudget.go:97–121` (no approval-mode field).

**Resolution (d8efc623):** New `elicitCoordinator` (`elicitation.go`) implements the §8.6 line 714 elicitation flow: per-task-tree serialization, concurrent-request batching onto one generic elicitation (line 719), a success cool-off window after approval during which requests auto-grant without re-eliciting (lines 722-726), and subtree-denial persistence on rejection (line 729) via the new `BudgetSource.Deny`. `ExtendLease` now routes every elicitation-mode request through the coordinator's `gate` and **fails closed** (returns an error) when no `Elicitor` is wired, instead of the prior silent auto-grant. The `extensionApproval` knob was already resolved (`ResolveApprovalMode`) but unused; the gate now consumes it. The production `leaseElicitor` (`cmd/lenny-gateway/lease_elicit.go`) presents the prompt over the §9.2 interaction store + client event stream and blocks for the user's decision (PhaseApproved/PhaseDenied/PhaseResponded/dismiss), wired in `newGatewayControlServer`. The downstream budget-effect of an approved grant remains F-8.6.3; the adapter trigger that drives ExtendLease in production remains F-8.6.6.

### - [ ] F-8.6.3 — Extension grant has no effect on downstream budget enforcement [High] — DEFERRED

**Spec:** §8.6 (line 643) and the cross-link to §8.3 say the extension raises the tree's `maxTokenBudget` (and other dimensions) so subsequent LLM calls and child spawns are admitted under the new limits.

**Implementation:** `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:250–267` calls `s.budgets.ApplyGrant`, which raises `MemoryBudgetSource.memTree.currentBudget` (`pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/membudget.go:233–235`). No other package reads that counter — `grep -rn "CurrentTokenBudget\|currentBudget" pkg --include="*.go"` shows only the lease-extension package itself plus its tests. The actual `delegation lease` enforcement lives in `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go` and uses an entirely separate `LeaseSlice` struct that the leasecontrol grant never updates. The Redis-backed budget counters (referenced in §8.3) and the gateway delegation service (`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go`) consume neither `leasecontrol.TreeBudget` nor any post-grant state.

**Effect:** A `GRANTED` extension response gives the adapter permission to retry the LLM call, but the gateway's own budget accounting is unchanged. The next child-spawn or LLM-proxy decision still sees the pre-extension limit. The control plane is in place but does not actually extend any budget.

**Severity:** High — the round-trip succeeds but the budget side effect §8.6 promises does not occur on the gateway side.

**Files:** `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/leasecontrol.go:250–267`; `pkg/gateway/leasecontrol/membudget.go:223–237`; `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go`.
