## §8.9 Task Tree <a id="8.9"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/08_recursive-delegation.md` (lines 999–1011)
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

Section §8.9 is a short normative declaration: the gateway maintains a complete task tree, and each node tracks `session_id`, `generation`, `pod`, `state`, `lease`, `budget consumed`, and `failure history`. The supplementary contract surfaces that depend on the §8.9 tree appear across §8 (the `lenny/get_task_tree` MCP tool at lines 540, 615–623, the `treeUsage` rollup at lines 905–917, the `treeVisibility` filtering at lines 311–326), §15.1 (the `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree` REST endpoint), and §10.4 (`session_tree_archive` durability). The implementation reconstructs the tree topology on-demand by walking `sessions.ParentSessionID` lineage pointers (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go::handleTree`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go::buildTree`) and provides an in-memory `treearchive.Memory` keyed by `(tenant_id, root_session_id, node_session_id)` (`pkg/gateway/treearchive/treearchive.go`). The topology is correct under default visibility, cross-tenant isolation is enforced, the cycle guard is defensive. However, the per-node attributes the spec enumerates (`generation`, `pod`, `lease`, `budget consumed`, `failure history`) are nowhere materialized on the tree response; `treeVisibility` filtering (full / parent-and-self / self-only) is not implemented; the MCP `treeNode` schema omits `runtimeRef` and uses `sessionId` instead of `taskId`; the §8.10 `session_tree_archive` Postgres table is not implemented (the production gateway binary instantiates `treearchive.NewMemory()`, so all archive state is lost on gateway restart); the §11.2 / §8.3 tree-budget Redis counters (`maxTreeSize`, `maxTreeMemoryBytes`, `childrenTotal`, `parallelChildren`) are not wired (only the pure ValidateChildSlice arithmetic exists in `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go`); and the `treeUsage` aggregator that walks the tree to sum descendant usage is absent. Findings count: 4 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] F-8.9.1 — Per-node attributes (`generation`, `pod`, `lease`, `budget consumed`, `failure history`) are not tracked on the tree node [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Line 1010 — "Each node tracks: session_id, generation, pod, state, lease, budget consumed, failure history."
- **Evidence:**
  - The MCP tool's `treeNode` carries only `{sessionId, state, children}` (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1112-1116`).
  - The REST `TreeNode` carries `{sessionId, state, runtimeRef, children}` (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:14-19`). `runtimeRef` is the only spec-listed identity attribute, and it is present only on the REST surface.
  - `grep -rn "generation\|Generation" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionstore/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/api/v1/session/` returns no hits. There is no `generation` concept on the session row, the tree node, or the archive.
  - The session row's `IsolationProfile` and `PoolRef` (`pkg/gateway/sessionstore/sessionstore.go:50-69`) carry pod-identity-adjacent fields, but neither is projected into the tree response. `grep -rn "pod" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go` shows no pod-id surface on the tree.
  - There is no "lease consumed", "budget consumed", or "failure history" on either tree-node struct. `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go` defines a pure `LeaseSlice` validation primitive but never persists the consumed quantities; `Session.FailureClass` / `Session.FailureReason` are scalar single-cause fields (`sessionstore.go:38-46`) with no chronological history.
- **Gap:** Operators and parent agents cannot inspect a child's pod assignment, recovery generation, remaining lease, accumulated budget consumption, or prior retry / failure history from the §8.9 tree. The spec's per-node tracking promise is the foundation for the §8.10 bottom-up recovery decision, the §11.2 budget audit, and the §15.1 admin investigation surface; without those attributes, those downstream contracts cannot be served from the tree itself.
- **Suggested resolution:** Extend both `TreeNode` (REST) and `treeNode` (MCP) with the spec-named fields. Source `pod` from `Session.PoolRef` (or a stronger pod identity if one is tracked elsewhere), `lease` from the lease record persisted alongside the session, `budget consumed` from the Redis delegation counters keyed by `root_session_id`, and `failure history` from a new per-session retry / recovery audit. `generation` requires a new monotonic counter incremented on each recovery reattach.

**Resolution:** `sessionstore.ProjectNodeAttributes(Session)` builds a shared `NodeAttributes` projection (`generation` ← `RecoveryGeneration`, `pod` ← `PodAssignment`, `lease` ← the persisted `DelegationLease` granted ceiling, `failureHistory` ← `{RetryCount, FailureClass, FailureReason}` omitted when the node has neither retried nor failed) that both the REST `TreeNode` and the MCP `treeNode` now carry under an `attributes` field, keeping the two surfaces semantically equivalent per §15.2.1. The evidence was partly stale: `RecoveryGeneration` and `PodAssignment` already exist on the session row, so no new counter was required. Live budget-consumption accounting against the lease is the §8.3 treebudget Redis counter surfaced through the §8.8 usage rollup (F-8.9.4) and the §16 billing surface rather than this static projection; the `lease` field carries the granted ceiling the consumption is measured against. Tier-1 pins cover the projection (`pkg/gateway/sessionstore/node_attributes_test.go`), the REST handler (`TestTreeNodeAttributes_spec_8_9_1010`), and the MCP handler (`TestGetTaskTreeSurfacesNodeAttributes_spec_8_9_1010`). Committed in `93654b95`.

### - [x] F-8.9.2 — `treeVisibility` filtering (full / parent-and-self / self-only) is not implemented [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.5.2 — F-8.5.2 and F-8.9.2 both report that get_task_tree applies no treeVisibility filtering; F-13.5.8 covers the separate delegate-time messaging-scope rejection check.

- **Spec:** Lines 311–326 — `treeVisibility` controls the scope of the task tree visible via `lenny/get_task_tree`. Three values, ordered `full → parent-and-self → self-only`, default `"full"`. Line 540 ties this to the MCP tool: "Visibility is controlled by the `treeVisibility` field on the delegation lease". Line 623 — "Returns the task hierarchy visible to the calling session (scoped by `treeVisibility`)."
- **Evidence:**
  - `grep -rn "treeVisibility\|TreeVisibility\|VisibilityFull\|VisibilityParent\|VisibilitySelf" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/` returns one hit at `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:35` — a comment that acknowledges the `parent-and-self` / `self-only` scoping is "applied by the delegation-policy layer that ships with `lenny/delegate_task`" but no such filter exists.
  - The MCP `get_task_tree` handler at `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:345-367` reads the requested root, lists every session in the tenant, and builds the full subtree via `buildTree`. There is no lease lookup, no visibility resolution, no scope check against the caller's lease.
  - There is no field on the session row, the delegation lease structure, or the deps that records the caller's effective `treeVisibility`. The `lenny/delegate_task` tool at `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:920-1003` does not accept or persist a `treeVisibility` value.
- **Gap:** A low-trust child can call `lenny/get_task_tree` and observe its siblings, uncles, and the entire tree — there is no enforcement of the spec's `parent-and-self` or `self-only` narrowing. The spec also says (line 540) that `messagingScope: siblings` requires `treeVisibility: full`; with no `treeVisibility`, the compatibility check is moot, but the security boundary it is meant to enforce is also absent.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add `TreeVisibility` to the lease record (or the session row when leases are not persisted independently), default to `"full"`, enforce monotonicity on inheritance (per spec lines 313–319), and filter `buildTree`'s output to honor the caller's effective visibility. Add `TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING` and `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE` rejection codes on `lenny/delegate_task` at lease issuance.

**Resolution:** Closed by `ad19c525` (same root cause as F-8.5.2). `TreeVisibility`
is stored on the session row (the §4.2 line 161 lease-on-session-row design),
defaults to `full` via `OrDefault`, and inheritance/monotonicity is enforced
in `delegation.Service.Delegate` (`resolveChildTreeVisibility`: inherit when
absent, narrow-or-equal accepted, widen rejected with `TREE_VISIBILITY_WEAKENING`,
HTTP 422). `buildTree`/`buildTreeNode` honor the caller's effective visibility
via `sessionstore.VisibleTree`. The `TREE_VISIBILITY_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_MESSAGING_SCOPE`
rejection (siblings scope vs. non-full visibility) is wired under F-13.5.8.

### - [x] F-8.9.3 — §8.10 `session_tree_archive` has no Postgres backing — production loses tree archive on restart [High] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Lines 129, 1062 in `08_recursive-delegation.md`; §7.1 lines 426–433 in `07_session-lifecycle.md`; §12.7 line 783 in `12_storage-architecture.md`. The `session_tree_archive` is described as a Postgres table keyed by `(root_session_id, node_session_id)` and is listed in the §12.7 erasure ordering (must precede `SessionStore` deletion to satisfy the FK on `session_tree_archive.root_session_id → sessions.id`).
- **Evidence:**
  - `find /Users/joan/projects/lenny -path '*/treearchive*' -name '*.go'` returns only `pkg/gateway/treearchive/treearchive.go` and its tests. There is no `pgstore` subdirectory and no Postgres-backed `Store` implementation.
  - `grep -l "session_tree_archive" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations/*.up.sql` returns no results — no migration creates the table.
  - `pkg/gateway/treearchive/treearchive.go:83-91` defines `Memory` (in-memory map with a sync.RWMutex). `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:793` instantiates `treeArchive := treearchive.NewMemory()` and wires that singleton into the sessionserver and mcptools dependencies (`main.go:956, 1043`).
  - `pkg/storerouter/storerouter.go:60` includes `session_tree_archive` in the `StoreTypeSession` doc comment, but no router enumerates a Postgres shard for it.
- **Gap:** On every gateway restart (rolling upgrade, replica failover, coordinator handoff), the archive of every settled child result is lost. This breaks (a) the §8.10 "re-await protocol" (lines 1062–1063) — a resumed parent cannot stream pre-handoff settled results because they are gone; (b) the §7.1 `awaiting_client_action` durability story (lines 426–433) — child completion events the spec promises to durably persist do not survive a restart; (c) the §15.1 coordinator-handoff reattach test (lines 1412–1421 of `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`) — `children_reattached` cannot be reconstructed because the archive is empty.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `0050_session_tree_archive.up.sql` migration creating the table with columns `(tenant_id, root_session_id UUID, node_session_id UUID, parent_session_id UUID, state TEXT, result JSONB, settled_at TIMESTAMPTZ, archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ, completion_seq BIGINT)`, FKs to `sessions(id)`, and RLS by `tenant_id`. Implement `pkg/gateway/treearchive/pgstore` against the `treearchive.Store` interface and switch the gateway binary off `NewMemory()`. Add `completion_seq` so the §15.1 reattach test's `completion_seq > resumeFromSeq` predicate has a real column to read.

**Resolution:** Migration `0100_session_tree_archive` creates the table with the prescribed columns, PK `(root_session_id, node_session_id)`, FK `root_session_id → sessions(id)` with no ON DELETE action (RESTRICT, so the §12.7 line 807 erasure ordering holds), `tenant_id → tenants(id)`, the `tenant_id`-leading scatter-gather index, a `(tenant_id, node_session_id)` index for `GetByNode`, RLS policy, and the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger. `pkg/gateway/treearchive/pgstore` implements the `treearchive.Store` contract via `pgtenant.InTx` (Archive is an idempotent `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` upsert; Replay orders by `settled_at, completion_seq`). `cmd/lenny-gateway` switches off the bare `NewMemory()`: when a Postgres pool is configured it wires `treearchive.NewCached(treearchivepg.New(pool), cap)` (the §8.10 LRU fronting the durable store), keeping the in-memory store only for developer mode. Tier-1 cache tests pin write-through/eviction/replay-warming; tier-2 `tests/tier2_component/rls/session_tree_archive_test.go` pins the trigger, RLS isolation, upsert idempotency, and settlement-order replay. Committed this batch.

### - [ ] F-8.9.4 — `treeUsage` is not aggregated or surfaced; no tree-walk usage rollup exists [High] — DEFERRED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.5.24, F-8.8.3 — All three report that usage and treeUsage rollups on TaskResult are not aggregated or surfaced by the gateway.

- **Spec:** §8.8 lines 905–917 — `treeUsage = {inputTokens, outputTokens, wallClockSeconds, podMinutes, credentialLeaseMinutes, totalTasks}`. Line 917 — "`treeUsage` is populated by the gateway from the task tree and is only available after all descendants have settled. ... For in-progress tasks or tasks with unsettled descendants, `treeUsage` will be `null`."
- **Evidence:**
  - `grep -rn "treeUsage\|TreeUsage" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/` returns one hit: the comment "the §8.8 usage and treeUsage rollups are not yet tracked" at `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1308`.
  - `pkg/gateway/usagestore/usagestore.go:18-54` carries per-session `{Sessions, Tokens{Input,Output}, PodMinutes}`. There is no `totalTasks` aggregator, no `wallClockSeconds`, no `credentialLeaseMinutes`, no tree-walking sum.
  - `toTaskResult` at `mcptools.go:1323-1334` constructs `{schemaVersion, taskId, state, error?}` with no `usage` or `treeUsage` block.
  - The §8.10 archive's `ArchivedNode` carries `State` and `Result string` (`pkg/gateway/treearchive/treearchive.go:25-48`); no usage fields are stored, so a tree-walk aggregator could not source per-node usage from the archive even if it existed.
- **Gap:** `lenny/await_children` returns a TaskResult with no usage information; the §8.8 contract that `treeUsage` becomes available "after all descendants have settled" cannot be tested. Billing and per-tree attribution surfaces (§16) have no canonical aggregator to call.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `treeUsage` aggregator that walks the §8.9 tree (joining `sessions` and `session_tree_archive`), sums the canonical usage axes, returns `null` while any descendant is non-terminal, and threads the result into `toTaskResult` and the §15.1 `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/usage` surface. Extend the archive to record per-node usage when the node is archived.

**Deferred:** The aggregator's null-while-unsettled control flow is implementable, but it has no truthful per-node usage source to sum. The §8.10 archive's `ArchivedNode` stores only `State` and `Result`; `usagestore` records a per-session session count and a tenant/runtime token rollup, not the per-session `{inputTokens, outputTokens, wallClockSeconds, podMinutes, credentialLeaseMinutes}` axes the §8.8 `treeUsage` requires; and the §8.3 `treebudget` token counter tracks *reserved* budget (the lease cap), not *consumed* usage. A `treeUsage` built today would sum zeros, which is worse than the spec's `null`. Closing this requires first capturing per-node usage at settle time (extend `session_tree_archive` with the usage axes, or record them on the session row), which is the prerequisite the suggested resolution's last sentence names. Re-attempt once a per-node usage capture exists; the duplicate F-8.8.3 / F-8.5.24 are scoped behind the same prerequisite.

### - [x] F-8.9.5 — MCP `get_task_tree` response omits `runtimeRef` and uses `sessionId` instead of `taskId` [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.5.1 — Both report the MCP get_task_tree treeNode omitting runtimeRef (and using sessionId instead of taskId) versus the correct REST TreeNode.

- **Spec:** Line 540 — "Each node includes `taskId`, `state`, and `runtimeRef`." (Describing the `lenny/get_task_tree` MCP result.)
- **Evidence:**
  - `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1111-1116` — `type treeNode struct { SessionID string json:"sessionId"; State string; Children []treeNode }`. No `runtimeRef`, no `taskId`.
  - The REST `TreeNode` at `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:14-19` does carry `RuntimeRef string json:"runtimeRef,omitempty"`. The MCP and REST surfaces are inconsistent.
  - `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools_test.go:338-355::TestGetTaskTreeTool` only asserts the response contains the session ID strings; it does not assert any of the §8.8 / §8.9 normative field names.
- **Gap:** An MCP consumer that follows the §8.5 contract and expects `taskId` will fail to deserialize; a consumer that expects `runtimeRef` will find the field absent. The mismatch also blocks any cross-runtime visibility decision a parent agent might make based on a child's runtime identity.
- **Suggested resolution:** Rename `SessionID` → `TaskID` (json `taskId`) on the MCP `treeNode`, add `RuntimeRef string json:"runtimeRef"` populated from the session row, and unify the REST and MCP schemas behind one shared struct so future field additions cannot drift.

**Resolution:** RuntimeRef half was already closed by F-8.5.1. Renamed `SessionID` → `TaskID` (json `taskId`) on both the MCP `treeNode` and the REST `TreeNode`; the §15.2.1 REST↔MCP semantic-equivalence rule is preserved and the §8.5 line 540 wire contract ("Each node includes `taskId`, `state`, and `runtimeRef`") is now honored end-to-end. Tier-1 pins (`TestGetTaskTreeUsesTaskIDField_spec_8_5_540`, `TestTreeUsesTaskIDField_spec_8_5_540`) assert the new field on both surfaces; tier-3 `rest_mcp_consistency/scaffolds_test.go` updated to compare `taskId`.

### - [x] F-8.9.6 — Tree-wide Redis budget counters (`maxTreeSize`, `maxTreeMemoryBytes`, `childrenTotal`, `parallelChildren`) are not wired [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Lines 354–360 — "Tree-wide limits: `maxTreeSize` caps the total number of pods across the entire task tree (all depths) ... `maxTokenBudget` caps total LLM token consumption across the tree." Line 360 — "Reservation: The gateway reserves budget using a single Redis Lua script (`budget_reserve.lua`) that atomically reads the parent's token budget counter, the parent's actual token usage counter, the tree-size counter, the parent's `childrenTotal` counter ... the parent's `parallelChildren` counter, and the tree-memory counter". Line 127 — "The gateway tracks cumulative tree memory via an atomic Redis counter alongside the existing `maxTreeSize` counter."
- **Evidence:**
  - `grep -rn "budget_reserve.lua\|budget_return.lua\|maxTreeMemoryBytes" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/` returns only the spec-comment hits in `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go` and no Redis Lua scripts. The directory `pkg/delegation/lease/` contains only the pure-Go `lease.go`, `lease_test.go`, and `fuzz_test.go`.
  - `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go:62-98::ValidateChildSlice` is a pure arithmetic check that takes `remainingTokenBudget, remainingChildren, remainingTreeSize` as inputs. It never reads or writes any backing store. The caller is responsible for the atomic reservation, but no caller does so atomically in Redis.
  - The `delegation` Redis concern is declared at `pkg/storerouter/storerouter.go:52` (`RedisConcernDelegation`) but no code path performs the keyed `{root_session_id}:dlg:*` reservation the spec describes.
  - The metrics catalog declares `lenny_delegation_parallel_children_high_watermark` (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`), but the counter is never observed.
- **Gap:** A pathological tree can exceed `maxTreeSize`, `maxTreeMemoryBytes`, `maxChildrenTotal`, or `maxParallelChildren` because no atomic reservation rejects the over-fan-out delegation. The §8.3 "Reservation" contract — including the TOCTOU-free atomic reservation across six counters — is uniformly absent.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add the Redis Lua scripts described in §8.3, wire them into `lenny/delegate_task`'s delegation service before pod allocation, and persist the rolling counters keyed by `root_session_id`. Integrate the §11.2 periodic Postgres checkpoint of the counters so Redis recovery reconstructs them.

**Resolution:** The primary gap was resolved by the §8.2 tree-budget cluster (commit `6b86cac9`, closing F-8.2.18 / F-8.2.12 / F-8.1.1): `pkg/gateway/treebudget` runs the atomic Redis Lua reserve/return scripts over the `{root_session_id}:dlg:*` counters (`tree_size`, `tree_memory`, per-parent `parallel_children` / `children_total`, `tokens`), wired into `delegation.Service.Delegate` before pod allocation and instantiated in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`; the §11.2 `quotaSyncIntervalSeconds` checkpoint persists them to Postgres for Redis recovery. The evidence was stale (it predated `6b86cac9`). This batch closes the one residual evidence bullet — the `lenny_delegation_parallel_children_high_watermark` histogram was declared in the catalog but never observed: the reserve script now tracks a per-tree high-watermark key (`{root_session_id}:dlg:parallel_children_hwm`), `treebudget.ObserveHighWatermark` reads-and-clears it (GETDEL), and the sessionserver samples it onto the §16.1 histogram (labels `pool`, `tenant_id`) once when the tree root settles. Tier-1 pins cover the watermark tracking (`treebudget_test.go`) and the root-settle gating (`highwatermark_internal_test.go`). Committed in `93654b95`.

### - [x] F-8.9.7 — `get_task_tree` performs an O(N) per-tenant scan to materialize one tree [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §8.9 implies the tree is a maintained structure: "The gateway maintains a complete task tree". The data model in §12.6 / §12.7 routes session-sharded tables by routing prefix so a tree co-locates on one shard for single-shard traversal.
- **Evidence:**
  - `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:356-364::lenny/get_task_tree` reads `deps.Store.List(ctx, tenant, ListFilter{})` — every session in the tenant — and then indexes by `ParentSessionID` to walk one tree.
  - `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:55-71::handleTree` does the same: full tenant list, build a parent index in-process, walk one tree.
  - The schema has `idx_sessions_root` on `root_session_id` (`migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql:101`) — exactly the index a tree-scoped query would use — but no query in the code path uses it.
- **Gap:** On a tenant with thousands of sessions, every `get_task_tree` call (and every `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree`, every `await_children` archive replay, every `cancel_child`) lists the whole tenant before walking one tree. The cost is linear in tenant size, not tree size.
- **Suggested resolution:** Add a `Store.ListByRoot(ctx, tenantID, rootSessionID) ([]Session, error)` method backed by `WHERE root_session_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2`, and route every tree walker through it. The MCP `treeNode` walker, the REST `handleTree`, `isDescendant`, `cancelSubtree`, and `treeRoot` all benefit.

**Resolution:** Added `Store.ListByRoot(ctx, tenantID, rootSessionID)` on `sessionstore.Store`; memstore filters by `row.RootSessionID == rootSessionID` (with own-id fallback for legacy rows); pgstore issues `SELECT … WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND root_session_id = $2::uuid` against the existing `idx_sessions_root` index. The REST `handleTree` and the MCP `lenny/get_task_tree` (and `lenny/cancel_child`'s authorization scan) now route through `ListByRoot(root.RootSessionID)`, so a tree-scoped query reads O(tree size) rows instead of O(tenant size). Empty rootSessionID returns no rows so a typo never collapses to a tenant dump. Tier-1 pins (`TestListByRootScopesToOneTree_spec_8_9_1010`, `TestListByRootEmptyRootReturnsNoRows_spec_8_9_1010`, `TestListByRootCrossTenantIsolation_spec_8_9_1010`, `TestTreeReadsOnlySessionsInTheRequestedTree_spec_8_9_1010`) cover scoping, empty input, cross-tenant isolation, and the REST handler's sibling-tree exclusion.

### - [x] F-8.9.8 — Tree walker uses `ParentSessionID` lineage; spec's `root_session_id` column is stored but unused [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Line 1010 — each node tracks `session_id`. §12.5 line 101 — `CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_root ON sessions (root_session_id)`. The schema design assumes single-shard tree traversal by `root_session_id`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `pgstore.Store.Create` at `pkg/gateway/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:54-98` writes `root_session_id = id` (the session's own id) for every freshly created session. Children created via `lenny/delegate_task` follow the same path (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go` flows through `Create`). The column is therefore set to the session's *own* id rather than the *tree root's* id.
  - The `selectList` at `pgstore.go:46-52` does not include `root_session_id`, so the column is unreadable from the Session struct. `grep -rn "RootSessionID\b" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionstore/` returns no struct field — the concept is not surfaced.
  - The tree walker therefore must walk `ParentSessionID` chains rather than query by root.
- **Gap:** The schema's `root_session_id` column is dead — it is always set to the session's own id and never used to query. The optimization the schema enables (single-shard `WHERE root_session_id = ?` query) is unreachable. Worse, a tree-scoped read currently has no way to identify a tree root without walking up the parent chain, which is what `treeRoot` does in `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go::treeRoot` — a linear walk for each operation.
- **Suggested resolution:** When `lenny/delegate_task` creates a child, set the child's `root_session_id` to the parent's `root_session_id` (the parent's root, not the child's own id). Add `RootSessionID` to the `sessionstore.Session` struct and to the `selectList`. Update the schema CHECK constraint to assert `root_session_id IS NOT NULL` and `parent_session_id IS NOT NULL OR root_session_id = id`.

**Resolution:** Added `RootSessionID string` to `sessionstore.Session`; pgstore selectList now reads `COALESCE(root_session_id::text, '')` and `scanSession` populates it. `delegation.Service.Delegate` stamps `RootSessionID = parent.RootSessionID` (falling back to `parent.ID` when the parent has no tracked root) so every child in a delegation tree shares the same root. Both memstore.Create and pgstore.Create implicitly inherit the parent's RootSessionID when the caller did not stamp one (memstore: in-memory lookup; pgstore: subquery), so derived sessions, watchdog-recreated rows, and tests that seed a chain without stamping `RootSessionID` end up in the parent's tree automatically. A standalone session (no parent) becomes its own root. Tier-1 pins (`TestCreateStandaloneSessionIsItsOwnRoot_spec_8_9_1010`, `TestCreateChildInheritsParentRoot_spec_8_9_1010`, `TestCreateCallerProvidedRootWins_spec_8_9_1010`, `TestDelegateChildInheritsParentRootSessionID_spec_8_9_1010`) cover the standalone, inheritance, caller-stamped, and deep-tree delegation paths.

### - [x] F-8.9.9 — `treearchive.Memory` is unbounded (no LRU, no eviction); spec calls for a 128-entry per-replica cache [Medium] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Line 129 — "If the parent later reads the child's result, the gateway fetches it from Postgres on demand (with a per-replica LRU cache, default 128 entries)."
- **Evidence:**
  - `pkg/gateway/treearchive/treearchive.go:83-145::Memory` uses `map[string]ArchivedNode` with no size cap, no LRU, no TTL.
  - `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:793` instantiates one `treearchive.NewMemory()` and wires it as the production archive (per F-8.9.3). The "cache" the spec describes is the archive itself, not a fronting cache.
- **Gap:** A long-lived gateway with many delegated trees will grow the archive map without bound. The spec's "default 128 entries" cache assumes a Postgres-backed authoritative store with the in-memory copy serving as a hot cache; the current implementation conflates the two.
- **Suggested resolution:** Once the Postgres backing exists (F-8.9.3), repurpose the memory implementation as an LRU cache with `default 128 entries` and a configurable cap, fronting the Postgres store rather than acting as the durable record.

**Resolution:** Unblocked by F-8.9.3 and closed in the same batch. `pkg/gateway/treearchive/cache.go` adds `Cached`, an LRU (`container/list` MRU/LRU + map) keyed by `(tenant_id, node_session_id)` that fronts the durable `Store`. `DefaultCacheEntries = 128` matches the spec; `NewCached(inner, cap)` takes a configurable cap (`--tree-archive-cache-entries` / `LENNY_TREE_ARCHIVE_CACHE_ENTRIES`). Archive writes through and refreshes the entry; Replay warms the cache; Get/GetByNode share one entry per node and evict the LRU tail past the cap. `cmd/lenny-gateway` wires `NewCached(treearchivepg.New(pool), cap)` as the production archive, so `treearchive.Memory` is now only the developer-mode durable store rather than the unbounded production record. Tier-1 `cache_test.go` pins write-through, miss-then-hit, node-key sharing, the eviction bound, replay warming, the default cap, and root-mismatch fall-through.

### - [x] F-8.9.10 — Cycle guard in tree walker uses node-id `seen` set rather than relying on the §8.2 cycle detector [Low] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §8.2 cycle detection runs at delegation time. §8.9 / §8.10 traversal assumes the tree is acyclic.
- **Evidence:**
  - `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/tree.go:78-94::buildTreeNode` carries a `seen map[string]bool` and short-circuits when a node id repeats. The comment at line 75–77 calls it "defensive in case of a corrupt store".
  - `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1423-1433::walk` has the same defensive `seen` set.
- **Gap:** Defensive code that papers over a hypothetical corruption can mask a real bug (e.g., a mis-set `ParentSessionID` after the §8.10 recovery path). The §8.2 cycle detector prevents cycles at delegation, but a recovery write that re-parents a node could still create one and the tree walker would silently truncate the cycle rather than surface an alert.
- **Suggested resolution:** When the `seen` guard short-circuits, emit a `tree_cycle_detected` audit event and a metric (`lenny_delegation_tree_cycle_detected_total`) so a corrupted store surfaces rather than silently truncates.

**Resolution:** Added `sessionserver.TreeCycleObserver` and `mcptools.TreeCycleObserver` interfaces, refactored both `buildTreeNode` (sessionserver) and `buildTree`/`walk` (mcptools) to thread a `treeWalkContext` carrying the observer, and wired `gatewaymetrics.Metrics.IncDelegationTreeCycleDetected(tenant_id, source)` on each repeated-node hit. Each walker source labels its rows distinctly (`rest` for `/v1/sessions/{id}/tree`, `mcp` for `lenny/get_task_tree`). The metric `lenny_delegation_tree_cycle_detected_total` is registered with prometheus at gateway startup, sitting outside §16.1 the same way `lenny_rate_limit_rejected_total` does. The audit-row half of the suggested resolution (a `delegation.tree_cycle_detected` row in the §11.7 hash-chained log) is **deferred** because §16.7 is a closed catalog of spec-listed events and the new event type requires a spec change; the metric is the operator-visible signal in v1, the audit row lands with a future §16.7 catalog extension.

### - [x] F-8.9.11 — MCP `get_task_tree` input schema requires `sessionId`; spec says no input parameters [Low] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** Lines 615–623 — `lenny/get_task_tree` is defined with an empty input schema (`{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[]}`) and "Returns the task hierarchy visible to the calling session (scoped by `treeVisibility`)." The caller is identified implicitly from the MCP session.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:345-367` — `InputSchema: ...required:["sessionId"]...`. The handler requires the caller to pass `sessionId` explicitly and uses that id as the root of the returned subtree.
- **Gap:** The implementation requires an explicit input parameter the spec does not name and uses it to *select an arbitrary tree* rather than implicitly identifying the caller's tree (which would be enforced by `treeVisibility` once that landed). The MCP surface therefore both diverges from the documented schema and exposes a tree-selection capability the spec did not intend (a tree-traversal by parent of an arbitrary tenant-owned session).
- **Suggested resolution:** Drop the input parameter, source the caller's session id from the MCP context (via `Deps.CallerSessionID` or equivalent), and apply F-8.9.2's `treeVisibility` scoping. If an admin tool needs to inspect an arbitrary tree, add a separate admin endpoint rather than overloading the agent-facing `lenny/get_task_tree`.

**Resolution:** Rewrote the `lenny/get_task_tree` registration so the input schema declares no required fields (`{"properties":{"sessionId":{...}},"required":[]}`), and the handler now sources the caller's session id from `callerSessionID(ctx, in.SessionID)` — the same principal-bound resolver every other §8.5 tool uses. A spec-conformant empty-args call from a bound principal walks the tree rooted at the principal's `SessionID`; the optional `sessionId` is the §15.2.1 transport-fallback used by tests and dev-headers callers that have not yet bound a session-scoped principal. An unbound caller passing no fallback is rejected with `VALIDATION_ERROR` rather than silently selecting an arbitrary tree. `treeVisibility` scoping lands with F-8.9.2.

### - [x] F-8.9.12 — Tree-archive cancellation cascade snapshots the `seen` set at one instant, never observing late-settling siblings [Info] — CLOSED
- **Spec:** §8.10 line 1062 — "the gateway first streams all already-settled child results from `session_tree_archive` in original-settlement order". §8.10 cancellation cascade applies to all descendants reached at the time of the cancel call.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1464-1500::cancelSubtree` walks the cancellation cascade by re-reading the session list it was passed in. Sessions that transition to terminal *during* the cascade are not re-walked.
  - This is a different concern from F-8.9.10 (silent cycle masking).
- **Gap:** None directly visible at v1 fan-out scales — the loop completes quickly and the spec does not require linearizable cancellation. As tree depth grows, the cancel cascade may miss a fast-finishing concurrent child that completed between the initial list and the per-node update.
- **Suggested resolution:** Document the v1 acceptance and revisit when the per-tree atomic counter work lands (F-8.9.6): a Redis-keyed `{root_session_id}:dlg:state` channel would let the cancellation cascade observe the active in-flight set rather than a snapshot.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own conclusion ("None directly visible at v1 fan-out scales"). The spec does not require linearizable cancellation; the redesign lands with F-8.9.6 (per-tree atomic counter). No v1 code change.

## §8.10 Delegation Tree Recovery <a id="8.10"></a>
**Spec source:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/08_recursive-delegation.md` lines 1012–1110.
**Audit method:** Enumerated normative requirements from §8.10, then searched implementation
(`pkg/delegation/recovery/`, `pkg/gateway/treearchive/`, `pkg/gateway/orphancleanup/`,
`pkg/task/state/`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools/`,
`pkg/audit/`, plus wiring in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` and the metric/audit catalogs).

### Summary

The implementation covers two pillars of §8.10 — orphan cleanup and the
session_tree_archive — and ships a pure, well-tested bottom-up recovery
function, but several normative requirements are absent or partial. The
biggest gap is that `pkg/delegation/recovery` is wired nowhere: no
gateway path drives `recovery.Recover` when a delegation tree node
fails. The §8.10 `child_failed` event, the deep-tree per-pool
recovery-deadline configuration, the §8.10 metric emission, the
delegation-lease persistence required by the "no re-evaluation"
guarantee, and the policy/orphan-cap audit events are all unimplemented.

### Findings

### - [x] F-8.10.1 — 1 — `pkg/delegation/recovery` is never invoked [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-8.2.24 — Both report that the pkg/delegation/recovery package implementing the §8.10 bottom-up traversal is built but never invoked from production code.

**Severity:** High (MUST gap; the §8.10 bottom-up traversal is the
section's central correctness story.)

**Spec:** Lines 1014–1027:
> The gateway tracks the full task tree independently of pods in the
> SessionStore. This enables recovery when any node in the tree fails.
> Recovery ordering: The gateway recovers delegation trees bottom-up
> (leaves first). For each level, the gateway attempts recovery of all
> nodes at that depth before moving to the next level up.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/delegation/recovery/recovery.go` provides `Recover`, `Levels`,
  `Config{LevelTimeout, TreeTimeout, Now}`, and the per-node `Outcome`
  values. The package is pure and unit-tested
  (`pkg/delegation/recovery/recovery_test.go`).
- Grep across `pkg/`, `cmd/`, and `internal/` for `recovery.Recover`,
  `recovery.Levels`, `delegation/recovery` yields only the package's own
  files and `tests/spec-map.json`. The gateway's resume path
  (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:handleResume`) processes a single
  session at a time; nothing collects failed delegation-tree nodes,
  groups them by depth, or applies the level/tree deadlines.
- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` wires the orphan sweeper and the watchdog
  but contains no reference to `recovery` or to any tree-level driver.
- The pure traversal cannot detect concurrent multi-level failures
  (§8.10 "Non-adjacent simultaneous failures") because no caller
  enumerates failed nodes.

**Impact:** The spec's bottom-up recovery guarantee is not realized. A
delegation tree with a failed mid-level node and still-running children
gets ad-hoc per-session resume only — there is no level deadline, no
tree deadline, no deterministic leaves-first ordering, and no
terminal-failure transition for unrecovered nodes.

**Resolution:** New `pkg/gateway/treerecovery.Orchestrator` is the
production driver the pure `pkg/delegation/recovery` package was missing.
`RecoverTree` enumerates a tree via `sessionstore.ListByRoot`, builds the
`recovery.Node` set (depth from the immutable `DelegationDepth`, the
per-node `ResumeWindow` from `ResumeEligibleUntil`), and invokes
`recovery.Recover` so failed nodes are grouped by depth and recovered
leaves-first under the `maxLevelRecoverySeconds` / `maxTreeRecoverySeconds`
budgets; unrecovered nodes are marked terminal (`expired` for an elapsed
per-node resume window per §8.10 line 1027, otherwise `failed`) and the
§16.1 line 144-145 `lenny_delegation_tree_recovery_duration_seconds` /
`_timeout_total` metrics are emitted (full_success / partial_failure /
total_timeout; level / tree). The gateway wires it in
`sessionserver`: `handleResume` calls `recoverDelegationTree` after
`emitChildrenReattached`, so a resumed tree's orphaned descendants are
brought to a known state bottom-up. The per-node reattach reuses the
existing `resumeOnPod` resume path; the `nodeNeedsRecovery` predicate
scopes recovery to descendants that lost their pod binding (the pod
registry is the liveness oracle), so a root that resumed for its own
reasons never tears down children still live on their pods. The
previously-dead `delegation-max-level-recovery-seconds` /
`delegation-max-tree-recovery-seconds` flags now feed the orchestrator.
The traversal runs detached from the request because it is bounded by
`maxTreeRecoverySeconds` (600s), not the HTTP deadline. Commit
`4cc6f317`. (F-8.2.24 is already closed as the §8.2-side duplicate of
this finding.)

---

### - [x] F-8.10.2 — 2 — `child_failed` event never injected [High] — CLOSED

**Severity:** High (MUST gap. The spec normatively states "the gateway
injects a `child_failed` event into the parent's session stream".)

**Spec:** Lines 1080–1089:
> When a child fails, the gateway injects a `child_failed` event into
> the parent's session stream with: child_task_id, failure
> classification (transient/permanent), error details, whether retries
> were exhausted. The parent agent can then decide to: re-spawn a
> replacement, continue with partial results, or propagate the failure
> upward.

**Evidence:**
- Grep across `pkg/`, `proto/`, and `cmd/` for `child_failed`,
  `childFailed`, `ChildFailed`, `EventChildFailed` returns nothing.
  (Only `cmd/runtimes/delegation-echo/main.go:309` uses the unrelated
  string `"CHILD_FAILED"` as an internal error code in the reference
  runtime, not as a session-stream event.)
- The cascade path at
  `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:cascadeToChildren` cancels
  children and archives them but emits no event into the parent's
  session stream.
- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:failSession` and the watchdog's
  forced-failure paths transition the child row to `failed` and archive
  it but never publish a `child_failed` event via `s.events.Publish` to
  the parent's stream. Compare against the implemented
  `children_reattached` event in `emitChildrenReattached`.

**Impact:** Parent agents have no in-band signal of a child failure
between `child_state` transitions. The spec's stated decision options
("re-spawn, continue with partial results, propagate upward") are not
exposed; orchestrators must poll or call `await_children` to discover a
failure.

**Resolution:** `recordSessionCompleted` now calls `emitChildFailed`
(`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go`): a delegated child reaching
`failed` publishes a `child_failed` event onto the parent's session
stream carrying `child_task_id`, transient/permanent `classification`
(via `session.ClassifyFailure`), `failure_class`/`failure_reason`, and
`retries_exhausted`. Non-`failed` terminals and root sessions are
skipped. Closed by a1d8fc1e.

---

### - [ ] F-8.10.3 — 3 — `await_completion` cascade behaves identically to `detach` [High] — DEFERRED

**Severity:** High (cascade behavior conflated with `detach`; spec
distinguishes them.)

**Spec:** Lines 1070–1078 (cascade table):
> | `await_completion` | Let running children finish (up to
> `cascadeTimeoutSeconds`), then collect results |
> | `detach` | Children become orphaned; results are stored but no
> parent collects them. Client can query via `get_task_tree`. |

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:199–246` (`cascadeToChildren`)
  branches only on `cancel_all`. Both `CascadeAwaitCompletion` and
  `CascadeDetach` fall through the `policy != CascadeCancelAll` early
  return at line 205, so neither distinguishes "collect results when
  the children finish" from "let the children outlive the parent with
  no collection".
- `pkg/api/v1/session/session.go:96–100` defines
  `CascadeAwaitCompletion` in the enum and `Resolve()` admits it, but
  no code path applies its "collect results" semantics or its
  `cascadeTimeoutSeconds` budget.
- The orphan sweeper (`pkg/gateway/orphancleanup`) terminates both
  `detach` and `await_completion` children when the cascade timeout
  elapses; it has no notion of "collect results" before terminating.

**Impact:** A delegator setting `cascadeOnFailure: await_completion`
gets the `detach` runtime behavior. Children continue running; their
results land in `session_tree_archive` but no synthesized
"parent-collected" boundary is produced. The behavior is silent — no
error, no warning.

**Deferred:** The only observable distinction between `await_completion`
and `detach` once the parent is terminal is the spec's "collect results"
step — synthesizing a parent-collected boundary that aggregates the
settled children's results (and `treeUsage`) into the parent's archived
TaskResult. Both policies already let children run to
`cascadeTimeoutSeconds` (orphan cleanup bounds both), and both archive
each child individually; `get_task_tree` reads either. The
result-aggregation source this collection requires is the same per-node
usage/result rollup that F-8.9.4 deferred ("no truthful per-node usage
source to sum; archive stores only State/Result"). Deferred pending
F-8.9.4 per-node collection capture. The lower-risk pieces — cascade
fallback audit (F-8.10.8) and orphan-cap behavior — are already closed.

---

### - [x] F-8.10.4 — 4 — Children-reattached event is not in original-settlement order, does not stream archive [High] — CLOSED

**Severity:** High (MUST gap; the spec specifies the order explicitly.)

**Spec:** Lines 1062 (Re-await protocol):
> When the resumed parent re-issues `lenny/await_children`, the gateway
> first streams all already-settled child results from
> `session_tree_archive` in original-settlement order, then enters
> live-wait for any still-running children. The parent agent sees a
> consistent, ordered view of all child outcomes regardless of which
> settled before or after the parent failure.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:541–576`
  (`emitChildrenReattached`) iterates `s.store.List` results in
  whatever order the store returns rows and reads each terminal
  child's payload from the live `sessionstore.Session` row, not from
  `treearchive.Replay`. `SettledAt` is never consulted.
- `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:422–481` (`lenny/await_children`)
  iterates `in.ChildIDs` in caller-supplied order; on each tick it
  calls `collectChildResults` (line 1385) which falls through to
  `resolveChild` (line 1349) — a per-id `archive.GetByNode` lookup.
  There is no `archive.Replay(rootSessionID)` streaming and no
  settlement-order sort. The package-level test
  `pkg/gateway/treearchive/treearchive_test.go:26` (`TestArchiveAnd
  ReplayInSettlementOrder`) only exercises the archive's own ordering;
  no test verifies that `await_children` returns results in
  settlement order.
- The archive's `Replay` (line 120 of `treearchive.go`) does sort by
  `SettledAt`, so the contract exists; the issue is that the resume
  path and `await_children` do not call it.

**Impact:** A parent re-awaiting children after pod loss sees results
in a non-deterministic order. The spec's "consistent, ordered view of
all child outcomes regardless of which settled before or after the
parent failure" is not delivered.

**Resolution:** `emitChildrenReattached`
(`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go`) now streams settled children from
`treeArchive.Replay(root)` in `SettledAt` order (carrying the archived
§8.8 result body), then appends still-active children. `await_children`'s
`collectChildResults` (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`) sorts the
`all`/`settled` result set by each child's settle witness with a stable
childIDs-order tie-break. Closed by a1d8fc1e.

### - [x] F-8.10.5 — 5 — Delegation lease record not persisted; no-re-evaluation guarantee unverifiable [High] — CLOSED

**Severity:** High (the §8.10 "Policy enforcement during recovery"
clause is the section's central security invariant and depends on
persisted lease state.)

**Spec:** Lines 1044–1049 ("Policy enforcement during recovery"):
> The gateway MUST NOT re-evaluate any node's `delegationPolicyRef`,
> `maxDelegationPolicy`, `contentPolicy`, `minIsolationProfile`, or
> other lease-scoped policy fields against the live policy state when
> bringing a node back up. Recovery uses the delegation lease record
> persisted at original approval time (via SessionStore), which
> includes the node's effective `maxDelegationPolicy` (after
> inheritance resolution per §8.3), its `delegationPolicyRef`, and —
> when `snapshotPolicyAtLease: true` was set on the root — the
> `snapshotted_pool_ids` set.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/sessionstore/sessionstore.go:28–137` defines `Session`.
  It carries `RuntimeRef`, `IsolationProfile`, `CascadeOnFailure`,
  `TracingContext`, etc., but no fields named or equivalent to
  `DelegationPolicyRef`, `MaxDelegationPolicy`, `ContentPolicyRef`, or
  `SnapshottedPoolIds`.
- `DelegationPolicyRef` exists only as a field of `runtimestore.Runtime`
  (`pkg/gateway/runtimestore/runtimestore.go:60`) — i.e., the live
  runtime registry, exactly what the spec says recovery MUST NOT
  consult.
- Grep across `pkg/`, `proto/` for `snapshotPolicyAtLease`,
  `snapshotted_pool_ids`, `SnapshottedPoolIds`, `MaxDelegationPolicy`
  returns no Go source matches.
- `pkg/delegation/lease/lease.go` validates child slices in-memory but
  has no persistence and no link to the session record.

**Impact:** A pod-loss recovery for a tree whose `DelegationPolicy`
narrowed between original approval and resume will either silently
re-evaluate against the live (narrower) policy — violating the
guarantee — or fail in undefined ways depending on which paths read
the runtime registry. The spec's "lease is a capability that survives
the pod loss" promise has no implementation backing.

**Resolution:** `sessionstore.DelegationLease` now carries the §8.10
lines 1044-1049 lease-scoped policy record — `DelegationPolicyRef`,
`MaxDelegationPolicy` (the resolved effective policy name),
`ContentPolicyRef`, and `SnapshottedPoolIDs` — alongside the resource
slice, riding the existing `delegation_lease` JSONB column (no migration
needed). The §8.2 delegation `Service.Delegate` captures these from the
resolved runtime `delegationPolicyRef` and effective `DelegationPolicy`
at original approval time via the new `stampLeasePolicy` helper, so a
later tree recovery resumes the node against the persisted record rather
than re-evaluating the live runtime registry. The lease-scoped
`minIsolationProfile` rides the session's first-class `IsolationProfile`
column and is not duplicated. v1 does not implement
`snapshotPolicyAtLease`, so `snapshotted_pool_ids` stays empty (live pool
labels) exactly as a pre-failure call would evaluate. Closed by ec46848d.

### - [x] F-8.10.6 — 1 — Per-level and tree recovery deadlines not configurable via Helm [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity:** Medium (SHOULD/capability unimplemented; the spec
explicitly states the values are deployer-configurable.)

**Spec:** Line 1042:
> Configure via Helm `delegation.maxTreeRecoverySeconds`.

Lines 1020–1023 also describe `maxLevelRecoverySeconds` (120s default,
per-level) and `maxTreeRecoverySeconds` (600s default, whole tree) as
Helm-configurable.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/delegation/recovery/recovery.go:22–29` defines
  `DefaultLevelTimeout = 120s` and `DefaultTreeTimeout = 600s` and the
  values can be overridden via `recovery.Config`, but no caller
  populates that struct from Helm or runtime config (HIGH-1).
- Grep `charts/lenny/values.yaml`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`, and
  `pkg/` for `maxLevelRecoverySeconds`, `maxTreeRecoverySeconds`,
  `MaxTreeRecoverySeconds` yields zero non-test references.
- The deep-tree formula in lines 1029–1040 cannot be applied: the
  parameters it references are not surfaced to operators.

**Impact:** A deployer running deep trees cannot follow the spec's
sizing guidance because the knob does not exist; the gateway always
uses the hardcoded defaults (when the recovery package is invoked,
which per HIGH-1 it never is).

**Resolution:** Added `delegation.maxLevelRecoverySeconds` /
`delegation.maxTreeRecoverySeconds` chart values (defaults `120` / `600`
per §8.10 lines 1022-1023) + `--delegation-max-level-recovery-seconds`
and `--delegation-max-tree-recovery-seconds` gateway flags. Both feed
the `recovery.Config.LevelTimeout` / `TreeTimeout` fields used by the
§8.10 traversal, and the gateway logs the effective values at startup.
Tier-1 `TestRecoverHonorsConfigLevelAndTreeOverrides_spec_8_10_1022_1023`
pins the operator-tunable path; tier-2 helm-unittests cover both the
chart default and the override flowing into LENNY_DELEGATION_*.

### - [x] F-8.10.8 — 3 — Orphan-cap fallback is silent (no audit event, no parent-stream annotation) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity:** Medium (recurring iter2/iter3 finding DEL-007: a
policy-changing gateway decision lacks an audit trail.)

**Spec:** Line 1103 (orphan cap):
> When a `detach` cascade policy would cause the tenant's active orphan
> count to exceed this cap, the gateway falls back to `cancel_all` for
> that delegation instead of detaching — the children are cancelled
> rather than orphaned.

The §8.10 cascade fallback is silent in the implementation; iter4 of
the spec review (carried over from DEL-007) recommended an audit event
`delegation.orphan_cap_fallback`.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:201–204`:
  ```go
  if policy == session.CascadeDetach && s.detachExceedsOrphanCap(ctx, sess.TenantID) {
      // §8.10 maxOrphanTasksPerTenant fallback.
      policy = session.CascadeCancelAll
  }
  ```
  The downgrade is applied with no `s.policyAuditSink` append, no
  `opsEmitter` event, no metric increment, and no event published on
  the parent session's stream.
- `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` has no
  `delegation.orphan_cap_fallback` event type, no `cascade.fallback`
  type, and no per-tenant orphan-cap event at all.
- Grep `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go` for `audit`, `Audit`,
  `AppendAudit` returns no matches in the cascade path.

**Impact:** An orchestrator that configured `detach` deliberately —
because it intends sub-trees to outlive the parent — sees its children
cancelled with no correlated reason. The deployer's audit trail also
loses the cap-driven policy override; only the rate-limit-style
gauge alert fires (and per MEDIUM-2 even that gauge is not actually
emitted).

**Resolution:** The cascade-fallback path now writes a `session.cascade_applied`
audit row (already in the §16.7 closed catalog) via the new
`recordCascadeApplied` helper, carrying `originalPolicy`, `effectivePolicy`,
`reason="orphan_cap_fallback"`, plus the parent and tenant identifiers
in Detail. A structured log line fires unconditionally for the §16.4
pipeline. Tier-1 `TestDetachFallbackEmitsCascadeAppliedAudit_spec_8_10_1103`
asserts the audit row content; `TestDetachUnderCapDoesNotEmitFallbackAudit_spec_8_10_1103`
guards the negative case.

### - [x] F-8.10.11 — 6 — `maxResumeWindowSeconds` × tree-recovery interaction not modeled [Medium] — CLOSED

**Severity:** Medium (the spec's `min(maxResumeWindowSeconds,
remaining maxTreeRecoverySeconds)` combination is required for correct
deadline composition.)

**Spec:** Line 1027:
> A node's individual resume window runs concurrently with tree
> recovery. If a node's `maxResumeWindowSeconds` expires before tree
> recovery reaches it, that node transitions to `expired` and its
> cascade policy is applied. Conversely, `maxTreeRecoverySeconds` can
> terminate a node's recovery attempt even if its
> `maxResumeWindowSeconds` has not yet elapsed. The effective recovery
> window for any node is therefore `min(maxResumeWindowSeconds,
> remaining maxTreeRecoverySeconds)`.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/delegation/recovery/recovery.go` only models level/tree
  deadlines; the per-node `Node` struct has no resume-window field and
  `Recover` does not accept a per-node deadline.
- Grep for `maxResumeWindowSeconds` in `pkg/` returns no matches in
  recovery code; the resume window is referenced in §7.3 / §7.1
  handling but never composed with tree-recovery deadlines.

**Impact:** Even if HIGH-1 were resolved, a node's individual resume
window would not interact correctly with the tree-recovery budget.
Recovery could either (a) keep retrying a node past its resume window,
or (b) abandon a node before its individual budget elapsed, depending
on caller wiring; the spec's `min(...)` invariant is not enforced.

**Resolution:** Extended `recovery.Node` with `ResumeWindow time.Duration`
(the per-session `maxResumeWindowSeconds` budget) and updated
`recovery.Recover` to clamp each attempt against
`min(node.ResumeWindow, level, tree)` per §8.10 line 1027. Three new
failure reasons distinguish which budget bound first
(`node resume window exceeded` / `level recovery deadline exceeded`
/ `tree recovery deadline exceeded`), so the §8.10 invariant is
observable post-recovery. Tier-1 tests cover both directions of the
`min(...)`: a short per-node window binding before the level cap and
the tree budget binding before a long per-node window.

### - [x] F-8.10.12 — 1 — Orphan-cleanup retention follow-up not implemented [Low] — CLOSED

**Severity:** Low (the spec's "Orphaned children are terminated and
their artifacts follow standard retention policy" is implicit; the
implementation transitions the row to `expired` but does not
explicitly invoke the retention GC.)

**Spec:** Line 1091:
> Orphaned children are terminated and their artifacts follow standard
> retention policy.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/orphancleanup/orphancleanup.go:115–152` (`sweepTenant`)
  flips the session to `expired` and archives it. It does not set
  `RetentionExpiresAt` or otherwise interact with the retention GC.
- `pkg/gateway/retentiongc` is a separate sweeper that processes
  terminal sessions per the §7.1 TTL; it will pick up the orphaned
  session on its own schedule (15-minute default), but no explicit
  coordination exists.

**Impact:** No correctness break — eventual cleanup occurs via the
retention GC — but the §8.10 prose suggests an active hand-off that is
not present in code. Worth a documentation note or an explicit nudge.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-5.2.26 (commit 8380ab72). The orphancleanup sweeper now invokes the gateway's `Server.OnSessionTerminal` (TerminalHook), which calls `recordSessionCompleted` → `emitTerminalLifecycle` → `rollRetentionOnTerminal` (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/lifecycle.go:165,181`). That rolls `RetentionExpiresAt` forward to `terminal_time + DefaultArtifactRetention`, so orphaned children inherit the standard §7.1 retention window measured from the expiry instant.

## §9.1 Where MCP Is Used <a id="9.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/09_mcp-integration.md` (lines 3-41)
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-22

### Summary

§9.1 enumerates six boundary rows (client↔gateway, adapter↔runtime intra-pod, parent↔child via gateway, gateway↔external MCP tools, gateway↔`type:mcp` runtimes, gateway↔pod control), the twelve platform MCP tools available to `type: agent` runtimes via the adapter manifest, and the four discovery surfaces (MCP `list_runtimes`, REST `GET /v1/runtimes`, OpenAI Completions `GET /v1/models`, Open Responses `GET /v1/models`) each of which MUST embed an `adapterCapabilities` block reflecting the serving adapter. The gateway-virtual MCP server at `POST /mcp` is built and registers all twelve platform tools (`pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`). The four REST/MCP discovery handlers exist, each embedding an `adapterCapabilities` block. Connector registry (`pkg/gateway/connectorstore`), connector OAuth 2.1 flow (`pkg/connectoroauth`, `pkg/gateway/admin/connector_oauth.go`), the elicitation chain primitives (`pkg/elicitation`), and the `type:mcp` runtime-side adapter path (`pkg/adapter/mcpruntime.go`, `pkg/adapter/mcp` client, `cmd/runtimes/mcp-reference`) are all built. However, the boundaries the spec names are unevenly implemented: the intra-pod platform MCP server is wired (`@lenny-platform-mcp` socket, nonce-authenticated) but registers zero `lenny/*` tools, so the §9.1 platform-tool surface is unreachable from a `type: agent` runtime via the adapter manifest path the spec names. The per-connector intra-pod MCP servers are absent (`connectorServers` manifest slot is always empty). The gateway-side dedicated MCP endpoint surface for `type: mcp` runtimes (`/mcp/runtimes/{name}`) does not exist (acknowledged as a v2 follow-on in `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:200-207`). The gateway carries no outbound MCP client for external MCP tool invocation — only the OAuth token-exchange half of the connector flow is wired. The `mcpEndpoint` field required on every `AuthorizedRuntime` discovery entry is absent from both the REST and MCP discovery shapes. The `/v1/models` OpenAI/Open Responses discovery returns `restAdapterCapabilities()` rather than the actual serving adapter's capabilities, breaking the "reflecting the capabilities of the adapter serving the request" invariant. The gateway `/mcp` adapter declares MCP protocol version `2025-06-18` but does not implement the Streamable-HTTP SSE channel the §15.1 / §15.4 contract describes (every JSON-RPC method returns a single JSON response — `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:20-21`). Counts: 3 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] F-9.1.1 — Intra-pod platform MCP server exposes no `lenny/*` tools [High] — CLOSED

- **Spec:** "Adapter ↔ Runtime (intra-pod) | MCP (local Unix socket servers) | Platform tools, per-connector tool servers." (line 8) and "The platform MCP server (available to `type: agent` runtimes via the adapter manifest) exposes: `lenny/delegate_task`, `lenny/await_children`, `lenny/cancel_child`, `lenny/discover_agents`, `lenny/output`, `lenny/request_elicitation`, `lenny/memory_write`, `lenny/memory_query`, `lenny/request_input`, `lenny/send_message`, `lenny/get_task_tree`, `lenny/set_tracing_context`" (lines 14-31).
- **Evidence:** `pkg/adapter/platformmcp.go:18-43` starts a `mcp.NewServer()` (from `pkg/adapter/mcp/server.go`) on the manifest's `MCPSocket`, but no `Register` call is ever made on that server. `grep -rn "srv.Register\|\.Register(mcp" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/` returns matches only in `pkg/adapter/mcp/server_test.go`. The only tool surface advertised to a `type: agent` runtime via the manifest is `manifestLocalTools()` (`pkg/adapter/manifest.go:184-195`), which returns the four §15 adapter-local tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `list_dir`, `delete_file`) over the §15.4.1 stdio `tool_call` binary protocol, not the §9.1 platform tools over the intra-pod MCP socket. `pkg/adapter/toolcall.go:35-58` confirms a `tool_call` for a `lenny/...` name is **not** handled and is relayed unchanged upstream; the gateway-side executor (`pkg/gateway/executor/pod.go:100-130 readAttachResponse`) only reads `response` envelopes and has no `lenny/*` dispatcher — so a platform-tool `tool_call` emitted by an agent over stdio has no handler at either end. The dedicated `TestHandleToolCallPlatformToolNotHandled` (`pkg/adapter/toolcall_test.go:97-104`) freezes this behavior.
- **Gap:** A spec-conformant `type: agent` runtime that dials `@lenny-platform-mcp` and calls `tools/list` receives an empty list; one that emits `lenny/delegate_task` as a stdio `tool_call` falls into the unhandled relay path. The §9.1 platform-tool catalog is reachable only via the gateway-edge `POST /mcp` HTTP endpoint, which a sandboxed agent on the cluster-internal pod network has no path to call. All twelve §9.1 platform tools are unreachable from a `type: agent` runtime via the spec-named integration path.
- **Suggested resolution:** Either (a) register a proxy handler on the intra-pod `pkg/adapter/mcp.Server` for every `lenny/...` name that forwards the `tools/call` to the gateway over an authenticated gRPC channel, or (b) replicate the `mcptools.Register` registration on the intra-pod server with handlers that issue per-session gateway calls. The path the manifest names (`platformMcpServer.socket`) must serve the §9.1 tool list and dispatch each call to the same gateway services `pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go` already drives.

**Resolution (commit `95bae6c0`):** Implemented option (a). The evidence was doubly accurate — the intra-pod server registered no tools AND was never wired in production (no `--mcp-socket`, no adapter→gateway dial). New `GatewayControl.ListPlatformTools` / `CallPlatformTool` RPCs carry the catalog and each call. The gateway `mcp.Server` gained `Catalog()` + `DispatchTool()` (non-HTTP entry points sharing a `toolErrorResult` builder with the `/mcp` handler), and `pkg/gateway/platformtools.Bridge` resolves the calling session's tenant/owner via `sessionstore.GetByID`, installs the §9.1 `authmw` principal, and dispatches against the same `*mcp.Server` the gateway-edge `/mcp` surface serves (so the two surfaces stay in lockstep). The bridge is wired into the `leasecontrol` GatewayControl server. On the pod side, `pkg/adapter/mcp.Server` gained a `ToolProvider` seam; the adapter installs a forwarder (`gatewaycontrol.Client`) bound to the pod's session so `tools/list` and `tools/call` for any `lenny/*` name proxy to the gateway. `lenny-adapter` gained `--mcp-socket` + `--gateway-grpc-addr` (mesh-mTLS dial reusing its identity cert, pinning the gateway DNS SAN); `lenny-controller` gained `--gateway-grpc-addr`, threaded through the Sandbox reconciler and `podspec` onto the adapter container, and the chart points every agent-pod adapter at `lenny-gateway.<ns>.svc:<grpcPort>`. With the SO_PEERCRED/nonce check already on the socket, the §4.7 line 942 boundary is now enforceable. The per-connector servers (F-9.1.2/F-9.3.2), the `type:mcp` dispatcher (F-9.1.3), and the `/mcp` SSE channel (F-9.1.7) remain separate subsystems; the forwarding infrastructure added here is the seam F-9.1.2 builds on. Tests: tier-1 (`mcp.DispatchTool`/`Catalog`, `leasecontrol` RPC matrix, `platformtools.Bridge` incl. principal injection, intra-pod Provider dispatch, `gatewaycontrol` client mapping, `podspec` args) + a tier-2 component test driving the full adapter-side socket → forwarder path + helm-unittest on the controller arg.

Adapter-side, `Server.sessionConnectors` resolves the permitted connectors during StartSession/Resume/ConfigureWorkspace, `writeSessionManifest` now populates `connectorServers`, and `startConnectorMCPServers` opens one `@lenny-connector-<id>` MCP server per connector (shared `listenIntraPodMCP` SO_PEERCRED/nonce path), each forwarding to the gateway via `*gatewaycontrol.Client`. `releaseSession` tears them down.
