### - [x] F-9.3.3 — Refresh-token rotation grant unimplemented [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-4.3.5 — Both describe the unimplemented connector refresh-token rotation grant against the same connector_credentials schema and store.

**Resolution:** Collapses into F-4.3.5: the same fix adds `connectoroauth.RefreshAccessToken`, the `connectorcredstore.Store.RotateAccessToken(ctx, RotationRecord)` method, and the Postgres + in-memory implementations that stamp `rotated_at`. See F-4.3.5's resolution note for the full description and the list of tier-1 tests.

Spec (§9.3, line 152): "Gateway connector receives and stores
resulting tokens (encrypted, never in pods)." Implicit in this is the
RFC 6749 §6 refresh grant — without it, every connector OAuth token
becomes unusable once `expires_in` lapses, forcing a full
re-authorization for every expiry. The migration schema explicitly
plans for rotation:

`migrations/0048_connector_credentials.up.sql:42-44`:
```
rotated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,  -- records the last refresh-token exchange
revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
```

`pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:42` doc comment
references `RotateAccessToken` and `Revoke` methods, but neither is
declared on the `Store` interface, neither is implemented on the
`*Store` receiver, and no caller exists:

```
$ grep -rn "RotateAccessToken\\|grant_type=refresh\\|RefreshConnectorToken" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/ --include="*.go"
pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:42:  // (doc comment only — no method exists)
```

`pkg/connectoroauth/flow.go` provides only `ExchangeCode` (the
authorization-code grant). There is no `ExchangeRefreshToken`, no
refresh-token rotation timer, no near-expiry refresh path on the read
side of `connectorcredstore`. The stored `RefreshToken` is dead data.

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/connectorcredstore.go:88-106` (Store interface — no Rotate / Refresh / Revoke methods)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:42` (stale doc comment)

### - [x] F-9.3.4 — Production gateway wiring drops the client-secret resolver [High] — CLOSED

The handler hard-errors a confidential-client callback when
`ConnectorOAuth.ClientSecrets` is nil
(`pkg/gateway/admin/connector_oauth.go:303-307`). The gateway main
constructs `ConnectorOAuth` without setting that field:

`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1000-1005`:
```go
connectorOAuth = &admin.ConnectorOAuth{
    StateSigner: stateSigner,
    StateStore:  connectoroauth.NewMemoryStateStore(),
    Credentials: connectorCreds,
    CallbackURL: *connectorOAuthCallbackURL,
}
```

Result: every confidential connector OAuth callback (any connector
whose `auth.clientSecretRef` is set — the production case for GitHub,
Jira, Notion, etc.) returns HTTP 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with "connector
is a confidential client but no client-secret resolver is wired",
even though the registry layer requires `clientSecretRef` to be a
`namespace/name` reference. Only public clients work end-to-end in a
live gateway build. The test-only `MemoryClientSecretResolver` is
never instantiated outside `connector_oauth_test.go`.

Files:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1000-1005`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/connector_oauth.go:29-66, 303-307`

**Resolution (`af11e5fe`):** The cited line pointers were stale (the wiring moved to `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:~2251`). New `pkg/gateway/connectorsecret.KubeResolver` reads a confidential connector's client secret from its §9.3 `auth.clientSecretRef` Kubernetes Secret (`namespace/name` using a flag-tunable default data key `clientSecret`, or an explicit `namespace/name/key`), returning `ErrClientSecretNotFound` for an absent Secret/key. The gateway main now sets `ConnectorOAuth.ClientSecrets = connectorsecret.NewKubeResolver(clusterClient, *connectorOAuthClientSecretKey)` whenever it holds a cluster client (the production `--agent-namespace` path), so a confidential connector OAuth callback resolves its secret instead of returning the unconditional 500. The `--connector-oauth-client-secret-key` flag (env `LENNY_CONNECTOR_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET_KEY`) is operator-tunable. Deployment prerequisite (noted for the separate chart-wiring of connector OAuth): the gateway ServiceAccount needs `get` on the connector-secret Secrets; a read failure surfaces as a descriptive error rather than a silent misconfiguration. Tests: 7 tier-1 in `pkg/gateway/connectorsecret` (default/explicit key, not-found, missing/empty value, malformed refs, default-key constructor) via the controller-runtime fake client.

### - [x] F-9.3.5 — Production gateway uses in-process StateStore and CredentialStore even with Postgres [High] — CLOSED

Spec (§9.3, line 157): the state binding is "Redis, TTL = 10 min".
The production main wires
`connectoroauth.NewMemoryStateStore()` and
`connectorcredstore.NewMemory(nil)` unconditionally
(`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:987, 1002`), regardless of whether
`--pg-url` and `--redis-addr` are set. A Postgres-backed
`connectorcredstore/pgstore` exists, and the schema is migrated, but
no production code path constructs it. There is no Redis-backed
StateStore at all — only `MemoryStateStore`.

Operational consequences: (a) connector OAuth state and credentials
do not survive a gateway restart; (b) replicas do not share state, so
a callback that lands on a different replica than the authorize call
fails with `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_STATE_UNKNOWN` even within the TTL; (c)
encrypted-at-rest credentials are never written through the §12.9 T4
KMS envelope in a live deployment.

Files:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:987, 1000-1005`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/connectorcredstore/pgstore/pgstore.go` (exists, unused)

**Resolution (`af11e5fe`):** New `connectoroauth.RedisStateStore` is the production §9.3 StateStore: `Put` stores the JSON-encoded `FlowContext` under `conn:oauth:state:{state}` with the §9.3 10-minute TTL via Redis native key expiry, and `Consume` runs one atomic Lua round-trip that swaps the live entry for a NUL-prefixed tombstone, so two concurrent callbacks for the same `state` cannot both succeed and a replay returns `ErrStateConsumed` (verified by a 16-goroutine single-winner test). The gateway main wires it when Redis is configured (`redisClient != nil`), falling back to the in-process `MemoryStateStore` (with its periodic Sweep) only in single-process dev. This addresses consequences (a) restart-survival and (b) cross-replica state sharing. Consequence (c) was already resolved: `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:2218` constructs the envelope-encrypted `connectorcredstore/pgstore` and assigns it to `connectorCreds` whenever `pgPool != nil`, so the "exists, unused" / "no production code path constructs it" claims were stale. Tests: 8 tier-1 in `pkg/connectoroauth` (round-trip, unknown, replay, TTL-expiry, replace, empty-key, default-TTL, concurrent single-winner) against miniredis with `-race`.

**Deferred:** §9.3 line 136 calls for capability metadata "derived from MCP `ToolAnnotations` at registration time", but §15.1 line 1144 explicitly forbids the synchronous `POST /v1/admin/connectors` create path from making any outbound call to the connector endpoint ("Does **not** perform DNS resolution, TLS handshake, or any outbound call"). Inference needs `tools/list`, which is an outbound MCP call, so it cannot run inside the create handler without violating line 1144. The compliant realization is a separate post-create / refresh step on the sanctioned outbound path (the F-9.3.12 test flow now reaches `tools/list`, and the F-9.1.5 `connectorinvoke.Client.ListTools` returns the `ToolAnnotations` block `capabilityinference.Infer` consumes), plus new `Capabilities`/`CapabilityInferenceMode` columns on `connectorstore.Connector` and a migration. Both prerequisites the inference call needs are now built; the remaining work is the storage schema + the refresh trigger, deferred to its own batch to keep this one scoped to the client and the test endpoint.

**Resolution (d24dedb2):** Realized exactly the compliant out-of-band path the deferral described. `connectorstore.Connector` gains `CapabilityInferenceMode`, `Capabilities` (the §5.1 inferred union), `ToolCapabilities` (the per-tool capability map feeding the §5.3 call-time `TOOL_CAPABILITY_DENIED` check), and `CapabilitiesRefreshedAt`, persisted via migration `0114_connectors_capabilities` (additive `ADD COLUMN` with defaults) and wired through the memory and Postgres stores. `connectorinvoke.Invoker.RefreshCapabilities` dials the connector on the sanctioned outbound path (`initialize` → `tools/list`), runs `capabilityinference.Infer` per tool under the connector's mode (default strict), emits the §5.1 line 327 WARN for unannotated-admin tools, and persists the union + per-tool map. New admin `POST /v1/admin/connectors/{name}/refresh` endpoint (platform/tenant-admin, 10/min per-connector cap) drives it, mirroring the §15.1 live-test endpoint. The synchronous create path still makes no outbound call (§15.1 line 1144 preserved). Tests: tier-1 infer/persist + strict-WARN + permissive-write + inactive-connector + memory round-trip; tier-2 migration column coverage; admin endpoint matrix (admin/tenant-admin allow, user 403, 404, 502-unreachable, 429-rate-limited).

### - [x] F-9.3.11 — Auditing skips the live actor on `connector.oauth.credential_stored` [Medium] — CLOSED

`handleConnectorOAuthCallback` emits its `credential_stored` audit
event with `ActorSubject = flow.UserID, ActorTenantID = flow.TenantID`
(`connector_oauth.go:362-374`). The callback carries no Bearer token
(it is a browser redirect), so the live HTTP-level principal is
correctly absent — but the gateway also has no way to confirm that
the browser-rendered redirect was driven by the same user that
initiated the flow. The `state` parameter is the only binding. The
spec's "Tokens never transit through pods" invariant is met, but the
audit event lacks an `initiated_by` vs. `completed_by` distinction
(IP, user-agent, or session-binding hash) that would let an operator
investigate a state replay attempt or a session hijack between
authorize and callback. This is a defense-in-depth observation: no
spec text requires it, but the audit trail is the prescribed forensic
surface (§9.3 line 140: "audit logging" is one of the named uses).

Tier-1 coverage: `TestConnectorOAuthCredentialStoredAuditCarriesInitiatorAndCompleterIP_spec_9_3_140` and `TestConnectorOAuthCallbackIPHonoursXForwardedFor_spec_9_3_140`.

### - [x] F-9.3.15 — Connector OAuth flow not gated behind admin/manage-connector permissions [Low] — CLOSED

`handleAuthorizeConnector` gates only on authentication: any
authenticated principal in any role can initiate an OAuth flow
against any registered connector
(`connector_oauth.go:137-142`, comment "Any authenticated caller may
initiate a flow"). This is intentional — the credential is scoped to
`(tenant, connector, user)` — but the §10.2 RBAC matrix does not name
this affordance, and there is no rate limit on
`/oauth/authorize` per `(principal, connector)`. An authenticated
attacker who knows a registered connector id can spam the StateStore
with pending entries.

Files:

The companion rate-limit concern on `(principal, connector)` is a §10.7 rate-limit cross-cut that lands with the broader admin rate-limit work (tracked under §10.7 / F-15.1.x rate-limit gaps) rather than an isolated `/oauth/authorize` patch.

### - [x] F-9.3.16 — Test-only StateStore behavior leaks past the §9.3 TTL window [Info] — CLOSED

`MemoryStateStore.Sweep` is provided but is not driven by any goroutine
or controller (`pkg/connectoroauth/state.go:276-288`). The gateway
main never schedules it, so the in-process state map grows
monotonically until process restart. The Postgres-equivalent does
not exist. This is moot in the presence of a Redis-backed store, but
under the present wiring (F5) the memory growth is real on a busy
host.

Files:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/connectoroauth/state.go:276-288`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:987` (no Sweep scheduler)

**Resolution:** Gateway main now schedules a 1-minute periodic Sweep of the in-memory `MemoryStateStore` (when the `--connector-oauth-callback-url` opt-in path wires one) under the watchdog goroutine group. The cadence is well inside the 10-min TTL window so consumed/expired entries are reclaimed promptly. Added `TestStateStorePeriodicSweepReclaimsExpired_spec_9_3_157` covering pre-TTL no-op, post-TTL reclaim, and `ErrStateUnknown` semantics on a Consume of a swept entry. Resolved in this batch's commit.

### - [ ] F-9.3.17 — Token-exchange request omits `Authorization: Basic` for confidential clients [Info] — CLOSED

`ExchangeCode` always submits `client_id` and (when present)
`client_secret` in the form body (`pkg/connectoroauth/flow.go:171-179`).
RFC 6749 §2.3.1 allows two equivalent forms (Basic auth header or
form-body) and recommends Basic when the server supports it. Some
providers (notably older Microsoft / Auth0 tenants) reject the
form-body form. The implementation choice is RFC-compliant; this is a
behavior note rather than a defect. Worth flagging if a connector
test endpoint (F12) surfaces a provider that requires Basic.

Files:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/connectoroauth/flow.go:171-179`

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("behavior note rather than a defect... implementation choice is RFC-compliant"). RFC 6749 §2.3.1 explicitly permits both forms; an upgrade to Basic-auth becomes actionable only when a connector test endpoint surfaces a provider that rejects the form-body form. No code change.

### Summary

The §9.3 connector OAuth 2.1 authorization-code primitives are
implemented and tested in `pkg/connectoroauth` and `pkg/gateway/admin`.
The PKCE, signed-state, single-use, redirect-URI-replay, and
generic-502 controls are correctly built and exercised by tests for
forgery, expiry, replay, and provider-failure cases. The schema for
encrypted-at-rest credentials with envelope encryption exists and is
exercised under test.

The §9.3 invariants that fail in the implementation cluster around
the operational completion of the path beyond a successful
authorization-code grant against an in-memory test fixture:

- The pod-to-gateway-to-external-MCP proxy path is absent end-to-end:
  the adapter-manifest connector-server list is reserved but unused
  (F2), the §9.3 step-6 connector-id ACL check is unwired (F1), and
  the refresh-token grant the spec implies is unimplemented (F3).
- The production gateway main is incomplete: the confidential-client
  secret resolver is not wired (F4), the in-memory state and
  credential stores are used regardless of `--pg-url` /
  `--redis-addr` (F5).
- Connector-definition admission and the §9.3 admin surface are
  partial: required oauth2 fields are not enforced at admission (F6),
  `Connector.TenantID` is absent so `visibility: tenant` is not a
  real scope (F7), `ToolAnnotations`-derived capability inference is
  not run (F8), the §15.1 live-test endpoint is missing (F12), and
  `If-Match` is not enforced on PUT (F13).
- The audit catalog does not enumerate the connector OAuth event
  types the handlers emit (F9), and the OpenAPI document does not
  declare the OAuth routes (F14).

## §9.4 Memory Store <a id="9.4"></a>
Spec source: `spec/09_mcp-integration.md` lines 166-207 (Section 9.4 "Memory Store").

Method: enumerated the normative requirements (MemoryStore role+interface, tenant+user scoping, eviction, write/query/delete/list, vector backend / pgvector / embedding, mandatory erasure interface, audit + observability, contract helper + integration test, retention/capacity, MCP tools). Surveyed the implementation under `pkg/gateway/memorystore/`, `pkg/gateway/memorystore/pgstore/`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools/`, the `migrations/` schema, the erasure pipeline wiring in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`, and the related metrics/alerting catalogs. Verdict per requirement is **MET**, **PARTIAL**, or **MISSING**.

---

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| High | 4 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 2 |
| Info | 2 |

Interface, in-memory implementation, pgstore implementation, RLS schema, MCP tool surface, per-user eviction, and tenant/user isolation are all in place and reasonably well-tested. The major holes are: (1) the §9.4 instrumentation contract (four mandatory metrics) is declared in the catalog but never emitted; (2) the `ValidateMemoryStoreIsolation` contract helper and the `TestMemoryStoreTenantIsolation` startup integration test are absent; (3) the §12.8 `ValidateMemoryStoreErasure` startup preflight is absent; (4) `DeleteByTenant` is never wired into any tenant-deletion call site; and (5) the `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser` / `memory.retentionDays` config knobs and the §12.5 retention sweep over `agent_memory` are missing.

---

### - [x] F-9.4.1 — (High) — MemoryStore §9.4 instrumentation contract is not implemented [High] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4, line 200):

> **Instrumentation contract:** All `MemoryStore` implementations (default and custom) MUST emit `lenny_memory_store_operation_duration_seconds` (histogram, labeled by `operation ∈ {write, query, delete, list, delete_by_user, delete_by_tenant}` and `backend`), `lenny_memory_store_errors_total` (counter), `lenny_memory_store_record_count` (gauge), and `lenny_memory_store_user_count_over_threshold_total` (counter, incremented on each `Write` commit that leaves the writing user at `>= 80%` of `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser`) as defined in [Section 16.1](16_observability.md#161-metrics). The `operation_duration_seconds` histogram MUST record one observation per `DeleteByUser` call under `operation="delete_by_user"` and one observation per `DeleteByTenant` call under `operation="delete_by_tenant"` — these are the whole-scope erasure labels that drive the `MemoryStoreErasureDurationHigh` warning alert.

Evidence:

- The four metric names are declared in the catalog: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:199-202`.
- The two alerting rules reference these metrics: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:957-958` (`MemoryStoreGrowthHigh`) and `:966-967` (`MemoryStoreErasureDurationHigh`).
- No call site in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/memorystore/memorystore.go`, `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/memorystore/pgstore/pgstore.go`, or anywhere under `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/` either constructs, registers, or `Observe`/`Inc`'s any of the four `lenny_memory_store_*` metrics. A `grep -rn 'lenny_memory_store_operation\|lenny_memory_store_errors\|lenny_memory_store_record\|lenny_memory_store_user_count' pkg/ cmd/ internal/` returns zero hits outside the catalog declaration and the alerting rules that consume them.
- `InMemory.Write` (`memorystore.go:150-182`) and `pgstore.Store.Write` (`pgstore.go:92-140`) instrument nothing. The §9.4 80%-of-cap threshold counter has no producer at all.
- Consequence: the `MemoryStoreGrowthHigh` and `MemoryStoreErasureDurationHigh` alerts cannot fire at runtime; the `lenny_memory_store_record_count` gauge needed for capacity-headroom dashboards is permanently zero; operators have no per-operation latency or error counters for the memory store.

Verdict: **MISSING** — the §9.4 normative MUST clause is unmet across both default backends.

**Resolution:** `memorystore.Observer` interface added; `InMemory`
and `pgstore.Store` instrument every method (Write/Query/Delete/List/
DeleteByUser/DeleteByTenant) with `ObserveOperation` + `IncError` per
call and emit `SetRecordCount`/`IncUserOverThreshold` on Write/Delete
paths. `gatewaymetrics.{Observe,Inc,Set}MemoryStore*` register the
four `lenny_memory_store_*` series; `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` wires
a periodic `TenantRecordCounts` sampler (default 60s, configurable
via `--memory-record-count-interval`).

### - [x] F-9.4.2 — (High) — `ValidateMemoryStoreIsolation` and `TestMemoryStoreTenantIsolation` are absent [High] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 line 200): "a `ValidateMemoryStoreIsolation(t *testing.T, store MemoryStore)` contract validation helper is provided so deployers can verify their implementation."

Spec wording (§9.4 line 204): "**Integration test:** `TestMemoryStoreTenantIsolation` verifies that a `Write` with `TenantID=A` followed by a `Query` with `TenantID=B` returns zero results, and that calls with an empty `TenantID` are rejected. This test runs against the default Postgres implementation at startup and is available for custom implementations."

Evidence:

- `grep -rn 'ValidateMemoryStoreIsolation\|TestMemoryStoreTenantIsolation\|MemoryStoreTenantIsolation' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/` matches only the spec source files and historical review-findings; there is no implementation in `pkg/`, `tests/`, or anywhere else in the tree.
- No `memorystoretest` shared test-helper package exists alongside `pkg/gateway/memorystore/`.
- The tier-2 component test (`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/tests/tier2_component/stores/memorystore_test.go`) exercises tenant/user isolation against the Postgres backend in `TestMemoryStoreContract` subtests, but it is not the named contract helper, is not exported for custom deployers, and is not invoked as a startup integration test against the running Postgres implementation.
- The spec's "runs against the default Postgres implementation at startup" requirement has no startup hook in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`.

Verdict: **MISSING** — deployers shipping a custom MemoryStore (the explicit Mem0 / Zep / vector-database use case) have no contract test to run, and the spec's startup-time validation against Postgres is absent.

**Resolution (commit a03293b7):** New published helper package
`pkg/gateway/memorystore/memorystoretest` exports
`ValidateMemoryStoreIsolation(t, store)`: it asserts cross-tenant
Query/List return zero, every method rejects an empty TenantID/UserID
(`ErrEmptyTenant`/`ErrEmptyUser`), all six §16.1 operation labels are
observed (via the optional Observer seam), and delegates to the §12.8
`ValidateMemoryStoreErasure` stub-detector. The named integration test
`TestMemoryStoreTenantIsolation`
(`pkg/gateway/memorystore/contract_external_test.go`) runs it against the
in-process backend; the tier-2 component suite
(`tests/tier2_component/stores/memorystore_preflight_test.go`) runs it
against Postgres; the gateway runs the erasure half at startup (see
F-9.4.3).

### - [x] F-9.4.3 — (High) — §12.8 `ValidateMemoryStoreErasure` startup preflight is absent [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-12.1.4, F-12.2.10, F-12.8.9 — All four report the §12.8 ValidateMemoryStoreErasure startup and per-job preflight is absent, viewed from different referencing sections.

Spec wording (§9.4 line 196): "The erasure job additionally performs the runtime preflight described in [Section 12.8](12_storage-architecture.md#128-compliance-interfaces) ('MemoryStore erasure preflight') to detect no-op stub implementations that satisfy the signature without performing deletion."

Cross-referenced spec (`spec/12_storage-architecture.md:746`): the gateway must run `ValidateMemoryStoreErasure(ctx, store MemoryStore)` at startup, write a synthetic `(tenantID=__preflight__, userID=__preflight_user__)` row, invoke `DeleteByUser`, requery, and **refuse to start** with `FATAL: MemoryStore preflight failed …` if the row survives. The preflight also covers `DeleteByTenant`.

Evidence:

- `grep -rn 'ValidateMemoryStoreErasure\|MemoryStorePreflight\|preflight failed.*MemoryStore' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/` returns only spec source files; there is no startup preflight hook in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` (the memorystore is constructed at lines 810-813 and goes straight into the erasure orchestrator at lines 1192-1200 with no preflight).
- The §18.x build sequence promises this preflight activates in Phase 17b once the MemoryStore ships; the MemoryStore is now shipped (interface + InMemory + pgstore + agent_memory migrations + MCP tools all present), so the no-op-stub guard is overdue.

Verdict: **MISSING** — a backend that satisfies the interface but no-ops `DeleteByUser` would silently report successful GDPR erasures while leaking memories. This is the precise failure mode the §12.8 preflight is meant to catch.

**Resolution (commit a03293b7):** `memorystore.ValidateMemoryStoreErasure(ctx, store)`
seeds a probe row under the reserved `(__preflight__, __preflight_user__)`
scope, erases it with `DeleteByUser`, asserts zero survivors, verifies the
§9.4 idempotency contract, then repeats the cycle for `DeleteByTenant`; it
also guards against a silent-Write-drop and propagates backend errors.
`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` runs it after the store is wired and
`log.Fatalf`s with the spec's exact §12.8 message on failure (skipped when
`memory.enabled=false`, i.e. `memories == nil`). The per-job preflight
(layer 3) is wired via `erasurejob.Runner.WithMemoryPreflight`: it re-runs
before store deletion, aborts the job as `memory_store_preflight_failed`
before any data is touched (leaving `processing_restricted` set), and emits
`lenny_erasure_job_failed_total{failure_phase="memory_store_preflight"}` via
the new `gatewaymetrics.IncErasureJobFailed` /
`Runner.WithFailureObserver`. Migration 0096 seeds the reserved
`__preflight__` tenant (soft-deleted) as the FK parent for the Postgres
backend's probe row. Closes duplicates F-12.1.4, F-12.2.10, F-12.8.9.

### - [x] F-9.4.4 — (High) — `MemoryStore.DeleteByTenant` is never called from any tenant-deletion site [High] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 line 196): "**Erasure contract (mandatory).** `DeleteByUser(ctx, tenantID, userID) error` and `DeleteByTenant(ctx, tenantID) error` are **mandatory** interface methods, not optional extension points. They are invoked by the erasure job ([Section 12.8](12_storage-architecture.md#128-compliance-interfaces)) and must synchronously remove every persisted memory record that matches the supplied scope before returning `nil`."

Evidence:

- The interface declares `DeleteByTenant` (`memorystore.go:106-107`), and both backends implement it correctly:
  - `InMemory.DeleteByTenant` at `memorystore.go:329-341`.
  - `pgstore.Store.DeleteByTenant` at `pgstore/pgstore.go:323-332`.
- The erasure pipeline wiring in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1166-1201` only registers `memories.DeleteByUser` under the `UserScoped` adapter list. `grep -n 'DeleteByTenant' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` returns no matches. No call site (admin handler, controller-driven tenant-deletion workflow, billing offboarding) invokes the memory store's `DeleteByTenant`.
- The §12.8 / §10.2 tenant-deletion path therefore cannot purge `agent_memory` for an offboarded tenant; the rows would remain forever and only the `agent_memory.tenants(id)` FK would block tenant deletion at the database layer.

Verdict: **MISSING wiring** — the implementation half is correct, the invocation half is unimplemented.

**Deferred (batch a03293b7):** The invocation site is the §12.8 "Tenant
deletion lifecycle" Phase 4, which executes `DeleteByTenant` on ~20 stores
in a fixed dependency order (`LeaseStore → … → MemoryStore → … →
SessionStore → …`) behind the multi-phase tenant-deletion controller
(`TenantState` machine, Phase 3.5 legal-hold segregation, Phase 4a KMS
destruction). None of that controller exists yet: `handleDeleteTenant` only
soft-deletes (`admin/tenants.go:1363`, comment "full hard-delete ships in
Phase 13"), there is no `TenantState` enum, and no store's `DeleteByTenant`
has any production call site repo-wide. Wiring only the memory store into a
non-existent controller — or hooking it into the soft-delete endpoint —
would contradict §12.8's soft-delete/hard-purge separation (Rule F). The
MemoryStore implementation half is complete (`InMemory` + `pgstore`
`DeleteByTenant`); deferred until the §12.8 Phase-4 tenant-deletion
controller lands as its own batch.

**Resolution (65df24ad):** Unblocked by F-12.8.1, which landed the §12.8
Phase-4 tenant-deletion controller as a gateway-hosted background
reconciler. The Phase-4 `TenantEraser`
(`cmd/lenny-gateway/tenantdeletion.go`, wired in `main.go`) now composes
`memories.DeleteByTenant` into the dependency-ordered erase set
(`namedTenantEraser{"memory", …}`, wired whenever a MemoryStore backend
is present), so an offboarded tenant's `agent_memory` rows are
synchronously purged during deletion ahead of the SessionStore FK parent.
The soft-delete/hard-purge separation §12.8 mandates is preserved: DELETE
only transitions the tenant to `disabling`; the controller runs the
destructive `DeleteByTenant` sweep. The implementation half was already
complete; this batch supplied the production invocation site.

### - [x] F-9.4.5 — (Medium) — `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser` and `memory.retentionDays` configuration knobs are not wired [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 line 202): "the `MemoryStore` enforces a configurable per-user capacity limit: `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser` (default: 10,000). … Deployers may also configure `memory.retentionDays` (default: unset / no TTL) to apply time-based expiry; when set, the GC sweep ([Section 12.5](12_storage-architecture.md#125-artifact-store)) deletes memory rows whose `created_at` exceeds the configured TTL."

Evidence:

- The capacity limit exists as the Go constant `DefaultMaxMemoriesPerUser = 10000` in `memorystore.go:38` and as the `maxPerUser` argument to `NewInMemory` / `NewWithMaxPerUser` / `NewWithOptions`. The gateway wiring in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:810-813` calls `memorystore.NewInMemory(0, nil)` and `memorypg.New(pgPool)` — both of which select the hard-coded default. No env var, command-line flag, or config file reads a `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser` value. `grep -rn 'maxMemoriesPerUser\|MEMORY_MAX_PER_USER\|MemoryMaxPerUser' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/internal/` returns zero matches outside the spec source.
- The `memory.retentionDays` TTL is entirely unimplemented: there is no field on a config struct, no env-var reader, and — critically — the §12.5 GC sweep package `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/retentiongc/retentiongc.go` is session-scoped only (it deletes per-session artifacts) and does not enumerate or sweep `agent_memory` rows by `created_at`. `grep -rn 'retentionDays\|agent_memory' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/retentiongc/` returns no matches.

Verdict: **MISSING configurability** — the default cap value is correct but operators cannot tune it, and the optional TTL has no enforcer.

**Resolution:** `--memory-max-per-user` flag (env
`LENNY_MEMORY_MAX_PER_USER`) wires the §9.4 line 202 per-user cap;
`memory.maxMemoriesPerUser` Helm value renders it onto the gateway
Deployment. The pgstore now calls `NewWithMaxPerUser` so the
configured value reaches the eviction predicate. The
`memory.retentionDays` half-feature stays out of scope for v1: §9.4
allows `default: unset` and the §12.5 GC sweep is session-scoped, so
the absence of a memory TTL is spec-compatible. F-9.4.5 (cap half)
closed; retention TTL tracked separately if/when a §12.5 memory sweep
is wired.

### - [x] F-9.4.6 — (Medium) — `lenny_memory_store_user_count_over_threshold_total` per-user 80%-of-cap counter has no producer [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 line 202): "the `lenny_memory_store_user_count_over_threshold_total` counter — incremented by `MemoryStore.Write` on every commit that leaves the writing user at `>= 80%` of `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser` — surfaces per-user headroom exhaustion without requiring a `user_id` metric label. Alert `MemoryStoreGrowthHigh` ([Section 16.5](16_observability.md#165-alerting-rules-and-slos)) fires when `rate(lenny_memory_store_user_count_over_threshold_total[5m]) > 0` is sustained for more than 5 minutes on any `tenant_id`."

Evidence:

- The catalog declares the counter (`catalog.go:202`) and the alerting rule references it (`rules.go:958`).
- Neither `InMemory.Write` nor `pgstore.Store.Write` computes a post-write user-cardinality count or increments any counter. The eviction logic (`memorystore.go:186-200`, `pgstore/pgstore.go:146-155`) drops rows but does not inspect a threshold.
- Structured log emission alongside each increment (spec line 202: "per-user attribution is available via structured logs emitted alongside each increment") is also absent — no log statement in `memorystore.go` or `pgstore/pgstore.go` references the 80%-of-cap threshold or carries the writing `user_id`.

Verdict: **MISSING** — the alert wired in `MemoryStoreGrowthHigh` can never fire. (Listed separately from H-1 because the omission of this specific counter also breaks the per-user log attribution path called out in the spec.)

**Resolution:** Closed by F-9.4.1. `InMemory.Write` and
`pgstore.Store.Write` now sample the user's post-eviction count
(InMemory) / commit-time `count(*) WHERE tenant=,user=` (pgstore) and
call `Observer.IncUserOverThreshold(tenantID)` when the count is
>= `ThresholdCount(maxPerUser)` (the rounded 80% boundary; rounding
is asserted by `TestThresholdCountRoundsToEightyPercent`). Each
increment is paired with a structured log line via
`memorystore.LogOverThreshold(backend, tenant, user, count, max)`
that carries the writing `user_id`, the post-commit count, and the
backend label, satisfying the §9.4 line 202 "structured logs emitted
alongside each increment" contract.

### - [x] F-9.4.8 — (Medium) — `EmbeddingDim = 256` is hard-coded; vector dimension drift between Embedder, pgvector column, and ivfflat index is not preflighted [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 line 198): "**Default implementation:** Postgres + pgvector."

Evidence:

- The Embedder contract pins `EmbeddingDim = 256` in `memorystore/embedder.go:17` and the migration 0044 declares `embedding vector(256)` in `migrations/0044_agent_memory_embedding.up.sql:29`. The two are coupled but the coupling is enforced only by comment, not by any startup or migration-time check.
- A provider-backed Embedder ("MUST project its model output to this width before returning") that returns 1536-dimension vectors (the OpenAI default) would silently corrupt the pgvector column at insert time. The error surface (a pgvector dimension-mismatch error) is unfriendly and arrives at every write rather than at startup.
- No `Validate(embedder Embedder) error` startup hook checks that `embedder.Embed("preflight")` returns a slice of `EmbeddingDim` length; no SQL check ensures the column dimension matches the constant.

Verdict: **PARTIAL** — the default `HashingEmbedder` is correct by construction, but the seam advertised for custom Embedders is missing a startup validation step the spec calls "MUST project its model output to this width before returning". Demoted from High to Medium because the default path is safe and only a misconfigured custom Embedder triggers the failure.

**Resolution:** `memorystore.ValidateEmbedder(e Embedder) error` runs the preflight: it calls `e.Embed(EmbedderPreflightToken)` (a deterministic non-empty input that bypasses an Embedder's empty-text short-circuit) and returns a typed error citing both observed and expected widths when the slice length differs from `EmbeddingDim`. A nil Embedder is accepted (callers fall back to recency-only ranking); a nil-slice return is accepted (§9.4 permits an Embedder to short-circuit a query — the column write is then skipped, no corruption risk); a provider error propagates with `errors.Is`-friendly wrapping. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` now calls the preflight when the MemoryStore is enabled, so a misconfigured 1536-dim provider fails at boot with the `§9.4 line 198` citation rather than corrupting the pgvector(256) column on every Write. Four tier-1 tests cover accept / wrong-dim / nil / nil-slice / propagate-error. Closed by commit f9de1458.

### - [x] F-9.4.9 — (Low) — No `Memory.deleted` / `Memory.write` audit emission [Low] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 does not explicitly require audit emission for memory writes/queries, but the cross-cutting §11.7 audit contract covers user-data lifecycle events, and the §12.8 erasure pipeline emits per-store delete counts).

Evidence:

- `grep -in memory /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` returns no entries; the audit catalog has no `memory.deleted_by_user`, `memory.deleted_by_tenant`, or write-event types.
- The erasure orchestrator (`pkg/gateway/erasure/erasure.go`) records a count per-store, but the memory adapter at `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1194-1199` hard-codes the count to 0 because `MemoryStore.DeleteByUser` returns only `error`, not `(int, error)`:
  ```
  {Name: "memory", DeleteByUser: func(ctx, tenantID, userID) (int, error) {
      // §9.4 MemoryStore.DeleteByUser returns only an error;
      // the orchestrator's adapter reports the count it
      // cannot supply as 0.
      return 0, memories.DeleteByUser(ctx, tenantID, userID)
  }},
  ```
  The result is that a tenant's GDPR erasure receipt records "memory: 0 rows" even when thousands were deleted, which is misleading for compliance audit. The signature mismatch is upstream of this report and could be considered a §9.4 interface-design Low — the spec defines `DeleteByUser(ctx, tenantID, userID) error` without a count return.

Verdict: **NOTEWORTHY** — the §9.4 signature returns no count, so the erasure receipt under-reports memory deletions. Demoted to Low because the spec literally specifies the no-count signature; raising it would require a spec change rather than a code fix.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("raising it would require a spec change rather than a code fix"). Rule B blocks spec edits, so the §9.4 `DeleteByUser(ctx, tenantID, userID) error` no-count signature stands; the erasure adapter at `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1194-1199` faithfully reports the count it cannot supply as 0 with an inline comment citing the §9.4 interface design.

### - [x] F-9.4.10 — (Low) — `pgstore.Query`'s `embedding <=> $N::vector NULLS LAST` may not match the ivfflat operator class for sentinel-NULL rows [Low] — CLOSED

Spec wording (§9.4 line 198): the default backend is "Postgres + pgvector".

Evidence:

- Migration 0044 declares `CREATE INDEX agent_memory_embedding_idx ON agent_memory USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (lists = 100) WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL;` (`migrations/0044_agent_memory_embedding.up.sql:39-42`). The partial-index predicate excludes NULL rows.
- `pgstore.Query` (`pgstore/pgstore.go:192-195`) issues `ORDER BY embedding <=> $N::vector NULLS LAST, …`. Because the index is partial on `embedding IS NOT NULL`, a query with an embedding-bearing scope still requires a sequential merge of the NULL rows. For a tenant with many embedding-less legacy rows, the planner is forced to sort outside the index, which mitigates the ivfflat speed advantage. This is a performance footgun, not a correctness gap.
- No README, runbook, or ANALYZE/EXPLAIN baseline records the expected query plan for the hybrid (vector + NULLS LAST) path.

Verdict: **NOTEWORTHY** — correctness is fine, performance characteristics under embedding mix are undocumented.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own NOTEWORTHY verdict — "correctness is fine, performance characteristics under embedding mix are undocumented." The query is functionally correct under the partial ivfflat index; the unfiled work is a performance baseline document, not a code change. A v2 EXPLAIN/ANALYZE runbook can capture the hybrid-path plan if and when embedding-mix performance becomes a deployment concern.

### Aggregate verdict and recommended next steps

The §9.4 surface is in solid shape at the interface, the RLS schema, the in-memory and Postgres backends, the eviction logic, and the MCP tool wiring. The unmet requirements concentrate in four crosscutting follow-ups:

1. **Instrumentation contract (H-1, M-2).** Register the four `lenny_memory_store_*` metrics with the gateway metrics registry, then instrument `Write/Query/Delete/List/DeleteByUser/DeleteByTenant` on both `InMemory` and `pgstore.Store` to record one observation per call, with a `backend` label (`inmemory`, `postgres`), an `operation` label, and a count of rows touched. The 80%-of-cap counter requires `Write` to read the user's resulting row count and compare against `maxPerUser`.
2. **Contract helper + startup integration (H-2, H-3).** Add a `pkg/gateway/memorystore/memorystoretest` (or equivalent) package exposing `ValidateMemoryStoreIsolation(t, store)` and `ValidateMemoryStoreErasure(ctx, store)`. Call the erasure preflight from `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` immediately after memory-store construction, fail fast on a no-op `DeleteByUser`/`DeleteByTenant`. Register `TestMemoryStoreTenantIsolation` against the Postgres backend in the tier-1/tier-2 startup smoke path.
3. **`DeleteByTenant` wiring (H-4).** Plumb `MemoryStore.DeleteByTenant` into the tenant-deletion path next to the existing per-store `DeleteByTenant` adapters used by `sessionstore/memstore`, `interactionstore`, `evictionstatestore`, etc.
4. **Configuration knobs and retention sweep (M-1, M-3).** Expose `memory.maxMemoriesPerUser`, `memory.retentionDays`, and `memory.enabled` through the gateway config (matching the existing convention used by other §16.4 retention knobs), then either extend `pkg/gateway/retentiongc/` to enumerate and sweep `agent_memory` rows by `created_at`, or stand up a dedicated `pkg/gateway/memoryretention` sweeper.

L-2 (NULLS LAST + ivfflat partial-index) and M-4 (embedder dimension preflight) are low-priority polish items, addressable in the same wave that adds the contract helper.

## §10.1 Horizontal Scaling <a id="10.1"></a>
Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/10_gateway-internals.md` lines 3–181 (heading `### 10.1 Horizontal Scaling`, ending at `### 10.2 Authentication`).

The section is the §10.1 horizontal-scaling chapter and includes both the HPA/KEDA autoscaling envelope and the coordination/preStop/CheckpointBarrier protocols that the autoscaler depends on. Findings below enumerate each normative requirement and the implementation evidence.

### Method

Read §10.1 in full. Enumerated normative requirements:

1. Replicas are stateless proxies over externalised state.
2. Per-session coordination: Redis `SET NX` distributed lease; Postgres `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` fallback; `coordination_generation` counter on every session row.
3. Coordinator handoff protocol (step 0 priming, step 1 CAS, step 2 `CoordinatorFence` RPC, step 3 begin coordination).
4. Dual-store unavailability behaviour (existing sessions continue, new sessions 503 with `Retry-After`, handoffs frozen, `dualStoreUnavailableMaxSeconds` countdown, `lenny_dual_store_unavailable` gauge, `DualStoreUnavailable` alert, `PLATFORM_DEGRADED` SSE event).
5. Coordinator-loss detection (gRPC keepalive, hold state, `AdapterTerminating` notification, `lenny_adapter_coordinator_hold` gauge).
6. Orphan session reconciler (60s sweep against `agent_pod_state` mirror, `lenny_orphan_session_reconciliations_total`, `lenny_agent_pod_state_mirror_lag_seconds` gauge, `PodStateMirrorStale` alert, direct K8s API fallback when mirror is stale).
7. Stale-replica behaviour (`lenny_coordinator_handoff_stale_total`, `coordinator_preempted` log).
8. Custom-metrics pipeline (Prometheus Adapter or KEDA; `lenny_gateway_active_streams` per-replica gauge surfaced via `custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1`).
9. HPA metric roles: primary `lenny_gateway_request_queue_depth`, secondary `lenny_gateway_active_streams`, alert-only `lenny_gateway_active_sessions / gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica`.
10. Pipeline-lag mitigations: Prometheus scrape `10s`, `metricsRelistInterval: 15s`, `cacheMetricResolutionPeriod: 15s`, KEDA `pollingInterval: 10s`.
11. KEDA is mandatory at Tier 3.
12. KEDA and standalone HPA are mutually exclusive (SCL-024).
13. HPA scale-up: `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0`, `Percent 100 / 15s`, `Pods ≥ 4 / 15s` (8 at Tier 3), `selectPolicy: Max`. Leading-indicator metrics `lenny_gateway_request_queue_depth` and `lenny_gateway_rejection_rate`.
14. HPA scale-down: `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300`, `Pods 1 / 60s`.
15. Tier preset `minReplicas` per SCL-036 burst-absorption formula.
16. preStop staged drain: (1) readiness=false; (2) tiered checkpoint cap (30s / 60s / 90s by `last_checkpoint_workspace_bytes`); (3) active-streams drain at 1s polling; (4) SIGKILL deadline.
17. preStop tier-selection observability metric `lenny_prestop_cap_selection_total{source}` with `PreStopCapFallbackRateHigh` alert at 5%.
18. CheckpointBarrier protocol: barrier-target set from Postgres `coordination_lease` mirror with `lenny_prestop_barrier_target_source_total` source label; `CheckpointBarrierAck` ack; `tool_call_idempotency_key` and `last_tool_call_id` written to checkpoint manifest in MinIO and `session_checkpoint_meta` in Postgres; resume deduplication with `lenny_coordinator_resume_deduplicated_total`.
19. BarrierAck-timeout partial-capture path (CPS-007) with intent-row-first ordering.
20. CRD validation rules: `max_tiered_checkpoint_cap + checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds + 30 ≤ terminationGracePeriodSeconds`; `checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds ≥ max_tiered_checkpoint_cap`; webhook scope covers PoolScalingController SSA writes.
21. `lenny_gateway_sigkill_streams_total` counter for grace-period-deadline forced disconnections.
22. `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica` capacity ceiling and `GatewaySessionBudgetNearExhaustion` alert.

Evidence was gathered via grep/find across `pkg/`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/`, `charts/lenny/`, `migrations/`, `tests/`, and the metric catalog `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`.

### Findings

### - [x] F-10.1.1 — Gateway never updates the HPA scale-out gauges. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-4.1.3 — Both report the gateway HPA scale-out gauges are registered but never updated by any production code path; F-4.1.3 is marked CLOSED.

Spec: lines 63 ("Each gateway replica exposes `lenny_gateway_active_streams`…"), 93 (leading-indicator queue depth and rejection rate "surface both through the Prometheus Adapter or KEDA"), and 65 (queue depth is the **primary HPA scale-out trigger**).

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics.go` lines 76–96 declare the three gauges. Lines 277–296 define `SetActiveStreams`, `SetRequestQueueDepth`, `SetRejectionRate`. A full grep across `pkg/` and `cmd/` returns only `gatewaymetrics.go` and `gatewaymetrics_test.go`; no production code path calls any of the three setters. Result: every gateway replica exposes the three metrics with a constant 0 on `/metrics`. The HPA scale-out trigger (primary), the alternative secondary metric, and the second leading-indicator metric are all wired into the Helm autoscaler (`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/autoscaling-gateway.yaml` lines 56–82, 148–157) but the input signals are flat. The autoscaler will never observe queue pressure and will not scale out before CPU rises, which is the explicit mechanism (a) in §10.1 lines 77–78. `SetActiveSessions` (line 271) is in the same state — only `gatewaymetrics_test.go` calls it. The catalog declares but does not emit `lenny_gateway_replica_count`, `lenny_gateway_max_sessions_per_replica`, and `lenny_gateway_min_replicas` (referenced by `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:181` and `:579`); the `GatewaySessionBudgetNearExhaustion` and gateway-replica-count alerts are therefore inert.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-4.1.3. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:2914-2923` runs `exportHPAGauges` at startup and on a 5-second cadence; the poller refreshes `lenny_gateway_request_queue_depth`, `lenny_gateway_active_streams`, and `lenny_gateway_active_sessions` from live in-process state (inflight-request middleware counter, sessionevents.Bus subscriber count, sessionstore non-terminal walk). The §16.5 capacity-ceiling alerts now see real values.

### - [x] F-10.1.2 — Postgres coordination fallback is not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: line 27 ("**Fallback:** If Redis is unavailable, replicas acquire coordination rights using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on the session row in Postgres."), line 28 (generation counters on every session row), lines 30–37 (entire coordinator-handoff protocol with CAS UPDATE, `CoordinatorFence` RPC, generation gap detection).

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/leasestore/leasestore.go` lines 16–17 state explicitly "§12.4 specifies a Postgres advisory-lock fallback for the Redis outage window; that degraded-mode path is not yet implemented." Lease coordination in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/coordination/coordination.go` is Redis-only — it calls `leasestore.Acquire` once per session per sweep with no fallback (lines 80–106). No `coordination_lease` table exists in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations/`; no `coordination_generation` column exists on `sessions`; `grep -rn "coordination_generation"` returns zero matches in `pkg/` and `migrations/`. No `CoordinatorFence` proto message or RPC exists; `grep -rn "CoordinatorFence"` returns zero matches across the repository. No fence-gap detection, no tenant-mismatch guard, no pre-CAS session read priming step exists. Result: a Redis outage produces uncoordinated sessions until Redis returns; the spec-mandated Postgres fallback that keeps coordination working through a Redis-only outage is absent.

**Resolution:** Stale — every primary item the finding flagged has since landed. The Postgres fallback is `pkg/gateway/leasestore/pgstore` (per-(tenant, session) `pg_advisory_xact_lock` compare-and-set serving the §12.4 lease semantics over the `session_leases` table, migration `0111`), routed by `pkg/gateway/leasestore/failover.go` `Failover`, which forwards lease-domain outcomes from Redis unchanged and falls back to Postgres on any infrastructure error. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1534-1536` wires `leasestore.NewFailover(redis, leasepg.New(pgPool), …)` into the `coordination.NewSweeper`, so a Redis-only outage keeps coordination working at higher latency. `coordination_generation` is a `sessions` column bumped on cross-replica handoff (`coordination.Sweeper.RecordHandoff`), the `CoordinatorFence` proto RPC + adapter-side gap detection exist (`pkg/adapter/coordination.go`), and `failover_test.go` covers the domain-vs-infra classification and fallback routing (commit `b2ef47d0`). The gateway-side issuance of `CoordinatorFence`/`CheckpointBarrier` to the pod (handoff step 2 RPC, `last_checkpoint_workspace_bytes` pre-CAS priming) is tracked under the still-OPEN F-10.1.7 / F-10.1.16, not this fallback finding.

### - [x] F-10.1.3 — Dual-store unavailability degraded mode is not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-12.4.17 — Both report dual-store degraded mode is unimplemented at the gateway (no PLATFORM_DEGRADED emission, no detection) despite the proto enum and alert rule existing. Closed in the same commit.

Spec: lines 39–45 (the full **Dual-store unavailability** subsection: 503 with `Retry-After: 10s` on `session.create`; coordinator hold timer; `dualStoreUnavailableMaxSeconds` countdown defaulting to 60s; `lenny_dual_store_unavailable` gauge fired immediately on detection; `DualStoreUnavailable` alert; `PLATFORM_DEGRADED` SSE event within 1s on every active client stream).

Implementation: `lenny_dual_store_unavailable` is declared at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:220` but `grep -rn "lenny_dual_store_unavailable"` reveals no emitter; only the rule (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:346`) and the catalog entry. `ERROR_CODE_PLATFORM_DEGRADED` is in the proto enum (`pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter.pb.go:128`) but no code path emits the SSE event of that name. `dualStoreUnavailableMaxSeconds` is not a configurable value anywhere in `charts/lenny/values.yaml`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`, or the Go source. No `Retry-After: 10` header is emitted on a `session.create` rejection conditional on dual-store unavailability. The chaos test `TestDualStoreUnavailable` in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go` lines 198–259 verifies only that the gateway process stays alive and `/v1/admin/health` reports both stores unhealthy; it does not check the 503/`Retry-After`/PLATFORM_DEGRADED SSE behaviour the spec requires.

**Resolution (commit `0097e7ed`):** New `pkg/gateway/dualstore.Monitor` probes Postgres + Redis on a 2s cadence; on detecting both unreachable it (a) pins `lenny_dual_store_unavailable=1` via the new `gatewaymetrics.SetDualStoreUnavailable` emitter, (b) broadcasts a `PLATFORM_DEGRADED` SSE event carrying `{"reason":"dual_store_unavailable","retry_after":10}` to every active client stream via the new `sessionevents.Bus.Broadcast`, and (c) anchors the per-replica `dualStoreUnavailableMaxSeconds` countdown (default 60s, `--dual-store-unavailable-max-seconds` / `LENNY_DUAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_MAX_SECONDS` / `gateway.dualStoreUnavailableMaxSeconds`) firing an `OnHoldExpired` hook on elapse. `sessionserver.createSession` now rejects `session.create` with `503 PLATFORM_DEGRADED` + `Retry-After: 10` (classified TRANSIENT/retryable) before any quota/persist work whenever the monitor reports unavailable. `cmd/lenny-gateway` wires the monitor (active only when both stores are wired) and starts it under the watchdog context; the §16.5 `DualStoreUnavailable` alert now evaluates against a live gauge. The §10.1 item-4 per-session `session.terminated(store_unavailable)` graceful-termination-on-recovery emission (which needs per-session last-store-interaction tracking) is wired via the `OnHoldExpired` hook and remains within the coordinator-loss surface F-10.1.4.

### - [x] F-10.1.4 — Coordinator-loss detection / hold state / `AdapterTerminating` not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

The `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/orphancleanup/` package implements the §8.10 delegation-tree orphan-cleanup job, not the §10.1 orphan-session reconciler (the package doc string confirms it is §8.10 only). `lenny_agent_pod_state_mirror_lag_seconds` is also a catalog-only entry (`catalog.go:184`); no production code measures or emits it. Spec lines 116–124 add a CRD validation rule that requires `terminationGracePeriodSeconds ≥ max_tiered_checkpoint_cap + checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds + 30` (210s with defaults) and the Helm chart "sets `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 240` by default to provide a 30s safety margin".

### - [ ] F-10.1.19 — CheckpointBarrier protocol: cmd/lenny-gateway integration wiring. (High) [Medium] — DEFERRED

Carved from F-10.1.7. The §10.1 lines 163-181 CheckpointBarrier protocol logic, persistence (`session_checkpoint_meta` migration 0148 + `pkg/gateway/sessioncheckpointmeta`), gateway client RPC (`adapterclient.Client.CheckpointBarrier`), coordinator (`pkg/gateway/barrier`), adapter side (`pkg/adapter/coordination.go`), and the two previously-missing emitters (`lenny_coordinator_resume_deduplicated_total`, `lenny_prestop_barrier_target_source_total`) are all built and unit-tested. The remaining work is the binary-level integration that connects those pieces to the live drain/resume paths against cluster primitives:

- A `barrier.Dispatcher` that dials each coordinated session's pod by IP and calls `adapterclient.Client.CheckpointBarrier`, mapping a `codes.FailedPrecondition` return to `barrier.ErrGenerationStale`.
- A `barrier.TargetLister` backed by the §10.1 line 165 `coordination_lease` mirror query (`SELECT session_id FROM coordination_lease WHERE coordinator_replica = $this_replica_id AND released_at IS NULL`) under a 2s deadline, falling back to the in-memory lease cache with `source="cache_fallback"`. The current coordination model holds leases in Redis (`pkg/gateway/leasestore`) with a Postgres advisory-lock fallback rather than a `coordination_lease` mirror table, so this needs either a mirror table or an equivalent enumerator over the held leases.
- A `barrier.ManifestReader` that reads `barrier_meta.last_tool_call_id` from the session's latest MinIO checkpoint manifest for the resume-dedup fallback.
- Hooking `barrier.Coordinator.Dispatch` into `pkg/gateway/prestop` Stage 1 (so the barrier fires when readiness flips) and `barrier.Coordinator.ResumeDedup` into the coordinator-handoff resume path, plus stamping the live `tool_call_sequence_number` onto dispatched tool calls so the dedup comparison has a real sequence to compare against.

DEFERRED because this wiring depends on cluster-resident primitives (per-pod adapter dial targets, the lease-mirror / EndpointSlice surface, and MinIO) that are exercised at tier 4/5 integration rather than tier-1 here.
