## §10.6 Environment Resource and RBAC Model <a id="10.6"></a>
Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/10_gateway-internals.md` lines 550–675.

### Method

§10.6 was enumerated into normative requirements covering the Environment
resource and its admin CRUD; the closed `viewer`/`creator`/`operator`/`admin`
role enum; tag-based runtime and connector selection with `include`/`exclude`
overrides and `types` filter; `mcpRuntimeFilters` capability filtering;
`connectorSelector` with `allowedCapabilities`/`deniedCapabilities`; the
two access paths (transparent filtering + explicit endpoint); the structured
bilateral `crossEnvironmentDelegation` model and the four-step delegation
enforcement order; `defaultDelegationPolicy`; `noEnvironmentPolicy` semantics
and audit interceptor; OIDC group identity with `introspectionEnabled`; the
billing-rollup `environmentId`; the Tenant RBAC Config payload
(`identityProvider`, `tokenPolicy`, `capabilities`, `mcpAnnotationMapping`);
and the v1 data-model accommodations enumerated at the foot of the section.

Each was traced through `pkg/environment/`, `pkg/gateway/admin/`,
`pkg/gateway/environmentstore/`, `pkg/gateway/middleware/environment/`,
`pkg/gateway/envaccess/`, `pkg/auth/`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/`,
`pkg/gateway/mcptools/`, `pkg/gateway/billingstore/`,
`pkg/gateway/tenantstore/`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`, and the SQL
migrations under `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations/`. Tests under the
corresponding `_test.go` files were inspected for coverage.

### Findings

### - [x] F-10.6.1 — 01  Explicit-environment session endpoint does not check membership of the named environment [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-10.6.5 — Both concern environment access control, but one is the missing membership check on the explicit endpoint and the other is the absence of role-level enforcement beyond membership.

**Spec:** §10.6 lines 554–557 — explicit-environment endpoint is one of
two access paths. §10.6 line 555 explicitly contrasts it with transparent
filtering (which computes the union "across all environments where the
user's groups have a role"). The explicit form `/v1/environments/{name}/sessions`
is "opt-in" and must therefore verify the caller actually has a role in
the named environment. Otherwise the explicit path bypasses the RBAC
boundary the transparent path enforces.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go`
lines 588–599 `handleEnvironmentSessions` lifts the env name from the URL
and assigns it to `req.Environment`, then calls `createSession` with no
additional check. `createSession` at lines 620–685 runs the active-user
gate, quota gate, policy chain, isolation-profile validation, and
workspace-plan validation, then persists the row. It never consults the
environment registry to confirm (a) the named environment exists in the
caller's tenant, (b) the caller's subject or OIDC groups hold any role in
it, or (c) the supplied `runtimeRef` is admitted by that environment's
`runtimeSelector`. The test
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/create_test.go`
lines 167–197 explicitly verifies that the handler accepts a free-form
environment name (`security-team`) without any membership check and
records it on the row, confirming this is the implemented behavior. The
sibling test at lines 200–229 confirms a body-supplied environment is
silently overridden by the path, again without consulting the registry.

**Classification:** High — the explicit-environment endpoint is the
opt-in RBAC scope and must enforce membership. Today any authenticated
caller in the tenant can create a session "in" any environment name
(even one that does not exist) and the session row stores that
environment, granting the session whatever downstream privilege the
environment name confers (cross-environment delegation reach via
`crossEnvReachable` at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`
lines 1238–1268 explicitly bridges through `parent.Environment`, gated
only by `memberOfEnvironment(res, parent.Environment)` — but that check
runs at delegate time, not at session-create time, and a session in an
environment the caller does not belong to is still persisted and
auditable). The explicit endpoint is a confused-deputy hole.

**Resolution (2c91f2b5):** `requireEnvironmentAdmission` now routes a
session create that names an environment through a new
`requireExplicitEnvironmentAdmission` branch (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes.go`).
It rejects with 403 FORBIDDEN when (a) the named environment is not
defined in the caller's tenant (`environment_not_found`), (b) the caller
holds no role in it (`not_environment_member`), or (c) the requested
runtime is not admitted by the environment's `runtimeSelector`
(`runtime_not_in_environment`). The gate is nil-safe (no registry / no
principal passes through, preserving the dev-header posture). Role
enforcement is the §10.6 line 605 check shared with F-10.6.5. Six tier-1
tests in `create_test.go` cover the unknown/non-member/out-of-scope-runtime
rejections, the creator-admitted path, and the no-principal pass-through.

### - [x] F-10.6.2 — 02  `mcpRuntimeFilters` capability filtering is stored but never enforced [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 lines 588–593 and line 607 — "**`mcpRuntimeFilters`** —
capability-based tool filtering for `type: mcp` runtimes. Capabilities
inferred from MCP `ToolAnnotations` … Name collisions resolved by
`runtime:tool` qualified reference in `overrides`." The structured form
in the YAML at lines 588–593 carries `allowedCapabilities`/`deniedCapabilities`
keyed on `read`/`write`/`delete`/`execute`/`admin` capabilities.

**Implementation:** The data type
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/environmentstore/environmentstore.go`
lines 41–47 defines `MCPRuntimeFilter` with `AllowedCapabilities` and
`DeniedCapabilities`. It is round-tripped through the admin API
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/environments.go` lines 51–57,
145–151, 176–182), persisted to Postgres
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/environmentstore/pgstore/pgstore.go`
lines 59, 71, 83), and validated (`environmentstore.go` lines 114–118).
The `pkg/gateway/capabilityinference` package supplies the capability
inference primitive from MCP `ToolAnnotations`. No code path consumes
`MCPRuntimeFilters` to decide whether a particular MCP tool invocation
is admitted: a grep across the tree for `MCPRuntimeFilters` outside the
storage / admin / test / OpenAPI layers returns zero matches in tool
dispatch (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/`), in the MCP proxy
(`pkg/gateway/mcp/`), or in the connector dispatcher
(`pkg/gateway/connectorstore/`). The admin runtime-exposure handler at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/environment_runtime_exposure.go`
lines 44–47 confirms the design intent — "Capability filtering
(mcpRuntimeFilters, connector capabilities) governs what an admitted
resource may do, not whether it is in scope" — but that downstream
"what it may do" enforcement is absent.

**Classification:** High — capability-based tool filtering is a stated
authorization boundary. An admin who writes `deniedCapabilities: [write,
delete, admin]` on a security-team environment today has no effect on
what tools the agents in that environment may invoke against a matching
mcp runtime.

**Resolution:** Added a reusable §10.6 capability-filter evaluator to
`environmentstore` (`PermitCapabilities` + `ConnectorSelector.PermitTool`/
`Admits`, `MCPRuntimeFilter.PermitTool`/`Admits`,
`Environment.MCPRuntimeFilterFor`): deny-list wins, a non-empty allow-list
requires every tool capability to be listed. Wired enforcement into the
two reachable dispatch points: (1) `connectorinvoke.Invoker.CallTool` now
resolves the calling session's environment (via the new
`WithEnvironments` resolver) and rejects a connector tool whose inferred
`ToolCapabilities` the environment's connectorSelector denies, before the
outbound dial — this closes the connector-capability half flagged in
F-10.6.3's resolution; (2) the `/mcp/runtimes/{name}` dispatcher
(`mcpruntimes`) gates a `tools/call` scoped to an environment
(`?environment=<name>`) by that environment's matching mcpRuntimeFilter,
resolving the tool's §5.1 capability from the runtime's
`toolCapabilityOverrides`/inference mode. Both paths fail closed on an
un-inferred tool (conservative §5.1 admin default) and emit the §5.3
call-time `TOOL_CAPABILITY_DENIED` code (newly registered in
`errorclassify` as a non-retryable policy denial). Commit landed this
batch.

### - [x] F-10.6.3 — 03  `connectorSelector.allowedCapabilities`/`deniedCapabilities` are not modeled [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 lines 595–599 — `connectorSelector` carries
`matchLabels`, `allowedCapabilities`, and `deniedCapabilities`. The
intent is parallel to `mcpRuntimeFilters`: the selector decides which
connectors are in scope, and the capability lists decide what those
connectors may do.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/environments.go` line 82
declares `ConnectorSelector SelectorPayload`. `SelectorPayload` at
lines 31–37 carries `matchLabels`, `matchExpressions`, `types`,
`include`, `exclude` — no `allowedCapabilities`/`deniedCapabilities`
keys. The storage type at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/environmentstore/environmentstore.go`
lines 71–72 stores `ConnectorSelector environment.Selector` with no
capability fields. The `environment.Selector` definition at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/environment/environment.go` lines 128–143
carries only the K8s-style selector plus `Types`/`Include`/`Exclude`.
The capability sublist that the spec puts on the `connectorSelector` is
not part of the wire shape, not part of the persisted body, and not
validated.

**Classification:** High — the `connectorSelector` capability list is a
documented enforcement surface. Today an admin cannot configure it
through any code path; the field is silently dropped from request
bodies and is invisible on `GET`. This compounds with F-10.6-02: there
is no connector capability filter either, but here even the schema is
missing.

**Resolution:** new `environmentstore.ConnectorSelector{Selector,
AllowedCapabilities, DeniedCapabilities}` type; `Environment.ConnectorSelector`
now carries the capability lists alongside the tag selector. The admin wire
shape gains `ConnectorSelectorPayload` with `allowedCapabilities`/
`deniedCapabilities`, round-tripped through Create/Get/Update and persisted in
the environments `body` jsonb. `environmentstore.Validate` rejects empty,
duplicate, and allowed∩denied-overlapping capability names (loose validation —
the §10.6 line 665 taxonomy is extensible and the §10.6 example itself names
`search`, not a §5.3 capability); the same check now also covers
mcpRuntimeFilter capability lists. Capability *enforcement* at connector
dispatch remains the separate gap noted alongside F-10.6.2. Tier-1
`TestConnectorSelectorCapabilityValidation_spec_10_6_595` +
`TestConnectorSelectorCapabilitiesWireRoundTrip_spec_10_6_595` /
`...RejectsOverlap...`; tier-2 store round-trip extended.

### - [x] F-10.6.4 — 04  Bilateral cross-environment-delegation wire shape uses `environment`, spec defines `targetEnvironment`/`sourceEnvironment` [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-10.6.13 — F-10.6.4 is the wire field-name deviation (environment vs targetEnvironment/sourceEnvironment) while F-10.6.13 is the outbound wildcard asymmetry; same subsystem, different defects.

**Spec:** §10.6 lines 613–625 — the structured `crossEnvironmentDelegation`
block has `outbound: [{targetEnvironment: ..., runtimes: ...}]` and
`inbound: [{sourceEnvironment: ..., runtimes: ...}]`. The two field
names carry the bilateral semantics (an outbound rule names the
permitted target; an inbound rule names the permitted source).

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/environments.go` lines 59–72
defines `CrossEnvRulePayload{Environment string ..., Runtimes ...}` —
a single `environment` field reused for both directions. The doc-comment
above the struct acknowledges the asymmetry ("the target for an
outbound rule, the permitted source for an inbound rule") but the JSON
tag in both contexts is the same literal string `"environment"`. A
client following the §10.6 YAML form will fail to round-trip: posting
`{"outbound":[{"targetEnvironment":"x", ...}]}` ignores `x` and stores
an empty peer; posting `{"inbound":[{"sourceEnvironment":"x", ...}]}`
likewise drops the source.

**Classification:** High — this is a wire-format incompatibility on a
security-critical structure. The bilateral declaration is the §10.6
correctness primitive for cross-environment delegation; a wire-shape
mismatch silently strips the peer name on every write, and the rule
falls back to the empty-string peer which `outboundPermits` and
`inboundPermits` in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/envaccess/envaccess.go`
lines 213–232 will never match. The result is that an admin POST in
the spec's documented form silently creates no-op rules.

**Resolution (2c91f2b5):** `CrossEnvRulePayload` is split into
`CrossEnvOutboundRulePayload` (`targetEnvironment`) and
`CrossEnvInboundRulePayload` (`sourceEnvironment`) in
`pkg/gateway/admin/environments.go`, with direction-specific
`toCrossEnvOutbound`/`toCrossEnvInbound`/`fromCrossEnvOutbound`/`fromCrossEnvInbound`
conversions. Both wire field names now round-trip to the shared
`environmentstore.CrossEnvRule.Environment` instead of being dropped. The
spec's documented YAML form posts correctly and `GET` emits the §10.6
field names. Tier-1 test `TestCrossEnvironmentDelegationWireRoundTrip_spec_10_6_613`
asserts the peer names persist and the JSON keys are
`targetEnvironment`/`sourceEnvironment` with no legacy `environment` key.

### - [x] F-10.6.5 — 05  No environment `Role` enforcement gates beyond membership detection [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-10.6.1 — Both concern environment access control, but one is the missing membership check on the explicit endpoint and the other is the absence of role-level enforcement beyond membership.

**Spec:** §10.6 line 605 — "Member roles: `viewer`, `creator`,
`operator`, `admin`." The names are load-bearing: a `viewer` reads, a
`creator` creates sessions, an `operator` adds operational tooling,
and an `admin` adds environment administration including member
management and policy edits.

**Implementation:** The role enum is defined and validated at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/environment/environment.go` lines 21–68,
including the `AtLeast` escalation helper. Membership resolution at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/envaccess/envaccess.go`
lines 62–75 returns the highest matching role and a "found" boolean.
Beyond that, no call site consults the returned role:
- The transparent-filter runtime view (`AuthorizedRuntimes` lines 98–125)
  ignores the role — any membership (even `viewer`) yields the union
  of runtimes the env's `runtimeSelector` admits.
- The explicit-environment session-create path (F-10.6-01) ignores the
  role entirely (it ignores membership too).
- Cross-environment delegation reach (`crossEnvReachable` at
  `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`
  lines 1232–1268) checks only that the caller is a member, not that
  the role is `creator` or higher.
- The access report at
  `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/access_report.go`
  reports the declared role but no admin gate runs against it.

**Classification:** High — the role enum is dead weight. An OIDC group
configured as `viewer` of a security-team environment can create
sessions in it (or, with F-10.6-01, in any environment), reach the
environment's runtimes through transparent filtering, and (through the
parent session's `Environment` field) reach cross-environment-delegated
runtimes — none of which the `viewer` role is meant to grant.

**Resolution (2c91f2b5):** the role enum is no longer dead weight — the
session-create path now consults the resolved role and requires at least
`creator` (`role.AtLeast(environment.RoleCreator)`) for every session that
names an environment, whether via the explicit endpoint or the body field
(`requireExplicitEnvironmentAdmission`, §10.6 line 605 "creator creates
sessions"). This is the load-bearing role gate. The two remaining items
the finding enumerates are addressed by construction: (1) the
transparent-filter runtime *view* returning the union to a `viewer` is the
read-only access the `viewer` role grants (§10.2 line 262 — viewers may
view runtimes), so it is not an escalation; (2) cross-environment
delegation reach via `parent.Environment` is now transitively gated,
because a session can only carry an environment if a `creator`+ created it,
so a `viewer` can no longer obtain the parent session that the delegate-time
`memberOfEnvironment` check operates on. Verified by
`TestExplicitEnvironmentViewerRejected_spec_10_6_605` (viewer → 403) and
`TestExplicitEnvironmentCreatorAdmitted_spec_10_6_605` (creator → 201).

### - [x] F-10.6.6 — 06  Tenant RBAC Config payload omits `identityProvider`, `tokenPolicy`, `capabilities`, `mcpAnnotationMapping` [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 line 665 — "Tenant RBAC Config: Managed via
`PUT /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/rbac-config`. Includes `noEnvironmentPolicy`,
`identityProvider` (OIDC), `tokenPolicy`, `capabilities` taxonomy
(platform defaults + tenant custom), `mcpAnnotationMapping` overrides."

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/rbac_config.go`
lines 20–27 defines `RBACConfigPayload` with only `tenantId` and
`noEnvironmentPolicy`. The doc-comment at lines 20–23 explicitly notes
"the §10.6 identityProvider, tokenPolicy, capabilities, and
mcpAnnotationMapping fields are not yet stored". `tenantstore.Tenant`
at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/tenantstore/tenantstore.go`
lines 25–118 has no fields for those four. No code path accepts,
validates, or persists them. The capability inference package
(`pkg/gateway/capabilityinference`) supplies the primitive, but the
per-tenant override hook (`mcpAnnotationMapping overrides`) is not
plumbed.

**Classification:** High — `identityProvider`, `tokenPolicy`, the
capability taxonomy, and the `mcpAnnotationMapping` override are all
load-bearing tenant configuration. Today a deployer cannot configure
the OIDC provider per tenant, cannot set the token policy per tenant,
cannot extend the capability taxonomy with tenant-custom capabilities,
and cannot override an mcp tool's inferred capability.

**Resolution:** `tenantstore.Tenant` gains an `RBACConfig` sub-object
(`IdentityProvider{Type, IntrospectionEnabled}`, opaque `TokenPolicy`
json.RawMessage, `Capabilities []string`, `MCPAnnotationMapping
map[string][]string`) persisted in a new `rbac_config` jsonb column
(migration 0097). `RBACConfigPayload` carries all four; PUT validates
(`identityProvider.type` ∈ {"", oidc}; `tokenPolicy` must be a JSON object;
`capabilities` non-empty + deduped; `mcpAnnotationMapping` values validated as
§5.3 capabilities via the existing `capabilityinference.ValidateOverrides`) and
GET round-trips them. `tokenPolicy` is stored verbatim and not interpreted —
§10.6 line 665 names the field but defines no sub-fields, so inventing its
structure would change the spec; the gateway round-trips it for forward
compatibility. `mcpAnnotationMapping` matches the `capabilityinference.Resolve`
overrides contract (§5.1 line 325). The live OIDC introspection check the
`identityProvider.introspectionEnabled` toggle gates is the separate F-10.6.8;
this finding lands the storage it reads. Tier-1
`TestRBACConfigRoundTripsExtraFields_spec_10_6_665` + four validation tests +
`TestRBACConfigCloneIsDeep_spec_10_6_665`; tier-2 pgstore round-trip + 0097
column assertion.

### - [x] F-10.6.7 — 07  `defaultDelegationPolicy` is stored but never applied at session create [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 line 601 and lines 629–637 — `defaultDelegationPolicy`
names the `DelegationPolicy` "applied to sessions created in this
environment". The effective-scope formula at line 629 makes the
delegation policy a factor of the scope: "(environment definition ∪
cross-environment permitted runtimes) ∩ delegation policy".

**Implementation:** The field is round-tripped through the admin API
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/environments.go`
lines 83, 161, 192), persisted to Postgres (pgstore.go lines 61, 73, 85),
and stored on the in-memory environment row. No code path consumes it:
the session-create flow at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go`
lines 620–685 never reads it, and the delegation dispatcher at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`
lines 982–988 hands the request to `deps.Delegation.Delegate` without
consulting the parent session's environment to look up the default
policy. A grep for `DefaultDelegationPolicy` outside the storage /
admin / test layers returns zero matches.

**Classification:** High — without the default policy being applied,
the §10.6 effective-scope formula collapses to "(environment definition
∪ cross-environment permitted runtimes)", with no intersection against
the delegation policy. A session created in a security-team environment
that points at a tightly-scoped `defaultDelegationPolicy` (the documented
purpose of the field) instead uses the platform-default or
request-supplied delegation policy.

**Resolution:** the effective DelegationPolicy resolution now consults the
session's environment. `filterByEffectiveDelegationPolicy` (the §8.3 line 244
discovery surface, the only place a DelegationPolicy is applied to narrow
runtimes today) collects every governing policy — the §8.3 runtime-level
policy plus the §10.6 environment `defaultDelegationPolicy` resolved via a new
`environmentDefaultPolicy` helper (session.Environment → environment →
`Service.ResolveActivePolicy`) — and admits a target only when all of them
permit it, the §10.6 line 629 `∩ delegation policy` intersection. The
intersection is restriction-only, matching the §8.3 least-privilege doctrine.
An unresolved env-default reference (no environment, no default, missing or
soft-deleted policy) imposes no restriction, the same conservative
fall-through the runtime-level resolver uses. The delegate-time target gate
that would consume the same resolution is the separate (still-absent) §8.3
tag-gate at admission; this finding closes the "stored but never applied" gap
by making the env-default participate in the effective scope. Tier-1
`TestDiscoverAgentsAppliesEnvironmentDefaultPolicy` /
`...IntersectsRuntimeAndEnvironmentPolicy` / `...MissingEnvironmentPolicyFailsOpen`
/ `...EnvironmentWithNoDefaultPolicyUsesRuntimeOnly` +
`TestResolveActivePolicy_spec_10_6_601` (+ nil-registry).

### - [ ] F-10.6.8 — 08  OIDC `introspectionEnabled` real-time group check is absent [Medium] — DEFERRED

**Spec:** §10.6 line 661 — "Identity: OIDC. Groups from LDAP/AD carried
as JWT claims. `introspectionEnabled: true` adds real-time group checks
at latency cost."

**Implementation:** Group identity is JWT-claim-only. The auth claim
shape at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/auth/jwt/jwt.go` lines 69–73
declares `Groups []string` parsed at `pkg/gateway/middleware/auth/auth.go`
lines 47–52 and 208. The membership resolver at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/envaccess/envaccess.go`
lines 42–55 only consults `c.Groups`. No OIDC token introspection
client (`/oauth2/introspect`, `RFC 7662`) is implemented; no per-tenant
toggle named `introspectionEnabled` is exposed (a grep returns only
spec-review hits). Token verification is purely signature- and
claim-based.

**Classification:** Medium — the spec presents `introspectionEnabled`
as a tunable, not as a hard requirement (the default is implicitly
"off"). The capability is unimplemented but the platform's safe-default
behavior is consistent with `introspectionEnabled: false`.

**Deferred:** the storage/config half is stale — `tenantstore.RBACConfig.
IdentityProvider.IntrospectionEnabled` already exists and round-trips
through `PUT/GET /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/rbac-config` (`rbac_config.go`).
The residual gap is the real-time RFC 7662 introspection call on the auth
hot path, which needs (a) a per-tenant introspection-endpoint URL +
client-credentials config (no field exists; only the global OIDC issuer
is configured), (b) a new RFC 7662 introspection client with a short-TTL
group cache (the "latency cost" the spec names), and (c) a tenant-RBAC
read wired into the auth middleware. That is a new auth subsystem rather
than wiring an existing surface; deferring leaves no enforcement hole
because the safe default (introspection off, JWT-claim groups only) is
already in effect.

### - [x] F-10.6.9 — 09  Billing-event schema has no `environmentId` field [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 line 663 — "Environment-level billing rollup (v1):
`environmentId` populated on all billing events for sessions created in
an environment context." §10.6 line 674 reinforces this in the v1
data-model accommodations: "`environmentId` as nullable field on
billing event schema from Phase 1".

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/billingstore/billingstore.go`
lines 109–139 declares the `Event` struct. The fields are `TenantID`,
`SequenceNumber`, `SchemaVersion`, `UserID`, `SessionID`, `ExperimentID`,
`VariantID`, `EventType`, `TokensInput`, `TokensOutput`, `PodMinutes`,
`CreatedAt`, `CorrectsSequence`, `CorrectionReasonCode`,
`CorrectionDetail`. There is no `Environment` or `EnvironmentID`
field. The pgstore implementation at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/billingstore/pgstore/pgstore.go`
makes no provision for it; the SQL columns persisted match the struct.

**Classification:** Medium — the §10.6 environment-level billing
rollup is impossible today. Aggregation by environment must fall back
to a join through the session row, which is fragile across erasure and
session retention windows. Severity is Medium rather than High because
the spec frames the rollup as a v1 accommodation (line 663 prefixes it
"v1") and downstream analytics aren't blocked, just less precise.

**Resolution:** `billingstore.Event` gains an `EnvironmentID` field,
migration 0091 adds the `environment_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`
column to `billing_events`, and pgstore round-trips it through Append /
Since / InsertFromStream. The three production emit sites
(`sessionserver.recordSessionCreated`, `sessionserver.markSessionTerminal`,
`watchdog.recordCompleted`) now stamp `sess.Environment` so every
environment-scoped session contributes to the §10.6 rollup. Unscoped
sessions retain the empty value.

### - [x] F-10.6.10 — 10  `GET /v1/runtimes` and `list_runtimes` do not accept the `?environmentId=` stub [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 line 672 — "`GET /v1/runtimes` and `list_runtimes`
accept optional `?environmentId=` stub". The accommodation is part of
the v1 data-model carve-out.

**Implementation:** The REST runtime list at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes.go`
lines 56–89 does not parse `environmentId` from `req.URL.Query()`.
The MCP `list_runtimes` tool at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`
lines 863–889 declares `InputSchema` accepting only `nameContains`. A
grep for `environmentId` returns zero matches in either handler. The
filter currently in place is the transparent-filter union from the
caller's membership; an explicit `environmentId` scope is not honored.

**Classification:** Medium — the stub does not need to enforce
anything per spec ("stub"), but the field's absence prevents clients
from probing the explicit-environment scope through the discovery
surface and prevents forward compatibility with the eventual scoping
behavior.

**Resolution:** REST `GET /v1/runtimes?environmentId=<name>` and MCP
`lenny/list_runtimes` (`environmentId` in InputSchema) now narrow the
post-transparent-filter result to runtimes the named environment's
`runtimeSelector` admits. A non-promoting stub: a runtime the §10.6
transparent filter already excluded stays excluded; an unknown
environment collapses the list to empty so a typo never broadens
visibility; an empty value is the v1 default no-op.

### - [x] F-10.6.11 — 11  No `/mcp/environments/{name}` explicit-MCP endpoint dispatcher [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 line 557 — explicit-environment endpoint exposes

(an explicit argument still wins). (2)+(3) the OpenAI Chat and Open
Responses translators now parse the §10.6 scoped model namespace
`environments/{name}/{model}` (`translator.splitEnvModel`): the named
environment is stamped on the implicit session and the bare model is used
as the runtime reference. The membership-enforcement concern referenced
from F-10.6-01 is the runtime/connector capability filter, now closed by

### - [x] F-10.6.12 — 12  Environment `Description` lacks validation; tenantId path/body cross-check absent [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.6 lines 562–565 — the resource has `description: "Security

are stored verbatim and that the `tenantId` on the body matches the
tenant the caller is authorized for.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/environmentstore/environmentstore.go`
lines 86–133 validates `Name` and `TenantID` for non-emptiness but
performs no length or character validation on `Description`. The admin
handler at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/environments.go`
lines 202–229 resolves the tenant from the body's `TenantID` via
`authorizedTenantForUser`. If the caller's authorized tenant resolves
to something different from the body, the resolver substitutes (the
function returns the authorized tenant), but this is silent — a body
that names a different tenant on `Create` will round-trip back with
the authorized tenant, with no error. On `Update` the body's `TenantID`
is also re-resolved silently.

**Classification:** Medium — silent body-vs-authorized tenant
substitution makes audit trails harder to reconcile (the request body
disagrees with the persisted row, but the API returned 201/200 without
a warning). Description length is unbounded.

**Resolution:** `environmentstore.Environment.Validate` rejects a
description longer than `MaxDescriptionLen` (1024 bytes); `Create` and

the body asserts a `tenantId` that disagrees with the authorized

### - [x] F-10.6.13 — 13  `targetEnvironment: "*"` wildcard semantics asymmetric with inbound `sourceEnvironment: "*"` [Low] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-10.6.4 — F-10.6.4 is the wire field-name deviation (environment vs targetEnvironment/sourceEnvironment) while F-10.6.13 is the outbound wildcard asymmetry; same subsystem, different defects.

**Spec:** §10.6 lines 613–625 — the inbound rule example uses
`sourceEnvironment: "*"` to denote "any source environment". The
outbound example uses a literal target name.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/envaccess/envaccess.go`
lines 213–232 — `inboundPermits` honors the `"*"` wildcard on the
source field (line 227), but `outboundPermits` line 215 matches
`rule.Environment == targetEnv` exactly, with no wildcard branch.
Symmetric outbound wildcards (`targetEnvironment: "*"` meaning
"reachable to any target environment with a matching inbound rule")
are not described in the spec but are also not rejected at admission
time — `Environment` is treated as a free string. An admin who writes
`{"environment":"*","runtimes":...}` on the outbound side will see no

**Classification:** Low — spec does not describe outbound wildcards;
the asymmetry is consistent with the spec text. The Low note is that
the admission validator does not reject a `*` target as malformed,
which leaves a footgun for admins reading the spec example and
generalizing.

**Resolution:** `Environment.Validate` (`pkg/gateway/environmentstore/environmentstore.go`) now rejects outbound rules with `targetEnvironment == "*"` or empty, and inbound rules with empty `sourceEnvironment` — `"*"` remains admissible inbound per §10.6 line 619. The admission error surfaces the specific field (`outbound[i].targetEnvironment` / `inbound[i].sourceEnvironment`) so admins writing the wrong form fail loudly rather than ship a silent no-op rule. Tier-1 cases: outbound-wildcard rejection, outbound-empty rejection, inbound-empty rejection, inbound-wildcard happy path.

0028 with the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger and the

**Resolution (positive confirmation, no code change):** Informational finding cataloguing §10.6 surfaces already aligned with spec — `lenny-noenvironmentpolicy-audit` interceptor, platform/tenant `noEnvironmentPolicy` semantics (fatal-startup vs deny-all default), live cross-env reachability checks, isolation-monotonicity emission with `cross_environment` boolean, transparent runtime filtering, and the access-report identity-by-environment matrix. Code paths cited in the finding are still in place. No action required.

### Summary

§10.6 has a strong foundation: the role enum, selector evaluator,
storage layer, admin CRUD, transparent-filter middleware,
no-environment-policy state machine, cross-environment-delegation
bilateral check, isolation-monotonicity check, and audit interceptor
are all built and well-covered by tests. The gaps cluster around
enforcement of the structures that are stored: capability filtering
(`mcpRuntimeFilters`, connector capabilities) is dead code from an
authorization standpoint; the role enum is detected but never
consulted for permission decisions; the explicit-environment
session endpoint accepts arbitrary environment names without
membership; the `defaultDelegationPolicy` field never reaches the
delegation dispatcher; the bilateral cross-environment wire shape
uses `environment` where the spec uses `targetEnvironment` and
`sourceEnvironment`; the Tenant RBAC Config payload covers only
one of the five spec-named fields; and the `environmentId` billing
rollup and `?environmentId=` discovery stub are unimplemented.

## §10.7 Experiment Primitives <a id="10.7"></a>
Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/10_gateway-internals.md` lines 677–1153.

### Method

§10.7 was enumerated into normative requirements covering the `ExperimentDefinition`
admin API resource (CRUD, status lifecycle, status-only PATCH); the closed
`active`/`paused`/`concluded` status enum and its transition matrix; the
`baseRuntime`/`variants[]` shape with per-variant `initialMinWarm`; the
`targeting.mode` enum (`percentage` | `external`); the `targeting.sticky` enum
(`user` | `session` | `none`); the `propagation.childSessions` enum (`inherit`
| `control` | `independent`); the reserved `"control"` variant identifier with
`422 RESERVED_IDENTIFIER`; the HMAC-SHA256 cumulative-weight bucketing algorithm
with first-match multi-experiment evaluation; the tenant-level
`experimentTargeting` block with OFREP and built-in OpenFeature SDK providers
(LaunchDarkly, Statsig, Unleash); the `experiment.targeting_failed` /
`experiment.unknown_variant_from_provider` / `experiment.unknown_external_id`
event surfaces; the SCL-023 per-tenant targeting circuit breaker (5/10s open,
30s half-open) with the `lenny_experiment_targeting_circuit_open` gauge; the
anonymous-session handling under both modes; the `ExperimentRouter` fail-closed
isolation monotonicity check at runtime (`422 VARIANT_ISOLATION_UNAVAILABLE`)
and the admission-time monotonicity check (`422 CONFIGURATION_CONFLICT`); the
tenant-floor advisory `experiment.variant_weaker_than_tenant_floor` event; the
delegation-propagation rules including the `inherited` flag; the eval submission
contract (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/eval` with `session:eval:write` permission,
accepted session states, per-session/per-tenant rate limits, `idempotency_key`
dedup, `maxEvalsPerSession` storage cap, `submitted_after_conclusion`
attribution); the EvalResult schema with `delegation_depth`, `inherited`, and
`submitted_after_conclusion` auto-population; the Results API EXP-002 query
filters (`delegation_depth`, `inherited`, `exclude_post_conclusion`,
`breakdown_by`); the BreakdownResponse shape; the `lenny_eval_aggregates`
materialized view with `evalAggregationRefreshSeconds` Helm parameter; the
Results API blinding constraint; the PoolScalingController state-transition
table (`active→paused`, `paused→active`, `*→concluded`) for variant pools and
the base-pool `(1 - Σ variant_weights)` re-adjustment; the sticky-cache
invalidation on transitions with `lenny_experiment_sticky_cache_invalidations_total`;
the `experiment.status_changed` audit event; and the rollback-trigger metrics
(`lenny_session_error_total`, `lenny_session_duration_seconds`, `lenny_eval_score`)
labelled by `variant_id`.

Each requirement was traced through `pkg/experiment/`,
`pkg/gateway/admin/experiments*.go`, `pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results*.go`,
`pkg/gateway/experimentstore/`, `pkg/gateway/evalstore/`,
`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter*.go`,
`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go`,
`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go`,
`pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go`, `pkg/gateway/ofrep/ofrep.go`,
`pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go`, `pkg/gateway/podsession/`,
`pkg/controller/poolscaling/` (controller, runnable, variants, strategy),
`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`, `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go`,
`pkg/gateway/tenantstore/`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`,
`cmd/lenny-controller/main.go`, and the SQL migrations under
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations/`. Tests under the corresponding
`_test.go` files were inspected for coverage.

### Findings

### - [x] F-10.7.1 — 01  PoolScalingController is not wired into any binary; variant pools are never reconciled [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 1092 and 1098–1106 — "PoolScalingController manages
variant pool lifecycle automatically" and the full state-transition table
(`active → paused` sets variant `minWarm = 0`; `paused → active` recomputes
from the formula; `* → concluded` sets `minWarm = maxWarm = 0` and deletes the
variant's `SandboxWarmPool` CRD). §10.7 lines 1102–1104 also bind base-pool
adjustment: every variant transition must trigger a recompute of the base
pool's `(1 - Σ variant_weights)` factor.

**Implementation:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/`
holds the `Reconciler` (controller.go), the `Runnable` adapter
(runnable.go:22–62), the `ResolveVariantRoles` helper (variants.go:69–126)
that builds the `ActiveVariant` set and feeds it into the strategy, and the
strategy package with the variant-pool and base-pool-adjustment formulas
(strategy/strategy.go:269–287). `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` (the only
controller-runtime binary) wires the `WarmPoolController`, the
`Sandbox→Pod` reconciler, and the CIDR-drift detector but **never registers
`poolscaling.Runnable`** with the manager. `grep -rn poolscaling
/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/` returns only the test-runner reference. No
`PoolConfigSource` implementation exists anywhere that reads the experiment
store and emits per-pool `PoolConfig` entries with the variant role/weight
populated. The variant-pool sizing logic exists as library code but no process
runs it.

**Classification:** High — every behavior in the §10.7 state-transition
table is absent in deployed builds. An `active → paused` transition does not
drain the variant pool; an `active → concluded` transition does not delete the
`SandboxWarmPool` CRD or restore base-pool capacity. The Results API is
internally consistent (gateway-only) but the underlying capacity machinery the
spec mandates is unbuilt and unconnected.

**Resolution:** The PoolScalingController library (`pkg/controller/poolscaling`)
was already complete and tested (Reconciler, Runnable, strategy formulas,
`ResolveVariantRoles`, `PoolStoreSource`); the gaps were the binary wiring and
the experiment-aware config source. `cmd/lenny-controller` now registers
`poolscaling.Runnable` whenever `--postgres-dsn` and an agent namespace are set,
feeding it a `PoolStoreSource` wrapped by the new
`poolscaling.ExperimentVariantSource`. The source reads every experiment across
tenants via the new `experimentstore` `ListAll` (Memory + pgstore; the Postgres
side uses the §4.2 platform-admin `InAllTenants` cross-tenant path) and rewrites
the affected pools by §10.7 status: **active** variants are sized by the §4.6.2
variant formula via `ResolveVariantRoles` (with base-pool `Σ variant_weights`
reduction), **paused** variant pools pin minWarm to 0 through the new
`PoolConfig.ForceZeroMinWarm` (maxWarm unchanged, CRD retained — spec line 1102),
and **concluded** variant pools are flagged `PoolConfig.DrainAndDelete` so the
new `Reconciler.drainAndDeleteWarmPool` drives the SandboxWarmPool to 0/0 and
deletes it once `status.readyCount` reaches 0, retaining the SandboxTemplate
(spec line 1104). Status precedence is active > paused > concluded; base-pool
restoration on pause/conclude is automatic because their weights leave the active
sum. The base pool is resolved by `PoolStoreBasePoolResolver` (the sole §5.2 pool
warming the experiment's base runtime; ambiguous matches conservatively skip the
adjustment rather than reduce the wrong pool). F-10.7.3 (built-in LaunchDarkly/
Statsig/Unleash SDK providers) stays OPEN — it needs vendor SDK module
dependencies and is independent of this wiring. Resolved this batch.

---

### - [x] F-10.7.2 — 02  OpenFeature targeting circuit breaker (SCL-023) is unimplemented; metric is declared but never emitted [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 835–844 — every tenant requires a per-tenant circuit
breaker on the OpenFeature evaluation hot path: open after 5 consecutive
failures within 10s (`circuitBreaker.failureThreshold`,
`circuitBreaker.windowSeconds`), stay open for 30s
(`circuitBreaker.openDurationSeconds`) before a half-open probe. While open,
the gateway must skip the OpenFeature call entirely and emit
`lenny_experiment_targeting_circuit_open = 1`. The
`ExperimentTargetingCircuitOpen` alert (§16.5) fires when the gauge is `1` for
60s, indicating a sustained targeting outage.

**Implementation:** `grep -rn circuit
/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/experiment /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver
/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/ofrep` returns no per-tenant breaker
state. `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter.go`
lines 168–216 constructs a fresh OFREP client every session creation,
performs a single per-experiment call, latches the per-request failure with a
local `failed` flag, but never persists state across requests — so the next
session creation absorbs another 200ms timeout, exactly the cascade SCL-023
exists to prevent. No `experimentTargeting.circuitBreaker` block is decoded by
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/experiment/external.go` (lines 74–82 list only
`Provider`/`TimeoutMs`/per-provider sub-blocks). The metric
`lenny_experiment_targeting_circuit_open` is declared in the catalog at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:205` and the
`ExperimentTargetingCircuitOpen` alert is wired in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1253-1259`, but no
code path sets the gauge — the alert can never fire.

**Classification:** High — the SCL-023 mitigation is the only mechanism that
caps the per-request blast radius of a targeting-service outage. Without it
every session creation on a tenant with a degraded provider pays the full
configured `timeoutMs` (default 200ms), so under sustained provider failure
the gateway absorbs the cost the spec is designed to bound. The corresponding
alert is also fundamentally inert.

**Resolution** (commit `d52ad11a`): Added a per-(tenant, provider) breaker
(`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/targetingbreaker.go`) consulted inside
`buildExternalEvaluator`'s closure — it opens after `failureThreshold`
consecutive failures within `windowSeconds`, stays open `openDurationSeconds`,
then admits one half-open probe (success closes, failure re-arms). While open
the gateway skips the OFREP call entirely. The
`lenny_experiment_targeting_circuit_open{tenant_id, provider}` gauge is now
registered and set on transitions, so the §16.5 alert can fire. Config block
`experimentTargeting.circuitBreaker.{failureThreshold=5, windowSeconds=10,
openDurationSeconds=30}` added to `TargetingConfig` with default-aware
accessors, Clone, and non-negative Validate.

### - [ ] F-10.7.3 — 03  Built-in OpenFeature SDK providers (LaunchDarkly, Statsig, Unleash) are not implemented [High] — DEFERRED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 779–782 — Lenny supports two external-targeting
integration paths: OFREP (recommended) and "OpenFeature SDK providers linked
into the gateway binary" for LaunchDarkly, Statsig, and Unleash. Lines
797–822 show the three corresponding `experimentTargeting.provider` examples.
The §10.7 enum closes on those four values, and a tenant configuring any of
them expects the gateway to honor that targeting.

**Implementation:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/experiment/external.go`
lines 15–20 declares the four provider enum values, lines 51–66 define the
LaunchDarkly/Statsig/Unleash config sub-blocks, and lines 143–160 validate
them at admission. But the runtime path at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter.go`
lines 176–181 short-circuits any non-OFREP provider:

```
if cfg.Provider != experiment.TargetingProviderOFREP || cfg.OFREP == nil {
    return nil
}
```

The comment at line 178 makes this explicit: "v1 ships the OFREP transport;
the built-in SDK providers (launchdarkly, statsig, unleash) need their vendor
SDKs." `grep -rn launchdarkly|statsig|unleash pkg/` produces no provider
implementation. A tenant configuring any of the three providers will pass
admission and then silently route every mode:external experiment to control
without any `experiment.targeting_failed` event (the failure path requires an
OFREP client to fail; here the gateway never even tries).

**Classification:** High — three of the four §10.7 targeting providers are
inert. The admission-time validation accepts a `launchdarkly`/`statsig`/`unleash`
provider as if functional, so deployers receive no signal that their
configuration will be ignored at runtime.

**DEFERRED (re-verified OPEN; environment-blocked):** The finding is
accurate — `experimentrouter.go` still short-circuits any non-OFREP
provider. Implementing the three providers requires linking their vendor
OpenFeature SDK modules into the gateway binary
(`github.com/open-feature/go-sdk-contrib/providers/{launchdarkly,statsig,unleash}`
plus each vendor's own SDK), none of which is reachable in this build
environment: there is no `vendor/` tree, none of the modules is in the
local module cache, none appears in `go.mod`, and the sandbox has no
network to `go get` them. Adding a hand-rolled HTTP reimplementation of
each vendor's evaluation API is explicitly not what §10.7 lines 779–782
mandate (it specifies the vendor SDK providers), would be a large
fragile surface, and the §10.7 OFREP path already covers
externally-targeted experiments. Re-attempt once the vendor SDK modules
are available offline: add the three providers behind the existing
`experiment.TargetingProvider` enum, construct each from its config
sub-block, and replace the OFREP-only guard with a provider switch.

### - [x] F-10.7.4 — 04  Eval submission endpoint omits idempotency, rate limiting, and `session:eval:write` permission gating [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 932–941 — the Eval Submission Contract mandates four
distinct controls on `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/eval`:

- **Caller permission:** "any authenticated principal with the `session:eval:write`
  permission for the tenant" (line 936) — a dedicated permission distinct from
  ordinary session management, sized for external scorer pipelines.
- **Rate limit:** per-session (default 100/min, `evalRateLimit.perSessionPerMinute`)
  and per-tenant (default 10,000/min, `evalRateLimit.perTenantPerMinute`)
  sliding-window counters in Redis, returning `429` with `Retry-After`.
- **Idempotency:** optional `idempotency_key` (≤128 bytes) in the request
  body; a same-`session_id`/same-key submission within 24h returns `200 OK`
  with the original record rather than inserting a duplicate.
- **Storage cap:** per-session bound of `maxEvalsPerSession` (default 10,000,
  max 100,000), with `429 EVAL_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` on breach.

**Implementation:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go`
implements only the storage cap (through `evalstore.ErrQuotaExceeded` at
lines 113–117). The handler:
- Is gated by `manage(s.handleEval)` at
  `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go:472`,
  which calls `requireSessionPermission(auth.PermManageOwnSessions, …)` at
  line 447. There is no `PermSessionEvalWrite` / `session:eval:write`
  constant: `grep -rn session:eval:write pkg/` returns nothing, and
  `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/auth/auth.go` defines only
  `PermManageOwnSessions` / `PermReadOwnSessions`. External scorer pipelines
  must therefore hold session-manage permissions broader than the spec's
  dedicated eval-write grant.
- Decodes the request into `EvalRequest` at
  `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go` lines 18–23,
  which contains `scorer`, `score`, `scores`, `metadata` only — no
  `idempotency_key` field. `grep -rn idempotency_key pkg/gateway/sessionserver
  pkg/gateway/evalstore` returns nothing. Duplicate submissions are always
  persisted as fresh records, contrary to the spec dedup window.
- Performs no rate-limit lookup. `grep -rn perSessionPerMinute|perTenantPerMinute|evalRateLimit
  pkg/` returns nothing. The Redis sliding-window counter is absent. The
  tenant-config `evalRateLimit` block is also not defined on
  `tenantstore.Tenant`.

**Classification:** High — three of the four contract dimensions are unimplemented.
The permission gap is the most significant: any holder of
`PermManageOwnSessions` (every regular user) can submit evals, whereas the
spec scopes the capability to a dedicated `session:eval:write` permission
intended for external scorers. The missing rate limit removes the cost cap
the spec relies on to prevent abusive eval flooding.

**Resolution (e24cbbf4):** All three remaining dimensions wired.
(1) Permission: new `auth.PermSessionEvalWrite` (`session:eval:write`,
§10.7 line 936) — a capability permission outside the §10.2 matrix,
granted to the session-owning built-in roles (user, tenant-admin,
platform-admin) and within the tenant-admin ceiling so a tenant may
grant it to a custom external-scorer role. `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/eval`
is now gated on it (the new `evalWrite` wrapper) instead of
`manage_own_sessions`. (2) Rate limit (§10.7 line 938): per-session
(default 100/min) and per-tenant (default 10000/min) over the existing
§11.1 `ratelimit.Counter`, returning `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`
and failing open on a counter error, enforced before the session lookup;
operator-tunable via `--eval-rate-limit-per-session/-tenant-per-min` and
`gateway.evalRateLimit.*`. The platform-wide sliding-vs-fixed-window
refinement remains F-11.2.3; a per-tenant config override remains future
work consistent with `maxEvalsPerSession` also being a global default.
(3) Idempotency (§10.7 lines 939-940): optional `idempotency_key`
(≤128 bytes, `400` on oversize); a repeat for the same session within 24h
returns `200` with the original record via `evalstore.FindByIdempotencyKey`
over a new `eval_results.idempotency_key` column (migration 0098). The
storage cap (dimension 4) was already wired.

### - [x] F-10.7.5 — 05  Eval handler does not populate `submitted_after_conclusion` or `delegation_depth` [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 868 and 905–907 — every `EvalResult` carries
`delegation_depth` (uint32, 0 for root sessions) "auto-populated by the
gateway from the session's delegation lineage", `inherited` (boolean,
mirroring `experimentContext.inherited`), and `submitted_after_conclusion`
(boolean, `true` when the eval is submitted after the experiment transitioned
to `concluded`). The Results API filters (lines 949–952) and the
sample-contamination warning (line 870) depend on these fields being
truthful.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go` lines 99–111
constructs the `evalstore.EvalResult` and copies only
`ec.ExperimentID`/`ec.VariantID`/`ec.Inherited` from the session context.
`DelegationDepth` is left at the zero value (the field is never assigned in
the handler), and `SubmittedAfterConclusion` is never computed — the handler
does not even fetch the experiment record to consult its status.
`grep -rn DelegationDepth pkg/gateway/sessionserver` returns no assignments,
and `grep -n SubmittedAfterConclusion pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go`
returns nothing. The store fields exist
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/evalstore/evalstore.go:50-55`,
migration `0029_eval_results.up.sql` lines 42–47), but they are forever
zero-valued and `false`.

Knock-on consequences in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results.go`:
- `?delegation_depth=0` (lines 134–142, 164–166) always returns every row
  (every row has `DelegationDepth == 0`).
- `?delegation_depth=1` (line 165) always returns the empty set.
- `?exclude_post_conclusion=true` (lines 152–158, 171–173) has no effect —
  every row's `SubmittedAfterConclusion` is `false`.
- `?breakdown_by=delegation_depth` (lines 228–231, 258–278) always yields a
  single bucket at value `0`.
- `?breakdown_by=submitted_after_conclusion` (lines 234–236) always yields a
  single bucket at value `false`.

**Classification:** High — three of the four EXP-002 filters and one breakdown
are functionally inert because the underlying data is never written. The
sample-contamination remediation the spec specifically anchors on these
filters (line 870) is unreachable for real eval workloads. Tests that exercise
the filter (e.g., `TestExperimentResultsDelegationDepthFilter` and
`TestExperimentResultsBreakdownByDelegationDepth` at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results_test.go`
lines 177 and 216) seed the field directly via `evalstore.Put`, masking the
absence in the production write path.

**Resolution:** `Session.DelegationDepth` (migration 0095, pgstore
round-trip) is stamped at delegation time (`parent.depth+1`) by
`delegation.Service.Delegate`; the eval handler copies it onto
`EvalResult.DelegationDepth` and computes `SubmittedAfterConclusion` by
consulting the attributed experiment's status (true when `concluded`).
Both fields now flow from the production write path. Closed by commit
df2deef2.

### - [x] F-10.7.6 — 06  Sticky-cache and its transition-time invalidation are absent [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-12.4.7 — Both report the experiment sticky-assignment Redis cache and its invalidation are absent, so assignment is recomputed on every session creation.

**Spec:** §10.7 line 1096 — `sticky: user` "caches variant assignments in
Redis keyed by `(user_id, experiment_id)` to avoid re-evaluating assignment
on every session creation. When an experiment transitions to `paused` or
`concluded`, the gateway flushes all cached `sticky: user` assignments for
that experiment (Redis `DEL` on all keys matching
`t:{tenant_id}:exp:{experiment_id}:sticky:*`)". On `paused → active` no
flush is required. The `lenny_experiment_sticky_cache_invalidations_total`
counter must be incremented on each flush.

**Implementation:** `grep -rn sticky pkg/gateway -l` shows uses of the
`Sticky` enum value but no cache structure exists. The router at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter.go`
lines 99–104 evaluates assignment fresh on every session creation; for
percentage mode the HMAC is recomputed on every call, and for external mode a
new OFREP request is issued every call. `handlePatchExperiment` at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go` lines 376–409
records the transition but issues no Redis `DEL`. The metric is declared in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:206` but no
emission site exists.

**Classification:** Medium — under the HMAC-deterministic algorithm the
correctness of `sticky: user` is preserved without the cache because the same
inputs always produce the same output. The performance-optimization gap is
real (every session-create hashes a per-tenant experiment list and, for
external mode, issues a synchronous provider call), but no functional
guarantee is broken for percentage mode. For external mode the absence is
more consequential: the spec says the OpenFeature client "is not called again
for subsequent sessions if a cached assignment exists" (line 831), so the
external-provider integration always pays the per-session evaluation cost.

- **Resolution:** Closed by F-12.4.7 (same batch) — confirmed duplicate. The new `experimentsticky.RedisCache` provides the per-`(user_id, experiment_id)` cache, the PATCH-to-paused/concluded flush DELs `t:{tenant}:exp:{exp}:sticky:*` (no flush on `paused → active`), and `lenny_experiment_sticky_cache_invalidations_total{experiment_id,transition}` is incremented on each flush, matching §10.7 line 1096 and §16.1 line 159.

### - [x] F-10.7.7 — 07  `initialMinWarm` is stored but never reaches the scaling formula's `BootstrapMinWarm` [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 695, 705–710 — each variant entry carries an optional
`initialMinWarm` that the PoolScalingController uses "during bootstrap mode
only" as the static `minWarm` floor before the demand history exists. Lines
706–709 detail the lifecycle: applied at variant pool creation, discarded
after the formula converges per §17.8.2, and not re-applied on `paused →
active` re-activations.

**Implementation:** The wire and storage paths preserve the field
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go:33,72,95`;
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/experimentstore/experimentstore.go:34-35`)
and the in-memory tier-2 test seeds it
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/tests/tier2_component/stores/experimentstore_test.go:34`).
But the controller-side type
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/variants.go:17-28`
carries only `ExperimentID`, `BasePool`, `VariantPool`, and `Weight`; the
`ActiveVariant`-to-`PoolConfig` resolver at lines 69–126 sets `PoolType`,
`VariantWeight`, and `SumActiveVariantWeights` but never touches `MinWarm`.
The strategy reads `BootstrapMinWarm` from `cfg.MinWarm`
(`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go:408`),
so the per-variant cold-start floor the spec defines never enters the
formula. (This compounds with F-10.7-01: no `PoolConfigSource` over the
experiment store exists at all, so the field has no transport even if the
struct were extended.)

**Classification:** Medium — `initialMinWarm` is the deployer's only knob
against the §10.7 cold-start latency penalty for a new variant pool. Every
new variant pool now bootstraps at `minWarm = 0` (the strategy's bootstrap
path returns `BootstrapMinWarm` which is unset from the experiment
definition), absorbing the full pod-startup latency for early traffic.

- **Resolution:** `ActiveVariant` (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/variants.go`) now carries an `InitialMinWarm int32` field, and `ResolveVariantRoles` stamps it onto the variant pool's `PoolConfig.MinWarm` when positive. `controller.targetMinWarm` already feeds `cfg.MinWarm` to the strategy as `BootstrapMinWarm`, which the strategy returns only in bootstrap mode and discards on convergence (§17.8.2), so the §10.7 lines 705-710 lifecycle (applied at creation, dropped after convergence, default 0) holds without further wiring. The experiment-store transport that constructs `ActiveVariant` slices remains F-10.7.1's scope; the named resolver defect (the type omitted MinWarm and the resolver never set it) is closed. Resolved in this batch's commit.

### - [x] F-10.7.8 — 08  Cross-experiment `Σ variant_weights ≥ 1` is not rejected at admission (`INVALID_VARIANT_WEIGHTS`) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §4.6.2 (referenced from §10.7 line 1092 and line 705) — when
multiple active experiments divert traffic from the same base pool, the
controller "aggregates their variant weights in a single pass" and rejects
the experiment configuration at admission time with `INVALID_VARIANT_WEIGHTS`
when the aggregate Σ ≥ 1. §10.7 line 1102 reinforces that the base-pool
adjustment uses the cross-experiment Σ.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/experiment/experiment.go` lines 220–242
validates only within a single Definition: it accumulates `totalWeight` over
that experiment's own `Variants` list and rejects when `totalWeight ≥ 1`. The
admin handler at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go` lines 224–261
runs that single-experiment validation and adds a cross-pool isolation check,
but never lists sibling experiments to compute the cross-experiment aggregate
on the same base runtime. `grep -rn ErrVariantWeightsExceedOne|sum.*variant
pkg/gateway/admin` returns nothing. The strategy at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/strategy/strategy.go`
lines 276–283 does enforce the rule at reconcile time, but the controller
itself is unwired (F-10.7-01), so neither path catches the violation in
practice.

**Classification:** Medium — operators can register multiple experiments
whose combined weight exceeds the base pool's traffic budget. The error
surfaces only when the controller eventually runs (which it doesn't, per
F-10.7-01), so the safety net the spec calls out is missing at both edges.

**Resolution:** `handleCreateExperiment` / `handleUpdateExperiment` now
call `rejectIfCrossExperimentWeightsExceed`, which sums variant weights
across the candidate (when active) plus every other active experiment on
the same `baseRuntime` and rejects Σ ≥ 1 with 422 INVALID_VARIANT_WEIGHTS.
Paused/concluded experiments and other base runtimes are excluded. Closed
by commit df2deef2.

### - [x] F-10.7.9 — 09  Per-dimension scores do not separately track `count` of submitting rows [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 line 1088 — "**Per-dimension aggregation semantics:** for
each dimension `d`, `count` equals the number of `EvalResult` records for
that scorer/variant where `scores[d]` is non-null (i.e., only results that
actually submitted a value for `d`); `mean`, `p50`, and `p95` are computed
only over those non-null values. A dimension's `count` may therefore be lower
than the enclosing scorer's `count` when some results omitted that dimension."

**Implementation:** This requirement is **met** in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results.go` lines
181–218: `aggregateVariant` walks each row's `Scores` map and appends to
`byScorerDim[scorer][dim]`, then calls `scorerStats(vals)` per dimension at
line 212, which counts only the rows that actually supplied that dimension.
No gap.

**Classification:** Resolved during audit — left in the document as positive
coverage evidence.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed. `aggregateVariant` populates
`byScorerDim[scorer][dim]` only from rows whose `Scores` map contains
`dim`, so each dimension's `count` reflects only the rows that supplied a
non-null value for it. Pinned by `TestExperimentResultsPerDimensionCount_spec_10_7_1088`
(commit df2deef2).

### - [x] F-10.7.10 — 10  `?delegation_depth=K&breakdown_by=delegation_depth` is not rejected with `400 INVALID_QUERY_PARAMS` [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 line 952 — `breakdown_by` is "not combinable with the
equality filter for the same field (i.e., `?delegation_depth=0&breakdown_by=delegation_depth`
is rejected with `400 INVALID_QUERY_PARAMS`)".

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results.go` lines
95–105 validates `breakdown_by` syntactically (it must be one of three field
names) but does not detect the overlap with an equality filter on the same
field. Lines 100–125 then run the filter pipeline and the breakdown
pipeline; with both present the breakdown bucketizes the pre-filtered subset,
which always produces a single bucket. No `INVALID_QUERY_PARAMS` is raised
and `grep -rn INVALID_QUERY_PARAMS pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results.go`
returns nothing.

**Classification:** Medium — the spec explicitly names the validation as a
guard against operator confusion. Today the gateway silently returns a
degenerate breakdown response (one bucket at the filtered value) instead of
the documented `400`.

**Resolution:** `handleExperimentResults` now rejects `breakdown_by`
combined with the equality/exclusion filter on the same field
(delegation_depth, inherited, or submitted_after_conclusion via its
`exclude_post_conclusion` filter) with 400 INVALID_QUERY_PARAMS, via the
new `conflictingFilterParam` helper. A breakdown on a different field than
the filter remains allowed. Closed by commit df2deef2.

**Spec:** §10.7 line 703 and §15.1 line 1005 — attempting to define a

### - [ ] F-10.7.12 — 12  `lenny_eval_aggregates` materialized view is not defined in any migration [Medium] — DEFERRED

**Spec:** §10.7 line 1088 — "the materialized view (`lenny_eval_aggregates`)
is defined in the schema migration system (alongside all other DDL) and is
created during database migration — never at runtime by the gateway". When
`evalAggregationRefreshSeconds == 0` the view still exists but is unused;
when positive, the gateway routes queries to the view and refreshes it.

**Implementation:** `grep -rn lenny_eval_aggregates
/Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations` returns no results. The base
`0029_eval_results.up.sql` migration creates the `eval_results` table and the
`(tenant_id, session_id, created_at)` and `(tenant_id, experiment_id,
created_at)` indexes, but no `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW lenny_eval_aggregates`
statement appears in any of the 109 migrations. Correspondingly, the gateway
configuration does not expose `evalAggregationRefreshSeconds` — `grep -rn
evalAggregationRefreshSeconds /Users/joan/projects/lenny` returns only spec
text and historical review notes. The Results API in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results.go` always
queries `evals.ListByExperiment` directly (line 90), with no branch on a
materialized-view config.

**Classification:** Medium — the spec-mandated DDL is missing. Operators
who would otherwise opt into the materialized-view path have no view to
refresh. The default `0`-value path (on-read aggregation from base tables) is
functional and is the only path the gateway exercises.

**Deferred:** `eval_results` is `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` (§12.3), so a
cross-tenant `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` run by the gateway's `lenny_app` role
is RLS-filtered to a single tenant — populating the view correctly requires a
dedicated `BYPASSRLS` aggregator role owning the matview plus a `SECURITY
DEFINER` refresh function (and a tenant-filtering view for the gateway read).
That is a §12.3/§13 security-model addition the cited §10.7 text does not
specify, and the security-sensitive DDL (`CONCURRENTLY` refresh,
`percentile_disc` over jsonb dimensions, the definer function) cannot be
validated against real Postgres in this environment (Docker unavailable, so
the tier-2 `tests/tier2_component/migrations` harness cannot run). Deferring to
a dedicated batch where the migration can be applied and the cross-tenant
isolation re-verified, rather than ship unvalidated DDL that could break the
prod-schema migration round-trip. The default on-read path remains functional.

### - [x] F-10.7.13 — 13  Variant-labelled rollback metrics (`lenny_session_error_total`, `lenny_session_duration_seconds`, `lenny_eval_score`) are not emitted [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 1120–1132 (Manual Rollback Triggers) — the example
rollback signals depend on three variant-labelled metrics:
`lenny_session_error_total{variant_id="treatment"}` (error rate per
variant), `lenny_session_duration_seconds{quantile="0.95",
variant_id="treatment"}` (p95 session latency per variant), and
`lenny_eval_score{scorer, variant_id}` (eval score per variant, used in the
safety-regression query at line 1128). Lines 1130–1131 frame these as the
hooks deployers wire to Prometheus rules.

**Implementation:** All three are declared in
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:208-211`
but `grep -rn lenny_session_error_total|lenny_session_duration_seconds|lenny_eval_score
pkg/ --include="*.go"` returns no emission sites — only catalog membership
and tests asserting catalog membership. The session-completion handlers
record durations and outcomes through pre-existing un-variant-labelled
metrics; the variant-labelled forms exist only in the catalog. Operators
cannot encode the §10.7 rollback alerts because the metrics they query do
not exist at runtime.

**Classification:** Medium — the rollback-trigger table is illustrative
("example thresholds, not platform defaults"), but the metrics it cites are
nonetheless required for the documented integration to work. Operators
following the spec verbatim will write rules against series that the
gateway never publishes.

**Resolution** (commit `9436e793`): Registered and emitted the §16.1 lines
161-164 family. `lenny_session_total` / `lenny_session_error_total` /
`lenny_session_duration_seconds` {tenant_id, session_type, variant_id} are
emitted at every terminal transition via a new `RecordSessionTerminal` hook
from `emitTerminalLifecycle` (session_type = §5.2 ExecutionMode; variant_id =
§10.7 enrollment; the failed state is the error outcome; duration is
creation-to-terminal wall-clock). `lenny_eval_score` {tenant_id, scorer,
variant_id} is emitted per submitted eval (scalar score) via a new
`ObserveEvalScore` hook from `handleEval`. `lenny_session_total` is included
because §16.1 line 162 makes it the rollback ratio's denominator. Both hooks
wired from `cmd/lenny-gateway`.

  at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/ofrep/ofrep.go` lines 111–155

  exists.
- `lenny_experiment_targeting_error_total`: catalog-only
  (`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:204`).

either inert (the two metrics) or structurally unreachable (the event).
The duration histogram in particular is the only mechanism for measuring the

/v1/admin/experiments`, `PUT /v1/admin/experiments/{name}`):** Validates

isolation monotonicity (each variant pool's `sessionIsolationLevel.isolationProfile`
must be at least as restrictive as the base runtime's default pool profile;

notes "This check runs in both real and `?dryRun=true` paths" for the

/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go` returns no

short-circuit before `r.experiments.Create` (line 242) or `r.experiments.Update`
(line 323), no `X-Dry-Run: true` response header, and no audit-event

configuration against the isolation-monotonicity check or the tenant-floor
advisory without committing the change. The §15.1 `dryRun` contract is part

(e.g., runtimes).

### - [x] F-10.7.16 — 16  Variant `Weight` must be in `(0, 1)`; spec allows `weight: 0.0` semantics around the boundary [Low] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 lines 693–694 — "`weight: 0.10 # fraction (0.0–1.0); 0.10 =
10% of traffic`". The pseudocode at lines 747–767 uses the variant directly
in the cumulative sum. A weight of exactly 0 is operationally meaningless
(no traffic) and a weight of exactly 1 leaves no remainder for control; the
spec's inequality `Σ weights < 1.0` only restricts the sum.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/experiment/experiment.go:235` rejects any
variant `Weight ≤ 0 || Weight ≥ 1`, which forbids both `0.0` and `1.0`
endpoints. Forbidding `0.0` is stricter than the spec text reads (a 0-weight
variant produces no enrollments but is otherwise harmless); forbidding `1.0`
matches the cross-Σ constraint. The variant-pool resolver at
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/variants.go:86-89`
applies the same `(0, 1)` constraint.

**Classification:** Low — the implementation is more conservative than the
spec, which only causes harm for operators staging a variant with
`weight: 0` (a documented experiment-staging pattern would be rejected at
admission). No correctness regression results.

**Resolution:** Relaxed the per-variant weight bound from `(0, 1)` to `[0, 1)` in `pkg/experiment/experiment.go` and `pkg/controller/poolscaling/variants.go`. A 0-weight variant is admitted (staged with no traffic); cross-Σ < 1.0 still blocks the trivial single-variant-of-1.0 case. Closed in this batch's commit.

### - [x] F-10.7.17 — 17  No experiment-state guard on `DELETE /v1/admin/experiments/{name}` [Low] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §10.7 line 1094 — "Concluded experiments are immutable". The
broader implication is that an active experiment's deletion would orphan
the variant pool, eval attribution on in-flight sessions, and the audit
chain. The spec does not explicitly forbid deletion at any specific state.

**Implementation:**
`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go:411-429`
deletes regardless of `Status`. No `CanDelete()` check exists. The
`admin.experiment.deleted` audit event fires unconditionally.

**Classification:** Low — the spec is silent on the precise rule, but the
implementation diverges from a defensive reading where deletion is permitted
only after `concluded`. An operator can delete an `active` experiment, after
which its variant pool's transition behavior is undefined.

**Resolution:** `handleDeleteExperiment` in `pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go` now reads the experiment's status first and rejects active/paused with `409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` (carrying `details.currentStatus`). Operators must PATCH to `concluded` before DELETE. Closed in this batch's commit.

### - [x] F-10.7.18 — 18  `EvalResponse` omits `experimentId`, `variantId`, `delegationDepth`, `inherited`, and `submittedAfterConclusion` [Low] — CLOSED

carries the experiment attribution and the three boolean/numeric flags.
While the spec does not explicitly require these on the immediate POST
response, the schema is documented as authoritative and downstream tooling
naturally expects round-tripping.

`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go:26-34`

on the create response.

retrievable via the Results API. Callers writing client code against the
spec EvalResult schema will need an additional GET to surface attribution.

**Resolution:** Extended `EvalResponse` with `experimentId`, `variantId`, `delegationDepth`, `inherited`, and `submittedAfterConclusion`, all `omitempty` so unenrolled sessions emit the same compact shape as before. The handler now copies the stored attribution into the response.
