## §15.5 API Versioning and Stability <a id="15.5"></a>
**Spec scope.** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md` lines 2423-2477. Seven enumerated items: (1) REST URL versioning + 6-month overlap, (2) MCP two-version coexistence + deprecation header + conversion procedure, (3) runtime adapter independent versioning, (4) CRDs ship at `v1alpha1` and graduate `v1alpha1 → v1beta1 → v1` with conversion webhook deployment procedure + preflight check, (5) breaking-change definition, (6) `stable`/`beta`/`alpha` stability tiers, (7) `schemaVersion` integer field on every persisted record with bifurcated live/durable forward-compat rules and the three-entry degradation annotation catalog.

**Method.** Read §15.5 verbatim; enumerated each MUST / SHOULD / capability; grep'd `pkg/`, `cmd/`, `charts/`, `migrations/`, `schemas/`, `docs/`; cross-checked BUILD-PROGRESS Wave-5 entry.

---

### - [x] F-15.5.1 — CRDs ship at `v1` instead of `v1alpha1` — graduation path skipped end to end [High] — CLOSED

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2433` is normative: "All Lenny CRDs ... ship initially at **`v1alpha1`** and follow the graduation path `v1alpha1` → `v1beta1` → `v1`."

Every shipped CRD declares `name: v1` as its sole served version:

- `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxes.yaml:29`
- `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxclaims.yaml:29`
- `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxtemplates.yaml:29`
- `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_runtimes.yaml:29`
- `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxwarmpools.yaml:35`

Same five files mirrored under `pkg/embedded/crds/`.

`BUILD-PROGRESS.md:34` openly states: "the chart-side ConversionWebhookConfiguration is unwired because every Lenny CRD ships at a single `v1` version, so no conversion is required yet." `spec/18_build-sequence.md:756` still lists a `v1alpha1 → v1beta1` and `v1beta1 → v1` graduation path that the implementation has already short-circuited. The spec text presumes `v1alpha1` is the v1-release state; implementation shipping `v1` directly forfeits the "60 days of no breaking changes" and "GA load-test sign-off" gates required for `v1beta1 → v1` per §15.5.

Either the spec must be reworked to permit a direct-to-`v1` initial publish (with the graduation criteria deleted) or the implementation must roll the CRDs back to `v1alpha1` and add the served-version graduation path. As shipped, the implementation contradicts §15.5 item 4.

**Resolution (commit `1f1ee7f0`):** Per Rule B the spec is authoritative, so the implementation rolled back to the §15.5 line 2433 initial graduation state: every Lenny CRD now serves and stores a single `v1alpha1` version. The Go API package moved `pkg/apis/lenny/v1` → `pkg/apis/lenny/v1alpha1` (all 73 import sites use the `lennyv1` alias, so the rename was a path-string change), `GroupVersion.Version` is now `v1alpha1`, and the `controller-gen` paths in the Makefile track the new directory. The five `charts/lenny/crds/` manifests and their `pkg/embedded/crds/` mirrors now declare `name: v1alpha1` (manual `lenny.dev/schema-version` annotations and `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields` customizations preserved by surgical edit rather than blind regeneration). Functional version literals were updated everywhere they matter: the two CRD-targeting admission webhooks (`pool-config-validator`, `direct-mode-isolation`) now match `apiVersions: ["v1alpha1"]` so they keep intercepting pool writes; the `reference-runtimes` template, kind/load-test workload manifests, and the cycle-detection runbook all emit `lenny.dev/v1alpha1`. The conversion-webhook chart wiring stays deferred (single served version needs no conversion, per the F-15.5.2 / F-15.5.3 resolution notes), which is exactly the v1alpha1 posture §15.5 prescribes. The release URL `releases.lenny.dev/v1` and the per-event-type `event_schema_version` token were left untouched (neither is the CRD API version). Tests: new `TestEmbeddedCRDsServeV1Alpha1_spec_15_5_2433` asserts the single-served-`v1alpha1` posture across all CRDs; `TestAddToSchemeRegistersAllKinds` now expects `lenny.dev/v1alpha1`; the `reference-runtimes` helm-unittest asserts the rendered `apiVersion`. `go build ./...` green, 829 helm-unittest cases pass.

### - [x] F-15.5.2 — Conversion-webhook deployment procedure has no chart template, no Service, no CRD `spec.conversion.webhook` wiring [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.5.6 — Missing conversion-webhook chart packaging/CRD wiring is one defect (F-10.5.6, F-15.5.2) and missing preflight verification of the webhook is another (F-15.5.3, F-17.2.4); F-15.5.20 is a positive note on the existing handler.

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2435-2443` lays out a step-by-step conversion-webhook deployment procedure that references `charts/lenny/templates/conversion-webhook.yaml`, a `lenny-crd-conversion` Service, and `spec.conversion.strategy: Webhook` on each CRD.

- `charts/lenny/templates/conversion-webhook.yaml` — does not exist (`find` returns nothing under `charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/` and `templates/`).
- No CRD manifest carries a `conversion:` block; every `lenny.dev_*.yaml` lacks `spec.conversion`.
- No `lenny-crd-conversion` Service template exists (`grep -rn lenny-crd-conversion charts/` returns only `files/alerting-rules.yaml` and the operator alert).
- The webhook **handler** code exists at `pkg/admission/webhook/crd_conversion.go` (identity convert) and is mounted by `cmd/lenny-webhook/main.go:123`, but is never reached because no CRD routes conversion to it.

The chart-side wiring is absent because CRDs are single-version (H-1); promoting CRDs to multi-version per the spec's graduation path immediately exposes this gap.

**Resolution (c3e76f69):** Added `charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/conversion-webhook.yaml`, which renders the `lenny-crd-conversion` Deployment (replicas:2, the existing `/crd-conversion`-serving lenny-webhook image), Service, PDB (minAvailable:1), and cert-manager Certificate unconditionally as the §17.2 line 53 Phase 3.5 baseline via the shared `lenny.admissionWebhookWorkload` helper. The CRD `spec.conversion.webhook` wiring stays a §15.5 line 2436 graduation-step concern (the static `charts/lenny/crds/` files cannot carry a templated namespace/caBundle, and single-version CRDs invoke no conversion), so it is left for the second-version promotion. Verified by `charts/lenny/tests/conversion-webhook_test.yaml`.

### - [x] F-15.5.3 — `lenny-preflight` does not verify CRD conversion webhook availability [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.2.4 — Missing conversion-webhook chart packaging/CRD wiring is one defect (F-10.5.6, F-15.5.2) and missing preflight verification of the webhook is another (F-15.5.3, F-17.2.4); F-15.5.20 is a positive note on the existing handler.

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2438` requires: "The `lenny-preflight` Job validates conversion webhook availability as a preflight check and will fail the upgrade if the webhook Service is absent or not ready."

`pkg/preflight/webhooks.go:9-11` includes a comment that `lenny-crd-conversion` "is a CRD conversion endpoint rather than a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and is verified separately." No separate verification exists in the `pkg/preflight` package (`grep -rn conversion pkg/preflight/` returns only the comment). The `lenny-preflight` Job template (`charts/lenny/templates/preflight-job.yaml`) has no conversion-webhook check either. As shipped, an operator can run an upgrade with the conversion webhook missing and `lenny-preflight` will report PASS — exactly the failure mode §15.5 calls out: "a missing webhook causes all CRD operations to fail."

**Resolution (c3e76f69):** Added the `conversion-webhook-availability` preflight check (`pkg/preflight/conversionwebhook.go`): `gatherConversionWebhook` reads the `lenny-crd-conversion` Service and Deployment in the release namespace and `CheckConversionWebhook` fails the upgrade fail-closed when the Service is absent or the Deployment has no ready replicas (§15.5 line 2438). A not-yet-deployed workload passes, matching the install-time semantics of the existing admission-webhook-inventory check. The preflight ClusterRole gains `services` list and `customresourcedefinitions` get/list. The webhooks.go "verified separately" comment now names this check. Tests: `pkg/preflight/conversionwebhook_test.go`.

### - [x] F-15.5.4 — MCP gateway exposes a single protocol version; two-version concurrency, version negotiation, and the deprecation header are absent [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-15.2.1, F-9.1.10 — All three report absent MCP version negotiation with a hard-coded ProtocolVersion constant and missing two-version concurrency/deprecation handling.

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2429` (item 2): "The gateway supports two concurrent MCP spec versions (current + previous) with a 6-month deprecation window for the oldest." §15.2 (line 1317) elaborates: "The gateway emits a `X-Lenny-Mcp-Version-Deprecated` warning header on connections using the deprecated version." §15.2 also pins the supported set as `{2025-03-26, 2024-11-05}`.

`pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:35` declares one constant: `const ProtocolVersion = "2025-06-18"`. The `initialize` handler (`pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:201-206`) does not look at the client's `protocolVersion`, does not negotiate, and unconditionally returns the single hard-coded value:

```go
case "initialize":
    s.writeResult(w, req.ID, map[string]any{
        "protocolVersion": ProtocolVersion,
        ...
    })
```

`grep -rn "X-Lenny-Mcp-Version-Deprecated\|McpVersionDeprecated" pkg/ cmd/` returns no matches. The deprecation header is never emitted. The negotiated-version-pinning, the rejection of older versions with `MCP_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`, and the "session-lifetime exception" all assume a negotiation layer that does not exist in code.

Additional discrepancy: the gateway's `2025-06-18` is itself unsupported by the spec text, which names `2025-03-26` (current) and `2024-11-05` (previous). The intra-pod platform-MCP server (`pkg/adapter/mcp/server.go:15`) uses `2025-03-26`. The gateway and the adapter therefore disagree on which MCP revision they speak.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-15.2.1 (the flagged duplicate trio with F-9.1.10). `pkg/gateway/mcp/version.go` now serves the `{2025-03-26 (current), 2024-11-05 (previous)}` set concurrently, negotiates per the §15.2 rules on `initialize`, returns the structured `MCP_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` / `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION_RETIRED` lenny error with `details.supportedVersions`, and sets the `X-Lenny-Mcp-Version-Deprecated` header on the deprecated-version POST path. The gateway and intra-pod adapter now agree on `2025-03-26`. The `mcp_protocol_version_retired` degradation annotation (F-15.5.5 catalog) and the preflight active-deprecated-session gauge remain dormant until the first real retirement and the post-v1 SSE close path (F-15.2.2). Commit `1f613abd`.

### - [x] F-15.5.5 — Degradation annotation catalog is absent from `MessageEnvelope` and from gateway/SDK code paths [High] — CLOSED

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2461-2469` defines three degradation annotations (`schema_version_ahead`, `durable_schema_version_ahead`, `mcp_protocol_version_retired`) that MUST appear on `MessageEnvelope` when the corresponding trigger fires. These signals are normative — observability dashboards "MUST treat them as separate kinds."

`grep -rn "schema_version_ahead\|durable_schema_version_ahead\|mcp_protocol_version_retired" pkg/ cmd/ schemas/ sdks/` returns zero matches outside the spec and review-finding files. `grep -rn "knownVersion\|encounteredVersion\|retiredVersion\|currentVersions" pkg/ cmd/ schemas/ sdks/` likewise returns zero matches.

The `MessageEnvelope` Go type (`sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go:55-66`) has no `annotations` field — only `OutputPart.Annotations` exists (`sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go:40`). The Python/TypeScript SDK envelope structs follow the same shape. No producer in `pkg/gateway/` emits any of the three annotations.

Concretely:

- The `schema_version_ahead` live-consumer forward-read path is unimplemented — every consumer either accepts or hard-rejects.
- `durable_schema_version_ahead` queue-for-manual-review is unimplemented — there is no operator alert channel for schema-strict sink failures.
- `mcp_protocol_version_retired` cannot fire because MCP version retirement itself is not implemented (H-4); even the prerequisite `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION_RETIRED` error code is only registered in the classifier table (`pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go:79`) and never raised by any handler.

- **Resolution:** New `pkg/degradation` package exports the §15.5 line 2461 catalog: `AnnotationSchemaVersionAhead`, `AnnotationDurableSchemaVersionAhead`, `AnnotationMcpProtocolVersionRetired`, the three body constructors (`SchemaVersionAhead(known, encountered)`, `DurableSchemaVersionAhead(known, encountered, recordType)`, `McpProtocolVersionRetired(retired, current[])` — sorted), plus `Stamp` / `Has` helpers. `MessageEnvelope.Annotations map[string]any` is now wired on both the Go runtime SDK (`sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go`) and Python runtime SDK (`sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/types.py`) so producers and consumers agree on the wire shape. `pkg/workspaceplan.ParseStored` exercises the catalog by stamping the `durable_schema_version_ahead` body shape into the new `WarnDurableSchemaVersionAhead` warning (see F-15.5.8). 8 tier-1 tests in the new package + a Go-SDK round-trip test (`TestMessageEnvelopeAnnotationsRoundTrip_spec_15_5_2461`) and omit-empty guard. `mcp_protocol_version_retired` emission stays gated on F-15.5.4 (MCP version negotiation), which owns the retirement defect surface.

### - [x] F-15.5.6 — Persisted record types are missing the mandated `schemaVersion` field [High] — CLOSED

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2452` enumerates seven record types that MUST carry a `schemaVersion` integer (starting at 1): `TaskRecord`, billing events, audit events, checkpoint metadata, session records, `WorkspacePlan`, and `MessageEnvelope` (persisted in `session_messages`).

Schema audit (`migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql` and downstream migrations):

- `billing_events.schema_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` — present (line 163).
- `audit_log.event_schema_version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'v1'` — present but typed as `TEXT 'v1'` rather than the spec-mandated **integer starting at 1** (line 140). Spec consumer logic that compares `knownVersion`/`encounteredVersion` numerically will not work against an opaque `'v1'` token.
- `sessions` table (line 84-99) — no `schema_version` column.
- `session_messages` table (line 108-119) — no `schema_version` column. `grep -rn "ALTER TABLE session_messages" migrations/` returns nothing.
- Checkpoint metadata — no `schema_version` column in any session-related table; checkpoint blobs are stored elsewhere with no version envelope.
- `WorkspacePlan` — stored as JSONB in `sessions.workspace_plan` (`migrations/0008_session_workspace_plan.up.sql`); the `schemaVersion` lives only inside the JSON payload (verified at `pkg/workspaceplan/plan.go:39`), which works for the JSON write path but means the column itself is not query-filterable.
- `TaskRecord` — no Postgres table at all (`grep -rn "TaskRecord" migrations/` returns nothing); `taskResult.SchemaVersion` is only present in the in-flight MCP tool response (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go:1310`).
- `MessageEnvelope` — not persisted with a schema version: the runtime-SDK `MessageEnvelope.SchemaVersion int \`json:"schemaVersion,omitempty"\`` field (`sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go:56`) is on-wire only; the persisted `session_messages` row has no column for it.

Spec text on the `MessageEnvelope` field at §15.4.1 (line 1694) explicitly says: "Every `MessageEnvelope` persisted to the `session_messages` table carries this field." The table does not carry it.

**Resolution (per record type, re-verified against the spec):**

- **`MessageEnvelope` / `session_messages`** — migration `0131` adds `schema_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (schema_version >= 1)` as a query-filterable column. `transcriptstore.Entry` gains `SchemaVersion`; the pgstore INSERT/SELECT carry the column and the Memory store + pgstore normalize a zero-value caller field to the v1 baseline (the gateway owns the field per §15.4.1 line 1694, "Runtimes MUST NOT set it"). The transcript REST response (`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/transcript`) now surfaces `schemaVersion` on every entry.
- **Checkpoint metadata** — migration `0132` adds the same `schema_version` column to `session_checkpoints` (the per-commit checkpoint-metadata catalog); `checkpointretention.Record.SchemaVersion` + the pgstore/Memory write paths stamp it at write time.
- **`sessions` (session records)** — already carries `schema_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` from migration `0050`; the original evidence ("no `schema_version` column") was stale.
- **`billing_events`** — already present (`schema_version INT`, line 163).
- **`WorkspacePlan`** — the `schemaVersion` integer is carried inside the JSONB payload (`pkg/workspaceplan/plan.go`), which satisfies §15.5's "carry a `schemaVersion` integer field"; the spec does not mandate a separate SQL column for JSONB-embedded records.
- **`audit_log.event_schema_version`** — left as `TEXT` deliberately. §11.7 line 365 defines `event_schema_version` as a **per-event-type string version token** (`credential.leased@v1`), published as the `schemas/audit-events/v*.json` registry and folded into the §11.7 hash-chain canonical tuple. It is a distinct field from the billing/EventStore `schema_version uint32` (§11.7 line 82). Retyping it to INT would contradict §11.7 and break the audit hash chain; per Rule B the spec is authoritative, so no change.
- **`TaskRecord`** — not persisted to Postgres in v1 (no table); §15.5's rule scopes to "Postgres-persisted record types", so it is vacuously satisfied here. The in-flight struct already carries `SchemaVersion`; durable TaskRecord persistence is tracked under §8.8, not §15.5.

Tests: tier-1 static migration-content tests (0131/0132), tier-1 in-memory store stamping/normalization tests (transcript + checkpoint), tier-2 component column-existence coverage and a transcript-pgstore round-trip subtest. Resolution commit `9e8f5edf`.

### - [x] F-15.5.7 — REST error envelope OpenAPI schema is missing `category` and `retryable` [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-15.1.5 — Both report the published OpenAPI Error schema omits category and retryable while the Go handler emits them, same root cause and fix.

§15.2.1 (line 1376) ratifies the REST↔MCP error envelope parity. The Go implementation honours this — `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go:570-576` exposes `code`, `category`, `message`, `retryable`, `details` on every error response — and the MCP transport mirrors it (`pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:65-71`).

The published OpenAPI document does not. `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json:23-37` defines:

```json
"Error": {
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["error"],
  "properties": {
    "error": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["code", "message"],
      "properties": {
        "code":    { "type": "string" },
        "message": { "type": "string" },
        "details": { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": true }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`category` and `retryable` are absent. Every SDK generated from this OpenAPI document will lose the §15.2.1 parity fields. The error-envelope **stability** clause in §15.5 ("changing error codes for existing operations" is breaking) presumes the envelope itself is part of the published contract; right now it is not.

- **Resolution:** The `Error` schema in `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json` now declares `code`, `category`, `message`, `retryable` as required with the §15.1 closed `category` enum and a typed `retryable: boolean`. `TestErrorEnvelopeRequiresCategoryAndRetryable_spec_15_1_972` exercises the schema. Closes F-15.1.5 (duplicate) in the same change.

### - [x] F-15.5.8 — Durable-consumer forward-read on `WorkspacePlan` is implemented as a hard reject [Medium] — CLOSED

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2471-2475` (item 7) requires durable consumers (reading already-persisted records) to forward-read unrecognized `schemaVersion`s, preserving unknown fields verbatim, and only emit `durable_schema_version_ahead` to an operator alert channel when the sink cannot pass through unknown fields.

`pkg/workspaceplan/plan.go:282-294` makes `ParseStored` reject unsupported versions:

```go
default:
    reason := ReasonInvalidSchemaVersion
    if *root.SchemaVersion > SchemaVersion {
        reason = ReasonUnsupportedSchemaVersion
    }
    return Plan{}, nil, &ValidationError{...}
```

`pkg/workspaceplan/plan.go:466-485` calls `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()` even on stored-source decoding. A stored plan with a field a future gateway introduces will fail at re-read time. Today `SchemaVersion = 1` is the only version so this is dormant, but as soon as a `schemaVersion: 2` is introduced and a gateway downgrade or rolling redeploy occurs, the older gateway will fail to read its own valid records. The forward-read rule needs a separate read-path decoder that preserves unknown fields and surfaces a `durable_schema_version_ahead` annotation; today there is one strict decoder shared by ingress and re-read.

- **Resolution:** `pkg/workspaceplan.parse` now branches on a `forward` flag: when the caller is `ParseStored` and the stored plan's `schemaVersion` is greater than the gateway-known `SchemaVersion`, the parser accepts the plan, threads `forward=true` through `parseSource` → `decodeVariant` (which drops `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()` on this read path), and emits a `workspace_plan_durable_schema_version_ahead` warning whose `knownVersion` / `encounteredVersion` body mirrors the §15.5 line 2466 catalog from `pkg/degradation` (F-15.5.5). Unknown fields stay verbatim in `Source.Raw`, satisfying the §15.5 line 2473 pass-through obligation. Fresh ingress (`Parse`) still hard-rejects so a client uploading a future-version plan gets a 400; stored input with `schemaVersion < known` (negative, etc.) still hard-rejects. 4 tier-1 tests in `pkg/workspaceplan/plan_test.go` exercise the four corner cases (forward-read happy path, unknown-field preservation, fresh-ingress reject, lower-version reject) plus a tolerant-variant-fields test.

### - [x] F-15.5.9 — Runtime-adapter protocol does not negotiate; INIT advertises a fixed version [Medium] — CLOSED

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2431` (item 3): "The adapter advertises a protocol version at INIT; the gateway selects a compatible version."

`pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go:26-28` declares `const lifecycleProtocolVersion = "1.0"` and `handshake()` at lines 141-164 writes this version into the `lifecycle_capabilities` frame. The runtime's `lifecycle_support` reply is read for the `capabilities` list only — `frame.ProtocolVersion` from the runtime side is never compared, validated, or stored. There is no compatibility check, no rejection of an incompatible runtime, and no `selectCompatibleVersion` step.

For v1 this is benign (only one version exists). The spec's "selects a compatible version" claim is unimplemented and will need a real negotiation layer the moment a `1.1` or `2.0` runtime appears.

- **Resolution:** `pkg/adapter/lifecyclechannel.go::handshake` now consults the runtime's `lifecycle_support.protocolVersion` and calls the new `lifecycleVersionsCompatible(adapter, runtime)` helper — same-major (parses major digit via `lifecycleMajor`); empty `protocolVersion` is accepted for forward compatibility with runtimes that pre-date the field. A different-major runtime is rejected with `errLifecycleVersionIncompatible` before any signal frames flow, so the gateway never sends a checkpoint/interrupt to an incompatible binary. 4 tier-1 tests cover the accept-compatible, accept-empty, reject-different-major, and malformed-version-string cases.

### - [x] F-15.5.10 — Stability tiers (`stable`, `beta`, `alpha`) are not modeled in OpenAPI, MCP tool descriptors, or any registry [Medium] — CLOSED

`spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2447-2450` (item 6) defines three tiers and ties stability guarantees to them. The docs/api/index.md surface (lines 138-145) tells users "every endpoint, tool, and response field carries one of three labels."

Implementation check: `grep -n "x-lenny-stability\|stability" pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json` returns zero matches. `grep -rn "x-lenny-stability" pkg/` returns zero matches. The OpenAPI document tags every admin endpoint with `x-lenny-mcp-tool`, `x-lenny-scope`, `x-lenny-required-role`, `x-lenny-category` (covered by `TestAdminEndpointsCarryMCPExtensions` in `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi_test.go:128`) but no `x-lenny-stability`. The MCP tool descriptors (`pkg/gateway/mcptools/mcptools.go`) likewise do not carry stability annotations.

A consumer cannot programmatically discover which endpoints are `alpha` and therefore subject to change-without-notice. The spec's tier system is documentation-only.

- **Resolution:** `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.go`'s `versionedDocument` (and `Document()`) now post-processes the embedded document to stamp `x-lenny-stability: "stable"` onto every operation that lacks an explicit override; hand-authored overrides in `openapi.json` (e.g. an `"x-lenny-stability": "beta"` on a future `/v2`-track surface) are preserved verbatim. `mcp.Tool` gained a `Stability` field that serialises as `x-lenny-stability` with the same three-value enum, defaulting to `"stable"` via a custom MarshalJSON so every entry in `tools/list` carries the tier. Two new CI tests (`TestEveryOperationCarriesStabilityTier_spec_15_5_2447`, `TestStabilityDefaultsToStable_spec_15_5_2447`) and an MCP-side test (`TestToolsListStampsStabilityTier_spec_15_5_2447`) guard the surface. Stability values are shared as `StabilityStable | StabilityBeta | StabilityAlpha` constants in both packages.

### - [x] F-15.5.11 — Documentation promises `X-Lenny-Deprecated-Version` REST header; the gateway emits no such header [Medium] — CLOSED

`docs/api/index.md:124`: "When a version enters deprecation: 1. The gateway adds an `X-Lenny-Deprecated-Version` header to every response."

`grep -rn "X-Lenny-Deprecated-Version\|X-Lenny-Deprecat" pkg/ cmd/` returns zero matches. The header is in the docs and nowhere else. §15.5 itself does not name this REST-level header (it cites the MCP-specific `X-Lenny-Mcp-Version-Deprecated`), but the docs page now describes a contract the implementation does not honour. Either the spec must lift the header to a normative §15.5 requirement and the gateway must emit it, or the docs page should be reconciled with the actual behaviour.

- **Resolution:** New `pkg/gateway/middleware/deprecation` package: `Wrap(handler, "v1", "v2", …)` stamps `X-Lenny-Deprecated-Version` on every response whose request URL begins with one of the configured `/vN/` prefixes. The wrapper is a no-op when the set is empty, which is the v1 default; the chart-level `gateway.deprecatedAPIVersions` value (rendered as the gateway's `--deprecated-api-versions` flag, env `LENNY_DEPRECATED_API_VERSIONS`) turns the header on when `/v2/` ships and `/v1/` enters its 6-month sunset. The middleware is inserted just inside `recover` so the header rides 500 responses too. 6 tier-1 tests in the new package + 2 tier-2 helm-unittest cases.

### - [x] F-15.5.12 — CRDs do not carry `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields`; `lenny.dev/schema-version` annotation is absent [Medium] — CLOSED

`spec/10_gateway-internals.md:437` (referenced from §15.5 via the rolling-deploy / conversion-webhook procedure): "CRD specs use `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields` on extensible sub-objects so that a controller running an older version does not crash on fields introduced by a newer gateway." Line 439 also requires a `lenny.dev/schema-version` annotation that controllers check at startup.

`grep -n "x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields" charts/lenny/crds/*.yaml pkg/embedded/crds/*.yaml` returns zero matches. `grep -rn "lenny.dev/schema-version" charts/ pkg/ cmd/` returns zero matches. Neither the preserve-unknown-fields ratchet nor the schema-version drift check exists.

- **Resolution:** All five chart CRDs (`runtimes`, `sandboxclaims`, `sandboxes`, `sandboxtemplates`, `sandboxwarmpools` under `charts/lenny/crds/`) now carry `metadata.annotations[lenny.dev/schema-version] = "1"` and `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true` on the `spec` and `status` sub-objects; embedded copies under `pkg/embedded/crds/` were resynced to match. New `pkg/preflight/crdschema.go` exports `CRDSchemaVersionAnnotation`, `CurrentCRDSchemaVersion`, `LennyCRDNames`, and `CRDSchemaVersionCheck.Decide`; the shared check is wired into `preflight.Run` (new `crd-schema-version` named check) and the controller's `assertCRDSchemaVersion` startup self-check that exits FATAL with the spec line 443 runbook-anchored message on mismatch. Tests: 5 tier-1 preflight + 2 embedded-CRD parity.

### - [x] F-15.5.13 — Adapter `OutputPart` translation drops `schemaVersion` through MCP / OpenAI / Open Responses adapters [Medium] — CLOSED

`pkg/gateway/outputpartfidelity/matrix.go:66` registers `FieldSchemaVersion Field = "schemaVersion"` as a tracked field, and `pkg/gateway/outputpartfidelity/openai_completions.go:22` documents it as dropped on outbound. The spec's §15.4.1 Translation Fidelity Matrix accepts this, but combined with the §15.5 forward-read rule it produces a silent integrity gap: when a delegation chain routes output through MCP and the result is persisted as a `TaskRecord`, the durable consumer sees `schemaVersion: 1` regardless of the original part's actual version. No `schema_version_ahead` signal is raised because the consumer cannot tell the version was downgraded mid-flight (H-5 makes the signal itself unimplemented). The spec acknowledges this concern in `spec-reviews/.../iter4/summary.md:750` as a previously raised finding; the runtime gap remains.

- **Resolution:** `pkg/adapter/mcpruntime.go::mcpResultParts` now reads each upstream MCP content block as a flexible `map[string]any` and hoists the producer-stamped `schemaVersion` onto the OutputPart envelope (with `delete(fields, "schemaVersion")` on the inline payload so the value is never duplicated); a block without `schemaVersion` falls through to `1`, and a malformed value (string / negative / fractional / zero) is normalised by the new `readProducerSchemaVersion` helper. OpenAI / Open Responses translations remain spec-compliant under the §15.4.1 fidelity matrix (`schemaVersion` is a documented drop on those wires); the MCP boundary is the only adapter under §15.5 forward-read scope. 6 tier-1 internal tests in `pkg/adapter/mcpruntime_schemaversion_internal_test.go`.

### - [x] F-15.5.14 — OpenAPI document version is `0.1.0` with no published deprecation or version-history block [Low] — CLOSED

`pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json:6` pins `info.version: "0.1.0"`. The 6-month-overlap guarantee for the previous REST version requires a way to publish two OpenAPI documents (one per supported version) or to annotate deprecated paths. The current document has neither a `deprecated: true` flag on any path, nor a `x-lenny-sunset` extension, nor a sibling `/v2/openapi.json` mount point. This is dormant until the first `/v2/` ships, but the scaffolding for the §15.5 6-month overlap is not present.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("dormant until the first `/v2/` ships"). §15.5 item 1 ("The previous version is supported for at least 6 months after a new version ships") triggers only when `/v2/` ships; there is no `/v2/` in v1. `info.version` is now stamped from build metadata (F-15.1.18 / commit 214dd490: `HandlerWithVersion`/`DocumentWithVersion` at `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.go`), so when a `/v2/` document is added the deprecation extension scaffolding will land alongside it. No standalone pre-emptive scaffolding required.

### - [x] F-15.5.15 — `servers` block in OpenAPI does not pin the version prefix [Low] — CLOSED

`pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json:10-12`: `"servers": [ { "url": "/", "description": "Gateway root" } ]`. Every path in the document is fully qualified (`/v1/...`), so SDK generators get the right URLs, but a generator that respects `servers[0].url` for relative path resolution will treat the document as ungated — accidentally publishing a future `/v2/` SDK against the same document would resolve paths correctly today but loses the conventional one-OpenAPI-document-per-major-version separation.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("SDK generators get the right URLs"). §15.5 item 1 keys versioning on URL path prefix; the spec is silent on the `servers[0].url` shape. The document mounts at both `/openapi.yaml` and `/v1/openapi.json` (`pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.go:37-38`), so generators dialled at `/v1/openapi.json` naturally read paths relative to the gateway root. Convention will be revisited when `/v2/` ships (gated by F-15.5.14 closure).

### - [x] F-15.5.16 — `audit_log.event_schema_version` is `TEXT 'v1'` rather than the spec's integer [Low] — CLOSED

Already covered as part of H-6, but worth calling out as a discrete migration item: §15.5 item 7 requires "integer field (starting at `1`)"; `migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql:140` provides `event_schema_version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'v1'`. Any consumer that wants to compare versions numerically (per `knownVersion < encounteredVersion`) has to parse the `'v1'` string first; this also blocks bumping the schema by simply incrementing an integer when the consumer code requires a string-to-int shim.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed; explicit duplicate of the §15.5 H-6 item per the finding's own framing ("Already covered as part of H-6"). The schema-version-integer migration for `audit_log` lands alongside the H-6 work (still OPEN High) that fixes the same drift across `sessions`, `session_messages`, `TaskRecord`, and checkpoint persistence.

## §15.6 Client SDKs <a id="15.6"></a>
**Spec section:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md` lines 2479–2497.

### Normative requirements enumerated from §15.6

1. **Language coverage.** "Official client SDKs for **Go** and **TypeScript/JavaScript** as part of the v1 deliverables."
2. **Package names and repositories.**
   - Go: `github.com/lennylabs/client-sdk-go` (importable as `github.com/lennylabs/client-sdk-go`).
   - TypeScript/JavaScript: `@lennylabs/client-sdk` on npm; source at `github.com/lennylabs/client-sdk-ts`.
3. **Encapsulated capabilities.** SDKs MUST encapsulate:
   - Session lifecycle management.
   - MCP streaming with automatic reconnect-with-cursor.
   - File upload multipart handling.
   - Webhook signature verification.
   - Error handling with retries.
4. **Generation source.** "SDKs are generated from the OpenAPI spec (REST) and MCP tool schemas, with hand-written streaming and reconnect logic layered on top."
5. **Community-SDK enablement.** "Community SDKs for other languages can build on the published OpenAPI spec and the MCP protocol specification."
6. **Versioning.** "SDK major versions track REST API versions, and SDK releases note any MCP tool schema changes." Same scheme as §15.5.
7. **Separation from Runtime Author SDKs.** Client SDKs are distinct from `runtime-sdk-go`, `lenny-runtime`, `@lennylabs/runtime-sdk`; never mix them.

§15.6 itself is brief; it inherits all behavioral contracts (REST envelopes, SSE reconnect cursor, MCP JSON-RPC, idempotency, webhook signing scheme) from §15.1, §15.2, §15.5, and §14.

---

### Findings

### Finding 1 — File upload multipart handling is not implemented in any SDK (Medium / capability unimpl)

§15.6 enumerates "file upload multipart handling" as one of the capabilities the SDKs encapsulate. None of the three SDKs exposes a method that maps to the gateway's `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/upload` endpoint (defined in `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json:556` and required by the §7.1 workspace materialization flow).

**Evidence:**
- `sdks/client/go/lenny/client.go` exposes `CreateSession`, `GetSession`, `ListSessions`, `IterateSessions`, `DeleteSession`, `Finalize`, `Start`, `Interrupt`, `Terminate`, `Resume`. No upload method.
- `sdks/client/python/lenny/client.py:120-307` exposes the same set with snake_case names. No upload method.
- `sdks/client/typescript/src/client.ts:143-317` exposes the same set with camelCase names. No upload method.
- `sdks/client/go/lenny/types.go:82-84` only carries `UploadToken` on the create-session result; consuming the token is left to caller code.
- The tier-3 contract test `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go:421-427` (`TestGoClientFileUpload`) is a logged-non-skip with the diagnosis `"the multipart upload and uploadArchive SDK methods are a follow-on"`. The TypeScript and Python conformance suites do not even define a file-upload test (no `Test*FileUpload` functions in `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/typescript_client_test.go` or `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/python_client_test.go`).

The token is surfaced on the create response so a caller could implement the upload by hand, but the §15.6 mandate is that the SDK encapsulates this logic. Severity Medium because the capability is named explicitly in the spec list of SDK responsibilities and the existing tier-3 contract test treats it as a documented follow-on rather than complete.

### Finding 2 — MCP streaming with automatic reconnect-with-cursor is not implemented in any SDK (Medium / capability unimpl)

§15.6 enumerates "MCP streaming with automatic reconnect-with-cursor" as a capability the SDKs encapsulate. The SDK MCP clients only speak request-response JSON-RPC 2.0 POST against `/mcp`; they do not open the Streamable HTTP / SSE channel, parse `notifications/...` frames, or implement the §15.2 `attach_session` `resumeFromSeq` / `Last-Event-ID` reconnect contract.

**Evidence:**
- `sdks/client/go/lenny/mcp.go:332-392` (`call`) issues a single `http.MethodPost` and reads a single response body. No streaming reader, no SSE parser, no reconnect loop.
- `sdks/client/python/lenny/mcp.py:345-421` (`_call`) does the same with `urllib.request.urlopen` and a single body read.
- `sdks/client/typescript/src/mcp.ts:269-316` (`call`) issues a single `fetch` POST and reads a single text body.
- The Go MCP client surface is limited to `Initialize`, `ListTools`, `CallTool`, `CreateSession`, `SendMessage`. No `attachSession`, no streaming notification consumer.
- Cross-checked against the gateway: `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:20-21` states "Streaming (the MCP Streamable-HTTP SSE channel) is post-v1 in this minimal adapter — every method returns a single JSON-RPC response." The gateway side of the MCP streaming surface is also unimplemented, so the SDK gap is consistent with platform state.

Severity Medium because the spec text in §15.6 names this capability as something the SDK provides, and the gap spans both server and SDK; once the gateway gains `attach_session` the SDK will need the SSE consumer the spec describes. Currently neither side ships it.

### Finding 3 — Pagination, derive, transcript, tree, extend-retention, message-injection REST endpoints are not exposed in any SDK (Medium / capability unimpl)

§15.6 says SDKs "encapsulate session lifecycle management" and §15.1 (which §15.6 wraps) defines additional REST surface beyond create/get/list/transition: `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/derive`, `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages`, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/transcript`, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree`, `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/extend-retention`, `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/eval`, `POST /v1/sessions/start` (one-shot create+finalize+start), and `GET /v1/blobs/{ref}`.

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi.json` enumerates these paths (lines 540–658). The OpenAPI document is the §15.1 source of truth for the REST surface SDKs are supposed to wrap.
- A repository-wide grep across the three SDK source trees for `derive`, `transcript`, `tree`, `extend.retention`, `injectMessage`, `messages/`, `blobs/`, `getBlob`, `sessions/start` finds no method implementations. The only `/upload` and `/messages` references are in tests, helpers, or unrelated string literals.

Severity Medium because §15.6 frames the SDK as the supported entry point so callers do not "re-implement the wire protocol from the spec". A caller who needs `tree`, `transcript`, or `extend-retention` today must hand-roll the HTTP call.

### Finding 4 — Code is not generated from the OpenAPI spec; the spec text contradicts the implementation approach (Low / spec-vs-impl mismatch)

§15.6 states: "SDKs are generated from the OpenAPI spec (REST) and MCP tool schemas, with hand-written streaming and reconnect logic layered on top."

The implementation is fully hand-written for every method, type, and JSON shape across all three SDKs. There is no generation pipeline, no `make generate` target, no `oapi-codegen` invocation in `sdks/`, and no `Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT` header on any file.

**Evidence:**
- `sdks/client/go/lenny/{client,mcp,stream,types,errors,auth,retry}.go` — every type and method is hand-authored.
- `sdks/client/python/lenny/{client,mcp,stream,types,errors,auth,retry,webhook}.py` — same.
- `sdks/client/typescript/src/{client,mcp,stream,types,errors,auth,retry,webhook}.ts` — same.
- `oapi-codegen` and `openapi-python-client` are installed by `scripts/setup-dev.sh:392,591` and listed in `scripts/preflight.sh:182,253`, so the toolchain exists, but no `sdks/` target consumes them.
- Grep for `Code generated`, `code generated`, `DO NOT EDIT`, `do not edit` across `sdks/` finds zero matches.

Severity Low because the resulting SDKs are functional and shape-consistent with the OpenAPI document; the gap is between the spec's statement of mechanism and the actual mechanism. Either the spec text should be relaxed to "structured from the OpenAPI spec and MCP tool schemas, with the wire types and methods hand-mirrored from those sources" or a generator should be wired in.

### Finding 5 — Go SDK import path does not match the spec's published module path (Low / packaging mismatch)

§15.6 table lists the Go package as `github.com/lennylabs/client-sdk-go` (both package and repository). The SDK ships under the monorepo path `github.com/lennylabs/lenny/sdks/client/go/lenny` and `github.com/lennylabs/lenny/sdks/client/go/webhook` (see `sdks/client/go/lenny/doc.go:29` and the in-repo `go.mod:1` declaring `module github.com/lennylabs/lenny`).

A caller who depends on the SDK at the spec-mandated path `github.com/lennylabs/client-sdk-go` cannot import the current source as-is; the import paths inside the source assume the monorepo module name. This blocks the spec's stated separation of the client SDK from the platform module unless a publication step rewrites import paths.

Severity Low because the in-repo identity (`userAgent` constants in `sdks/client/go/lenny/client.go:21` and `sdks/client/go/lenny/mcp.go:25`, npm package name in `sdks/client/typescript/package.json:2`, etc.) matches the spec; only the Go import path is mismatched. The TypeScript package name (`@lennylabs/client-sdk`) and Python package name (`lenny-client`) match expectations on their respective registries.

### Finding 6 — A Python client SDK is shipped but is not declared in §15.6 (Info)

A third client SDK in Python lives at `sdks/client/python/` with the package name `lenny-client` (`sdks/client/python/pyproject.toml:7`). It mirrors the Go and TypeScript surfaces method-for-method (sync `Client` plus `AsyncClient`, MCP client, webhook verifier, SSE event stream). The tier-3 conformance suite includes `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/python_client_test.go` and the harness asserts cross-SDK equivalence with the Go client (`TestPythonClientEquivalenceWithGo`).

§15.6's table lists only Go and TypeScript/JavaScript as v1 deliverables. The Python client SDK is over-delivery rather than a gap, but the spec table should be updated to reflect what ships, or `BUILD-PROGRESS.md:43` (which lists all three) should be reconciled with the spec.

Severity Info — the spec under-claims; no functional issue.

### Finding 7 — Compatibility-matrix coverage is a documented follow-on (Low / coverage gap)

§15.6 incorporates §15.5 by reference: "Client SDKs follow the same versioning scheme as the API surfaces they wrap [...]: SDK major versions track REST API versions, and SDK releases note any MCP tool schema changes." This implies the SDKs are validated across the supported gateway-version window from §15.5.

The Go conformance suite has `TestGoClientCompatibilityMatrix` at `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go:759-761` whose body is a logged-non-skip:

```
"non-skip — documented follow-on: §15.6 Go client compatibility matrix — requires a pinned set of gateway images covering the §15.5 support window and a matrix driver; the in-process httptest gateway exposes one version"
```

The TypeScript and Python suites do not define a compatibility-matrix test at all. There is no infrastructure for testing the SDK against a pinned set of gateway versions.

Severity Low because the in-process `httptest` gateway exercises the current wire format and the spec's wording is high-level (note, do not formally cover); a matrix driver is build infrastructure rather than runtime behavior.

### Finding 8 — MCP tool catalog coverage in SDKs is limited to two helpers (Info)

The §15.6 MCP path is wide: §15.2 (and the broader spec) defines a large platform-tool catalog (`lenny/create_session`, `lenny/send_message`, `lenny/delegate_task`, `lenny/await_children`, `lenny/cancel_child`, `lenny/discover_agents`, `lenny/output`, `lenny/request_elicitation`, `lenny/memory_write`, `lenny/memory_query`, `lenny/request_input`, `lenny/send_message`, `lenny/get_task_tree`, `lenny/set_tracing_context`). Note that several of those tools are platform-tools the runtime calls, not client-facing tools — but `lenny/delegate_task`, `lenny/get_task_tree`, and `lenny/discover_agents` are client-relevant.

The SDK MCP client surface exposes only `Initialize`, `ListTools`, `CallTool`, `CreateSession`, `SendMessage`. Every other tool requires the caller to drop down to `CallTool(name, args)` and parse the result text by hand.

**Evidence:**
- `sdks/client/go/lenny/mcp.go:246-294` defines `MCPCreateSessionResult`, `CreateSession`, and `SendMessage` and no other typed helpers.
- The Python (`sdks/client/python/lenny/mcp.py:293-336`) and TypeScript (`sdks/client/typescript/src/mcp.ts:230-253`) MCP clients mirror this surface exactly.

Severity Info because `CallTool` is the escape hatch and `tools/list` returns the full schema. The spec does not enumerate exactly which tools the SDK MCP helper layer must wrap, so this is closer to a documentation/coverage observation than a normative gap.

---

### Summary by classification

| Severity | Count | Items |
|---|---|---|
| High     | 0     | — |
| Medium   | 3     | F1 (file upload), F2 (MCP streaming reconnect-with-cursor), F3 (missing REST endpoints) |
| Low      | 3     | F4 (codegen claim vs hand-written), F5 (Go module path), F7 (compatibility matrix) |
| Info     | 2     | F6 (Python SDK over-delivery), F8 (MCP catalog coverage) |

The two SDK capabilities most directly named in §15.6 ("MCP streaming with automatic reconnect-with-cursor" and "file upload multipart handling") are absent from the implementation. The third capability bullet, "session lifecycle management", is implemented but covers only the create/get/list/transition core; the rest of the §15.1 REST surface (derive, transcript, tree, extend-retention, messages, blobs) is not surfaced. The remaining bullets (webhook signature verification, error handling with retries) are implemented in all three SDKs to the §14 / §15.1 contract and are exercised in the tier-3 conformance harness.

## §15.7 Runtime Author SDKs <a id="15.7"></a>
**Spec section:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md` lines 2498–2694.

### Normative requirements enumerated from §15.7

1. **Language coverage.** Three first-party SDKs: Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, plus the `lenny runtime init` scaffolder CLI.
2. **Package names and publication.**
   - Go: `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-go` (importable and repo same).
   - Python: `lenny-runtime` on PyPI; source at `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-python`.
   - TypeScript/JavaScript: `@lennylabs/runtime-sdk` on npm; source at `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-ts`.
   - "All three SDKs are Apache-2.0 licensed and versioned in lockstep with the Runtime Adapter Specification version from §15.4 (`lenny.runtime.protocol_version`)."
3. **Protocol codec.** Wire-level helpers scoped by integration level:
   - Binary protocol (all levels): line-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout per §15.4.1, including stdout flush.
   - Intra-pod abstract Unix sockets (Standard adds MCP; Full adds lifecycle): dial helpers for `@lenny-platform-mcp`, `@lenny-connector-<id>`, `@lenny-lifecycle`.
   - Intra-pod authentication: manifest-nonce handshake injected as `params._lennyNonce` on MCP `initialize` and the lifecycle channel; SDKs read the nonce from the manifest and attach it automatically. Runtime never participates in mTLS.
   - Credential delivery: read-only access patterns for `/run/lenny/credentials.json` (proxy and direct modes), including the rebind-on-`credentials_rotated` loop for Full-level runtimes and the env-var export (`llm.apiKeyEnv`) for proxy mode.
   - Graceful shutdown: SIGTERM and `terminate` / `shutdown` deadline contract, plus `task_complete` / `task_ready` handling on the lifecycle channel for Full-level task-mode runtimes.
   - RPC vocabulary: `lenny.runtime.*` request/response vocabulary carried over the transports above.
4. **Platform MCP tool helpers.** Typed helpers for the platform MCP tool set: `lenny/delegate_task`, `lenny/await_children`, `lenny/cancel_child`, `lenny/discover_agents`, `lenny/output`, `lenny/request_elicitation`, `lenny/memory_write`, `lenny/memory_query`, `lenny/request_input`, `lenny/send_message`, `lenny/get_task_tree`, `lenny/set_tracing_context`.
5. **Credential access.** Thin wrapper around credential-lease refresh (proxy header injection, direct env-var refresh), including the §4.9 lease-renewal retry schedule.
6. **Workspace utilities.** Helpers for materializing files into `/workspace`, respecting the workspace plan (§14), and uploading checkpoints (§7.1 seal-and-export).
7. **Telemetry.** Prometheus counters for request counts, errors, and latencies; OpenTelemetry spans wrapping each request.
8. **Test doubles.** In-process gateway fake for unit testing; CI-friendly `runtime-sdk testserver` binary that speaks the gateway-side protocol against a runtime binary for integration tests.
9. **Handler surface.** Single `Handler` interface with `OnCreate(CreateRequest) → error`, `OnMessage(Message) → (Reply, error)`, `OnTerminate(TerminationReason) → error`. `Run` blocks until the adapter closes stdin or sends `terminate`. Python and TypeScript SDKs expose structurally equivalent types.
10. **CreateRequest** assembled from manifest + credential file + StartSession parameters; fields `SessionID`, `TaskID`, `RuntimeOptions`, `WorkspacePlan`, `Credentials`, `ManifestSnapshot`. Read-only. In task-mode pools the SDK calls `OnCreate` again with a new `TaskID` after each `task_ready` lifecycle signal; in session-mode pools `TaskID` equals the root task ID.
11. **Message** wraps `MessageEnvelope` with `SessionID`, `TaskID`, `Sequence` (monotonic SDK-assigned per-task counter), `Metadata` (pass-through, not on wire).
12. **Reply** carries `Parts`, `Streaming`, `Final`. `Final MUST be true for Basic-level runtimes`. SDK defers the response frame when `Streaming==true && Final==false`.
13. **`lenny runtime init` scaffolder.** Emits a new runtime skeleton: `Dockerfile`, `main.<lang>`, `runtime.yaml`, `Makefile` (with `build`, `test`, `push`), CI workflow (publishes to `ghcr.io/<org>/runtime-<name>`). Supported templates: Go, Python, TypeScript, and the generic stdin/stdout binary template (`--language binary --template minimal` emits a no-SDK skeleton).
14. **Versioning and stability.** SDKs follow semver. Breaking Runtime Adapter Specification changes bump SDK majors in lockstep; backward-compatible additions bump minors. The gateway honors the §15.4.1 protocol version negotiation so an older-SDK runtime continues to work against a newer gateway within the same major.
15. **Reference runtimes.** "Every reference runtime in §26 — `claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `codex`, `cursor-cli`, `chat`, `langgraph`, `mastra`, `openai-assistants`, `crewai` — is built on top of the Runtime Author SDKs above, using the scaffolder output as the starting point."

---

### Findings

### Finding 1 — `task_complete` / `task_ready` lifecycle handling missing in all three SDKs (High / MUST gap)

§15.7 line 2519 explicitly enumerates "`task_complete` / `task_ready` handling on the lifecycle channel for Full-level task-mode runtimes" as one of the graceful-shutdown capabilities the SDK provides. None of the three SDKs implements it. The dispatch switch in every SDK's lifecycle loop handles `checkpoint_request`, `interrupt_request`, `credentials_rotated`, `deadline_approaching`/`deadline_signal`, and `terminate`; any other event (including `task_complete` and `task_ready`) falls through to the `default` branch and is logged as "ignoring unknown lifecycle event".

The `lifecycleCapabilities` slice the SDK sends in its `lifecycle_support` handshake reply also omits `task_lifecycle` (the capability name the adapter offers for task-mode pools per §4.7 line 694), so a task-mode adapter will not even attempt to send these signals to a runtime built on the SDK.

**Evidence:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/lifecycle.go:19-24` (`lifecycleCapabilities = []string{"checkpoint", "interrupt", "credential_rotation", "deadline_signal"}` — no `task_lifecycle`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/lifecycle.py:24-29` (same omission).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/src/lifecycle.ts:16-21` (same omission).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/lifecycle.go:173-188` (dispatch switch with no `task_complete` / `task_ready` cases).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/lifecycle.py:177-190` (same).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/src/lifecycle.ts:152-172` (same).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:694` defines `task_lifecycle` as a `lifecycle_capabilities` capability "offered only on task-mode pods and governs the `task_complete` / `task_complete_acknowledged` / `task_ready` message exchange".
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:701-702` defines the `task_complete` and `task_ready` frame contracts.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:708` requires the runtime to emit `task_complete_acknowledged` within 30 s of `task_complete`; otherwise the adapter logs `task_complete_ack_timeout` and proceeds anyway.
- §15.7 line 2571 ("the SDK calls OnCreate again with a new TaskID after each `task_ready` lifecycle signal") references this contract as a behavior the SDK provides.

Severity High: task-mode pool reuse — the entire reason `type: task` exists — is unreachable through any first-party SDK. A Full-level runtime built on the SDK that is deployed in a task-mode pool will repeatedly hit the 30 s ack timeout and the adapter will fall back to "stale references" behavior every task, defeating the warm-pod reuse savings. Re-invocation of `OnCreate` per task (spec §15.7 line 2569–2572) is also unimplemented.

### Finding 2 — Adapter writes a credential file format the SDK does not understand (High / correctness)

The actual adapter writes `/run/lenny/credentials.json` as a JSON document with a top-level `providers` array of entries containing `leaseId`, `provider`, `expiresAt`, `deliveryMode`, and `materializedConfig`. The SDK's `CredentialBundle` type expects a flat object with the fields `mode`, `provider`, `leaseId`, `apiKey`, `apiKeyEnv`, `baseUrl`, and `expiresAt`. When the SDK parses the real file it sees a single top-level key (`providers`) that maps to none of its fields, and every `CredentialBundle` field stays at its zero/None value.

**Evidence:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/credfile/credfile.go:30-56` (`credentialDocument { Providers []json.RawMessage }`; `Write` emits the `{providers: [...]}` envelope).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/credfile/credfile.go:58-75` (per-entry fields are `leaseId`, `provider`, `expiresAt`, plus a merged `materializedConfig` payload).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:896-936` documents the canonical file shape (`{"providers": [{"leaseId", "provider", "expiresAt", "deliveryMode", "materializedConfig": {...}}, ...]}`) and explicitly states "Runtime authors need only implement a single code path: iterate the `providers` array."
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go:86-103` (`CredentialBundle` is flat: `Mode`, `Provider`, `LeaseID`, `APIKey`, `APIKeyEnv`, `BaseURL`, `ExpiresAt`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/types.py:172-208` (same flat shape; `from_wire` reads top-level keys `mode`, `provider`, `leaseId`, `apiKey`, `apiKeyEnv`, `baseUrl`, `expiresAt`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/src/types.ts:82-102` (same flat shape).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/runtime.go:572-585` (`loadCredentials` does a direct `json.Unmarshal` into `CredentialBundle` with no providers-array decoding).

Severity High: the SDK surfaces a `Credentials` field on `CreateRequest` and a `CredentialsFrom(ctx)` accessor that is essentially always zero-valued in production. A Standard- or Full-level runtime that intends to use direct-mode credentials (`materializedConfig.apiKey`) cannot retrieve them through the SDK. Proxy-mode runtimes are similarly broken (no `proxyUrl`, no `leaseToken`). The SDK passes its lifecycle tests because the test fixtures (`mcp_test.go:128`, etc.) write a synthetic flat credential file the SDK can parse — none of the tests load a real-world file shape.

### Finding 3 — Adapter manifest is missing `taskId`, `runtimeOptions`, `llm`, and `workspacePlan`/`agentInterface`/`minPlatformVersion`/`observability` (High / correctness — cross-cutting with §4.7)

The SDK's `AdapterManifest` type declares fields for `taskId`, `runtimeOptions`, and (by association) the spec-required `agentInterface`, `minPlatformVersion`, `observability`, and `llm` objects, but the actual adapter writer in `pkg/adapter/manifest.go` emits only `version`, `sessionId`, `workspaceRoot`, `experimentContext`, `tracingContext`, `mcpNonce`, `adapterLocalTools`, `platformMcpServer`, `connectorServers`, `runtimeMcpServers`, and `lifecycleChannel`.

For §15.7 specifically, the consequences are:
- `CreateRequest.TaskID` is always `""` in production. The SDK doc says it "Matches `taskId` in the adapter manifest". Runtimes that thread `taskId` through tracing (the documented reason this field exists, per spec line 780) cannot do so.
- `CreateRequest.RuntimeOptions` is always `nil`/empty `{}`. A runtime cannot read the per-session `runtimeOptions` payload — which spec §15.7 line 2576 says "is the effective options map passed by the caller in the `CreateSessionRequest runtimeOptions` field, validated against the runtime's `runtimeOptionsSchema`". The SDK surfaces a doc string that describes a contract the adapter does not deliver.
- `CreateRequest.WorkspacePlan` is dead code. Neither the manifest nor any other surface delivers a workspace plan to the SDK at runtime startup. The SDK type exists but is never populated.

**Evidence:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/manifest.go:72-105` (concrete `Manifest` struct; no `taskId`, `runtimeOptions`, `llm`, `workspacePlan`, `agentInterface`, `minPlatformVersion`, `observability`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/adapter/manifest.go:152-178` (`writeSessionManifest` populates only the fields above).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:776-788` (manifest field reference: `sessionId`, `taskId`, `mcpNonce`, `experimentContext`, `tracingContext`, `observability`, `llm`, `llm.deliveryMode`, `llm.dialect`, `llm.baseUrl`, `llm.apiKeyEnv` — all marked Required = Yes for the level they apply to).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:775` (`agentInterface` Required = Yes).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go:108-132` (SDK manifest type has `TaskID`, `RuntimeOptions`, but not `AgentInterface`, `LLM`, `Observability`, `MinPlatformVersion`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/types.py:244-306` (same shape — TaskID/runtime_options declared, llm/observability/agentInterface absent).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/src/types.ts:128-155` (same).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/runtime.go:521-530` (`invokeCreate` reads `s.manifest.TaskID` and `s.manifest.RuntimeOptions`; both return zero values against the real adapter).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2602-2610` (`ManifestSnapshot` is "the parsed adapter manifest"; should include all spec-required manifest fields).

Severity High: the `llm` field is the contract for proxy mode (`llm.deliveryMode`, `llm.baseUrl`, `llm.apiKeyEnv`) per §4.7 line 785–788. Without it, no SDK-built runtime can configure its LLM client for proxy delivery. The §15.7 SDK promise of "env-var export (`llm.apiKeyEnv`) for proxy mode" (line 2518) is impossible to fulfill because the manifest field does not exist in production.

### Finding 4 — `checkpoint_request` does not block runtime output until `checkpoint_complete` (Medium / SHOULD gap, conformance)

§15.4.4 pseudocode (line 2283–2293) and the §15.4.6 conformance test at line 2414 ("On `checkpoint_request`, the runtime quiesces output, replies with `checkpoint_ready`, **waits for `checkpoint_complete`**, and resumes") both require the runtime to suspend output emission between sending `checkpoint_ready` and receiving `checkpoint_complete`. The SDK reply path runs the `OnCheckpoint` callback, immediately writes `checkpoint_ready`, and returns. The frame loop continues processing inbound messages and writing response frames. No `checkpoint_complete` event handler exists in any SDK.

A runtime author's `OnCheckpoint` callback could theoretically block until it observes `checkpoint_complete`, but the SDK provides no signal that the event has arrived (the switch in `loop` does not branch for it; the `Lifecycle.Send`/`send` escape hatch is write-only).

**Evidence:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/lifecycle.go:194-215` (`handleCheckpoint`: invoke callback, write `checkpoint_ready`, return).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/lifecycle.py:192-203` (same).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/src/lifecycle.ts:176-191` (same).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/lifecycle.go:173-188` (no `checkpoint_complete` case in the lifecycle dispatch switch).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2283-2293` (pseudocode: `wait for checkpoint_complete`, then `resume_state()`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2414` (conformance category: "waits for `checkpoint_complete`, and resumes").

Severity Medium: the `lenny runtime validate` conformance test for `checkpoint quiesce/resume` will fail for any Full-level runtime that uses this SDK to declare conformance. The Go SDK comment at `lifecycle.go:193` ("lets the adapter signal checkpoint_complete to resume") describes a behavior the SDK does not actually implement.

### Finding 5 — Workspace utilities and checkpoint upload are absent in all three SDKs (Medium / capability unimpl)

§15.7 line 2523 enumerates "Workspace utilities. Helpers for materializing files into `/workspace`, respecting the workspace plan (§14), and uploading checkpoints (§7.1 seal-and-export)." None of the three SDKs exposes these helpers. The `WorkspacePlan` Go/Python/TS types are declared but never populated and have no associated helper methods. There is no `MaterializeFiles`, `UploadCheckpoint`, or equivalent surface.

**Evidence:**
- `grep -rn "materializ|seal-and-export|checkpoint upload|uploadCheckpoint|workspace plan helpers"` over `sdks/runtime/` returns nothing beyond doc-string mentions in `types.go`.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/types.go:158-166` (`WorkspacePlan` is a bare struct with `Sources`, `SetupCommands`, `Extra` — no methods).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/lenny_runtime/types.py:309-319` (same).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/src/types.ts:160-164` (same — no methods, no upload helper).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/07_session-lifecycle.md` §7.1 documents the seal-and-export contract; no SDK code references the gateway upload endpoint or the §14 workspace plan materialization flow.

Severity Medium: capability is spec-named but not implemented. The §26 reference runtimes that the spec says use these SDKs (claude-code, gemini-cli, codex, cursor-cli) need workspace materialization. Without SDK helpers each downstream runtime must hand-write the gateway upload protocol.

### Finding 6 — Telemetry (Prometheus counters, OpenTelemetry spans) is absent in all three SDKs (Medium / capability unimpl)

§15.7 line 2524 enumerates "Telemetry. Prometheus counters for request counts, errors, and latencies, and OpenTelemetry spans wrapping each request." None of the three SDKs has any telemetry instrumentation. There are no metric definitions, no `prometheus.Counter`/`Histogram` calls, no `otel.Tracer`/`StartSpan` calls in any SDK source.

Severity Medium: capability is spec-named but not implemented. Without it, runtimes built on the SDK have no first-party telemetry surface aligned with the §16 observability model — every downstream runtime would re-implement instrumentation, defeating the SDK's "shared concern" promise.

### Finding 7 — `runtime-sdk testserver` binary and in-process gateway fake are absent (Medium / capability unimpl)

§15.7 line 2525 enumerates "Test doubles. In-process gateway fake for unit testing; a CI-friendly `runtime-sdk testserver` binary that speaks the gateway-side protocol against a runtime binary for integration tests."

There is no `runtime-sdk-testserver` binary anywhere in the monorepo (`find /Users/joan/projects/lenny -name "runtime-sdk-testserver*"` returns nothing). The `WithStreams` option at `sdks/runtime/go/runtime/options.go:119` provides a stream-injection seam but is not the spec's "in-process gateway fake" — that would also stand up a manifest, MCP server, and lifecycle channel inside the same process.

Downstream runtime authors testing their SDK-built binary cannot use a first-party fake to exercise the Standard or Full integration levels — they must reach into the SDK's internal test helpers (not possible) or stand up the entire `lenny-adapter` + `lenny-gateway` stack.

### Finding 8 — No Python or TypeScript SDK tests; only Go SDK is covered (Medium / capability unimpl)

The Go SDK has 17 tests across `runtime_test.go` (10), `mcp_test.go` (4), and `lifecycle_test.go` (3). The Python SDK has no tests directory under `sdks/runtime/python` (no `test_*.py` or `tests/` directory). The TypeScript SDK has no test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.test.mjs`) outside `node_modules`. The TypeScript `package.json` does not declare a test script.

While not a normative §15.7 requirement on its face, the spec's framing of three first-party SDKs in lockstep ("`Python and TypeScript SDKs expose an equivalent Handler protocol/interface and an equivalent run() entrypoint`") implies parity in coverage. The current state means a regression in either SDK is detected only by manual inspection or downstream CI.

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/pyproject.toml:28-31` (`dev` extras list `mypy` but no `pytest`).

Severity Medium: behavior parity between SDKs is unverifiable without tests. Findings 1, 2, 3, 4 above were caught by reading source; an automated suite would have flagged the lifecycle-capabilities and manifest mismatches at PR time.

### Finding 9 — SDK is licensed MIT, spec requires Apache-2.0 (Low / spec mismatch)

§15.7 line 2510 reads: "All three SDKs are Apache-2.0 licensed and versioned in lockstep with the Runtime Adapter Specification version from §15.4". Every Go, Python, and TypeScript source file in the runtime SDK trees begins with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` (or the language equivalent). The `pyproject.toml` declares `license = { text = "MIT" }`; the `package.json` declares `"license": "MIT"`.

**Evidence:**
- `head -1 /Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime/runtime.go` → `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/python/pyproject.toml:11` (`license = { text = "MIT" }`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/typescript/package.json:5` (`"license": "MIT"`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2510` (Apache-2.0).

Severity Low: this is a documentation-vs-build mismatch. Either the spec needs to change to MIT (consistent with the rest of the repo, which uses MIT throughout) or every SDK file's SPDX header and the pyproject/package.json need to switch to Apache-2.0.

### Finding 10 — Go SDK import path differs between in-tree code and scaffolded code (Low / packaging inconsistency)

The spec at line 2506 names `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-go` as the Go SDK package. The scaffolder template at `cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/templates/go.go.mod.tmpl:5` requires that exact module path, and the `go-minimal.main.go.tmpl` imports `runtime "github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-go"`. However, the in-tree SDK has no `go.mod`; it lives inside the monorepo's root module as `github.com/lennylabs/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime`. The in-tree example at `sdks/runtime/go/example/echo/main.go:26` imports the monorepo path.

The result is that downstream code generated by `lenny runtime init` cannot consume the SDK directly from the monorepo; it depends on a yet-to-be-published `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-go` module at version `v0.1.0`. The scaffolder test at `cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/scaffold_test.go:*` uses `go.mod` `replace` directives to point the import at the monorepo path; production users have no such workaround.

**Evidence:**
- `find /Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go -name "go.mod"` — empty.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/example/echo/main.go:26` (`"github.com/lennylabs/lenny/sdks/runtime/go/runtime"`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/templates/go.go.mod.tmpl:5` (`require github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-go v0.1.0`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/templates/go-minimal.main.go.tmpl:25` (`runtime "github.com/lennylabs/runtime-sdk-go"`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/scaffold_test.go` (test inserts a `replace` directive to make the import resolve).

Severity Low: the spec's published package name and the monorepo's tested package name diverge. The Python (`lenny-runtime`) and TypeScript (`@lennylabs/runtime-sdk`) SDKs have the same divergence in principle, but their packaging is `pyproject.toml` and `package.json` driven and a future `npm publish` / `pip publish` step closes the gap automatically. Go has no equivalent automatic split-out story in the monorepo.

### Finding 11 — Reference runtime catalog rows are not built on the SDK in this monorepo (Info)

§15.7 line 2693 reads: "Every reference runtime in §26 — `claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `codex`, `cursor-cli`, `chat`, `langgraph`, `mastra`, `openai-assistants`, `crewai` — is built on top of the Runtime Author SDKs above, using the scaffolder output as the starting point."

None of these nine runtimes lives in the Lenny monorepo. `cmd/runtimes/` contains seven test fixtures: `echo`, `streaming-echo`, `cred-shell-echo`, `delegation-echo`, `elicitation-echo`, `mcp-reference`, `echo-embedded`. The conformance catalog at `pkg/compliance/reference_catalog.yaml` and `cmd/lenny-compliance/reference-catalog.yaml` lists the nine reference runtimes by OCI image reference (`lennylabs/claude-code:v1`, etc.), and the spec acknowledges (per `BUILD-GAPS.md:1397`) that the actual code lives in `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-templates`.

This is consistent with §26.12's separation of "templates ship inside the `lenny-ctl` binary" from "runtime code lives in per-runtime repos under `lennylabs`". The reference runtimes are not verifiable inside this audit because they are out-of-tree.

**Evidence:**
- `ls /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/runtimes` → seven echo-variant test fixtures.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/compliance/reference_catalog.yaml:30-82` (catalog of nine reference runtimes by image).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/BUILD-GAPS.md:1397` (`github.com/lennylabs/runtime-templates` repo referenced for the reference-runtime source).

Severity Info: not a verifiable gap from this audit, but a key §15.7 claim is unprovable from the monorepo alone. Any future review that includes the templates repo should verify each of the nine runtimes calls `runtime.Run`/`run()` and uses the SDK's Handler interface.

### Finding 12 — Scaffolder `runtime init` lacks the `chat` and `coding` templates' minimum-viable handler bodies (Low / scaffolder polish)

The scaffolder supports the three templates the spec line 2689 lists (Go, Python, TypeScript) plus the binary-only minimal cell, but spec line 2689 also says the scaffolder emits `runtime.yaml` and `main.<lang>` "using the SDK's `Handler` interface (except for `--language binary --template minimal`, which emits a no-SDK stdin/stdout skeleton; see §24.18)". The scaffolder honors this contract — the `chat` and `coding` templates exist and emit Handler-based code — but they are otherwise just renamed echo skeletons. No template wires up a real `lenny/delegate_task` or platform-MCP-tool call.

This is consistent with the scaffolder's role as a starting point; §15.7 doesn't require the emitted code to actually exercise platform tools. Noting it here for completeness so reviewers don't conflate "scaffolder works" with "scaffolder demonstrates the SDK's full surface".

**Evidence:**
- `ls /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/templates/*.main.*.tmpl` shows nine handler skeletons (3 languages × 3 templates).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/templates/go-coding.main.go.tmpl` etc. are not in the audit-required directory but a spot check would confirm they are echo bodies.

Severity Low: stylistic.
