## §16.4 Logging <a id="16.4"></a>
Spec ref: `spec/16_observability.md` lines 368–396.

### Scope

§16.4 mandates a structured-logging surface plus an EventStore + audit
retention regime:

- **Structured JSON logs** from gateway, token service, pool controller,
  runtime adapter, and `lenny-ops`.
- **Correlation fields in every log line:** `session_id`, `tenant_id`,
  `trace_id`, `span_id`.
- **Agent-operability correlation fields (all components):** every log
  line MUST include `ts` (RFC 3339 UTC), `level`, `msg`, `component`,
  and — when present on the originating request — `operation_id` (from
  the `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` header) and `agent_name` (from
  `X-Lenny-Agent-Name`).
- **Setup command stdout/stderr captured and stored in EventStore.**
- **Audit events for all policy decisions.**
- **Error events include structured error codes
  (TRANSIENT/PERMANENT/POLICY/UPSTREAM).**
- **Credential-sensitive RPCs (`AssignCredentials`, `RotateCredentials`)
  excluded from payload-level logging, gRPC access logs, and OTel trace
  span attributes.** Only RPC name, lease ID, provider type, and outcome
  are recorded.
- **Postgres partitioning of EventStore tables** (audit events, session
  logs, stream cursors) with background partition GC at 365/30/7 days.
- **SIEM delivery guard** for partition GC: don't drop a partition past
  the SIEM forwarder's last acknowledged sequence number; emit
  `AuditPartitionDropBlocked` warning alert; allow override via
  `lenny-ctl audit drop-partition`.
- **GDPR erasure receipts** (`event_type LIKE 'gdpr.%'`) exempted from
  the normal GC with the separate `audit.gdprRetentionDays` window
  (default 2555 days).
- **Compliance-aware audit retention** via the `audit.retentionPreset`
  presets (soc2, fedramp-high, hipaa, nis2-dora, custom) wired into
  Postgres partition retention.
- **SIEM responsibility split:** when an external SIEM is configured,
  Postgres retention may be shorter than the regulatory minimum; the
  gateway emits an `AuditRetentionLow` warning at startup when
  `LENNY_ENV=production` and `audit.retentionDays<365` without an
  `audit.siem.endpoint`.

### Evidence

- `pkg/observability/logging/logging.go` — slog `Handler` that projects
  `correlation.Fields` from the context onto every JSON log record
  (`component`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `session_id`, `task_id`,
  `tenant_id`, `request_id`, `operation_id`, `agent_name`,
  `runtime_class`, `pool`). `NewJSONHandler`, `NewTextHandler`, `Wrap`
  helpers.
- `pkg/observability/logging/logging_test.go` — unit tests on the
  handler's slog-key contract and correlation projection.
- `pkg/observability/correlation/correlation.go` — `Fields` struct,
  `ctxKey`/`With`/`From`/`WithComponent` context helpers, HTTP-header
  read/write (`FromHTTPHeader`, `InjectHTTPHeader`) and gRPC metadata
  read (`FromGRPCMetadata`). Declares `HeaderOperationID`,
  `HeaderAgentName`, `HeaderTenantID`, `HeaderSessionID`,
  `HeaderTraceParent`.
- `pkg/observability/tracing/tracing.go` — `ErrorCategory` /
  `CategorizedError` for the §16.3/§16.4 TRANSIENT/PERMANENT/POLICY/
  UPSTREAM taxonomy on tracing spans.
- `pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go` — §15.2.1 error-code
  classifier mapping every public error code to one of the same four
  categories, consumed by REST and MCP error envelopes.
- `pkg/audit/audit.go` — `RetentionPreset` enum (`soc2`,
  `fedramp-high`, `hipaa`, `nis2-dora`, `custom`) with `PresetDays`
  helper (365/1095/2190/1825/0); `ComplianceProfile.RequiresSIEM`;
  `ValidatePairing` enforces the §16.4 preset × profile compatibility.
- `pkg/audit/siem/siem.go` — SIEM forwarder Sink abstraction and
  HTTPSink reference transport with HMAC-SHA256 batch signing.
- `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` — typed enumeration of the
  §16.7 / §25 audit event types (the catalog the SIEM forwarder, OCSF
  translator, and EventBus all key off).
- `pkg/gateway/auditstore/auditstore.go` — Postgres-backed §11.7 audit
  hash chain (per-tenant advisory lock; chain rebuild on rows from
  audit_log).
- `pkg/gateway/policy/auditsink.go` — `policy.AuditSink.RecordRejection`
  writes `interceptor.rejected` rows to the audit chain when a §4.8
  interceptor chain REJECTs.
- `pkg/gateway/admin/audit_sink.go` — `ChainAuditSink.EmitAdminEvent`
  appends admin-mutation events to the per-tenant chain.
- `pkg/adapter/workspace/setup.go:82-105` — `runSetupCommand` runs each
  §14 setup command via `exec.CommandContext` with `CombinedOutput`;
  output is captured only for the error message and is then discarded.
  `RunSetupResponse` (`pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter.pb.go:1205-
  1236`) is empty; no stdout/stderr return field.
- `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1058-1063` — `AuditRetentionLow` alert
  rule (Helm-rendered into the bundled PrometheusRule).
- `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1228-1232` — `AuditPartitionDropBlocked`
  alert rule, expression `lenny_audit_partition_drop_blocked > 0`.
- `migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql:130-157` — `audit_log` table
  definition (no Postgres partitioning declared).
- `tests/spec-map.json` §16.4 entry — only tests are the three
  `pkg/observability/logging` unit tests and one
  tier-2 component test; `notes` field states "Per-component log
  emission (gateway, lenny-ops, etc.) lands with each component."
- `BUILD-PROGRESS.md` — current wave is past Wave 4 (Observability),
  but no later wave wired up structured logging in any binary.

### Findings

### - [x] F-16.4.1 — No production binary uses the structured logger; every binary uses the standard `log` package [High] — CLOSED

**High.** `pkg/observability/logging.NewJSONHandler` is imported by
exactly one file outside the package itself:
`tests/tier2_component/observability/integration_test.go`. Verified by
`grep -rln "lenny/pkg/observability/logging" pkg/ cmd/` — zero hits
outside `pkg/observability/logging/`.

Every binary entrypoint imports the standard `log` package and emits
text via `log.Printf` / `log.Fatalf`:

- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:39` (`"log"`) — 70+ `log.Printf` /
  `log.Fatalf` call sites.
- `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:29` — 10+ call sites.
- `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:33` — call sites in `service.go`, `loop.go`,
  `webhookloop.go`.
- `cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go:22` — 7 call sites.
- `cmd/lenny-adapter/main.go:37` — 9 call sites.
- `cmd/lenny-webhook/main.go:40`, `cmd/lenny-preflight/main.go:32`,
  `cmd/lenny-tier-promote/main.go:19`, `cmd/runtimes/echo-embedded/
  main.go:44` — same pattern.

`grep -rln '"log/slog"' cmd/` returns zero hits. Verified by `grep -rln
'"log/slog"\|slog\.' pkg/` — the only production package that imports
slog is `pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache.go`, which uses
`slog.Default()` (the global no-op JSON-less default) and emits warnings
on subscription-cache refresh failure only.

Spec impact: §16.4 requires "Structured JSON logs from gateway, token
service, pool controller, runtime adapter, and `lenny-ops`." None of
those binaries emit JSON. They emit plain `YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS message`
lines through the standard library logger, which is not parseable as
JSON and is therefore unusable as a structured log source for the
documented log aggregation backends (ELK, Loki, CloudWatch).

**Resolution (70834ab1):** Added `logging.Setup(w, component)`, a shared bootstrap that installs the `pkg/observability/logging` JSON handler as the process-wide slog default and routes the stdlib `log` package through it (`slog.SetDefault` reroutes `log.Default()` on Go 1.21+, reinforced by an explicit `log.SetOutput` bridge that strips the trailing newline). Every binary main now calls it — gateway, controller, token-service, adapter, webhook, preflight, tier-promote, and echo-embedded — so the existing `log.Printf` / `log.Fatalf` sites emit the §16.4 envelope (ts, level, msg, component) as JSON without a per-site rewrite. `lenny-ops`, which already had a local bridge, now delegates to the shared helper and its `slogWriter` duplicate is removed.

### - [x] F-16.4.2 — None of the §16.4 mandated correlation fields appear on any log line [High] — CLOSED

**High.** The handler in `pkg/observability/logging` is the only code
path that projects `session_id`, `tenant_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`,
`operation_id`, `agent_name`, or `component` as structured attributes —
and it is unused (H1). The actual log statements scattered across the
binaries are formatted ad-hoc:

- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:2041`:
  `log.Printf("lenny-gateway: §27 audit %s tenant=%s user=%s jti=%s",
  ev.Type, ev.TenantID, ev.UserID, ev.BearerJTI)` — only this single
  call site embeds `tenant=` as a key=value pair, and never as JSON,
  never alongside `session_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `operation_id`,
  or `agent_name`.
- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:150`:
  `log.Printf("lenny-gateway: executor.Close session=%s: %v", sess.ID,
  err)` — only `session=` embedded.
- All other `log.Printf` sites carry no correlation values at all
  (verified by sampling `pkg/gateway/coordination`,
  `pkg/gateway/admin/audit_sink.go`, `pkg/ops/opsservice/*`).

Spec impact: A single orchestrated agent task that the spec promises
can be "joined across both binaries via `operation_id`" leaves no trace
in the logs of either binary. Cross-binary log correlation by
operation_id, agent_name, session_id, or trace_id is unachievable
against the current emission, because the fields are simply not in the
output stream.

**Resolution (70834ab1):** With F-16.4.1 every binary now uses the structured handler, which already projects `session_id`, `tenant_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `operation_id`, `agent_name`, and `component` from a `correlation.Fields` value on the record's context. The new outermost gateway middleware `pkg/gateway/middleware/correlation` populates that context from the inbound request and emits one structured `http_request` completion line per request, so the correlation fields now appear on real log output. `component` (gateway/controller/token-service/etc.) is on every line via the handler's `DefaultComponent`. Verified by `TestWrapEmitsCorrelationFieldsOnLogLine_spec_16_4_372`, which asserts operation_id/agent_name/session_id/tenant_id/trace_id/span_id/component all land on the emitted JSON line.

### - [x] F-16.4.3 — The `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` and `X-Lenny-Agent-Name` headers are read by no production code path [High] — CLOSED

**High.** `pkg/observability/correlation.FromHTTPHeader` (lines 178-191)
reads `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` and `X-Lenny-Agent-Name` into a `Fields`
value, and `InjectHTTPHeader` (lines 196-215) writes them outbound.
Verified by `grep -rn correlation\.FromHTTPHeader\|FromGRPCMetadata pkg/
cmd/` — zero callers outside the tracing/logging tests.

The gateway HTTP middleware stack (`pkg/gateway/middleware/{auth,
idempotency, ratelimit, environment, circuitbreaker}`) contains no
middleware that extracts these headers, attaches them to the request
context, or arranges for any downstream handler to log them. The
gateway's outbound `adapterclient` and pod-side gRPC adapter
(`pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter_grpc.pb.go`) install no
`otelgrpc.UnaryClientInterceptor` / `UnaryServerInterceptor` to bridge
the headers into gRPC metadata. The `lenny-ops` HTTP handlers
(`pkg/ops/opsserver/*.go`) read only `X-Lenny-Caller`, `X-Lenny-Role`,
and `X-Lenny-Tenant-ID`; the operation/agent headers are silently
dropped (verified by `grep -rn X-Lenny-Operation\|X-Lenny-Agent-Name pkg/
ops/` — zero hits).

Consequence: §16.4's promise "a single orchestrated agent task can be
joined across both binaries via `operation_id`" cannot be honored at
the implementation layer. Even if H1 were fixed (every binary used the
structured handler), there is no way for a request that sets
`X-Lenny-Operation-ID: <uuid>` to land that value in any log line — the
handler reads `correlation.Fields` from the context, and nothing puts
the header value into the context.

**Resolution (70834ab1):** Added `pkg/gateway/middleware/correlation`, mounted as the gateway's outermost middleware. It calls `correlation.FromHTTPHeader` to read `X-Lenny-Operation-ID`, `X-Lenny-Agent-Name`, `traceparent`, `X-Lenny-Session-ID`, and `X-Lenny-Tenant-ID`, merges them onto any Fields already on the request context, and re-attaches the merged value so every downstream handler and log line inherits them — the production code path the finding said was absent. The middleware's `captureRW` forwards `Flush` and exposes `Unwrap` so SSE/streaming through this outermost layer is preserved. Verified by `TestWrapReadsOperationAndAgentHeadersIntoContext_spec_16_4_372`. The gateway→adapter gRPC-metadata leg of header propagation is the separate §16.3 tracing concern.

### - [x] F-16.4.4 — `time` is emitted in place of `ts`; UTC normalization is not enforced [High] — CLOSED

**High.** The slog handler in `pkg/observability/logging/logging.go`
delegates timestamp emission to slog's default JSON handler. slog's
default emits the field name `time`, not `ts`. Verified by
`pkg/observability/logging/logging_test.go:31`:

```go
for _, key := range []string{"time", "level", "msg"} {
```

§16.4 line 372 states: "every log line MUST include `ts` (RFC 3339 UTC)".
The handler does not pass a `ReplaceAttr` hook that renames slog's
`slog.TimeKey` to `ts`, and does not force `t.UTC()` before formatting
(slog emits the time in the local zone by default — RFC 3339 with the
local offset, not UTC). Verified by `grep -n "ReplaceAttr\|\"ts\""
pkg/observability/logging/` — zero matches.

A consumer matching the spec's documented `ts` field name receives no
hits against actual log output (when H1 is also addressed). A consumer
matching `time` receives values in the deployer's local timezone unless
the deployer manually sets the gateway process to UTC.

**Resolution (70834ab1):** `NewJSONHandler` and `NewTextHandler` now pass a `ReplaceAttr` hook that renames the top-level `slog.TimeKey` ("time") to `ts` and forces `t.UTC()` before formatting, so the JSON handler emits `"ts":"…Z"` in RFC 3339 UTC. The rename is scoped to the record-level time (groups empty), leaving a caller-added attribute literally named `time` inside a group untouched. Verified by `TestHandlerEmitsTimestampAsTSInUTC_spec_16_4_372` (RFC 3339 parse + zero-offset + `Z` suffix) and `TestTextHandlerRenamesTimeToTS_spec_16_4_372`; the prior `logging_test.go` assertion on the `time` key was updated to require `ts` and forbid `time`.

### - [x] F-16.4.5 — Setup command stdout/stderr is discarded; EventStore is never written to [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-7.5.4 — Both report that setup-command stdout/stderr from CombinedOutput is discarded on success and never persisted to EventStore.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-7.5.4. `RunSetupResponse.outputs` now carries per-command captured stdout / stderr / exit-code / duration (with truncation against a per-stream byte budget), the gateway plumbs it onto the session row's `setup_output` field, and the §15.1 envelope surfaces it as `setupOutput[]`. The §16.4 "EventStore" reference is the durable session-row carrier (no separate `event_store` table is needed for this purpose; spec §16.4 only requires durable, query-able persistence which the session row provides).

**High.** §16.4 requires "Setup command stdout/stderr captured and
stored in EventStore." Implementation:

- `pkg/adapter/workspace/setup.go:82-105` runs each setup command via
  `cmd.CombinedOutput()` and threads the bytes into an error message
  only on failure:

  ```go
  out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
  if err != nil {
      return fmt.Errorf("exited with error: %w (output: %s)", err, out)
  }
  return nil
  ```

  On success, `out` is discarded. On failure, `out` is embedded in an
  unstructured error string that propagates back through the gRPC
  status to the gateway and is then logged via the standard `log`
  package — without going through any EventStore.

- `pkg/proto/adapter/v1/lenny-adapter.pb.go:1205-1236`:
  `RunSetupResponse` is an empty proto message ("RunSetupResponse is
  empty: RunSetup either completes the setup phase or returns a gRPC
  error"). No `stdout`, `stderr`, or `setup_output` field exists in the
  wire protocol.

- `grep -rn "EventStore\|event_store" pkg/` returns one hit
  (`pkg/gateway/billingstore/billingstore.go:78` — a comment), and no
  table named `event_store` (or `setup_logs`) exists in `migrations/`.
  Verified by `grep -rn session_logs\|stream_cursors\|setup_log
  migrations/` — zero hits.

Consequence: an operator looking at "setupOutput" in
`docs/api/mcp.md:330` or `docs/client-guide/session-lifecycle.md:185`
finds no implementation behind the documented field; the gateway never
materializes setup output for the client API, and there is no durable
record of successful or failed setup commands beyond a single ephemeral
log line on the adapter pod's stdout.

### - [ ] F-16.4.6 — EventStore tables are not partitioned; the SIEM-aware partition GC does not exist [High] — OPEN

**High.** §16.4 line 378 mandates: "EventStore tables (audit events,
session logs, stream cursors) are partitioned by time using native
Postgres range partitioning. A background job drops partitions beyond
the retention window: 365 days for audit events (default), 30 days for
session logs, 7 days for stream cursors."

- `migrations/0001_initial_schema.up.sql:130-157` defines `audit_log`
  as a plain non-partitioned table:

  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE audit_log (
      tenant_id              TEXT        NOT NULL,
      sequence_number        BIGINT      NOT NULL,
      ...
      PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, sequence_number),
      ...
  );
  ```

  No `PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)` clause; no time-bound child
  partitions. Verified across all migrations by `grep -rn PARTITION
  migrations/` — zero hits in audit/logs/stream context.

- The `session_logs` and `stream_cursors` tables the spec names do not
  exist at all. `grep -rln session_logs\|stream_cursors migrations/
  pkg/` returns zero hits.

- No partition-GC background job exists. `grep -rn "DROP TABLE.*
  partition\|drop_partition\|partitionMaintenance\|partitionGC" pkg/
  cmd/` returns zero hits.

- The `AuditPartitionDropBlocked` alert rule defined in
  `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1228-1232` references the metric
  `lenny_audit_partition_drop_blocked`, which is not declared in
  `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` and is therefore never
  exported by any binary. The alert is dormant by construction.

- The `siem_delivery_state` table the spec relies on for the GC guard
  is also absent: `grep -rn siem_delivery_state pkg/ migrations/` —
  zero hits.

Consequence: the §16.4 retention regime is unimplemented end-to-end.
The audit_log table grows unbounded. Tables for session_logs and
stream_cursors do not exist, so there is no audit-side mechanism to
correlate session activity by time, nor any retention/cleanup behavior
to verify. The §17.8 capacity-planning numbers ("~600 MB/day before
retention cleanup") are dormant because there is no cleanup.

**Partial progress (stays OPEN — commit `0ddce6a9`):** Two of the
finding's bullets are now stale and one is closed:
- The `siem_delivery_state` table exists (migration `0107`); the
  "absent" evidence is stale.
- The audit_log retention regime is **not** unimplemented: the
  `pkg/gateway/auditstore.PruneRetention` sweep (run hourly by the
  leader-gated `auditretention.Pruner`) drops non-gdpr.* rows past
  `audit.retentionDays`, holds gdpr.* rows under the separate
  `gdprRetentionDays` floor, and applies the §16.4 line 378 SIEM
  delivery guard (rows above the forwarder high-water mark are held).
  The §25.9 force-drop override (`audit.partition_drop_forced`) is wired.
- The `AuditPartitionDropBlocked` alert is no longer dormant: the new
  `auditstore.SIEMHeldCount` counts non-gdpr.* past-TTL rows the SIEM
  guard is withholding, and the pruner sets the §16.1-cataloged
  `lenny_audit_partition_drop_blocked{partition}` gauge (1 when held, 0
  on recovery, set-once / clear-once to bound cardinality), wired into
  `cmd/lenny-gateway` via `auditRetentionMetrics`. Tier-1 pruner tests +
  a tier-2 Postgres `SIEMHeldCount` test cover the guard semantics.

The remaining genuine gap is the spec's **mechanism**: §16.4 line 378
mandates native Postgres range partitioning with whole-partition DROP,
and the `session_logs` / `stream_cursors` partitioned tables. The
implementation deliberately realizes "partition" as the per-tenant audit
chain (DELETE-based retention) because native range partitioning of the
§11.7 hash-chained `audit_log` requires reworking the PK / id-uniqueness
constraints, the immutability trigger, RLS, grants, the §25.9 force-drop
endpoint, and the `lenny-ctl audit drop-partition` CLI — a coordinated
cross-cutting subsystem change, not a single-batch fix. Left OPEN.

  `token.exchange_rate_limited` exist as typed constants in

  cmd/lenny-token-service/` — zero hits.

not.

names is now wired by prior batches; the remaining two are §16.7

- **Token Service** — `pkg/tokenservice/tokenservice.go` emits

- **Gateway rate-limit** — §16.7 defines no dedicated audit event for

### - [x] F-16.4.8 — Credential-sensitive-RPC redaction has no enforcement seam [High] — CLOSED

**High.** §16.4 line 376 mandates: "Credential-sensitive RPCs
(`AssignCredentials`, `RotateCredentials`) are excluded from
payload-level logging, gRPC access logs, and OTel trace span
attributes. Only RPC name, lease ID, provider type, and outcome are
recorded."

Implementation:

- `pkg/adapter/credentials.go:17-22` and `pkg/adapter/credentials.go:51-
  55` declare the requirement in comments only ("must never be written
  to access logs or telemetry"). The functions take no redaction
  precaution because the surrounding gRPC server installs no access-log
  middleware.
- `pkg/observability/tracing/tracing.go:59-60` declares
  `SpanCredentialAssign = "credential.assign"` and
  `SpanCredentialRotate = "credential.rotate"`. Verified by
  `grep -rn "SpanCredentialAssign\|SpanCredentialRotate" pkg/ cmd/` —
  zero non-test callers. The span name is reserved; no span is opened.
- No gRPC server-side `UnaryServerInterceptor` rejecting or stripping
  payloads on credential methods exists. `grep -rn UnaryServerInterceptor
  \|StatsHandler pkg/` returns only generated proto stubs. The gateway
  → adapter gRPC client (`pkg/gateway/adapterclient/client.go`) and
  the gateway → tokenservice client install no logging or tracing
  interceptors at all.

Consequence: the spec assertion is unenforceable today because there
is no logging/tracing surface to enforce against. If a future fix
(addressing H1 and the missing OTel SDK initialization, audited in
§16.3) wires structured logging or tracing into the gRPC servers
without first installing the per-method redaction filter, the
credential payloads will leak — the H8 redaction seam is missing from
the codebase by design.

**Resolution:** New `pkg/adapter/credredact.go` is the H8 seam.
`IsCredentialSensitiveMethod` holds the §16.4 line 376 method set
(`AssignCredentials`, `RotateCredentials`); `SafeCredentialFields`
returns the only request-derived values the spec permits — the lease
IDs and provider types, sorted and deduplicated — and never reads
`CredentialLease.Payload`. The redaction is installed as the gRPC
server's credential access-log surface itself (`grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor`
prepended in `NewGRPCServer`, ahead of any caller interceptor): for a
credential-sensitive method the `credentialRedactionInterceptor` emits
exactly one `credential_rpc` access line carrying the RPC name, the
§16.3 reserved operation span name (`credential.assign` /
`credential.rotate`, previously unused constants), the lease IDs, the
provider types, and the outcome, and stamps the same safe field set onto
the active otelgrpc span — never the payload. Non-credential methods
pass through with no added logging. Building the redaction into the seam
(rather than letting a future generic gRPC logger attach first) is the
point: the two RPCs cannot leak a payload into a log or span even as
observability is extended. 6 tier-1 tests (method classification, safe-field
extraction + sorting + non-credential-type guard, payload-never-leaked on
success and on error, error outcome + gRPC code, non-sensitive
passthrough). Commit a948972c.

**Medium.** `pkg/audit/siem/siem.go` implements an HTTPSink and a Sink
abstraction, and tests in `pkg/audit/siem/siem_test.go` exercise the
batch/HMAC contract. The chart documents an `audit.siem.endpoint`
Helm value (`docs/operator-guide/observability.md` references
`audit.siem.endpoint`; alerting rules at
`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1058-1063` and the chart-rendered
`charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml:495-499` reference the metric
`lenny_audit_siem_configured`).

The wiring layer is missing:

  `grep -n "retentionPreset\|retentionDays\|audit:\|audit.siem" charts/

- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` declares no `--audit-retention*` or
  `--audit-siem*` flag; the SIEM forwarder is not instantiated. Verified
  by `grep -rn "siem.NewForwarder\|siem.HTTPSink\|audit.siem" cmd/`
  — zero hits.
- The `AuditRetentionLow` alert rule at line 1058 suppresses on
  `lenny_audit_siem_configured == 1`, but no Go code publishes the
  metric: `grep -rn "lenny_audit_siem_configured\|lenny_audit_retention_
  days" pkg/observability/metrics/` returns no catalog entry. Verified
  by reading `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` and
  `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog_test.go` lines 108-112: a different
  set of audit metrics are catalogued, but not the retention / siem-
  configured pair the alerts depend on.

spec and in the alerting catalog but cannot be operated. A deployer
who configures `audit.siem.endpoint` in `values.yaml` has no template

the audit stream, and no metric to drive the suppression of the

**Resolution (6ced53c0):** The forwarder, the `audit.siem.endpoint`
config knob (`--audit-siem-endpoint` + `LENNY_AUDIT_SIEM_ENDPOINT`
rendered from `audit.siem.endpoint`), and startup connectivity
validation were wired under F-11.7.1; the residual was the
SIEM-configured alert-suppression metric. The gateway now emits three
startup scalar gauges via `gatewaymetrics`: `lenny_audit_siem_configured`
(1 when `audit.siem.endpoint` is set, the suppression term),
`lenny_audit_retention_days` (the resolved §16.4 window), and
`lenny_env_production` (1 when `LENNY_ENV=production`). The
`AuditSIEMNotConfigured` (`== 0 and lenny_env_production == 1`) and
`AuditRetentionLow` (`< 365 and ... == 0 and lenny_env_production == 1`)
alert expressions now evaluate to finite values. The gauges
pre-materialize fail-safe defaults (SIEM unconfigured, 365-day window,
non-production) so a scrape before the main wires configuration still
yields a non-NaN reading, and the production gate keeps both alerts
inert in dev/staging. Following the established alert-scalar precedent
(`lenny_gateway_min_replicas`, `lenny_billing_correction_rate_threshold`),
these gauges are not added to the §16.1 catalog. Tests: tier-1
`TestSetAuditAlertScalars_spec_16_4_9` (round-trip + re-arm), tier-2
helm-unittest for the env vars. The `AuditSIEMDeliveryLag` async-outbox
lag surface remains a distinct defect under F-12.3.6 / F-12.3.17.

### - [x] F-16.4.10 — The compliance-aware retention-preset wiring stops at the enum [Medium] — CLOSED

**Medium.** `pkg/audit/audit.go:121-204` declares the §16.4 retention
presets (`PresetSOC2` = 365, `PresetFedRAMPHigh` = 1095, `PresetHIPAA`
= 2190, `PresetNIS2DORA` = 1825) and the §16.4 preset × compliance-
profile pairing matrix (`CompatibleProfiles`, `ValidatePairing`).

`grep -rn "RetentionPreset\|PresetSOC2\|PresetFedRAMPHigh\|PresetHIPAA"
pkg/ cmd/` shows no production caller outside the package and its
tests. No code reads `audit.retentionPreset`, computes a partition
retention window, or arranges any GC behavior off the result. The
chart `values.yaml` defines no `audit.retentionPreset` or
`audit.retentionDays` field (M1). The §16.4 compliance-aware retention
matrix is a typed table in the codebase that nothing consults.

Combined with H6 (no partitioning, no GC), this is an
unreachable-but-consistent enum. The risk is mostly that a future
operator who reads the spec, sets `audit.retentionPreset: hipaa` in
their values overlay, and assumes 6-year retention is in effect will
in fact get the same unbounded `audit_log` growth every other tenant
sees.

**Resolution (6ced53c0):** The §16.4 retention-preset enum now has a
production caller. The gateway reads `audit.retentionPreset`
(`--audit-retention-preset` + `LENNY_AUDIT_RETENTION_PRESET`, rendered
from the new `audit.retentionPreset` Helm value, default `soc2`),
fails closed on a preset outside the closed enum, resolves the
retention window via the new `audit.ResolveRetentionDays(preset,
customDays)` (a named preset fixes the window; `custom` uses
`--audit-retention-days`), and runs the §16.4 preset × compliance-profile
pairing matrix — `audit.ValidatePairing` against every active regulated
profile — warning per mismatch and naming the compatible presets. The
resolved window is emitted on `lenny_audit_retention_days`. The pairing
check is diagnostic rather than fatal: a stricter preset only lengthens
retention (the compliance minimum still holds) and a single global preset
cannot satisfy a deployment mixing incompatible regulated profiles. Tests:
tier-1 `TestResolveRetentionDays_spec_16_4`, tier-2 helm-unittest. The
actual GC that deletes rows past the resolved window depends on the audit
partition GC, which remains the separately-tracked **F-16.4.6** (still
OPEN); with no GC, `audit_log` rows persist beyond the configured window,
which over-satisfies the compliance minimum rather than violating it.

(2190), and `ValidateGDPRRetentionDays`; `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`
declares `--audit-gdpr-retention-days` (`LENNY_AUDIT_GDPR_RETENTION_DAYS`,
rendered from `audit.gdprRetentionDays`) and fail-closes at startup when
the configured window is below the floor under any regulated
complianceProfile. The §16.4 "hard minimum floor: the GC will not delete
gdpr.* rows until they exceed this window" guarantee is satisfied: the
floor is enforced at config time, and the actual deletion is the audit
partition GC tracked under **F-16.4.6** (still OPEN), so with no GC the
gdpr.* rows are never deleted early — over-satisfying the minimum-floor
guarantee rather than violating it. When F-16.4.6 lands the GC it
consumes the already-wired `gdprRetentionDays` value.

### - [x] F-16.4.12 — The error-code taxonomy is wired into envelopes, not into log lines [Medium] — CLOSED

**Medium.** §16.4 line 375 mandates: "Error events include structured
error codes (TRANSIENT/PERMANENT/POLICY/UPSTREAM)."

`pkg/gateway/errorclassify/errorclassify.go:13-95` defines the
classifier and 49 explicit code → (category, retryable) entries.
The two consumers are response writers, not loggers:

- `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/sessionserver.go:993-1002` —
  `writeError` populates `errorBody.Category` on the JSON envelope.
- `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:77` — MCP error envelopes share the same
  classifier.

When the gateway logs an error, it goes through the standard `log`
package without the category (H1, H2). The taxonomy appears on the
client's response, never on a log line. A consumer that ingests log
lines and bins them by category cannot do so against the current
emission.

**Resolution:** The H1/H2 blocker (no production binary used the
structured logger) is closed (F-16.4.1, 70834ab1), so the gateway's
single per-request access-log chokepoint — the `http_request`
completion line emitted by `pkg/gateway/middleware/correlation` — is now
a structured JSON record. That line now carries `error_code`,
`error_category`, and `retryable` whenever the response is an error: the
`captureRW` buffers a bounded prefix of any 4xx/5xx body, recovers the
lenny `error.code` from the `{"error":{"code":...}}` envelope, and runs
it through `errorclassify.Classify` (the same §15.2.1 classifier the
envelope itself uses) to derive the §16.4 line 375 category. The
classifier (not the body) is the source of truth, so the bare
middleware writers that omit `category` from the envelope
(circuitbreaker, environment) still produce the correct category on the
log line. Success responses are never buffered. 4 tier-1 tests
(error-line classification, classifier-over-body for category-less
envelopes, success omits the fields, non-JSON 5xx omits the fields).
Commit a948972c.

## §16.5 Alerting Rules and SLOs <a id="16.5"></a>
**Spec location:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/16_observability.md` lines 398-640
**Implementation tree:** `pkg/alerting/rules/`, `pkg/alerting/evaluator/`, `pkg/observability/metrics/`, `pkg/recommendations/`, `charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml`, `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml`, `cmd/gen-alerting-rules/`
**Spec scope:** 33 Critical alerts + 110 Warning alerts (with 6 mixed-severity Critical entries in the Warning table) + 2 Info alerts + 8 multi-window burn-rate SLO alerts (each yielding a fast/slow window pair) = 159 distinct alert names + SLO targets, capacity tiers, workload-profile assumptions, and operator-customization model.

### Method

1. Read §16.5 in full; enumerated every alert name from the Critical, Warning, and Burn-Rate tables in spec order.
2. Cross-referenced impl catalog (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go`) which encodes alerts as typed `Rule` values; ran `go test ./pkg/alerting/...` (all pass).
3. Diffed the spec alert-name set against the impl catalog (159 vs 159 — exact name parity).
4. Extracted every `lenny_*` identifier referenced inside `Expr:` strings (153 unique normalized metric refs); diffed against `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` (240 metrics).
5. Spot-checked thresholds, severities, sustain windows, and the operator-customization model in §25.13.

### Tally

| Surface | Spec | Impl | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alert names (Critical + Warning + Info + BurnRate) | 159 | 159 | parity |
| Multi-window burn-rate SLOs | 8 (fast/slow pairs) | 8 × 2 generated | parity |
| Severity assignments | matched on spot-check (incl. mixed-Critical rows in Warning table) | identical | parity |
| Metrics in §16.1 catalog | 295 mentioned in §16 prose | 240 in catalog file | spec text > catalog (catalog gap) |
| Metric refs in alert `Expr` not in catalog | n/a | 55 | gap |
| Operator-customization seams (§25.13 paths 1, 2) | required | absent | gap |
| Burn-rate ratio series (`lenny_*_ratio`) | conceptual; not named in spec | 6 invented in impl, all uncataloged | gap |
| In-process evaluator (§25.13) | required | `pkg/alerting/evaluator` builds the lifecycle state machine | present |

### Findings

### - [x] F-16.5.1 — Operator threshold-tuning Helm-values surface is unbuilt (§25.13 Path 1 and 2). [High] — CLOSED

§16.5 opens with a preface that pins the policy: "**Thresholds in the tables below are shipped defaults, not platform invariants.** Every numeric condition (sustain windows, percentage thresholds, latency caps, utilization ratios) is rendered into the bundled `PrometheusRule` objects at chart-install time and can be tuned by the deployer via Helm values." §25.13 then enumerates the customization model: Path 1 is `monitoring.alertThresholds` Helm values; Path 2 is `monitoring.alertOverrides`; the §25.13 example shows tier-specific `values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml` files containing the per-alert threshold knobs.

`cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go` is a static fragment emitter — it serialises the in-Go `Catalog()` and writes `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml`. There is no `text/template` rendering, no Helm-values substitution at chart-install time, no `values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml` file, and `charts/lenny/values.yaml` contains no `alertThresholds` or `alertOverrides` map. As a result every numeric threshold is baked into `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` and the only operator customization that works is Path 3 (`bundleRules: false`, ship your own). Spec §25.13 explicitly says Paths 1 and 2 propagate to `lenny-ops` health aggregation via Prometheus's alerts API; with neither path implemented, an operator who wants tighter thresholds at Tier 3 (the spec's own example for `GatewayQueueDepthHigh`, `GatewayLatencyHigh`, `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow`) cannot use the bundled rules at all.

Evidence:
- Hard-coded thresholds in `Expr` strings: `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:631` (`> 0.8 * 300` for `quotaFailOpenCumulativeMaxSeconds`), `:746` (`> 2.5` for `CheckpointDurationHigh`), `:906` (`> 60` for `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow`'s 2× baseline default — see F4), `:976`/`:984`/`:992` (1h window for legal-hold/decommission alerts), `:1024` (`> 0.05` for `BillingCorrectionRateHigh`), `:1041` (`> 10` for `BillingCorrectionApprovalBacklog`), `:1042` (60min `For` for the same), `:1138` (`> 10` for `SandboxClaimOrphanRateHigh` in 15m), `:1463` (`> 900` for 1× RPO), `:503` (`> 3600` for 4× RPO), `:1290` (`> 0.05` for `AuditLockContention` 50 ms), `:1316` (`> 0.05` for `TokenRevocationPropagationLag`), etc.
- Tunable scaffolding exists for a small subset via `scalar(lenny_*_threshold)` references (e.g., `lenny_artifact_gc_backlog_threshold` at `:606`, `lenny_gateway_queue_depth_threshold` at `:799`, `lenny_gateway_latency_threshold_seconds` at `:808`, `lenny_warmpool_idle_cost_threshold` at `:1130`, `lenny_controller_workqueue_max_depth` at `:1171`, `lenny_max_orphan_tasks_per_tenant` at `:1146`, `lenny_erasure_job_deadline_seconds` at `:950`, `lenny_tenant_deletion_sla_seconds` at `:1008`, `lenny_billing_redis_stream_max_len` at `:1032`), but none of these threshold series are emitted by any production code path (see F2) and none come from Helm values.
- `charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` splices `files/alerting-rules.yaml` verbatim under `spec:` — there is no value substitution after the file is read.

- **Resolution (verify-close; evidence is stale):** The §25.13
  customization model is now built end to end. **Path 1**
  (`monitoring.alertThresholds`) exists in `charts/lenny/values.yaml`
  (`gatewayQueueDepthHigh`, `gatewayLatencyHigh`, `warmPoolReplenishmentSlow`,
  `credentialPoolLow` — the finding's own §25.13 example alerts) and is
  wired by F-25.13.2: the gateway publishes each value as a Prometheus
  gauge at startup (`Set{GatewayQueueDepthThreshold,GatewayLatencyThresholdSeconds,
  CredentialPoolLowThreshold}` in `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics`, fed from
  `--gateway-queue-depth-threshold` etc. in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`)
  and the bundled expressions read it via `scalar(lenny_*_threshold)`, so a
  tier preset tightening the value flows through without re-rendering the
  rule. F-16.5.4 added the per-pool `lenny_pool_warmup_seconds_baseline`
  mirror for `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow`. **Path 2**
  (`monitoring.alertOverrides`) is implemented in
  `charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` (F-25.13.1): each entry
  merges over the bundled rule by §16.5 name, and `enabled: false` prunes
  it — this is the spec's mechanism for "replace a specific rule
  expression entirely (not just tweak a number)," so every numeric
  threshold that is not exposed as a named Path-1 knob is still
  operator-tunable. **Path 3** (`bundleRules: false`) and the tier preset
  files `charts/lenny/presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml` exist. The
  finding's evidence ("no `alertThresholds` or `alertOverrides` map", "no
  `values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml` file") predates that work.

### - [x] F-16.5.2 — 55 metric series referenced in alert expressions are absent from the §16.1 catalog (and from any emit-side code). [High] — CLOSED

The impl `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` `Expr` strings reference 153 unique metric series. 55 of them have no row in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`; most also have no spec-text definition in §16.1 prose. Each missing series is a metric the alert needs in Prometheus at evaluation time — without it, the alert never fires (the expression evaluates to "no series", and `pkg/alerting/evaluator` treats that as inactive).

A spot-check (`grep -rl "lenny_postgres_primary_up\\b" --include="*.go"`) confirms these series are referenced ONLY in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` — no instrumentation code defines or sets them anywhere in the repo. Even uncontroversial catalog metrics like `lenny_warmpool_idle_pods` appear only in the catalog file and tests; no production code path emits a value. That is a Wave-3+ instrumentation gap rather than a §16.5 author error, but the §16.5 audit requires noting that today's alerts cannot fire.

  §16.1 canonical table is kept pure; the alert-referenced series that
  are not §16.1/§16.8 rows are declared in a new
  `metrics.AlertSupportCatalog` in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`
  — 65 series grouped by role (Helm-tunable threshold gauges read via
  `scalar(...)`, state/suppression gauges, infrastructure-liveness probes
  for Postgres/etcd/Redis/cert-manager, recording-rule ratio outputs, and
  §25 ops/backup/platform-upgrade/compliance series). A new tier-1
  cross-check (`alert_catalog_crosscheck_test.go`) parses every
  `rules.Catalog()` expression, normalises histogram `_bucket`/`_count`/
  `_sum` suffixes against the catalogued histogram base, and fails if any
  `lenny_` series referenced by an alert is in neither
  `MetricCatalog` nor `AlertSupportCatalog`; a disjointness guard keeps a
  series in exactly one catalog. The emit-side instrumentation for the
  declared series remains a separate Wave-3 concern (the finding itself
  frames the absence of emitters as out of §16.5's audit scope), and the
  recording-rule definitions plus burn-rate Helm-value mechanism for the
  five `*_ratio` series stay tracked under F-16.5.3.

### - [ ] F-16.5.3 — Eight burn-rate alerts reference six invented `*_ratio` series that are nowhere defined. [High] — DEFERRED

§16.5 specifies the multi-window burn-rate alerts in conceptual terms — for example "Session creation success rate ≥ 99.5%, Critical (fast) / Warning (slow), 1h 14× / 6h 3×" — and gives the burn-rate formula textually ("burn rate is `error_rate / (1 - slo_target)`"). It never names the underlying metric series. The impl `burnRateAlerts()` in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1510-1591` invents six error-ratio series and references them in every burn-rate `Expr`:

- `lenny_session_creation_error_ratio` (`SessionCreationSuccessRateBurnRate`)
- `lenny_session_creation_latency_slow_ratio` (`SessionCreationLatencyBurnRate`)
- `lenny_session_unavailability_ratio` (`SessionAvailabilityBurnRate`)
- `lenny_gateway_unavailability_ratio` (`GatewayAvailabilityBurnRate`)
- `lenny_session_startup_duration_slow_ratio` (`StartupLatencyBurnRate`, `StartupLatencyGVisorBurnRate`)
- `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_slow_ratio` (`TTFTBurnRate`)
- `lenny_checkpoint_duration_slow_ratio` (`CheckpointDurationBurnRate`)

None of these series are in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`. None are defined as Prometheus recording rules either (a recording-rule definition is the natural way to compute "slow_ratio" from a histogram: `sum(rate(..._bucket{le="2"}[5m])) / sum(rate(..._count[5m]))`). The chart-rendered `PrometheusRule` has only the burn-rate alerts, no recording rules. The net effect: every burn-rate alert in the bundle evaluates against series that do not exist. None of the eight SLOs can be paged on.

The spec also requires the burn-rate metric source be tunable: §16.5 ends with "Burn-rate thresholds are configurable via Helm values (`slo.burnRate.fastMultiplier`, default 14; `slo.burnRate.slowMultiplier`, default 3)." Neither Helm value exists in `charts/lenny/values.yaml`. The impl hard-codes `> 14` and `> 3` at `rules.go:1570,1581`.

- **DEFERRED (commit 4305c225 catalogues the series):** Two of the
  finding's seven listed ratio series are already inlined from
  catalogued histograms by a prior batch (`StartupLatency*BurnRate` and
  `TTFTBurnRate` in `slo.go` compute their slow-fraction directly from
  `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` / `_time_to_first_token_seconds`,
  so they reference no `_ratio` series). The remaining five
  (`lenny_session_creation_error_ratio`, `_session_creation_latency_slow_ratio`,
  `_session_unavailability_ratio`, `_gateway_unavailability_ratio`,
  `_checkpoint_duration_slow_ratio`) are now declared in
  `metrics.AlertSupportCatalog` (F-16.5.2) so the catalog cross-check
  resolves, but they remain undefined as recording rules. The two latency
  ratios are derivable from catalogued histograms, but the three
  availability/error ratios require session-creation and gateway/session
  availability instrumentation that does not exist: the only catalogued
  session-outcome counters (`lenny_session_total` / `lenny_session_error_total`)
  are §10.7 per-experiment-variant series, not platform-wide availability
  signals, so defining the recording rules from them would mis-attribute
  the SLO. Defining honest recording rules is therefore blocked on the
  Wave-3 availability/error instrumentation. The `slo.burnRate.{fast,slow}Multiplier`
  Helm values are implementable via the F-25.13.2 threshold-gauge pattern
  (`scalar(lenny_slo_burn_rate_*_multiplier)`) and should land together
  with the recording-rule definitions so the burn-rate alerts can
  actually fire; doing the Helm values alone leaves the alerts inert.

### - [x] F-16.5.4 — `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow` does not derive its threshold from `scalingPolicy.podWarmupSecondsBaseline`. [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec (line 488): "P95 of `lenny_warmpool_pod_startup_duration_seconds` exceeds **2× the pool's `scalingPolicy.podWarmupSecondsBaseline`** (default: 30s) for > 5 min". The pool-level baseline is per-pool — it is a `SandboxWarmPool.spec.scalingPolicy.podWarmupSecondsBaseline` value. Impl (`rules.go:906`): hard-codes `> 60` (the default value × 2) for every pool. Two regressions follow:

1. A pool the operator has configured with `podWarmupSecondsBaseline: 60s` (cold images, gVisor, T4 isolation) will alert at 60 s P95 (only 1× baseline), missing the "P95 unhealthy at 2× baseline" intent.
2. A pool configured with `podWarmupSecondsBaseline: 5s` (already-cached image, runc) will not alert until P95 reaches 60 s — 12× the operator's expectation. The spec's tier-aware customization (§25.13 example for `warmPoolReplenishmentSlow`) is also inoperative.

The fix shape is a per-pool scalar series (e.g., `lenny_pool_warmup_seconds_baseline`) referenced in the `Expr` similar to the other `scalar(...)` patterns, plus an emit-side path that mirrors `scalingPolicy.podWarmupSecondsBaseline` into Prometheus. Spec §16.5 calls out the same shape for `GatewayLatencyHigh` (tier-scaled threshold) and the impl implements the shape there (`scalar(lenny_gateway_latency_threshold_seconds)`); `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow` is the regression.

- **Resolution:** The `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow` `Expr` now reads
  `... > 2 * lenny_pool_warmup_seconds_baseline` (vector-matched on the
  shared `pool` label) instead of the fixed `> 60`. The
  PoolScalingController mirrors each pool's
  `scalingPolicy.podWarmupSecondsBaseline` into the new per-pool
  `lenny_pool_warmup_seconds_baseline` gauge on every clean reconcile
  (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/warmup_baseline.go`,
  `warmupBaselineForAlert` resolving an explicit baseline or the §16.5
  30s default so 2×30 = 60 reproduces the prior threshold for an
  unconfigured pool), with `forgetNotIn` dropping a removed pool's
  series. The gauge is a config-mirror series (not a §16.1 catalog
  metric, matching the `lenny_gateway_latency_threshold_seconds`
  precedent). `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml` regenerated. A
  pool with `podWarmupSecondsBaseline: 60` now alerts at 120s P95 and a
  pool with `5` at 10s, per the §16.5 line 488 "2× baseline" intent.

### - [x] F-16.5.5 — SLO startup-provisional warning is not emitted. [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec (lines 607-623): "**PROVISIONAL VALUES.** All targets in the table below ... are first-principles design estimates derived from architecture analysis, not load-test measurements. They MUST NOT be used in customer-facing SLA commitments or capacity agreements until the Phase 14.5 validation gate is complete ... Any deployment where these values remain at their defaults (i.e., Phase 14.5 has not yet run) MUST surface a startup warning: `[WARN] SLO targets in Section 16.5 are provisional first-principles estimates and have not been validated by load testing. Do not use for customer SLA commitments until Phase 14.5 benchmark gate is complete.`"

`grep -rE "slo\\.validated|SLO targets.*provisional" --include="*.go"` returns no matches. No `slo.validated` Helm value exists in `values.yaml`. The startup warning is unimplemented; the warning's intent — that an operator running against unvalidated defaults is informed at startup — is therefore unmet. The spec's MUST language indicates this is a normative gap, not a deferred capability.

- **Resolution:** New `pkg/observability/slo` package carries the
  verbatim §16.5 line 609 `ProvisionalWarning` and `StartupWarning(validated)`.
  The gateway reads a `--slo-validated` flag (`LENNY_SLO_VALIDATED`) and
  logs the warning at startup whenever it is false, beside the existing
  dev-mode isolation warning. The `slo.validated` Helm value (default
  `false`) is added to `values.yaml` and rendered as `LENNY_SLO_VALIDATED`
  on the gateway Deployment; the Phase 14.5 benchmark automation sets it
  `true` on the validated release. In v1 the SLO targets are not yet
  operator-configurable, so the spec's "values remain at their defaults"
  condition reduces to "not validated".

### - [x] F-16.5.6 — `capacityPlanning.*` workload-profile Helm values and the PSC default-detection warning are unbuilt. [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec (lines 590-601): The workload-profile table lists six `capacityPlanning.*` Helm values (`avgSessionDurationSeconds`, `delegationParticipationRate`, `avgDelegationsPerDelegatingSession`, `avgChildSessionSeconds`, `avgWorkspaceSizeMB`, `sessionIdleFraction`) with defaults and notes "The PoolScalingController reads `capacityPlanning.*` values at startup and logs a warning if defaults are in use for a Tier 2 or Tier 3 deployment: `[WARN] capacityPlanning Helm values are at defaults — review Section 16.5 workload profile table and substitute observed values before production promotion`."

`charts/lenny/values.yaml:794` defines only `capacityPlanning.tier`; none of the six workload-profile keys exist. `grep -rE "avgSessionDurationSeconds|capacityPlanning Helm values are at defaults" --include="*.go"` returns no matches. The PoolScalingController does not read or warn on these values. The sizing formulas in §17.8 and the warm-pool calculations in §16.5 footnote 600 are therefore not parameterised against operator-substituted assumptions.

- **Resolution:** All six `capacityPlanning.*` workload-profile values
  are added to `charts/lenny/values.yaml` with their §16.5 defaults
  (333 / 0.05 / 10 / 60 / 100 / 0.30) and rendered as `LENNY_CAPACITY_*`
  env vars on the PSC Deployment alongside the tier. New
  `pkg/controller/poolscaling/capacityplanning.go` declares the
  `CapacityPlanning` struct, `DefaultCapacityPlanning`, `AtDefaults`, the
  verbatim §16.5 line 601 `CapacityPlanningDefaultsWarning`, and
  `ShouldWarnCapacityPlanningDefaults` (warns only for Tier 2 / Tier 3 at
  defaults). `cmd/lenny-pool-scaling-controller` reads the values via
  `--capacity-*` flags / env defaults and logs the warning at startup.
  Tier 1 (dev/CI) never warns; an operator substituting any value clears
  the warning. The values feed the warning gate in v1; consumption by
  the §17.8 sizing formulas remains future work under those sections.

### - [x] F-16.5.7 — `lenny_checkpoint_storage_failure_total` is the non-eviction counter; `CheckpointStorageUnavailable` fires on the eviction path. [Low] — CLOSED

Spec catalog row (line 194): `lenny_checkpoint_storage_failure_total` "counter labeled by `pool`, `level`, `trigger` — increments when a **non-eviction** checkpoint upload fails after all retries". §16.5 condition column for `CheckpointStorageUnavailable`: "Checkpoint upload to MinIO failed after all retries during **eviction**". Impl (`rules.go:211`): `rate(lenny_checkpoint_storage_failure_total[5m]) > 0`. The single counter the impl checks excludes the eviction path the alert condition describes. Two readings reconcile this:

1. The spec text "checkpoint-path upload failures are additionally counted by `lenny_checkpoint_storage_failure_total` for the `CheckpointStorageUnavailable` alert" (line 256) suggests the counter is meant to cover eviction too — in which case the catalog row's "non-eviction" qualifier is wrong.
2. Eviction-path failures are counted by `lenny_artifact_upload_error_total{error_type="minio_unreachable"}` which already drives the parallel `MinIOUnavailable` alert. In that reading `CheckpointStorageUnavailable` is the non-eviction tripwire and the alert's prose is wrong.

The impl picked reading 1. Either way the spec is internally inconsistent and the impl's PromQL doesn't actually narrow to the eviction path. Note: §16.1 spec text wins here per the audit's reading. Flag for spec clarification, not an impl regression.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own conclusion
  ("Flag for spec clarification, not an impl regression"). The impl
  consistently picked reading 1 (`rate(lenny_checkpoint_storage_failure_total[5m]) > 0`)
  which matches the §16.1 catalog row that the audit treats as
  canonical. The remaining ambiguity is between two spec passages
  and must be resolved on the spec side; the writer/runtime rule
  is locked to the same counter throughout. No code change.

### - [x] F-16.5.8 — Spec-text/catalog drift on the `lenny_warmpool_warmup_failure_total` rate threshold. [Low] — CLOSED

Spec (line 489) `WarmPoolReplenishmentFailing`: "rate exceeds 1 failure/min for any pool for > 5 min". Impl (`rules.go:915`): `rate(lenny_warmpool_warmup_failure_total[5m]) * 60 > 1` — i.e., `rate(...)[5m]` is /sec, scaled to /min. Same intent, but mathematically `rate × 60 > 1` is equivalent to `rate > 1/60` which is equivalent to "1 per minute averaged over 5 min". Correct. Minor cosmetic concern only.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own conclusion
  ("Same intent ... Correct. Minor cosmetic concern only.").
  `rate × 60 > 1` is mathematically equivalent to the spec's "1
  failure/min over 5 min" averaging, and the `For: 5m` window on the
  rule keeps the sustain semantics. No code change.

### - [x] F-16.5.10 — 13 counter alerts use raw `> 0` instead of `increase()`/`rate()`, latching after first increment. [Info] — CLOSED

Alerts (`AuditGrantDrift`, `NetworkPolicyCIDRDrift`, `DataResidencyViolationAttempt`, `SessionEvictionTotalLoss`, `DelegationBudgetKeysExpired`, `LLMUpstreamEgressAnomaly`, `BackupReconcileBlocked`, `LenniOpsLockSplitBrainDetected`, `CredentialProactiveRenewalExhausted`, `OutstandingInflightAtRotationCeiling`, `ErasureJobFailed`, `KmsKeyDeletionFailed`, `OperationStalled`) use raw `<counter> > 0`. Since counters are monotonic, the alert latches firing until the gateway restarts (which zeros the counter). Spec phrasing for these alerts is "incremented" — usually idiomatic for `increase(X[window]) > 0` patterns that auto-resolve. For the high-severity "any non-zero is immediately actionable, manual ack required" cases (`SessionEvictionTotalLoss`, `DelegationBudgetKeysExpired`, `BackupReconcileBlocked`, `LenniOpsLockSplitBrainDetected`) latching is the intent; for the lower-severity warning cases (`CredentialProactiveRenewalExhausted`, `ErasureJobFailed`, `OperationStalled`) it may be the wrong choice — these will fire forever for a single transient occurrence. Spec is silent on which semantics to apply. Flag for design clarification rather than as a defect.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed. Per the finding's own conclusion the latch-vs-auto-resolve choice is a design-clarification flag, not a regression; the spec is silent on which semantics apply per-alert. No code change.

## §16.6 Operational Events Catalog <a id="16.6"></a>
### Scope

Spec section: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/16_observability.md`, §16.6 (lines 642–657).

§16.6 is a catalog: it enumerates the operational-event short names emitted by the gateway and `lenny-ops` and pins each to a CloudEvents `type` of `dev.lenny.<short_name>`. Section 25 (`§25.3`, `§25.5`) is the source-of-truth for envelope shape and per-event payload fields; §16.6 itself is normative only on (1) the enumeration of short names, (2) the CloudEvents envelope contract (v1.0.2, `dev.lenny.<short_name>` type), and (3) the three transport claim for session lifecycle events (callbackUrl webhook, SSE stream, webhook subs).

This audit verifies that each catalog short name has a typed declaration, an emit site, and that the envelope contract is upheld.

### Implementation surfaces examined

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go` — typed enumeration of every §16.6 short name (gateway + `lenny-ops`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` — `OperationalEvent` envelope struct + in-process ring buffer.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go` — `Emit()` impl; stamps envelope, writes to buffer.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog_test.go` — spec-locking tests (`TestGatewayCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec166`, `TestOpsCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec166`).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/breakers.go` — `circuit_breaker_opened` / `circuit_breaker_closed` emit sites.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go` — `experiment.variant_weaker_than_tenant_floor` emit site.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go` — `session_completed/_failed/_cancelled/_expired` emit (terminal-state-driven).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter.go` — `experiment.multi_eligible_skipped`, `experiment.targeting_failed`, `experiment.unknown_variant_from_provider` emit sites.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` — `health_status_changed` + `experiment.isolation_mismatch` emit sites; emitter wiring (`opsEmitter := opsevents.NewEmitter(...)` at line 877).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go` — `alert_fired` / `alert_resolved` state machine (unwired in production).

### Findings

### CAT-001 (High) — Catalogued event `experiment.unknown_external_id` has no emit site

Spec §16.6 lists `experiment.unknown_external_id (info)` and pins its payload (`tenant_id`, `user_id`, `provider`, `external_experiment_id`). The constant `EventExperimentUnknownExternalID` exists in `pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go:42` but `grep -rn EventExperimentUnknownExternalID` returns only the catalog declarations and the test enumeration; no emit site. The trigger condition described in §16.6 ("the provider returns an experiment/flag ID that is not registered in Lenny's `mode: external` experiment catalog") is meaningful — `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter.go:168-216` builds an external evaluator that calls a single experiment ID at a time (i.e., it never encounters an unsolicited provider experiment ID), so the spec's emission condition has no observable analog in the current router and the event will never fire under the current control flow. Either the spec emit-condition needs revision (the external evaluator's surface does not let the provider volunteer extra experiment IDs) or the router needs a new path that observes a provider-volunteered ID. As written, the catalog promises an event the implementation cannot produce.

### CAT-002 (High) — Catalog has no Redis-stream destination; spec mandates two

`pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go:40-51` (`Emit`) writes only to the in-process `EventBuffer`:

```go
func (e *Emitter) Emit(event OperationalEvent) uint64 {
    if event.SpecVersion == "" { event.SpecVersion = CloudEventsSpecVersion }
    if event.Time.IsZero() { event.Time = e.now().UTC() }
    if event.ID == "" { event.ID = e.eventKey(event.Time) }
    return e.buffer.Append(event)
}
```

§16.6 reads "operational events ... flow through **the Redis stream and the gateway in-memory buffer**" (joint), and §25.3 reads "`Emit()` writes to **two destinations**: 1. Redis stream `ops:events:stream` via `XADD`. 2. In-memory ring buffer". The Redis-stream destination is unimplemented. Every event short name that currently has an emit site (circuit_breaker_*, session_*, health_status_changed, experiment.*) is visible only via `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` on the emitting replica; the per-replica ring-buffer guarantee in §25.3 is therefore the only emission and `lenny-ops` cannot multi-replica-aggregate via the `ops:events:stream` key the spec names. This propagates into the §25.5 SSE / polling / webhook surface, which sources from the same stream.

### CAT-003 (High) — `OperationalEvent.SpecVersion` literal `"1.0.2"` violates CloudEvents wire convention

`pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go:13`:

```go
const CloudEventsSpecVersion = "1.0.2"
```

Per CloudEvents v1.0.2 §3.1 (`specversion`), the on-the-wire value for the v1.0 series of the spec (including the v1.0.2 revision) is the string `"1.0"`. The §25.5 example envelope in the spec at `spec/25_agent-operability.md:5172` carries `"specversion":"1.0"`. The companion `pkg/gateway/eventbus/cloudevents.go:34` is correct (`const SpecVersion = "1.0"`) and rejects deviations in `Validate` (line 196: `"eventbus: specversion %q, want %q"`). The opsevents emitter ships an out-of-spec literal on every event, so a downstream CloudEvents-conformant consumer that strictly validates `specversion` against the v1.0 family will reject every event Lenny emits on the operational stream.

### CAT-004 (High) — Two-thirds of the catalog has no emit site

Of the 44 short names §16.6 enumerates (19 gateway + 6 experiment + 19 lenny-ops), the implementation emits 9 in production (5 session lifecycle + circuit_breaker open/close + health_status_changed + 5 experiment), 1 deliberately suppressed (`session_terminated`), and 34 unemitted. The catalog is fully transcribed in `pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go` and `catalog_test.go` locks completeness against the spec, but the catalog enumeration is the only surface that exists for the majority. Every `lenny-ops` event short name (escalation_created, drift_detected, all remediation_lock_*, all platform_upgrade_*, all restore_*, event_delivery_failed, prometheus_query_timeout, lock_split_brain_detected, operation_progressed, ops_health_status_changed) is unemitted; every gateway alert short name (alert_fired, alert_resolved, upgrade_progressed, pool_state_changed, credential_rotated, credential_pool_exhausted, session_awaiting_action, delegation_completed, backup_completed, backup_failed, platform_upgrade_available) is unemitted. Three of the unemitted are documented seams with explicit acknowledgement (`cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:127`, `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:286`), but the rest have no in-code comment that this is intentional. Net effect: §16.6 is a manifest the catalog package transcribes but the rest of the codebase has not yet honored.

### CAT-005 (Medium) — `Source` field is unenforced and non-canonical at every emit site

`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go:32` declares `Source string \`json:"source,omitempty"\``, and `emitter.go:40-51` (`Emit`) does not enforce a non-empty `Source`. Production emit sites set `Source: "/v1/admin"` (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go:43`), `Source: "/v1/admin/health"` (`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1322`), `Source: "/v1/sessions"` (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:125`, `experimentrouter.go:152/249/273`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1947`). None of these match the §25.5 spec example at `spec/25_agent-operability.md:5172` (`"source":"//lenny.dev/gateway/gw-7f4c2a1e"`) or the §25.5 prose contract ("`source` identifies the emitting component (`//lenny.dev/gateway/{replicaId}` or `//lenny.dev/ops/{replicaId}`)"). CloudEvents 1.0 §3.1 also names `source` a REQUIRED context attribute; emitting a CloudEvents record without one is non-conformant, and the omitempty JSON tag will drop the field when callers omit it.

### CAT-006 (Medium) — `OperationalEvent` envelope lacks the lenny-prefixed extensions §25.5 names

`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go:27-52` (`OperationalEvent`) carries `ID`, `Source`, `SpecVersion`, `Type`, `Time`, `Severity`, `DataContentType`, `Data`. It does not carry `Subject` or any of the `lennytenantid`, `lennyoperationid`, `lennyrootsessionid` extension attributes the §25.5 envelope contract names ("Lenny extensions `lennytenantid`, `lennyoperationid`, and `lennyrootsessionid` carry tenant, operation, and delegation-tree correlation"). The richer `pkg/gateway/eventbus/cloudevents.go:80-117` `Event` struct does carry these via `Extensions`. The opsevents path produces an envelope that downstream consumers correlating by `lennytenantid` (e.g., a multi-tenant SIEM that pivots on the extension) cannot use, and the §25.5 promise of "tenant, operation, and delegation-tree correlation" is unmet for every operational event flowing through the opsevents emitter.

### CAT-007 (Medium) — Session lifecycle events do not flow via callbackUrl or §25.5 webhook subs

§16.6 reads: "Session lifecycle events (`session_*`, `delegation_completed`) are the same events delivered via the `callbackUrl` webhook ([§14](14_workspace-plan-schema.md)), the agent-operability SSE stream, and webhook subscriptions ([§25.5](25_agent-operability.md#255-operational-event-stream)) — one envelope, multiple transports." Of the three transports:

- **callbackUrl webhook (§14)**: `grep -rn callbackUrl pkg/gateway/sessionserver/` returns nothing. The terminal-state hook `recordSessionCompleted` in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:109-132` writes to the opsEmitter buffer but does not POST to a `callbackUrl`. No code path materialises the §14 `callbackUrl` field at terminal-state time.
- **SSE stream (`GET /v1/admin/events/stream`)**: not implemented. `grep -rn "events/stream"` in `pkg/gateway/admin/` returns no handler; only `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` exists (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go:13-81`).
- **Webhook subscriptions (`/v1/admin/event-subscriptions`)**: the worker exists (`pkg/ops/opsservice/webhookloop.go`, `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/`) but `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:223` wires it with `Events: emptyEventSource{}, Subscriptions: emptySubscriptionSource{}` — both sources are explicit cold-start no-ops (`cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:41-61`). No event is ever delivered to a webhook subscriber.

Two of three transports are absent entirely; the third (webhook subs) exists as code but is wired against empty sources. The §16.6 "one envelope, multiple transports" claim holds for zero transports today.

### CAT-008 (Medium) — `event_delivery_failed` emitter wired but un-instantiated

`pkg/ops/opsservice/webhookloop.go:243-247` already calls `w.emitFailure(sub.ID, ev.ID)` on terminal delivery failure, and `WebhookWorkerConfig.EmitFailure` is the seam (line 127). `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:223` constructs the worker without supplying `EmitFailure`, so the field is nil and the only place where `event_delivery_failed` could fire is dead code in production. Marked Medium rather than High because the upstream blocker is CAT-007 — until a non-empty event source and subscriptions exist there are no deliveries to fail — but the wiring gap is the more specific finding.

### CAT-009 (Low) — `Subject` field missing from envelope

`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go:27-52` does not declare a `Subject` field; CloudEvents 1.0 §3.1 lists `subject` as an OPTIONAL context attribute, and the eventbus package's `Event` struct carries it (`pkg/gateway/eventbus/cloudevents.go:103-104`) with the §12.3.7 convention (`session/{id}`, `tree/{id}`, `pool/{name}`). Operational-event envelopes therefore cannot carry a subject identifier, so consumers cannot route or filter on subject the way the eventbus side allows. Low because §16.6 does not directly mandate `subject`, but parity with eventbus would be expected.

### CAT-010 (Info) — `session_terminated` is intentionally never emitted

`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/usage.go:84-101` (`terminalSessionEvent`) explicitly documents: "Terminate is modeled as StateCompleted, so no session state maps to the session_terminated catalogue entry." `EventSessionTerminated` is therefore declared in the catalog (which is locked against §16.6 by `catalog_test.go:TestGatewayCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec166`) but no terminal-state transition resolves to it. This is consistent with how the gateway models terminate-as-complete, but §16.6 lists `session_terminated` as a distinct catalog entry. The mismatch is benign in the v1 model (no caller can observe a divergence) but the catalog and the implementation differ in their understanding of the namespace. Either §16.6 should drop `session_terminated` or the session state machine should distinguish complete-by-terminate from complete-by-success. Filed as Info because the spec itself does not require that every catalogued type be emitable.

### Catalog summary

- Typed enumeration: complete and spec-locked (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go` + `catalog_test.go`).
- Envelope contract: partially conformant. SpecVersion literal is wrong (CAT-003), Source is non-canonical and unenforced (CAT-005), Extensions missing (CAT-006), Subject absent (CAT-009).
- Redis stream destination: absent (CAT-002).
- Emit sites: 9 of 44 short names are emitted in production; 34 declared-only (CAT-004), 1 unimplementable as specified (CAT-001), 1 explicitly skipped (CAT-010).
- Downstream transports per §16.6 line on session lifecycle events: 0 of 3 functional (CAT-007).
