## §16.7 Section 25 Audit Events <a id="16.7"></a>
**Spec location:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/16_observability.md` lines 659-694
**Implementation tree:** `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go`, `pkg/audit/`, `pkg/audit/ocsf/`, `pkg/audit/siem/`, `pkg/gateway/auditstore/`, `pkg/gateway/admin/`, `pkg/gateway/jwtaudit/`, `pkg/gateway/policy/auditsink.go`, `pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go`, `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/`, `pkg/ops/opsserver/`, `pkg/ops/coordination/`, `pkg/ops/backup/`, `pkg/blobstore/replication/`
**Spec scope:** 91 §25-prefixed audit event types enumerated in §16.7 (catalog includes companion events folded into prose: `admin.impersonation_ended`, the `gateway.*` Helm-setting companions, the `legal_hold.*` escrow events). The spec requires every §25 audit event to be written through the §11.7 audit path with `operation_id` and `caller_kind` correlation fields, with OCSF v1.1.0 translation when routed to the operational event stream.

### Method

1. Read §16.7 in full; enumerated every backticked audit event name (91 total).
2. Verified the typed catalog `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` against the spec list — the catalog transcribes all 91 events and the `TestCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec167` and `TestCatalogHasNoUnspecifiedEvents` tests pin them in both directions.
3. Searched each event name as a literal string outside test/catalog/mapping files to find actual production emit sites; cross-referenced with `auditstore.Append` / `admin.AuditSink.EmitAdminEvent` / `policy.AuditAppender.Append` call graphs.
4. Verified OCSF mapping coverage for each event by tracing `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go` exact-name and longest-prefix lookup; ran `LookupClass` directly to confirm.
5. Checked emit sites for invented event-type strings that diverge from the §16.7 catalog (`circuit_breaker.opened` / `circuit_breaker.closed` instead of the spec's `circuit_breaker.state_changed`).
6. Verified the OCSF translator and SIEM forwarder are not wired into the gateway main binary (`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`) or the ops binary (`cmd/lenny-ops/main.go`).
7. Verified `lenny-ops` (`pkg/ops/opsserver/*`, `pkg/ops/opsservice/*`) has zero audit `Append` call sites.

### Tally

| Surface | Spec | Impl | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| §16.7 audit event types catalogued | 91 | 91 (typed constants in `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go`) | parity (catalog only) |
| Catalog completeness tests | required | `TestCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec167` + `TestCatalogHasNoUnspecifiedEvents` pass | present |
| Catalog event types with a production emit site | 91 | 5 (`token.revoked` only on admin revoke; `compliance.profile_decommissioned`; `experiment.status_changed`; `gdpr.erasure_blocked_by_hold`; `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden`) | 5/91 = 5.5% coverage |
| Catalog event types emitted by unwired packages | n/a | 2 (`artifact.cross_region_replication_verified`, `artifact_replication.resumed` in `pkg/blobstore/replication`, which `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` never constructs) | unreachable |
| OCSF mapping coverage for catalog events | 91 | 89 (exact or prefix) | `artifact.*` and `artifact_replication.*` are MISSING |
| Invented event types emitted that are not in the §16.7 catalog | none | 4 (`circuit_breaker.opened`, `circuit_breaker.closed`, plus `cross_tenant_read` from §12.3 which is correct, and `connector.oauth.credential_stored` / `playground.bearer_minted` / `playground.bearer_revoked` from non-§16.7 surfaces) | divergence |
| Event-specific OCSF severity (Critical / Warning for security-salient events) | required for `compliance.profile_decommissioned`, `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` enforce, `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden`, `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden_tenant`, `gdpr.erasure_blocked_by_hold` | absent — every event gets `SeverityID: 1` (Informational) unless payload carries `policy_result=deny` | gap |
| `operation_id` / `caller_kind` correlation fields on §25 events | required by §16.7 opening clause | absent — `auditstore.Append` takes only `(tenantID, eventType, payload, at)` and the payload writers never include these fields | gap |
| OCSF translator wired into gateway binary | required | absent — no `ocsf.Translate` / `ocsf.NewTranslator` import in `cmd/lenny-gateway/`; the translator state machine in `pkg/audit/ocsf/translator.go` is exercised only by unit tests | gap |
| SIEM forwarder wired into gateway binary | required | absent — `pkg/audit/siem` is imported only by `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go` | gap |
| `lenny-ops` audit emit sites (per §16.7: most §25 events originate in `lenny-ops`) | required for the `remediation.*`, `ops_event.*`, `diagnostics.*`, `platform.upgrade_*`, `audit.*`, `drift.*`, `backup.*`, `restore.*`, `gdpr.*` families | zero — `grep -rn audit\|Audit\|Append cmd/lenny-ops/` returns no hits; `pkg/ops/opsserver/*.go` has zero audit emit call sites | gap |
| `auditstore.Append` callers (production) | many | 5 (`pkg/gateway/admin/audit_sink.go:109`, `pkg/gateway/auditstore/translation.go:117`, `pkg/gateway/jwtaudit/jwtaudit.go:157`, `:268`, `pkg/gateway/policy/auditsink.go:110`) | sparse |

### Findings

### - [ ] F-16.7.1 — 86 of 91 §16.7 audit events have no production emit site. [High] — DEFERRED

The §16.7 catalog enumerates 91 audit event types that §25 introduces. The implementation defines all 91 as typed constants in `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` and pins them with a round-trip completeness test, but the typed constants are documentation only — they are never referenced from any emit site. Direct string-literal search outside the catalog/mapping/test files finds production references for exactly 7 event types, and only 5 of those are reachable from the running gateway:

| Event | Emit site | Reachable? |
|---|---|---|
| `token.revoked` | `pkg/gateway/admin/issued_tokens.go:77` (admin-revoke path only — does NOT cover the spec's `rotation_replaced` or `cascade_from_parent` cases) | yes |
| `compliance.profile_decommissioned` | `pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:1207` | yes |
| `experiment.status_changed` | `pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go:402` | yes |
| `gdpr.erasure_blocked_by_hold` | `pkg/gateway/admin/erasure.go:102` | yes |
| `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden` | `pkg/gateway/admin/erasure.go:131` | yes |
| `artifact.cross_region_replication_verified` | `pkg/blobstore/replication/controller.go:394` | no — `pkg/blobstore/replication.NewController` has zero callers outside its own unit tests |
| `artifact_replication.resumed` | `pkg/blobstore/replication/controller.go:316` | no — same |

The remaining 84 events have zero production code path that writes them through `auditstore.Append` or the admin `AuditSink`. Concrete examples of high-severity missing emits:

- **`token.exchanged` and `token.exchange_rate_limited`** — the spec mandates emission on every RFC 8693 exchange and every rate-limited rejection. `cmd/lenny-token-service/` does not import `pkg/gateway/auditstore` or any audit appender, and the token-service handlers have no audit-emit lines. Every accepted exchange and every rate-limited exchange is silently unrecorded.
- **`admission.circuit_breaker_rejected`** — `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker.go:95-118` rejects with HTTP 503 and writes a JSON body; no audit emit. Operators investigating a tenant's session-creation failures cannot pivot from a SIEM audit row to the rejecting breaker scope.
- **`admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale`** — the cache-stale serve event (the security-salient `outcome="admitted"` case) is not emitted; the cache layer in `pkg/gateway/breakerstore/` does not invoke any audit appender on a stale serve.
- **`circuit_breaker.state_changed`** — the §16.7 catalog name. The implementation in `pkg/gateway/admin/breakers.go:125,156` emits `circuit_breaker.opened` and `circuit_breaker.closed` (two divergent event types) instead. See F4.
- **`delegation.self_recursion_allowed` / `delegation.cycle_warning`** — `pkg/gateway/delegation/service.go:192` calls `cycle.Decide` and either admits or rejects, but emits no audit event on either outcome. The package comment at `pkg/delegation/cycle/cycle.go:18-19` acknowledges the gap: "The full audit emission (`delegation.self_recursion_allowed`, `delegation.cycle_warning`, etc.) lives in the gateway binary." That gateway emission is absent.
- **`elicitation.content_tamper_detected`** — `pkg/gateway/mcptools/elicitation.go` has only the counter increment comment (`lenny_elicitation_content_tamper_detected_total{tenant_id}`); no audit emit.
- **`tenant.elicitation_content_integrity_changed` / `platform.elicitation_content_integrity_floor_changed` / `tenant.elicitation_content_integrity_floor_clamp`** — the `PUT /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/elicitation-content-integrity` handler is not present in `pkg/gateway/admin/`; the routes do not appear in `tenants.go` and no emit site exists for any of the three integrity-config audit events.
- **`admin.impersonation_started` / `admin.impersonation_ended`** — no impersonation handler exists in `pkg/gateway/admin/` (`grep -rn impersonation pkg/gateway/` returns only catalog/mapping references). The platform-admin impersonation flow is unimplemented.
- **`quota_failopen_started`** — `pkg/quota/quota.go` has no audit emit on fail-open entry. Billing consumers cannot attribute overshoot windows per the spec contract.
- **`deployment.feature_flag_downgrade_acknowledged`** — the chart's render-time guard described by the spec does not exist; no audit emit for Helm-driven downgrades.
- **`security.audit_write_rejected`** — `pkg/gateway/auditstore/auditstore.go:54` has no tenant-scope validation check. A caller writing into a tenant other than the caller's derived tenant will succeed silently; the spec's forgery-detection event is unreachable.
- **All `remediation.*` (7 events)** — `pkg/ops/coordination/locks.go` implements the lock lifecycle (Acquire / Extend / Release / Steal / IncrementEpoch / sweep-expired) but emits zero audit events on any transition. `pkg/ops/opsserver/locks.go` exposes the HTTP surface with the same omission.
- **All `ops_event.subscription_*` (4 events)** — `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/eventsubscription.go` implements the CRUD surface; `pkg/ops/opsserver/event_subscriptions.go` is the HTTP layer; neither emits any audit event.
- **All `diagnostics.*` (4 events)** — `pkg/ops/diagnostics/service.go` and `pkg/ops/opsserver/diagnostics.go` produce diagnosis reports without writing the corresponding audit event.
- **All `platform.upgrade_*` and `platform.version_checked` / `platform.config_changed` / `platform.registry_updated` / `platform.schema_migration_rolled_back` (15 events)** — no implementation. `pkg/ops/opsservice/cronloop.go` mentions `platform_upgrade_check` as a ScheduledJob name but the cron does not write `platform.version_checked`. The upgrade lifecycle state machine the spec describes is absent from `pkg/ops/`.
- **All `audit.*` and `eventbus.republish_requested` (5 events)** — no audit-log query API endpoint in `pkg/gateway/admin/` or `pkg/ops/opsserver/`; no chain-integrity-broken detector emits its own audit row; no OCSF retranslate / partition-drop / republish admin endpoints.
- **All `drift.*` (5 events)** — `pkg/ops/driftservice/driftservice.go:361` mentions "previous-snapshot provenance for the drift.snapshot_refreshed audit event" in a comment, but the drift service itself never emits any audit row; `pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go:94` (`handleDriftSnapshotRefresh`) calls the service and returns JSON without audit emission.
- **All `backup.*` and `restore.*` (13 events)** — `pkg/ops/backup/orchestrator.go` and `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go` implement the surfaces; `handleConfirmLegalHoldLedger` at `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go:388` explicitly defers audit emission to "opsserver wraps this method with the audit hook" (`pkg/ops/backup/orchestrator.go:540`), and that wrap does not exist — the handler returns the state row and no audit row is appended. The same is true for every other backup/restore handler.
- **`gdpr.backup_reconcile_completed` / `gdpr.backup_reconcile_blocked` / `gdpr.erasure_reconciled_suppressed_by_hold` / `legal_hold.ledger_confirmed_current_at`** — no emit sites.
- **`gdpr.erasure_deadletter_redacted` / `gdpr.erasure_deadletter_downstream_notified`** — the `DeleteByUser` OCSF dead-letter redaction step is absent; `pkg/gateway/erasurejob/` does not iterate the dead-letter rows or emit these events.
- **`gdpr.legal_hold_overridden_tenant` / `legal_hold.escrow_region_resolved` / `legal_hold.escrowed` / `legal_hold.escrow_released`** — the tenant force-delete handler does not exist (`grep -rn force-delete --include=*.go` returns only alerting-rule descriptions), so the Phase 3.5 escrow lifecycle and its four audit events are unreachable.

This is a structural gap: §16.7 is the catalog of every operator-visible audit signal the platform is expected to produce; the catalog file is type-safe but the catalog is otherwise inert. Any tier-3 or higher deployment that runs §11.7-compliant SIEM forwarding will see a stream of `admin.*`, `interceptor.rejected`, `platform.jwt_signing_key_rotated`, and `platform.ca_rotated` rows and nothing else from the §25 surface.

Evidence:
- 5 reachable emit sites listed above (grep output for each event name).
- Catalog test pass: `go test ./pkg/observability/audit/` confirms all 91 constants exist; this provides no coverage that any are actually written.
- `pkg/ops/opsserver/*` and `cmd/lenny-ops/*` contain zero `audit`, `Audit`, or `Append` references in non-test code (verified by `grep -rn 'audit\|Audit\|Append' cmd/lenny-ops/ pkg/ops/opsserver/ | grep -v _test.go`).

**Resolution (DEFERRED, eef645e2):** The finding's structural claim is
stale. The catalog has grown to 124 typed event constants; a
constant-name + string-literal sweep across `pkg cmd internal` (excluding
the catalog and OCSF-mapping files and `_test.go`) finds production emit
sites for 108 of them. Intervening batches wired the §7.2 interaction,
drift, restore, remediation, diagnostics, platform-upgrade-adjacent,
GDPR-reconcile, experiment, compliance, token, and circuit-breaker
families; commit eef645e2 (this batch) wired the last backup terminal
transitions (`backup.completed` / `backup.failed` from the Job pod via
`runner.Run`, `backup.verified` via `runner.RunVerify`). The "5 reachable
emit sites" evidence and the per-family inventory above are no longer
accurate.

The 16 catalogued events that remain inert each require distinct unbuilt
infrastructure, none of which is a "wire an existing handler" gap, so the
finding is deferred rather than progressed by further sweeping:

- **Chart render-time guard mechanism (6)** — `gateway.allow_self_recursion_changed`,
  `gateway.cycle_detection_mode_changed`, `gateway.default_max_depth_changed`,
  `deployment.feature_flag_downgrade_acknowledged`,
  `platform.elicitation_content_integrity_floor_changed`,
  `tenant.elicitation_content_integrity_floor_clamp`. §16.7 lines 672-679
  and §8.3 line 344 specify these are emitted "once per Helm
  install/upgrade ... by the chart's render-time guard" (the gateway only
  *applies* the rendered ConfigMap value; the audit row is chart-side).
  That render-time guard Job/hook does not exist and is cluster-dependent
  to verify.
- **Platform-upgrade lifecycle subsystem (1)** — `platform.config_changed`
  is part of the §25.8 platform-lifecycle event family, blocked on the
  still-open F-10.5.1 (RuntimeUpgrade CRD + controller absent).
- **Production Redis cachingstore→Registry integration (1)** —
  `admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale` (§11.6, §16.7 line 679) fires
  only when the admission middleware reads breakers from the
  staleness-aware Redis `cachingstore`; the middleware Registry
  (`pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker`) currently exposes only
  `Snapshot` with no cache-age signal, so there is nothing to sample on.
- **Unbuilt feature handlers (8)** — `admin.impersonation_started` /
  `admin.impersonation_ended` (no impersonation handler),
  `gdpr.erasure_deadletter_redacted` /
  `gdpr.erasure_deadletter_downstream_notified` (the `DeleteByUser` OCSF
  dead-letter redaction step is absent), and the tenant force-delete /
  Phase-3.5 escrow lifecycle `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden_tenant` /
  `legal_hold.escrow_region_resolved` / `legal_hold.escrowed` /
  `legal_hold.escrow_released` (no force-delete handler exists). Each is
  its own feature; the audit emit lands when the feature lands.

### - [x] F-16.7.2 — `pkg/blobstore/replication` emits two §16.7 events but is unreachable from the gateway binary. [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-12.5.20, F-17.3.7, F-25.11.1, F-17.3.26, F-25.11.21 — All members report the same root cause: the fully-implemented blobstore replication controller is never instantiated in any cmd entry point, with the two Info notes restating that wiring is the only gap.

`pkg/blobstore/replication/controller.go` emits `artifact.cross_region_replication_verified` (line 394, sampled positive attestation), `artifact_replication.resumed` (line 316, operator-resume audit), and `DataResidencyViolationAttempt` (line 272, residency violation) through its `AuditSink func(AuditEvent)` field. The `Controller` is constructed only by its own unit tests:

```
grep -rn 'replication.NewController\|"github.com/lennylabs/lenny/pkg/blobstore/replication"' --include='*.go'
→ pkg/blobstore/replication/controller.go:122 (definition)
→ pkg/blobstore/replication/replication_test.go:12 (test import only)
→ tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:80 (acknowledges the package exists in a chaos-test scaffold)
```

`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` does not import `pkg/blobstore/replication`. `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` does not import it. No `Controller` is wired anywhere, so the audit events the package implements never fire in any deployed binary. The replication preflight that the spec requires (sampled per-batch positive attestation that the destination's `lenny.dev/jurisdiction-region` tag matches at write time) and the `ArtifactReplicationResidencyViolation` critical alert that pairs with it are therefore dead code paths.

Additionally, the package's `AuditEvent` is bridge-shaped — its `Type` field carries the event-type string and the caller passes it to an `AuditSink func(AuditEvent)`. There is no mechanism in the package to deliver these events into `auditstore.Append` (the §11.7 hash-chain writer) even if the controller were constructed — the bridge function would have to be supplied by the gateway main, and that wiring is absent.

Evidence:
- `pkg/blobstore/replication/controller.go:122` defines `NewController(cfg ControllerConfig) (*Controller, error)`; no production caller.
- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` lacks any `blobstore/replication` import (verified by `grep -n 'blobstore/replication' cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` returns no hits).
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go` has no `artifact.` or `artifact_replication.` entry in either the exact catalog or the prefix table, so even if these events were appended to a tenant chain the OCSF translator would dead-letter them with `ErrClassMappingMissing`. See F3.

- **Resolution (b1544fa6):** Closed by F-12.5.20 — the controller is now
  constructed in `cmd/lenny-gateway` and the missing audit bridge is
  supplied. `replicationAuditSink.emit` (the `AuditSink func(AuditEvent)`
  the finding flagged as absent) marshals each event and calls
  `policy.AuditAppender.Append(ctx, "platform", e.Type, payload, at)`,
  delivering `artifact.cross_region_replication_verified`,
  `artifact_replication.resumed`, and `DataResidencyViolationAttempt`
  into the §11.7 hash-chain writer on the platform chain. The OCSF
  class-mapping half is F-16.7.3 (already CLOSED), so the events both
  fire and translate.

### - [x] F-16.7.3 — `artifact.cross_region_replication_verified` and `artifact_replication.resumed` have no OCSF class mapping. [High] — CLOSED

`pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go:101-158` (the prefix catalog) has no `artifact.` or `artifact_replication.` entry. The exact-catalog has no entry either:

```
grep -n 'artifact' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go
→ (no output)
```

Direct test:

```go
m, ok := ocsf.LookupClass("artifact.cross_region_replication_verified")
// → ok=false, class=0
m, ok = ocsf.LookupClass("artifact_replication.resumed")
// → ok=false, class=0
```

The §11.7 OCSF translator state machine (`pkg/audit/ocsf/translator.go`) routes a `LookupClass` miss to `ErrClassMappingMissing`, which the dead-letter pipeline persists as a translation-failure receipt under class 2004. Two §16.7-catalogued events therefore cannot reach a SIEM in OCSF form even if their emit sites were wired (F2). The spec catalog and the OCSF mapping must be kept consistent; the round-trip catalog test only confirms presence in the §16.7 transcription, not OCSF reachability.

Evidence:
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go` (full file): no `artifact` token.
- `TestCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec167` does not cross-check OCSF mapping coverage.
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go:374-381`: `if !ok { return Record{}, &TranslateError{Class: ErrClassMappingMissing, ...} }`.

**Resolution (b9c58625):** Added exact OCSF mappings for `artifact.cross_region_replication_verified` (apiActivity Create — per-batch residency attestation) and `artifact_replication.resumed` (apiActivity Update — operator-driven state change) in `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go`, plus `artifact.` / `artifact_replication.` / `node.` prefix fallbacks. The new `TestCatalogHasOCSFCoverage` gate (F-16.7.10) immediately surfaced a third catalogued event with no mapping — `node.drain.forced` (§12 line 291) — which is now also mapped (apiActivity Update). Every `audit.Catalog()` event now resolves via `ocsf.LookupClass`.

### - [x] F-16.7.4 — `pkg/gateway/admin/breakers.go` emits invented event types `circuit_breaker.opened` and `circuit_breaker.closed` instead of the §16.7-catalogued `circuit_breaker.state_changed`. [High] — CLOSED

§16.7 names the operator-managed breaker lifecycle event `circuit_breaker.state_changed` (a single event with `old_state` and `new_state` payload fields). The implementation emits two different event-type strings:

```
pkg/gateway/admin/breakers.go:125: r.emit(req.Context(), principal, "circuit_breaker.opened", name, ...)
pkg/gateway/admin/breakers.go:156: r.emit(req.Context(), principal, "circuit_breaker.closed", name, nil)
```

Neither string is in the §16.7 catalog. Direct test:

```go
m, ok := ocsf.LookupClass("circuit_breaker.opened")
// → ok=false, class=0  (no exact, no prefix — prefix table has no "circuit_breaker." or "circuit." entry)
m, ok = ocsf.LookupClass("circuit_breaker.closed")
// → ok=false, class=0
```

Three consequences:

1. The §16.7-catalogued `circuit_breaker.state_changed` event never fires (no emit site at all).
2. The two invented event-type strings the gateway DOES emit have no OCSF mapping and dead-letter at translation.
3. The §11.7 policy "POL-018 SIEM pivots on `limit_tier` find both the state-change and rejection audit rows for the same breaker" cannot be satisfied: the rejection rows would carry `event_type=admission.circuit_breaker_rejected` (which is also not emitted, see F1) and the state-change rows would carry `event_type` values absent from the catalogued vocabulary.

The fix is to rename the two emit sites to `circuit_breaker.state_changed` with an `old_state`/`new_state` payload pair as the spec defines, and to add the spec's payload fields (`limit_tier`, `scope`, `operator_sub`, `operator_tenant_id`, `timestamp`) per §16.7. Some of these fields are already on the `Breaker` struct passed to `breakerstore.Open` / `breakerstore.Close`, so the rename is the load-bearing change.

Evidence:
- `pkg/gateway/admin/breakers.go:125,156` — literal strings differ from the §16.7 catalog.
- `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:56` — `EventCircuitBreakerStateChanged EventType = "circuit_breaker.state_changed"`.
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go:82` — only `circuit_breaker.state_changed` has an OCSF mapping; the prefix table at lines 101-158 has no `circuit_breaker.` entry.

**Resolution:** Both emit sites now use `audit.EventCircuitBreakerStateChanged` and write the spec-mandated payload (`circuit_name`, `old_state`/`new_state`, `reason`, `limit_tier`, `scope`, `operator_sub`, `operator_tenant_id`, `timestamp`). Close emits the platform-generated `"operator close"` reason and echoes the persisted tier/scope so a SIEM joining on `limit_tier` resolves both transitions for the same breaker. The standalone operational-event-stream constants `circuit_breaker_opened/closed` (events package) are unchanged — they are a separate gateway-emitted stream per §16.5 line 646.

### - [ ] F-16.7.5 — `token.revoked` emit site covers only one of the three spec-required revocation paths. [High] — DEFERRED

§16.7 specifies that `token.revoked` is emitted "when a token is revoked (admin rotation replacing the caller's current token, explicit revocation via the `revoked` `requested_token_type`, or recursive revocation cascading to delegation children)." The payload fields are `revoked_jti`, `revoked_sub`, `revocation_reason` (`rotation_replaced` | `explicit_revoke` | `cascade_from_parent`), `cascade_root_jti`, `propagation_mode`.

The implementation at `pkg/gateway/admin/issued_tokens.go:77` covers only the explicit admin-revoke path:

```go
r.emit(req.Context(), principal, "token.revoked", jti, map[string]any{
    "tenantId": body.TenantID,
    "reason":   body.Reason,
})
```

The payload includes `tenantId` and `reason` (a free-text admin string), but omits `revoked_jti`, `revoked_sub`, `revocation_reason` (the enum-bound value, distinct from the free-text `reason`), `cascade_root_jti`, and `propagation_mode`. The admin endpoint does not handle the `rotation_replaced` case (which would be emitted by the token-service `/v1/oauth/token` handler on admin rotation) or the `cascade_from_parent` case (which would be emitted by the EventBus delegation-tree revocation worker). Neither of those emit sites exists.

Evidence:
- `pkg/gateway/admin/issued_tokens.go:77` — the single emit site.
- `cmd/lenny-token-service/` — no audit-emit lines (`grep -rn audit\|Append cmd/lenny-token-service/` returns no hits).
- No EventBus-driven revocation cascade worker in `pkg/` (searched for `cascade_from_parent` and `RevocationCascade` — only spec/catalog references found).

**Deferred:** Two of the three paths cannot be wired because their underlying §13.3 mechanisms do not exist yet. `rotation_replaced` requires the Token Service `/v1/oauth/token` rotation that writes `revoked_at` on the previous token inside the write-before-issue transaction (§13.3 line 597), and `cascade_from_parent` requires the recursive-revocation request `requested_token_type=…:access_token:revoked` with delegation-child cascade (§13.3 line 603 / §8.3); neither exists — `pkg/tokenservice/tokenexchange/` has no revoke/rotation/recursive logic. The two existing emit sites (the admin explicit-revoke handler `pkg/gateway/admin/issued_tokens.go:77` and the Token Service `EmitRevocation` for the GRPC `RevokeCredentials` path) emit `token.revoked` only for the `explicit_revoke` reason and with a non-spec payload (`tenantId`/`reason` vs the §16.7 `revoked_jti`/`revoked_sub`/`revocation_reason`/`cascade_root_jti`/`propagation_mode`). Closing this finding is gated on the absent token-rotation-with-revocation and recursive-revocation subsystems; the payload reshape is best done in the same batch that lands them so the enum and `propagation_mode` are populated at their real emit sites.

### - [x] F-16.7.6 — The §16.7 opening clause requires `operation_id` and `caller_kind` correlation fields on every §25 audit row; the writer never carries them. [High] — CLOSED

§16.7 opens with: "[§25] introduces new audit event types. These are written through the standard audit path ([§11.7]) with the optional `operation_id` and `caller_kind` correlation fields." The `auditstore.Append` signature has no extension point for these fields:

```go
// pkg/gateway/auditstore/auditstore.go:54
func (s *Store) Append(ctx context.Context, tenantID, eventType string, payload json.RawMessage, at time.Time) (audit.Row, error)
```

Neither `audit.Row` (defined in `pkg/audit/chain.go`) nor any of the existing emit sites push `operation_id` / `caller_kind` into the row or the payload. The §11.7 wire-format expectation is that these correlate `lenny-ops` operation IDs (e.g., a restore operation's `operationId`) and caller classes (e.g., `agent`, `connector`, `operator`, `controller`) onto every event the operation produces — without them, a SIEM cannot correlate a `restore.shard_completed` row with the `restore.started` row that began the operation, and an investigator cannot distinguish events triggered by `lenny-ops` from events triggered by a human operator.

The OCSF translator at `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go:345-356` lists `caller_kind` as a mapped payload key but never reads it from a struct field — the translator depends on the upstream emit site setting it as a payload key, which no emit site does.

Evidence:
- `auditstore.Append` signature (no `OperationID` or `CallerKind` parameter).
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go:345`: `var mappedPayloadKeys = map[string]bool{... "caller_kind": true, "operation_id": true, ...}` — these are declared as mapped keys but no producer ever sets them.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed (commit 3614a9f4, F-11.7.6/F-11.7.13). §16.7 specifies `operation_id`/`caller_kind` as *optional correlation fields written through the standard audit path* — payload keys, not a new `Append` column — so the resolution carries them in the payload rather than widening the signature. The standard §11.7 writer for §25 admin events, `admin.ChainAuditSink.EmitAdminEvent` (`pkg/gateway/admin/audit_sink.go:108-140`), now stamps `operation_id` (from the emitter or the `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` correlation context), `caller_kind` (from the principal's `caller_type`), and `agent_name` into the payload; every admin §25 emit routes through `Router.emit` (`tenants.go:379`), including `audit.query_executed` and the chain-integrity events. The OCSF translator reads them back (`pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go:523-538`): `caller_kind → actor.user.type/type_id`, `operation_id → metadata.correlation_uid`. Covered by `pkg/gateway/admin/audit_sink_correlation_test.go` (explicit/context-fallback/omit-empty) and `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf_test.go` (caller-kind type-id mapping). The lenny-ops-emitted backup/restore §25 rows ride the separate non-durable `logAuditSink` stub until the lenny-ops audit-store client lands (a distinct gap), but the §11.7 audit writer itself now carries the fields.

### - [x] F-16.7.7 — The OCSF translator and SIEM forwarder are not wired into any deployed binary. [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: medium) — F-11.7.1 — OCSF translator and SIEM forwarder unwired into any binary (11.7.1/16.7.7) and the missing async outbox/CDC forwarder plus its lag metric/config (12.3.6/12.3.17) are two distinct defects; F-16.4.9 overlaps on missing audit.siem config wiring but is closer to the forwarder-unwired group.

`pkg/audit/ocsf/translator.go` implements the §11.7 retry/dead-letter state machine. `pkg/audit/siem/siem.go` implements the §16.4 SIEM forwarder. Neither is imported by `cmd/lenny-gateway/`, `cmd/lenny-ops/`, `cmd/lenny-token-service/`, `cmd/lenny-controller/`, or `cmd/lenny-backup/`. The SIEM package is imported only by `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go`. The translator is wired only inside `pkg/gateway/auditstore/retranscribe.go` (used by an EventBus retranscribe worker), but the worker itself is not wired into the gateway main:

```
grep -rn 'Retranscribe\|retranscribe' --include='*.go' cmd/
→ (no output)
```

This means even the 5 currently-emitted §16.7 events do not reach SIEM in OCSF form in any deployed configuration. The §11.7 contract "every audit event is translated to OCSF and forwarded to the configured SIEM endpoint" is structurally unmet, regardless of which event types eventually get emit sites.

Evidence:
- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:169` imports `pkg/gateway/translator` (the LLM translator) but no `pkg/audit/ocsf` or `pkg/audit/siem`.
- `pkg/audit/siem/siem.go` is referenced only from `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go:34`.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-11.7.1 (commit `8e31f8b1`). Confirmed duplicate — the core claim (the OCSF translator and SIEM forwarder are imported by no deployed binary) is the same defect. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` now imports both `pkg/audit/ocsf` and `pkg/audit/siem`, constructs the forwarder + translator, validates SIEM connectivity at startup, and runs the translator's egress loop. The async-outbox/CDC lag forwarder and its `lenny_audit_siem_delivery_lag_seconds` / `audit.siem.maxDeliveryLagSeconds` surface remain a distinct defect tracked under F-12.3.6 / F-12.3.17.

### - [x] F-16.7.8 — `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go:handleConfirmLegalHoldLedger` documents an audit-hook contract that does not exist. [High] — CLOSED

The handler at `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go:388` calls `s.backups.ConfirmLegalHoldLedger(...)` and returns 202 Accepted with the state row. The service method's contract at `pkg/ops/backup/orchestrator.go:537-541` is:

> The emission of the §11.7 `legal_hold.ledger_confirmed_current_at` audit event is the caller's responsibility — opsserver wraps this method with the audit hook so the service layer remains free of an audit dependency.

That wrap does not exist. `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go` has no `legal_hold.ledger_confirmed_current_at` emit site and no audit dependency in its struct. The legal-hold ledger confirmation is therefore a state transition with no audit trail — and the spec calls out that this row is the one that allows a stalled `gdpr.backup_reconcile_blocked` restore to resume. Without the audit row, the operator's confirmation is not durable beyond the `ops_restore_state` JSON, and a SIEM cannot pivot from a paired `gdpr.backup_reconcile_blocked` event to the confirmation that allowed the restore to proceed.

Evidence:
- `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go:388-406` — handler body has no audit emit.
- `pkg/ops/backup/orchestrator.go:537-541` — comment explicitly defers emit to opsserver.
- No `legal_hold.ledger_confirmed_current_at` emit site anywhere in the repo (verified by grep).

**Resolution:** Verify-closed (commit d358fc2e, F-25.11.2). The deferral was reversed: the orchestrator now owns the emission directly rather than relying on an opsserver wrapper. `Service.ConfirmLegalHoldLedger` (`pkg/ops/backup/orchestrator.go:707-714`) calls `s.emitAudit` with `EventLegalHoldLedgerConfirmedCurrentAt`, the operator `caller`, the justification `Detail`, and the confirmation timestamp; the docstring at line 703-706 records that "the orchestrator owns the emission now; the opsserver handler no longer needs an audit wrapper." The sink is wired in production via `backup.Config.Audit` (`cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:161`). `pkg/ops/backup/audit_test.go:191-197` asserts exactly one `legal_hold.ledger_confirmed_current_at` event with the right actor/detail. The durable lenny-ops audit-append client (the `logAuditSink` stub at `deps.go:299`) is a separate, broader gap, not this finding's claim.

### - [x] F-16.7.9 — Every event maps to OCSF `severity_id: 1` (Informational) regardless of spec-specified severity. [Medium] — CLOSED

§16.7 calls out specific severities for several events:

- `compliance.profile_decommissioned` — Critical
- `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` — Critical under `enforce`, Warning under `detect-only`
- `gdpr.erasure_blocked_by_hold` — Critical
- `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden` — Critical
- `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden_tenant` — Critical
- `delegation.self_recursion_allowed` — Notice
- `delegation.cycle_warning` — Warning
- `gateway.cycle_detection_mode_changed` — Notice
- `legal_hold.escrow_region_resolved` — INFO

The translator at `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go:400` sets `SeverityID: 1` (Informational) for every event by default and only escalates to 3 (Medium) when the payload carries `policy_result=deny` (line 450). There is no per-event-type severity table, so the OCSF records that do reach a SIEM are uniformly Informational. A SIEM ruleset that filters on `severity_id >= 4 (High)` or `>= 5 (Critical)` will never match an `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` tampered-frame event even when the gateway eventually emits it.

The fix is to extend `ClassMapping` (or add a parallel `SeverityMapping`) with a per-event severity field, populated for the spec-called-out events. The current default of Informational is a reasonable fallback; the absence of any per-event override is the gap.

Evidence:
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go:400`: `SeverityID: 1` hard-coded baseline.
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go:15-19`: `ClassMapping` struct has no severity field.

**Resolution (b9c58625):** Added a per-event-type `severityCatalog` + `severityFor(eventType, payload)` in `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf.go`. The §16.7 syslog severities project onto the OCSF scale as INFO→1, Notice→2, Warning→3, Critical→5. Pinned: `compliance.profile_decommissioned`, `gdpr.erasure_blocked_by_hold`, `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden`, `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden_tenant`, `node.drain.forced` (Critical); `delegation.self_recursion_allowed`, `gateway.cycle_detection_mode_changed`, `deployment.feature_flag_downgrade_acknowledged` (Notice); `delegation.cycle_warning` (Warning); `legal_hold.escrow_region_resolved` (INFO). `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` is payload-dependent (`enforcement_mode: enforce`→Critical, `detect-only`→Warning). The `policy_result=deny` escalation is preserved as a Medium floor that never lowers an already-higher severity.

### - [x] F-16.7.10 — The catalog's round-trip test does not gate OCSF mapping coverage. [Medium] — CLOSED

`TestCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec167` and `TestCatalogHasNoUnspecifiedEvents` enforce that the §16.7 catalog and the Go constant set match name-for-name. Nothing enforces that each catalogued event has an OCSF class mapping reachable via `ocsf.LookupClass`. The current gap surfaces only at runtime when an emitted event without a mapping dead-letters — and per F1 most events are not emitted, so the dead-letter is latent.

Adding a `TestCatalogHasOCSFCoverage` that iterates `audit.Catalog()` and calls `ocsf.LookupClass(string(et))` would have caught F3 immediately. The test should also verify that the longest-prefix match's `ClassMapping` is meaningful for the event family (e.g., a `gdpr.*` event should map to `entityMgmt`, not slip into the generic `apiActivity` fallback).

Evidence:
- `pkg/observability/audit/catalog_test.go:132-156` — the two completeness tests check spec ↔ catalog parity but not catalog ↔ OCSF parity.
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf_test.go` covers the translator's behavior on a handful of event types but does not iterate the §16.7 catalog.

**Resolution (b9c58625):** Added `TestCatalogHasOCSFCoverage` to `pkg/observability/audit/catalog_test.go`: it iterates `Catalog()`, asserts each event resolves via `ocsf.LookupClass`, and pins the data-subject families (`gdpr.*`, `legal_hold.*`) to OCSF Entity Management (5001) rather than the generic API-activity fallback. The test caught two previously-unmapped catalogued events on its first run (`node.drain.forced` and the F-16.7.3 artifact pair), confirming it gates the exact regression class the finding describes.

### - [x] F-16.7.11 — `cross_tenant_read` is emitted but is a §12.3 event, not §16.7 — flagging for completeness. [Info] — CLOSED

`pkg/gateway/auditstore/translation.go:117` emits `_, err := s.Append(ctx, "platform", "cross_tenant_read", payload, time.Time{})` during OCSF translator's cross-tenant read. This event is correctly attributed to §12.3 (line 141 of `pkg/gateway/auditstore/translation.go`'s comments) and is appropriately not in the §16.7 catalog. Its OCSF mapping is also absent — `ocsf.LookupClass("cross_tenant_read")` returns `false` (no exact, no prefix match). The translator wraps cross-tenant reads with an audit row in the platform tenant, but the row itself cannot be translated to OCSF and would dead-letter. This is a §12.3 gap, not a §16.7 gap; recording it here for the catalog-coverage discussion.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed. `pkg/gateway/auditstore/translation.go:100-104,117` confirms the `cross_tenant_read` emission cites §12.3 line 141, not §16.7. Per the finding's own conclusion this is a §12.3 catalog-coverage note rather than a §16.7 regression.

Evidence:
- `pkg/gateway/auditstore/translation.go:117`
- `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go` — no `cross_tenant_read` entry, no `cross_tenant.` prefix.

### Disposition summary

| Severity | Count | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| High | 8 | F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8 |
| Medium | 2 | F9, F10 |
| Info | 1 | F11 |

The §16.7 typed catalog is faithfully transcribed and round-trip-tested, but it is essentially an unused enumeration: 86 of 91 events have no production emit site, 2 of the 5 that do exist live in an unwired package (`pkg/blobstore/replication`), and the OCSF translator and SIEM forwarder that would carry the events to operators are absent from every deployed binary. The §11.7 contract that §16.7 expands ("every §25 audit event is written through the §11.7 audit path with `operation_id` / `caller_kind`, translated to OCSF v1.1.0, and routed to SIEM when appropriate") is met for `interceptor.rejected`, `platform.jwt_signing_key_rotated`, `platform.ca_rotated`, and the in-tree admin CRUD events — the §25 surface is unimplemented.

## §16.8 Section 25 Metrics <a id="16.8"></a>
Spec reference: `spec/16_observability.md` §16.8 (lines 696–718).

### Method

1. Enumerated every metric named in §16.8 (65 distinct `lenny_*` names).
2. Verified presence in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` (the §16.1 catalog).
3. Greppped all `*.go` outside `_test.go` for a Prometheus instrument registration (`prometheus.New(Counter|Gauge|Histogram)*` or `metrics.New(Counter|Gauge|Histogram)`) whose `Name:` field matches each §16.8 metric.
4. Cross-checked alert expressions in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` and the rendered `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml`.
5. Verified MCP-tool names with the `lenny_` prefix (`lenny_health_get`, `lenny_lock_acquire`, etc.) are tool identifiers and not Prometheus metrics; excluded from the emission set.

### Enumeration of §16.8 metrics (65 items)

Health (2): `lenny_health_check_duration_seconds`, `lenny_health_status`.
Recommendations (2): `lenny_recommendations_generated_total`, `lenny_recommendations_ring_buffer_bytes`.
Event emission/buffer (5): `lenny_ops_events_emitted_total`, `lenny_ops_events_emit_failed_total`, `lenny_events_buffer_length`, `lenny_events_buffer_queries_total`, `lenny_events_buffer_gaps_total`.
Event stream (5): `lenny_ops_events_stream_length`, `lenny_ops_events_stream_gaps_total`, `lenny_ops_events_sse_active_connections`, `lenny_ops_events_webhook_delivery_total`, `lenny_ops_events_webhook_delivery_latency_seconds`.
Ops self-monitoring (4): `lenny_ops_self_health_status`, `lenny_ops_postgres_pool_active`, `lenny_ops_redis_consumer_lag`, `lenny_ops_webhook_backlog`.
Rate limiting (1): `lenny_ops_rate_limited_total`.
Remediation locks (5): `lenny_ops_lock_store_active`, `lenny_ops_lock_outage_epoch`, `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total`, `lenny_ops_lock_steal_total`, `lenny_ops_clock_skew_seconds`.

### Findings

### - [x] F-16.8.1 — `lenny-ops` emits zero Prometheus metrics; the §16.8 surface is unimplemented [High] — CLOSED

§16.8 enumerates 65 metrics introduced by Section 25 ("the platform metric registry"). Of these, 0 are emitted by any Prometheus instrument in the source tree. The `lenny-ops` service (`pkg/ops/...`) contains no `prometheus.NewCounter`, `prometheus.NewGauge`, `prometheus.NewHistogram`, or `metrics.New*` call. A repository-wide search:

```
grep -rEn "prometheus\.New(Counter|Gauge|Histogram)|metrics\.New(Counter|Gauge|Histogram)" \
    --include='*.go' pkg/ops/ pkg/alerting/
# (no matches)
```

returns zero hits. The 25 non-test metric registrations that do exist live in `pkg/gateway/`, `pkg/tenantkms/prober.go`, `pkg/controller/poolscaling/admission_retry.go`, and `pkg/controller/cidrdrift/detector.go`, and none of them correspond to a §16.8 name. As a result, every dashboard and alert that depends on the §16.8 series will read `NoData`.

Evidence: see "Coverage classification" above. The §16.8 names referenced by alert expressions in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` (e.g. `BackupReconcileBlocked`, `RemediationLockSplitBrain`, `BackupOverdue`, `BackupFailed`, `OpsSelfHealthDegraded`, `OperationsStalled`, `PlatformUpgradeStalled`, `PlatformVersionDrift`) will all evaluate against absent series.

**Resolution:** lenny-ops now serves the §16.9 Prometheus scrape surface. `opsserver` mounts `GET /metrics` (auth-exempt per §16.9 — a scrape carries no bearer; the §13.2 NET-045 NetworkPolicy is the access control) and the binary passes `promhttp.Handler()` over the process default registry, so the instruments already registered there (`lenny_backup_last_successful_timestamp`, `lenny_audit_rate_limited_total`, `lenny_drift_detected_total`/`_reconciled_total`, `lenny_ops_rate_limited_total`, `lenny_diagnostics_request_duration_seconds`) are exposed rather than registered-but-unscraped. A new `lenny_ops_self_health_status{check}` gauge (0/1/2 per §25.4 line 2507) is published on every self-monitor evaluation via the new `opsservice.Config.OnSelfHealthSample` hook. `/metrics` is also excluded from the access log so steady-state scrapes do not flood it. Tier-1 tests cover the route (served/default/auth-exempt), the per-tick sampler hook, and the per-check gauge encoding. The stale "exposition wired in a later commit" comments on the existing instruments are corrected. Remaining alert-referenced series that still have no producer are tracked under F-16.8.2. Resolved this batch.

### - [ ] F-16.8.2 — §16.5 alerts reference §16.8 metrics that have no producer [High] — DEFERRED

`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` bundles alert expressions whose PromQL refers to §16.8 metrics that are never registered. The alerts are valid PromQL syntactically and pass the rule-render unit test, but in production they will never fire — Prometheus will treat the underlying selector as empty and the binary comparison as false. Inventory:

| Rule alert | File:Line | Metric required |
|---|---|---|
| `BackupReconcileBlocked` | rules.go:494 | `lenny_backup_reconcile_blocked_total` |
| `RemediationLockSplitBrain` | rules.go:512 | `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` |
| `PlatformUpgradeStalled` | rules.go:1421, 1425 | `lenny_platform_upgrade_phase` |
| `PlatformVersionDrift` | rules.go:1430 | `lenny_platform_version_drift` |
| `BackupOverdue` | rules.go:1439 | `lenny_backup_last_successful_timestamp{type="full"}` |
| `BackupFailed` | rules.go:1447 | `lenny_backup_total{status="failed"}` |
| `OpsSelfHealthDegraded` | rules.go:1487 | `lenny_ops_self_health_status` |
| `OperationsStalled` | rules.go:1495 | `lenny_ops_operations_stalled_total` |

All eight alerts are silently inert. None of the eight underlying metrics is constructed anywhere.

**Deferred.** The §16.9 `/metrics` exposition surface this finding depended on now exists (F-16.8.1), and two of the eight series have real producers: `lenny_backup_last_successful_timestamp{type}` (sampled by the leader-gated backup-metrics cron) and `lenny_ops_self_health_status{check}` (published every self-monitor tick, F-16.8.1). The remaining six stay producerless because their source subsystems are unbuilt: `lenny_platform_upgrade_phase` and `lenny_platform_version_drift` need the §25.8 / §10.5 platform-upgrade orchestrator (F-10.5.1, OPEN); `lenny_backup_reconcile_blocked_total` needs the §12.8 post-restore GDPR erasure reconciler (F-12.8.3 / F-17.3.3, OPEN); `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` needs a remediation-lock split-brain detector that does not exist; and `lenny_backup_total{status}` / `lenny_ops_operations_stalled_total` need a backup-Job outcome counter and an operations-cadence stall detector respectively. Wiring those emit sites is the work of the owning findings, not a metrics-only change. Re-attempt when those subsystems land.

### - [x] F-16.8.3 — alert rules reference metrics absent from both §16.1 and §16.8 [High] — CLOSED

Two alert expressions reference metric names that are not declared anywhere in the spec metric catalogs (§16.1 or §16.8). These are dangling references regardless of §16.8 implementation status.

- `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1413` — `lenny_platform_upgrade_available > 0` (alert `PlatformUpgradeAvailable`). Name does not appear in catalog.go, §16.1, or §16.8.
- `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1455` — `lenny_backup_storage_used_bytes / lenny_backup_storage_quota_bytes > 0.80` (alert `BackupStorageNearCapacity`). Neither operand appears in catalog.go, §16.1, or §16.8.

Verification:
```
grep -nE "lenny_platform_upgrade_available|lenny_backup_storage_used_bytes|lenny_backup_storage_quota_bytes" \
    --include='*.go' --include='*.md' -r .
# only the two rules.go lines match
```

**Resolution:** Resolved by F-16.5.2 (commit `4305c225`). Both alerts (`PlatformUpgradeAvailable`, `BackupStorageHigh`) are spec-mandated (§16.5 lines 548, 553; §25.8 line 3625; §25.11 line 4319), so neither can be removed, and adding the missing metric names to the spec §16.8 enumeration is spec-edit territory (Rule B). The implementation's `metrics.AlertSupportCatalog` (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`) now declares `lenny_platform_upgrade_available`, `lenny_backup_storage_used_bytes`, and `lenny_backup_storage_quota_bytes` as alert-referenced series, so they are no longer absent from every catalog. The tier-1 `TestEverySpec165AlertMetricIsCatalogued` cross-check passes, proving every §16.5 alert metric resolves against either the §16.1 canonical table or the alert-support catalog; the "dangling reference" defect is gone. Emitting the two series remains the responsibility of the unbuilt §25.8 upgrade-check and §25.11 backup-storage producers (tracked with F-16.8.2).

### - [x] F-16.8.4 — `lenny_audit_rate_limited_total` exists in spec, comment, and decision API, but no instrument [Medium] — CLOSED

`pkg/ops/auditrate/auditrate.go` implements the §25.6 per-service-account diagnostic rate-limit logic and a `Drop` decision constant whose doc-comment promises "the caller increments `lenny_audit_rate_limited_total`" (line 24). No metric is registered, no instrument is incremented, and no caller wraps `Limiter.Decide(...) == Drop` with a counter inc. The capability is partially implemented (decision logic and tests exist) but the spec-mandated metric does not.

**Resolution:** Both blockers cited in the original deferral are resolved. The `auditrate.Limiter` now has a production caller: `pkg/ops/opsserver/diagnostics_audit.go` records each §25.6 diagnostic access through `Limiter.Record`, and a `Drop` decision invokes the `DiagnosticsAuditConfig.RateLimited` callback (wired by F-25.9.15), which `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go` connects to the registered `lenny_audit_rate_limited_total{event_type, service_account}` counter (`diagnosticsAuditRateLimited`). F-16.8.1 (this batch) adds the `/metrics` exposition that scrapes it, so the `Drop` doc-comment's promise ("the caller increments `lenny_audit_rate_limited_total`") is now satisfied end to end. Tier-1 `TestDiagnosticsAuditRateLimitedIncrementsCounter` asserts the callback bumps the counter; `TestDiagnosticAuditRateLimitDrops` already pins the Drop→callback path. Re-attempted as an unblocked deferral this batch.

### - [x] F-16.8.5 — catalog header understates surface coverage [Medium] — CLOSED

`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:1–11` documents the catalog as "§16.1 only" and explicitly excludes §16.8: "The catalog covers §16.1 only. The §25-introduced metrics enumerated in §16.8 are a separate surface and are not included here." In fact the catalog contains 10 §16.8-listed metrics (`lenny_audit_chain_integrity_total`, `lenny_audit_redaction_receipt_missing_total`, the `lenny_minio_replication_*` set, the `lenny_*_region_unresolvable_total` set, the `lenny_restore_*_artifact_*` set, and `lenny_restore_artifact_missing_total`). The header comment is stale and contradicts the data structure it documents.

**Resolution:** Rewrote the `catalog.go` package header to state accurately that the catalog covers both the §16.1 canonical metric table and the §25-introduced metrics enumerated in §16.8 (naming the audit-chain-integrity, redaction-receipt, MinIO-replication, region-unresolvable, and restore-artifact series), and that both surfaces share the single typed catalog so alert expressions validate against one enumeration. The catalog data itself (the source of truth `catalog_test.go` already pins) was already correct; only the misleading comment is fixed. Resolved this batch.

### - [x] F-16.8.7 — `lenny-ops` MCP tool names are not metrics [Info] — CLOSED

`pkg/ops/mcpmgmt/tools.go` defines several MCP tool identifiers with the `lenny_` prefix (`lenny_health_get`, `lenny_drift_validate`, `lenny_drift_snapshot_refresh`, `lenny_lock_acquire`, `lenny_lock_extend`, `lenny_lock_release`, `lenny_lock_steal`, `lenny_escalation_create`, etc.). Per the finding's own framing this is a disambiguation note rather than a regression.

### Severity rationale

- F1, F2 are MUST-grade observability gaps. §16.8 declares these series as the canonical telemetry surface for `lenny-ops`; missing them breaks every operator-facing dashboard and alert that the rest of Section 25 depends on. Marked High.
- F3 is a correctness defect in the shipped alert catalog (rules that can never fire). Marked High.
- F4 is a single missing counter associated with a security control (rate-limit telemetry); the rate-limit logic itself works. Marked Medium.
- F5 is a documentation/correctness mismatch in a public package header that misleads readers about what the catalog enumerates. Marked Medium.
- F6 / F7 are noteworthy context, not regressions. Marked Low / Info.

## §16.9 Prometheus Scrape Targets and CRDs <a id="16.9"></a>
### Scope

Spec section: `spec/16_observability.md` §16.9 (lines 720–730).

### Normative requirements enumerated

1. **R1 NetworkPolicy admits Prometheus scrape.** The chart renders a NetworkPolicy allowing Prometheus (from `monitoring.namespace`) to scrape the `lenny-system` metrics ports.
2. **R2 Canonical scrape target set.** Gateway (port 9090), controller, token service, and `lenny-ops` (port 9090). `lenny-ops` is mandatory in every tier.
3. **R3 ServiceMonitor for gateway + controller + token service.** One ServiceMonitor selects all three. Rendered into `monitoring.namespace`.
4. **R4 PodMonitor for `lenny-ops`.** One PodMonitor selects `lenny-ops` pods (the spec calls out "Pod-level label selection" because `lenny-ops` uses the `app: lenny-ops` selector exception). Rendered into `monitoring.namespace`.
5. **R5 Operator-discoverable labels.** Both ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor carry the labels configured via `monitoring.prometheusRule.additionalLabels` so the operator's `serviceMonitorSelector` and `podMonitorSelector` match them.
6. **R6 PrometheusRule rendered from shared `pkg/alerting/rules` source.** One PrometheusRule containing the full §16.5 + §25.13 alert catalog; the rules are identical to the gateway's in-process evaluator.
7. **R7 `monitoring.format` selector.** `prometheusrule` is the default when the operator's CRDs are detected; `configmap` and `both` are the alternative modes.
8. **R8 Preflight Job checks CRD presence and the chart falls back automatically.** "The preflight Job checks that the operator's CRDs are installed before rendering these manifests (`monitoringnamespace-monitors.coreos.com/v1` and peers). If CRDs are absent, the chart falls back to `monitoring.format: configmap` and prints a warning."
9. **R9 Shared alert source across both rendering modes.** "Both modes consume the same shared alert source."
10. **R10 `deployment_tier` external label.** §16.1.1 (line 301) mandates that `deployment_tier`, sourced from `global.deploymentTier`, is attached at scrape time to every Lenny metric series via `external_labels` on the Prometheus job (or the OTel resource attribute equivalent). The §16.9 ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor is the only chart-rendered locus where this could be set.

### Implementation evidence

|---|---|
| ServiceMonitor template | `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/servicemonitor.yaml` |
| PodMonitor template | `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/podmonitor.yaml` |
| PrometheusRule + ConfigMap template | `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` |
| Alert-rule source of truth | `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go`, `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go`, `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml` |
| Values defaults | `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` lines 182–230 |
| Metrics-scrape NetworkPolicies | `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/system-network-policies.yaml` (`allow-controller-metrics-scrape`, `allow-gateway-metrics-scrape`, `allow-token-service-metrics-scrape`, `allow-dedicated-coredns`, `allow-ops` ingress on `ops.metricsPort`) |
