### Findings

### - [x] F-16.9.1 — ServiceMonitor selects controller, but no controller Service exists [High] — CLOSED

The ServiceMonitor's `matchExpressions` includes `controller` under `lenny.dev/component`:

```
# templates/servicemonitor.yaml
matchExpressions:
  - key: lenny.dev/component
    operator: In
    values:
      - gateway
      - controller
      - token-service
```

A search of every chart template for `kind: Service` returns:
- `lenny-ops` (templates/ops-deployment.yaml:174)
- `lenny-gateway` and `lenny-gateway-pods` (templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:255, 286)
- `lenny-token-service` (templates/token-service-deployment.yaml:81)
- webhook services under `templates/admission-policies/`

There is **no Service for `lenny-controller`**. The controller Deployment renders only ServiceAccount, ClusterRole(Binding), Role(Binding), and Deployment; no `kind: Service` at all (`templates/controller-deployment.yaml`, `templates/controller-rbac.yaml`).

Without a backing Service, the Prometheus Operator cannot translate the ServiceMonitor controller entry into any scrape target. The controller's metrics endpoint is never discovered through the operator path, violating R2 (canonical target set must include the controller) and R3 (ServiceMonitor must cover the controller). R1 is also partially violated: scrape ingress is admitted by the NetworkPolicy, but nothing on the operator-discovery side can reach it because no Endpoints object materializes.

The servicemonitor unit test (`tests/servicemonitor_test.yaml` lines 51–62) asserts only that the ServiceMonitor's selector lists `controller`; it does not verify that an underlying Service exists. The gap is invisible to the test suite.

**Required fix:** Add a `lenny-controller` Service (port `metrics` → targetPort `metrics`) in `templates/controller-deployment.yaml`, parallel to the gateway and token-service Services. Add a test asserting the Service is rendered.

**Resolution:** CLOSED by `e9882485`. Added a `lenny-controller` ClusterIP Service (port `metrics` → targetPort `metrics`, `lenny.dev/component: controller` selector) in `templates/controller-deployment.yaml` so the Prometheus Operator resolves the ServiceMonitor controller selector into Endpoints. `controller-deployment_test.yaml` now asserts the Service renders and tracks a `controller.metricsPort` override.

### - [x] F-16.9.2 — Controller metrics port — Service expectation, NetworkPolicy admission, and container listener disagree [High] — CLOSED

Three different layers state three different things about the controller metrics port:

1. `values.yaml` line 22 declares `controller.metricsPort: 9090` and documents it as "the port the controller serves Prometheus metrics on".
2. `templates/system-network-policies.yaml:239` admits ingress on `controller.metricsPort` (= 9090) in `allow-controller-metrics-scrape`.
3. `templates/controller-deployment.yaml:48,65` hardcodes `--metrics-bind-address=:8080` and exposes containerPort `metrics: 8080`. The binary default in `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:92` is `:8080`.

The controller actually serves on 8080. The NetworkPolicy admits 9090. Any Prometheus scrape via the documented port is dropped by the policy or refused by the listener; the operator path is doubly broken (no Service + wrong NetworkPolicy port). The controller `metricsPort` value never flows into the Deployment's `--metrics-bind-address` or its containerPort.

**Required fix:** Either wire `controller.metricsPort` into both the binary flag and the containerPort, or change the value to 8080 and update R2 (spec text claims the canonical port is 9090 for the gateway and `lenny-ops` specifically; controller is unstated). Aligning the binary flag, the containerPort, the NetworkPolicy, and a new controller Service onto the same value is the minimum fix.

**Resolution:** CLOSED by `e9882485`. The controller Deployment now binds `--metrics-bind-address=:{{ .Values.controller.metricsPort }}` and names the metrics containerPort on the same value (default 9090), so the binary flag, the containerPort, the `allow-controller-metrics-scrape` NetworkPolicy (already on `controller.metricsPort`), and the new `lenny-controller` Service all agree on one port. Tests assert the flag and containerPort and a `controller.metricsPort` override.

### - [x] F-16.9.3 — PodMonitor port name `metrics` is not present on the `lenny-ops` pod [High] — CLOSED

`templates/podmonitor.yaml:42-46` declares:

```
podMetricsEndpoints:
  - port: metrics
```

For a PodMonitor, `podMetricsEndpoints[*].port` is the **name of a containerPort on the pod**, not a Service port. The `lenny-ops` pod template at `templates/ops-deployment.yaml:117-119` exposes only:

```
ports:
  - name: http
    containerPort: {{ .Values.ops.httpPort }}
```

There is no containerPort named `metrics`. The Prometheus Operator's endpoint discovery for this PodMonitor will skip every `lenny-ops` pod because no containerPort matches the `metrics` selector, so `lenny-ops` is never scraped through the operator path. R2 (mandatory `lenny-ops` scrape) and R4 (PodMonitor covers `lenny-ops`) both fail.

Note: the Service in front of `lenny-ops` does have a `metrics` port (lines 184–190), but a PodMonitor does not consult Services; only ServiceMonitors do.

**Required fix:** Either add a containerPort named `metrics` (containerPort = `ops.metricsPort`) to the `lenny-ops` pod template (the listener is the same as `http`, so the additional port entry is purely a labelling concern), or change the PodMonitor to reference the existing `http` port via `port: http` plus an explicit `path: /metrics`, which is already declared.

**Resolution:** CLOSED. Verify-closed — the `lenny-ops` pod template already exposes a named `metrics` containerPort (added by F-16.9.10, commit `ac2eb08d`), so the PodMonitor `port: metrics` selector matches. `ops-deployment_test.yaml` asserts the named containerPort and `servicemonitor_test.yaml` asserts the PodMonitor endpoint references it.

### - [x] F-16.9.4 — Preflight CRD-presence check and automatic `configmap` fallback are absent [High] — CLOSED

R8 mandates a preflight check that the Prometheus Operator CRDs are installed before rendering ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor / PrometheusRule, with automatic fallback to `monitoring.format: configmap` plus a warning if they are absent. §18.7 build-sequence line 154 reiterates: "The CRD-presence preflight check that falls back to `configmap` when the Prometheus Operator is absent ships at the same time."

Implementation:
- `pkg/preflight/run.go` performs admission-webhook inventory, phase-stamp consistency, host-sharing flags, NetworkPolicy parity audits, and SPIFFE/SA-token-audience uniqueness. There is no CRD lookup of any kind.
- `templates/preflight-job.yaml` RBAC (lines 36–48) grants list/get on ValidatingWebhookConfigurations, NetworkPolicies, Deployments, ConfigMaps; nothing on `apiextensions.k8s.io/CustomResourceDefinition`.
- `templates/prometheusrule.yaml`, `templates/servicemonitor.yaml`, and `templates/podmonitor.yaml` gate solely on `monitoring.bundleRules` / `monitoring.format` / `monitoring.serviceMonitor.enabled`. No fallback logic and no warning are emitted when the chosen format references a missing CRD.
- ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor are gated on `monitoring.serviceMonitor.enabled` which defaults to `false`, so the stock render skips the CRDs. The PrometheusRule defaults to `format: "prometheusrule"`, so a fresh install **on a cluster without the operator** fails `kubectl apply` on the PrometheusRule (`no matches for kind PrometheusRule in version monitoring.coreos.com/v1`) with no preflight catch.

**Required fix:** Add a preflight check that lists CustomResourceDefinitions for `servicemonitors.monitoring.coreos.com`, `podmonitors.monitoring.coreos.com`, and `prometheusrules.monitoring.coreos.com`. If any are absent and `monitoring.format != "configmap"` (or `serviceMonitor.enabled: true`), fail closed with a remediation message, or — per the spec — automatically downgrade `monitoring.format` to `configmap`, emit a Helm `NOTES.txt` warning, and skip rendering ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor. Wire the CRD watch into the preflight RBAC.

**Resolution:** Took the spec's automatic-fallback branch. New chart helpers (`lenny.monitoring.operatorPresent`, `lenny.monitoring.effectiveFormat`, `lenny.monitoring.renderMonitors` in `_helpers.tpl`) detect the Prometheus Operator CRDs at render time via `.Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"`. When `monitoring.format` selects the operator CRDs (`prometheusrule`/`both`) but they are absent, `prometheusrule.yaml` degrades the effective format to `configmap` (so `kubectl apply` does not fail on a missing PrometheusRule CRD), the ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor are not rendered, and `NOTES.txt` prints the fallback warning. On a cluster with the operator, `.Capabilities` carries the CRD and the operator manifests render. The Go preflight check `PrometheusOperatorCRDCheck` (`pkg/preflight/promoperator.go`) lists the three CRDs and raises a non-blocking advisory naming the missing ones; it is wired into `preflight.Run` (`MonitoringFormat` config field) and the lenny-preflight binary (`--monitoring-format`, passed by `preflight-job.yaml`). The existing `apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefinitions` RBAC (granted for the crd-schema-version check) already covers the read, so the finding's RBAC evidence was stale. Tests: tier-1 preflight check (present/missing/skip), helm-unittest fallback suite (`monitoring-fallback_test.yaml`: configmap degrade for prometheusrule/both, no monitors when operator absent, enabled flag cannot override the CRD gate), plus capabilities-gated prometheusrule/servicemonitor suites. Resolved this batch.

### - [x] F-16.9.5 — `deployment_tier` external label is not attached anywhere [High] — CLOSED

§16.1.1 (line 301) states: "The `deployment_tier` label … is a static label sourced from Helm (`global.deploymentTier`) and always carries one of `tier1`, `tier2`, or `tier3` … It is attached at scrape time to every Lenny metric series via `external_labels` on the Prometheus job (or the equivalent OpenTelemetry resource attribute), so it is available on all alerts without requiring per-metric instrumentation." The §16.5 alert `Tier3GCPressureHigh` and the §16.10 OpenSLO export both depend on this label being present.

Implementation:
- No `global.deploymentTier` key exists in `charts/lenny/values.yaml` (the `global:` block only carries `devMode` and `spiffeTrustDomain`, lines 431–440).
- The ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor templates do not set any static relabel adding `deployment_tier`, nor any equivalent (the operator-level `external_labels` is on the Prometheus CR, not on a ServiceMonitor; a ServiceMonitor sets `targetLabels`, `metricRelabelings`, or `relabelings`). Neither template carries any relabel directive.
- No tier preset (`presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml`) sets a tier label anywhere.
- The OTel `pkg/observability/metrics` package does not attach a `deployment_tier` resource attribute (search returns no hits).

`Tier3GCPressureHigh` (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:597`, `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml:392`) evaluates `lenny_gateway_gc_pause_fleet_p99_ms{deployment_tier="tier3"} > 50`. With no series carrying the label, the alert can never fire on any tier. The §16.9 ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor templates are the natural place to inject the static relabel.

**Required fix:** Add `global.deploymentTier` to `values.yaml` and tier presets, then add a static relabel in both ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor that writes `deployment_tier = {{ .Values.global.deploymentTier }}` (e.g., via `metricRelabelings` with `replacement` + `targetLabel`). Document that the `external_labels`-mechanism is the operator-managed Prometheus CR which is out of chart scope; the ServiceMonitor relabel is the supported substitute when the chart cannot write to the Prometheus CR.

**Resolution:** CLOSED by `e9882485`. Added `global.deploymentTier` (default `tier1`) to `values.yaml` and to the tier1/2/3 presets alongside `capacityPlanning.tier`, and a `deployment_tier` `metricRelabelings` entry on both the ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor endpoints per §16.1.1, so `Tier3GCPressureHigh` and the §16.10 OpenSLO export resolve the label. The note in `values.yaml` records that the Prometheus CR `external_labels` is out of chart scope and the relabel is the supported substitute. `servicemonitor_test.yaml` covers the default, an override, and the empty-value omission.

### - [x] F-16.9.6 — Spec text describes `monitoring.format: prometheusrule` as gating the ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor too; implementation splits the gate [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-17.1.14 — F-16.9.6 asserts a gap in how monitoring.format gates ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor, while F-17.1.14 concludes the same gating aligns with the spec and reports no gap, so they reach opposite conclusions about the same area.

The §16.9 narrative reads: "Deployers who run the Prometheus Operator … should set `monitoring.format: prometheusrule` (the default when the operator's CRDs are detected). With this setting: The chart renders one `ServiceMonitor` … and one `PodMonitor` …". The plain reading is that `monitoring.format: prometheusrule` controls all three operator CRDs.

Implementation:
- `templates/prometheusrule.yaml` gates rendering on `monitoring.format` (`prometheusrule` / `both`).
- `templates/servicemonitor.yaml` and `templates/podmonitor.yaml` gate on a separate flag `monitoring.serviceMonitor.enabled` (default `false`).

The result: a deployer who sets `monitoring.format: prometheusrule` and runs the operator still gets no scrape targets unless they additionally flip `monitoring.serviceMonitor.enabled: true`. The two gates are independent. The §16.9 text does not document or justify the split; it implies a single switch.

**Required fix:** Either collapse the gates so ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor render whenever `monitoring.format` ∈ {`prometheusrule`, `both`}, or amend the spec text to document the two-gate split with rationale. The chart comment at `templates/servicemonitor.yaml:9-19` explains the split as a CRD-presence concern, which is the same concern §16.9 says the preflight (F4 above) is supposed to handle — so once F4 lands, the split loses its justification and the single-gate model becomes safe.

**Resolution:** Collapsed the gate, made safe by F-16.9.4 landing in the same batch. `lenny.monitoring.renderMonitors` renders the ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor whenever `monitoring.format` ∈ {`prometheusrule`, `both`} (or `serviceMonitor.enabled` forces them on) AND the operator CRDs are present, so the default `format: prometheusrule` install on a cluster with the operator now renders the scrape monitors with the single switch the §16.9 text implies. The CRD-presence check keeps a cluster without the operator from rendering a monitor that would fail `kubectl apply`, which was the original justification for the separate `serviceMonitor.enabled` gate; `serviceMonitor.enabled` is retained only as an explicit override to force monitors when `format: configmap`. Closes the F-17.1.14 overlap (the gate now matches the §16.9 single-switch reading). Resolved this batch.

### - [x] F-16.9.7 — Token-service Service routes `metrics` to its gRPC container port [Medium] — CLOSED

`templates/token-service-deployment.yaml:92-98`:

```
ports:
  - name: grpc
    port: {{ .Values.tokenService.grpcPort }}
    targetPort: grpc
  - name: metrics
    port: {{ .Values.tokenService.metricsPort }}
    targetPort: grpc
```

The container exposes only `grpc` and `http-token` containerPorts (lines 48–52). The metrics Service port targets `grpc`. The token-service binary is invoked with `--addr=:httpPort --grpc-addr=:grpcPort --issuer=…` — there is no metrics flag and no separate metrics listener. Either the binary multiplexes Prometheus scrape onto the gRPC listener (unusual, and not documented in the deployment template comment), or the scrape will hit the gRPC port and receive a gRPC error frame instead of `/metrics`. The spec asserts that "token service" is one of the canonical scrape targets (R2).

Confirm at the binary level whether `/metrics` is actually served on the gRPC port; if it is, document the mux in the template comment. If it is not, add a separate metrics listener and containerPort.

**Resolution:** CLOSED. Verify-closed — the token-service binary takes `--metrics-addr` (`cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go`) and the Deployment renders `--metrics-addr=:{{ .Values.tokenService.metricsPort }}` with a dedicated `metrics` containerPort and a Service `metrics` port targeting `metrics` (not `grpc`), resolved by `a4229b71`. The finding's described `targetPort: grpc` state is stale. `token-service-deployment_test.yaml` asserts the listener flag, the containerPort, and the Service port → `metrics` target.

### - [x] F-16.9.8 — `monitoring.format` has no validation [Medium] — CLOSED

`templates/prometheusrule.yaml` reads `.Values.monitoring.format` and switches on three string literals. There is no `values.schema.json` (none exists under `charts/lenny/`), no `required` template guard, no allow-list check. A typo (`prometheus-rule`, `Prometheus-rule`) silently renders nothing, with no warning. The same applies to `monitoring.serviceMonitor.enabled` (a non-bool truthy value can confuse Helm's `if`).

**Required fix:** Either add a `required` check (e.g., `{{- if not (has $format (list "prometheusrule" "configmap" "both")) }}{{ fail … }}{{- end }}`) or add a `values.schema.json` with an `enum` constraint.

**Resolution:** CLOSED by `e9882485`. Added the `lenny.monitoring.validateFormat` helper in `_helpers.tpl`, invoked from `prometheusrule.yaml` ahead of the `bundleRules` gate so it fires on every render regardless of whether the catalog would otherwise emit. An out-of-range `monitoring.format` fails with `monitoring.format must be one of [prometheusrule configmap both]; got %q`. `prometheusrule_test.yaml` asserts the `failedTemplate` message.

### - [x] F-16.9.9 — §16.9 metions one ServiceMonitor "for the gateway, controller, and token service"; CoreDNS (port 9153) is scrapeable per §13.2 NET-045 but not covered [Medium] — CLOSED

The dedicated CoreDNS pod runs in `lenny-system` (per `templates/system-network-policies.yaml:244-280` `allow-dedicated-coredns` opening :9153 to monitoring), and §13.2 NET-045 lists CoreDNS among the components needing Prometheus scrape. §16.9 itself omits CoreDNS from the canonical list and the ServiceMonitor does not include it.

This is technically consistent with §16.9 as written, but the operator-managed flow then leaves CoreDNS unscraped on a stock install — the deployer must add their own scrape config. Either the spec should add CoreDNS to the §16.9 set (and a CoreDNS Service/ServiceMonitor entry should be added), or the chart should document the omission. Treating as Medium because the §16.9 text is silent and the spec is the source of truth; flag for spec-vs-implementation reconciliation.

**Resolution:** CLOSED by `e9882485`. §16.9 defines the canonical scrape set as the gateway, controller, Token Service, and `lenny-ops`; CoreDNS is intentionally outside it, and adding it to the set is spec-edit territory (Rule B). Took the documentation branch: the `servicemonitor.yaml` header now records that the dedicated CoreDNS pod (`lenny-system`, TCP 9153) is scrapeable through the §13.2 NET-045 NetworkPolicy but sits outside the §16.9 operator-managed set, so a deployer who wants CoreDNS metrics supplies their own scrape config.

### - [x] F-16.9.10 — Container ports lack the named `metrics` entry on gateway and ops pods, masking the F3 / F5 class of bug [Low] — CLOSED

Gateway pod (`templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:224-232`) exposes containerPorts `http`, `grpc`, `llm-proxy`. No `metrics`. Ops pod exposes only `http`. Token-service exposes `grpc`, `http-token`. Adding an explicit containerPort named `metrics` per pod (even when it points to the same listener as `http`) would make F3 self-evident from the manifest and would let a single PodMonitor pattern (`port: metrics`) work uniformly across every component. Pure hygiene; no functional change beyond unlocking F3's "PodMonitor port-name fix" path.

- **Resolution:** Added a named `metrics` containerPort on the gateway and lenny-ops pod templates. /metrics is served on the same HTTP listener as /healthz; the named entry surfaces the metrics endpoint in the rendered pod spec and lets PodMonitor `port: metrics` discovery match uniformly across control-plane components. New helm-unittest assertions in `gateway-deployment_test.yaml` and `ops-deployment_test.yaml` exercise the named-port presence.

### - [x] F-16.9.11 — ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor scrape `path: /metrics` is hardcoded; spec says nothing wrong, but no override is exposed [Low] — CLOSED

Both templates hardcode `path: /metrics`. The `monitoring.serviceMonitor` values block exposes `interval` and `scrapeTimeout` but no `path` or `scheme`. A deployer with a non-standard metrics path (some Prometheus operator deployments use `/-/metrics` for `kube-state-metrics`-style services) cannot override without forking the chart. Operator-tunable per memory guidance `feedback_fixes_must_align_with_spec.md`; spec does not mandate exposing the override, so Low.

- **Resolution:** Added `monitoring.serviceMonitor.path` (default `/metrics`) to `charts/lenny/values.yaml`; `servicemonitor.yaml` and `podmonitor.yaml` now render `path` from the value. New helm-unittest assertions in `tests/servicemonitor_test.yaml` cover the default and the override path.

### - [x] F-16.9.12 — No `scheme: HTTPS` option for scraping mTLS-protected metrics endpoints [Low] — CLOSED

Section §10.3 mandates mTLS between control-plane components. The gateway metrics listener shares the `http` port (8080), which the deployment exposes as plaintext HTTP for liveness/readiness. The chart's `mtls.enabled` flag does not flow into the ServiceMonitor (no `scheme: HTTPS`, no `tlsConfig`). If a deployer wraps the metrics path behind TLS, no scrape works. Spec §16.9 does not currently require HTTPS scraping; flag as Low for future-proofing because §10.3 implies an inconsistency.

- **Resolution:** Added `monitoring.serviceMonitor.scheme` (default `http`) and `monitoring.serviceMonitor.tlsConfig` (default `{}`) values; `servicemonitor.yaml` and `podmonitor.yaml` render `scheme` and the Prometheus Operator `TLSConfig` block verbatim when scheme is non-default. Operators fronting /metrics with TLS (kube-rbac-proxy or an in-process mTLS listener) opt in without forking the chart. Tests in `tests/servicemonitor_test.yaml` cover the default-absent + HTTPS-present render paths.

### - [x] F-16.9.13 — `monitoring.format: prometheusrule` default works only when the operator is present [Info] — CLOSED

`values.yaml:196` defaults `monitoring.format: "prometheusrule"`. On a vanilla Kubernetes cluster without the Prometheus Operator CRDs, `helm install` succeeds (PrometheusRule manifest is rendered) but `kubectl apply` (or Helm's apply phase) fails with "no matches for kind PrometheusRule in version monitoring.coreos.com/v1", producing a confusing install failure mid-way through. This is exactly the failure mode the missing F4 preflight is meant to prevent; calling out separately because the default is the production-hostile setting until F4 lands.

- **Resolution:** Verify-closed. This is a meta-observation that
  the production-hostile install surface evaporates once F-16.9.4
  ("Preflight CRD-presence check and `configmap` fallback are
  missing") lands. The actionable item is F-16.9.4 (still OPEN);
  no separate fix needed for this Info note.

### - [x] F-16.9.14 — Test coverage exists for the rendered templates but does not verify cross-template invariants [Info] — CLOSED

`tests/servicemonitor_test.yaml` (137 lines) checks: render gate, namespace, label-selector contents, scrape interval, additional labels, alternate namespace. It does not check:
- That a Service with `lenny.dev/component: gateway` (or controller/token-service) actually exists with a `metrics` port (the foundational invariant for ServiceMonitor matching).
- That the `lenny-ops` pod template carries a containerPort named `metrics` (the invariant the PodMonitor depends on).
- That `controller.metricsPort` agrees between values, NetworkPolicy admission, Service port, and binary listener.

Adding these cross-template assertions is the unit-test path to catching F1, F2, F3 at chart-test time.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed as a second-order test-coverage observation. The §16.9 F1/F2/F3 root-cause findings (ServiceMonitor controller selector with no controller Service, controller metricsPort disagreement across values/NetworkPolicy/binary, PodMonitor `port: metrics` mismatch with `lenny-ops` containerPort name) remain OPEN; cross-template invariants land naturally with each F1/F2/F3 remediation. No separate work owed at this roll-up level.

### - [x] F-16.9.15 — §16.9 comment in `servicemonitor.yaml` and `podmonitor.yaml` cites a NET-045 NetworkPolicy that is split across multiple per-component policies [Info] — CLOSED

Both templates' comments reference "the §13.2 NET-045 metrics-scrape NetworkPolicies (rendered by `system-network-policies.yaml`)". The actual rendering is four separate policies (`allow-controller-metrics-scrape`, `allow-gateway-metrics-scrape`, `allow-token-service-metrics-scrape`, `allow-dedicated-coredns`) plus the `allow-ops` ingress clause carrying the lenny-ops metrics port. The comment is accurate as a reference but does not enumerate the per-component split, so a reader auditing the scrape path has to chase five rules instead of one. Pure documentation note.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("Pure
documentation note"). Confirmed the four NET-045 NetworkPolicies plus
`allow-ops` render at `charts/lenny/templates/system-network-policies.yaml:231`,
`:259`, `:309`, `:330`, `:674`, and the §13.2 NET-045 comment is
accurate as written in `charts/lenny/templates/servicemonitor.yaml:12`
and `charts/lenny/templates/podmonitor.yaml:8,13`. No code change.

## §16.10 OpenSLO Export <a id="16.10"></a>
Scope: `spec/16_observability.md` §16.10 (lines 732–736) against the
implementation tree (`pkg/alerting/`, `pkg/observability/`,
`cmd/gen-alerting-rules`, `charts/lenny/`, and tests).

### Normative requirements extracted from §16.10

The subsection is two paragraphs but each MUST/normative claim is
independently testable. The normative requirements are:

| ID    | Requirement (spec §16.10)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R-001 | The Helm chart renders the latency and availability SLOs from §16.5 as OpenSLO v1 YAML documents when `monitoring.openslo.enabled: true`. Default `false`. (lines 732–734)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| R-002 | The rendered documents reference the canonical metric names listed in §16.5 (e.g., `lenny_session_creation_duration_seconds`, `lenny_session_availability_ratio`) so the export and the bundled rules share one metric vocabulary. (line 734)                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| R-003 | The rendered documents carry the Lenny tier labels `deployment_tier="tier1" \| "tier2" \| "tier3"` so external SLO tooling produces burn-rate alerts consistent with the bundled multi-window alerts. (line 734)                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| R-004 | When enabled, the chart emits a `ConfigMap` containing OpenSLO `SLO`, `SLI`, and `AlertPolicy` objects for the deployer's tooling to consume. (line 736)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| R-005 | The export is sourced from the same §16.5 alert catalog that drives the bundled `PrometheusRule` (`pkg/alerting/rules`), so the OpenSLO ConfigMap is "a view of the same source" and cannot drift from the in-process evaluator or the `PrometheusRule`. (line 736 plus §16.9 architectural constraint about a single shared source)                                                                                                     |
| R-006 | The export covers the §16.5 SLO catalog: Session creation success rate, Session creation latency, Time to first token, Session availability, Gateway availability, Startup latency (runc and gVisor), Checkpoint duration. (§16.5 SLO table at lines 611–621 plus the burn-rate table at lines 629–638, both cross-referenced by §16.10 as the source the export must render)                                                              |

### Evidence

**Implementation searches.**

- `grep -rin "openslo\|OpenSLO"` across `pkg/`, `cmd/`, and `charts/`
  returns zero matches. There is no Go package, no chart template, no
  `values.yaml` block, and no generator command that emits OpenSLO YAML.
- `charts/lenny/templates/` contains 27 templates; none is named
  `openslo*.yaml` or references the OpenSLO `apiVersion`. The only
  alert-bearing templates are `prometheusrule.yaml` (for the §16.9
  Prometheus Operator path) and `podmonitor.yaml` /
  `servicemonitor.yaml`. The bundled rule body lives at
  `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml` and renders as
  `PrometheusRule` only.
- `charts/lenny/values.yaml` lines 185–230 define the `monitoring`
  block. It exposes `monitoring.namespace`, `monitoring.bundleRules`,
  `monitoring.format` (with the documented `prometheusrule | configmap`
  modes), `monitoring.prometheusRule`, `monitoring.configMap`, and
  `monitoring.serviceMonitor`. There is no `monitoring.openslo` key
  and no `monitoring.openslo.enabled` toggle. `grep -n
  "openslo\|slo\|sli\|burn"` over the file is empty.
- `cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go` only renders the `PrometheusRule`
  spec.groups fragment from `rules.Catalog()` into
  `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml`. It has no OpenSLO output
  path and no `-format openslo` flag.
- `pkg/alerting/rules/render.go` only defines `RenderPrometheusRule`
  and `RenderRuleGroups`. No `RenderOpenSLO` (or equivalent) function
  is exported. `Rule` does carry an `SLO` field (rendered into the
  Prometheus `slo` annotation by `buildRuleGroup`), but that string
  is only the human-readable SLO label (e.g., "Session creation
  success rate >= 99.5%"), not a parsed SLO target.
- `pkg/observability/` contains `metrics/`, `tracing/`, `correlation/`,
  `audit/`, and `logging/` — no `slo/` or `openslo/` subpackage.
- `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go` enumerates every subcommand. There is no
  `slo`, `slo export`, or `slo validate` subcommand. (The
  `docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md` "planned" walkthrough
  instructs deployers to run `lenny-ctl slo export --format openslo`,
  but the binary rejects that command with `unknown command "slo"`.)
- `tests/spec-map.json` (entry for §16.10) maps the section to
  `pkg/observability/slo`, but that package does not exist on disk
  (`find pkg -type d -name "*slo*"` returns only
  `pkg/gateway/slotcounter`, which is the §5.2 sandbox-slot counter
  and unrelated). The same entry lists zero tests and is marked
  `blocked_until_phase: 14.5`.
- `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml` line 96 explicitly defers §16.10:
  `reason: deferred; justification: OpenSLO export is built in Wave 7
  (Phase 14.5)`.

**Build-status cross-check.**

- `BUILD-PROGRESS.md` "Current wave: Wave 7." Phase 13 (Full
  observability, audit, lenny-backup, compliance) is marked Done.
- `spec/18_build-sequence.md` line 612 schedules
  `[§16.10] OpenSLO export rendered behind monitoring.openslo.enabled`
  as a Phase 13 deliverable (the "Observability catalog and chart
  wiring" cluster), not Phase 14.5. The spec-map-exception
  justification contradicts the build sequence.
- Phase 14.5 is "Post-hardening SLO re-validation"
  (`tests/tier7_load/scenarios/post_hardening_slo/`), a load-test
  re-baseline, not the OpenSLO export deliverable.

**Customer-facing docs and README.**

- `README.md` line 81 advertises "Prometheus alerting rules and
  OpenSLO definitions drop into any standard observability stack."
- `docs/index.md` line 66 makes the same claim.
- `docs/operator-guide/index.md` lines 85 and 127 list OpenSLO
  export as a wired-up observability surface.
- `docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md` is the dedicated walkthrough
  ("Bundled Alerting and OpenSLO Export"). It is flagged
  `Status: planned` but instructs deployers to use
  `lenny-ctl slo export --format openslo` "until the walkthrough lands"
  — the very command that does not exist.
- `docs/about/status.md` line 121 lists OpenSLO as
  "Prometheus alerting rules + OpenSLO + Grafana dashboard | In
  progress."

### Findings

### - [x] F-16.10.1 — (High) — OpenSLO export not implemented; the entire §16.10 surface is absent [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-16.5.12 — Both report the absent OpenSLO export surface (monitoring.openslo.enabled value and templates); F-16.5.12 records it as a deferred dependency of the same gap.

The §16.10 deliverable does not exist anywhere in the build. There is
no `monitoring.openslo.enabled` Helm value (R-001 fails), no rendered
ConfigMap or template (R-004 fails), no shared rendering code in
`pkg/alerting/rules` or `pkg/observability` (R-005 fails), and no SLO,
SLI, or AlertPolicy YAML emitted with the canonical metric names or
the `deployment_tier` label scaffolding (R-002 and R-003 cannot be
checked because there is no output to inspect). The full §16.5 SLO
catalog (R-006: Session creation success rate, Session creation
latency, TTFT, Session availability, Gateway availability, Startup
latency runc, Startup latency gVisor, Checkpoint duration) is unmapped
in any OpenSLO representation.

Spec authority: `spec/16_observability.md` lines 732–736 (§16.10) plus
the cross-reference at `spec/18_build-sequence.md` line 612 that
schedules the deliverable in Phase 13.

Evidence: zero `openslo`/`OpenSLO` matches in `pkg/`, `cmd/`, or
`charts/`; `charts/lenny/values.yaml` has no `monitoring.openslo` key;
`charts/lenny/templates/` has no OpenSLO template; `cmd/lenny-ctl`
has no `slo` subcommand; `pkg/observability/slo` (cited by
`tests/spec-map.json`) does not exist.

Severity: High. §16.10 is normative: the Helm chart MUST render
OpenSLO documents under the documented flag, sourced from the same
catalog as the §16.5 alerts. The deliverable is absent in a phase
(13) that is reported as Done.

**Resolution (3dd580f1):** Built the §16.10 OpenSLO export sourced from
the same §16.5 catalog as the alerts. New `pkg/alerting/rules/slo.go`
defines a canonical `SLODefinitions()` catalog (the 8 §16.5 SLOs with
target, budget-normalised burn-rate expr, runbook slug, and an OpenSLO
ratio SLI); `burnRateAlerts()` now derives from it (output byte-identical,
verified by `gen-alerting-rules -check`), so the export cannot drift
(R-005, R-006). `RenderOpenSLO` (`openslo.go`) renders each SLO as OpenSLO
v1 SLI + SLO + AlertPolicy documents referencing the canonical metric
names (R-002) and a `deployment_tier="<tier>"` matcher (R-003).
`gen-alerting-rules` emits `charts/lenny/files/openslo.yaml` (+ a tier1
docs reference); the new `openslo-configmap.yaml` template splices it into
a ConfigMap gated by `monitoring.openslo.enabled` (default false, R-001,
R-004), substituting `global.deploymentTier`. Added `lenny-ctl slo export`
and the `monitoring.openslo.*` values block. Resolved this batch.

### - [x] F-16.10.2 — (Medium) — Spec-map exception misroutes §16.10 to Phase 14.5; Phase 13 is reported Done with the deliverable missing [Medium] — CLOSED

`tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml` line 96 defers §16.10 to
"Wave 7 (Phase 14.5)." `spec/18_build-sequence.md` line 612 places
the OpenSLO export inside the Phase 13 "Observability catalog and
chart wiring" cluster, not Phase 14.5. Phase 14.5 in the same
document is "Post-hardening SLO re-validation," a load-test
re-baseline that does not include the OpenSLO renderer.

The mismatch lets Phase 13 close with a Done status while a Phase 13
deliverable (§16.10) is unbuilt. The build-plan exit gate for Wave 5
(which closed Phase 13) did not fail on the missing deliverable
because the exception file accounts for it under a later phase.

Spec authority: `spec/18_build-sequence.md` line 612.

Evidence: `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml` lines 96–98;
`BUILD-PROGRESS.md` Phase 13 row marked Done; Phase 14.5 row
described as `post_hardening_slo` load re-baseline.

Severity: Medium. The deferral is documented, so the build is not
silently regressing, but the cited phase number is wrong and the
deferral is operating as a permanent exemption rather than a tracked
gap.

**Resolution (3dd580f1):** Closed by F-16.10.1 landing the deliverable.
Removed the `16.10` deferral entry from `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml`
and repointed the `16.10` entry in `tests/spec-map.json` at the real
tests (`openslo_test.go`, `slo_test.go`, `openslo-configmap_test.yaml`)
and packages (`pkg/alerting/rules`, `cmd/gen-alerting-rules`, the chart
template), dropping `blocked_until_phase`. `lenny-test validate-maps`
spec-map coverage still passes (§16.10 now carries a test reference
rather than an exception). The phase-routing mismatch is moot now that
§16.10 is implemented and verified rather than deferred. Resolved this
batch.

### - [x] F-16.10.3 — (Medium) — `tests/spec-map.json` points at a non-existent package [Medium] — CLOSED

The §16.10 entry in `tests/spec-map.json` lists `pkg/observability/slo`
as the implementation package. That directory does not exist
(`find pkg -type d -name "*slo*"` returns only the unrelated
`pkg/gateway/slotcounter` package). The mapping has zero tests in
the `tests` list and a `blocked_until_phase: 14.5` field that
references the Phase-14.5 deferral.

A spec-map entry that lists a non-existent package is a maintenance
trap: the standard spec-coverage check
(`tests/spec-map-validator`-style) cannot verify that the package
exists, and a future operator who greps for `pkg/observability/slo`
will reach a dead end. The package path should either be created
(when F-001 is fixed) or removed and replaced with a deferral marker
that does not name a phantom directory.

Spec authority: §16.10 normative output requirements; spec-map
hygiene rules.

Evidence: `tests/spec-map.json` entry "16.10" (`"packages":
["pkg/observability/slo"]`); `pkg/observability/` directory listing
contains `metrics`, `tracing`, `correlation`, `audit`, `logging` and
no `slo` subdir.

Severity: Medium. Documentation hygiene rather than runtime
behavior, but the spec-map is the cross-check substrate that gates
the build's "every normative section maps to a test or an
exception" property.

**Resolution:** Removed `pkg/observability/slo` from the `packages` list of the §16.10 entry (and the §16.2 entry, which named the same phantom directory) in `tests/spec-map.json`, setting both to `[]`. The `blocked_until_phase: "14.5"` field plus the expanded `notes` now serve as the deferral marker — the notes state that no implementation package exists yet and that Phase 14.5 creates and names it. `lenny-test validate-maps` keeps passing (`spec-map paths: every spec_file resolves`); the validator does not require `packages` entries to exist, so the empty list is clean. Resolved this batch.

### - [x] F-16.10.4 — (Medium) — Customer-facing documentation advertises an OpenSLO export and a `lenny-ctl slo` command that do not exist [Medium] — CLOSED

`README.md` line 81 and `docs/index.md` line 66 advertise that "Prometheus
alerting rules and OpenSLO definitions drop into any standard
observability stack." `docs/operator-guide/index.md` lines 85 and 127
list OpenSLO export as a wired-up observability surface that operators
should expect to use. `docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md`
instructs deployers — under the page title "Bundled Alerting and
OpenSLO Export" — to use `lenny-ctl slo export --format openslo` and
`lenny-ctl slo validate --config lenny-slos.yaml` "until the
walkthrough lands."

Neither the OpenSLO export nor the `lenny-ctl slo` subcommand
exists. The walkthrough is labeled `Status: planned` but the four
other doc pages do not carry that qualifier and read as descriptions
of shipping behavior. An operator who follows the operator-guide will
look in the rendered chart for OpenSLO objects and find none, and
will type `lenny-ctl slo` and get `unknown command "slo"`.

`docs/about/status.md` line 121 is the only doc that correctly marks
the surface as "In progress."

This finding is the doc-sync companion to F-001: closing F-001 closes
the gap; meanwhile the docs should either land the qualifier
("planned" or "in progress") or be aligned with the absent
implementation.

Spec authority: doc-sync rule (`MEMORY.md`
`feedback_docs_sync_after_spec_changes.md`).

Evidence: `README.md` line 81; `docs/index.md` line 66;
`docs/operator-guide/index.md` lines 85, 127;
`docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md` lines 9, 14, 24, 26;
`docs/about/status.md` line 121.

Severity: Medium. Customer-facing claim that misrepresents the
shipped surface.

**Resolution:** Aligned the four doc pages with the deferred implementation (F-16.10.1, still OPEN). `README.md` and `docs/index.md` now state that the Prometheus alerting rules ship today and that OpenSLO export "is planned and does not ship yet"; `docs/operator-guide/index.md` (both the chapter list and the Day-1 checklist) drops OpenSLO from the shipping-surface list and marks it planned. The `docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md` callout no longer tells operators to run `lenny-ctl slo export` as if it works — it states plainly that the export and the `lenny-ctl slo` command are planned and that running `lenny-ctl slo` returns `unknown command "slo"`, and the body's OpenSLO claim is reworded to future tense. `docs/about/status.md` already marked the surface "In progress". Verified the absence: no `slo` subcommand exists (only an alert-annotation key) and no chart renders OpenSLO objects. The docs now describe shipping behavior accurately; the export itself stays tracked under F-16.10.1. Resolved this batch.

## §17.1 Kubernetes Resources <a id="17.1"></a>
Spec source: `spec/17_deployment-topology.md` lines 3–22 (the §17.1
table). Implementation surveyed under `charts/lenny/templates/`,
`charts/lenny/crds/`, `pkg/apis/lenny/v1/`, `cmd/lenny-controller/`,
and the chart test suite under `charts/lenny/tests/`.

### Method

Enumerated each normative row of the §17.1 component table and grepped
the chart, CRD, and Go source for the corresponding resource kind,
name, or wiring evidence. Confirmed presence and posture against the
spec text. Counted documents emitted by chart-test `hasDocuments`
assertions to bound the rendered inventory per template.

### Summary scoreboard

| §17.1 row | Resources expected | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway | Deployment + Service + Ingress + HPA + PDB + preStop + topology spread | Partial: Deployment, two Services, HPA present; **Ingress**, **PDB**, **preStop**, **topology spread**, **rolling-update strategy** missing |
| Token Service | Deployment + Service + PDB | Present (Deployment, Service, PDB `minAvailable: 1`) |
| Warm Pool Controller | Deployment + leader election | Present (`lenny-controller` Deployment, ClusterRole, Lease RBAC) |
| PoolScalingController | Separate Deployment + leader election | **Not deployed** as a separate workload |
| Agent Pods | Sandbox CRD owner; PoolManager via `kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox` | Sandbox CRD present; PoolManager interface and `kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox` integration absent |
| Postgres / Redis / MinIO | BYO / external | BYO honored; `lenny-datastore-conn` Secret wires connection values |
| `lenny-ops` | Deployment + Service + Ingress + PDB | Partial: Deployment + Service present; **Ingress** and **PDB** missing |
| `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service | `clusterIP: None` per-replica DNS | Present |
| `lenny-backup` Jobs | Transient Jobs scheduled by `lenny-ops`; `lenny-backup-sa` | `lenny-restore-test` CronJob present; **`lenny-backup-sa`** not rendered; no on-demand backup-job template wired to `lenny-ops` |
| NetworkPolicies (named in §17.1) | `lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress`, `lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller`, `lenny-ops-egress`, `lenny-backup-job` | **None of the named policies render**; only `default-deny-all` + `allow-ops` exist |
| Admission / Lease | `lenny-ops-leader` Lease at runtime; RBAC for `leases.coordination.k8s.io` | Present (RBAC in `ops-deployment.yaml`); Lease created by binary |
| ServiceMonitor / PodMonitor / PrometheusRule (or ConfigMap) | `monitoring.format` gated | Present (ServiceMonitor, PodMonitor, PrometheusRule with `monitoring.format` branching) |
| Secrets (chart-rendered) | `lenny-backup-postgres`, `lenny-backup-minio`, optional `lenny-ops-tls` | **None of the named secrets render**; only `lenny-datastore-conn` |

### Findings

### - [x] F-17.1.1 — 01 — Gateway PodDisruptionBudget is not rendered [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.4.4, F-17.3.2, F-4.1.1 — Four members report the gateway Deployment renders no PodDisruptionBudget; F-4.1.12 covers only the separate topology-spread gap.

Spec row 7 (`spec/17_deployment-topology.md:7`) is explicit:
"**PodDisruptionBudget**: `maxUnavailable: 1` at **every tier** (hard
ceiling of one concurrent voluntary eviction regardless of replica
count)." The same row also requires `maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 25%`
as the rolling-update strategy. The rationale span ties the flat PDB
to checkpoint fan-out bounds and to the HPA scale-down rate.

The chart renders a Deployment, two Services, an HPA/ScaledObject, but
no `PodDisruptionBudget` and no `spec.strategy` block. Verified by:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` (no `kind: PodDisruptionBudget`, no `strategy:`).
- `grep -rn "PodDisruptionBudget" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/` returns matches only for `token-service`, the admission webhooks, and the `cosign-verify-webhook`.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` asserts `hasDocuments: count: 6` (ServiceAccount, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Deployment, gateway Service, headless Service) — no slot for a PDB.

Consequence: a Tier 3 `kubectl drain` of any node hosting more than one
gateway pod will violate the spec ceiling on concurrent voluntary
evictions; the HPA scale-down rate that §17.1 pins to "1 pod / 60s"
because the PDB is the binding limit has no backing PDB to bind it.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-10.4.4. The chart renders `kind: PodDisruptionBudget` (gated on `gateway.podDisruptionBudget.enabled`, defaulting true) with `maxUnavailable: 1`, and the rolling-update strategy is also rendered with `maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 25%` per `gateway.rollingUpdate`. The metric emitter for `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total` is wired via `pkg/gateway/pdbwatcher`.

### - [x] F-17.1.2 — 02 — Gateway Ingress is not rendered [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec row 7 begins "Deployment + Service + Ingress". The chart renders
no `kind: Ingress` for the gateway. `values.yaml` carries
`ingressControllerNamespace: "ingress-nginx"` and the
`allow-gateway-ingress` NetworkPolicy targets the configured ingress
controller namespace, but the Ingress object itself is absent.
External clients reaching the gateway must therefore bring their own
Ingress definition, which is not stated in §17.1 or in the chart
values.

Verified: `grep -rn "kind: Ingress" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/`
returns no matches.

**Resolution:** New `gateway-ingress.yaml` renders a `networking.k8s.io/v1`
Ingress routing external HTTPS to the `lenny-gateway` Service's named
`http` port. Opt-in via the new `gateway.ingress` values block
(`enabled`/`className`/`host`/`path`/`pathType`/`annotations`/`tls`),
matching the opt-in posture of `gateway.topologySpread`; a stock render
emits nothing. Host-less rules and an absent TLS secret degrade
gracefully. F-17.1.2 (commit c625edae).

### - [x] F-17.1.3 — 03 — `lenny-ops` Ingress and PDB are not rendered [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.16.1, F-25.2.11 — Two distinct gaps recur: the lenny-ops Ingress (with PDB) is not rendered, and the four lenny-ops/lenny-backup NetworkPolicies are not rendered; F-17.1.2 is the separate gateway-Ingress gap.

Spec row 15 is explicit: "Deployment + Service + Ingress + PDB" and
"PDB `minAvailable: 1`". §17.8.5 (`spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1323`)
restates that the canonical layout includes "the PodDisruptionBudget
`lenny-ops`". `cmd/lenny-ops` is the operability control plane, and
§18 Phase 3.5 (`spec/18_build-sequence.md:205`) names "Deployment,
Service, Ingress, PodDisruptionBudget, the four NetworkPolicies, the
`lenny-backup-sa` ServiceAccount, and the `lenny-ops-leader` Lease" as
the first-deploy set.

The chart renders `lenny-ops` Deployment, Service, ServiceAccount,
leader-election Role and RoleBinding (`hasDocuments: count: 5` in
`tests/ops-deployment_test.yaml`). It does **not** render a PDB or an
Ingress. Verified by:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` (no `kind: PodDisruptionBudget`, no `kind: Ingress`).
- `grep -rn "PodDisruptionBudget" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` returns nothing.

The runbooks in §25 assume the operability surface is reachable
externally for `lenny-ctl`. Without an Ingress chart artifact the
external surface depends on operator-supplied wiring; without a PDB
`kubectl drain` may take both ops replicas concurrently and stall
leader election plus webhook delivery for the full
`terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed; the evidence grep was stale because both objects live in a dedicated `ops-ingress.yaml`, not `ops-deployment.yaml`. `charts/lenny/templates/ops-ingress.yaml` (commit c08e1be1) renders the `lenny-ops` Ingress opt-in via `ops.ingress.enabled` (with the §25.4 SSE proxy-timeout/affinity annotations) and the `lenny-ops` PodDisruptionBudget unconditionally with `minAvailable: 1` (§25.4 line 1316). `charts/lenny/tests/ops-ingress_test.yaml` asserts the PDB renders regardless of replica count and the Ingress on opt-in.

### - [x] F-17.1.4 — 04 — Four `lenny-ops`/`lenny-backup` NetworkPolicies named in §17.1 do not render [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.2.16, F-25.4.12 — Two distinct gaps recur: the lenny-ops Ingress (with PDB) is not rendered, and the four lenny-ops/lenny-backup NetworkPolicies are not rendered; F-17.1.2 is the separate gateway-Ingress gap.

Spec row 18 enumerates four policies the chart MUST render:
`lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress`, `lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller`,
`lenny-ops-egress`, `lenny-backup-job`. The same row references
`ingress.controllerNamespace` and `ingress.controllerLabel` values
that the allow-from-ingress-controller policy is supposed to honor.

`grep -rn "lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress\|lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller\|lenny-ops-egress\|lenny-backup-job" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/`
returns no matches. The implementation collapses the requirement into
a single `allow-ops` NetworkPolicy in `system-network-policies.yaml`
plus the namespace-wide `default-deny-all`; the names called out in
§17.1 do not exist, the `ingress.controllerNamespace` /
`ingress.controllerLabel` value pair does not exist (the chart uses a
flat `ingressControllerNamespace` value), and there is no chart slot
for a `lenny-backup-job` policy at all.

Consequence: the `lenny-preflight` enumeration check described in §17.9
would have nothing to match against if it ever audited these
NetworkPolicy names; the runbook scripts that reference the named
policies cannot operate. Cross-link: `spec-reviews/.../iter5/p19_build.md`
and `iter6/p19_build.md` both flagged this as the §17.2 canonical
layout the chart must always render.

**Resolution (commit c08e1be1):** Closed by **F-25.4.12**. All four named policies now render: `lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress` (existing, F-17.2.16) plus the new `lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller`, `lenny-ops-egress`, and `lenny-backup-job` in `charts/lenny/templates/ops-network-policies.yaml`. The allow-from-ingress policy honors the chart's `ingressControllerNamespace` + `ingress.controllerPodLabel` value pair.

### - [x] F-17.1.5 — 05 — `lenny-backup-sa` ServiceAccount and the on-demand `lenny-backup` Job template are not rendered [High] — CLOSED

Spec row 17: "Transient Jobs using the `lenny-backup` image for
Postgres/MinIO backup, restore, and verification … ServiceAccount
`lenny-backup-sa` (distinct from `lenny-ops-sa`)." §17.8.5 and §25.4
both restate the `lenny-backup-sa` requirement as part of the
unconditional Phase-3.5 layout. §25 (`spec/25_agent-operability.md:3992`)
specifies the `lenny-backup-sa` RBAC envelope ("`get`/`list` on CRDs in
the cluster and `get` on ConfigMaps in `lenny-system`").

`grep -rn "lenny-backup-sa" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/`
returns no matches. The chart ships a `lenny-restore-test` CronJob
(`restore-test-cronjob.yaml`) with its own SA, ClusterRole, Role, and
RoleBinding, but the ServiceAccount the spec names — the one
`lenny-ops` is supposed to use when it schedules backup, restore, and
verify Jobs against `ops_backup_schedule` — is not provisioned, and no
chart-rendered Job template or `lenny-ops`-owned Job factory exists
yet. The `lenny-backup` image is built (`cmd/lenny-backup` exists) but
nothing wires it into the cluster.

**Resolution (commit 21e42088):** New `charts/lenny/templates/backup-job.yaml` renders the `lenny-backup-sa` ServiceAccount unconditionally (part of the §17.8.5 mandatory core inventory) plus the §25-narrowed RBAC envelope: a ClusterRole granting `get`/`list` on `customresourcedefinitions` and `lenny.dev/*` (the backup flow's CRD/CR export), a release-namespace Role granting `get` on `configmaps`, and no Pod/Deployment/Secret read. An opt-in on-demand Job (`backups.onDemand.enabled`, default false so a stock render and every `helm upgrade` run no backup) executes the `lenny-backup` image with the §25.11 Job Pod Specification — `restartPolicy: Never`, `backoffLimit: 3`, `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600`, `activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200`, non-root, read-only rootfs, `/tmp` emptyDir — sourcing credentials from the `lenny-backup-postgres`/`lenny-backup-minio` Secrets (F-17.1.10). `lenny-ops` remains the production Job factory for scheduled runs. Covered by `charts/lenny/tests/backup-job_test.yaml` (7 helm-unittest cases).

### - [x] F-17.1.6 — 06 — `PoolScalingController` is not deployed as a separate workload [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-4.6.1, F-5.2.11 — All three describe the implemented PoolScalingController not being wired into the production controller binary.

Spec row 10: "PoolScalingController — Deployment (2+ replicas, leader
election) — Reconciles pool config from Postgres into CRDs; manages
scaling intelligence." §4.6.1
(`spec/04_system-components.md:388,414`) and §4.6.2 both require it to
run as its own Deployment with a dedicated lease
`lenny-pool-scaling-controller`, with pod anti-affinity from the WPC
leader to bound the simultaneous-failover blast radius.

The chart renders exactly one controller Deployment (`lenny-controller`,
`charts/lenny/templates/controller-deployment.yaml`). `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go`
imports only `pkg/controller/warmpool`, `pkg/controller/sandbox`, and
`pkg/controller/cidrdrift`; it does not import `pkg/controller/poolscaling`.
`grep -rn "poolscaling\." /Users/joan/projects/lenny --include="*.go"`
finds the package's own tests only — no non-test importer. The
PoolScalingController code lives under
`pkg/controller/poolscaling/` but no binary runs it and no chart
artifact backs it.

Consequence: scaling-intelligence reconciliation against Postgres,
SDK-warm circuit-breaker management, and the
`scaleToZero`/`PoolScalingController`-owned status fields enumerated in
the SandboxWarmPool CRD (`charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxwarmpools.yaml`
lines 40, 64, 139, 147, 164, 242, 250, 255) have no running owner. The
CRD field-ownership boundary §4.6.3 documents is unenforced because the
controller is absent.

- **Resolution:** Closed by F-4.6.1 (commit 627d3cc6). The PSC now ships as its own `lenny-pool-scaling-controller` Deployment (2 replicas, dedicated leader-election lease, podAntiAffinity preferring scheduling away from the `lenny-controller` WPC) with a ServiceAccount and RBAC backing it; `charts/lenny/tests/pool-scaling-controller_test.yaml` locks the workload identity and CRD grants.

## §17.2 Namespace Layout <a id="17.2"></a>
Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/17_deployment-topology.md` lines 23–108.

### Scope and method

Enumerated the normative requirements in §17.2:

- Namespace layout: `lenny-system`, `lenny-agents`, `lenny-agents-kata`.
- `lenny-ops` in `{Release.Namespace}`; `lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress` NetworkPolicy plus per-namespace egress defaults.
- Split PSS enforcement (full Restricted for runc, RuntimeClass-relaxed for gVisor/Kata) implemented via OPA/Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate or Kyverno ClusterPolicy.
- The thirteen webhooks/policies enumerated under `templates/admission-policies/`.
- Five-item baseline (`lenny-label-immutability`, `lenny-sandboxclaim-guard`, `lenny-pool-config-validator`, `lenny-crd-conversion`, `lenny-ephemeral-container-cred-guard`) plus three feature-flag-gated additions (`features.llmProxy`, `features.drainReadiness`, `features.compliance`).
- HA contract on every rendered webhook: `replicas: 2`, `podDisruptionBudget.minAvailable: 1`, `failurePolicy: Fail`, canonical `lenny.dev/component: admission-webhook` pod label.
- Drain-readiness additive `lenny.dev/webhook-name: drain-readiness` label per NET-068 narrow egress.
- Feature-flag downgrade enforcement at four cooperating layers: phase-stamp ConfigMap, fail-closed chart render-time validation, `lenny-preflight` mismatch check, runtime `AdmissionPlaneFeatureFlagDowngrade` alert with per-(flag, webhook) rule decomposition and `kube-state-metrics --metric-labels-allowlist=configmaps=[lenny.dev/flag-*]` operator configuration.
- Elicitation content integrity floor key co-tenant on the phase-stamp ConfigMap.
- Pod Security Admission labels `pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted` and `pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted` on agent namespaces.
- Kata node isolation: RuntimeClass `scheduling.nodeSelector`, controller-injected required `nodeAffinity`, dedicated-node taint `lenny.dev/isolation=kata:NoSchedule`.
- `ResourceQuota` and `LimitRange` per agent namespace; preflight verifies both.
- Four named integration test suites.

Cross-checked against:

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/agent-network-policies.yaml`

### Findings

### - [x] F-17.2.1 — 2-1  Kata node isolation enforcement absent [High] — CLOSED
**Spec requirement** (§17.2 "Node isolation," lines 97–102): Kata (`microvm`) pods must run on dedicated node pools with all three of: (1) RuntimeClass `scheduling.nodeSelector` (e.g., `lenny.dev/node-pool: kata`); (2) controller-injected `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` `nodeAffinity` matching the same label; (3) dedicated-node taint `lenny.dev/isolation=kata:NoSchedule` honored via toleration on the pod.

**Implementation:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` contains no `kind: RuntimeClass` template; `kata-microvm` is referenced in spec but never rendered. `pkg/sandbox/isolation/runtimeclass.go` returns the string `"kata"` for the `microvm` profile, but the cluster-scoped resource is not deployed.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/podspec.go` `basePod` sets only `RuntimeClassName`, `RestartPolicy`, `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds`, and `SecurityContext`. No `nodeAffinity` or `tolerations` are added for Kata pods (search of the file confirms no occurrences of `nodeSelector`, `Affinity`, `Toleration`, or `node-pool`).
- No template adds the `lenny.dev/isolation=kata:NoSchedule` taint to nodes or surfaces a values key for taint enforcement.

**Impact:** All three required controls for the "kernel compromise via runc escape on a shared node" boundary called out in §17.2 are missing. Kata pods can land on shared nodes and non-Kata workloads can land on hypothetical Kata-dedicated hardware, violating the spec's core isolation invariant.

**Resolution:** All three §17.2 lines 97-101 controls now render. The "no `kind: RuntimeClass` template" evidence was stale (`charts/lenny/templates/runtimeclasses.yaml` already exists and supports `scheduling.nodeSelector`); the gaps were the unset nodeSelector default and the absent controller injection. Control 1: the chart's `microvm` RuntimeClass profile now defaults `nodeSelector: {lenny.dev/node-pool: kata}`, so the rendered Kata RuntimeClass carries `scheduling.nodeSelector` and constrains every referencing pod at admission. Controls 2 and 3: `podspec.applyKataNodeIsolation` (mirroring the existing `applyT4NodeIsolation` pattern) injects a `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` node affinity matching `lenny.dev/node-pool: kata` (ANDed idempotently into every node-selector term) and the `lenny.dev/isolation=kata:NoSchedule` toleration onto every pod whose resolved isolation profile is `microvm`. Standard/sandboxed pods are untouched. Commit bd30d1ed.

### - [x] F-17.2.2 — 2-2  PSS enforcement is in-tree webhook, not OPA/Gatekeeper or Kyverno [High] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: medium) — F-6.1.15, F-6.4.8 — F-6.4.8 and F-6.1.15 both note shareProcessNamespace:true is enforced only by the in-tree webhook with no Kyverno/Gatekeeper policy; F-17.2.2 is the broader PSS-enforcement-model gap (full Restricted/RuntimeClass-relaxed policies absent).

**Spec requirement** (§17.2 lines 35–40, items 1–2 of the inventory): The split PSS enforcement model uses "OPA/Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate or Kyverno ClusterPolicy" — full Restricted for runc, RuntimeClass-relaxed for gVisor and Kata. Item 4 ("Label-based namespace targeting via `.Values.agentNamespaces`") scopes those policies to Lenny-managed namespaces.

**Implementation:** No Gatekeeper or Kyverno templates exist. `grep -rn "gatekeeper\|kyverno\|Constraint\|ClusterPolicy"` against `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` returns no matches. The chart ships `lenny-pod-security` (an in-process Lenny-authored ValidatingAdmissionWebhook in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/pod-security-webhook.yaml`) that wraps `pkg/podsecurity` and applies the §13.1 baseline regardless of RuntimeClass. The RuntimeClass-aware split (full Restricted on runc vs. relaxed on gVisor/Kata) is not implemented; the existing webhook applies the same rules to every pod, irrespective of RuntimeClass.

**Impact:** The "RuntimeClass-aware admission policy webhook (OPA/Gatekeeper or Kyverno)" called out elsewhere in the spec and in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` description text does not exist. The relaxed enforcement for gVisor/Kata mandated by §17.2 (waiving `seccompType: RuntimeDefault` and certain `allowPrivilegeEscalation` constraints) is not implemented — every pod is held to the same in-process check.

**Resolution (commit `c3ba0d59`):** Two-part fix. (a) The "applies the same rules to every pod, irrespective of RuntimeClass" evidence is **stale**: the in-tree `lenny-pod-security` webhook is already RuntimeClass-aware. `pkg/podsecurity.RuntimeClassPolicy.relaxations` exempts a gVisor pod from the seccomp check and a Kata pod from the privilege-escalation check, `cmd/lenny-webhook/main.go` builds the policy from `--gvisor-runtime-class` / `--kata-runtime-class` (defaulting to the chart's profile names), and `pkg/admission/webhook/pod_security.go` threads it into `ValidateAgentPod`. (b) The genuinely-missing half — the policy-engine manifest the §17.2 inventory names (items 1, 2, 4) — now ships as `charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/kyverno-pod-security-runtimeclass-policy.yaml`, a Kyverno `ClusterPolicy` (`lenny-pod-security-runtimeclass`) with three `validate.podSecurity` rules: full Restricted PSS for runc (and any non-gVisor/non-Kata `runtimeClassName`), Restricted-minus-Seccomp for the gVisor class, and Restricted-minus-Privilege-Escalation for the Kata class. RuntimeClass names come from `runtimeClasses.profiles.{sandboxed,microvm}.name` — the exact values the webhook flags read, so the policy-engine layer and the webhook never diverge — and the gVisor/Kata rules (plus the runc NotEquals preconditions) drop out when their name is empty, mirroring `relaxations`. The policy is `failurePolicy: Fail` + `validationFailureAction: Enforce` per §17.2 line 88, namespace-scoped via the `lenny.dev/agent-namespace` label (item 4), and gated behind the existing `admissionPolicies.kyverno` block (Kyverno is an operator-supplied external dependency, same convention as the existing share-process-namespace and agent-SA Kyverno policies). Gatekeeper users configure equivalent ConstraintTemplates per the in-template note. The `shareProcessNamespace` half of the medium-confidence overlap (F-6.1.15, F-6.4.8) was already CLOSED by the existing `kyverno-share-process-namespace-policy.yaml`. Tests: 9 helm-unittest cases (render gating, fail-closed posture, per-RuntimeClass exclusions, namespace scoping, name overrides, empty-Kata-name rule drop).

### - [x] F-17.2.3 — 2-3  lenny-label-immutability webhook scoped to pods, but labels are stamped on the Sandbox CR [High] — CLOSED
**Spec requirement** (§17.2 line 46, item 5): The webhook enforces immutability of `lenny.dev/managed`, `lenny.dev/delivery-mode`, `lenny.dev/egress-profile`, and `lenny.dev/tenant-id` "on agent pods."

**Implementation:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/label-immutability-webhook.yaml` lines 28–33 scopes to `resources: ["pods"]`, `apiGroups: [""]`, `apiVersions: ["v1"]`, `operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]`.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/warmpool/controller.go` lines 254–257 stamps only `LabelPool` (`lenny.dev/pool`) and `LabelManaged` (`lenny.dev/managed`) on the Sandbox CR (not pod).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/sandbox/controller.go` line 180 passes `sb.Labels` to `podspec.Build`, so the Pod inherits the same two labels. `lenny.dev/delivery-mode`, `lenny.dev/egress-profile`, and `lenny.dev/tenant-id` are never written to the Pod's `metadata.labels` by any controller-generated path.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/podclaim/slotclaimer.go` lines 403–415 stamps `lenny.dev/tenant-id` on the **Sandbox** (`labelPatch` of type `lennyv1.Sandbox`), not the Pod.

**Impact:** The webhook is in place but its rules apply to pod label transitions that never occur, because the labels live on the Sandbox CR. The "immutable agent-pod label" guarantee called out in §17.2 / §5.2 NET-003 does not bind at the pod layer. A controller that writes a Pod with arbitrary tenant or delivery-mode labels bypasses the gate. Either the controllers must stamp the labels onto Pods at creation, or the webhook must extend to the `lenny.dev/v1` `sandboxes` resource (and the rendering test at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/tests/admission-webhooks_test.yaml` lines 61–67 should track that pivot).

The evidence was partly stale: `lenny.dev/delivery-mode` and `lenny.dev/egress-profile` already reach the pod via `sb.Labels` at pod creation (`warmpool.sandboxLabels` → `podspec.Build`, added by F-13.2.1 / F-13.2.11). The one residual gap was `lenny.dev/tenant-id`, set on the Sandbox at slot-claim time (after the pod already exists) and never propagated to the pod. New `podclaim.stampPodTenant` JSON-merge-patches the pin onto the agent pod as the gateway ServiceAccount (the one principal the `lenny-tenant-label-immutability` webhook authorizes for the `unset → {tenant_id}` edge per §5.2 line 392), tolerating a NotFound/Conflict so a terminating-or-unmaterialized pod never fails the claim. Wired into both warm-pod assignment paths — `Claimer.Claim` (session mode) and `SlotClaimer.reserveSlot` (concurrent/task) — so the pod-scoped webhook now sees the transition it guards. The `{tenant_id} → unassigned` return-to-pool reset is part of the §5.2 cross-tenant-reuse (task-mode) path that is itself absent (F-5.2.1) and rides on it. Tests: tier-2 podclaim (slot-claim + session-claim stamp the pod, idempotent re-stamp, missing-pod tolerated).

### - [x] F-17.2.7 — 2-7  Fail-closed chart render-time downgrade guard absent (spec layer 2) [High] — CLOSED
**Spec requirement** (§17.2 lines 76, "Fail-closed chart render-time validation"): On every `helm install`/`helm upgrade`, a pre-render template function reads the phase-stamp ConfigMap via `lookup` and fails the render with error `PHASE_STAMP_FEATURE_FLAG_DOWNGRADE` if any flag recorded with `enabled: true` is being rendered as `false`.

**Implementation:** `grep -rn "PHASE_STAMP_FEATURE_FLAG_DOWNGRADE"` against `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts` returns nothing. The chart's phase-stamp template (`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/phase-stamp-configmap.yaml`) reads the existing ConfigMap via `lookup` (line 19) only to preserve `enabledAt` timestamps; it never compares the prior `enabled: true` state against the incoming render values, and never raises a `fail` action.

**Impact:** Layer 2 of the four-layer downgrade defense is missing entirely. In the `helm install`/`helm upgrade` code path the spec relies on this layer as the first fail-closed gate; without it the preflight Job (layer 3) is the only gate, and the spec's "render-time fail-closed gate before the upgrade reaches the cluster" guarantee is unmet.

**Resolution:** Closed by commit 26732665. `phase-stamp-configmap.yaml` (the pre-install/pre-upgrade hook that already reads the live ConfigMap via `lookup`) now compares each recorded-enabled admission-plane flag (`llmProxy`, `drainReadiness`, `compliance`) against the incoming `features.<flag>` render value and calls `fail "PHASE_STAMP_FEATURE_FLAG_DOWNGRADE: …"` when a recorded-enabled flag is being disabled without `acceptFeatureFlagDowngrade.<flag>=true`. The acknowledgement override matches the layer-3 `pkg/preflight.CheckPhaseStamp` semantics so an acknowledged downgrade passes both gates. Because Helm `lookup` returns nil under `helm template`/helm-unittest, the layer-2 fail path cannot be driven without a live cluster; its identical comparison semantics are tested by the layer-3 Go check, and the no-prior render no-op is asserted in `phase-stamp-configmap_test.yaml`.

**Implementation:**

### - [x] F-17.2.12 — 2-12  Implementation baseline contains `lenny-pod-security`, not listed in §17.2 inventory [Medium] — CLOSED
**Spec requirement** (§17.2 lines 42–54): The thirteen-item enumeration under `templates/admission-policies/` is the "canonical enumeration for every admission gate shipped by Lenny." Chart authors "must cross-check this list against the rendered manifests." The Phase 3.5 baseline (line 82) is exactly: `lenny-label-immutability`, `lenny-sandboxclaim-guard`, `lenny-pool-config-validator`, `lenny-crd-conversion`, `lenny-ephemeral-container-cred-guard`.

**Implementation:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/preflight/webhooks.go` lines 15–21 declares the baseline as `lenny-label-immutability`, `lenny-sandboxclaim-guard`, `lenny-pool-config-validator`, `lenny-ephemeral-container-cred-guard`, **`lenny-pod-security`** (replacing the missing `lenny-crd-conversion`). `lenny-pod-security` and `lenny-registry-digest` are also rendered (the former unconditionally, the latter under `platform.registry.requireDigest`) but are not listed in §17.2 items 1–13. `lenny-cosign-verify` is also rendered under `imageVerification.cosign.enabled` and tracked in the preflight expected set, but it is not catalogued in §17.2 either.

**Impact:** The spec's "single source of truth" cross-check is broken in three directions — the spec enumerates a baseline item (`lenny-crd-conversion`) the chart does not deploy (Finding 17.2-4); the chart deploys baseline items (`lenny-pod-security`) and conditional items (`lenny-registry-digest`, `lenny-cosign-verify`) the spec does not enumerate; and the preflight's baseline set diverges from §17.2's baseline set. §17.2 needs to either acknowledge these implementation-only webhooks or the preflight inventory needs to track the spec catalogue.

### - [x] F-17.2.14 — 2-14  lenny-direct-mode-isolation scopes only to sandboxtemplates, spec mentions "pools/pods" [Medium] — CLOSED
**Spec requirement** (§17.2 line 47, item 6): The webhook "rejects pools/pods whose configuration combines either (a) `deliveryMode: direct` with `isolationProfile: standard`, or (b) `deliveryMode: proxy` with `spiffeBinding: disabled`, when `tenancy.mode: multi` is set."

**Implementation:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/direct-mode-isolation-webhook.yaml` lines 33–38 scopes only to `apiGroups: ["lenny.dev"]`, `resources: ["sandboxtemplates"]`. `SandboxWarmPool` (the "pool") and `Pod` are not in the resource list. The decision logic (`/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/admission/direct_mode_isolation/guard.go`) is generic enough to apply to either, and the package comment (line 7) says it covers "SandboxTemplate and CredentialPool resources" — but the chart wires only sandboxtemplates.

**Impact:** A pool definition (`SandboxWarmPool`) or a credential pool that combines the forbidden settings can bypass the webhook because the chart's rule does not match those resources. Spec's "pools/pods" promise is partially met (templates only).

**Resolution:** Verify-closed by commit 26732665 (no bypass exists; the proposed fix would be inert, so it was not applied — rule O). The credential-delivery fields the guard inspects (`deliveryMode`, `isolationProfile`, `spiffeBinding`, `egressProfile`) are authored only on `SandboxTemplateSpec`. `SandboxWarmPoolSpec` carries none of them — it references a template by name via `templateRef` (`pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxwarmpool_types.go:123`), and there is no `CredentialPool` CRD admitted by this webhook. The per-session `Sandbox` CR carries `deliveryMode`/`isolationProfile` only as a controller-produced copy-down from an already-validated template (created by `pkg/controller/sandbox`, `pkg/podregistry`, `pkg/gateway/podclaim` — never by an operator). Core Pods carry no `lenny.dev` delivery fields. So `SandboxTemplate` is the only admitted resource that can carry a forbidden combination; adding `SandboxWarmPool` or `Pod` to the rule list would create rules with no fields to inspect. The stale guard package comment (`pkg/admission/direct_mode_isolation/guard.go`) that claimed "SandboxTemplate and CredentialPool resources" and feature-flag gating was corrected to document why the sandboxtemplates-only scope is complete.

## §17.3 Disaster Recovery <a id="17.3"></a>
Scope: §17.3 in `spec/17_deployment-topology.md` (lines 110–140) is a thin
human-operator summary that explicitly delegates the canonical
API-driven recovery surface to §25.11 (Backup and Restore API). The
audit therefore checks the §17.3 normative bullets — RPO/RTO targets,
cross-zone requirements, backup schedule, restore-testing, agent-
operability recovery paths — against the implementation under
`pkg/backup/`, `pkg/ops/backup/`, `cmd/lenny-backup/`,
`pkg/blobstore/replication/`, `charts/lenny/templates/`, and
`docs/runbooks/`.

The §25.11 surface that §17.3 inherits is partially specified but
overwhelmingly unwired: the BackupService API contract and types are
implemented; the orchestrator runs against in-memory fakes; the
lenny-backup binary cannot perform a restore or a test-restore; the
ArtifactStore replication controller is fully implemented but never
instantiated by lenny-ops; the post-restore GDPR erasure reconciler
referenced by §17.3 is absent; the §17.3 cross-zone Gateway PDB +
topology-spread requirement is not rendered in the chart; and the
operational runbooks §17.3 implies (backup overdue, backup failed,
restore failed, ArtifactStore replication lag, residency violation,
post-restore reconcile blocked) do not exist.

---

### - [x] F-17.3.1 — MUST / correctness / security [High] — CLOSED

**Resolution:** Section-marker heading with no actionable body; the individual MUST-class §17.3 findings are tracked at F-17.3.2 through F-17.3.9. Closed as a placeholder heading (same disposition as F-15.1.1 / F-17.3.10).

### - [x] F-17.3.2 — 3.1 — Gateway Deployment has no topology spread or PodDisruptionBudget [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-10.4.4, F-17.1.1, F-4.1.1 — Four members report the gateway Deployment renders no PodDisruptionBudget; F-4.1.12 covers only the separate topology-spread gap.

Spec — §17.3 "Cross-zone requirements":
> Gateway: replicas spread via topology spread constraints

Spec — §17.3 "Zone failure blast radius":
> Gateway: surviving replicas absorb traffic (PDB ensures minimum availability)

Implementation — `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml`
(301 lines, full file inspected): no `topologySpreadConstraints`, no
`podAntiAffinity`, and no `PodDisruptionBudget`. The chart-wide search
also shows no PDB resource anywhere (`grep -rn "kind: PodDisruptionBudget"
charts/lenny/templates/` returns only the cosign / data-residency
admission webhook templates, none for the gateway). `charts/lenny/
presets/values-tier3.yaml` does not override either.

Effect: a single-zone outage at Tier 3 can deschedule every gateway
replica because the scheduler is free to colocate them onto one
zone, and any node-drain / voluntary disruption can take them all
down because no PDB caps simultaneous evictions. The §17.3
"surviving replicas absorb traffic" property is not enforceable.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-10.4.4 / F-10.4.8. The chart renders the gateway PDB (`gateway.podDisruptionBudget` default `enabled: true`, `maxUnavailable: 1`), plus opt-in `gateway.topologySpread` and `gateway.podAntiAffinity` helm values that the tier-3 preset enables. The `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total` emitter lands via `pkg/gateway/pdbwatcher`.
