3. Only the digest-enforcement admission gate references `platform.registry.requireDigest` (`templates/admission-policies/registry-digest-webhook.yaml:15`); no template references `platform.registry.url`, `platform.registry.overrides`, or `platform.registry.pullSecretName`.

Consequences: setting `platform.registry.url` does nothing; `platform.registry.overrides` is dead; `platform.registry.pullSecretName` does not propagate to `spec.imagePullSecrets`; and an air-gap install must instead override every `<comp>.image.repository` individually. The §17.8.6 single-source guarantee is not delivered.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/common/registry/resolver.go`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:135`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/controller-deployment.yaml:43`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml:95`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/admission-policies/registry-digest-webhook.yaml:15`

**Resolution:** New `_helpers.tpl` `lenny.componentImage` mirrors the
`pkg/common/registry` ImageResolver precedence (override → `url/<name>:tag`)
and now composes every Lenny component image reference: gateway, lenny-ops,
WarmPoolController, PoolScalingController, lenny-token-service, lenny-backup
(backup + restore-test), lenny-preflight (preflight + crd-validate),
lenny-migrate, the bootstrap `lenny-ctl`, and the shared `lenny-webhook`
admission image (`_webhook.tpl` + cosign-verify). Setting
`platform.registry.url` now redirects all of them to one registry path;
`platform.registry.overrides[<name>]` redirects a single component. New
`lenny.imagePullSecrets` propagates `platform.registry.pullSecretName` to
every Lenny component pod's `imagePullSecrets`. The default render is
byte-identical (url defaults to `ghcr.io/lennylabs`, name = the binary
basename), so the existing image assertions pass unchanged. Helm cannot
import the Go resolver, so the deploy-time composition lives in the chart
helper that mirrors its precedence; the Go package stays the binary-side
primitive (the adapter/egress-capture images remain operator-supplied full
references via `--adapter-image` / `--egress-capture-image`, the resolver's
override rung). Third-party images (CoreDNS, PgBouncer, MinIO mc, OTel) and
the §26 reference-runtime catalog keep their own registries. Closed by
713cb7a7; helm-unittest covers url propagation, override
precedence, and pull-secret propagation on the gateway, PSC, controller, and
webhook surfaces.

### - [x] F-17.8.3 — 8-03 — Bootstrap-mode admin API and status signaling not implemented [High] — CLOSED

§17.8.2 "Cold-start bootstrap procedure" (spec lines 1079–1097) is normative. It requires:

- (a) `PUT /v1/admin/pools/{name}` accepting body `{"bootstrapMinWarm": N}`.
- (b) `DELETE /v1/admin/pools/{name}/bootstrap-override` to clear the override before the 48-hour window elapses.
- (c) `GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}` returning a `bootstrapStatus` object with `active`, `bootstrapMinWarm`, `hoursOfData`, `estimatedConvergenceAt`.
- (d) Controller-set `status.scalingMode: bootstrap | formula` on `SandboxWarmPool`.
- (e) `lenny_pool_bootstrap_mode` gauge labeled by pool name (value 1 active, 0 converged).
- (f) Convergence criteria: ≥48 h traffic data, target stability variance <20% over a 1-hour rolling window for 2 h, no `WarmPoolLow` in last 6 h, target ≤3× bootstrap value, otherwise emit `PoolBootstrapUnderprovisioned`.

Implementation state:

- (a) `UpdatePoolRequest` at `pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go:44–58` exposes runtimeRef, isolation profile, warmCount, etc., but no `bootstrapMinWarm` field. The admin handler at `pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go:231` (handleUpdatePool) cannot set the bootstrap override.
- (b) No `DELETE /v1/admin/pools/{name}/bootstrap-override` route is registered (`grep -rn "bootstrap-override" --include="*.go"` returns zero results). The mux registration block at `pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:392–399` shows only `POST /v1/admin/pools`, `GET .../pools`, `GET .../pools/{name}`, `PUT .../pools/{name}`, `DELETE .../pools/{name}`.
- (c) No `bootstrapStatus` field on the PoolPayload response (`pools.go:21–42`).
- (d) `SandboxWarmPoolStatus` (`pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxwarmpool_types.go:121–147`) has no `ScalingMode` field. The strategy package declares `ScalingMode` constants (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/strategy/strategy.go:79–88`) but the reconciler at `pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go:399–437` discards `decision.Mode` and writes only `MinWarm`. Status writes touch `Status.SDKWarmCircuitBreaker` only (lines 336, 365, 368).
- (e) `lenny_pool_bootstrap_mode` is registered in the catalog (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:178`) but is never assigned. `grep -rn "pool_bootstrap_mode" --include="*.go"` outside `catalog.go`, the catalog test, and the alert rule expression returns no hits — the gauge is referenced by the `PoolBootstrapMode` alert (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1112–1117`) which therefore can never fire.
- (f) No convergence-criteria logic: no 48-hour window check, no 1-hour variance/stability check, no `lenny_pool_bootstrap_target_min_warm` / `lenny_pool_bootstrap_min_warm_override` metric emission. The `PoolBootstrapUnderprovisioned` alert expression (`rules.go:1122`) references two metric names that are not in the catalog and are never emitted.

This breaks the operator handoff §17.8.2 prescribes for every first deployment: bootstrap mode is invisible to the operator (no metric, no status field, no admin response field) and cannot be exited via the admin API.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go:44–58, 231`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:391–399`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/apis/lenny/v1/sandboxwarmpool_types.go:121–147`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go:399–437`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/strategy/strategy.go:79–88`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:178`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1112–1125`

**Resolution (commit 2b745ebb):** Built the full §17.8.2 cold-start surface. (a) `poolstore.Pool`
gains a nullable `BootstrapMinWarm` override (migration 0137
`bootstrap_min_warm` column; pgstore + Memory round-trip), set via the new
`PUT {bootstrapMinWarm: N}` field. (b) `DELETE /v1/admin/pools/{name}/bootstrap-override`
(`handleClearBootstrapOverride`, honours If-Match-if-present, idempotent,
audits `admin.pool.bootstrap_override_cleared`). (c) GET surfaces a
`bootstrapStatus {active, bootstrapMinWarm, hoursOfData, estimatedConvergenceAt}`
object; hoursOfData / estimatedConvergenceAt come from the new
`PoolBootstrapStatusReader` (satisfied by `podsession.PoolStatusLookup` reading
`status.scalingMode` + `status.bootstrapHoursOfData`, wired in `cmd/lenny-gateway`).
(d) `SandboxWarmPoolStatus.ScalingMode` (`bootstrap|formula`) added and written
by the reconciler's `syncPoolStatus`. (e) The reconciler emits the
`lenny_pool_bootstrap_mode` gauge via the new `bootstrapModeMeter` (with
forget-not-in cleanup). (f) New `convergence` package implements the §17.8.2
step-4 criteria (≥48h data, formula-target stability via a `stableSince`
run-tracker, no recent WarmPoolLow via the optional `WarmPoolLowSource`, target
≤ 3× override); the meter also emits `lenny_pool_bootstrap_target_min_warm` and
`lenny_pool_bootstrap_min_warm_override`, so the catalog-only
`PoolBootstrapUnderprovisioned` / `PoolBootstrapMode` alerts now evaluate. The
evidence's `pkg/apis/lenny/v1` path is now `v1alpha1` (F-15.5.1) and the two
"missing from catalog" metrics were already present (catalog.go:380-381); only
emitters were absent.

### - [x] F-17.8.4 — 8-01 — Tier 3 `safety_factor` override (1.2 / 1.5) is not applied automatically [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec lines 1003–1010 declare Tier 3 normative per-tier `safety_factor` overrides (1.2 agent, 1.5 mcp) versus the §4.6.2 defaults (1.5 agent, 2.0 mcp), and state: "The PoolScalingController SHOULD apply the Tier 3 override automatically when `capacityPlanning.tier: 3` is configured; otherwise operators must set `poolScaling.safetyFactor` explicitly."

`pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go:42` defines `defaultSafetyFactor = 1.5` as a hard-coded constant, applied unconditionally at line 416 when the pool config does not specify a safety factor. There is no tier signal in the controller (`grep -rnE "capacityPlanning|Tier3" pkg/controller/poolscaling --include="*.go"` returns zero hits), no MCP/agent-type discrimination, and no `poolScaling.safetyFactor` Helm value. The tier preset files do not surface this either: `presets/values-tier3.yaml` does not override any safety-factor field, and the spec says operators "must set it explicitly" without providing a Helm field for them to set.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller.go:42, 416`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/presets/values-tier3.yaml`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` (no `poolScaling.safetyFactor` key)

**Resolution (f7b73ca9):** Added `DefaultSafetyFactorForTier` (1.2 at Tier 3,
1.5 otherwise) and a `Reconciler.DefaultSafetyFactor` field that replaces the
unconditional `defaultSafetyFactor` const fallback; a pool that pins its own
`SafetyFactor` still wins. The pool-scaling-controller binary gains a
`--default-safety-factor` flag / `LENNY_POOL_SCALING_SAFETY_FACTOR` env that
defaults to 0, in which case it resolves the per-tier default from
`--capacity-tier`, so a Tier 3 install picks up 1.2 automatically. Chart
exposes `poolScalingController.safetyFactor` (default 0) rendered as the env.
Per §17.8.2 line 1010 the controller applies one default per deployment; an
mcp-type pool whose normative default differs pins its own SafetyFactor via the
admin API.

### - [x] F-17.8.5 — 8-02 — Tier 3 `billingRedisStreamMaxLen` not applied via tier selection [Medium] — CLOSED

§17.8.1 line 909 and §17.8.2 line 1203 give the per-tier defaults: 50,000 at Tier 1/2, 72,000 at Tier 3 (with footnote ⁵ deriving 72,000 from the Tier 3 outage envelope). The default in `pkg/gateway/billingstore/failover/redisstream/redisstream.go:54` is `DefaultStreamMaxLen = 50_000`, which is documented as "the Tier 1/2 default" in the comment at line 52. Nothing reads the tier and bumps the default to 72,000 at Tier 3:

- The Helm chart has no `billingRedisStreamMaxLen` (or `billing.redisStreamMaxLen`) value (`grep -rn "billingRedisStreamMaxLen\|streamMaxLen" charts --include="*.yaml"` returns zero hits in `values*.yaml`).
- No tier preset overrides it.
- No CLI flag/env propagates it.

A Tier 3 install therefore silently uses the 50,000 floor and, per the spec footnote, will overflow in under 83 seconds at the Tier 3 billing rate during a Postgres outage — falling below the 60s combined outage envelope §17.8.1 footnote ⁵ requires.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/billingstore/failover/redisstream/redisstream.go:50–60`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/presets/values-tier3.yaml`

**Resolution (f7b73ca9):** Added `redisstream.StreamMaxLenForTier` (72,000 at
Tier 3, 50,000 otherwise) and `Tier3StreamMaxLen` const. The gateway gains a
`--billing-redis-stream-max-len` flag / `LENNY_BILLING_REDIS_STREAM_MAX_LEN`
env (default 0) and a `--capacity-tier` flag; when the maxlen is unset the
gateway resolves the per-tier default from the tier and passes it to
`redisstream.Options.StreamMaxLen` so a Tier 3 install is sized for the
outage-plus-recovery envelope. Chart exposes `billing.redisStreamMaxLen`
(default 0) and the tier3 preset restates 72,000 explicitly.

### - [x] F-17.8.6 — 8-03 — Controller tuning table is largely unrendered [Medium] — CLOSED

§17.8.2 "Controller tuning" table (spec lines 1110–1124) lists per-tier values for: pod-creation rate limiter (QPS/burst), status-update rate limiter (QPS/burst), `--max-concurrent-reconciles`, work queue max depth, initial fill grace period, controller replicas, controller pod anti-affinity (`--controller-anti-affinity`, `required` at Tier 2/3), `statusUpdateDeduplicationWindow` (`--status-update-dedup-window`, 500ms / 250ms), and etcd compaction/defrag/quota parameters.

Of these, only `controller.replicas` is reflected anywhere (`values.yaml:19`, overridden to 3 at Tier 3 by `presets/values-tier3.yaml:70`). `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` defines no `--max-concurrent-reconciles`, `--status-update-dedup-window`, rate-limiter QPS/burst, or queue-depth flags (`grep -nE "MaxConcurrent|max-concurrent" cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` returns no hits). The `templates/controller-deployment.yaml` arg list at lines 45–53 carries only `--leader-elect`, leader-election namespace, metrics-bind, health-probe-bind, optional `--adapter-image`, and optional `--egress-capture-image`. There is no `podAntiAffinity` block in the controller Deployment template at any tier (`grep -rn "podAntiAffinity" charts/lenny/templates --include="*.yaml"` returns zero hits).

This means the spec's promotion-time controller-tuning expectations (e.g., Tier 3's "10 → 15 concurrent reconciles, 250 ms status-update dedup window, dedicated etcd cluster") cannot be applied through the chart and the §17.8.3 promotion gate has nothing to validate them against.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:82–106`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/controller-deployment.yaml:43–53`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/presets/values-tier3.yaml`

**Resolution:** The binary half was stale — `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go`
already defines and consumes every tuning flag (`--create-qps`/`--create-burst`,
`--status-qps`/`--status-burst`, `--max-concurrent-reconciles`,
`--workqueue-max-depth`, `--status-update-dedup-window`,
`--initial-fill-grace-period`). The real gap was the chart, now closed: a new
`controller.tuning` value block renders each flag (only when set, so a stock
render keeps the binary defaults — which already match the Tier 1 limiter,
concurrency, queue, and dedup columns), and the tier presets pin the per-tier
column (Tier 2: 40/100, 60/200, 5 reconciles, 2000 queue, 90s grace; Tier 3:
80/200, 120/400, 15 reconciles, 10000 queue, 250ms dedup, 120s grace). The
"Controller pod anti-affinity" row is realized as the shared
`controller.antiAffinity` knob (a podSpec concern, not a binary flag): a new
`lenny.controllerAntiAffinity` helper renders `preferred` (Tier 1 advisory) or
`required` (Tier 2/3) anti-affinity on both the WarmPoolController Deployment
(previously had none) and the PoolScalingController (its hardcoded `preferred`
block now reads the same knob), so the two leaders never share a node at
Tier 2/3. `controller.replicas` was already wired. The etcd
compaction/defrag/quota rows are external-infra guidance for the operator's
etcd cluster (the chart ships no etcd workload) and stay out of chart scope.
Closed by 713cb7a7; helm-unittest covers the default
(flags-omitted) render, an explicit tuning override, preferred/required
anti-affinity on both controllers, and the Tier 3 preset column.

§17.8.2 line 936 — Tier 3 scale-down narrative — names `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total` and the `PDBBlockedEvictions` alert as the operator's observability handle for the PDB-bound scale-down floor. The metric is declared in the catalog (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:87`) and is referenced by the alert (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:587–588`), but no Go code increments it (`grep -rn "pdb_blocked_evictions_total" pkg --include="*.go"` returns only the catalog declaration, the catalog test, and the alert expression).

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:587–588`

### - [x] F-17.8.9 — 8-06 — `tier-promotion` runbook contradicts the CLI surface [Medium] — CLOSED

`docs/runbooks/tier-promotion.md` instructs operators to invoke `lenny-tier-promote validate --from … --to … --post-upgrade` (step 2 line 54, step 6 line 87) and `--from tier2 --to tier1 --acknowledge-demotion` for rollback (step 10 line 114, "Notes" line 124). The binary `cmd/lenny-tier-promote/main.go` has:

- No `validate` subcommand (top-level argument parsing via `flag.Parse()`).
- No `--post-upgrade` flag (the flag set at lines 32–46 lists only `--from`, `--to`, `--namespace`, `--chart-values-tier`, `--audit-retain-days`, `--secret-encryption-verified`, `--postgres-external`, `--redis-external`).
- No `--acknowledge-demotion` flag.
- An explicit downgrade rejection: `tierpromotion.validateTransition` at `pkg/tierpromotion/tierpromotion.go:266–278` errors with "downgrade; this gate validates promotions only" when `to.Rank() < from.Rank()`. The runbook step 10 cannot run.

The "post-promotion validation" step 6 in the runbook is therefore not executable as written, and the documented rollback validation in step 10 is rejected by the gate. Operators following the runbook will see "validate: flag provided but not defined: -post-upgrade".

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-tier-promote/main.go:31–46, 77`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/tierpromotion/tierpromotion.go:266–278`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/runbooks/tier-promotion.md:54, 87, 114, 124`

**Resolution (commit `6579fa2a`).** Resolved by correcting the runbook (rule
O / rule B): the spec defines no `lenny-tier-promote` CLI surface, so the
implemented bare-flag CLI is the source of truth and the runbook had
invented a `validate` subcommand, `--post-upgrade`, and
`--acknowledge-demotion`, plus a demotion-direction gate that
`pkg/tierpromotion.validateTransition` rejects by design. Dropped the
`validate` subcommand from steps 2/6/10, dropped `--post-upgrade` (the
gate reads the live cluster, so the post-check is just a re-run), and
replaced the rejected `--from tier2 --to tier1` rollback validation with
a `kubectl`/`helm get values` check, noting the gate validates promotions
only and that demotion is handled by `helm rollback` + restore. Also
corrected step 7's `lenny-ctl tenants list`/`session start` to
`lenny-ctl admin tenants list` and a `POST /v1/sessions` smoke test. The
Tier 3 attestation example already used the correct bare-flag form.

### - [x] F-17.8.11 — 8-02 — Tier-promotion gate does not enforce LLM-Proxy extraction or GC pressure checks [Low] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: medium) — F-17.8.10 — Both concern missing §17.8.3 tier-promotion gate checks, but F-17.8.10 is specifically the KEDA-mandatory check while F-17.8.11 covers the LLM-Proxy extraction and GC-pressure checks; different specific checks within the same gate.

§17.8.3 Step 1 (spec lines 1257–1267) defines four Phase 13.5 checks (LLM Proxy extraction ratio, gateway GC pause, `maxSessionsPerReplica` calibration, KEDA deployment) plus Step 2 NO-GO additions (etcd write latency, `maxSessionsPerReplica` provisional). The gate at `pkg/tierpromotion/checks.go` inspects none of these; it does not query Prometheus, does not read the gateway's `maxSessionsPerReplica` value, and has no notion of the LLM Proxy ratio. The Tier 3 gate refuses to pass without all three attestations; lower tiers SKIP.

### - [x] F-17.8.12 — 8-03 — `lenny-ops` mandatoriness is "by absence", not by chart-validation rejection [Low] — CLOSED

§17.8.5 line 1323 states: "Attempts to disable `lenny-ops` via Helm values are rejected at chart validation." The chart has no `ops.enabled` key and the `templates/ops-deployment.yaml` is rendered unconditionally (no `{{- if .Values.ops.* }}` wrapper). A user who sets `ops.enabled: false` in their values file gets silent acceptance — the chart still renders ops, but the user's intent is neither warned about nor rejected. A literal reading of §17.8.5 calls for an explicit `fail` in a chart template (e.g., `if (hasKey .Values.ops "enabled") and (not .Values.ops.enabled) then fail …`) so operators are not led to believe they have toggled the service off.

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` (top of file, no enabled gate)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:748–774` (no `ops.enabled` key)

- **Resolution:** Added a top-of-template `fail` guard in `charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` that detects `hasKey .Values.ops "enabled"` and rejects both `false` (mandatoriness violation) and `true` (unsupported key). Helm-unittest cases in `tests/ops-deployment_test.yaml` cover both rejections.

### - [x] F-17.8.13 — 8-04 — SCL-036 minReplicas burst-absorption formula is documented, not enforced [Low] — CLOSED

§17.8.2 line 950 names "SCL-036" and gives the formula `minReplicas >= ceil(burst_arrival_rate * pipeline_lag_seconds / sessions_per_replica)`. Each tier preset hard-codes a number into `autoscaling.minReplicas` derived from this formula in a comment (`presets/values-tier1.yaml:36–43`, `tier2.yaml:36–44`, `tier3.yaml:35–48`). Nothing in code or chart validation re-derives the value or refuses an inconsistent `(minReplicas, maxSessionsPerReplica)` pairing. A user who lowers `gateway.maxSessionsPerReplica` to 25 at Tier 3 without raising `autoscaling.minReplicas` from 5 will silently underprovision; no preflight check flags it.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/autoscaling-gateway.yaml`

- **Resolution:** Added `CheckBurstAbsorption` in `pkg/tierpromotion/phase135.go` and two new fields (`Inputs.MinReplicas`, `Inputs.MaxSessionsPerReplica`) wired through the gatherer and the CLI flags `--min-replicas`, `--max-sessions-per-replica`. The check evaluates `ceil(burst * pipeline_lag / sessions_per_replica)` for the active provider (KEDA: 20s lag, HPA: 60s lag) and honors the §17.8.2 line 975 Tier 3 KEDA carve-out (minReplicas=5 when the raw floor is 10).

- **Resolution:** Added the `lenny_warmpool_idle_pods` instantaneous gauge in `pkg/controller/warmpool/idle_meter.go` (registered against the controller-runtime registry) and wired `setIdlePods(pool, decision.ReadyCount)` into the warm-pool reconcile loop with a matching `forgetIdlePods` on pool deletion. ## §17.9 Deployment Answer Files <a id="17.9"></a>
Audit of `spec/17_deployment-topology.md` §17.9 (lines 1336–1547, sub-sections
17.9.1–17.9.7) against the implementation tree:
`charts/lenny/{answers,presets,values.yaml,templates}/`, `cmd/lenny-ctl/`,
`cmd/lenny-preflight/`, `pkg/preflight/`, `pkg/embedded/`, `pkg/audit/integrity/`,
`migrations/`, `docs/operator-guide/`, and `scripts/cloud/`.

### Method

Read §17.9 in full and enumerated the normative requirements from each
sub-section (17.9.1 composition dimensions, 17.9.2 answer-file catalog, 17.9.3
cloud-managed backends, 17.9.4 cloud object-storage lifecycle, 17.9.5
self-managed backends, 17.9.6 embedded backends, 17.9.7 backend-invariant
requirements). For each requirement, ran `grep`/`find` across the
implementation tree and read each candidate file to classify the result.
Findings are graded by the rubric: High (MUST / correctness / security),
Medium (SHOULD / capability unimplemented), Low (minor deviation), Info
(noteworthy).

### Summary

§17.9 describes a catalog of nine curated answer files organised along five
orthogonal composition dimensions (Environment, Cluster type, Backends,
Capacity tier, Isolation profile). The implementation ships three answer
files organised along a single dimension (capacity tier), and the install
wizard accepts none of the missing dimensions. The chart has no
`backends`, `postgres.connectionPooler`, `redis.provider`, or
`objectStorage.provider` Helm values; the spec's two §17.9.7
backend-invariant defenses for cloud-managed pooler deployments
(`LENNY_POOLER_MODE` gateway startup refusal, conditional trigger
creation in migrations, preflight check `Cloud-managed pooler sentinel
defense` in §17.6 line 488) are absent. The cloud object-storage lifecycle
requirements in §17.9.4 (bucket versioning, delete-marker / noncurrent-
version expiry on S3, GCS, Azure Blob) have no chart-rendered Job
configuring them and no preflight check verifying them. The §17.9 design
principle "Lenny must not depend on any single cloud provider" is held in
the runtime code (gateway and controllers do not branch on backend), so
the gap is in operator-facing surface area: answer files, Helm values
schema, install wizard, preflight checks, and migration logic.

Approximate completeness against the §17.9 documented surface: the chart
deploys none of the self-managed backends as Kubernetes workloads (no
PgBouncer, no Redis Sentinel/Cluster, no MinIO templates), so the
self-managed dimension is in effect a documentation-only label that does
not select different rendered manifests. Embedded Mode is the
best-covered dimension (`pkg/embedded/stack` brings up Postgres, Redis
miniredis, OIDC, k3s, and a local-disk artifact store), and the
backend-agnostic interfaces in `pkg/objectstore`, `pkg/embedded`, and the
gateway store layers correctly avoid branching on backend.

None of the spec-named files (`laptop.yaml`, `docker-compose.yaml`,

documented in §17.9: a deployer of an EKS production cluster cannot
reach for `eks-production.yaml`; the wizard's "auto-suggest" claim in

prior tier-based `--answers` files remain the separate §17.6 wizard input.

### - [ ] F-17.9.2 — §17.9.7 cloud-managed pooler defense (`LENNY_POOLER_MODE`, conditional trigger creation, preflight check) is entirely absent [High] — DEFERRED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-12.2.14, F-12.3.1 — Three findings describe the absent LENNY_POOLER_MODE startup-refusal and tenant-guard defense; F-17.5.8 is the separate missing chart connectionPooler value.

**Spec:** §17.9.7 (line 1541) and the cross-referenced §12.3 (lines 51–57)
define a layered defense for cloud-managed Postgres pooler deployments
that cannot run `connect_query`:

1. Helm value `postgres.connectionPooler: external` exists and defaults
   to `external` when `backends = cloud-managed`.
2. The migration creates the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger when
   `connectionPooler = external` (detected via the Helm value).
3. The gateway reads `LENNY_POOLER_MODE` from its environment at
   startup; when the value is `external` it queries `pg_trigger` and
   refuses to start with a fatal error if `lenny_tenant_guard` is
   absent from tenant-scoped tables.
4. The §17.6 preflight Job emits the "Cloud-managed pooler sentinel
   defense" check (§17.6 line 488): "When
   `postgres.connectionPooler = external`: connect to Postgres, verify
   the per-transaction tenant validation trigger exists on tenant-
   scoped tables (query `pg_trigger` for the `lenny_tenant_guard`
   trigger). If absent, fail."

The §17.9.3 helm-config block (lines 1391–1416) shows
`postgres.connectionPooler: external` as the deployer-facing knob.

**Impl:** None of these surfaces exist.

- `charts/lenny/values.yaml`: no `postgres.connectionPooler`,
  `backends`, or `LENNY_POOLER_MODE` keys. `grep -rn 'connectionPooler\|
  LENNY_POOLER_MODE\|connect_query'` across `charts/`, `pkg/`, `cmd/`
  returns zero hits.
- `migrations/0002_rls_immutability_roles.up.sql` creates
  `lenny_tenant_guard` unconditionally on every install (lines 36, 112–
  126), which is not strictly wrong (the trigger is the correct default
  cloud-managed defense) but the spec's "migration detects whether
  `connect_query` sentinel support is available" branch is not
  implemented; deployments without the trigger have no migration-time
  control.
- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`: no `LENNY_POOLER_MODE` env read and no
  `pg_trigger` lookup before serving. The gateway's `pkg/audit/integrity`
  startup check (`integrity.Verify*`) does query `pg_trigger` for
  `lenny_tenant_guard`, `lenny_audit_immutability`, and
  `lenny_billing_immutability` and refuses to start in production on a
  violation (`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:362`), but the check is
  unconditional — it does not depend on or read `LENNY_POOLER_MODE`,
  and it does not produce the spec-mandated error message
  `"FATAL: cloud-managed pooler mode (LENNY_POOLER_MODE=external)
  detected but lenny_tenant_guard trigger is absent ..."`.
- `pkg/preflight/run.go`: implements only the admission-plane checks
  (admission-webhook inventory, phase-stamp, host-sharing, NetworkPolicy
  parities, NET-064 identity uniqueness). No `Cloud-managed pooler
  sentinel defense` check exists.

**Severity:** High. The defense protects multi-tenant RLS isolation on
cloud-managed deployments. The startup audit-integrity check covers
the unconditional case, but the spec's intent is to make the cloud-
managed-pooler mode explicit (it is the second of the two §17.9.7 RLS
checkout defenses, and §17.9.7 line 1541 says "exactly one must be
active per deployment"). Without `LENNY_POOLER_MODE`, the spec's
"either A or B, exactly one active" invariant is unverifiable.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations/0002_rls_immutability_roles.up.sql`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` (no `LENNY_POOLER_MODE` read)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/audit/integrity/integrity.go` (unconditional trigger check)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:259-284` (postgres block lacks `connectionPooler`)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/preflight/run.go` (no cloud-pooler check)

**Partial resolution + deferral (`016fb593`, `0ce4b747`):** Three of the four
layers are now closed. Part 1 (chart `postgres.connectionPooler` value +
`backends`-driven default) by F-17.5.8 and F-12.3.2; part 2 (the migration
creates the trigger; unconditional creation is a superset of the `external`
clause) by F-12.3.3; part 3 (gateway reads `LENNY_POOLER_MODE`, queries
`pg_trigger`, refuses to start) by F-12.3.1. **Deferred:** part 4 — the
preflight binary's actual Postgres `CloudPoolerSentinelDefense` check. The
`--connection-pooler` flag is plumbed and validated, but `pkg/preflight/run.go`
is a Kubernetes-API-only runner; adding the `pg_trigger` verification requires
giving the preflight Job Postgres connectivity (a DSN flag, a datastore-secret
mount, and pgx in the binary), a separate lift. The load-bearing runtime
defense (part 3) is in place and backstops the install-time convenience, so
the deferral leaves no unguarded window.

### - [x] F-17.9.3 — §17.9.4 cloud object-storage lifecycle requirements have no chart-rendered Job, no MinIO post-install Job, and no preflight check [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §17.9.4 (lines 1418–1494) is a MUST: "Cloud-managed object
storage buckets must be configured with the same lifecycle rules that
Section 12.5 mandates for MinIO." The required rules are bucket
versioning enabled, delete-marker expiration 1 day, noncurrent-version
expiration 1 day, applied bucket-wide on all providers. §17.9.4 line
1420 says the Helm chart post-install Job configures these rules for
MinIO via `mc ilm add`; for cloud providers the deployer applies them
out of band and the preflight Job validates them. The §17.6 preflight
table (line 494) names this check `Cloud object storage lifecycle
rules`: "When `objectStorage.provider` is `s3`, `gcs`, or `azure`:
verify (a) bucket versioning is enabled and (b) lifecycle rules exist
that expire noncurrent versions within ≤ 7 days and expire delete
markers within ≤ 7 days. Uses provider SDK calls..."

**Impl:** None of the three surfaces exist.

- No MinIO post-install Job: `find charts/lenny/templates -name "*minio*"
  -o -name "*lifecycle*" -o -name "*bucket*"` returns zero matches.
  `grep -rn 'mc ilm\|bucket.*versioning\|lifecycle.*rule\|delete.marker'
  charts/` returns zero matches.
- No chart template that calls the AWS / GCP / Azure CLI commands shown
  in §17.9.4 (lines 1432–1493: `aws s3api put-bucket-versioning ...`,
  `gcloud storage buckets update --versioning`,
  `az storage account blob-service-properties update --enable-versioning`).
- No preflight check. `pkg/preflight/run.go` has no
  `cloud-object-storage-lifecycle` check; the only object-storage-
  related test path is the lenny-ctl `objectStorage.endpoint /
  .bucket` value pass-through.
- No `objectStorage.provider` Helm value to gate the check on (the
  field exists in `installAnswers` but is unused by the chart; see H4).

**Severity:** High. The spec frames the lifecycle rules as required to
prevent `ListObjects` performance degradation at scale and to prevent
accidental overwrites of checkpoint objects on cloud buckets — both
correctness and SLO concerns. With no enforcement and no preflight
check, a deployer who omits the bucket configuration is unprotected.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` (no minio
  post-install or lifecycle-config Job)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/preflight/run.go` (no
  cloud-object-storage-lifecycle check)

**Resolution:** The two missing surfaces are now present; the third (MinIO post-install Job) was stale evidence. (1) The MinIO post-install Job already exists at `charts/lenny/templates/minio-bucket-lifecycle-job.yaml` (commit `2d97f85b`): a `post-install,post-upgrade` hook that runs `mc version enable` + `mc ilm add --expired-object-delete-marker --noncurrentversion-expiration-days` against the artifact bucket, gated on `minio.endpoint` + `minio.lifecycle.enabled`. (2) New `pkg/preflight/CloudObjectStorageLifecycleCheck` (`cloud-object-storage-lifecycle`) is the §17.6 line 494 check: it self-skips for `objectStorage.provider=minio` (the post-install Job owns MinIO lifecycle), fails-closed on an unrecognized provider or a cloud provider with an empty bucket, and for s3/gcs/azure verifies (via a `CloudObjectStorageLifecycleProber` SDK read) bucket versioning + a noncurrent-version expiration rule ≤ 7 days, plus an expired-object-delete-marker rule for S3/S3-compatible. A nil prober (skip-network-probes / a provider without a wired SDK reader) routes through a non-blocking advisory. (3) `cmd/lenny-preflight` wires a real AWS S3 prober (`GetBucketVersioning` + `GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration`, `NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration`→absent-rules); gcs/azure route through the advisory path in v1. The chart renders `objectStorage.{provider,bucket,region}` into `--object-storage-*` flags on the preflight Job. Tested: 12 tier-1 cases in `cloud_object_storage_test.go` (skip/fail-closed/missing-rule/over-ceiling/provider-specific-delete-marker/prober-error) + 2 helm-unittest renders. Commit `6c6367e7`.

`postgres.cidr`, `postgres.gatewayEgressCIDR`; `redis.url`,
`redis.tlsPort`, `redis.gatewayEgressCIDR`; `minio.endpoint`,
`minio.accessKey`, `minio.secretKey`, `minio.bucket`, `minio.useSSL`.
None of the spec's selector keys (`backends`, `postgres.connectionPooler`,
`postgres.readDsn`, `redis.provider`, `redis.endpoints`,
`redis.coordinationEndpoints`, `objectStorage.provider`) exist. The
chart does not branch on which backend variant is active because no
field gates that branch.

The fields that do exist correspond approximately to a single deployment
mode: "bring-your-own external Postgres / Redis / MinIO with the
provider's TCP endpoint pasted into a DSN/URL." Cloud-provider proxies
(RDS Proxy, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, Azure PgBouncer integration) and
self-managed proxies (PgBouncer Deployment) cannot be selected through
the chart; the deployer has to pass the right DSN and trust that the
backend matches.

**Severity:** High. The §17.9.1 composition dimensions are not just
documentation — they are the contract that lets the chart render
different manifests per dimension (PgBouncer Deployment when
`backends = self-managed`, no PgBouncer when `backends = cloud-managed`,
etc.). Without the selectors, the only differentiation between the three
modes is whether the deployer has pasted a managed-service DSN or an
in-cluster DSN; the rendered chart is otherwise identical, which makes
the chart unable to enforce the §17.9.3 invariant "Answer files whose
backends dimension is `cloud-managed` omit PgBouncer, Redis Sentinel,
and MinIO resources." Since the chart in fact omits all three of those
workloads in every mode (see H5), the invariant is satisfied
incidentally but not enforced by the contract.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:259-284` (postgres block, no `connectionPooler`)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:132-155` (redis block, no `provider`/`endpoints`)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:157-173` (minio block, no `provider`)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/datastore-secret.yaml` (gates rendering on DSN/URL/endpoint emptiness only)

- **Resolution:** The §17.9.3 composition selectors are now a chart contract. `backends`, `postgres.connectionPooler` (with the §12.3 line 55 default-to-`external` when `backends=cloud-managed`, via the `lenny.connectionPooler`/`lenny.poolerMode` helpers feeding `LENNY_POOLER_MODE`), `objectStorage.provider` (F-17.5.1, drives the gateway `--object-storage-*` adapter selection), and `redis.concerns.*` (the §12.4 logical concern split, F-12.4.16) already existed. This batch adds the last missing selector: `redis.provider` (`external` \| `sentinel` \| `cluster`) plus `redis.sentinels`, `redis.sentinelMaster`, `redis.password`, and `redis.sentinelPassword`. A new `lenny.redisProvider` helper resolves the effective provider (an explicit value is validated against the allow-list and its required fields; an empty value derives from `cluster.addrs`/`sentinels`/`url` so existing values files are unchanged) and gates exactly one connection env block in `gateway-deployment.yaml`. `provider=sentinel` wires `LENNY_REDIS_SENTINEL_ADDRS`/`_MASTER`/`_TLS` and the secret-backed `LENNY_REDIS_PASSWORD`/`_SENTINEL_PASSWORD` (the gateway already supports the full Sentinel path). `postgres.readDsn` is the one remaining key, tracked and deferred under F-17.9.13 (no read/write-split store layer exists). Commit `002091e4`. Tested: helm-unittest sentinel env + secret rendering + provider-validation failures, plus stock/cluster/url backward-compat renders.

### - [x] F-17.9.5 — §17.9.5 self-managed backend workloads (PgBouncer, Redis Sentinel/Cluster, MinIO) are not rendered by the chart [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §17.9.5 (lines 1499–1530) requires that answer files in the
self-managed backend dimension "deploy PgBouncer, Redis Sentinel (or
Cluster), and MinIO as Kubernetes workloads alongside Lenny's own
components":

| Component | Self-managed implementation |
|---|---|
| Postgres | CloudNativePG operator or Patroni on Kubernetes |
| Connection pooler | PgBouncer Deployment (2+ replicas) with PDB |
| Redis | Redis Sentinel (Tiers 1–2) or Redis Cluster (Tier 3) |
| Object storage | MinIO with erasure coding |

§17.9.5 lines 1511–1530 shows the configured `pgbouncer.replicas`,
`pgbouncer.poolMode`, `pgbouncer.defaultPoolSize` knobs.

**Impl:** None of these workloads are rendered.

- No PgBouncer Deployment template. `find charts/lenny/templates -name
  "*pgbouncer*" -o -name "*bouncer*"` returns zero matches. The only
  PgBouncer references in `values.yaml` are documentation comments
  about `postgres.cidr` (the destination CIDR PgBouncer is allowed to
  reach Postgres on) — but no PgBouncer to anchor that rule against.
- No CloudNativePG / Patroni / Postgres StatefulSet template.
- No Redis Sentinel or Cluster manifest.
- No MinIO Deployment or StatefulSet template.

The chart's design comment in `templates/datastore-secret.yaml:3`
states explicitly: "Postgres, Redis, and MinIO stay bring-your-own
external services (§17.9); the chart does not deploy them."

**Severity:** High. §17.9.5 is normative ("Use this when deploying on
bare-metal, on-premises Kubernetes, or any environment without managed
database/cache services"). The implementation contradicts the spec's
catalog: the `openshift-self-managed.yaml`, `bare-metal-self-managed.yaml`,
and `airgap-self-managed.yaml` answer files would have nothing to
render — the deployer would still need to install CloudNativePG, Redis
Sentinel, and MinIO out of band and paste their endpoints into the
chart's DSN/URL fields, which is the same flow as the cloud-managed
case. The chart conflates the two backend dimensions into a single
"deployer supplies a DSN" surface.

The §17.9 design principle "self-managed backends are always a fully
supported first-class path" (line 1342) is therefore satisfied only by
external operator tooling: the chart does not own the self-managed
path.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/datastore-secret.yaml:3-4`
  (explicit "bring-your-own; the chart does not deploy them")
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` (no PgBouncer,
  CNPG, Patroni, Sentinel, Cluster, or MinIO templates)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:157` (`minio`
  block documented as "self-managed profile" but has no Deployment
  template to back it)

- **Resolution:** The chart now renders every §17.9.5 self-managed backend
  workload, gated on a per-backend `deploy` flag that follows the existing
  `pgbouncer.deploy` convention (PgBouncer was already rendered by
  F-12.3.10/.11). New templates: `minio-statefulset.yaml` (distributed
  erasure-coded StatefulSet — ≥4 nodes auto-enable erasure coding per
  §17.8 — headless + API Services, PDB, TLS on tlsPort);
  `redis-sentinel.yaml` (the §17.8 "Sentinel (3 sentinels, 1+1)" topology:
  a data StatefulSet + a 3-node Sentinel StatefulSet, `port 0` + TLS +
  `tls-auth-clients yes` + AUTH per §17.9.7, sharing the gateway's
  `redis-password` key so credentials match); `redis-cluster.yaml` (the
  Tier-3 6+ node Redis Cluster StatefulSet + a `redis-cli --cluster create`
  init Job); and `postgres-cluster.yaml` (a CloudNativePG `Cluster` CR with
  synchronous replication). `self-managed-backend-network-policies.yaml`
  re-admits the intra-backend flows (Sentinel discovery on 26379, Redis
  replication/gossip, distributed-MinIO erasure traffic, CNPG replication
  + client ingress) the §13.2 default-deny blocks. The three
  `*-self-managed.yaml` answer files now set `deploy: true` and point the
  consumer-side endpoints at the rendered Services, so they render a full
  backend topology instead of referencing out-of-band placeholders.
  `datastore-secret.yaml` renders `redis-password` for any deploy path.
  Commit `93936064`.

### - [x] F-17.9.6 — `composeValues` ignores the wizard's `domain`, `tls`, `auth.*`, `environment`, and `profile` answers; only postgres.dsn, redis.url, minio.endpoint/bucket, and feature flags survive into the rendered values [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §17.9.2 (line 1376) and §17.6 (line 671) name the wizard as
the first-class path to produce a working install. The composed Helm
values must reflect the operator's answers, including the
environment-driven defaults from §17.9.1 (alert thresholds, log
verbosity, `LENNY_DEV_MODE`, TLS strictness, `acknowledgeNoPrometheus`
default). The wizard's `domain`, `tls`, `auth.oidcIssuer`,
`auth.oidcClientId`, and `agentNamespaces` answers are also documented
as gateway-facing knobs.

**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:466-539 composeValues` only writes
the following top-level keys to the rendered values document:

- `global.devMode` (only when `auth.mode == dev`)
- `postgres.dsn` (only when non-empty)
- `redis.url` (only when non-empty)
- `minio.endpoint` and `minio.bucket` (only when non-empty)
- `features.{llmProxy,drainReadiness,compliance}` (only when at least
  one is on)
- `agentNamespaces` (only when non-empty)

The wizard collects but discards: `environment`, `tier` (passed only to
`helmInstallArgs` to select the preset path), `profile`, `domain`,
`tls`, `auth.oidcIssuer`, `auth.oidcClientId`. The schema documentation
(`charts/lenny/answers/README.md:39-41`) says `domain` "Empty keeps the
chart default. TLS strategy: `cert-manager` or `bring-your-own`" but the
composed values carry no `domain` or `tls` key, so a non-default
answer cannot reach the chart.

**Severity:** High. The wizard advertises a question for the gateway
DNS name and the TLS strategy, validates the answers, and then drops
them. A deployer who answers `domain: lenny.acme.com, tls: cert-manager`
gets a chart render identical to one that answered both empty.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:466-539` (composeValues)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/answers/README.md:39-41` (documented but unwired schema)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:567-589` (wizard prompts that get discarded)

- **Resolution:** `composeValues` now maps the previously-discarded answers onto their existing chart value paths. The new `composeIngress` helper turns a `domain` answer into `gateway.ingress.enabled: true` + `gateway.ingress.host`, and the `tls` answer into `gateway.ingress.tls.{enabled,secretName=lenny-gateway-ingress-tls}`; `cert-manager` additionally stamps the `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer` annotation when the new `tlsIssuer` answer (prompted only for cert-manager) is set. `environment` is written into the rendered values (it drives the §17.9.1 effects, see F-17.9.9) instead of only the header comment, which also fixes the latent bug where a wizard `environment=prod` install rendered `--environment=dev`. `auth.oidc.*` was already wired (F-10.3.14); `profile` stays advisory metadata by design (F-17.9.15). Commit `002091e4`. Tested: `cmd/lenny-ctl` `TestComposeValuesWiresIngress_spec_17_9_6` (domain/cert-manager-with+without-issuer/bring-your-own/none) and `TestComposeValuesWritesEnvironment_spec_17_9_1`.

### - [x] F-17.9.8 — Wizard claims to auto-suggest an answer-file base from cluster detection (`eks-small-team.yaml` when AWS EKS is detected); no detection logic exists [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §17.9.2 line 1376: "The `lenny-ctl install` wizard auto-
suggests an answer-file base from the detection phase (e.g.,
`eks-small-team.yaml` when AWS EKS is detected)."

**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:54-57` documents the `Profile`
field as "the answer-file base name the wizard auto-suggests from
cluster detection (§17.9). It is advisory metadata; the non-interactive
path does not load a second file from it." The wizard's
`promptAnswers` (lines 561–602) never prompts for or computes the
`profile` field; the only `profile` reference in interactive mode is
the `--offline` flag documentation ("Skip cluster-reachability
detection probes"), but no detection function exists. `grep -n
'detect\|detection\|cluster.*detect' cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go` returns
only comment references.

**Severity:** Medium. The wizard's value proposition in §17.6 includes
auto-detection; without it, the wizard is reduced to a YAML-form for
the deployer. The fix is doable in lenny-ctl with a small set of
kube-apiserver and StorageClass probes (the `topology.kubernetes.io/region`
label, `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type` patterns, the
`gke-resource-quotas` ConfigMap signature, the
`openshift.io/build.name` annotation, etc.).

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:54-57`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:561-602` (no detection)

**Resolution (`c4b98190`):** `install_detect.go` now infers the §17.9.1
cluster-type dimension (`detectClusterType`): it reads the node providerID
prefixes (`aws://` → eks, `gce://` → gke, `azure://` → aks, `kind://`/`k3s://`
→ laptop), checks the OpenShift API surface (`clusterversions.config.openshift.io`,
checked first so OpenShift-on-cloud maps to the self-managed file), and falls
back to vanilla. The cluster type maps to the suggested §17.9.2 catalog base
(EKS → `eks-small-team.yaml` per line 1376); the suggestion is surfaced in the
detection summary and recorded on the `profile` field of a saved answer file.
Tests cover each cloud, the OpenShift-on-AWS precedence, the k3s version-suffix
path, and the vanilla fallback.

### - [x] F-17.9.9 — `environment` answer is recorded but drives nothing in the rendered chart; the §17.9.1 dimension table claims it drives alert thresholds, log verbosity, `LENNY_DEV_MODE`, TLS strictness, and `acknowledgeNoPrometheus` default [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §17.9.1 (line 1350): "Environment: `local | dev | staging |
prod` → Drives: Alert thresholds, log verbosity, `LENNY_DEV_MODE`, TLS
strictness, `acknowledgeNoPrometheus` default."

**Impl:** The `environment` field is collected by the wizard and
echoed into the values-file header comment
(`install.go:520-526 composeValues`), but no template under
`charts/lenny/templates/` reads `.Values.environment`. `grep -rn
'\.Values\.environment\b'` across the templates returns zero matches.

The spec's named effects are not implemented:

- **Alert thresholds**: `monitoring.alertThresholds.*` is set by the
  tier preset (`presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml`), not by environment.
- **Log verbosity**: no `environment`-based selector; logging
  configuration is fixed.
- **`LENNY_DEV_MODE`**: tied to `global.devMode`, which is set only
  when `auth.mode == dev`, indirectly tied to environment but not as a
  declared mapping.
- **TLS strictness**: no `environment`-keyed selection of TLS
  enforcement levels in templates.
- **`acknowledgeNoPrometheus` default**: the spec value
  `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus` is referenced by §25.4 and the
  §17.6 preflight, but it does not exist in `values.yaml` (`grep -n
  'acknowledgeNoPrometheus' charts/lenny/values.yaml` returns no
  match). The default cannot vary by environment because there is no
  value to default.

**Severity:** Medium. The environment dimension is one of the five
composition axes; its claimed effects do not materialise.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/install.go:567-573`
  (collected) and `:520-526` (only echoed to header)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` (no
  `.Values.environment` reference)
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:185-230`
  (`monitoring` block has no `acknowledgeNoPrometheus` key)

- **Resolution:** The `environment` dimension now drives a concrete, rendered chart effect. A new `lenny.gatewayLogLevel` helper maps the pre-existing top-level `environment` value (the §17.5.2 KMS posture, reused as the §17.9.1 dimension) to gateway log verbosity: `local`/`dev` render `LENNY_LOG_LEVEL=debug`, `staging`/`prod` render `info`; the gateway already reads `LENNY_LOG_LEVEL` (`pkg/observability/logging.Setup`). `gateway-deployment.yaml` renders the env from the helper. The missing `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus: false` value was added (the §17.6 Prometheus-reachability preflight and §25.4 line 819 reference it; Tier 2/3 presets keep it false so a missing Prometheus is blocking there). The wizard writes `environment` into the composed values (F-17.9.6) so a wizard install reacts too. `LENNY_DEV_MODE` (via `global.devMode`), TLS strictness (via `backends`), and alert thresholds (tier presets) remain the existing mechanisms; this finding's gap was that `.Values.environment` drove nothing rendered, which the log-level helper resolves. Commit `002091e4`. Tested: helm-unittest `LENNY_LOG_LEVEL=debug` (default dev) / `info` (prod).

`runtimescaffold` templates are a separate developer-scaffold concern and stay
per-runtime; this finding is the chart-wide seeded-runtime default.)

### - [ ] F-17.9.13 — `postgres.readDsn` (read-replica reader endpoint) is not a Helm value [Medium] — DEFERRED

**Spec:** §17.9.3 (line 1400): "`readDsn: 'postgres://...'  # Read
replica endpoint (provider reader endpoint)"

**Impl:** `charts/lenny/values.yaml:259-284` defines only
`postgres.dsn`. No `readDsn`. `grep -rn 'readDsn\|read_dsn\|read.replica'
charts/ pkg/gateway/` returns zero matches.

**Severity:** Medium. The gateway has no plumbing to route read-only
queries to a read replica; whether the gateway code already
distinguishes read-only paths is out of scope for §17.9 but the
operator-facing knob is missing either way.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:259-284`

- **Deferred:** The gateway has no read/write-split store layer. It constructs a single `*pgxpool.Pool` from `--postgres-dsn` (plus the optional `--postgres-billing-audit-dsn` for the §12.3 R-03 split), and the `storerouter.StoreRouter` interface exposes only write-or-either shard pools — there is no `ReadShard`/read-pool seam, and read-heavy callers (session status, task tree, audit reads, usage reports) read through the primary. §12.3 line 146 is a SHOULD. Adding only a `postgres.readDsn` Helm value + gateway env would be a hollow knob (rule O): the gateway would open a pool nothing routes to. Read-replica routing is a dedicated store-layer effort (thread a read pool through the read-only query paths) and is deferred to that batch; the Helm value lands with it.

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.9.7 — Both report that the §17.9.2 CI lint of answer files against values.schema.json cannot run because no values.schema.json exists and the Go struct test is not equivalent.

test suite; this is the closest mechanism. However:

- The validation surface is the wizard's struct, not the chart's

  through `helm template -f <answer> -f presets/values-tierN.yaml`.

**Severity:** Medium. Partial coverage of the documented intent.

**Files:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/install_test.go:559`
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/.github/workflows/release.yml:294`

**Resolution:** Closed by F-17.6.5 (duplicate of F-17.9.7). The precise gap this finding names — "a file that validates against `installAnswers` may still produce an invalid chart values document if the `composeValues` mapping breaks" — is now caught: tier-3 `TestComposedAnswerFilesConformToChartSchema` parses each shipped wizard answer file, runs it through `composeValues`, and validates the composed chart-values document against the generated `values.schema.json`. The validation surface is now the chart's values shape (via the composed output), not the wizard struct. Runs in the standard `go test` CI job. Commit `a58506ad`.

## §23.1 Why Lenny? <a id="23.1"></a>
Spec subsection audited: `spec/23_competitive-landscape.md` §23.1 "Why Lenny?", lines 68–116 (eight architectural differentiators 1–8, eight additional capabilities 9–16, trade-offs paragraph).

Implementation tree audited: repository-wide. §23.1 is positioning prose, so the testable claims are forward-references to specific spec sections plus the names of components, RPCs, interfaces, and protocols those sections cover. Each numbered differentiator was checked against the cited implementation paths.

Method: read §23.1 end-to-end; extract each differentiator's testable claims (capability names, integration levels, RPC names, interface names, endpoint paths, isolation profile names, phase enums, propagation modes, file counts); cross-check against the implementation tree using grep + targeted reads.

### Summary

§23.1 is overwhelmingly accurate as positioning copy. The eight architectural differentiators (1–8) all map to concrete code paths, and the eight additional platform capabilities (9–16) all surface in the gateway or adjacent binaries. The trade-off paragraph honestly names the costs Lenny pays for the differentiators it claims.

Two material inaccuracies stand out and warrant fixes:

1. **§23.1 differentiator 6 overclaims MCP Tasks at the gateway's external MCP interface.** The MCP edge (`pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go`) handles only `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. The MCP Tasks protocol methods (`tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/result`) are not registered; only the internal task state machine and the protocol-state mapping function (`pkg/task/state/state.go`) exist. The §15.2 audit (`/tmp/lenny-build-gaps/15.2.md`, F-15.2.x) documents this gap independently.
2. **§23.1 capability 9 names "round-robin or weighted selection" but no `weighted` strategy exists.** Spec §4.9 line 1587–1589 and `pkg/credential/credential.go:58-60` both enumerate exactly three strategies: `least-loaded`, `round-robin`, `sticky-until-failure`. The §23.1 phrasing introduces "weighted" as a fourth strategy that has no implementation or normative definition anywhere else in the spec.

A handful of smaller inaccuracies surface around: a missing `CredentialRouter` interface that §23.1 capability 9 names as "pluggable" (only `pkg/gateway/credassign` exists with no swap point); a missing `GuardrailsInterceptor` built-in named in capability 10; the action enum is documented as "ALLOW, DENY, or MODIFY" while spec §4.8 and the proto define the middle action as `REJECT`; "health scoring" framing that is in fact a boolean `Healthy` flag, not a score; and a wrong cross-reference ("Section 8, Principle 5") that does not resolve in §8 (the design philosophy section has no numbered principles).

Every other claim — runtime types `agent` + `mcp`, three execution modes, three isolation profiles, 13 interceptor phases, REST + MCP (`initialize`/`tools/*`) + OpenAI Chat + Open Responses surfaces, hash-chained audit, GDPR erasure with billing pseudonymization via `erasure_salt`, 6-phase tenant deletion lifecycle, session replay modes `prompt_history`/`workspace_derive`, HMAC-SHA256 bucketing, three propagation modes (`inherit`/`control`/`independent`), three sticky modes (`user`/`session`/`none`), pluggable `MemoryStore` with pgvector default, the `SemanticCache` interface, scale-to-zero, billing event stream with monotonic sequence numbers, SIEM forwarding, SPIFFE-bound leases — has direct, named backing in the implementation.

### Findings

### 23.1-MED-001 — Differentiator 6 claim "Lenny implements MCP Tasks at the gateway's external MCP interface" is unimplemented

**Severity: Medium.** §23.1 marks this as an "architectural commitment reflected in the spec sections cited, not roadmap aspirations" (line 70), yet the MCP Tasks methods are not wired at the external MCP surface.

**Spec text (§23.1 line 82):** "Lenny implements MCP Tasks at the gateway's external MCP interface ([Section 9](09_mcp-integration.md)); internal delegation between gateway and agent pods uses a custom gRPC protocol with equivalent semantics."

**Evidence:**
- `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:200-215` is the gateway's external MCP method dispatcher. The `switch req.Method` only handles `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. There is no `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/result`, or `tasks/create` dispatch.
- `pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go:20-21` self-documents the gap: "Streaming (the MCP Streamable-HTTP SSE channel) is post-v1 in this minimal adapter — every method returns a single JSON-RPC response."
- `pkg/task/state/state.go:72-93` implements `MCPProtocolState` — the state-to-string mapping the Tasks protocol needs — but this function is consumed only by tests (`pkg/task/state/state_test.go`) and is not invoked from any MCP request handler.
- The 15.2 build-gap audit (`/tmp/lenny-build-gaps/15.2.md` F-15.2 cluster) independently documents that the entire MCP Streamable-HTTP transport, `attach_session`, `notifications/tasks/statusUpdate`, MCP Tasks final-state frames, and elicitation/streaming dispatchers are unimplemented at the gateway edge.

**Affected paths:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/mcp/mcp.go` — handler dispatch, no Tasks methods.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/task/state/state.go` — protocol-state mapping that is never called from the MCP surface.

### 23.1-MED-002 — Capability 9 names "round-robin or weighted selection" but no `weighted` strategy exists

**Severity: Medium.** The §23.1 differentiator names a strategy that contradicts spec §4.9 and the implementation, both of which list a different three-element enum.

**Spec text (§23.1 line 92):** "Credential pools with round-robin or weighted selection, health scoring, automatic failover, and emergency revocation."

**Evidence:**
- Spec §4.9 lines 1587–1589 documents exactly three strategies: `least-loaded` (default), `round-robin`, `sticky-until-failure`.
- `pkg/credential/credential.go:58-65` defines the closed enum: `StrategyLeastLoaded`, `StrategyRoundRobin`, `StrategyStickyUntilFailure`, with `AllAssignmentStrategies()` returning exactly those three.
- A repository-wide search for `weighted` / `Weighted` in `pkg/credential/` and `pkg/gateway/credentialpool*/` returns zero matches. The string never appears anywhere in code, schema, or other spec sections.
- The implementation also has no "health scoring" — `pkg/credential/select.go:21-23` defines `Healthy bool` on `CredentialCandidate`, a binary flag, not a score; `nextHealthy` (`select.go:106-115`) walks past unhealthy candidates without ranking.

**Affected paths:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/23_competitive-landscape.md:92` — phrasing names "weighted" and "health scoring".
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/04_system-components.md:1583-1589` — actual three strategies named.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/credential/credential.go:58-65` — implementation enum.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/credential/select.go:21-23` — `Healthy` is a bool.

### 23.1-MED-003 — `CredentialRouter` named in capability 9 has no implementation

**Severity: Medium.** §23.1 capability 9 names "Pluggable `CredentialRouter` interface for cost-aware, latency-based, or intent-based routing across providers" but no such interface exists.

**Spec text (§23.1 line 92):** "Pluggable `CredentialRouter` interface for cost-aware, latency-based, or intent-based routing across providers."

**Evidence:**
- Spec §4.9 lines 1558–1591 does define the `CredentialRouter` interface (the spec source the §23.1 sentence pulls from), but a repository-wide `grep -rn 'CredentialRouter\|credentialrouter'` returns zero matches in `pkg/`, `cmd/`, or `sdks/`.
- `pkg/gateway/credassign/credassign.go:26-50` defines the `Assigner` interface that owns credential assignment. The Assigner is hard-coded to use the pool's `assignmentStrategy` field (`pkg/credential/select.go:SelectCredential`) — there is no swap point for cost-aware, latency-based, or intent-based routing. The "hints map" extension point the spec §4.9 paragraph 1591 describes is absent.
- `pkg/gateway/credassign/credassign.go:32` self-documents the seam: "Assigner is the shared §4.9 credential-assignment surface the gateway depends on" — but only one implementation (`Service`) and one client adapter (`Client`) exist; the interface is for in-process vs out-of-process Token Service, not for a deployer-pluggable router.

**Affected paths:**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/credassign/` — no `CredentialRouter` interface, no `hints` map.

### 23.1-LOW-004 — `GuardrailsInterceptor` built-in is named by §23.1 and §4.8 but has no implementation

**Severity: Low.** §23.1 capability 10 names a built-in `GuardrailsInterceptor` that is also documented in spec §4.8 line 976 (priority 400, disabled by default). Neither the built-in interceptor itself nor any of the wiring described in §4.8 line 1070 exists in code.

**Spec text (§23.1 line 94):** "The `GuardrailsInterceptor` (disabled by default) provides the hook point for external content classifiers (AWS Bedrock Guardrails, Azure Content Safety, Lakera Guard, or custom gRPC services)."

**Evidence:**
- `grep -rn 'Guardrail\|guardrail' pkg/` returns zero matches anywhere in the gateway, adapter, or controller code.
- Spec §4.8 lines 976 and 1070 name `GuardrailsInterceptor` as a priority-400 built-in that runs at `PreDelegation`, `PreLLMRequest`, `PostLLMResponse`, and `PostAgentOutput`. The §23.1 sentence pulls from that table.
- Of the built-in evaluators named in §4.8 (AuthEvaluator, QuotaEvaluator, DelegationPolicyEvaluator, GuardrailsInterceptor, RetryPolicyEvaluator), only `QuotaEvaluator` is implemented (`pkg/gateway/policy/quotaevaluator.go`). The others are referenced from spec-side `interceptor_name` constants but have no evaluator code.
- The 13 interceptor phases (capability 10) themselves are implemented and named exactly as the §23.1 sentence enumerates (`pkg/gateway/interceptor/interceptor.go:34-49` lists `PhasePreAuth` through `PhasePostConnectorResponse`), and the external `RequestInterceptor` gRPC service is wired (`pkg/proto/interceptor/v1/lenny-interceptor_grpc.pb.go`). A deployer who registers an external interceptor at `PostAgentOutput` / `PreLLMRequest` gets the same effect; only the named built-in shortcut is missing.

**Affected paths:**

### 23.1-INFO-013 — Trade-off paragraph is honest and accurate

**Severity: Info.** The six trade-offs §23.1 names — workspace materialization latency, credential pool complexity, runtime-author adapter integration cost, no built-in eval scoring, no automatic experiment lifecycle management, pre-warmed pods consuming resources when idle — are each backed by code and operational decisions that match the listed cost:

- `pkg/adapter/workspace/materialize.go` and `pkg/adapter/staging.go` cover the §7.1 step where a session waits for files to land before agent code starts.
- `pkg/credential/credential.go`, `pkg/gateway/credassign/`, and `pkg/gateway/credfallback/` cover pool / lease / fallback machinery.
- §15.4.3 integration levels (Basic / Standard / Full) make the adapter cost explicit; Standard/Full need gRPC.
- `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/eval` (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/eval.go`) is pull-based by design; no statistical inference is computed.
- Experiment lifecycle transitions are admin-driven (`pkg/gateway/admin/experiments.go`); no automatic conclude/pause exists.
- `pkg/controller/warmpool/` maintains pre-warmed pods; spec §6 and Prometheus alerts (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` `WarmPoolBootstrapping`, idle-pod-minutes cost rule) cover the cost surface.

The honesty of the trade-off list is consistent with the project doc-style rule against marketing language; no gaps.

## §23.2 Community Adoption Strategy <a id="23.2"></a>
Spec section: `spec/23_competitive-landscape.md` lines 117–141 (`### 23.2 Community Adoption Strategy`).
Implementation tree audited: repo root, `docs/`, `.github/`, `sdks/`, `charts/`, `packaging/`.

### Testable claims in §23.2

1. Persona "Runtime authors" entry point: runtime adapter contract (§15.4); local dev `lenny up` (Embedded Mode, primary) plus `make run` (Source Mode, contributors).
2. Persona "Platform operators" entry point: Helm chart, `lenny-ctl bootstrap`, Admin API (§15.1).
3. Persona "Enterprise platform teams" entry point: comparison guides and enterprise-controls docs (§4.8, §8, §10).
4. TTHW < 5 minutes target with `lenny up` (Embedded Mode).
5. "CI includes a TTHW smoke test that validates both paths on every merge."
6. Governance model: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `GOVERNANCE.md`, BDfN → steering committee transition criteria, ADR process in `docs/adr/`, public issues + discussions forum.
7. `CONTRIBUTING.md` must include a prominent early-development notice stating the project is in active pre-release development and that unsolicited PRs will not be reviewed or merged until Phase 17a.
8. License resolved to MIT (ADR-008); `LICENSE` file at repo root.
9. v1 runtime-adapter distribution is "standard Go module hosting, container registries, and Helm chart repositories" (community runtime registry is post-v1).
10. Phase 17 deliverable: published comparison guides for Lenny vs E2B, Daytona, Fly.io Sprites, Temporal, Modal, and LangGraph.

### Findings

### - [x] F-23.2.1 — 2-1 — Root `CONTRIBUTING.md` is missing the §23.2-mandated early-development notice (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec claim.** §23.2 says: "The Phase 2 `CONTRIBUTING.md` must include a prominent early-development notice stating that the project is in active pre-release development and that unsolicited PRs will not be reviewed or merged until Phase 17a (community launch)." The spec verb is "must include".

**Evidence.**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/CONTRIBUTING.md` is 35 lines. It contains the strings "design phase", "highest-signal contributions right now are design feedback, not code", and points to `docs/about/contributing.md` for the long-form version, but it does not contain the words "pre-release development", "unsolicited PRs", "will not be reviewed", or "Phase 17a". `grep -in "early\|unsolicited\|active pre-release\|pre.release development"` against the root file returns no matches.
- The long-form `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/about/contributing.md` line 34 carries the substantive notice ("the early phases (Phase 0 through Phase 2) are maintainer-driven; unsolicited PRs against core platform components will not be reviewed or merged").
- §23.2 names the file `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the root file is what GitHub surfaces in the "Contributing" link on the repo page).

**Classification.** Medium. The notice exists, but the spec ties it to the root `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which is what a prospective contributor sees first. The current root file softens the message ("design feedback, not code") without naming Phase 17a or stating the no-merge-of-unsolicited-PRs policy. The remediation is to mirror the two sentences from `docs/about/contributing.md:34` into the root file (or to inline a single explicit sentence).

**Resolution:** Root `CONTRIBUTING.md` now carries a prominent blockquote notice immediately after the intro, stating the project is in active pre-release development, that unsolicited pull requests will not be reviewed or merged until Phase 17a (community launch), that bug reports and discussion are welcome at any phase, and that the notice is removed as part of the Phase 17a review — the verbatim §23.2 line 133 obligation. Closed this batch.

### - [x] F-23.2.2 — 2-2 — Tier-11 TTHW Go test is not invoked by any CI workflow (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-23.2.6 — F-23.2.2 reports the tier-11 TTHW test is not invoked by CI, while F-23.2.6 reports the named tier7b tthw.go benchmark file does not exist; related but different gaps.

**Spec claim.** §23.2: "CI includes a TTHW smoke test that validates both paths on every merge." §18.38 names `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw.go` as the Phase 17a benchmark deliverable, and TESTING.md §22.7 names the documentation gate.

**Evidence.**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go` exists (391 lines), is in the `tier11_docs_test` package, references `§22.7` budget, and is mapped in `tests/spec-map.json` to §22.7.
- `tests/groups.yaml` lists `tier: docs` in both the `pr` and `nightly` groups.
- However, `.github/workflows/pr.yml` does not invoke `lenny-test --group pr` or `lenny-test --tier docs`. The `docs` job (lines 255–278) only runs `markdown-link-check` against `docs/` and `spec/`. `grep -rn "tier11\|--tier docs\|tier: docs" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/.github/workflows/` returns no hits for the test runner.
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` chains `e2e-kind-full`, `e2e-cloud`, `chaos`, `security`, `load`, and `mutation` tiers; it does not run `tier docs`, and the spec deliverable `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw.go` does not exist (the `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/` directory ships `audit_lock`, `checkpoint_duration`, `credential_lifecycle`, etc., but no `tthw.go`).
- BUILD-PROGRESS.md line 62 marks Phase 17a "Done", which is inconsistent with the missing TTHW load scenario.

**Classification.** Medium. The Go-level TTHW assertion exists in-tree but is not part of any merge gate, and the spec-named benchmark file is absent. The §23.2 "every merge" claim is therefore unfulfilled.

**Resolution:** The `docs` job in `.github/workflows/pr.yml` now sets up Go, builds `lenny-test`, and runs `./bin/lenny-test --tier docs`, which executes `tests/tier11_docs/...` including `time_to_hello_world_test.go`. The TTHW gate is therefore part of the per-PR merge gate (§23.2 line 127). Verified locally: `lenny-test --tier docs` passes in ~9s. The separate spec-named load benchmark `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw.go` is F-23.2.6's scope (overlap noted) and remains its own item. Closed this batch.

### - [x] F-23.2.3 — 2-3 — Krew plugin manifest uses placeholder version `v0.0.0` and zero-hash SHA256 across all five platforms (Low) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec claim.** §17.6 / §24.0 (referenced from §23.2 persona table via the Helm-chart + krew install path) and §18.38 ("`kubectl-lenny` krew plugin packaging per §24.0 with a krew-index PR opened by release automation").

**Evidence.**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/packaging/krew/lenny.yaml` declares `spec.version: v0.0.0`, every `uri` points at the `v0.0.0` release archive, and every `sha256` is sixty-four zeros.
- The file's header comment names the placeholder convention ("The version, uri, and sha256 values below are placeholders") and points at the release automation that substitutes them on tag push.
- No tag has been cut, so the krew manifest cannot be applied by a real `kubectl krew install lenny` yet.

**Classification.** Low / Info. The manifest is functionally a template that the release pipeline rewrites, the comment block is explicit about this, and §23.2 does not assert tagged-release availability. Flagged so the audit trail records the placeholder state. The deliverable becomes High once a v1 tag is cut without the substitution running, but that is a release-pipeline concern outside §23.2.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing "The
manifest is functionally a template that the release pipeline
rewrites, the comment block is explicit about this, and §23.2 does
not assert tagged-release availability." The substitution at
`release.yml` tag-push time replaces `v0.0.0` and the zero-hash
SHA256 with the real values before the krew-index PR is opened. The
"becomes High once a v1 tag is cut" condition is a release-pipeline
concern outside §23.2.

### - [x] F-23.2.4 — 2-4 — ADR number cited in §23.2 as `ADR-008`; on-disk file is `ADR-0008` (Low) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Resolution:** Verify-closed. Per the finding's own classification
"`ADR-0008` is the canonical form per the rest of the repo"
(`docs/adr/0007-sandboxclaim-optimistic-locking.md` and the
`docs/adr/0000-*` template both use the four-digit convention).
Reconciling the spec prose to match is rule-B blocked (spec edit
forbidden). The on-disk ADR remains the authoritative artifact.

### - [x] F-23.2.5 — 2-5 — Runtime author publishing doc describes a "community registry" submission flow that §23.2 declares post-v1 (Low) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec claim.** §23.2 line 139: "A community runtime registry — where runtime authors publish versioned adapter packages for operator discovery and installation — is planned as a post-v1 platform service. In v1, runtime adapters are distributed via standard Go module hosting, container registries, and Helm chart repositories."

**Evidence.**
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/runtime-author-guide/publishing.md` line 10: "register it with a Lenny deployment, distribute it as a Go module, and publish to the community registry."
- Same file line 300: "## Community Registry — The Lenny community registry is a catalog of published runtimes. Publishing to the registry makes your runtime discoverable by other Lenny users."
- Same file line 345: "Submit to the registry via pull request to the community registry repository."
- Same file line 347: a "Registry Validation" subsection describes a CI pipeline that "Pulls your published image", "Runs the compliance suite", and "Publishes the entry".
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/about/contributing.md` line 226–228 correctly notes the registry as "planned as a post-v1 platform service".

**Classification.** Low. The publishing doc gives a runtime author the impression that a community registry submission is part of v1, while §23.2 (the spec) is explicit that v1 distribution is Go modules + container registries + Helm chart repositories only. The remediation is to either (a) label the publishing.md community-registry subsection as post-v1, or (b) update §23.2 if the registry has been pulled forward. Without one of those, the spec and the docs disagree.

**Resolution:** Took option (a). `docs/runtime-author-guide/publishing.md`
intro updated to state v1 distribution is Go modules + container
registries + Helm chart repositories and the registry is post-v1; the
"## Community Registry" heading is now "## Community Registry
(planned, post-v1)" with an inline pointer to §23.2 and a v1-fallback
note.

- **Persona 1 / runtime authors (claim 1).** The runtime adapter contract is documented at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/runtime-author-guide/adapter-contract.md` and `integration-levels.md`. `lenny up` is wired in `cmd/lenny/main.go:55` (the `case "up"` dispatch); `make run` is the Makefile target at line 109–110. SDKs ship under `sdks/runtime/{go,python,typescript}` with the §15.4.1 frame loop and the §15.4.2 state machine.
- **Persona 2 / platform operators (claim 2).** Helm chart at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/` (Chart.yaml v0.1.0, templates for gateway, controller, lenny-ops, Token Service, web playground, webhooks, NetworkPolicies, RBAC, PrometheusRule, ServiceMonitor, bootstrap Job). `lenny-ctl bootstrap` is wired at `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:485` (`cmdBootstrap`, drives `POST /v1/admin/bootstrap`). Admin API surface lives at `pkg/gateway/...` and §15.1.
- **Persona 3 / enterprise platform teams (claim 3).** Comparison guides live at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/about/comparisons.md`, with H2 sections for each of the six §23.2-named platforms (Lenny vs E2B, Daytona, Fly.io Sprites, Temporal, Modal, LangGraph/LangSmith) plus extra coverage for Google Scion, NVIDIA OpenShell, and Alibaba OpenSandbox. The §23.2 "Phase 17 deliverable" (claim 10) is therefore satisfied; BUILD-PROGRESS marks Phase 17a Done.
- **Governance (claim 6).** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/GOVERNANCE.md` carries the BDfN model and the transition criteria (3+ regular contributors per the §23.2 wording). `docs/about/governance.md` is the long-form version. ADR process is documented at `docs/adr/index.md` and ADR-0000 sets the MADR-3.0.0 template, with ADR-0007 and ADR-0008 as the worked examples. `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant v2.1) and `SECURITY.md` (GitHub private vulnerability reporting; 72h ack, 7d assessment, 90d remediation target) are present. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,feature_request,config}.{md,yml}` and `.github/workflows/dco.yml` (DCO sign-off check on every PR) are wired.

### Method notes

- Searched for the §23.2-named files in the repo root and under `docs/`, `.github/`, `sdks/`, `charts/`, `packaging/`.
- Read the spec section once and translated each substantive sentence into a falsifiable check (file present / string present / CI step invoked / ADR mapped).
- For TTHW, cross-referenced `tests/groups.yaml`, `tests/spec-map.json`, `.github/workflows/pr.yml`, `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, and the in-tree TTHW test source.
- For governance and CONTRIBUTING, checked both the root file and the long-form `docs/about/` counterpart, because §23.2 names the root-level file.

### Severity calibration

- High would apply to a missing license, a missing CODE_OF_CONDUCT, or a security-disclosure gap. None present.
- Medium covers the two spec-mandated behaviors that are silently unmet today (the early-dev notice not being in the root CONTRIBUTING, and the merge-gate TTHW smoke not running).
- Low covers cosmetic / documentation-internal inconsistencies that will not block adoption but should be reconciled.
- Info covers cross-section artifacts (the missing Phase 17a tier-7 TTHW load scenario) that the audit surfaces for the reader's record without proposing a §23.2 spec change.
