## §25.2 Architecture Overview <a id="25.2"></a>
Reviewed: 2026-05-23.

Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` lines 128–406 (heading `## 25.2 Architecture Overview`, ending at `## 25.3 Gateway-Side Ops Endpoints`).

§25.2 establishes the two-deployment split (gateway + `lenny-ops`), enumerates the gateway-side ops-facing endpoints, lists the `lenny-ops` subsystems and the external dependencies the binary connects to, and codifies the cross-section API conventions (degradation envelope, pagination/cursors/gap detection, dry-run/confirm pattern, error envelope with categories, filter parameter names, operation correlation headers, canonical progress envelope, and the `ops_operation_baselines` table). Most of these conventions are normative — every §25.3+ endpoint reuses them by reference.

### Method

Read §25.2 in full. Enumerated normative architecture elements:

1. **The Split** — gateway hosts client traffic, admin API, ops-facing endpoints (health/recommendations/platform/events-buffer), `/metrics` (Prometheus scrape target), and the EventEmitter writing to Redis stream + in-memory ring buffer (lines 132–153).
2. `lenny-ops` Deployment hosts: Operational Event Stream (25.5), Diagnostic Endpoints (25.6), Runbook Index (25.7), Platform Upgrade Orchestration (25.8), Audit Log Query (25.9), Configuration Drift Detection (25.10), Backup and Restore (25.11), MCP Management Server (25.12) (lines 155–171).
3. `lenny-ops` connects to: Postgres, Redis, K8s API, MinIO, Prometheus, Gateway admin API (line 169–170).
4. `lenny-ops` is **external-only** via an Ingress — no internal cluster workload reaches it (line 43, NetworkPolicy boundary).
5. **Split criterion table** (lines 178–186) — features requiring in-process state live in the gateway; the rest live in `lenny-ops`.
6. **Terminology** (lines 192–200): in-memory, in-process, gateway-local, platform-scoped, shared-state.
7. **Canonical Degradation Envelope** (lines 202–232): `degradation.{level, primarySource, actualSource, fallbackPath, confidence, unavailableFields, thresholdSource, warnings, since}`; omitted when healthy.
8. **Pagination** (lines 234–275): canonical `cursor / limit / since / until / sortOrder` params; response envelope with `pagination.{cursor, hasMore, limit, cursorKind, headCursor}`; cursors opaque; `gapDetected` recovery.
9. **Dry-Run / Confirm Pattern** (lines 277–300): mutating endpoints accept `confirm:true`; without it return 200 + dry-run preview; `acknowledgeDataLoss` style fields return 400 once confirm is supplied but acknowledgment is missing.
10. **Error Response Envelope** (lines 302–329): `error.{code, category, message, retryable, suggestedRetryAfter, details, documentationUrl}`; categories `TRANSIENT / PERMANENT / POLICY / AUTH`; `Retry-After` mirrors `suggestedRetryAfter`.
11. **Filter Parameter Naming** (lines 331–344): canonical names for `eventType / severity / resourceType / resourceId / tenantId / actorId / status / since / until`.
12. **Operation Correlation Headers** (lines 346–353): `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` and `X-Lenny-Agent-Name` are advisory; propagated to audit/operational events/structured logs.
13. **Canonical Progress Envelope** (lines 355–403): `progress.{percent, completedSteps, totalSteps, currentStep, currentStepDetail, etaSeconds, etaConfidence, etaMethod, rateMetric, startedAt, lastProgressAt, stalledForSeconds}`; `ops_operation_baselines (kind, p50_duration_ms, p90_duration_ms, sample_size, last_updated)` Postgres table; `operation_progressed` events at step transitions and `{10,25,50,75,90,95,99}` percent thresholds; `OperationStalled` bundled alert wired off `stalledForSeconds`.

Evidence gathered via grep/find across `pkg/ops/`, `cmd/lenny-ops/`, `pkg/gateway/admin/`, `pkg/gateway/opsevents/`, `pkg/gateway/health/`, `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/`, `charts/lenny/templates/`, and `migrations/`.

### Findings

### - [x] F-25.2.1 — Gateway-side operational `EventEmitter` does not write to the Redis stream. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.3.1, F-25.3.18, F-25.5.1 — Four members describe the gateway EventEmitter never writing to the Redis ops:events:stream, and two describe the unimplemented SSE /v1/admin/events/stream endpoint; the lag gauge and CLOSED service findings are distinct.

**Resolution:** Stale evidence. The producer half landed when `events.StreamEmitter` (`pkg/gateway/events/streamemitter.go`) was wired into `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` (and the controller and token-service): when Redis is available, every `Emit` XADDs the event to `ops:events:stream` with `MAXLEN ~ DefaultStreamMaxLen` and always tees a copy into the in-process `EventBuffer` (the §25.5 fallback), inverting the previous buffer-only behavior back to the spec model. The consumer half (the read side the gateway producer feeds) is the new `RedisEventSource` from commit 97ae8442. Closed by 97ae8442 (consumer) plus the prior StreamEmitter wiring.

Spec: lines 150–152 — "Internal: EventEmitter writes to **Redis stream** on state changes + in-memory ring buffer (fallback for Redis outage)". The ASCII diagram explicitly names the Redis stream as the primary destination and the in-memory buffer as the *fallback* the `lenny-ops` event stream reads "when Redis is down" (also reaffirmed at line 158: "reads Redis stream, falls back to gw buffer").

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go` lines 15–18 and 40–51 — `Emit` writes only to the in-process `EventBuffer`. The Redis-stream destination is acknowledged as a documented seam ("v1 writes each event to the in-process EventBuffer; the §25.3 Redis-stream destination is added alongside the §10.1 Redis EventBus"). Confirmed by `grep -rn "ops:events:stream\|XAdd" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/`: zero matches. Consequence: under §25.2's intended architecture the Redis stream is the *primary* destination and the in-memory ring buffer is a *fallback for Redis outage*; the implementation inverts this — every event lives only in the per-replica ring buffer (lost on restart, invisible across replicas). The `lenny-ops` operational event stream consumer (§25.5) currently has no Redis stream to read from; `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go` lines 41–61 wires `emptyEventSource{}` / `emptySubscriptionSource{}` to the webhook delivery worker for exactly this reason. The split described at line 150 is not yet realised in either direction (the gateway does not publish, the ops consumer cannot subscribe).

### - [x] F-25.2.2 — `lenny-ops` `/metrics` Prometheus scrape target is not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 148 and 169 implicitly, and §25.4 / the NetworkPolicy and PodMonitor wiring at `charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` lines 84–86 + `system-network-policies.yaml` lines 676–683 explicitly — `lenny-ops` pods expose Prometheus metrics that the monitoring namespace scrapes on `ops.metricsPort` (default `9090`, mapped onto the same HTTP listener as the §25 surface per the chart comment "the binary serves /metrics on the same mux as the §25 HTTP surface; the §13.2 NET-045 monitoring-scrape NetworkPolicy and podmonitor.yaml scrape it").

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go` lines 150–168 register `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/v1/admin/diagnostics/connectivity`, `/v1/admin/runbooks`, `/v1/admin/runbooks/{name}/steps`, `/v1/admin/ops/health`, and the various sub-route registrars, then `/mcp/management*`. No `/metrics` handler is registered on the `opsserver.Server` mux. `grep -n "/metrics\|MetricsHandler\|promhttp" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` returns zero matches. The `cmd/lenny-ops` binary serves only the `opsserver.New(...)` mux on `*addr` (main.go lines 303–319). Consequence: the chart annotates pods with `prometheus.io/scrape: "true"` and the `allow-ops` NetworkPolicy admits scrapes on `ops.metricsPort`, but every scrape returns 404. No `lenny-ops` self-metrics reach Prometheus — the §25.4 self-health monitor's `lenny_ops_*` metrics, the `OperationStalled` alert source, and any leader-election / loop-runner instrumentation are unscrapeable.

**Resolution:** Stale evidence — resolved by 316d6e21. `pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go` now registers `GET /metrics` on the server mux (the `Options.Metrics` handler, defaulting to `promhttp.Handler()` over the process default registry), exempt from the §25.4 OIDC gate per the §13.2 NET-045 scrape NetworkPolicy. `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` wires `Metrics: promhttp.Handler()`, and the binary registers its self-health and upgrade collectors on the default registry so the §16.9 scrape reflects them. The `OperationStalled` alert source half is the separate `stalledForSeconds` progress instrumentation tracked by F-25.2.7/F-25.2.14.

### - [x] F-25.2.3 — Canonical degradation envelope is not a wired-in cross-cutting primitive. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 202–232 — the degradation envelope is the **canonical response-level signal for every endpoint whose data quality depends on external dependency availability** (line 223). Endpoints "serving from their primary source omit `degradation` entirely (or return `level:healthy` with no other fields set)" (line 232). The envelope fields `level / primarySource / actualSource / fallbackPath / confidence / unavailableFields / thresholdSource / warnings / since` are normative, with `thresholdSource` specifically called out for health and recommendations responses.

Implementation: `grep -rn '"degradation"\|primarySource\|fallbackPath\|thresholdSource\|unavailableFields' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/` returns no hits in any handler that emits an admin/ops response (gateway health/recommendations, ops connectivity, drift, locks, escalations, backup, diagnostics, MCP management). No shared package (`pkg/ops/conventions`, `pkg/observability/degradation`, etc.) defines a `Degradation` struct or marshaller. The `lenny-ops` connectivity endpoint at `pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go` lines 230–245 returns `{dependencies, healthy}` instead of a degradation envelope; the gateway health handler at `pkg/gateway/health/handler.go` likewise emits a flat per-component shape. Consequence: every degradation-eligible endpoint either omits the envelope or invents its own shape, which the rest of §25 (the §25.5 event stream, §25.6 diagnostics, §25.13 alerts) is then unable to interpret uniformly. Agents cannot use `degradation.confidence` to decide how much to trust a response, cannot follow `degradation.fallbackPath` for retry strategy, and cannot tell from `thresholdSource` whether health/recommendations rules are compiled-in defaults or operator-customised.

**Resolution:** Stale evidence — resolved by prior batches. The shared `pkg/ops/conventions.Degradation` struct now carries the full normative field set (`level / primarySource / actualSource / fallbackPath / confidence / unavailableFields / thresholdSource / warnings / since`), and it is wired as a cross-cutting primitive on the degradation-eligible endpoints: the gateway health `Report` (`pkg/gateway/health/service.go:287`), the capacity-recommendations response (`pkg/gateway/recommendations/service.go:293`), and the Operations Inventory page (`pkg/ops/operations/inventory.go:243`); the §25.6 diagnostics report structs (`pkg/ops/diagnostics/service.go`) carry the field. Health/recommendations stamp `level` + `thresholdSource` (asserted by `TestReportStampsThresholdSource_spec_25_13_4848` and the recommendations equivalent). The finding's connectivity-endpoint example is spec-defensible as-is: the §25.6 connectivity probe reports per-dependency reachability directly, so its data quality does not degrade from a fallback (spec line 204). Wiring landed across c4f70777 (health/recommendations thresholdSource) and the conventions package (655426b9/8cc36492).

### - [x] F-25.2.4 — Canonical pagination envelope, cursor/`gapDetected` semantics not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: medium) — F-25.3.17 — Both describe the buffer endpoint lacking the canonical §25.2 pagination envelope, with gap fields emitted at the response root instead of under pagination.

Spec: lines 234–275. List endpoints accept `cursor / limit / since / until / sortOrder`; responses carry `items + pagination.{cursor, hasMore, limit, cursorKind, headCursor}`; cursors are opaque; gap detection includes `gapDetected: true`, `gapReason`, `oldestAvailableCursor`, `suggestedAction:"resync"`.

Implementation: `grep -rn 'cursorKind\|headCursor\|gapDetected\|oldestAvailableCursor' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/` returns no matches outside of test fixtures. The §25.3 buffer endpoint (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go` lines 51–81) accepts only `since`, `eventType`, `severity`, `limit` and returns whatever `EventBuffer.Query` produces — no `pagination` object, no `cursorKind`, no head-cursor signal. The §25.4 list endpoints under `pkg/ops/opsserver/{locks,escalations,event_subscriptions}.go` and the §25.11 backup-list endpoint do not emit the canonical envelope either. Consequence: agents that follow §25.2 expecting `pagination.cursorKind` to disambiguate cursor flavour and `gapDetected` to trigger a resync see neither; cursor-incompatibility traversals (a refinement called out at line 260 — "agents treat cursor incompatibility as a gap and reset") cannot be coded against this surface because the signal does not exist.

**Resolution:** Stale evidence — resolved by 662adf20. The §25.3 buffer endpoint now returns the canonical pagination envelope: `pkg/gateway/events/buffer.go` `Pagination` carries `cursor / hasMore / limit / cursorKind ("buffer-seq") / headCursor / gapDetected / gapReason / oldestAvailableCursor / suggestedAction ("resync")`, and the ops event-source mirror (`pkg/ops/events/interface.go:80-87`) carries `cursorKind / headCursor / oldestAvailableCursor`. The HTTP handler asserts the envelope at the wire level (`TestEventBufferEndpointCSVFilter_spec_25_3_15` checks `page.Pagination.CursorKind == "buffer-seq"`). The §25.4 list endpoints parse `cursor / limit / since / until / sortOrder` via `conventions.ParsePageParams`. The flagged duplicate F-25.3.17 (gap fields at response root vs under `pagination`) was already CLOSED by the same change.

### - [x] F-25.2.5 — Canonical dry-run / confirm pattern not enforced uniformly. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 277–300. The pattern applies to `PUT /v1/admin/pools/{name}/warm-count` (when change >50% of current), `PUT /v1/admin/platform/config`, `POST /v1/admin/backups` (full backups in production), `POST /v1/admin/restore/execute`, `POST /v1/admin/drift/reconcile`. Without `confirm:true`, endpoints return 200 + `dryRun:true` + `preview.{resourcesAffected, estimatedDowntime, warnings}`. Endpoints requiring an additional acknowledgment field (e.g., `acknowledgeDataLoss:true`) return 400 with an actionable error once `confirm:true` is supplied but the ack is missing.

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go` and `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/platform.go` — `grep -n 'dryRun\|confirm' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/platform.go` returns no `confirm`/`dryRun` handling in either. The §25.11 backup-creation endpoint (`pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go` and `pkg/ops/backup/service.go`) does implement the `Confirm` flag and the `production` gate (`cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go` lines 92–98), but `dryRun:true` + `preview.{resourcesAffected, estimatedDowntime, warnings}` is not part of its response shape. `pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go` — `grep -n 'dryRun\|preview\|resourcesAffected' pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go` returns zero matches; the §25.10 reconcile endpoint does not return a canonical preview. Consequence: the cross-cutting safety primitive that §25 banks on (an agent can always "preview before mutate") is missing on the three highest-blast-radius mutating endpoints (pool warm-count, platform config, drift reconcile), and partially missing on backup/restore (the `dryRun` semantic isn't on the response shape even when `Confirm: true` is honoured).

**Resolution:** Verify-closed plus one fix. Prior batches already wired the §25.2 dry-run/confirm preview onto pool warm-count (`pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go` `handleUpdatePoolWarmCount`), platform config (F-25.8.5 configservice), drift reconcile + snapshot refresh (`pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go`), and restore/execute (`backup.RestoreRequest.Confirm`/`AcknowledgeDataLoss`, with the 400 `RESTORE_ACKNOWLEDGE_REQUIRED` path). The remaining gap was backup creation, which returned a 400 `RESTORE_REQUIRES_CONFIRM` instead of the §25.2-mandated 200 + dry-run preview when a production full backup omitted `confirm`. Added `backup.PreviewBackup`/`backup.CreatePreview` (resourcesAffected/estimatedDowntime/warnings) and made `handleCreateBackup` short-circuit to `200 {dryRun:true, preview}` (no row inserted); the orchestrator keeps its confirm gate as a library-level guard. spec: §25.2 lines 287-300, §25.11 line 3883. Commit 4855b646.

### - [x] F-25.2.6 — Canonical error response envelope with `category`/`retryable`/`suggestedRetryAfter` not implemented uniformly. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 302–329. Every error returns `error.{code, category, message, retryable, suggestedRetryAfter, details, documentationUrl}`. Categories are `TRANSIENT / PERMANENT / POLICY / AUTH`. `Retry-After` HTTP header mirrors `suggestedRetryAfter`. "Every error code defined in this section includes a `Category` in its error-codes table" (line 329).

Implementation: `grep -rn 'suggestedRetryAfter\|documentationUrl\|"category"' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/admin/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/opsserver/` returns no hits. The gateway admin error helper (`writeError` referenced from `pkg/gateway/admin/bootstrap.go` lines 60–65) emits `{code, message, details}` without `category`, `retryable`, or `suggestedRetryAfter`. The §25.12 MCP management server (`pkg/ops/mcpmgmt/server.go` lines 218–236, 268–277) does map `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` and `SCOPE_FORBIDDEN` to `data.{code, retryable}` but neither `category` nor `suggestedRetryAfter` is populated. The §25.11 backup error path in `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go` writes raw HTTP statuses without the canonical envelope. Consequence: every error code defined later in §25 cites a `Category` in its error-codes table (line 329 explicit promise) that never appears on the wire. Agents cannot programmatically distinguish a transient 5xx from a policy 409 without category-specific code lookup tables; the `Retry-After` advisory mechanism is non-functional because `suggestedRetryAfter` is never emitted.

**Resolution:** The gateway admin `writeError` (`pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go`) now emits the §15.1/§25.2 envelope `error.{code, category, message, retryable, suggestedRetryAfter?, details?}`, sourcing `category`/`retryable` from the shared §15.2.1 `errorclassify` catalog so the admin surface reports the same pair as REST and MCP. Added `errorclassify.ClassifyStatus(code, status)` + `errorclassify.Known(code)` so the admin API's large bespoke-code vocabulary derives a status-appropriate pair (429/5xx → TRANSIENT retryable; other 4xx → PERMANENT non-retryable) instead of the provisional `(TRANSIENT, true)` fallback that would wrongly mark a 404 retryable. A retryable 429/5xx admin error now stamps `suggestedRetryAfter` + a matching `Retry-After` header (5s default, overridable via `writeErrorRetryAfter`). The §25.12 MCP management server error `data` now carries `category` alongside `code`/`retryable` (SCOPE_FORBIDDEN→AUTH, ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE→TRANSIENT). The §25.11 backup/drift opsserver paths already routed through `conventions.WriteError`. Gateway admin uses the §16.3 taxonomy (UPSTREAM); lenny-ops uses the §25.2 taxonomy (AUTH). spec: §15.1 line 944, line 972; §25.2 lines 302-329. Commit 4855b646.

### - [x] F-25.2.7 — Canonical progress envelope and `ops_operation_baselines` table not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 355–403. Every long-running operation (platform upgrades, restores, backups, backup verifications, drift reconciliations, webhook backlog drains) includes a `progress` object in their status endpoint responses **and** in the Operations Inventory (§25.4). The envelope's `etaMethod` values, `etaConfidence` thresholds, and the `historical_p50` baseline derivation are all normative. The `ops_operation_baselines (kind, p50_duration_ms, p90_duration_ms, sample_size, last_updated)` Postgres table "is updated on each operation completion" (line 397). Progress events emit on step transitions OR `percent` crossings of `{10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95, 99}` (line 401). `OperationStalled` bundled alert fires off `stalledForSeconds > 0` (line 399).

Implementation: `grep -rn 'ops_operation_baselines\|etaMethod\|etaConfidence\|stalledForSeconds\|operation_progressed\|rateMetric' /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations/` returns no matches. No `progress` object on any ops endpoint response. No `ops_operation_baselines` migration. The §25.11 backup service (`pkg/ops/backup/service.go`) tracks job lifecycle but does not surface `progress`. The §25.5 webhook delivery worker (`pkg/ops/opsservice/webhookloop.go`) has no `stalledForSeconds` instrumentation. `OperationStalled` is not in the alert catalog (verified by `grep -rn "OperationStalled" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/`). Consequence: every long-running operation in §25.8/25.10/25.11 returns a non-canonical status shape that omits the universal fields agents need to display progress UX, estimate completion, or detect stalls. The progress-events fan-out at `{10,25,50,75,90,95,99}` percent thresholds (line 401) is also absent — agents cannot subscribe to `operation_progressed` to avoid polling.

**Resolution:** Wired the normative §25.2 progress-envelope behaviors end to end (the `conventions.Progress` envelope and `operations.Compute` ETA chain already existed but had no production caller). (1) New `ops_operation_baselines` table (migration 0128) + `operations.MemoryBaselineStore` (exact nearest-rank p50/p90 over a bounded sample window) + `pkg/ops/baselinestore` Postgres store (mirrors the aggregate, falls back to the persisted row for the cross-replica/post-restart path). The upgrade orchestrator records the platform_upgrade completion duration on its Complete transition via a new `upgradeservice.BaselineRecorder` seam (a rollback is not recorded). (2) `operations.Compute` now gates `historical_p50` on `SampleSize >= HistoricalP50MinSamples (3)` (§25.2 line 394) and makes `stalledForSeconds` cadence-relative (`max(0, now-lastProgressAt - ExpectedCadence)`, null within cadence; per-kind cadence in `operations.ExpectedCadence`). (3) The Inventory enriches every in-progress operation's Progress through that chain on each List/Get (`SetProgressBaselines`), drawing the baseline from the store; terminal/paused operations are left untouched (a completed op is not stalled). (4) `operations.CrossedThresholds` + a leader-only `opsinventory.Observer` (the `operations-observe` reconciler) emits `operation_progressed` on step transitions and `{10,25,50,75,90,95,99}` percent crossings and maintains the stalled gauge (see F-25.2.14). Commit `accd7b81`.

The leader/follower split, the `LeaderLoopsRunning` introspection on `/readyz` (`opsserver.go` lines 199–204), and the leader-gated loop set (cron evaluator, webhook delivery, scheduled-backup) match §25.2's architectural intent. Worth noting as a positive baseline alongside the gaps above.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("Worth
noting as a positive baseline"). Current chart still emits `replicas: 2`
(at `charts/lenny/values.yaml:1236`) and `pkg/ops/opsservice/leader.go:76-84`
sets `ReleaseOnCancel: true` + `Identity: identity` on the LeaseElector
config; no code change required.

### - [x] F-25.2.16 — `cmd/lenny-ops` runs with mandatory dependencies optional. (Info) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: line 169 — "Connects to: Postgres, Redis, K8s API, MinIO, Prometheus, Gateway admin API" reads as the steady-state dependency set; §25.4 calls out which are mandatory vs graceful-degrade.

Implementation: `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` makes Postgres optional (lines 132–140), Redis optional (lines 142–168), K8s optional (lines 175–182 — "running without leader election"), and the gateway URL optional (lines 187–196). The chart manifest (`ops-deployment.yaml` lines 14–22) describes this explicitly as "left unset by default so a stock render runs lenny-ops in the §25.4 degraded single-process mode." This deliberate single-process degraded mode is consistent with §25.4's degradation envelope intent but is worth flagging: a stock `helm install` of the chart launches an `lenny-ops` Deployment that has no Postgres, no Redis, no leader-election quorum, and a `noopElector{}` that prevents any leader-gated loops from running. Operators who do not wire `LENNY_POSTGRES_DSN` / `LENNY_REDIS_URL` get a service that serves the §25 HTTP surface but performs no backups, no webhook delivery, no escalation persistence, and no audit query — a configuration that may surprise an operator who reads §25.2's connection list as a steady-state requirement.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing ("deliberate
single-process degraded mode is consistent with §25.4's degradation
envelope intent"). The chart's `ops-deployment.yaml` already documents
the unset defaults; tighter startup gates against a stock degraded
deployment are tracked under §25.4 startup-gate findings.

### Summary

§25.2 establishes two contracts: (a) the deployment split between the gateway and `lenny-ops`, and (b) the cross-cutting API conventions that every §25.3+ endpoint reuses. Contract (a) is implemented (`lenny-ops` exists as a separate Deployment, leader election runs, RBAC is correct, the split criterion is honoured by the route registration). Contract (b) is largely unimplemented: the canonical degradation envelope (F3), pagination envelope (F4), dry-run/confirm pattern on the high-blast-radius mutating endpoints (F5), error envelope with `category`/`retryable`/`suggestedRetryAfter` (F6), progress envelope and `ops_operation_baselines` (F7), correlation headers (F8), and the canonical filter-parameter vocabulary (F9) are all missing. The two architectural seams within (a) — Redis stream as the primary destination for the EventEmitter (F1) and `/metrics` on `lenny-ops` (F2) — are also unimplemented. Two dependency edges in the architecture diagram (MinIO, Prometheus) are not wired (F10), and the operator-facing Ingress that makes `lenny-ops` reachable from outside the cluster is not rendered by the chart (F11). High-severity findings (F1–F7) block the §25 surface from honouring its own cross-cutting promises; medium findings (F8–F14) leave agent-facing observability and reliability primitives non-functional.

## §25.3 Gateway-Side Ops Endpoints <a id="25.3"></a>
Reviewed: 2026-05-23.

Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` lines 407–773 (heading `## 25.3 Gateway-Side Ops Endpoints`, ending at `## 25.4 The lenny-ops Service`).

§25.3 enumerates the gateway-side ops endpoints that share the admin API's listener: the Platform Health API (`GET /v1/admin/health[/summary|/{component}]`), the Capacity Recommendations service (`GET /v1/admin/recommendations`), Version and Config Introspection (`GET /v1/admin/platform/version` + `GET /v1/admin/platform/config`), Event Emission (the in-process behaviour writing to both a Redis stream and an in-memory ring buffer), and the Gateway Event Buffer query endpoint (`GET /v1/admin/events/buffer`). It defines the `SuggestedAction` shape used on degraded/unhealthy responses, the alert-state-derived health derivation rules, the recommendation rules engine with sliding-window ring buffers, the `EventEmitter`'s two destinations + best-effort semantics, the stable `eventKey` with disk-checkpointed nonce, the `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service for buffer fan-out, the §25.3 metric set, and the §25.3 error-code table.

### Method

Read §25.3 in full. Enumerated normative gateway-side ops endpoints:

1. **Platform Health API** — `GET /v1/admin/health`, `GET /v1/admin/health/{component}`, `GET /v1/admin/health/summary`. `HealthService` Go interface. Three data sources: in-process metric registry; Redis circuit-breaker state via `StoreRouter.PlatformRedis()`; lightweight 2-second parallel dependency probes against Postgres / Redis / MinIO / K8s API / cert-manager / connectors. In-memory alert-state tracker that evaluates the same threshold expressions as the bundled Prometheus alerting rules, sharing the `pkg/alerting/rules` source. 5-second per-replica probe cache. The endpoint never returns 5xx — it reports what it can observe. Structured `SuggestedAction` (singular) and `SuggestedActions[]` (ranked alternatives, ordered by descending `confidence`). `lenny_health_check_duration_seconds` (histogram) and `lenny_health_status` (gauge). `UNKNOWN_HEALTH_COMPONENT` 404 / `PERMANENT`.
2. **Capacity Recommendations** — `GET /v1/admin/recommendations` with optional `?category=` filter. `CapacityService` + `MetricReader` interfaces. Deterministic rules engine over a sliding-window in-memory ring buffer (per-replica). `lenny_recommendations_generated_total` (counter) and `lenny_recommendations_ring_buffer_bytes` (gauge). `gateway.recommendations.windowOverrides` and `platform.recommendations.disabledRules` Helm-driven knobs. Errors `UNKNOWN_RECOMMENDATION_CATEGORY` (400 / `PERMANENT`) and `RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE` (503 / `TRANSIENT`, gated on `ops.recommendations.disableOnPrometheusOutage`).
3. **Version and Config Introspection** — `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` returns the gateway's compiled-in metadata. `GET /v1/admin/platform/config` returns the effective merged config with secrets redacted to `"***"`.
4. **Event Emission** — `EventEmitter` writes each emitted CloudEvents v1.0.2 record to (1) Redis stream `ops:events:stream` via `XADD` with `MAXLEN ~ 10000`, and (2) an in-memory ring buffer (500 events, ~250 KB). Best-effort Redis. Emitter is called by the alert state evaluator, the upgrade state machine, the pool state manager, the circuit breaker handler, the session manager, the credential pool manager, and the health service. Event-type catalogue covers `alert_fired / alert_resolved`, `upgrade_progressed`, `pool_state_changed`, `circuit_breaker_opened/closed`, `credential_rotated`, `credential_pool_exhausted`, `session_failed`, `backup_completed/failed`, `platform_upgrade_available`, `drift_detected`, `health_status_changed`, `ops_health_status_changed`, `escalation_created`, `remediation_lock_acquired/released`. `lenny_ops_events_emitted_total` and `lenny_ops_events_emit_failed_total` metrics.
5. **Gateway Event Buffer** — `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` accepts `?since={monotonic_id}&eventType=&severity=&limit=` (default 100, max 500). Ring buffer of 500 events. `eventKey` composed as `{replicaID}:{emittedAt}:{nonce}`, globally unique across replicas, stable across restarts via periodic disk checkpoint of the nonce counter. Pagination response uses the canonical `pagination.gapDetected: true` + `pagination.oldestAvailableCursor` envelope (§25.2). Headless Service `lenny-gateway-pods` for per-replica DNS SRV polling. `bufferAge` field on responses. Metrics `lenny_events_buffer_length`, `lenny_events_buffer_queries_total`, `lenny_events_buffer_gaps_total`.

Evidence gathered via grep/find across `pkg/gateway/admin/`, `pkg/gateway/health/`, `pkg/gateway/health/backends/`, `pkg/gateway/recommendations/`, `pkg/gateway/opsevents/`, `pkg/alerting/`, `pkg/recommendations/rules/`, `pkg/gateway/eventbus/`, `cmd/lenny-gateway/`, and `charts/lenny/templates/`.

### Findings

### - [x] F-25.3.1 — `EventEmitter` does not write to the Redis stream. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.2.1, F-25.3.18, F-25.5.1 — Four members describe the gateway EventEmitter never writing to the Redis ops:events:stream, and two describe the unimplemented SSE /v1/admin/events/stream endpoint; the lag gauge and CLOSED service findings are distinct.

**Resolution:** Closed by F-25.2.1. The §25.3 `Emit()` Redis-stream destination is satisfied by `events.StreamEmitter`: when Redis is wired it XADDs to `ops:events:stream` (MAXLEN-approximated) and always writes the in-memory ring buffer first, so a Redis-write failure logs and returns the error while the buffer write still succeeds (the §25.3 line 703 fallback). The `lenny_ops_events_emit_failed_total` Redis-outage counter cited in the evidence is the §25.3 metrics surface tracked by F-25.3.11, not this finding. The 97ae8442 consumer closes the read side.

Spec: lines 654–667 — `Emit()` writes to both `(1) Redis stream ops:events:stream via XADD with MAXLEN ~ 10000` and `(2) In-memory ring buffer (500 events, ~250 KB). The buffer is always written, regardless of Redis availability.` Lines 703: `If Redis is unreachable, Emit() skips the Redis write, logs the event at WARN level, and increments lenny_ops_events_emit_failed_total. The in-memory ring buffer write always succeeds.` This is the load-bearing primary destination — the in-memory buffer is the fallback path.

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go` lines 15–18, 40–51 — `Emit` only calls `e.buffer.Append(event)`. The Redis-stream destination is an acknowledged seam ("v1 writes each event to the in-process EventBuffer; the §25.3 Redis-stream destination is added alongside the §10.1 Redis EventBus"). `grep -rn "ops:events:stream\|XAdd" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents/` returns zero matches. `lenny-ops` consequently has no Redis stream to read from; the §25.5 / §25.2 fallback model is inverted (the ring buffer is the only source, not the fallback). ### - [x] F-25.3.3 — Health derivation does not run the alert-state tracker; verdicts are flat probe outputs, not derived from firing alerts. (High) [Medium] — DEFERRED

Spec: lines 443–451. "Component status is derived deterministically from the same threshold expressions used by the alerting rules (Section 16.5): `healthy` — no firing alerts for this component; `degraded` — warning-severity alerts firing; `unhealthy` — critical-severity alerts firing. The `HealthService` maintains an in-memory alert state tracker that evaluates the same threshold expressions as the bundled Prometheus alerting rules (Section 25.13), but reads from the in-process metric registry. Both sides share the rule definitions via the `pkg/alerting/rules` package — the gateway tracker and the rendered Helm manifests are generated from a single source."

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/health/health.go` line 137 `Aggregator.Report()` runs each registered `Checker` and takes the worst returned `Status` — there is no alert-state tracker, no threshold-expression evaluator, no severity-derived mapping. `pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go` lines 14–18 defines a state machine (`StateInactive → StatePending → StateFiring`) but `grep -rn "evaluator.New\|alerting.Evaluator\|alertEvaluator" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/` returns zero hits — the evaluator is module-only, never instantiated by the gateway. Lines 11–13 of the package doc admit this: "The §16.6 emit wiring and the production ExprEvaluator are added when the gateway metric pipeline lands." Consequence: the spec's promise that `/v1/admin/health` "returns accurate results even when Prometheus itself is unreachable" because the gateway evaluates the same rules in-process is unfulfilled; the verdict is whatever the registered probe says, decoupled from the §16.5 / §25.13 alert catalogue. An alert that fires in Prometheus does not change the gateway's health verdict, and a component whose probe is `healthy` will report `healthy` even while a critical alert is firing against its metrics.

**Deferred (this batch):** the alert-state-derived health verdict requires an in-process `ExprEvaluator` that resolves the §16.5 PromQL alert expressions against the gateway's in-process metric registry (`rate(...)`, `histogram_quantile(...)`, and label-aggregated comparisons over instantaneous registry values). Building that registry-backed PromQL evaluator and wiring `pkg/alerting/evaluator` into the gateway is the explicit subject of OPEN **F-25.13.6** ("In-process alert tracker has no Prometheus-backed `ExprEvaluator`; not wired into gateway"). F-25.3.3 unblocks once F-25.13.6 lands the evaluator; the severity→status mapping (`warning` firing → degraded, `critical` firing → unhealthy) and the `HealthService` tracker then layer on top.

**Re-deferred (rule N, after F-25.13.6 closed):** the evaluator blocker is now cleared — `pkg/alerting/inproceval` evaluates the §16.5 catalogue against the in-process registry and the gateway runs the `alertEvaluator` tracker. The remaining F-25.3.3 work is independent of the evaluator and not a clean drop-in: the spec verdict is "no firing alerts **for this component**", but `pkg/alerting/rules.Rule` carries no component association (no `Component`/category field; grep confirms none), and `pkg/gateway/health` aggregates per-subsystem `Checker`s by name. Deriving per-component health from firing alerts therefore requires (a) a rule→health-component mapping across the full ~167-rule catalogue, (b) exposing the live tracker's firing-set + per-rule severity to the `Aggregator`, and (c) layering the severity→status precedence onto `Report()`. That mapping is a judgment-heavy, catalogue-wide design step in its own right; building a partial or name-heuristic mapping now would yield a half-correct health verdict. Tracked as a dedicated batch rather than chased as a second-order unblock.

### - [x] F-25.3.8 — `eventKey` uses `buildVersion` as `replicaID`; cross-replica uniqueness is broken; disk-checkpoint of nonce is absent. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: line 748 — `eventKey` is `{replicaID}:{emittedAt}:{nonce}` where `replicaID` is "unique" per replica; the nonce counter is "stable across restarts (the nonce counter survives via a periodic checkpoint to local disk; on restart, the counter resumes from `last_checkpointed + safe_skip_window` to avoid any chance of replaying an old nonce)." Line 752: deduplication across replicas uses `eventKey`.

Implementation: `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` line 877 — `opsEmitter := opsevents.NewEmitter(opsevents.NewEventBuffer(0), buildVersion)`. `buildVersion` is the gateway's compile-time version string (e.g., `"dev"` for stock builds, line 191), which is identical across every replica of the same image. `pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go` lines 19–24 — the `Emitter` keeps the nonce in an `atomic.Uint64` that starts at zero on every process launch; no disk checkpoint, no `last_checkpointed + safe_skip_window` recovery. Lines 53–62 admit the gap: "v1 keeps the nonce in-process — the §25.3 disk checkpoint that survives a restart is a refinement." Consequence: two gateway replicas serving the same `buildVersion` produce identical `eventKey`s (`dev:<same nanos>:<same nonce>` is possible under simultaneous emit), defeating the cross-replica deduplication the §25.2 fallback (gateway buffer fan-out to `lenny-ops`) relies on. A gateway restart resets the nonce to 1 and replays keys, so a `lenny-ops` consumer that has already processed `dev:<t>:1` cannot tell a fresh post-restart `dev:<t'>:1` apart from a replay.

**Resolution (76ed9a52):** The replicaID half was stale — the emitter is constructed with `resolveReplicaID()` (LENNY_REPLICA_ID, else hostname + random suffix), not `buildVersion`, so cross-replica uniqueness already held and the random-suffix default is replay-safe across restarts. The remaining disk-checkpoint half is now implemented: a shared `keyer` (replacing the duplicated `eventKey`/`nonce` logic in both `Emitter` and `StreamEmitter`) carries an optional `nonceCheckpoint` that persists a high-water mark every N ticks (atomic temp-file + rename) and, on restart, resumes the counter from `last_checkpointed + safe_skip_window` per §25.3 line 748, so a pinned-replica-id deployment cannot replay an old nonce. `window` is widened to the package default when below `every` so the safe-skip window always exceeds the unpersisted-tick gap. Wired behind `--ops-nonce-checkpoint-path` / `LENNY_OPS_NONCE_CHECKPOINT_PATH` and the `gateway.opsEvents.nonceCheckpointPath` chart value (default off). Tier-1: restart-resume + no-replay, persist cadence, window-below-every default, missing-file fresh start, corrupt-file fallback; tier-2 helm-unittest for the env rendering.

### - [x] F-25.3.12 — Recommendations service does not honour `disabledRules` / `windowOverrides` / `disableOnPrometheusOutage`. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Resolution (this batch):** `NewCapacityServiceWithConfig(reader, Config{DisabledRules, WindowOverrides, DisableOnPrometheusOutage})` threads all three knobs: disabled rules are skipped (§25.3 line 604), per-category `WindowOverrides` resolve the rule's sliding window via `windowFor` (line 596), and `DisableOnPrometheusOutage` returns the typed `ErrRecommendationsUnavailable` when the reader implements the optional `AvailabilityReporter` and reports down (line 625). `GetRecommendations` validates `?category=` against the closed enum and returns `ErrUnknownCategory`. The admin handler maps the two typed errors to `400 UNKNOWN_RECOMMENDATION_CATEGORY` / `503 RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE` instead of a flat `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The gateway parses `--recommendations-disabled-rules`, `--recommendations-window-overrides` (category=duration CSV), and `--recommendations-disable-on-prometheus-outage`, and the chart renders them from `gateway.recommendations.{disabledRules,windowOverrides,disableOnPrometheusOutage}` (verified via `helm template`). Tier-1: disabled-rule skip, window-override application, unknown-category, the outage/available/no-opt-out matrix, the two admin error-code mappings, and the flag parser.

### - [x] F-25.3.13 — `OperationalEvent` is a local struct, not a `cloudevents.Event` alias; `subject` / extension attributes are absent. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: medium) — F-25.3.19 — F-25.3.13 and F-25.3.19 both report the absent subject attribute on OperationalEvent; F-12.6.21 concerns a different struct (eventbus Event) in another package.

Spec: lines 654–663 — "OperationalEvent is a CloudEvents v1.0.2 Event — see §12.6. `type OperationalEvent = cloudevents.Event`." Lines 650–652 — "Every emitted event is a CloudEvents v1.0.2 JSON record" with `id`, `type` (`dev.lenny.<short_name>`), `datacontenttype` (`application/ocsf+json` for audit-bearing, `application/json` for non-audit), and a `subject` attribute referenced in §16.6.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` lines 27–52 defines a local `OperationalEvent` struct with `ID`, `Source`, `SpecVersion`, `Type`, `Time`, `Severity`, `DataContentType`, `Data`. No `subject`, no extension-attribute map. `grep -rn "cloudevents/sdk-go\|cloudevents.Event" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/` returns no hits — the CloudEvents SDK is not used. (A separate `pkg/gateway/eventbus/cloudevents.go` exists but is the audit-event pipeline, unrelated to `opsevents`.) Consequence: the wire format diverges from the §12.6 CloudEvents envelope contract `opsevents` claims to implement. A `lenny-ops` or external CloudEvents consumer cannot rely on standard CE attributes that aren't on the wire (`subject` in particular is documented as a §16.6 attribute and is missing).

**Resolution (662adf20):** `subject` was already first-class (F-25.3.19). Added an `Extensions map[string]string` to `OperationalEvent` (`pkg/gateway/events/buffer.go`) with custom `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` that flatten extension attributes into the top-level CloudEvents structured-content object and round-trip them back, mirroring `pkg/gateway/eventbus.Event`; a stray extension keyed on a structured attribute name never clobbers the first-class field. The literal `type OperationalEvent = cloudevents.Event` go-sdk alias is intentionally not adopted — the CloudEvents SDK is deliberately not vendored, the same documented decision the §12.3.7 audit envelope (`eventbus.Event`) follows, and the native struct marshals to the identical CloudEvents v1.0.2 wire format. Tier-1: extension flatten/round-trip + no-clobber.

### - [x] F-25.3.14 — `EventEmitter` Go interface signature does not match the spec. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-4.0.10 — Both report that EventEmitter is a concrete struct with an Emit signature that drops ctx and returns uint64 instead of matching the spec interface.

### - [x] F-25.3.15 — `eventType` and `severity` query parameters are single-value; spec admits CSV. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: §25.2 lines 336–340 (cross-cutting filter parameter naming, referenced by §25.3) — `eventType` and `severity` accept CSV form. §25.3 lines 720 specifies the buffer endpoint's `?eventType=` and `?severity=` parameters without restricting to single values.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go` lines 74–77 passes `q.Get("eventType")` and `q.Get("severity")` directly to `opsevents.EventFilter`. `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` lines 183–192 `matchFilter` treats each as a single literal match (`f.Severity != ""` → exact-equality; `f.EventType != ""` → exact or short-name-suffix match). No CSV split, no multi-value disjunction. Consequence: an agent that follows §25.2's canonical-filter contract and sends `?severity=critical,warning&eventType=alert_fired,circuit_breaker_opened` to the buffer receives an empty page (the comma-joined token matches nothing) rather than the expected union.

**Resolution (662adf20):** `EventFilter` now exposes `Matches(OperationalEvent)` which splits each field on commas (trimming whitespace, ignoring empty tokens) and matches the §25.2 union per dimension; the two dimensions still intersect. The duplicate `matchFilter` in `pkg/ops/events/service.go` was deleted and delegates to `EventFilter.Matches`, so the gateway buffer and the lenny-ops stream share one matcher. The admin/poll handlers pass the raw CSV query string unchanged. Tier-1 (union, whitespace, all-empty CSV, single-value no-regression, intersection) plus a tier-2 HTTP test for the exact `?severity=critical,warning&eventType=...` scenario.

### - [ ] F-25.3.16 — `/v1/admin/recommendations` does not surface the `degradation` / `dataAvailable` post-restart contract. (Medium) [Medium] — DEFERRED

Spec: lines 588–597, 606–608. After a gateway restart, ring buffers are empty and recommendations include `"confidence": 0.0` and `"dataAvailable": false`. "No recommendations are generated for categories with insufficient data."

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/recommendations/service.go` line 94 — `if !e.Triggered { continue }` skips the recommendation entirely when its evaluator returns `Triggered: false`. The post-restart contract per the spec is that the rule emits a recommendation tagged `confidence: 0` / `dataAvailable: false` so an agent can see the rule exists but is starved of data. The implementation's `DataAvailable: false` path returns no recommendation at all (lines 122/132/142/152/162/172 all return zero-value `Evaluation{}` when the metric is missing). Consequence: an agent cannot distinguish "no warm-pool issue" from "warm-pool rule cannot evaluate because Prometheus / ring buffer is empty"; the spec's "I know the rule ran but it had no data" signal is lost.

**Deferred (this batch):** the spec is internally contradictory here and resolving it would require a spec change (which a hook forbids). Line 589 says post-restart empty windows yield recommendations with `confidence: 0.0` and `dataAvailable: false` (the finding's reading — emit a degraded entry). Line 608 says "No recommendations are generated for categories with insufficient data" (no entry), and the committed `TestGetRecommendationsEmptyWhenNoData` already encodes that no-entry reading deliberately. The two cannot both hold for the metric-absent case, so implementing the finding's fix would overturn an existing test on an ambiguous basis. Unblocking this needs a spec clarification of which case ("empty window" vs "insufficient data") governs the metric-absent path; until then the no-entry behaviour stands. The §25.4 `degradation` envelope half is already present (`RecommendationsResponse.Degradation`).

### - [x] F-25.3.17 — Buffer query response uses `gapDetected` at the response root, not under `pagination.gapDetected`. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: medium) — F-25.2.4 — Both describe the buffer endpoint lacking the canonical §25.2 pagination envelope, with gap fields emitted at the response root instead of under pagination.

Spec: line 750 — "the response includes the canonical `pagination.gapDetected: true` envelope (Section 25.2) along with `pagination.oldestAvailableCursor`." §25.2 pagination envelope is `pagination.{cursor, hasMore, limit, cursorKind, headCursor, gapDetected, gapReason, oldestAvailableCursor, suggestedAction}`.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` lines 73–88 — `BufferedEventPage` has top-level `Events`, `Cursor`, `HasMore`, `GapDetected`, `OldestAvailableCursor`, `BufferAge`. No `pagination` envelope wrapper, no `cursorKind`, no `headCursor`, no `gapReason`, no `suggestedAction: "resync"`. Consequence: agents following §25.2's canonical pagination read `pagination.gapDetected` and receive a missing field, even though the gateway computed the gap. This is the same regression class as F4 in §25.2 audit (no canonical pagination envelope), localised to §25.3's specifically-cited "canonical envelope" promise.

**Resolution (662adf20):** `BufferedEventPage` now nests a `Pagination` struct carrying the §25.2 canonical fields — `cursor`, `hasMore`, `limit`, `cursorKind` (always `buffer-seq`), `headCursor`, and on eviction `gapDetected` + `gapReason` + `oldestAvailableCursor` + `suggestedAction: "resync"`. `Query` populates it; the admin and lenny-ops poll handlers serialize the page unchanged, so the gap fields now ride under `pagination` rather than at the response root. Tier-1 (envelope fields, gap-recovery fields) + a JSON-shape test asserting the gap fields are NOT at the root. **F-25.2.4** is NOT closed by this: it additionally covers the §25.4 locks/escalations/event-subscription list endpoints and the §25.11 backup-list endpoint, which still lack the envelope — only its buffer-endpoint overlap is addressed here.

### - [x] F-25.3.18 — `lenny-ops` Redis stream consumer wiring is absent (no producer at gateway, no consumer in opsservice). (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.2.1, F-25.3.1, F-25.5.1 — Four members describe the gateway EventEmitter never writing to the Redis ops:events:stream, and two describe the unimplemented SSE /v1/admin/events/stream endpoint; the lag gauge and CLOSED service findings are distinct.

The cold-start cursor snaps to the stream tail so the MAXLEN backlog is not replayed to subscriptions. Producer→consumer round-trip pinned by `TestStreamProducerConsumerRoundTrip_spec_25_5` over miniredis.

The gateway never writes to the stream; the ops consumer cannot read what isn't written. ### - [x] F-25.3.19 — `subject` attribute on `OperationalEvent`, mirroring the §16.6 event catalogue, is absent. (Low) [Medium] — CLOSED

### - [x] F-25.3.20 — Capacity-recommendations `MetricReader` is not populated by gateway subsystems. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 588–597 — ring buffers store one sample per emission for the configured window. The gateway's metric registry (line 439, "in-process metric registry") feeds the ring buffers, and the rules engine reads from those buffers via `MetricReader`.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/recommendations/metricreader.go` lines 41–63 implements `WindowStore` with a `Record(name, labels, value)` method. `grep -rn "\.Record(" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/recommendations/ /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/` returns no production callers — no gateway subsystem populates the store with `lenny_warmpool_exhausted_total`, `lenny_credential_pool_utilization`, `lenny_gateway_cpu_utilization_ratio`, `lenny_pod_oom_killed_total`, `lenny_storage_utilization_ratio`, or `lenny_quota_rejection_ratio` samples. Even the recommendations `NewCapacityService` in the gateway main wire-up is not present (`grep -n "recommendations.NewCapacityService\|WithRecommendations" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` returns no hits — `/v1/admin/recommendations` is never registered on a stock gateway start). Consequence: even with the package present, the endpoint never serves real data — the route does not mount, and even if it did, the rules engine sees an empty store.

**Resolution (this batch):** the route-mount half was already stale (`WithRecommendations(NewCapacityServiceWithConfig(...))` is registered in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` and the store is created with its ring-buffer-bytes gauge). The store-population gap is now closed by `pkg/gateway/recommendations/sampler.go`: a `Sampler` reads the §25.3 recommendation source metrics directly out of the gateway's in-process Prometheus registry (new `gatewaymetrics.Metrics.Gatherer()`) and `Record`s them into the `WindowStore` on a 30-second loop launched under `watchdogCtx`. Counters aggregate across label sets with `aggSum` and the ratio gauges with `aggMax` (the "any pool" framing), recorded under the nil-label aggregate the evaluators query. Series that originate in another process (warm-pool exhaustion from the controller, kubelet OOM kills) are not in the gateway registry and are served by `lenny-ops` through its Prometheus reader per the §25.3 per-replica-scope note; the sampler lists every evaluator metric so a metric added to the gateway registry later is sampled with no further wiring. Tier-1: 6 sampler tests (gauge record, aggMax/aggSum across labels, skip-unregistered, end-to-end evaluator fires after sampling, nil-safe) plus a gatewaymetrics build check.

### - [x] F-25.3.21 — `health` checkers are sequential, not parallel; aggregate runtime is the sum of probe latencies. (Low) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: line 441 — "Probes run in parallel."

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/health/health.go` `Aggregator.Report()` (lines 137–170) iterates checkers in a single goroutine: `for _, c := range checkers { comp := c.Check(ctx); ... }`. With the spec's full probe set (Postgres, Redis, MinIO, K8s API server, cert-manager, connectors) each at a 2-second timeout, a slow-or-down dependency serializes the response: worst-case ≥12 seconds vs the spec's "all probes wait at most 2 s". Consequence: a single unreachable backend stalls the whole `/v1/admin/health` response well beyond the spec's per-probe ceiling.

**Resolution:** `Aggregator.Report` now fans out across goroutines via `sync.WaitGroup`; each Checker runs in its own goroutine, result slots are pre-allocated to avoid a mutex, and the aggregate runtime is bounded by the slowest probe. The package-doc comment cites §25.3 line 441 directly. Tier-1 test `TestProbesRunInParallel_spec_25_3_441` registers eight 80ms probes, asserts the aggregate completes well under `n × delay`, and tracks peak concurrent in-flight to confirm goroutine overlap.

### - [x] F-25.3.22 — `lenny_gateway-pods` headless Service exists and mounts correctly. (Info) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.16.6 — Both confirm the lenny-gateway-pods headless Service is correctly rendered (matching/no-gap observations of the same resource).

Spec: line 754 — the Helm chart renders a headless Service (`lenny-gateway-pods`, `clusterIP: None`) alongside the standard ClusterIP Service for per-replica DNS SRV discovery.

Implementation: `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` lines 282–296 renders `Service/lenny-gateway-pods` with `clusterIP: None`, selectors matching the gateway Deployment, and a comment that references §17.1. `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` line 194 covers the test. The Service plumbing for the §25.3 buffer fan-out path is in place — the gap is the consumer side (F18) and the actual ring-buffer route, both of which depend on the missing primary Redis pipeline (F1).

**Resolution:** Verify-closed; `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:589-601` renders `Service/lenny-gateway-pods` with `clusterIP: None` (lines drifted from 282-296). No gap per own framing. The §25.3 consumer-side ring-buffer pipeline gaps are tracked under F1/F18.

### - [x] F-25.3.23 — `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` honours the spec's compiled-in-metadata contract; config redaction key-prefix list is conservative. (Info) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 627–640. Version returns `gateway.version`, `gitCommit`, `buildDate`, `goVersion`. Config returns the effective merged configuration with secret values redacted to `"***"`.

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/admin/platform.go` lines 22–94. The version handler emits `GatewayVersion / GitCommit / BuildDate / GoVersion` populated from `PlatformInfo` and `runtime.Version()`. The config handler redacts on key prefixes (`secret`, `password`, `token`, `key`, `credential`) — the list is sound but key-prefix scanning is sensitive to non-obvious key names (e.g., `JWT_SIGNING_PEM` does not contain any of the markers and would leak). Defensive belt-and-suspenders works only because the caller is expected to pre-redact. This is conservative-enough behaviour but worth flagging as the only redaction path. The `OpsServiceURL` extension on the response (lines 17–22 / lines 39–43) for `lenny-ctl` auto-discovery is an addition beyond the spec and is left noted.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed; `pkg/gateway/admin/platform.go:17-82` confirms `GatewayVersion/GitCommit/BuildDate/GoVersion` are emitted per spec, `OpsServiceURL` is the documented §25.14 lenny-ctl auto-discovery extension (`json:"opsServiceURL,omitempty"`), and the prefix-redaction policy is per the finding's own framing "conservative-enough behaviour". No code change required.

### Summary

§25.3 promises five normative endpoints + an emitter behaviour: Platform Health, Capacity Recommendations, Platform Version + Config, the Event Emitter (Redis stream + in-memory ring buffer), and the Gateway Event Buffer query. The implementation routes the four query endpoints (health, recommendations, platform version/config, events buffer) and wires per-replica ring buffers and a per-replica emitter, but the underlying contract is shallow: the emitter does not write to the Redis stream (F1, F18) so the gateway → `lenny-ops` pipeline is dark; the in-memory alert-state tracker that derives health verdicts from the §16.5 catalogue is not wired (F3); the dependency-probe set covers only Postgres / Redis / circuit-breaker cache, not MinIO / K8s API / cert-manager / connectors (F4) and runs serially (F21); the structured `SuggestedAction` shape is reduced to a free-form string with no ranked-alternatives form (F2); the `eventKey` uses `buildVersion` as the per-replica identifier and has no disk checkpoint (F8); the §25.3 metrics are not emitted (F11) and the §25.3 error-code envelope is not used (F12); the recommendations service uses neither the spec's threshold formulas nor the recommendation-target fields (F6, F7) and is not wired into the gateway main at all (F20); CloudEvents conformance is partial (F13, F14, F19) and the canonical pagination envelope is not adopted (F17). High-severity findings (F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F8, F9, F11, F18) block the §25.3 contract from being honoured end-to-end; medium findings (F5, F7, F10, F12–F17, F20) leave operator-facing semantics divergent from the spec. The HTTP wiring, the headless Service, and the platform-version handler land cleanly.

## §25.4 The `lenny-ops` Service <a id="25.4"></a>
Reviewed: 2026-05-23.

Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` lines 776–2549 (heading `## 25.4 The lenny-ops Service`, ending at `## 25.5 Operational Event Stream`). §25.4 is the canonical reference for the `lenny-ops` Deployment: its Helm-value surface, Kubernetes resources (Deployment, Service, ServiceAccount, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, PodDisruptionBudget, Ingress), leader election, dependency model (Postgres, Redis, K8s API, gateway admin, Prometheus, MinIO), self-monitoring, OIDC authentication, idempotency, remediation-coordination (locks with split-brain prevention), escalation tiers, gateway client and metrics source with fan-out fallback, `/v1/admin/me` capability discovery, `/v1/admin/operations` inventory, TLS, structured logging, and rate limiting.

### Method

Read §25.4 in full; enumerated the normative deployment/runtime/security/coordination surface:

1. **Deployment** — `lenny-ops` Deployment, single replica by default with leader election; tier-aware Helm values (`ops.replicas`, `ops.image`, `ops.resources`, `ops.gateway`, `ops.prometheus`, `ops.ingress`, `ops.sessionAffinity`, `ops.rateLimiting`, `ops.tls`, `ops.acknowledgePlaintextAdminAPI`, `ops.leaderElection`, `ops.selfHealth`, `ops.webhooks`, `ops.idempotency`, `ops.locks`, `ops.escalation`, `ops.events`, `ops.recommendations`, `ops.drift`, `ops.audit`) plus shared top-level keys `monitoring`, `backups`, `platform`, `security` (lines 786–917).
2. **Kubernetes resources** — Deployment with non-root + read-only-FS + drop-all caps + `emptyDir /tmp` + `topologySpreadConstraints` when `replicas >= 2` + Prometheus scrape annotations; startup/readiness/liveness probes with the `/healthz?strict=true` strict variant; `lenny-ops` ClusterIP Service with `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` (3h timeout) + `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service for per-replica fan-out; ServiceAccount `lenny-ops-sa` with namespace Role `lenny-ops-namespace` and ClusterRole `lenny-ops-cluster` covering deployments/scale, pods/pods-log/events, batch/jobs, configmaps, leases, CRDs, `lenny.dev/*`, nodes; three NetworkPolicies (`lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress`, `lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller`, `lenny-ops-egress`) plus the `lenny-backup-job` NetworkPolicy; PodDisruptionBudget `minAvailable: 1`; Ingress with the `ops.ingress.*` knobs (host, TLS secret, idle timeout, annotations); leader election via K8s Lease `lenny-ops-leader` with the singleton workloads (backup scheduling, webhook delivery, reconciliation goroutines, `platform_upgrade_check`, `bundleRules` reconciler) (lines 991–1373).
3. **Dependencies and degradation modes** — Postgres, Redis (both optional/degraded), K8s API + gateway admin (required), Prometheus (required at Tier 2/3, optional Tier 1, with `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus` opt-out), MinIO (optional/degraded for backup verification only) (lines 1375–1452).
4. **Storage routing** — `StoreRouter.PlatformPostgres()`, `PlatformPostgres(region)`, `SessionShard`, `AuditShard`, `AllAuditShards`, `AllSessionShards`, `PlatformRedis()` for the named ops_* tables and `ops:` Redis prefix (lines 1455–1512).
5. **Multi-replica scaling** — read-heavy fan-out, leader-only mutations, `ops.locks.memoryTier` defaults `"single-replica-only"`; opt-outs for in-memory tier (lines 1518–1556).
6. **Authentication** — OIDC middleware shared with gateway, JWT roles `platform-admin`/`tenant-admin`, RFC 9068 `scope` claim narrowing (lines 1562–1567).
7. **`GET /v1/admin/me`, `/me/authorized-tools`, `/me/operations`** — single-call discovery returning identity/authorization/rateLimits/token/platform/capabilities/links (lines 1569–1644).
8. **`GET /v1/admin/operations`, `/operations/{id}`** — unified Operations Inventory across upgrade, restore, backup, escalation, lock, idempotency, drift_reconciliation, webhook_delivery_pending operations with canonical `operationId` format and the `degradation` envelope on partial responses (lines 1646–1786).
9. **`GatewayClient`** — dedicated `lenny-ops-sa` JWT, ClusterIP for shared-state calls, headless Service via `ReplicaDiscovery` for per-replica fan-out methods (`QueryAllEventBuffers`, `GetHealthFromAllReplicas`, `GetRecommendationsFromAllReplicas`) (lines 1790–1898).
10. **Metrics source and fan-out fallback** — `MetricSource`/`PrometheusWithFallback` with the documented "Prometheus unreachable" definition, per-replica circuit breakers, cache TTLs (10s/30s), partial-aggregation degradation, aggregate-before-evaluate recommendations, pool bottleneck diagnostics scrape fallback, OIDC token lifecycle (pre-emptive refresh, minimum TTL enforcement, 401-triggered revocation detection) (lines 1900–1974).
11. **Rate limiting** — per-`sub` token bucket, default 20 r/s burst 50, `lenny_ops_rate_limited_total` (lines 1976–1986).

### Findings

### - [x] F-25.4.1 — `lenny-ops` lacks an OIDC authentication middleware; every endpoint is unauthenticated. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 1562–1567 ("Authentication"). "Same OIDC middleware as the gateway admin API. `lenny-ops` validates JWT tokens using the same OIDC issuer and JWKS endpoint. Requires `platform-admin` or `tenant-admin` role on all endpoints. No anonymous access except `/healthz`." Line 1567 also mandates RFC 9068 `scope`-claim handling.

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go` lines 134–170 (`New`) registers every route on a bare `http.ServeMux` with no middleware chain. The same package's `callerIdentity` (`backup.go` lines 87–96) reads `X-Lenny-Caller` and defaults to `"operator"`; `callerRole` (`locks.go` lines 64–74) reads `X-Lenny-Role`, defaulting to `platform-admin`; `callerTenant` (line 78) reads `X-Lenny-Tenant-ID`. `grep -rn "Authorization\|jwt\|JWT\|oidc" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns only doc comments acknowledging that "JWT middleware lands" later (`mcpmgmt/server.go` lines 280–287, `mcpmgmt/tools.go` line 71). `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` and `deps.go` build no OIDC verifier, no JWKS client, no token middleware. Consequence: every `/v1/admin/*` endpoint on `lenny-ops` accepts unauthenticated requests; a caller setting `X-Lenny-Role: platform-admin` grants itself the full scope-pattern surface for remediation locks, backup/restore, and drift reconciliation. The §25.4 invariant "No anonymous access except `/healthz`" is violated by every endpoint other than `/healthz`. This is a critical security regression — the spec already deems `lenny-ops` Ingress-only because callers carry platform-admin JWTs; without the middleware, any peer that reaches the Ingress acts as platform-admin.

**Resolution:** Added the §25.4 lines 1562-1564 OIDC authentication + role gate to `pkg/ops/opsserver` (`auth.go`). `Options.Auth *AuthConfig` wraps every operability route (the Kubernetes probes `/healthz` and `/readyz` are exempt — the kubelet carries no bearer) in the reused gateway `authmw.Wrap` middleware with `RequireAuth` forced on, then a `requireAdminRole` gate that rejects any principal lacking `platform-admin` or `tenant-admin` with the §25.2 canonical 403. The `callerIdentity`/`callerRole`/`callerTenant` helpers now read the verified principal (`authmw.FromContext`) first; the `X-Lenny-Caller`/`X-Lenny-Role`/`X-Lenny-Tenant-ID` headers are only consulted when no principal is present (dev / embedded with no AuthConfig wired), so a valid bearer's identity can no longer be spoofed by a header. The production binary builds the verifier from the shared HMAC key and refuses to start without it (see F-25.4.20). Tier-1 tests cover unauthenticated 401, non-admin 403, platform-admin/tenant-admin admit, probe exemption, invalid-token rejection, and principal-over-header identity. Closed in this batch's commit.

### - [x] F-25.4.2 — `GET /v1/admin/me`, `/me/authorized-tools`, `/me/operations` are not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 1569–1644. `GET /v1/admin/me` is the agent's single-call discovery endpoint returning identity, authorization (including `authorizedLockScopes` derived from scope-pattern rules and `subjectToGuards` from `x-lenny-guards`), `rateLimits.currentTokensAvailable`, token lifecycle, `platform.{installationId, version, tier, namespace}`, `capabilities.{prometheusAvailable, bundledRulesLoaded, opsReplicas, mtlsInternal, lockMemoryTier, tenantFiltering, mcpManagementServer, openApiAvailable, headlessServiceFallback}`, and the `links` discovery block. `/me/authorized-tools` returns the MCP tool inventory pre-filtered for the caller. `/me/operations` is the alias for `?actor=me`. `audit.identity.discovered` is emitted on first call. Error code `AUTHORIZED_TOOLS_UNAVAILABLE` (503). Metric `lenny_ops_me_requests_total`.

Implementation: `grep -rn "/v1/admin/me\|me/authorized-tools\|me/operations\|installationId\|identity.discovered\|lenny_ops_me_requests" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns no matches. The `lenny-ops` mux registers nothing under `/v1/admin/me`. Consequence: the canonical entrypoint §25.4 designs the agent flow around — "a fresh agent typically follows these in order: `authorizedTools` for its callable surface, `myOperations` for in-flight work, `platformHealth` for current platform state" (line 1632) — does not exist. Agents must trial-call every endpoint to discover what they can do, which §25.4 explicitly calls out as the failure mode the endpoint avoids ("An agent arriving with a valid token has no built-in way to know what it can do without making trial calls and observing 403s.", line 1569).

**Resolution (commit ffa160e1):** New `pkg/ops/opsserver/me.go` registers `GET /v1/admin/me`, `/me/authorized-tools`, and `/me/operations`. The me response carries the full §25.4 blocks: `identity` (sub/displayName/callerType/issuer), `authorization` (roles, tenantScope `*` for platform-admin or the tenant ID for tenant-admin, the RFC 9068 `scope` echoed as `tools:*` when absent, `authorizedLockScopes` derived per role — the platform set vs the tenant-scoped subset, and the `subjectToGuards` confirm/acknowledgeDataLoss rules), `rateLimits` (the caller's live token-bucket balance via a new `RateLimiter.Snapshot`), `token`, `platform` (installationId/version/tier/namespace/URLs from a new `MeConfig`), `capabilities` (the live install-state snapshot — prometheusAvailable, lockMemoryTier, tenantFiltering, mcpManagementServer, headlessServiceFallback, opsReplicas read live from the Endpoints counter), and the `links` discovery block. `identity.discovered` is emitted on the first call per caller subject (deduplicated via a process `sync.Map`) and `lenny_ops_me_requests_total{caller_type}` increments on every call. `/me/authorized-tools` filters the MCP management registry by the caller's `x-lenny-required-role` and `x-lenny-scope`, annotating confirm-guarded tools, and returns `503 AUTHORIZED_TOOLS_UNAVAILABLE` with the OpenAPI fallback hint when the MCP server is unwired. `/me/operations` is the `actor=me` alias over the Operations Inventory (F-25.4.3). Wired in `cmd/lenny-ops` with the platform-context flags and capability snapshot. Tier-1/2 tests cover the platform-admin/tenant-admin response shapes, the dedup, the scope-narrowed tool inventory, the rate-limits surface through the real auth gate, and the me/operations alias.

**Potential overlap** (confidence: high) — F-25.2.13 — Both concern the §25.4 Operations Inventory but F-25.2.13 is the missing progress envelope within the inventory while F-25.4.3 is the absence of the inventory endpoints themselves.

Paginated scatter-gather view across `platform_upgrade`, `restore`, `backup`, `backup_verification`, `escalation_open`, `escalation_buffered`, `remediation_lock`, `idempotency_in_progress`, `drift_reconciliation`, `webhook_delivery_pending`; filters `actor/status/kind/since/until/tenantId/operationId/limit/cursor`; canonical `operationId` format (`upgrade-...`, `lock-...`, `restore-...`, `esc-...`, etc.); per-operation `resources` block with discovery URLs; `OPERATION_NOT_FOUND` and `OPERATIONS_INVENTORY_PARTIAL` error codes; `operation_progressed` event subscription; metrics `lenny_ops_operations_inventory_requests_total`, `lenny_ops_operations_inventory_kinds_returned`; audit `operations.inventory_queried`.

Implementation: `grep -rn "/v1/admin/operations\|operations_inventory\|inventory_queried\|OPERATIONS_INVENTORY_PARTIAL" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns no matches. No package owns the unified inventory; each subsystem still answers its own status endpoint with no aggregation. Consequence: an agent asking "what is in flight platform-wide?" must query every subsystem individually (locks, escalations, restores, backups, etc.) and reconstruct the merge, defeating §25.4's design that "the Operations Inventory endpoint provides a unified, filterable view" (line 1647). Watchdog flows that depend on the canonical `operationId` form to decode subsystem URLs cannot work because no endpoint produces them.

**Resolution (commit ffa160e1):** `pkg/ops/opsserver/operations.go` registers `GET /v1/admin/operations` and `/operations/{id}` on the lenny-ops mux over the already-built `pkg/ops/operations.Inventory` scatter-gather framework. New `pkg/ops/opsinventory` source adapters project the wired subsystems onto the canonical `Operation` envelope: `LockSource` (remediation_lock/held), `EscalationSource` (escalation_open/escalation_buffered, mapping persistence tier → awaiting_flush/in_progress/completed), and `UpgradeSource` (platform_upgrade, mapping the phase → paused/in_progress/failed/completed); the §25.10 drift `ReconcileSource` (already an `operations.Source`) is registered for drift_reconciliation. Each adapter emits the spec `resources` block and a decodable `operationId` carrying the §25.4 kind prefix. The handler applies the §25.4 line 1736 authorization rules — tenant-admin auto-restricted to its own + own-tenant operations, `actor=*`/specific-sub requiring platform-admin, a hidden single-operation lookup returning `OPERATION_NOT_FOUND` rather than 403 — parses the `actor/status/kind/since/until/tenantId/operationId/limit` filters, returns `207 OPERATIONS_INVENTORY_PARTIAL` with the degradation envelope when a source's store is unreachable, increments `lenny_ops_operations_inventory_requests_total{actor_kind}` + observes `lenny_ops_operations_inventory_kinds_returned`, and emits the `operations.inventory_queried` audit event. The `restore`, `backup`/`backup_verification`, `idempotency_in_progress`, and `webhook_delivery_pending` kinds plug into the same framework as their subsystems expose enumeration (restore and idempotency have no list API today; backup IDs use a `bkp-` natural-key prefix to reconcile with the `backup` kind prefix when restore enumeration lands). Tier-1 source-adapter tests and tier-2 handler tests (actor/tenant visibility matrix, 207 partial, get/not-found/hidden, unmapped-without-inventory) cover the surface.

### - [x] F-25.4.4 — `Idempotency-Key` header, `ops_idempotency_keys` table, and `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`/`IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` enforcement are absent. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.17.5 — Both report missing Idempotency-Key enforcement on lenny-ops mutating endpoints; F-25.4.4 is the more complete version covering the table and error codes.

Spec: lines 1988–2057. `Idempotency-Key` is required at Tier 2/3 on `POST /v1/admin/platform/upgrade/start`, `POST /v1/admin/restore/execute`, and `POST /v1/admin/backups type=full`; the primary key is `(key, caller_id)` so callers cannot collide; standard 24h TTL, long-running 7d TTL; Postgres outage returns `IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) on required endpoints and `degradation.warnings` on optional ones; error codes `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS` (409), `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` (400), `IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` (503), `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OWNED_BY_OTHER_CALLER` (403); SQL schema with `(key, caller_id)` PK and `expires_at` index.

Implementation: `grep -rn "Idempotency-Key\|ops_idempotency_keys\|IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED\|IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE\|OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS\|IdempotencyService" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations` returns no matches. There is no migration creating `ops_idempotency_keys` (the latest migration is `0049_artifact_store.up.sql`; only `0046_ops_event_subscriptions.up.sql` is an ops_* table). `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go` lines 100–125 (`handleCreateBackup`) and lines 308–342 (`handleRestoreExecute`) read no `Idempotency-Key` header. Consequence: a `restore/execute` retried after a transient network failure executes twice; an upgrade started twice spawns two upgrade orchestrations. The Tier 2/3 contract that agents "rely on idempotency keys to safely retry mutations" (line 1989) is unmet on every mutating endpoint.

**Resolution.** New `pkg/ops/opsidem` middleware implements the §25.4 contract distinct from the gateway's §11.5 (tenant, key) idempotency: records key on `(key, caller_id)` (caller_id = OIDC sub via `callerIdentity`), classify the required Tier 2/3 endpoints (`POST /v1/admin/platform/upgrade/start`, `POST /v1/admin/restore/execute`, `POST /v1/admin/backups` type:full → `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` when the header is omitted at the `--production` tier, optional at dev), apply the two TTL classes (24h standard, 7d long-running for upgrade/restore), replay a completed row without re-executing, return `409 OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS` (with `elapsed`), `403 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OWNED_BY_OTHER_CALLER` on cross-caller reuse, and fail closed `503 IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` on a store outage for required endpoints while letting optional endpoints proceed with a `degradation.warnings` envelope. Migration 0116 creates the platform-scoped `ops_idempotency_keys` table with the `(key, caller_id)` PK + `expires_at` index exactly per the §25.4 SQL; `pkg/ops/opsidem/pgstore` is the durable Postgres store (verified against real Postgres), wired in `cmd/lenny-ops` when a pool is present (MemoryStore otherwise), with an hourly `PruneExpired` retention sweep. The middleware sits inside the auth wrapper in `opsserver.New` so caller_id resolves from the verified principal. Commit 0112cf2b.

**Resolution:** Added `pkg/ops/opsserver/ratelimit.go`: a `RateLimiter` of per-`sub` `golang.org/x/time/rate` token buckets (§25.4 line 2001 defaults 20 rps / burst 50, configurable via `--rate-limit-rps` / `--rate-limit-burst` ← `ops.rateLimiting.{requestsPerSecond,burst}`). It sits inside the auth wrapper (so it keys on the authenticated principal sub) and rejects an over-budget request with §25.2 429 `RATE_LIMITED` plus a `Retry-After` header, incrementing the newly-registered `lenny_ops_rate_limited_total{service_account}` counter. The limiter is in-process (§25.4 line 2003).
