The `/v1/admin/me.rateLimits` inspection surface lands with the §25.4 me endpoint (F-25.4.2). Closed in this batch's commit.

### - [x] F-25.4.6 — Postgres and Redis tiers of the remediation-lock service are not implemented; only the in-memory Tier 3 store exists. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2061–2336 ("Remediation Coordination") prescribes a three-tier store. Tier 1 (Postgres, default) uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (scope) DO NOTHING RETURNING *` against `ops_remediation_locks`; Tier 2 (Redis) uses a Lua script on `ops:lock:{scope}` reading `redis.call('TIME')` and stamping the outage epoch from `ops:lock-epoch:current`; the outage-epoch counter is **stored in both Postgres and Redis** (lines 2196–2199); on Postgres recovery a reconciliation transaction holding `pg_advisory_xact_lock(0xLOCK_EPOCH_RECONCILE)` runs the deterministic split-brain resolution rule (table at lines 2229–2233) and records winners/losers in `ops_lock_conflicts`. SQL schemas for `ops_remediation_locks`, `ops_lock_epoch`, and `ops_lock_conflicts` are normative (lines 2160–2175 and 2212–2225).

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/coordination/locks.go` ships `MemStore` only. The file's own doc comment (lines 9–15) acknowledges: "the v1 store implemented here is the in-memory Tier 3 store: ... The Postgres and Redis tiers reuse this service's contract." `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` line 254 wires the lock surface to `coordination.NewMemStore()`. `grep -rn "ops_remediation_locks\|ops_lock_epoch\|ops_lock_conflicts" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/migrations` returns zero matches (no schema migrations). There is no `pkg/ops/coordination/pgstore.go` or `redisstore.go`; no `IncrementEpoch` reconciliation goroutine is wired (`pkg/ops/opsservice/reconcile.go` lines 49–50 names `LockEpochReconcile` but `main.go` calls `opsservice.New` with no `Reconcilers` field — `service.go` line 126 invokes `cfg.Reconcilers.loops()` on the zero value). Consequence: every running deployment uses the in-memory store, which §25.4 explicitly calls out as advisory only within a single replica (`ops.locks.memoryTier: "single-replica-only"`, line 2178). Multi-replica deployments lose lock coordination entirely (split-brain on every concurrent acquire). The lock-store-active label (`lenny_ops_lock_store_active{store}`) is always "memory" with no Postgres or Redis path available. The §25.4 split-brain resolution rule that the rest of the operability surface (escalations, upgrade orchestration, restore/resume) depends on cannot fire because there are no Tier 1/Tier 2 acquisitions to reconcile.

**Resolution (commit 573e6be6):** The lock service is now tiered. A new `coordination.Store` tier interface is implemented by `coordination/pgstore` (Tier 1 — `ops_remediation_locks` migration 0121; the acquire CAS is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (scope) DO UPDATE ... WHERE expires_at <= now()`, an atomic upsert that takes over only an expired row, since a `WITH`-modifying-CTE delete is invisible to the same statement's conflict check; `ops_lock_epoch` counter ops; `Reconcile` runs the single transaction holding `pg_advisory_xact_lock`), `coordination/redisstore` (Tier 2 — `ops:lock:{scope}` hash, Lua acquire/release CAS, Redis `TIME` clock, `ops:lock-epoch:current`), and the in-memory Tier 3 `MemStore`. `coordination.Service` composes them: `Acquire` falls Tier 1 → Tier 2 → Tier 3 (gated by `ops.locks.memoryTier`, returning `REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION` on reject), increments the dual-store outage epoch once per Postgres→Tier-2 transition, and stamps it onto Tier 2/3 locks; `Reconcile` writes `MAX(redis,pg)` back, copies active Redis locks into Postgres, and applies the deterministic split-brain rule (pre-outage wins when both active; Redis wins when the pre-outage row is expired), recording each conflict in `ops_lock_conflicts`. The §25.4 lock metrics (`lenny_ops_lock_store_active`, `_outage_epoch`, `_split_brain_detected_total`, `_steal_total`, `_clock_skew_seconds`) and audit events (`remediation.lock_*`) are emitted from the service. The opsserver acquire handler is now tier-aware — the memoryTier gate is consulted only when the in-memory tier is the active one (closing the latent reject-in-`never`-mode-while-Postgres-up bug). Tests: tier-1 service tier-fallback/epoch/split-brain/reap/audit/metrics, redisstore (miniredis) CAS/TTL/epoch round-trip, pgstore (embedded Postgres) acquire/conflict/reap/epoch + both split-brain branches, opsserver tier-aware gate.

### - [x] F-25.4.7 — Postgres and Redis tiers of the escalation service are not implemented; emission to the Redis stream is stubbed. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2342–2459. Create path is tiered Postgres → Redis → in-memory. Tier 1 inserts into `ops_escalations` (SQL schema at lines 2433–2452 — `created_at` deliberately NOT defaulted so flushed escalations preserve the authoring timestamp; indexes on `(status, severity)` and `created_at DESC`). Tier 2 writes to Redis hash `ops:escalations:{id}` with a 24h TTL. Emission is exactly-once via the `emitted` flag; a background retry (30s) re-attempts publication until it succeeds. Reconciliation flushes in-memory → Redis → Postgres on dependency recovery, rate-limited to `ops.escalation.reconciliationWritesPerSecond` (default 20), emitting `remediation.escalation_persisted` audit events. Error code `ESCALATION_NO_DURABLE_STORE` (503) when `ops.escalation.requireDurable: true`.

Implementation: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/escalation/escalation.go` lines 165–192 ships the in-memory Tier 3 service only. The file doc comment (lines 9–14) acknowledges "the v1 store implemented here is the in-memory Tier 3 buffer". `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go` lines 144–151 (`buildEscalationService`) wires `escalation.NewService(logEmitter{})`; the `logEmitter` (lines 126–142) logs the event and returns `false` so the escalation's `emitted` flag never flips true. There is no `pkg/ops/escalation/pgstore.go` or `redisstore.go`, no migration creating `ops_escalations`, and no flush-reconciliation goroutine wired (`opsservice/reconcile.go` line 46 names `EscalationFlush` but it is unconfigured in `main.go`). `ops.escalation.requireDurable` is also missing from `charts/lenny/values.yaml`. Consequence: every escalation is created as `persistence: "buffered-memory"` regardless of Postgres/Redis availability; an Operations Inventory consumer (if it existed — see F3) would always see `escalation_buffered`/`escalation_open` as in-memory; the cap is 100 (`bufferCapacity` constant); restarts lose every escalation; the `escalation_created` event is never published to consumers; the retry goroutine that should re-attempt emission (line 2406–2407) is not wired into the leader loop.

**Resolution (commit 183ebe0f):** The escalation service is now tiered. A new `escalation.Store` interface is implemented by `escalation/pgstore` (Tier 1, `ops_escalations` migration 0122, upsert + filtered list + emission-retry projection, Postgres outage → `ErrStoreUnavailable`), `escalation/redisstore` (Tier 2, the `ops:escalations:{id}` hash with 24h TTL + SCAN list), and the refactored in-memory `MemStore` (Tier 3). The `Service` orchestrates them: `Create` attempts each durable tier in order falling back to memory (or `503 ESCALATION_NO_DURABLE_STORE` when `requireDurable` is set), stamping the accepting tier onto `persistence`; `Get`/`List`/`Update` read from the highest reachable tier; emission stays exactly-once with a cross-tier `RetryEmission`. The leader-only `EscalationFlush` reconciler (wired into `opsservice.Config.Reconcilers` in `main.go`) promotes buffered records upward preserving `createdAt` + `emitted`, rate-limited to `reconciliationWritesPerSecond`, emitting `remediation.escalation_persisted`. The stale "emission stubbed" half was already fixed (`streamEscalationEmitter` returns true on a successful stream publish). `cmd/lenny-ops` composes the durable tiers from the pg pool / Redis client; `ops.escalation.{requireDurable,reconciliationWritesPerSecond}` render as flags; the HTTP layer adds the §25.4 Tier-3 durability warning to the 202 body. Tests: tier-1 service tier-fallback/flush/requireDurable, Redis (miniredis) round-trip, Postgres (embedded) round-trip, opsserver warning, helm-unittest flag render.

### - [x] F-25.4.10 — Helm chart does not render an `Ingress`, a `PodDisruptionBudget`, `topologySpreadConstraints`, or the `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service; readiness probe is non-strict. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 991–1024 + 1356–1373 + 1380–1398. The chart must render a `lenny-ops` Ingress (host, TLS secret, idle timeout, className, annotations), a `PodDisruptionBudget {minAvailable: 1}` regardless of replica count, `topologySpreadConstraints` when `ops.replicas >= 2`, and a `lenny-ops` Service with `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` (3h timeout) for SSE. The readiness probe is `/healthz?strict=true` returning 503 with a dependency-degradation body until Postgres AND K8s API are reachable; the liveness/startup probes use `/healthz` permissively. The Deployment runs non-root with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` plus an `emptyDir` at `/tmp`.

Implementation: `find /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts -iname '*ingress*' -o -iname '*pdb*'` returns no `lenny-ops` Ingress or PDB templates. `grep -n "topologySpread\|PodDisruptionBudget\|publishNotReadyAddresses\|clusterIP: None\|sessionAffinity" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` returns no matches. The `lenny-ops` Service (`ops-deployment.yaml` lines 173–190) is a flat ClusterIP without `sessionAffinity`; no `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service is rendered for `lenny-ops` (the gateway chart's headless Service at `gateway-deployment.yaml` line 282–298 is for the gateway's own per-replica fan-out — but `lenny-ops` has no client wired against it per F8). `ops-deployment.yaml` lines 120–131 readiness probe uses `/healthz` (non-strict); the binary registers no `?strict=true` handler (`opsserver.go` lines 181–183 — `handleHealthz` always returns 200). No `emptyDir` for `/tmp` is rendered. Consequence: a single-replica `lenny-ops` evicted during a node drain has no PDB to slow the eviction, no spread to keep multi-replica deployments off the same node, and no Ingress (so the chart is structurally incompatible with the spec'd external-only access mode). The readiness probe always returns ready, even if Postgres and K8s API are both unreachable, so the Service routes traffic to a replica that cannot serve. SSE clients (`/v1/admin/events`, `/v1/admin/operations` streaming) do not get sticky routing through reconnects. The `readOnlyRootFilesystem` posture is rendered but with no `emptyDir` mount, so any temp-file write will fail (the binary doesn't write temp files today, but the spec calls the seam out explicitly).

**Resolution (commit c08e1be1):** New `charts/lenny/templates/ops-ingress.yaml` renders the lenny-ops `Ingress` (opt-in via `ops.ingress.enabled`, with SSE idle-timeout proxy annotations) and the always-rendered `PodDisruptionBudget {minAvailable: 1}`. `ops-deployment.yaml` now mounts a writable `/tmp` emptyDir under the read-only root, adds `topologySpreadConstraints` (hostname, maxSkew 1) when `ops.replicas >= 2`, and adds a startup probe plus a readiness probe that uses the strict gate `/healthz?strict=true` when `ops.production` (the stock degraded render, which leaves Postgres unwired, keeps the graceful `/readyz`). `opsserver.handleHealthz` now honors `?strict=true`, returning 200 only when both the Postgres and Kubernetes probes pass and 503 with the degraded dependencies named otherwise. The `lenny-gateway-pods` headless Service already existed (that part of the finding was stale); it gained an explicit `publishNotReadyAddresses: false`. Tier-1 helm-unittest + opsserver Go tests cover every branch.

Spec: lines 1455–1512. `lenny-ops` uses the platform's `StoreRouter` (Section 12.6) to access Postgres and Redis. Specific methods named: `PlatformPostgres()`, `PlatformPostgres(region)` (CMP-058), `SessionShard(sessionID)`, `AuditShard(tenantID)`, `AllSessionShards()`, `AllAuditShards()`, `PlatformRedis()`. Implementation: `grep -rn "StoreRouter\|PlatformPostgres\|PlatformRedis\|AuditShard\|SessionShard\|AllSessionShards\|AllAuditShards" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns no matches. `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` lines 132–168 wires a raw `pgxpool.Pool` and a `redis.UniversalClient` directly into the dependency probes; the lock/escalation/backup services are wired against in-memory stores instead of the StoreRouter abstraction. Tier-1 tests cover the param matrix, the not-found/upstream/unavailable error mappings, and bare-seconds `?since=`.

### - [x] F-25.4.19 — TLS-default posture (NET-070): `ops.tls.internalEnabled`, plaintext acknowledgment guard, `lenny_ops_admin_api_tls_handshake_total{plaintext}` alerting, and the `lenny-preflight` `ops-admin-tls` probe are absent. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2520–2546. `ops.tls.internalEnabled: true` is the non-dev default; the GatewayClient calls the gateway internal admin API on port 8443 (the gateway's `internalTLSPort`) using the cluster trust bundle + an operator-supplied CA via `ops.tls.caBundleConfigMap`. Plaintext is admitted only when `ops.tls.internalEnabled: false` AND `ops.acknowledgePlaintextAdminAPI: true` (auto-implied by `global.devMode: true`); the chart `required` guard fails `helm install/upgrade` with a message pointing at NET-070 otherwise. `lenny_ops_admin_api_tls_handshake_total{result}` is emitted on every `GatewayClient` request attempt; a `plaintext` result fires the `OpsAdminAPIPlaintextDetected` critical alert (§16.5). `lenny-preflight` runs an `ops-admin-tls` handshake probe against the gateway's internal TLS port verifying SAN coverage of the `lenny-gateway` ClusterIP hostname.

Implementation: `ops.tls`, `ops.acknowledgePlaintextAdminAPI`, and `ops.tls.caBundleConfigMap` are absent from `charts/lenny/values.yaml` (see F9). `ops-deployment.yaml` line 100 hardcodes `--gateway-url=http://lenny-gateway.{namespace}.svc:{gateway.internalPort}` — always plaintext, with no TLS/internal-tls option. `grep -rn "lenny_ops_admin_api_tls_handshake_total\|OpsAdminAPIPlaintextDetected\|ops-admin-tls\|acknowledgePlaintextAdminAPI\|internalEnabled" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns no matches. The Helm chart `required` guard refusing plaintext outside dev mode is not implemented. Consequence: the GatewayClient transit (when wired — F8) carries the `lenny-ops-sa` JWT with platform-admin scope in cleartext between pods, exactly the threat model NET-070 fixes. Compromise of any `lenny-system` sidecar with packet capture (or any admission-webhook peer) can lift the replayable platform-admin token. The `OTLPPlaintextEgressDetected` alert symmetry §25.4 banks on for parity (line 2545) cannot fire on the ops surface.

**Resolution:** Some pieces were already present (`ops.tls.internalEnabled`/`certSecretName`, the `OpsAdminAPIPlaintextDetected` alert in `pkg/alerting/rules`, the network-policy port keyed to `internalEnabled`); this batch completes the posture. `ops.tls.internalEnabled` now **defaults to `true`** per the spec ("defaults to true in every non-dev profile"), matching the OTLP-068 secure-default precedent. New `ops.acknowledgePlaintextAdminAPI` value + `charts/lenny/templates/ops-tls-guard.yaml` `{{ fail }}` render-time guard (modeled on `otlp-tls-guard.yaml`) refuse `helm install`/`upgrade` when `internalEnabled: false` is set without the acknowledgment outside `global.devMode`. `ops-deployment.yaml` renders the admin-API URL TLS-aware (`https://…:internalTLSPort` + `--gateway-internal-tls=true`, or the acknowledged plaintext `http://…:internalPort`), mounts the projected SA token, and mounts `ops.tls.caBundleConfigMap` (passed as `--gateway-ca-bundle-file`, loaded into the client transport's RootCAs). The `lenny_ops_admin_api_tls_handshake_total{result}` instrument (`plaintext`/`tls`/`tls_error`) emits on every `GatewayClient` request — the exact metric the existing `OpsAdminAPIPlaintextDetected` alert reads — exercised each tick by the F-25.4.8 `gateway_auth` self-health probe. New `pkg/preflight.OpsAdminTLSCheck` (`ops-admin-tls`) dials the gateway internal-TLS port, validates the handshake + SAN coverage of the `lenny-gateway` ClusterIP hostname, is skipped under the acknowledged plaintext path, and is wired into `cmd/lenny-preflight` + the preflight Job args. Tests: tier-1 `OpsAdminTLSCheck` decision matrix, client handshake-result classification (closed with F-25.4.8); tier-2 helm-unittest `ops-tls-guard` (default-passes / unack-fails / ack-passes / devMode-passes) + deployment TLS-vs-plaintext URL + caBundle mount + netpol-default-flip fixup.

Implementation: `charts/lenny/values.yaml` line 374 carries `releaseChannel.publicKeyPath` (good). `requireDigest: false` is at line 373; `grep -rn "requireDigest" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` reveals only the value rendered into the gateway deployment context — no admission-time enforcement gate. `platform.upgradeChannel` is not exposed under the top-level `platform:` block (gating per F17, since no cron polls it anyway). `platform_upgrade_check_cache` is absent from migrations (F13). Consequence: air-gapped operators cannot follow the documented setup steps to disable upgrade polling cleanly or pre-populate the cache; the digest-enforcement gate exists as a Helm value but does not flow through to any chart template that wires the value into a verifying admission control.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed; the three knobs land in lockstep with their gating findings, all still OPEN: `platform.upgradeChannel: ""` requires F-25.4.17 (cron evaluator's `platform_upgrade_check` is unwired), `platform_upgrade_check_cache` requires F-25.4.13 (the `ops_*` Postgres schemas are unmigrated), and `requireDigest: true` admission enforcement requires the §17.6 image-pull policy work tracked under §17.6 / §5.3 SHA pinning. Adding the standalone Helm value with no downstream wiring would create an inert promise.

### - [x] F-25.4.24 — `lenny-ops` HTTP server lacks the structured-logging primitive §25.4 documents. (Low) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2499–2509. JSON log lines include `ts/level/msg/component/operation_id/agent_name/trace_id`. The trace_id is propagated from `X-Lenny-Operation-ID`/`X-Lenny-Agent-Name` request headers (§25.2 Operation Correlation Headers).

Implementation: `grep -rn "trace_id\|operation_id.*log\|component.*log\|structured.*log\|slog\|zap\|zerolog" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns no matches; the implementation uses Go's stdlib `log` (line-text format) throughout. The HTTP middleware does not read `X-Lenny-Operation-ID`/`X-Lenny-Agent-Name` correlation headers; `grep -rn "X-Lenny-Operation-ID\|X-Lenny-Agent-Name" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops` returns no matches. Consequence: operators cannot grep `lenny-ops` container logs by operation ID to correlate a restore failure across the request, the worker, and the audit trail. Log aggregation (Loki, ELK, CloudWatch) cannot index by structured fields because the lines are free-text.

**Resolution:** `pkg/ops/opsserver/middleware.go` adds two HTTP middlewares wired around the `Server` mux in `New`: `withCorrelation` reads `X-Lenny-Operation-ID`, `X-Lenny-Agent-Name`, `traceparent`, `X-Lenny-Tenant-ID`, and `X-Lenny-Session-ID` from the inbound request (via `correlation.FromHTTPHeader`), stamps `component=lenny-ops` per §16.4, merges onto any pre-existing context scope, and stores the resulting `correlation.Fields` on the request context. `withAccessLog` emits one `slog.LevelInfo` line per request carrying `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms`; the §25.4 JSON handler (`pkg/observability/logging.NewJSONHandler`) auto-projects the correlation fields as top-level structured attributes (`component`, `operation_id`, `agent_name`, `trace_id`, …). `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` installs `configureStructuredLogging()` immediately after flag parsing: it builds the JSON handler with `DefaultComponent: "lenny-ops"`, sets it as `slog.Default`, and bridges the stdlib `log` package onto the slog logger via `slogWriter` so every legacy `log.Printf` call surfaces in the §25.4 envelope. `ContextWithComponent` exposes the same component-stamping helper to background loops (leader-elected reconcilers) so non-HTTP log lines also carry the binary label.

### - [x] F-25.4.25 — `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus` opt-out, `ops.recommendations.disableOnPrometheusOutage`, and the `lenny-preflight` Prometheus-reachability check are absent. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 1416–1452. `lenny-preflight` checks for a reachable Prometheus endpoint at `ops.prometheus.url`; emits tier-specific INFO/WARN messages; Tier 2/3 operators who intentionally run without Prometheus must set `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus: true` to suppress the warning. `ops.recommendations.disableOnPrometheusOutage: true` makes recommendation endpoints return 503 instead of fan-out fallback.

Implementation: `charts/lenny/values.yaml` lines 185–305 (the `monitoring:` block) carries no `acknowledgeNoPrometheus` key. `grep -rn "acknowledgeNoPrometheus\|disableOnPrometheusOutage\|RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE\|ops.prometheus.url\|prometheus.unreachableThreshold" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops` returns no matches. The `lenny-preflight` package (`grep -rn "prometheus\|/api/v1/query\|tier1\|tier2\|tier3" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-preflight 2>/dev/null`) likewise contains no Prometheus reachability check (the package may not exist at all in this scope). Consequence: the Tier-2/3 deployment contract requiring an explicit prometheus URL is unenforced; operators silently lose recommendations and historical diagnostics with no preflight signal, and there's no opt-out flag to acknowledge the choice.

**Resolution (commit a9577fb6):** `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus` was already present (stale evidence); the recommendation Prometheus-outage opt-out existed under `gateway.recommendations.disableOnPrometheusOutage` (the gateway hosts the recommendation service, `pkg/gateway/recommendations` already returns `RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE` when configured). The two real gaps are now closed. New `pkg/preflight/PrometheusReachabilityCheck` (`prometheus-reachability`) probes `ops.prometheus.url` via the Prometheus query API (any HTTP < 500 = reachable), is non-blocking by construction (§25.4 line 1467), emits the tier-specific advisory (INFO at Tier 1, WARN at Tier 2/3 suppressed by `monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus`), and skips the live dial under `skipNetworkProbes`. Wired into `cmd/lenny-preflight` + the Job args (`--prometheus-url`/`--platform-tier`/`--acknowledge-no-prometheus` from `ops.prometheus.url`/`global.deploymentTier`/`monitoring.acknowledgeNoPrometheus`); the cmd's report loop now surfaces advisory Reasons on passed checks (previously only "ok" printed, hiding the cosign/prometheus WARNs). The opt-out value moved to the spec-canonical `ops.recommendations.disableOnPrometheusOutage` (§25.4 line 944), with the gateway Deployment rendering `--recommendations-disable-on-prometheus-outage` from it. Tier-1 reachability decision matrix (tier × configured × reachable × acknowledged) + URL-naming test; tier-2 helm-unittest for the preflight args and the relocated gateway opt-out arg.

### - [x] F-25.4.26 — Multi-replica scaling safety knob (`ops.locks.memoryTier: "single-replica-only"`) and Endpoint-based replica detection are absent. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2178–2188 + 1518–1556 ("Multi-Replica Lenny-Ops Scaling"). The default `"single-replica-only"` mode detects single-replica deployments via K8s Endpoints lookup at startup and re-checks every 30s; multi-replica deployments with this default reject Tier 3 acquisitions with `503 REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION`.

Implementation: `pkg/ops/coordination/locks.go` ships only `MemStore`; there is no `memoryTier` config or single-replica check; `Acquire` always succeeds in-memory regardless of replica count. `grep -rn "memoryTier\|REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops` reveals the error code is defined (`locks.go` line 62, `ErrCodeNoCoordination`) but never raised. Consequence: when the chart is rendered with `replicas: 2` (current default, `values.yaml` line 749), every Tier 3 lock acquisition silently grants un-coordinated per-replica locks. Two agents acting on `pool:default-gvisor` from different `lenny-ops` replicas both succeed and run conflicting remediations.

**Resolution (commit 4cf8e76e):** New `pkg/ops/coordination/gate.go` adds the `MemoryTier` policy (`single-replica-only` default, `always`, `never`, parsed/validated at startup) and a `CoordinationGate` that the acquire handler consults before the in-memory store. `pkg/ops/opsservice/replicas.go` adds an `EndpointsReplicaCounter` that reads the `lenny-ops` Service Endpoints (synchronous startup lookup + 30s re-check per §25.4 line 2208) and satisfies `coordination.ReplicaCounter`. Under `single-replica-only`, a multi-replica deployment rejects an in-memory acquire with `503 REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION`/`TRANSIENT`; `always` grants the lock with a replica-local `degradation.warnings` entry; `never` rejects every Tier-3 acquire. The gate governs only acquisition (release/extend/steal/reads are unaffected). Wired in `cmd/lenny-ops` (clientset-backed counter when a cluster connection exists; nil counter → single-replica behavior in single-process dev). Helm: `ops.locks.memoryTier` value, `--locks-memory-tier`/`--ops-service-name` args, `POD_NAMESPACE` downward-API env, and `endpoints` get/list/watch on the `lenny-ops-namespace` Role. Since the v1 lock store is always the in-memory tier, the gate evaluates on every acquire; the Postgres/Redis tiers (F-25.4.6) will consult the active tier first when they land. Tier-1 tests cover the gate matrix, the Endpoints counter (fake clientset, including read-error retention and zero-floor), and the handler branches; tier-2 helm-unittest covers the args/env/RBAC.

### - [x] F-25.4.28 — `noopElector` in `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go` does not implement `ReleaseOnCancel` behavior or expose the holder identity for `kubectl get leases`. (Info) [Medium] — CLOSED

### - [x] F-25.4.30 — Spec'd `ops.gateway.url` defaults to HTTPS port 8443 (NET-070); chart hardcodes plaintext `http://lenny-gateway:{gateway.internalPort}`. (High — duplicate of F19 with chart-template scope) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 836–841 — `ops.gateway.url: "https://lenny-gateway:8443"` is the documented default; "chart renders `http://lenny-gateway:8080` only when `ops.tls.internalEnabled=false` AND `ops.acknowledgePlaintextAdminAPI=true` (or dev mode)."

Implementation: `charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` line 100 — `- --gateway-url=http://lenny-gateway.{{ .Release.Namespace }}.svc:{{ .Values.gateway.internalPort }}` is hardcoded plaintext with no conditional on `ops.tls.internalEnabled`. The Helm value `gateway.internalTLSPort` is referenced (line 703 of `system-network-policies.yaml`) for the NetworkPolicy but never wired into the `lenny-ops` `--gateway-url` argument. Consequence: every deployment unconditionally uses the plaintext admin API path, regardless of the deployer's TLS posture preferences. Cross-listed for the chart-side scope of F19 because the violation is concretely in `ops-deployment.yaml`.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed as an explicit duplicate of F-25.4.19 (the High §25.4 finding covering the full NET-070 TLS-default posture — `ops.tls.internalEnabled`, plaintext acknowledgment guard, `lenny_ops_admin_api_tls_handshake_total{plaintext}` alerting, and the `lenny-preflight` `ops-admin-tls` probe). The chart-template scope this finding flags (`ops-deployment.yaml --gateway-url` hardcoded to plaintext) is the same code path; the NET-070 chart `required` guard, the conditional URL rendering, and the wiring of `gateway.internalTLSPort` into the `--gateway-url` argument all land under F-25.4.19. Closing the chart-template scope in isolation would create an inert partial fix because the chart `required` guard, the TLS-handshake metric, and the preflight probe are co-dependent. F-25.4.19 stays OPEN.

### Summary

§25.4 is the largest single section in §25, and it is also the most thinly implemented. The HTTP surface in `pkg/ops/opsserver` registers about a third of the endpoints `lenny-ops` is supposed to host, every endpoint runs without authentication or rate limiting, the prescribed Helm-value surface is reduced to seven knobs (versus several dozen documented), and the chart renders neither the Ingress, PDB, topology spread, headless Service, prescribed RBAC, nor the four NetworkPolicies. The §25.4 invariants that hold the rest of the operability surface together — multi-tier storage for locks/escalations/idempotency with split-brain prevention, the canonical OIDC + scope-based authorization, the `GatewayClient` with fan-out fallback, the Prometheus-backed `MetricSource`, the `/v1/admin/me` and `/v1/admin/operations` discovery endpoints — are unimplemented. Sixteen High findings (F1–F14, F19, F20, F30), eight Medium findings (F15–F18, F22, F25, F26), three Low/Info findings (F21, F23, F24, F27, F28, F29) reflect that depth.

The architectural gap is dominant: most §25.4 features depend on substrates (OIDC middleware, `StoreRouter` with shard methods, Postgres ops_* schemas, headless fan-out client, Prometheus source) that simply have no code today. A small number of fixes would unblock large blocks of the surface — for example, landing the OIDC middleware (F1, F20) and the `ops_*` migrations (F13) would unlock the per-`sub` rate limiter (F5), idempotency (F4), durable locks (F6), and durable escalations (F7) together.

## §25.5 Operational Event Stream <a id="25.5"></a>
Reviewed: 2026-05-23.

Spec source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` lines 2550–2807 (heading `## 25.5 Operational Event Stream`, ending at `## 25.6 Diagnostic Endpoints`). §25.5 is the canonical reference for the operational-event feed: the Redis `ops:events:stream` capped stream (with the gateway in-memory ring buffer as fallback), the CloudEvents v1.0.2 envelope (with OCSF for audit-bearing events), the SSE/polling/webhook delivery surfaces, the webhook subscription registry (Postgres tables, secret lifecycle, generation-stamped cache and invalidation RPC, SSRF/DNS-rebinding protections, tenant isolation), the canonical pagination/cursor model with gap detection, the degradation envelope across the four outage matrices, the §25.5 metrics, and the §25.5 error codes.

### Method

Read §25.5 in full; enumerated the normative event-stream surface:

1. **Redis capped stream** — Key `ops:events:stream`, `XADD` with `MAXLEN ~ {ops.events.streamMaxLen}`; tier defaults (10k/50k/100k) and `~500B` event size budget; stream-ID-as-monotonic-eventId; eviction → `pagination.gapDetected: true` (lines 2552, 2592–2611).
2. **CloudEvents envelope** — JSON record per CloudEvents v1.0.2 JSON Format; `type = dev.lenny.<short_name>` (e.g., `dev.lenny.alert_fired`, `dev.lenny.upgrade_progressed`, `dev.lenny.operation_progressed`); `source = //lenny.dev/{gateway|ops}/{replicaId}`; extensions `lennytenantid`, `lennyoperationid`, `lennyrootsessionid`; `id ≡ eventKey`; `severity` as an extension attribute; `datacontenttype: application/ocsf+json` + OCSF v1.1.0 record in `data` for audit-bearing events (lines 2554–2556).
3. **Endpoints** — `GET /v1/admin/events/stream` (SSE), `GET /v1/admin/events` (polling), `POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/admin/event-subscriptions` and `/{id}`, `GET /v1/admin/event-subscriptions/{id}/deliveries`, plus `POST /v1/admin/event-subscriptions/{id}/rotate-secret` from the secret-lifecycle section (lines 2560–2569, 2729).
4. **Go interface** — `EventStreamService` with `StreamEvents`, `ListEvents`, `CreateSubscription`, `ListSubscriptions`, `GetSubscription`, `UpdateSubscription`, `DeleteSubscription`, `ListDeliveries` (lines 2574–2585).
5. **Emission responsibility** — Both gateway and `lenny-ops` write the same Redis stream and the gateway's in-memory ring buffer (via an internal RPC when `lenny-ops` emits); `lenny-ops` emits the §16.6 ops-originated catalogue (`ops_health_status_changed`, `escalation_created`, `remediation_lock_*`, `drift_detected`, `platform_upgrade_*`, `operation_progressed`); `source` carries the emitter (`gateway` or `lenny-ops`) (line 2590).
6. **Webhook subscriptions** — Postgres tables `ops_event_subscriptions` (id, callback_url, types, severity, secret_hash, secret_fingerprint, description, created_by, created_by_tenant_id, tenant_filter, generation, created_at, updated_at, active) and `ops_event_deliveries` (subscription_id, event_id, event_type, status, attempts, last_attempt_at, last_error, created_at, expires_at) with the two indexes; `deliveryRetentionDays` tier defaults; nightly `LIMIT 10000` purge at 03:45 UTC; `deliveryTrackingMode: metric-only` / `failures-only` with `failuresOnlyRetentionDays` (lines 2613–2664).
7. **Cursor model** — Opaque base64 cursor encoding `source_kind ∈ {redis, buffer, mixed} || ":" || source_position`; agents MUST NOT parse cursors; `pagination.cursorKind`; cross-source translation by `eventKey`; gap behavior with `oldestAvailableCursor`; ordering key is the `eventKey` (`{replicaID}:{emittedAt}:{nonce}`) (lines 2666–2675).
8. **SSE delivery** — Holds an open response, `XREAD BLOCK 0` on a goroutine; SSE frame `data:` carries the full CloudEvents JSON record; SSE `id:` carries the CloudEvents `id` so `Last-Event-ID` resumes via `XRANGE`; canonical query filters `?eventType`, `?severity`, `?resourceType`, `?resourceId`, `?since`; per-connection independent read cursors (no consumer group); Redis-down fallback to the gateway buffer (`GET /v1/admin/events/buffer`) every 2 s with periodic `:degradation` comment line; transparent `XREAD` ↔ buffer transition with last-eventKey tracking and `:gap` comment when no continuation can be located (lines 2677–2685).
9. **Polling delivery** — Canonical pagination envelope (`items`, `pagination.cursor`, `pagination.hasMore`, `pagination.cursorKind`, `pagination.headCursor`); chronological order by default with `?sortOrder=desc` reversal; transparent source fallback; `pagination.gapDetected: true` and `pagination.oldestAvailableCursor` when the encoded source cannot be honored; canonical `degradation` envelope on buffer service (lines 2687–2699).
10. **Webhook delivery** — Per-subscription background goroutine; Redis stream (or buffer) read; `Content-Type: application/cloudevents+json`; headers `X-Lenny-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256), `X-Lenny-Event-Type`, `X-Lenny-Event-Id`, `X-Lenny-Delivery-Id` (UUID per attempt), `X-Lenny-Delivery-Attempt` (1-based); 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff (1s / 5s / 30s); after exhaustion the row is `failed` in `ops_event_deliveries` and an `event_delivery_failed` event is emitted (not redelivered to the same subscription) (lines 2701–2713).
11. **Webhook secret lifecycle** — Server-side generation of a 256-bit CSPRNG secret, SHA-256 stored as `secret_hash`, plaintext returned once with the `secretRotationWarning`; never logged; never returned on read endpoints; `POST /v1/admin/event-subscriptions/{id}/rotate-secret` with a 60-second dual-secret overlap; `DELETE` revokes (in-flight deliveries finish); audit events `ops_event.subscription_created`, `subscription_secret_rotated`, `subscription_updated`, `subscription_deleted`; first-8-char SHA-256 fingerprint in the created audit event (lines 2715–2733).
12. **SSRF and DNS-rebinding protections** — HTTPS-only (HTTP needs `ops.webhooks.allowHTTP`); registered domain (not raw IPv4/IPv6 literal); per-delivery DNS resolve + private-CIDR check covering RFC 1918, RFC 4193, RFC 3927, loopback, multicast, reserved, K8s service+pod CIDRs (via `ops.webhooks.blockedCIDRs`); explicit IMDS block (`169.254.169.254`, `metadata.google.internal`, `fd00:ec2::254`); HTTP client does NOT follow redirects; optional `ops.webhooks.domainAllowlist` suffix allowlist (lines 2735–2745).
13. **Subscription cache and invalidation** — In-memory cache populated on startup and on every CRUD; synchronous in-process update + `subscription_cache_invalidate` internal RPC over the headless Service across replicas; `generation` counter per subscription checked before each delivery (deleted-but-not-yet-invalidated is skipped); 60-second periodic refresh; cold-start with Postgres-down logs loudly and emits `ops_health_status_changed` with `subscriptionsUnavailable: true`; refresh non-blocking (lines 2747–2756).
14. **Tenant isolation** — `platform-admin` defaults to `tenantFilter: "*"`; `tenant-admin` may only create subscriptions with `tenantFilter: "{their-tenant}"`; `403 SUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_FORBIDDEN`; `created_by_tenant_id` column; per-event match before dispatch; platform-scoped events match only `*` filters; SSE/polling apply the same filter (lines 2758–2766).
15. **Degradation matrix** — Four cases (Redis down / Gateway down / Postgres down / Redis+Gateway down / Postgres+Redis down) each with documented response shape; per-replica `lenny-ops` local ring buffer of 500 events for ops-originated events during the Redis+Gateway dual outage; recovery flush of the local buffer with `eventKey` deduplication (lines 2768–2780).
16. **Metrics** — `lenny_ops_events_stream_length` (gauge), `lenny_ops_events_stream_gaps_total` (counter), `lenny_ops_events_sse_active_connections` (gauge), `lenny_ops_events_webhook_delivery_total{subscription_id, status}` (counter), `lenny_ops_events_webhook_delivery_latency_seconds{subscription_id}` (histogram); the operator-facing `lenny_ops_events_stream_maxlen` reference in the memory-monitoring alert (lines 2786–2792, 2606).
17. **Error codes** — `INVALID_EVENT_FILTER` (400 PERMANENT), `WEBHOOK_VALIDATION_FAILED` (422 PERMANENT), `EVENT_STREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (503 TRANSIENT), `EVENT_STREAM_DEGRADED` (200 metadata), `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND` (404 PERMANENT), `SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` (503 TRANSIENT), plus `SUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_FORBIDDEN` (403 from §25.5 tenant-isolation) (lines 2795–2802, 2763).
18. **Audit events** — `ops_event.subscription_created`, `ops_event.subscription_updated`, `ops_event.subscription_deleted` (lines 2804–2806).

Evidence gathered via `grep`/`find` across `pkg/gateway/eventbus/`, `pkg/gateway/opsevents/`, `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/`, `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/pgstore/`, `pkg/ops/opsserver/`, `pkg/ops/opsservice/`, `pkg/webhookdelivery/`, `cmd/lenny-ops/`, `migrations/`, and `pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go`.

### Findings

### - [x] F-25.5.1 — The Redis `ops:events:stream` is not written or read. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-25.2.1, F-25.3.1, F-25.3.18 — Four members describe the gateway EventEmitter never writing to the Redis ops:events:stream, and two describe the unimplemented SSE /v1/admin/events/stream endpoint; the lag gauge and CLOSED service findings are distinct.

**Resolution:** The stream is now both written and read. Write: `events.StreamEmitter` creates the `ops:events:stream` key via `XADD` with `Approx` `MAXLEN` honoring `DefaultStreamMaxLen` (operator-tunable), producing the CloudEvents-bearing entries from the gateway, controllers, and lenny-ops. Read: `opsservice.RedisEventSource` (commit 97ae8442) consumes the same key by `XRANGE` from an opaque per-process cursor. The remaining §25.5 query surfaces that sit on top of the stream (the SSE `GET /v1/admin/events/stream` and polling `GET /v1/admin/events`, and the opaque source-kind cursor encoding) are the separate F-25.5.2 / F-25.5.3 / F-25.5.4. Closed by 97ae8442 plus the prior StreamEmitter wiring.

### - [x] F-25.5.2 — `GET /v1/admin/events/stream` (SSE) is not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2562, 2677–2685. The SSE handler holds an open response, `XREAD BLOCK 0` on a goroutine, frames each event as a CloudEvents JSON record on the `data:` line, sends the CloudEvents `id` on the SSE `id:` line so clients can resume with `Last-Event-ID`, applies canonical filters (`?eventType`, `?severity`, `?resourceType`, `?resourceId`, `?since`), per-connection independent read cursor (no consumer group), transparent buffer-poll fallback every 2 s when Redis is unreachable with `:degradation`/`:gap` comment lines.

The session SSE stream (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events.go`) and the SDK SSE parser (`sdks/client/go/lenny/stream.go`) target the `/v1/sessions/{id}/events` surface, not the operational stream. Consequence: agents and watchdogs cannot subscribe to the operational event feed via SSE; the canonical real-time channel of §25.5 is unavailable.

**Resolution:** `events.Service.HandleStream` is registered at `GET /v1/admin/events/stream` (`registerEventStreamRoutes`) and wired from `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` (`EventStream: eventStream`). It holds the response open, replays the backlog after the resume point, then streams live frames; each frame's `id:` line carries the CloudEvents id (eventKey) so a client reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` resumes by eventKey, and an evicted resume point emits a `:gap` comment. Filters honour `?eventType/?severity/?resourceType/?resourceId/?since`. A latent bug was fixed: the opsserver access-log `statusRecorder` now forwards `Flush()`, without which the SSE `http.Flusher` assertion failed and the stream aborted. Closed by f359b02c.

### - [x] F-25.5.3 — `GET /v1/admin/events` (polling) is not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

The gateway exposes only `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go` + `pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:300`) — the §25.3 buffer endpoint, not the §25.5 polling surface. The buffer endpoint returns `BufferedEventPage` (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` lines 72–88) with `Events`, `Cursor` (a `uint64` monotonic id), `HasMore`, `GapDetected`, `OldestAvailableCursor`, `BufferAge` — none of `cursorKind`, `headCursor`, `?sortOrder`, the canonical filter set (`?resourceType`, `?resourceId`), or the source-translating opaque base64 cursor. Consequence: agents that prefer polling cannot read the operational stream; even the buffer endpoint, which §25.5 designates as the fallback source, is not reachable through the §25.5 polling URL.

**Resolution:** `events.Service.HandlePoll` is registered at `GET /v1/admin/events` and returns the §25.2 canonical envelope: `items` plus `pagination.{cursor, hasMore, cursorKind, headCursor}` with opaque base64 source-kind cursors. It honours `?cursor=` (opaque), `?limit=` (default 100, max 1000), `?sortOrder=asc|desc`, the canonical filter set, and reports `pagination.gapDetected` + `oldestAvailableCursor` when the cursor's event has been evicted. Bad input (unknown event type/severity, malformed cursor/sortOrder/since) returns `400 INVALID_EVENT_FILTER`. The Redis→buffer transparent source fallback is the F-25.5.14 degradation matrix; the cursor already encodes the source kind so it is forward-compatible. Closed by f359b02c.

### - [x] F-25.5.4 — The cursor model is uncoded. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2666–2675 ("Event cursors are opaque strings containing an internal representation that always round-trips correctly regardless of which source served the response. The cursor encodes both the source kind and the source-specific position: cursor := base64(source_kind || ":" || source_position) Where source_kind is one of `redis`, `buffer`, or `mixed`... The canonical ordering key is `eventKey` (a ULID-like `{replicaID}:{emittedAt}:{nonce}`)").

Implementation: `grep -rn "cursorKind\|source_kind\|mixed.*cursor\|base64.*source" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops` returns no matches. `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` line 73 uses a bare `uint64` `Cursor` field; nothing encodes the source kind, nothing translates between sources by `eventKey`. The `eventKey` itself is built (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/emitter.go` lines 53–62 — `{replicaID}:{emittedAt}:{nonce}`), but it is never used as the cross-source translation key because there is only one source (buffer). Consequence: when Redis is added, cursors handed out by Redis will not round-trip to the buffer and vice versa; the §25.5 contract that "Agents MUST NOT parse cursors — they opaquely round-trip them" cannot be honored.

**Resolution:** `pkg/ops/events/cursor.go` encodes the opaque cursor as `base64(source_kind || ":" || eventKey)` with `source_kind` one of `redis`, `buffer`, or `mixed`. The source position is the canonical `eventKey` (`{replicaID}:{emittedAt}:{nonce}`), which is source-independent, so a cursor produced by any source is translated by `EventBuffer.Lookup(eventKey)` — a foreign (redis) cursor whose event is still retained round-trips and the page reports `cursorKind: "mixed"`; an evicted key reports `gapDetected`. The lenny-ops Service now stamps a unique nonce-bearing eventKey on every publish so the cursor and SSE `Last-Event-ID` resume are unambiguous. Closed by f359b02c.

### - [x] F-25.5.8 — `POST /v1/admin/event-subscriptions/{id}/rotate-secret` and the §25.5 secret lifecycle are not implemented. (High) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2715–2733. (1) Secret server-generated as 256-bit CSPRNG and stored as SHA-256 hash in `secret_hash`; (2) plaintext returned **once** in the response body with the `secretRotationWarning`; (3) `rotate-secret` endpoint generates a new secret, returns it once, updates the stored hash, with a 60-second dual-secret overlap window (HMAC-verifying both old and new); (4) read endpoints (`GET .../`, `GET .../{id}`) omit the secret field entirely; (5) audit events `ops_event.subscription_secret_rotated`, `subscription_created`, `subscription_updated`, `subscription_deleted`; (6) created audit event records the first-8-char SHA-256 fingerprint of the secret.

Implementation: `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/eventsubscription.go:79–83` (`CreateRequest`) accepts a caller-supplied `Secret` rather than generating one server-side; `pgstore.go:88` and `eventsubscription.go:217` persist the plaintext `Secret` in the `secret` column; the response includes the plaintext on both create AND every subsequent `GET` (the `Subscription` struct keeps `Secret string \`json:"secret,omitempty"\`` line 72 with no `OnRead` redaction). No `rotate-secret` route is registered; `grep -rn "rotate-secret\|secret_rotated\|secretRotationWarning\|secret_fingerprint" /Users/joan/projects/lenny` returns no matches. No 60-second dual-secret overlap exists in the HMAC sign path (`pkg/webhookdelivery/transport.go:85–89` signs with the single `Secret`). No audit emission is wired. **Resolution:** The secret is generated server-side (256-bit CSPRNG, `whsec_` prefix), stored only as its SHA-256 hash + 8-char fingerprint, returned once on create/rotate with the `secretRotationWarning`, and omitted from all read endpoints. `POST .../{id}/rotate-secret` rotates the hash, records `previous_secret_fingerprint` + `secret_rotated_at` for the 60s `WithinRotationOverlap` window, and audits `subscription_secret_rotated`. Closed by f9936930.

Spec: lines 2735–2745. (1) HTTPS-only (HTTP needs `ops.webhooks.allowHTTP`); (2) host must be a registered domain — not a raw IPv4 or IPv6 literal, and not a URL whose path/userinfo carries an IP literal (`https://example.com@127.0.0.1/`); (3) per-delivery DNS resolution + private-CIDR check against RFC 1918, RFC 4193, RFC 3927, loopback, multicast, reserved, and the K8s service+pod CIDR ranges (`ops.webhooks.blockedCIDRs`); (4) IMDS addresses explicitly blocked (`169.254.169.254`, `metadata.google.internal`, `fd00:ec2::254`); (5) HTTP client does NOT follow redirects (redirect from whitelisted callback = failure); (6) optional `ops.webhooks.domainAllowlist` suffix allowlist.

Implementation: `pkg/ops/eventsubscription/eventsubscription.go:172–192` (`validateCreate`) checks only that `callbackUrl` parses, the scheme is `http`/`https`, and the host is non-empty — no IP literal rejection, no allowlist suffix, no DNS resolution. `pkg/webhookdelivery/transport.go:103–110` correctly sets `CheckRedirect: http.ErrUseLastResponse` (the redirect block is wired), but `Deliver` (lines 117–138) calls `http.Client.Do` directly with no pre-DNS resolve, no resolved-IP private-range check, no IMDS denylist, no `domainAllowlist` or `blockedCIDRs` consultation. `grep -rn "allowHTTP\|domainAllowlist\|blockedCIDRs\|169\\.254\\.169\\.254\|metadata\\.google\\.internal\|fd00:ec2::254" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/webhookdelivery` returns no matches — none of the SSRF knobs is wired. Consequence: a malicious or compromised `platform-admin` caller registers `https://127.0.0.1:8080/restricted` or `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/...` as a callback URL and forwards every operational event into the loopback or the cloud IMDS; on Azure/AWS this is a credential-exfiltration channel. The DNS-rebinding gap §25.5 explicitly calls out ("The check happens on every delivery — this closes the DNS rebinding gap where a URL that resolves to a legitimate IP at subscription time later resolves to `127.0.0.1`", line 2741) is wide open: even if the create-time check were added, every subsequent delivery would still re-resolve and could hit a private IP.

**Resolution:** New `eventsubscription.SSRFValidator` (scheme gate with `allowHTTP`, IP-literal + metadata-host rejection, suffix `domainAllowlist`, per-resolve private/reserved/CGNAT/IMDS/`blockedCIDRs` check) runs at create and update; `webhookdelivery.Transport.WithSSRFGuard` re-validates before every delivery dial, closing the DNS-rebinding gap. Closed by f9936930.

Implementation: `pkg/ops/opsserver/event_subscriptions.go:16–23` defines its own error map keyed on `eventsubscription.ErrCodeNotFound = "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND"` (not `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND`), `ErrCodeInvalid = "VALIDATION_ERROR"` (not `INVALID_EVENT_FILTER` or `WEBHOOK_VALIDATION_FAILED`), and `ErrCodeNoDurableStore = "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"` (not `SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`). Consequence: agents reading §25.5 cannot match on the documented codes; SDK-side retry classification breaks because `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` is a coarser category than `SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` and an SDK that hard-codes the §25.5 mapping is given a different code.

**Resolution:** The subscription surface now emits the canonical §25.5 codes — `INVALID_EVENT_FILTER` (400), `WEBHOOK_VALIDATION_FAILED` (422), `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND` (404), `SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` (503), and `SUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_FORBIDDEN` (403) — through `eventSubscriptionErrorMap`. The stream-surface codes (`EVENT_STREAM_UNAVAILABLE`/`_DEGRADED`) belong to the unbuilt SSE/poll endpoints (F-25.5.2/.3). Closed by f9936930.

### - [x] F-25.5.13 — The subscription cache, generation-stamped invalidation RPC, and cold-start signaling are absent. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2747–2756. (1) Cache populated on startup and on every CRUD; (2) synchronous in-process update + `subscription_cache_invalidate` internal RPC over the headless Service across replicas; (3) per-subscription `generation` counter checked before each delivery; (4) 60-second periodic refresh; (5) cold-start logs loudly and emits `ops_health_status_changed` with `subscriptionsUnavailable: true` when Postgres is down; (6) refresh is non-blocking.

Implementation: `pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache.go` implements (1) (synchronous initial load, line 69), (4) (30-second default refresh, line 55 — NOTE the spec says 60 s, the code says 30 s as the worker reconcile cadence), and (6) (background goroutine, line 70). None of (2), (3), or (5) is implemented: there is no `subscription_cache_invalidate` RPC over the headless Service, no `generation` field on `WebhookSubscription` (`webhookloop.go:32–42`) and no per-delivery check, and no `subscriptionsUnavailable: true` flag is emitted to `ops_health_status_changed` from the cold-start path (the cache "stays empty on failure" per `subscriptioncache.go:67–68` comment, with no signal raised). The `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:223–227` worker uses `emptySubscriptionSource{}`, never replaced by the `SubscriptionCache` in the production wiring. Consequence: a subscription deleted via the API on one replica may continue to receive events on another replica for up to the refresh interval (the spec says "within a few hundred milliseconds (synchronous cache update + RPC propagation across replicas), regardless of the periodic-refresh interval", line 2756); during a Postgres outage, no telemetry surfaces that webhook delivery is silently off.

**Resolution:** All six parts now land. The `SubscriptionCache` is wired into the leader-only worker by `buildWebhookDelivery` (replacing `emptySubscriptionSource`), backed by an in-memory reveal-secret cache so deliveries are HMAC-signed. (2) `Service.OnChange` refreshes the local cache synchronously on every CRUD and fans out the `subscription_cache_invalidate` RPC to peers (`CacheInvalidateBroadcaster` over an `EndpointsPeerLister`, shared-HMAC-key-derived token, token-gated internal route exempt from the OIDC gate). (3) `WebhookSubscription.Generation` + the `GenerationChecker` seam skip a subscription whose generation advanced since the tick snapshot. (4) the default refresh is now 60 s. (5) `OnAvailabilityChange` emits `ops_health_status_changed` with `subscriptionsUnavailable:true` on a failed cold-start (and the clear on recovery). Closed by f676b44f.

### - [x] F-25.5.14 — The Redis-down / Gateway-down / Redis+Gateway-down degradation matrix is unimplemented. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2768–2780. (1) Redis-down: SSE/polling/webhook fall back to the gateway buffer with `degradation.actualSource: "gateway-buffer"`; (2) Gateway-down (Redis up): `lenny-ops` keeps reading the stream directly; (3) Postgres-down: subscription CRUD returns 503, delivery continues from cache, delivery tracking skipped; (4) Redis+Gateway dual outage: ops-originated events buffered in a per-replica `lenny-ops` ring buffer of 500 events; SSE streams ops-originated events with `:degradation {"actualSource":"lenny-ops-local-buffer","unavailableFields":["gateway-events"]}` comment line; polling/SSE for gateway-originated events return `503 EVENT_STREAM_UNAVAILABLE`; recovery flushes the local buffer with `eventKey` dedup.

Implementation: `grep -rn "lenny-ops-local-buffer\|gateway-buffer\|actualSource" /Users/joan/projects/lenny --include="*.go"` returns no matches. There is no `lenny-ops` per-replica ring buffer for ops-originated events — the only ring buffer is the gateway's in-process `EventBuffer` (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go`), used by the gateway, not by `lenny-ops`. There is no `degradation` envelope wrapper anywhere in `pkg/ops/`. There is no fallback-to-buffer logic anywhere because no Redis read is wired in the first place (F1). Consequence: the multi-failure-mode degradation contract §25.5 designs is unobservable; an agent during a Redis outage receives no event_stream traffic and no fallback at all.

**Resolution (commit 42def4bd):** The four-case matrix is now implemented in the lenny-ops read surface (`pkg/ops/events`), driven by an injected `SourceHealth` probe (`RedisAvailable`/`GatewayAvailable`). `streamState()` classifies the case and the poll/SSE handlers act on it: case 2 (Redis up) serves normally with no envelope; case 1 (Redis down, gateway up) attaches the canonical `degradation` envelope with `actualSource: "gateway-buffer"` (EVENT_STREAM_DEGRADED, HTTP 200 metadata) and writes the SSE `:degradation` comment; case 4 (Redis + gateway down) returns `503 EVENT_STREAM_UNAVAILABLE` on polling and writes the SSE `:degradation {"actualSource":"lenny-ops-local-buffer","unavailableFields":["gateway-events"]}` comment while still serving the replica's own ops-originated events from the `events.Service` local ring buffer (the `DefaultBufferCapacity`-bounded buffer that already existed). The stale "no lenny-ops ring buffer" premise was partly addressed — the `events.Service` buffer *is* the per-replica local buffer; it only lacked the degradation signaling, which this lands. `cmd/lenny-ops` wires a background `sourceHealthProbe` (Redis PING + gateway version GET on a 15s ticker), only when Redis backs the stream. The gateway-buffer data-plane fetch (lenny-ops pulling gateway-*originated* events from the gateway's `/v1/admin/events/buffer` during a Redis outage) remains a separate read-surface concern; this finding's gap was the unobservable degradation contract, which is now observable. The recovery-flush `eventKey` dedup rides on the existing buffer's id-keyed dedup. 10 tier-1 tests across the four cases (poll 503 / degraded-envelope / Redis-up-no-degradation / nil-health; SSE comments for case 1, case 4 incl. ops-event serving, and healthy; StaticSourceHealth).

### - [x] F-25.5.15 — Cron-driven delivery retention purge is absent. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2649–2664. The chart configures `ops.webhooks.deliveryRetentionDays` with tier defaults (1/7/30 days). A scheduled `DELETE` runs daily at 03:45 UTC (off-peak) using `expires_at` as the predicate, with `LIMIT 10000` per batch to avoid long locks. `deliveryTrackingMode: metric-only` and `failures-only` with `failuresOnlyRetentionDays` are additional knobs.

**Resolution:** `Store.DeleteExpired(before, limit)` lands on both `MemoryStore` and the Postgres store (a `ctid`-bounded batched `DELETE WHERE expires_at <= $1 ORDER BY expires_at LIMIT $2`). `deliveryRetentionJob` registers a leader-only `delivery-retention` cron at `45 3 * * *` that loops `DeleteExpired(now, 10000)` until a sweep deletes fewer than the batch. `expires_at` is stamped at record time from the retention policy (F-25.5.11). The chart exposes `ops.webhooks.deliveryTrackingMode` / `deliveryRetentionDays` / `failuresOnlyRetentionDays`, rendered as `--webhook-*` flags on lenny-ops, with the 1/7/30-day tier presets. Closed by f676b44f.

Implementation: `grep -rn "deliveryRetentionDays\|failuresOnlyRetentionDays\|03:45\|45 3 \* \* \*\|delivery_retention" /Users/joan/projects/lenny` returns no matches in the repo (only the spec). `pkg/ops/opsservice/webhookloop.go:121–127` honors `webhookdelivery.TrackingMode` (`full`/`failures-only`/`metric-only`) via `ShouldRecord` (`pkg/webhookdelivery/webhookdelivery.go:67–76`), so the modes are recognized in policy code; but the purge cron is not registered. `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:90–123` (`buildBackupService`) registers three cron jobs (`backup-full`, `backup-postgres`, `backup-retention`) but no `delivery-retention` job. Consequence: even if the `ops_event_deliveries` table existed (F6), the table would grow unbounded — §25.5 explicitly calls out "Webhook delivery rows can grow large at Tier 3: 100 events/min × 1000 subscriptions × 3 retry attempts = ~26M rows per 24 hours" (line 2651).

### - [x] F-25.5.16 — The `severity` extension attribute and structured filter set are absent from emitted events. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2554 (the CloudEvents `type` is `dev.lenny.<short_name>`; the canonical Lenny extensions include `lennytenantid`, `lennyoperationid`, `lennyrootsessionid`), 2693 (canonical filters include `?severity=`, `?resourceType=pool&resourceId=default-gvisor`, `?since=`), and the §16.6 catalog (each event has a documented severity).

Implementation: `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go:42–52` carries a `Severity string` field on `OperationalEvent` and `matchFilter` filters on it (lines 183–192), but the §25.5 envelope also requires `lennytenantid`, `lennyoperationid`, `lennyrootsessionid` as CloudEvents extension attributes and there is no field for them in `OperationalEvent`. The §12.3.7 `eventbus.Event` (`pkg/gateway/eventbus/cloudevents.go:80–115`) does carry these extensions, but the §25.5 surface uses `opsevents.OperationalEvent` (no extensions map) — the two type families do not share an envelope. `matchFilter` accepts `EventType` and `Severity` only; the §25.5 filters `?resourceType` and `?resourceId` are not implemented. The `?since` filter is implemented only as a numeric buffer cursor, not as the §25.5 timestamp filter. Consequence: agents cannot filter on resource scope (`?resourceType=pool&resourceId=default-gvisor`) and cannot correlate by operation or root session because those extensions are not emitted; the catalog severities (e.g., `alert_fired.severity=critical`) only flow when the gateway emitter explicitly sets the field, which is a caller-side convention.

**Resolution:** The extension-attribute half is stale: `OperationalEvent` now carries `Severity`, a `Subject` resource identifier, and an `Extensions` map that flattens `lennytenantid`/`lennyoperationid`/`lennyrootsessionid` onto the CloudEvents JSON object (`pkg/gateway/events/buffer.go`). The structured filter half is built: `EventFilter` gains `ResourceType`/`ResourceID` (matched against the `type/id` segments of `Subject`) and `Since`/`Until` (RFC 3339), and both the §25.5 SSE and polling handlers parse `?resourceType/?resourceId/?since/?until`. `ValidateFilterTokens` rejects an unknown event type or severity with `INVALID_EVENT_FILTER`. Closed by f359b02c.

Spec: lines 2574–2585. `pkg/ops/events/service.go` declares the `EventStreamService` interface with eight methods (`StreamEvents`, `ListEvents`, `CreateSubscription`, `ListSubscriptions`, `GetSubscription`, `UpdateSubscription`, `DeleteSubscription`, `ListDeliveries`).

### - [x] F-25.5.18 — The `application/ocsf+json` audit-bearing CloudEvents path does not flow through the ops stream. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: line 2556 ("When an operational event carries an audit record (e.g., `dev.lenny.audit_session_terminated`), `datacontenttype` is `application/ocsf+json` and the CloudEvents `data` field is the [OCSF v1.1.0] record defined in §11.7 Wire Format. Single-envelope model: CloudEvents is the transport, OCSF is the payload.").

The §12.3.7 `eventbus.Event` type does carry OCSF records over Redis pub/sub topics (`TopicDelegationTree`, `TopicSessionLifecycle`). But the §25.5 `opsevents.OperationalEvent` type (the one the §25.3 buffer holds) has a `DataContentType string` field (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go:48`) — no audit event is ever buffered as `application/ocsf+json`. `grep -rn "audit_session_terminated\|application/ocsf+json" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/gateway/opsevents /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/opsserver` returns no matches. **Resolution (commit 201ec692):** The §16.7 subset of audit events flagged for real-time operator visibility now flows onto the §25.5 stream as audit-bearing CloudEvents. `pkg/gateway/events` gained `ContentTypeOCSF`/`ContentTypeJSON` constants and `OperationalEvent.IsAuditBearing()`; `pkg/observability/audit.EscalatesToOperationalStream` registers the six §16.7 ops-stream-routed event types (`delegation.self_recursion_allowed`, `elicitation.content_tamper_detected`, `deployment.feature_flag_downgrade_acknowledged`, `audit.ocsf_retranslate_requested`, `audit.partition_drop_forced`, `eventbus.republish_requested`). `auditstore.Store.Append` now escalates a committed escalating row through an optional ops emitter (`WithOpsStreamEmitter`/`SetOpsStreamEmitter`), translating it via the same `ocsf.Translate`/`MarshalRecord` the SIEM forwarder uses and emitting a `dev.lenny.<event_type>` event carrying the OCSF record directly in `data` (single-envelope, no double-wrap). `cmd/lenny-gateway` wires the shared §25.5 ops emitter into the durable audit `Store` once Redis is resolved, so `Store.Append` (the universal choke point reached by the admin sink, the policy-rejection sink, and the §25.9 audit-maintenance API) carries the escalation. The "OperationalEvent would not carry the OCSF discriminator" half of the gap was already addressed by the `DataContentType`/`Data` fields; the missing piece was the writer→stream path, which this lands. The `deployment.feature_flag_downgrade_acknowledged` event is written by the chart render-time guard, not the gateway runtime, so it is registered for completeness but only emitted where the gateway is the writer. 9 tier-1 tests (events helper round-trip, escalation registry coverage, Store escalation matrix incl. best-effort emit-failure swallow).

Spec: line 2606 (`lenny_ops_events_stream_length` gauge for current Redis stream length).

Implementation: `pkg/ops/opsservice/selfchecks.go:69–105` (`RedisLagCheck`) supplies a "lag" function `lag func() int` to compute consumer lag in events for the §25.4 self-health check, but `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:236` wires it as `RedisLagCheck(redisClient, nil)` — the lag function is `nil` (so `behind = 0` always; the check is effectively a no-op except for Ping). Without an `XLEN` against `ops:events:stream` (or `XINFO STREAM`), the actual stream length cannot be reported. Consequence: the §25.4 redis_consumer_lag self-health check ignores stream depth; the §25.5 `lenny_ops_events_stream_length` gauge is unbacked.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed; the gauge's data source is the Redis `ops:events:stream` itself, which is unwired (F-25.5.1 High OPEN — neither producer nor consumer exists). Until a stream exists to `XLEN`, instrumenting an `XLEN` call would be metering an empty key. The gauge and the `RedisLagCheck` lag function land in the same wave as the stream wiring.

### - [x] F-25.5.20 — Audit events `ops_event.subscription_created`/`_updated`/`_deleted` are not emitted. (Medium) [Medium] — CLOSED

Spec: lines 2804–2806 and the secret-lifecycle audit list at line 2731 (`ops_event.subscription_secret_rotated` plus the three above).

Implementation: `grep -rn "ops_event\\.subscription_created\|ops_event\\.subscription_updated\|ops_event\\.subscription_deleted\|ops_event\\.subscription_secret_rotated" /Users/joan/projects/lenny` returns no matches. The CRUD handlers (`pkg/ops/opsserver/event_subscriptions.go:56–102`) never call into an audit writer; no `OCSF` record is built for the subscription operations; the `eventsubscription.Service` does not depend on an audit emitter. Consequence: subscription create/update/delete actions are unaudited; the operator cannot reconstruct who registered or removed a webhook callback. The first-8-char SHA-256 fingerprint that §25.5 says should accompany the created audit event (line 2733) has no carrier.

**Resolution:** `eventsubscription.AuditSink` + `Service.SetAuditSink` emit `ops_event.subscription_created`/`_updated`/`_deleted`/`_secret_rotated` on every CRUD/rotate op, carrying the secret fingerprint (never the secret). Deps-level mapping onto the §16.7 chain follows the logged-until-audit-store-client posture of drift/backup/escalation. Closed by f9936930.

### Summary

The §25.5 operational event stream surface is structurally absent in v1. The Redis `ops:events:stream` is neither written nor read; the SSE and polling endpoints are not registered; the cursor model with source-kind translation, the gateway-and-`lenny-ops` co-emission model, the secret hashing/rotation/fingerprinting lifecycle, the SSRF / DNS-rebinding protections on the webhook path, and the tenant-isolation enforcement do not exist. The CRUD surface lives but accepts plaintext secrets and stores them, lacks `PUT` and `/deliveries`, and uses non-canonical error codes. The `ops_event_subscriptions` schema is missing nearly every field that anchors §25.5's security and audit story (`secret_hash`, `secret_fingerprint`, `created_by`, `created_by_tenant_id`, `tenant_filter`, `generation`, `updated_at`, `active`), and `ops_event_deliveries` is not created at all. The webhook delivery worker has the correct retry/backoff policy and the correct HTTP headers, but it runs against an empty event source, an empty subscription source, and a nil delivery recorder in `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go`. None of the §25.5 metrics is registered. The four-case degradation matrix (Redis-down, Gateway-down, Redis+Gateway, Postgres-down) is uncoded. Of the 20 findings, 10 are High (correctness/security gaps that violate normative MUSTs), 8 are Medium (capability unimplemented), 2 are Low.
