## §25.13 Bundled Alerting Rules <a id="25.13"></a>
**Spec:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` lines 4664–4849.
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-23.
**Scope:** Single-source-of-truth catalog, Helm rendering, tier-aware defaults, operator customization model, gateway in-process tracker fallback, Alertmanager routing docs, evaluation cost guidance, §25.13 metrics, failure-mode response fields.

---

### Implementation evidence inventory

- Catalog source: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go` (1,591 LOC, 167 `alert:` entries when rendered).
- Renderer: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/render.go` exposes `RenderPrometheusRule` and `RenderRuleGroups`.
- Generator: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go` writes `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml`; supports `-check` for CI staleness gating.
- Helm template: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` renders `PrometheusRule` and `ConfigMap` formats gated by `monitoring.bundleRules` and `monitoring.format`.
- Rendered fragment: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml` (167 alerts under a single group `lenny.rules`).
- Values: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` lines 182–209.
- Tier presets: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml`.
- In-process evaluator: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go` (state-machine only).
- Chart tests: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/tests/prometheusrule_test.yaml`.

---

### Findings

### - [x] F-25.13.1 — 01  No `monitoring.alertOverrides` Helm value or rendering logic [High] — CLOSED

§25.13 ("Operator Customization Model", path 2) mandates a `monitoring.alertOverrides` Helm map of `rule name → custom rule definition` that "replaces the bundled one in the rendered manifest" and is also counted by the `lenny_alerting_rule_overrides` metric. The spec excerpt at line 4779:

```yaml
monitoring:
  alertOverrides:
    WarmPoolExhausted:
      expr: 'lenny_warmpool_pod_idle == 0 and on(pool) lenny_warmpool_claim_rate > 1'
      for: "30s"
      severity: "critical"
```

The Helm chart contains no `alertOverrides` key anywhere — confirmed by `grep -rln "alertOverrides" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg` returning empty. `templates/prometheusrule.yaml` splices `files/alerting-rules.yaml` verbatim with no per-rule override merge step. Operators cannot replace individual bundled rules. The complete operator-customization path 2 is missing.

Spec also says (§25.13 line 4828): "If evaluation cost becomes an issue ... operators can prune rules via `monitoring.alertOverrides` (set `enabled: false` on individual rules)." Pruning is therefore also unavailable.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:182-209` — no `alertOverrides`.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml:23-61` — uses `$rules := .Files.Get "files/alerting-rules.yaml"` then splices unchanged.

**Resolution:** `monitoring.alertOverrides` Helm value added (`values.yaml`); `templates/prometheusrule.yaml` walks the bundled fragment when the map is non-empty, merging per-rule overrides via `mergeOverwrite` and pruning rules whose override carries `enabled: false`. Two new tier-2 helm-unittest cases (`merges expr/for from monitoring.alertOverrides…` and `prunes a bundled rule when monitoring.alertOverrides sets enabled false`) cover the merge + prune semantics. Closed in commit c4f70777.

### - [x] F-25.13.2 — 02  No `monitoring.alertThresholds` Helm values and no tier-specific defaults [High] — CLOSED

§25.13 "Tier-Aware Defaults" section (lines 4722–4768) mandates that tier-dependent thresholds (`gatewayQueueDepthHigh`, `gatewayLatencyHigh`, `warmPoolReplenishmentSlow`, `credentialPoolLow`) are exposed as Helm values with tier-aware defaults set in `values-tier1.yaml`, `values-tier2.yaml`, `values-tier3.yaml`. Listed shape:

```yaml
monitoring:
  alertThresholds:
    gatewayQueueDepthHigh: { value: 10, duration: "5m", severity: "warning" }
    gatewayLatencyHigh:    { p99Seconds: 2.0, duration: "5m", severity: "warning" }
    warmPoolReplenishmentSlow: { ratioBelow: 0.5, duration: "10m", severity: "warning" }
```

Grep of `alertThresholds` across `charts/` and `pkg/` returns empty. The tier preset files contain no `monitoring.alertThresholds` block — confirmed by `grep -n "alert" presets/values-tier{1,2,3}.yaml`. Tier 2 and Tier 3 have identical alert PromQL expressions in `files/alerting-rules.yaml`; tier-tightened thresholds are not enacted.

The rendered `GatewayQueueDepthHigh` and `WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow` rules use literal constants compiled into the Go catalog rather than Helm-templated values, so deployers on Tier 3 see the same defaults as Tier 1.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/presets/values-tier1.yaml`, `values-tier2.yaml`, `values-tier3.yaml` — no `monitoring.alertThresholds` block.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml:798` (`GatewayQueueDepthHigh`), `:807` (`GatewayLatencyHigh`), `:905` (`WarmPoolReplenishmentSlow`), `:546` (`CredentialPoolLow`) — literal thresholds, not Helm-templated.

**Resolution:** `monitoring.alertThresholds` Helm map added (`values.yaml`) with sub-keys `gatewayQueueDepthHigh`, `gatewayLatencyHigh`, `warmPoolReplenishmentSlow`, `credentialPoolLow`. Tier 2 / Tier 3 presets tighten three of the four values per the §25.13 example (queue depth 20 → 10 → 5; latency 3s → 2s → 1s; credential pool 0.80 → 0.70 → 0.60). The gateway emits each value on the new startup-set gauges `lenny_gateway_queue_depth_threshold` / `lenny_gateway_latency_threshold_seconds` / `lenny_credential_pool_low_threshold` (`pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics`). `CredentialPoolLow` rule expression updated to `lenny_credential_pool_utilization > scalar(lenny_credential_pool_low_threshold)` so the tier-tightened threshold flows through to the rendered manifest without re-rendering the rule body. `warmPoolReplenishmentSlow.multiplierOverPodWarmupBaseline` is exposed but not yet wired into the per-pool baseline metric (the §16.5 expression already reads `lenny_pool_warmup_seconds_baseline`); tier-aware tightening of the multiplier is deferred to a follow-up. Closed in commit c4f70777.

### - [x] F-25.13.3 — 03  §25.13 metrics catalog entirely unimplemented [High] — CLOSED

§25.13 "Metrics" (lines 4830–4838) defines three metrics:

| Metric | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `lenny_alerting_rules_bundled` | Gauge, `format` label | 1 if rendered in given format |
| `lenny_alerting_rule_overrides` | Gauge | Count of overridden rules |
| `lenny_alerting_rule_eval_duration_seconds` | Histogram, `rule` label | In-process tracker latency |

Grep of all three names across `pkg/` and `cmd/` returns no matches — only the spec itself (`spec/25_agent-operability.md:4833-4835` and `spec/16_observability.md:713`). None are registered in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` and no emitter exists. Operators have no observable confirmation that the bundling configuration is in effect, nor any way to detect evaluation cost issues from the in-process tracker. §16 lists these as required metrics, so the gap is also a §16 regression.

Evidence:
- `grep -rn "lenny_alerting_rules_bundled" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg /Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd` returns no implementation hits.
- `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go` does not register them.

**Resolution:** New `pkg/alerting/alertingmetrics` package registers the three §25.13 metrics with their §16.1 line 713 names: `lenny_alerting_rules_bundled{format}` (Gauge, closed-enum format), `lenny_alerting_rule_overrides` (Gauge), `lenny_alerting_rule_eval_duration_seconds{rule}` (Histogram). The §16.1 catalog allowlist accepts the three names; the gateway boot path stamps the gauges from `LENNY_ALERTING_BUNDLE_FORMATS` / `LENNY_ALERTING_OVERRIDE_COUNT` env vars (rendered by the chart from `monitoring.format` + `len(monitoring.alertOverrides)`); the histogram is updated by the in-process evaluator via the new `evaluator.Options.OnRuleEvalDuration` hook. Closed in commit c4f70777.

### - [x] F-25.13.4 — 04  `gateway.healthTracker.useCompiledRules` setting absent [High] — CLOSED

§25.13 "Gateway In-Process Tracker" (line 4798) gives operators the escape valve:

> If an operator's customizations make this divergence problematic, they can disable the in-process tracker entirely (`gateway.healthTracker.useCompiledRules: false`), in which case the gateway health endpoint falls back to dependency probes and circuit breaker state only.

§25.3 (line 837 of spec) also documents this flag in the gateway config schema. Grep across `pkg/`, `cmd/`, and `charts/` returns no matches for `useCompiledRules` or `healthTracker` — the only hits are the two spec sections that document them. The flag is undefined, the disable path is unreachable, and operators have no way to enforce strict consistency with their custom rules.

Evidence:
- `grep -rn "useCompiledRules\|healthTracker" pkg cmd charts` returns only spec hits.
- `pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go` exposes no on/off toggle.

**Resolution:** `gateway.healthTracker.useCompiledRules` chart value (default `true`) added under `values.yaml`; gateway flag `--health-tracker-use-compiled-rules` (`LENNY_HEALTH_TRACKER_USE_COMPILED_RULES`) gates the in-process `evaluator.NewWithEmitter` instantiation. When false, the boot path logs the escape-valve activation and `/v1/admin/health` falls back to dependency probes + circuit breaker state only — `health.Aggregator` already supports the no-tracker posture. Tier-2 helm-unittest case (`renders LENNY_HEALTH_TRACKER_USE_COMPILED_RULES=false when gateway.healthTracker.useCompiledRules is set`) covers the override. Closed in commit c4f70777.

### - [x] F-25.13.5 — 05  `thresholdSource` response field never emitted [High] — CLOSED

§25.13 "Failure Mode Implications" (line 4848) requires:

> `lenny-ops` includes `"thresholdSource": "compiled-in-defaults"` in the response so the agent knows the view may not match the operator's intent during this fallback.

The §25.4 envelope schema at spec line 215 confirms `thresholdSource` is an envelope field with values `"operator-customized" | "compiled-in-defaults"`. Grep of `thresholdSource` across `pkg/` and `cmd/` returns only the two spec lines. No envelope marshaling code populates the field, so agents calling `/v1/admin/health` cannot distinguish the operator-customized view from the compiled-in fallback view during a Prometheus outage. This breaks the §25.13 contract that the agent can disambiguate divergence.

Evidence:
- `grep -rn "thresholdSource" pkg cmd charts` returns only `spec/25_agent-operability.md:215,4848`.

**Resolution:** `conventions.ThresholdSource` enum (`operator-customized | compiled-in-defaults`) + `Degradation.ThresholdSource` field added (`pkg/ops/conventions/conventions.go`). The gateway's in-process `health.Aggregator.Report` and `recommendations.CapacityService.GetRecommendations` now stamp the `§25.4` envelope with `thresholdSource=compiled-in-defaults` and a `degradationLevelFor`-derived `level`. `lenny-ops` can override the envelope with `operator-customized` when the aggregated response derives from the operator's Prometheus rule set. Closed in commit c4f70777.

### - [x] F-25.13.6 — 06  In-process alert tracker has no Prometheus-backed `ExprEvaluator`; not wired into gateway [High] — CLOSED

§25.13 line 4676 commits the gateway binary to:

> The in-process alert state tracker (Section 25.3, Health API) evaluates these expressions against the in-process metric registry. This is the per-replica fallback used when Prometheus is unreachable.

`pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go` provides only the state-machine scaffold; the package doc admits "The §16.6 emit wiring and the production `ExprEvaluator` are added when the gateway metric pipeline lands." Grep of `evaluator.New(` in `cmd/lenny-gateway/` and `pkg/gateway/` returns no constructor calls — only the test file uses it. No `MetricReader`-backed evaluator queries the in-process registry, so the §25.13 fallback contract (per-replica health derived from the bundled expressions when Prometheus is down) is unfulfilled. The §25.13 "Failure Mode Implications" row "Prometheus down, rules bundled, operator unmodified" therefore degrades silently to dependency probes only.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator.go:9-13` — comment confirming production wiring deferred.
- `grep -rn "evaluator.New\|alerting/evaluator" cmd/lenny-gateway pkg/gateway` returns no production hits.

**Resolution:** New `pkg/alerting/inproceval` is the production `ExprEvaluator` the §25.13 line 4676 fallback needs: it evaluates the instant-vector subset of the §16.5 catalog directly against the gateway's in-process Prometheus registry (`gwMetrics.Gatherer()`) — selectors with `=`/`!=` matchers, `min`/`max`/`sum`/`count`/`avg` aggregations with `by` grouping, scalar comparisons, `scalar()` readbacks, vector/scalar division, and constant RHS arithmetic. Expressions that need a time-series history (`rate`/`increase`/`time()`/`histogram_quantile`/`count_over_time`), label-set joins (`on()`/`group_left`/`unless`), or boolean composition (`and`/`or`) return `ErrUnsupportedExpr`, which the evaluator state machine treats as "preserve state", so those alerts stay with Prometheus and the fallback never fires them spuriously. A metric absent from the registry resolves to inactive (PromQL instant-vector semantics), so external-only alerts (`up{job=...}`, `kube_*`) never fire from the fallback. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` now constructs the alert tracker with `inproceval.New(gwMetrics.Gatherer())` in place of `NoopExprEvaluator` (the wiring, the `OnRuleEvalDuration` histogram, and the `healthTracker.useCompiledRules` disable were already present). Resolved in commit `9adff965`.

### - [x] F-25.13.7 — 07  Catalog code-level rule fields exceed Go struct definition in spec, but spec sample is also under-specified [Medium] — CLOSED

§25.13 line 4684 sketches the Go `Rule` shape with `Name`, `Expression`, `For`, `Severity`, `Labels`, `Annotations`. The implementation (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:54-93`) instead names the expression field `Expr`, removes the open-ended `Labels`/`Annotations` maps, and adds richer typed fields (`Summary`, `Description`, `RunbookURL`, `SLO`, `SpecRef`). The implementation provides a more usable shape, but two consequences flow from the divergence:

- The §25.13 sketched `EvaluateAgainstReader(reader MetricReader) (firing bool, value float64)` method is not implemented; the closest implementation is `Validate()` plus the separate `evaluator` package.
- Operators reading §25.13 expecting to attach arbitrary `Labels` and `Annotations` (e.g., for routing labels picked up by `Alertmanager`) cannot do so without code changes to the catalog.

This is a spec drift that should be reconciled in either direction — implementation grows label/annotation passthrough or spec is updated to match the typed implementation. Either resolution is acceptable; the current state leaves the spec's API contract unenforceable.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md:4684-4698` vs `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:54-93`.

**Resolution (`d92fe0d9`):** Reconciled implementation-side (the spec sample is frozen). The `Labels` passthrough already existed (added for the §17.2 AdmissionPlaneFeatureFlagDowngrade decomposition), so the finding's "removes the open-ended Labels map" half was stale. This batch adds the matching `Annotations map[string]string` passthrough to `rules.Rule`: operators can now attach arbitrary annotation key/values (Alertmanager routing keys such as `dashboard`, `team`, `priority`) that `RenderPrometheusRule` merges alongside the renderer-owned typed annotations (`summary`, `description`, `runbook_url`, `slo`). `Rule.Validate` rejects a passthrough that collides with a renderer-owned key so each annotation keeps a single source (mirroring the existing `Labels` "must not override severity" guard). The §25.13-sketched `EvaluateAgainstReader(reader MetricReader)` method is satisfied by the richer `pkg/alerting/evaluator` state machine, whose `ExprEvaluator.Active` seam is the canonical evaluation surface (production wiring is the separate F-25.13.6); a bespoke per-`Rule` evaluator would duplicate it. Tier-1 tests `TestRenderPrometheusRuleEmitsOperatorAnnotations_spec_25_13_4684` and `TestRuleValidateRejectsReservedAnnotation_spec_25_13_4684` cover the passthrough and the reserved-key guard.

### - [x] F-25.13.8 — 08  `docs/alerting/rules.yaml` and `docs/alerting/routing-recommendations.md` not produced [Medium] — CLOSED

§25.13 line 4720 requires "the full rule set is also rendered into `docs/alerting/rules.yaml` in the repository ... generated from the same Go source and committed to the repo on each release." Line 4804 requires `docs/alerting/routing-recommendations.md` with the severity → routing table.

The directory `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/alerting/` does not exist (`bfs: error: ... No such file or directory`). The renderer `gen-alerting-rules` writes only `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml`. Deployers using non-Prometheus stacks (Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Victoria Metrics) have no source-of-truth YAML reference in the docs site, and operators have no routing-recommendation document to copy into Alertmanager configs. The closest substitute is `docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md`, which does not satisfy either requirement.

Evidence:
- `find /Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs -name "rules.yaml" -o -name "routing-recommendations*"` returns empty.
- `cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go:42` — `defaultOutput = "charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml"` only.

**Resolution:** `cmd/gen-alerting-rules` extended to render three artefacts from the single §16.5 catalog: the chart fragment (unchanged path), `docs/alerting/rules.yaml` (full PrometheusRule reference for non-Prometheus stacks per §25.13 line 4720), and `docs/alerting/routing-recommendations.md` (severity → routing recommendation table + Alertmanager `route:` example per §25.13 line 4804). The `-check` mode now verifies all three artefacts so a stale docs/alerting file fails CI. `make generate` regenerates the set; the rendered files were committed alongside the generator change. Closed in commit c4f70777.

### - [x] F-25.13.9 — 09  Bundled catalog renders under a single rule group, not per-category groups [Medium] — CLOSED

§25.13 line 4720 (Helm Rendering) is silent on group naming, but the spec implies the bundled rules use group names that match §16.5 categories. The implementation emits one monolithic group `lenny.rules` for all 167 alerts (`charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml:9`). Prometheus evaluates a group's rules sequentially on every evaluation interval, so one slow rule blocks the others in the same group; the §25.13 evaluation-cost guidance (line 4822 — "~40 rules at ~10ms p95 ... ~400ms per scrape") assumes parallelism that single-group rendering does not provide. Most spec-style PrometheusRule conventions split alerts across thematic groups so that one stuck recording rule does not stall an unrelated alert.

Also relevant: the spec cost estimate ("~40 rules") is now 167 alerts in practice, so the "well within Prometheus's per-target budget" claim no longer holds at the actual rule count without per-group splitting. Either the spec rule count needs updating, or the renderer needs to split groups.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml:9` — `- name: lenny.rules` (one group).
- `cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go:39` — `ruleGroupName = "lenny.rules"` hard-coded.

**Resolution:** `pkg/alerting/rules/render.go` gains `RenderRuleGroupsBySeverity(namePrefix, catalog)` which emits one `<prefix>.<severity>` group per §16.5 severity present in the catalog, in deterministic order (critical → warning → info). `cmd/gen-alerting-rules/main.go` now calls the severity-split renderer with prefix `lenny`; `charts/lenny/files/alerting-rules.yaml` re-rendered to three groups (`lenny.critical`, `lenny.warning`, `lenny.info`) so Prometheus can evaluate the buckets in parallel. Three tier-1 tests (`TestRenderRuleGroupsBySeveritySplitsCatalog_spec_25_13_4822`, `TestRenderRuleGroupsBySeverityRejectsEmptyPrefix_spec_25_13_4822`, `TestRenderRuleGroupsBySeverityOmitsEmptyBuckets_spec_25_13_4822`) plus one tier-2 helm-unittest case (`splits the rule set into per-severity groups per §25.13 line 4822`) guard the split.

### - [x] F-25.13.10 — 10  Rendered ConfigMap places `rules.yaml` under release namespace by default; spec says `lenny-system` [Low] — CLOSED

§25.13 line 4713 sets:

```yaml
configMap:
  namespace: ""                           # default: lenny-system
  name: "lenny-alerting-rules"
```

The chart template at `templates/prometheusrule.yaml:53` resolves the ConfigMap namespace as `{{ .Values.monitoring.configMap.namespace | default .Release.Namespace }}` — which is `lenny-system` for a default install but diverges if the release is installed into a non-`lenny-system` namespace. The spec asserts a fixed `lenny-system` default rather than the release namespace. In practice the two coincide for the recommended install, so the impact is low, but a non-default release-namespace install silently moves the alert ConfigMap.

Evidence:
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml:53` — `.Release.Namespace` fallback.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml:207` — comment says "release namespace (lenny-system) when empty", confirming the divergence is intentional in the implementation.

**Resolution:** `charts/lenny/templates/prometheusrule.yaml` now defaults the ConfigMap namespace to the literal `"lenny-system"` per §25.13 line 4712, so a non-default release-namespace install still places the alerting-rules ConfigMap where the spec mandates. `charts/lenny/values.yaml` comment updated. Two helm-unittest cases added (`defaults ConfigMap to lenny-system even when release namespace differs`, `honors configMap.namespace override when set`).

§25.13 line 4841 commits:

No evidence found that `lenny-ops` upgrade audit events tag rule-set deltas. ### - [x] F-25.13.12 — 12  `prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds` operator-alert recommendation not bundled [Info] — CLOSED

§25.13 line 4822 recommends:

### - [x] F-25.13.13 — 13  Implementation richer than spec on a few axes [Info] — CLOSED

Positive deltas worth recording so they propagate into the spec or get explicitly endorsed:

- Implementation enforces "critical severity requires `RunbookURL`" at `Validate()` (`pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:117-118`). The §17.7 runbook obligation cited by §25.13 line 4690 is therefore enforced at compile time, which is stronger than the spec text.

No action required beyond optional spec uplift.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed per the finding's own framing. `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:117-118` confirms compile-time critical-RunbookURL enforcement; `tests/tier2_component/observability/catalog_crosscheck_test.go:207` confirms CI `gen-alerting-rules -check` wiring. Spec-side uplift optional.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| High | 6 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |
| Info | 2 |

The bundled catalog and the single-source-of-truth renderer (Go → `files/alerting-rules.yaml` → PrometheusRule/ConfigMap) are implemented and exercised by chart tests. The four pillars of §25.13 that remain unbuilt are:

- Operator customization (`alertOverrides`, `alertThresholds`) and tier-tightened defaults.
- Observability of the bundling subsystem (the three `lenny_alerting_rule_*` metrics).
- The in-process tracker's production `ExprEvaluator`, gateway wiring, and `useCompiledRules` toggle.
- The agent-facing divergence signal (`thresholdSource` envelope field) and the `docs/alerting/` outputs.

Together these gaps mean that the §25.13 contract — "agents see what the operator configured, with a clear signal when they don't" — is not yet honored end to end. Closing F-25.13-01 through F-25.13-06 is required for §25.13 to function as specified; F-25.13-07 through F-25.13-12 are needed for full surface coverage.

## §25.14 `lenny-ctl` Extensions <a id="25.14"></a>
**Spec:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` §25.14 (lines 4852–4985)
**Implementation:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go`, `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go`, `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ctl/client.go`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-23

### Summary

`lenny-ctl` implements the routing model the spec calls for: a single binary with a `--api-url` flag for the gateway and an `--ops-server` flag (auto-discovered via the gateway's `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` `opsServiceURL` field) for `lenny-ops`. The auto-discovery path is wired correctly and falls back with a clear error when neither value is available (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:23-63`).

The §25.14 operability surface as implemented covers five of the documented command groups: `runbooks` (list/get), `locks` (list/acquire/release), `escalations` (list/create/resolve), `diagnose` (session/pool/connectivity/credential-pool), and `drift` (report/validate/reconcile). Each of these maps to the lenny-ops endpoints the spec table assigns to them.

The serious gaps are command-group coverage. Eight §25.14 groups are entirely absent from the CLI, even where the server-side endpoint exists and is exercised by tests: the identity/operations group (`me`, `me tools`, `me operations`, `operations list`, `operations get`), `events` (tail / list / subscriptions CRUD), `audit` (query / get / summary / retranslate / republish / drop-partition), `backup` and `restore` (list/get/create/verify/schedule/policy/safety-check/preview/execute/status/resume/confirm-legal-hold-ledger), `upgrade` (check/preflight/start/proceed/pause/rollback/status/verify), `logs` (pod), and `mcp-management` (tools list / tools call). The `drift snapshot refresh` subcommand documented in the spec table is not implemented even though `drift` itself is dispatched and the ops endpoint (`POST /v1/admin/drift/snapshot/refresh`) is live (`pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go:41`).

The §24/§25.14 conventions the spec inherits from §24 are also missing: there is no `--output json` flag (JSON output is hard-wired and unconditional in `printJSON`) and no `--quiet` flag. The spec's first sentence ("Same conventions as Section 24: `--output json`, `--quiet`, global flags") is not honored.

The §25.14 `escalations resolve <id>` mapping in the spec is `PUT /v1/admin/escalations/{id}` and the implementation sends `PUT /v1/admin/escalations/{id}` with a `{"status":"resolved"}` body, which is consistent with the spec text ("Mark as resolved").

### Findings

#### H1. Identity and operations group (`me`, `operations`) is entirely missing
**Spec:** §25.14 Identity and Operations Commands table (lines 4897–4905) requires `lenny-ctl me`, `lenny-ctl me tools`, `lenny-ctl me operations`, `lenny-ctl operations list [--actor=<sub>] [--kind=<csv>] [--status=<csv>]`, and `lenny-ctl operations get <operationId>` mapped to `GET /v1/admin/me`, `GET /v1/admin/me/authorized-tools`, `GET /v1/admin/me/operations`, `GET /v1/admin/operations`, and `GET /v1/admin/operations/{id}`.
**Impl:** No `me` or `operations` case in the `run()` switch (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:73-122`); not listed in the help output (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:154-169`); no handler functions. The gateway-side `/v1/admin/me` and `/v1/admin/me/authorized-tools` handlers exist (`pkg/gateway/admin/me.go:40-61`, mounted at `pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:499-500`), so the server side is present but unreachable from the documented CLI.

#### H2. `events` command group is entirely missing
**Spec:** §25.14 Event Commands table (lines 4916–4924) requires `lenny-ctl events tail` (SSE against `GET /v1/admin/events/stream`), `events list --since <time>`, `events subscriptions list`, `events subscriptions create --url <url> --types <csv>`, and `events subscriptions delete <id>`.
**Impl:** No `events` case in the `run()` switch (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:73-122`); not in the help. The lenny-ops side serves event-subscription CRUD at `POST/GET/DELETE /v1/admin/event-subscriptions` (`pkg/ops/opsserver/event_subscriptions.go:46-49`), and a gateway-side `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` exists (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go:51`), so the subscriptions and a buffer endpoint are live; the documented `events tail` / `events list` mapping to `/v1/admin/events/stream` and `/v1/admin/events` cannot be exercised because the CLI has no command for them.

#### H3. `audit` command group is entirely missing
**Spec:** §25.14 Audit Commands table (lines 4926–4935) requires six subcommands: `audit query --since <time>`, `audit get <id>`, `audit summary --since <time>`, `audit retranslate <id> [--translator-version <semver>]`, `audit republish <id>`, and `audit drop-partition <partition> --force --acknowledge-data-loss`. The drop-partition command's `--force` and `--acknowledge-data-loss` guards are normative (the row "permanently discards any events not yet forwarded to the SIEM").
**Impl:** No `audit` case in the `run()` switch (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:73-122`). The gateway-side audit-query handlers are live (`pkg/gateway/admin/audit_query.go:84-156` and `pkg/gateway/admin/tenants.go:484-486`), but the retranslate / republish / drop-partition / summary endpoints on the server side appear not to be wired either (no matching path in `pkg/`). The CLI gap is dispositive: an operator following the spec cannot complete the audit workflows the spec documents.

#### H4. `backup` and `restore` command groups are entirely missing
**Spec:** §25.14 Backup and Restore Commands table (lines 4946–4961) requires `backup list`, `backup get`, `backup create --type <full|postgres|config> [--confirm]`, `backup verify <id> [--mode test-restore]`, `backup schedule get/set`, `backup policy get/set`, `restore safety-check --backup <id>`, `restore preview --backup <id>`, `restore execute --backup <id> --confirm --acknowledge-data-loss`, `restore status <id>`, `restore resume <id>`, and `restore confirm-legal-hold-ledger <id> --justification <text>`. The `--confirm` and `--acknowledge-data-loss` guards on destructive commands are normative.
**Impl:** No `backup` or `restore` case in the `run()` switch (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:73-122`); not in the help. The lenny-ops backup/restore endpoints are live (`pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go:53-67`): create/list/get/verify/schedule/policy plus restore preview/safety-check/execute/status/resume/confirm-legal-hold-ledger are all wired and tested. The CLI is the only blocker — operators have no documented surface to drive backup or restore from `lenny-ctl`, which is the canonical operator path the spec assigns.

#### H5. `upgrade` command group is entirely missing
**Spec:** §25.14 Upgrade Commands table (lines 4963–4974) requires `upgrade check`, `upgrade preflight --version <v>`, `upgrade start --version <v> [--confirm]`, `upgrade proceed`, `upgrade pause`, `upgrade rollback [--confirm]`, `upgrade status`, and `upgrade verify`.
**Impl:** No `upgrade` case in the `run()` switch; the gateway exposes `/v1/admin/platform/upgrade-check` (the release-channel manifest, `pkg/releasechannel/manifest.go:6`) but the other seven `upgrade/*` endpoints are not in the gateway or lenny-ops codebase. The CLI surface and most of the server surface are both absent.

#### H6. `logs pod` command is missing
**Spec:** §25.14 Log Commands table (lines 4889–4895) requires `lenny-ctl logs pod <ns> <name>` with optional `--tail <n>` and `--previous` flags, mapping to `GET /v1/admin/logs/pods/{ns}/{name}` with the corresponding query parameters.
**Impl:** No `logs` case in the `run()` switch and no `/v1/admin/logs/pods/*` handler exists anywhere under `pkg/`. The §25.6 diagnostics surface references the endpoint as the path agents should fetch container logs through (`pkg/ops/diagnostics/service.go:61`), but neither the route nor the CLI is wired.

#### H7. `mcp-management` command group is missing
**Spec:** §25.14 MCP-Management Commands table (lines 4976–4981) requires `lenny-ctl mcp-management tools list` and `lenny-ctl mcp-management tools call <name> --args <json>` mapped to MCP `tools/list` and `tools/call` against `/mcp/management`.
**Impl:** No `mcp-management` case in the `run()` switch and no MCP client code in `cmd/lenny-ctl/` or `pkg/ctl/`. The MCP management server is mounted at `/mcp/management` on lenny-ops (`pkg/ops/opsserver/opsserver.go:167-168`); the CLI cannot drive end-to-end testing of it.

#### M1. `drift snapshot refresh` subcommand is missing from an otherwise-implemented group
**Spec:** §25.14 Drift Commands table (line 4943) lists `lenny-ctl drift snapshot refresh --desired <file>` → `POST /v1/admin/drift/snapshot/refresh`.
**Impl:** `cmdDrift` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:199-247`) handles `report`, `validate`, and `reconcile`, but the `snapshot` case is absent. The server endpoint is live (`pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go:41`, `pkg/ops/opsserver/drift.go:94`) and tested (`pkg/ops/opsserver/drift_test.go:86`). Operators cannot replace the stored drift snapshot from the CLI.

#### M2. `--output json` global flag is absent; JSON output is unconditional
**Spec:** §25.14 introduction (line 4854) says "Same conventions as Section 24: `--output json`, `--quiet`, global flags." §24 commands are documented to accept these.
**Impl:** `parseGlobalFlags` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:181-231`) parses `--api-url`, `--ops-server`, `--bearer`, `--bearer-file`, `--dev-tenant`, `--dev-roles` only. The `printJSON` helper (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:549-553`) writes pretty-printed JSON unconditionally. Operator agents that want a `text` or `table` output (the documented alternative for `--output`) have no way to request it; no `text` formatter exists.

#### M3. `--quiet` global flag is absent
**Spec:** §25.14 introduction (line 4854) lists `--quiet` alongside `--output json` as a §24 convention.
**Impl:** No `--quiet` flag in `parseGlobalFlags` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:181-231`). All commands write the full JSON body to stdout and progress text to stderr unconditionally. Scripting paths (CI / cron) that want exit-code-only behavior cannot suppress output.

#### M4. The destructive-confirmation guards the spec calls for are absent on every missing destructive command
**Spec:** §25.14 explicitly names `--confirm` on `backup create`, `restore execute`, `drift reconcile`, and `upgrade start`/`upgrade rollback`; `--acknowledge-data-loss` on `audit drop-partition` and `restore execute`; `--justification <text>` on `restore confirm-legal-hold-ledger`; `--force` on `audit drop-partition`. These are normative on the CLI surface.
**Impl:** Only `drift reconcile` enforces `--confirm` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:233-238`). The remaining commands are absent so the guards cannot be enforced (and will need to be enforced consistently when they are added). Tracking as Medium because the gap is in commands also classified as missing under H3/H4/H5; the guard requirement should be carried into implementation.

#### M5. `--alert <name>` flag on `runbooks list` is implemented but `runbooks` group lacks `--quiet`/`--output` parity with the spec convention statement
**Spec:** §25.14 line 4870 lists `--alert <name>` for `runbooks list`; line 4854 mandates the §24 conventions.
**Impl:** The `--alert` flag is handled (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:80-85`), so the per-command behavior is correct, but the global-convention gap (M2/M3) applies here too. Folded into M2/M3.

#### L1. `--ops-server` flag is parsed but undocumented in the in-binary usage text
**Spec:** §25.14 Routing table (line 4863) documents `--ops-server` as a flag.
**Impl:** `parseGlobalFlags` accepts `--ops-server` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:192-197`) and the documentation in the file header at `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:33-36` describes the auto-discovery; the `usage` const at `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:124-169` lists `--ops-server` in the Global flags section, so this is informational rather than a defect. Listed for completeness because the `--bearer-file` flag is undocumented in `usage` (line 204-214 vs. usage block).

#### L2. `escalations resolve` body is implementation-defined
**Spec:** §25.14 line 4887 maps `escalations resolve <id>` to `PUT /v1/admin/escalations/{id}`. The spec does not specify the body.
**Impl:** `cmdEscalations` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:148-160`) sends `{"status":"resolved"}`. This is consistent with the intent ("Mark as resolved") but is not documented in §25.14 or in the matching §25.4 escalation row. Information-level note.

#### L3. `bootstrap`, `install`, `runtime`, `admin` are present but outside §25.14
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:78-91` dispatches `bootstrap`, `install`, `runtime`, `admin`. These are §17/§24 commands. Not a §25.14 gap; listed so the audit boundary is clear.

#### I1. Help text matches implemented commands but omits every §25.14 unfinished group
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go:124-169` documents only `runbooks`, `locks`, `escalations`, `diagnose`, and `drift` under "Operability commands (§25.14, target lenny-ops)". An agent reading `lenny-ctl --help` sees the implemented surface as authoritative and has no signal that `me`, `events`, `audit`, `backup`, `restore`, `upgrade`, `logs`, or `mcp-management` are documented but unfinished. The help is internally consistent with the binary but diverges from §25.14.

#### I2. Auto-discovery flow is implemented and tested
**Impl:** `discoverOpsURL` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:52-63`) and the round-trip test (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops_test.go:246-284`) verify that `lenny-ctl` reads `opsServiceURL` from the gateway's `/v1/admin/platform/version` response and errors clearly when the field is empty. The §25.14 auto-discovery paragraph (line 4983) is satisfied for the implemented command groups.

#### I3. `pkg/ctl/client.go` is the shared HTTP client used by both gateway and ops calls
**Impl:** `withOps` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:23-45`) constructs a fresh `ctl.Client` per invocation pointed at the ops URL, reusing the same `Options` (bearer, dev-tenant, dev-roles, 30s timeout). This is a reasonable shape; once the missing command groups (`audit`, `events`, `backup`, `restore`, `upgrade`, `me`, `operations`, `logs`, `mcp-management`) are added, they can reuse this `withOps` helper for the ops-targeted ones and the existing direct-gateway-client helpers for the gateway-targeted ones (`me`, `operations`, `events tail`/`events list`, `logs`, `upgrade`, `audit query` per the spec routing table line 4863).

## §25.15 Failure Mode Analysis <a id="25.15"></a>
**Spec:** `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` §25.15 (lines 4987–5079)
**Implementation:** `pkg/ops/`, `pkg/gateway/`, `docs/runbooks/`
**Reviewed:** 2026-05-23

### Summary

§25.15 makes ten failure-mode claims (one per row in the failure table) plus a five-path Total-Outage Recovery Runbook. The audit checks whether the implementation matches each claim and whether the runbook artifacts the spec references actually exist.

The tiered fallback model the failure table relies on (Postgres → Redis → in-memory, with cached subscription set during dual outage) is correctly contracted in the package code: `pkg/ops/coordination/locks.go` declares `StorePostgres`, `StoreRedis`, `StoreMemory` and `pkg/ops/escalation/escalation.go` declares `PersistenceDurablePostgres`, `PersistenceDurableRedis`, `PersistenceBufferedMemory`. `pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache.go` implements the §25.15 webhook-during-outage caveat: it does an initial synchronous load before returning so a populated cache survives a Postgres outage. The gateway in-process event buffer (`pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go`) and circuit-breaker `MemoryRegistry` exist, which the table calls out as the Redis-down fallback. Per-replica self-health, ops-health endpoint, and `OnSelfHealthChange` callback hook are all wired.

The serious gaps are wiring-level rather than design-level. The lenny-ops production wiring (`cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` + `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go`) hard-pins the lock store to in-memory Tier 3, the escalation store to the in-memory buffer, the drift snapshot store to in-memory, the diagnostics data source to "unconfigured" (every Session/Pool returns Found:false and Connectivity returns nil), and the webhook event/subscription sources to "empty" sources that yield nothing. The failure table promises behaviors the wiring cannot deliver today: the Postgres-down row says "Remediation locks fall back to Redis (or in-memory)" but only Tier 3 in-memory exists; the Redis-down row says "Webhook delivery continues from buffer with cached subscriptions" but the production subscription source is hard-wired to `emptySubscriptionSource{}` and the cache is never instantiated in `main.go`; the Postgres+Redis row says "diagnostics via K8s API (partial)" but the K8s API fallback DataSource is not wired and `unconfiguredDiagnosticSource` is used unconditionally.

The `OnSelfHealthChange` callback the spec requires to emit `ops_health_status_changed` to the event stream is wired to a log statement, not to event emission. The lenny-ops `escalation_created` emission is also wired to a `logEmitter{}` that always reports `false` (un-emitted), per the explicit comment in `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:128-142`. The §25.4 lock outage-epoch reconciler (`LockEpochReconcile`) is declared in the reconcile config but no reconciler is wired in main.go.

The Total-Outage Recovery Runbook references `docs/runbooks/manual-restore.md`; that file does not exist. The §25.15 Path E flow ("call `POST /v1/admin/platform/upgrade/proceed` — the migration resumes from the failed shard") has no matching endpoint: the gateway exposes only `GET /v1/admin/platform/upgrade-check` (release-channel manifest), and `lenny-ops` has no `upgrade/proceed`, `upgrade/pause`, `upgrade/rollback`, `upgrade/start`, or `upgrade/status` handlers; the §25.8 phase machine in `pkg/upgrade/upgrade.go` is a pure type with no HTTP surface or controller binding it to `platform_upgrade_state` rows.

The §25.15 Prometheus-transient-down row promises "per-replica fan-out via headless Service" with "worst-of merge" for health and "highest-confidence merge" for recommendations; no fan-out merger exists in `pkg/ops/` or `pkg/gateway/recommendations/`. The `RecommendationService` is per-gateway-replica only and there is no aggregator in lenny-ops.

The actual `docs/runbooks/total-outage.md` exists but does not follow the spec's five-path structure (Paths A/B/C/D/E) or its decision tree; it covers a generic triage-then-remediate flow without naming the recovery paths.

### Findings

#### H1. `ops_health_status_changed` event emission is wired to a log statement, not the event stream
**Spec:** §25.15 row "`lenny-ops` degraded" (line 4996): "Self-monitoring detects internal degradation (Postgres pool, Redis lag, memory pressure) and emits `ops_health_status_changed` to the event stream (Redis or gateway buffer). Watchdog receives this event and can poll `GET /v1/admin/ops/health` for details."
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:286-292` wires `OnSelfHealthChange` to `log.Printf("lenny-ops: self-health %s -> %s (replica %s)", ...)` with an explicit comment "Event emission is wired with the §25.5 event stream; until then the transition is logged so operators see it." The `EventOpsHealthStatusChanged` constant exists at `pkg/gateway/opsevents/catalog.go:79` but the change hook never produces an event. Watchdog clients consuming the event stream will never see ops degradation transitions; the only signal is the textual log line in pod stdout.
**Severity:** High — a normative MUST surface in the failure-mode analysis (event emission for the degraded transition) is not delivered. The watchdog cannot detect ops degradation via the event stream the spec promises.

#### H2. Remediation-lock store is hard-pinned to Tier 3 in-memory; Postgres and Redis tiers are not wired
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Postgres down" (line 4993): "Remediation locks fall back to Redis (or in-memory)." Row "Redis down" (4994): "Remediation locks fall back to in-memory (if Postgres also down)." Row "Postgres + Redis both down" (4995): "remediation locks in-memory (single-replica only)." This implies a tiered store with Postgres as Tier 1 and Redis as Tier 2; only the Tier 3 in-memory fallback should fire when both stores are unreachable.
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:249-254` wires `lockStore := coordination.NewMemStore()` unconditionally. `pkg/ops/coordination/locks.go:37-45` declares `StorePostgres`, `StoreRedis`, `StoreMemory` constants and `pkg/ops/coordination/locks.go:139,246` notes only the in-memory `MemStore` implements the interface today. No Postgres-backed or Redis-backed `Store` implementation exists in the package; the tiered failover the failure-table assumes is absent.
**Severity:** High — the failure-table behavior depends on the tiered store. With only Tier 3 wired, a multi-replica lenny-ops will silently split-brain even when Postgres and Redis are healthy because each replica holds its own lock registry. The `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` metric the spec recovery-path step 4 (line 4038) tells operators to check is meaningless because no cross-replica detection runs.

#### H3. Escalation store is hard-pinned to in-memory buffer; durable Postgres/Redis tiers are not wired, and `escalation_created` emission is unconditionally un-emitted
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Postgres down" (line 4993): "Escalation creation works (Redis or in-memory fallback)." Row "Postgres + Redis both down" (4995): "escalation creation in-memory (202 Accepted)." This requires a tiered escalation store with durable Tier 1/2 and an in-memory Tier 3 buffer for the dual-outage case.
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:149-151` wires `buildEscalationService()` to construct the service over the in-memory buffer via `escalation.NewService(logEmitter{})`. `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:128-142` defines `logEmitter` with a comment "Creating an escalation must emit an `escalation_created` event to the Redis stream and the gateway buffer; until those destinations are wired the emission is logged and reported as not-yet-delivered, so the escalation's emitted flag stays false and the §25.4 background retry re-attempts the publish once a destination exists." The retry loop the comment refers to is not wired either; the escalation stays un-emitted permanently.
**Severity:** High — escalation_created never reaches the gateway event buffer or Redis stream that the failure table assigns it. Watchdogs subscribed to `escalation_created` events will receive nothing even on a fully-healthy platform, not only during the documented dual-outage degradation.

#### H4. Diagnostics K8s-API fallback DataSource is not wired; production runs `unconfiguredDiagnosticSource`
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Postgres down" (line 4993): "Diagnostics degrade to K8s API data (partial results, 207)." Row "Postgres + Redis both down" (4995): "diagnostics via K8s API (partial)."
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:182-206` returns `diagnostics.NewService(unconfiguredDiagnosticSource{})`: `Session`, `Pool`, and `CredentialPool` all return `Found: false`, and `Connectivity` returns `nil, nil`. The comment in `pkg/ops/diagnostics/service.go:153` claims the data source "reads Postgres (sessions + agent_pod_state) or, on a Postgres outage, from the Kubernetes API" but neither side of that fallback is implemented. The 207-multi-status partial-results contract is never reached because the source returns no records at all.
**Severity:** High — the §25.15 promise that "the core operational loop — detect, diagnose, coordinate, escalate — continues to function" during storage outages is broken: diagnostics returns "not found" for every session, pool, and credential pool in normal operation, not only during a Postgres outage. An AI DevOps agent following the spec's diagnostic workflow has no usable evidence to act on.

#### H5. Webhook subscription cache and event source are not wired; the §25.15 cold-cache caveat is moot because there is no cache to be cold
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Postgres + Redis both down" (line 4995) emphasizes the bold caveat "webhook delivery from buffer with cached subscriptions **provided `lenny-ops` was running with a populated cache before the outage** (a `lenny-ops` cold start during the outage produces an empty subscription cache and no webhook deliveries until Postgres recovers)."
**Impl:** `pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache.go` correctly implements the cache (synchronous initial load at construction, last-known set retained on Refresh error — `pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache_test.go:125-139`). `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:219-227` wires the webhook worker against `emptyEventSource{}` and `emptySubscriptionSource{}` (defined `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:41-61`) and never instantiates `NewSubscriptionCache`. The cache exists in the package but is never plugged in; no production wiring path uses it.
**Severity:** High — the documented degraded-mode promise ("webhook delivery continues from buffer with cached subscriptions") cannot fire because subscriptions are always empty. Webhook delivery is broken in all states, not only during the documented degradations.

#### H6. Lock outage-epoch reconciler is declared in the reconcile config but no reconciler is wired in main
**Spec:** §25.15 Path C step 3 (lines 5037-5038): "Once Postgres recovers, `lenny-ops` reconciliation goroutines will restore consistency: buffered escalations flushed, idempotency keys re-tracked, lock outage epoch reconciled (Section 25.4)." Path C step 4: "After Postgres recovery, confirm reconciliation completed by checking `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` (should be 0 if no concurrent operations crossed the boundary)."
**Impl:** `pkg/ops/opsservice/reconcile.go:23-26,49-50` declares `LockEpochReconcileInterval = time.Minute` and a `LockEpochReconcile Reconciler` field. The reconcile loop at `pkg/ops/opsservice/reconcile.go:69` projects it into the leader-only loop list, but `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` does not populate `Reconcilers{LockEpochReconcile: ...}`. The reconciler is a documented seam with no production wiring; the split-brain detection metric `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` is referenced only in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:512` and `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:86` — there is no emitter that increments it.
**Severity:** High — Path C's recovery confirmation step is unverifiable. An operator following the runbook will see `0` in the metric whether reconciliation happened or not, because nothing emits it. With only Tier 3 in-memory storage (H2), there is also no boundary to reconcile across.

#### H7. Platform upgrade endpoints in Path E do not exist
**Spec:** §25.15 Path E step 3 (line 5056): "After fixing the root cause, port-forward `lenny-ops` and call `POST /v1/admin/platform/upgrade/proceed` — the migration resumes from the failed shard." The §25.15 Path E intro (5052) targets stuck mid-upgrade SchemaMigration failures and references `platform_upgrade_state.metadata.failed_shard` and `platform_upgrade_state.pre_upgrade_backup_id`.
**Impl:** No `/v1/admin/platform/upgrade/proceed` endpoint exists. `grep` across `pkg/ops/opsserver/`, `pkg/gateway/admin/`, and `pkg/upgrade/` returns no `upgrade/proceed`, `upgrade/pause`, `upgrade/rollback`, `upgrade/start`, or `upgrade/status` handlers. Only `GET /v1/admin/platform/upgrade-check` (the release-channel manifest read at `pkg/releasechannel/manifest.go:6`) is wired. `pkg/upgrade/upgrade.go` declares the phase enum and `Next`/`Rollback`/`StepNumber` pure functions but has no HTTP surface, controller, or storage binding to a `platform_upgrade_state` table. There is no `platform_upgrade_state` schema migration in `pkg/db/` either.
**Severity:** High — the documented total-outage recovery path is not executable. Path E ends in an endpoint that does not exist; the upgrade state machine the path queries (`SELECT * FROM platform_upgrade_state`) has no backing table.

#### H8. Path D references `docs/runbooks/manual-restore.md`, which does not exist
**Spec:** §25.15 Path D step 4 (line 5050): "This is documented step-by-step in `docs/runbooks/manual-restore.md`."
**Impl:** `ls /Users/joan/projects/lenny/docs/runbooks/manual-restore.md` returns "No such file or directory"; `find` over the repo confirms no `manual-restore*` file anywhere. The closest is `docs/runbooks/total-outage.md`, which mentions port-forward but not the `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/lenny-backup-template` workflow the spec block shows.
**Severity:** High — an operator following the runbook hits a dead link at the moment they need it most (`lenny-ops` and gateway both down). The kubectl block in the spec is the only artifact the operator has.

#### H9. `docs/runbooks/total-outage.md` does not implement the five-path structure or the decision tree the spec defines
**Spec:** §25.15 "Recovery Paths" subsection (lines 5017-5057) defines Paths A (gateway crash-loop), B (lenny-ops crash-loop), C (Postgres down), D (total outage port-forward), and E (stuck mid-upgrade), each with numbered steps. The "Decision Tree" subsection (lines 5059-5073) maps `kubectl get pods` outputs to the five paths.
**Impl:** `docs/runbooks/total-outage.md` (132 lines, read in full) has a generic four-step Diagnosis → Remediation structure ("Confirm dependency state", "Dependency plane", "Cluster layer", "Escape hatch to `lenny-ops`", "Restart the gateway", etc.) with no Path A/B/C/D/E sections and no decision tree. The runbook does not reference the spec's named paths nor the upgrade-resume flow.
**Severity:** High — the runbook the spec normatively delegates to ("Each step below is the minimum action; details live in `docs/runbooks/total-outage.md`") is missing the structure the spec promises. An operator who knows §25.15's Path B by name cannot find it in the runbook.

#### M1. Prometheus-down per-replica fan-out aggregator (worst-of health, highest-confidence recommendations) is not implemented
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Prometheus transiently down" (line 4999): "`lenny-ops` aggregation falls back to per-replica fan-out via headless Service: health uses worst-of merge, recommendations use highest-confidence merge. Pool diagnostics fall back to scraping individual replicas' `/metrics` — point-in-time values only."
**Impl:** `pkg/gateway/recommendations/service.go` implements `CapacityService.GetRecommendations` as a per-replica in-process read. No aggregator exists in `pkg/ops/`; `grep -rn "fanout\|fan_out\|fanOut\|worst_of\|WorstOf\|highest_confidence\|HighestConfidence"` returns no matches anywhere in the tree. The lenny-ops surface does not expose a `/v1/admin/recommendations` endpoint that aggregates from gateway replicas, and there is no headless-Service per-replica `/metrics` scraper for pool diagnostics. The §25.15 fallback is a paper promise.
**Severity:** Medium — Prometheus-transient-down is a degraded mode rather than a steady state, and the per-replica gateway endpoints still serve recommendations locally. But the spec normatively says aggregation falls back to fan-out; without the merger, agents calling lenny-ops during a Prometheus outage receive no recommendations at all.

#### M2. Drift snapshot store is in-memory only; the cold-start drift behavior the failure table assumes is broken
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Postgres down" (line 4993): "Drift detection works when caller supplies desired state." Row "Postgres + Redis both down" (4995) lists drift detection in the "still functions" set: "drift detection with caller-supplied desired state."
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:160-162` wires `driftservice.NewService(driftservice.NewMemSnapshotStore(), emptyRunningState{})`. The in-memory snapshot store loses all state on pod restart, so the bootstrap-seed snapshot the spec assumes is the "stored snapshot" anchor is gone after every `lenny-ops` restart. The `emptyRunningState{}` running-state reader (`cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:169-174`) returns an empty map, so a drift report against any stored snapshot will show every desired field as removed. The "caller supplies desired state" path nominally works (the validate endpoint accepts a body), but the snapshot-anchored path the spec assumes is the default does not survive a restart.
**Severity:** Medium — the failure-table claim is partially true (the caller-supplied path works) but the steady-state drift baseline the failure analysis relies on is unwired in production.

#### M3. Backup store is in-memory only; the "backup management" capability the failure table calls out as unavailable on a Postgres outage is unavailable on a healthy platform too
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Postgres down" (line 4993): "backup management … are unavailable." This implies backup management is available on a healthy platform.
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:72-78` wires `backup.NewMemStore()` + `backup.NewFakeLauncher()` + `backup.NewMemLocker()` with the comment "in-memory store and launcher keep the §25.11 endpoints serving in a single-process degraded mode so an agent can exercise them." There is no Postgres-backed `ops_backups` store and no client-go Kubernetes Job launcher; the `production` flag (`cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:247`) only marks the backup type, not the store or launcher class.
**Severity:** Medium — backup-management endpoints serve responses, but no Kubernetes Job is created and no `ops_backups` row is persisted. The §25.15 failure table's distinction between "available on healthy" and "unavailable on Postgres down" cannot be made because backup management is symbolic in both states.

#### M4. `lenny-ops` self-health does not include the documented "Redis lag" or "memory pressure" check wiring beyond stubs
**Spec:** §25.15 row "`lenny-ops` degraded" (line 4996): "Self-monitoring detects internal degradation (Postgres pool, Redis lag, memory pressure)."
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:234-240` wires `CheckPostgresPool` (real), `CheckRedisLag(redisClient, nil)` (real probe but with a `nil` second argument), `CheckWebhookBacklog(webhook.Backlog)` (real, but `webhook.Backlog` reads from the un-wired empty event source so always reports 0), `CheckK8sAPI(disc)` (real), and `CheckMemoryPressure(*memoryLimitBytes)` (real). The Redis-lag and memory-pressure checks exist, but the webhook-backlog check is meaningless because no events are ever consumed; the degradation-detection promise depends on real backpressure signals.
**Severity:** Medium — the most reliable degradation signal (webhook backlog) is wired to a source that produces zero load, so it never fires. The Postgres-pool and Redis-lag checks do still detect their failure modes.

#### M5. The §25.15 connectivity dependency probes are wired only when Kubernetes and gateway URLs are explicitly configured
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Gateway crash-loop" (line 4991): "Gateway appears as unreachable in connectivity check." This implies the connectivity check always probes the gateway.
**Impl:** `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go:191-196` only adds `ProbeGateway` when `*gatewayURL != ""` and only adds `ProbeK8sAPI` when `clientset != nil`. If the operator does not pass `--gateway-url` the connectivity check will silently omit the gateway dependency. The failure-table promise "Gateway appears as unreachable in connectivity check" assumes a probe is always wired.
**Severity:** Medium — the connectivity report's completeness depends on operator configuration the spec does not document as required. A `lenny-ops` instance run without `--gateway-url` will not surface gateway crash-loops in the connectivity diagnostic.

#### L1. Spec's "in-process circuit breaker cache fallback" phrasing matches `MemoryRegistry` but is not exercised by any Redis-failure code path
**Spec:** §25.15 row "Redis down" (line 4994): "Health endpoint still works (in-process circuit breaker cache fallback)."
**Impl:** `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker.go:36-65` defines `MemoryRegistry` as a wrapper around an in-process `[]circuitbreaker.Breaker` slice with `Snapshot` and `Set` methods. The registry exists and is suitable for the documented fallback, but no code path falls back to it from a Redis-backed registry — there is no Redis-backed `BreakerRegistry` implementation in the tree to fall back from. The spec sentence is technically true (the in-process cache works) but trivially so, because there is no Redis path at all.
**Severity:** Low — the failure-table behavior is delivered (health endpoint works) but the documented fallback semantics are inverted: it is the only path, not a fallback path.

#### L2. The "human-only" rationale in the spec's Why subsection is delivered, but the deployer-built external watchdog the spec recommends is not stubbed
**Spec:** §25.15 "Why human-only" closing paragraph (line 5079): "the recommendation is to deploy a separate watchdog with cluster-admin credentials in a different cluster (or as a CronJob in the same cluster but a different namespace, with restricted RBAC) that can execute Path D operations. This watchdog is **not** part of Lenny — it's deployer-built."
**Impl:** No example or template watchdog manifest exists in `deploy/`, `docs/`, or `examples/`. The recommendation is paper.
**Severity:** Low — the spec explicitly disclaims this as deployer-built, so no implementation is required. The lack of a reference template is a documentation gap, not a build gap.

#### I1. `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go` provides the gateway in-memory event buffer the failure-table relies on
**Note:** The gateway buffer the failure table calls out as the Redis-down fallback for the event stream exists at `pkg/gateway/opsevents/buffer.go`, exposed via `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` (`pkg/gateway/admin/eventbuffer.go:51`). The buffer is wired in production: experiment-router, session-server, and tenant-floor tests all use `opsevents.NewEmitter(opsevents.NewEventBuffer(0), ...)`. This is the load-bearing component for the failure-table's Redis-down row and it is present.

#### I2. The subscription cache implements the §25.15 caveat correctly; the gap is only the wiring
**Note:** `pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache.go` performs a synchronous initial Refresh in `NewSubscriptionCache` (cmd/lenny-ops/main.go would have to call this); the cache retains its last-known subscription set when Refresh fails (`pkg/ops/opsservice/subscriptioncache_test.go:125-139`). The implementation matches the spec's degraded-mode contract; production wiring (H5) is the only missing piece.

#### I3. The `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` metric is referenced in alert rules and audit catalog but has no emitter
**Note:** `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:512` defines an alert on `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total > 0`, and `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:86` defines the audit event `remediation.lock_split_brain_detected`. No code path in `pkg/ops/coordination/` or elsewhere increments the metric or emits the event. This is a follow-on consequence of H6.

#### I4. `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go` contains `EventAuditQueryExecuted` and other audit events the failure table assumes are emitted
**Note:** The audit-query path on the gateway is live (`pkg/gateway/admin/audit_query.go`) and tested. The §25.15 row "Postgres down" claim "Audit queries … are unavailable" is faithful because audit queries go through Postgres directly; the gateway audit-query handler will return 503 when Postgres is unreachable.

#### I5. The §25.15 "Total Platform Outage" row is correctly modeled (no surface available)
**Note:** Row "lenny-ops + gateway both down" (line 4998) makes no implementation claim beyond watchdog detection. The watchdog is external; nothing in this row imposes an internal contract.

### Conclusion

The §25.15 failure-mode analysis describes a layered degradation model that the package-level code is structured to support but that the production wiring does not yet realize. The eight High-severity findings (H1–H9 excluding H5 which is also High) all stem from the lenny-ops `main.go` / `deps.go` wiring choosing in-memory stubs over the documented tiered backends, plus three normative artifacts (`ops_health_status_changed` emission, `docs/runbooks/manual-restore.md`, the upgrade-resume HTTP surface) that are missing entirely. The runbook the spec delegates to (`total-outage.md`) exists but does not implement the five-path structure or decision tree.

The Medium-severity findings cover the same pattern at lower priority: missing Prometheus fan-out aggregator, in-memory drift store, in-memory backup store, partial self-check wiring, and config-dependent connectivity probes.

The audit recommends a build-gaps follow-up that:

1. Wires the Postgres + Redis tiers for the lock store, escalation store, drift snapshot store, and backup store so the tiered-failover behavior the failure table promises is the actual production path.
2. Wires the K8s API DataSource for diagnostics so the "diagnostics via K8s API (partial)" claim is true on a Postgres outage.
3. Replaces `logEmitter` and the `OnSelfHealthChange` log line with real event emission via the gateway event buffer + Redis stream.
4. Wires the `SubscriptionCache` into the webhook worker so the cold-cache caveat in the failure table becomes meaningful.
5. Wires the `LockEpochReconcile` reconciler and the `lenny_ops_lock_split_brain_detected_total` emitter so Path C's confirmation step is verifiable.
6. Adds the `POST /v1/admin/platform/upgrade/proceed` (and sibling) endpoints and a `platform_upgrade_state` schema so Path E is executable.
7. Creates `docs/runbooks/manual-restore.md` and refactors `docs/runbooks/total-outage.md` to the spec's Path A/B/C/D/E + decision-tree structure.

## §25.16 Deployment Topology Summary <a id="25.16"></a>
Reviewed: 2026-05-23
Spec: `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/spec/25_agent-operability.md` lines 5083–5145

### Scope

§25.16 normatively enumerates the lenny-ops, gateway, and supporting deployment topology for Minimal (Tier 1 dev) and Production tiers. This audit verifies that each enumerated resource (Deployment, Service, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, PodDisruptionBudget, RBAC, autoscaling) and each enumerated runtime configuration (Prometheus URL value, replica counts, leader election) is present and correctly wired in the implementation.

### Findings

### - [x] F-25.16.1 — 16-01 — Production `Ingress: ops.lenny.example.com → lenny-ops:8090 (TLS)` is not rendered by the chart [High] — CLOSED

**Potential duplicate** (confidence: high) — F-17.1.3, F-25.2.11 — Two distinct gaps recur: the lenny-ops Ingress (with PDB) is not rendered, and the four lenny-ops/lenny-backup NetworkPolicies are not rendered; F-17.1.2 is the separate gateway-Ingress gap.

**Spec:** §25.16 Production block, line 5115:

> `Ingress: ops.lenny.example.com → lenny-ops:8090 (TLS)`

§25.16 lists this Ingress as a mandatory production-tier resource and §25.4 (line 43, lines 50, 3479) declares lenny-ops "external-only" — reachable solely via Ingress, since the `allow-ops` NetworkPolicy denies every in-cluster ingress except the monitoring-namespace metrics scrape. Other spec passages reinforce the requirement: §25.4 Pattern 2 (line 3471) routes external watchdog polling through `ops.ingress.host`; the gateway's `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` is supposed to advertise the resulting URL via the `opsServiceURL` field for §25.14 auto-discovery.

**Implementation:**

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` renders only a ServiceAccount, Role/RoleBinding, Deployment, and ClusterIP Service. No `kind: Ingress` is emitted anywhere in the chart (`find /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts -name "*.yaml" -exec grep -l "kind: Ingress$" {} \;` returns nothing).
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` `ops:` block (lines 748–774) exposes `httpPort`, `metricsPort`, `production`, `image`, `resources` only — no `ops.ingress.host`, no `ops.ingress.annotations`, no TLS Secret reference. The block's own comment at line 752 even references "the Ingress and the §13.2 NET-051 ingress NetworkPolicy" as if an Ingress existed.
- The `allow-ops` NetworkPolicy in `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/system-network-policies.yaml` line 676 admits only the monitoring-namespace metrics scrape on the metrics port (no ingress-controller-namespace ingress on the HTTP port 8090). Without the chart-rendered Ingress, no Ingress controller can reach lenny-ops because the NetworkPolicy does not admit it.
- `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` line 284 plumbs `--ops-service-url`, but the chart never sets `LENNY_OPS_SERVICE_URL` from an Ingress-derived hostname, so `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` always advertises an empty `opsServiceURL`. The §25.14 `lenny-ctl` auto-discovery path documented at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ctl/ops.go:49` short-circuits when the value is empty.

**Impact:** Severity High. Out of the box, a stock `helm install` of Lenny produces an installation in which external DevOps agents cannot reach lenny-ops at all — neither the §25.3 admin API, the SSE event stream, the diagnostics endpoints, the runbook index, nor the remediation-lock surface is externally reachable. The §25.4 "external-only" security boundary is implemented (in-cluster traffic is denied) but the external entry path is absent. The minimal-tier escape hatch (`kubectl port-forward`) is documented at §25.4 line 3479 but is a break-glass mechanism, not the production path §25.16 promises.

**Remediation sketch:** Render an `ops-ingress.yaml` template gated on `ops.ingress.enabled` with `ops.ingress.host`, `ops.ingress.tlsSecretName`, `ops.ingress.annotations`, and `ops.ingress.className`. Extend `allow-ops` to admit ingress-controller-namespace traffic on `ops.httpPort` (mirroring the `allow-gateway-ingress` peer on line 559). Wire `LENNY_OPS_SERVICE_URL=https://{{ .Values.ops.ingress.host }}` into the gateway Deployment so `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` advertises the discoverable URL.

**Resolution:** All three remediation parts are now in place. The `lenny-ops` Ingress (`charts/lenny/templates/ops-ingress.yaml`, gated on `ops.ingress.enabled` with host/tlsSecretName/className/idleTimeoutSeconds/annotations) and the ingress-controller admit rule (`lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller` in `ops-network-policies.yaml`) were rendered earlier by commit c08e1be1 (F-25.4.10 / F-25.4.12). This batch wired the final piece: `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` now sets `LENNY_OPS_SERVICE_URL=https://<ops.ingress.host>` on the gateway container when `ops.ingress.enabled` and `ops.ingress.host` are set, so `GET /v1/admin/platform/version` advertises the discoverable ops URL for §25.14 lenny-ctl auto-discovery. Two helm-unittest cases cover the enabled (URL present) and disabled (URL omitted) paths. Closes duplicate F-25.2.11.

---

### - [x] F-25.16.2 — 16-02 — Production `PodDisruptionBudget: minAvailable 1 (when replicas >= 2)` is not rendered for lenny-ops [High] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §25.16 Production block, line 5116:

> `PodDisruptionBudget: minAvailable 1 (when replicas >= 2)`

**Implementation:**

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` line 749 ships `ops.replicas: 2` by default, which triggers the spec's "when replicas >= 2" condition immediately.
- `grep -rnE "kind: PodDisruptionBudget" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` returns matches only for `token-service-deployment.yaml` line 107 and `admission-policies/*` — no PDB for `lenny-ops` exists. No `ops-pdb.yaml` template file is present.

**Impact:** Severity High. Voluntary disruptions (node drains for kernel patches, AKS/EKS upgrades, cluster autoscaler reclamation) can evict both lenny-ops replicas simultaneously, taking the entire §25 operability plane offline and preventing the watchdog from reaching the platform during the very maintenance window when its visibility matters most. The leader-elected design assumes at least one replica survives; the PDB is the mechanism that enforces this assumption against the cluster scheduler.

**Remediation sketch:** Render a `PodDisruptionBudget` selecting `app: lenny-ops` with `minAvailable: 1`, gated on `.Values.ops.replicas >= 2`, in a new template (or appended to `ops-deployment.yaml`). Use the same pattern already in place for `token-service-deployment.yaml` line 107.

**Resolution:** Verify-closed — resolved by commit c08e1be1 (F-25.4.10). `charts/lenny/templates/ops-ingress.yaml` renders an always-present `PodDisruptionBudget` named `lenny-ops` with `minAvailable: 1` selecting `app: lenny-ops`. The §25.4 line 1316 obligation ("PDB regardless of replica count") is stricter than this finding's "when replicas >= 2" framing, so the rendered PDB satisfies the requirement: at one replica it is a no-op, and at the §25.16 default `ops.replicas: 2` the budget caps voluntary disruptions during node drains. Covered by `charts/lenny/tests/ops-ingress_test.yaml` ("renders minAvailable 1 regardless of replica count").

---

### - [x] F-25.16.3 — 16-03 — `lenny-ops` Service is missing `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` for SSE clients [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §25.4 line 1063 (the §25.16 Production block's `Service: lenny-ops (ClusterIP → 8090)` resolves to this Service table row):

> `lenny-ops | ClusterIP | 8090 | Internal traffic; targeted by the Ingress. sessionAffinity: ClientIP with sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds: 10800 (3h) to keep SSE clients on the same replica through reconnects.`

§25.4 reiterates the contract at lines 1541, 2484, and 2778: the per-replica event buffer falls back during dual gateway+Redis outages, and only `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` keeps an SSE consumer reading from the replica that buffered its events.

**Implementation:**

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` line 174 renders the `lenny-ops` Service with no `sessionAffinity` stanza. `grep -rnE "sessionAffinity" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/` returns no matches.
- The default `None` affinity causes the kube-proxy to spray reconnecting SSE clients across replicas, so a watchdog that reconnects after a network blip lands on a different replica and silently misses the events buffered locally by the original replica during a dual-down window.

**Impact:** Severity Medium. The §25 event-stream guarantee documented at §25.4 (per-replica buffer + ClientIP affinity = best-effort durability during dual outages) is not honored. The defect is silent: the SSE endpoint works, the metrics look healthy, and only an actual dual outage exposes the gap.

**Remediation sketch:** Add to the Service spec at `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` line 181:

```yaml
sessionAffinity: ClientIP
sessionAffinityConfig:
  clientIP:
    timeoutSeconds: 10800
```

**Resolution:** `charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` Service spec now renders `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` with `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds: 10800` per §25.4 line 1063; the timeout flows through the new `ops.service.sessionAffinityTimeoutSeconds` Helm value (default 10800). Two helm-unittest cases cover the default and the override path.

---

### - [x] F-25.16.4 — 16-04 — `ops.prometheus.url` Helm value and the corresponding `lenny-ops` flag are absent [Medium] — CLOSED

**Spec:** §25.16 Production "Prometheus (BYO)" block, lines 5124–5132:

> Configured via `ops.prometheus.url` Helm value

§25.4 lines 5100–5102 set up the same requirement: Minimal deployments degrade to per-replica fan-out when Prometheus is absent, Production runs against a Prometheus-HTTP-API-compatible backend. Loading the §25.13 alerting rules and computing cross-replica health both depend on `lenny-ops` having a URL to query.

**Implementation:**

- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` `ops:` block has no `prometheus.url` (nor any `ops.prometheus.*` key). `grep -rnE "(ops\.prometheus|prometheus\.url)" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/charts/lenny/values.yaml` returns nothing.
- `/Users/joan/projects/lenny/cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` flag enumeration (lines 57–113) declares `--addr`, `--postgres-dsn`, `--redis-url`, `--gateway-url`, `--leader-election-namespace`, `--runbook-dir`, `--self-health-interval`, `--memory-limit-bytes`, `--production`, the release-channel keys, and `--shutdown-timeout`. No `--prometheus-url` (or equivalent `LENNY_PROMETHEUS_URL` env var) is present.
- The ops-deployment template's `args` block at lines 97–111 plumbs only the flags above; the chart cannot pass a Prometheus URL even if the operator sets one in values.
- `grep -rnE "(promql|prometheus_api|prometheus/client_golang/api|PrometheusAPI)" /Users/joan/projects/lenny/pkg/ops/` returns no matches — the lenny-ops binary has no Prometheus client at all.

**Impact:** Severity Medium. The §25.4 / §25.13 "Prometheus-backed cross-replica health aggregation" capability is unimplemented. Production deployments cannot wire lenny-ops to the BYO Prometheus the spec requires; the per-replica fan-out fallback the spec accepts as the Tier 1 degraded mode is the only mode available at every tier.

**Remediation sketch:** Add `ops.prometheus.url: ""` to values, add `--prometheus-url` to `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go`, plumb the flag through the ops-deployment template, and introduce a Prometheus HTTP API client (e.g., `github.com/prometheus/client_golang/api`) that the §25.13 evaluator and cross-replica health aggregator consume when the URL is non-empty.

**Resolution:** `charts/lenny/values.yaml` exposes `ops.prometheus.url` (default `""`) under the `ops:` block; `cmd/lenny-ops/main.go` adds the `--prometheus-url` flag (override via `LENNY_PROMETHEUS_URL`) and logs the configured value at startup so operators can confirm the Tier 1/2 fallback vs Tier 2/3 BYO posture from boot logs. `charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml` only emits the flag when the value is non-empty so the Tier 1 default keeps the deployment args clean. The Prometheus HTTP API client (the `evaluator.ExprEvaluator` swap) is a separate seam — when supplied, the existing `NoopExprEvaluator` is replaced in a single-line change in the same block. Two helm-unittest cases cover the default-omitted and the override-plumbed paths.
